diseases.name: Abdominal Migraine - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Abdominal migraine is a type of migraine that primarily affects children but can also occur in adults. It is characterized by recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, often accompanied by nausea and vomiting. While it may not be as widely recognized as other forms of migraine, understanding abdominal migraine is crucial for effective management and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of abdominal migraine, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of abdominal migraine can vary from person to person but typically include:
Severe Abdominal Pain: Often described as crampy or colicky, usually located around the navel.
Nausea and Vomiting: Many individuals experience significant nausea, which may lead to vomiting.
Loss of Appetite: Affected individuals may not feel like eating during an episode.
Pallor: Some may appear pale or have a change in skin color during an attack.
Fatigue: After an episode, individuals often feel tired or lethargic.

diseases.name: Abetalipoproteinemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Abetalipoproteinemia is a rare genetic disorder that affects the body's ability to absorb dietary fats and fat-soluble vitamins. This condition is significant not only because of its rarity but also due to the serious health complications it can cause if left untreated. Individuals with abetalipoproteinemia often face challenges related to nutrient absorption, leading to a range of symptoms that can impact their quality of life. Understanding this condition is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: Fat Malabsorption: This leads to diarrhea, steatorrhea (fatty stools), and weight loss.

Nutritional Deficiencies: Deficiencies in fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) can lead to various health issues, including: Vitamin A Deficiency: Night blindness and vision problems. Vitamin D Deficiency: Bone pain and increased risk of fractures. Vitamin E Deficiency: Neurological problems, including ataxia and peripheral neuropathy. Vitamin K Deficiency: Increased bleeding and bruising.
Vitamin A Deficiency: Night blindness and vision problems.
Vitamin D Deficiency: Bone pain and increased risk of fractures.
Vitamin E Deficiency: Neurological problems, including ataxia and peripheral neuropathy.
Vitamin K Deficiency: Increased bleeding and bruising.
Growth Retardation: Children may experience delayed growth and development.
Neurological Symptoms: These can include muscle weakness, coordination problems, and cognitive difficulties.

diseases.name: Abnormal Gait : Symptoms, Causes and Treatments
diseases.description: The way a human being walk is called gait. Walking may look straightforward and uncomplicated, but several body parts, including eyes, ears, brain, muscles, and sensory nerves, rely on each other for a proper gait. When these body parts fail to function, it causes walking difficulties or gait disorders.
symptoms: The common symptoms of abnormal gait are as follows:
Difficulty walking
Balance issues
Instability
People with gait disorder also experience the following:
Dizziness
Light-headedness
Vertigo
Motion sickness
Double vision
Some patients may experience other symptoms due to their underlying health conditions.

diseases.name: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: Causes, Diagnosis & Treatment
diseases.description: Women have menstrual cycles from the age of 11-12 years to about 50 years. In these 40 years’ time span women is likely to have a few episodes of bleeding which is not her usual cycle. If this abnormality persists then one needs to become concerned and consult a gynecologist. There may be an increase in the number of days of bleeding, there could be heavy bleeding with clots there could be associated pain or the bleeding could be irregular. It is normal for menstrual bleeding of a woman to last up to 7 days. Abnormal bleeding can happen when the menstrual period is not regular (when bleeding is longer than normal) is heavier than normal, or when the patterns of bleeding changes. What is a normal menstrual cycle? A normal cycle that comes every 28-35 days lasts for 7-8 days and is not associated with pain or clots. During the menstrual cycle, two hormones -estrogen and progesterone act on the lining (endometrium) of the uterus and causes it to grow. At the end of the cycle, this endometrium sheds and this is seen as menstrual bleeding. The menstrual cycle begins with the first day of the bleeding of one period (referred to as D1) and ends with the first day of the next period. An average cycle lasts approximately 28 days, but it can be shorter or longer. If the cycle is longer than 35 days or shorter than 21 days, it is considered abnormal. Abnormal uterine bleeding includes:

diseases.name: Abscess: Types, Symptoms, Causes & Treatment
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT
symptoms: The symptoms of abscess include:
A painful tender red mass
Pus in the middle
Head or a point appears as the condition progresses and then ruptures

The condition may even aggravate, if no proper care is taken. Also, it may spread the infection into the tissues or even into the bloodstream. If the infection spreads deeper into the tissue, the person may also develop a fever or feel sick.

diseases.name: Absence Seizure- Symptoms & Causes
diseases.description: Absence seizures are characterized by transient, unexpected losses in consciousness. This condition affects children more than adults.
symptoms: Looking for a blank facial expression that lasts a few seconds is the quickest way to identify an absence seizure. People who experience absence seizures do not speak, listen, or appear to understand what is going on. Occurrence of such episodes can happen at any time.
Other signs and symptoms include:
Being completely still
Making a chewing motion with the mouth
Fluttering of eyelids
Not talking or moving suddenly
If you have jerking motions in addition to the absence seizure, it could be an indication of another form of seizure.

diseases.name: Acanthosis Nigricans: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Acanthosis nigricans is a skin condition that is characterized by areas of dark, velvety discolouration in the body folds. This skin condition is usually a symptom of an underlying disorder.
symptoms: The only signs of acanthosis nigricans are skin changes. People may notice dark, thickened, velvety skin in the body folds and creases, usually in the armpit, groin, and back of the neck. The skin may emit an odor or itch.

diseases.name: Acetabular Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acetabular fractures are significant injuries that involve the acetabulum, the socket of the hip joint where the femur (thigh bone) fits. These fractures can lead to severe complications, including chronic pain, mobility issues, and long-term disability. Understanding acetabular fractures is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Hip Pain: Severe pain in the hip or groin area is the most common symptom.
Inability to Bear Weight: Patients often find it difficult or impossible to put weight on the affected leg.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling and bruising around the hip joint may occur.
Deformity: In some cases, the leg may appear shorter or turned outward.

diseases.name: Achalasia: Causes, Symptoms, Prevention, and Treatment
diseases.description: Achalasia is a rare disorder in which the damaged nerves in the esophagus prevent it from working correctly. Consequently, your esophagus becomes paralyzed and dilated over time and finally loses the ability to squeeze food down into your stomach.
symptoms: The symptoms of achalasia develop slowly, with symptoms lasting months or years. They include the following:
Dysphagia (trouble swallowing and feeling as if food is stuck in the esophagus) is the most common early sign of this condition.
Regurgitation of the undigested food
Pain or discomfort in the chest
Heartburn
Belching
Chest pain that comes and goes
Coughing at night
Pneumonia (from aspiration of food into the lungs)
Weight loss
Vomiting

diseases.name: Achilles Tendinitis
diseases.description: Achilles tendinitis is an overuse injury of the Achilles tendon, the band of tissue that connects calf muscles at the back of the lower leg to your heel bone. It most commonly occurs in runners who have suddenly increased the intensity or duration of their runs. It's also common in middle-aged people who play sports, such as tennis or basketball, only on the weekends.
symptoms: Pain and stiffness along the Achilles tendon in the morning
Pain along the tendon or back of the heel that worsens with activity
Severe pain the day after exercising
Thickening of the tendon
Bone spur (insertional tendinitis)
Swelling that is present all the time and gets worse throughout the day with activity

diseases.name: Achilles Tendon Rupture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The Achilles tendon is the largest tendon in the human body, connecting the calf muscles to the heel bone. An Achilles tendon rupture occurs when this tendon is completely torn, often resulting in significant pain and loss of mobility. This injury is particularly significant for athletes and active individuals, as it can severely impact their ability to participate in sports and daily activities. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for an Achilles tendon rupture is crucial for effective management and recovery.
symptoms: Sudden Pain: A sudden, sharp pain in the back of the ankle or calf is often the first symptom experienced.
Swelling: Swelling around the heel and ankle may occur shortly after the injury.
Difficulty Walking: Individuals may find it challenging to walk or bear weight on the affected leg.
A "Pop" Sound: Many people report hearing a popping sound at the moment of injury.
Stiffness: Stiffness in the ankle and difficulty moving the foot may develop.

diseases.name: Achromatopsia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Achromatopsia is a rare visual disorder characterized by a complete absence of color vision, leading to a world perceived in shades of gray. This condition significantly impacts the quality of life for those affected, as it can hinder daily activities, social interactions, and overall well-being. Understanding achromatopsia is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for their families, educators, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of achromatopsia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Individuals with achromatopsia experience a range of symptoms, including:
Complete Color Blindness: The inability to perceive any colors, seeing only shades of gray.
Photophobia: Increased sensitivity to light, making bright environments uncomfortable.
Nystagmus: Involuntary eye movements that can affect visual stability.
Reduced Visual Acuity: Difficulty seeing fine details, often leading to blurred vision.
Strabismus: Misalignment of the eyes, which can occur in some individuals.

diseases.name: Acid Reflux (GERD)
diseases.description: GERD is a long-term condition in which stomach contents flow back into the esophagus, causing heartburn and other symptoms.
symptoms: Heartburn
Regurgitation of food or sour liquid
Chest discomfort
Chronic cough or hoarseness

diseases.name: Acl Tear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: An Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) tear is a common injury that affects the knee joint, particularly among athletes and active individuals. The ACL is one of the key ligaments that help stabilize the knee, and its injury can significantly impact mobility and quality of life. Understanding ACL tears, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is crucial for anyone involved in sports or physical activities. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ACL tears, making the information accessible to a general audience.
symptoms: Sudden Pain: Many individuals report a sudden, sharp pain in the knee at the time of injury.
Swelling: Swelling typically occurs within a few hours after the injury due to fluid accumulation in the joint.
Instability: A feeling of the knee "giving way" or instability is common, making it difficult to walk or bear weight.
Limited Range of Motion: Individuals may experience difficulty bending or straightening the knee.
Popping Sound: Some people report hearing a "pop" at the moment of injury.

diseases.name: Acne
diseases.description: Acne is a chronic skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads, pimples, nodules, and cysts. Acne commonly appears on the face, forehead, chest, upper back, and shoulders. While it primarily affects teenagers, it can occur at any age.
symptoms: Whiteheads (closed plugged pores)
Blackheads (open plugged pores)
Pimples (papules)
Pustules (papules with pus)
Nodules (large solid painful lumps)
Cystic lesions (painful, pus-filled lumps)

diseases.name: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)
diseases.description: Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is a disease caused by human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). HIV damages the immune system and decreases the ability of your body to fight against infections and diseases. In the early 1980s, doctors described unusual infections and cancers among gay men. These men developed unusual pneumonia caused by Pneumocystis carinii and cancers like Kaposi sarcoma and died due to a severe deficiency in their body’s immune defenses. By September 1982, CDC had named this condition as AIDS or acquired immune deficiency syndrome and proposed that it causes a defect in the cell-mediated immunity of the body. Later, the disease was also shown to affect intravenous drug abusers and patients suffering from hemophilia. In 1984, the human immunodeficiency virus was discovered as the cause of AIDS by scientists Luc Montagnier and Robert Gallo. Clinically, HIV infection progresses through 3 stages, namely, acute primary infection, stage of clinical latency and AIDS. Throughout these stages, the immunity of the individual progressively decreases, and the number of immune cells present reduces. When the immunity of the individual infected with HIV becomes extremely weak, specific immune cells in his body known as CD4 cells decrease below 200 cells/mm3, and he develops AIDS. AIDS is the most serious phase of HIV infection. In this phase, the patient suffers AIDS symptoms like severe, life-threatening infections, cancers and neurological complications of AIDS. HIV infection is diagnosed by testing for antibodies against HIV in the blood of the patient. A few tests which detect the presence of viral DNA and CD4 cell counts are used to guide AIDS treatment. According to worldwide the statistics published by the World Health Organisation, by the end of 2016, 36.7 million people were infected with HIV. Additionally, 1.6 million deaths occurred due to causes related to AIDS. The African continent has the highest number of people affected. Currently, AIDS is described as a pandemic, a disease which has spread across continents. People in developing countries are most affected, as HIV infection increases the chances of acquiring infections like tuberculosis and dying due to AIDS-related complications. AIDS also affects the economy of the country because a majority of the individuals affected are in the productive age group. Studies have reported that ninety-five percent of individuals with HIV infection live in developing countries. Poverty, the presence of other severe illnesses, unavailability of appropriate medical care and ignorance aggravates the burden of AIDS in these nations.

diseases.name: Acrocyanosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acrocyanosis is a condition characterized by a bluish discoloration of the extremities, particularly the hands and feet. This phenomenon occurs due to a decrease in blood flow to the skin, often resulting from various underlying factors. While acrocyanosis itself is generally not harmful, it can be a sign of other health issues that may require attention. Understanding acrocyanosis is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, as well as knowing when to seek medical help.
symptoms: The primary symptom of acrocyanosis is the bluish discoloration of the skin, particularly in the extremities. Other symptoms may include:
Coldness in the affected areas
Numbness or tingling sensations
Swelling in the fingers or toes
Skin that appears shiny or smooth

diseases.name: Actinic Cheilitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Actinic Cheilitis is a condition that affects the lips, primarily caused by prolonged exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light. It is significant because it can lead to more serious conditions, including squamous cell carcinoma, if left untreated. Understanding Actinic Cheilitis is crucial for early detection and management, especially for individuals who spend considerable time outdoors or have a history of sun exposure. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of Actinic Cheilitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Dryness and Cracking: The lips may become dry, leading to cracks and fissures.
Scaling: White or yellowish scales may develop on the lips.
Discoloration: The affected area may appear lighter or darker than the surrounding skin.
Sensitivity: The lips may become sensitive to touch or temperature changes.
Swelling: In some cases, the lips may appear swollen or inflamed.

diseases.name: Actinic Keratosis (AK) : Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Actinic keratosis (AK) is a scaly rough, patch on the skin which develops from years of sun exposure. If left untreated, the risk of actinic keratoses turning into a type of skin cancer, known as squamous cell carcinoma is about 5% to 10%.
symptoms: Typically, the first symptom of actinic keratosis are rough, raised bumps on the skin that may vary in colour but often have a brown or yellow crust on top. These bumps can be grey, pink, red, or the same colour as the skin. The symptoms can also include the following:
● Bleeding
● Dry, scaly lips
● Burning, stinging, or itching
● Loss of colour in the lips
● Pain or tenderness

diseases.name: Actinomycosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Actinomycosis is a rare but significant bacterial infection that primarily affects the soft tissues of the body. It is caused by a group of bacteria known as Actinomyces , which are typically found in the mouth and gastrointestinal tract. While it is not a common condition, understanding actinomycosis is crucial due to its potential to cause serious health issues if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of actinomycosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of actinomycosis can vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include:
Cervicofacial Actinomycosis: Swelling and pain in the jaw or neck, formation of abscesses, and drainage of pus.
Thoracic Actinomycosis: Cough, chest pain, fever, and difficulty breathing.
Abdominal Actinomycosis: Abdominal pain, fever, and gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea and vomiting.
Pelvic Actinomycosis: Pelvic pain, abnormal vaginal discharge, and fever.

diseases.name: Active Surveillance of Prostate Cancer - An overview
diseases.description: Active surveillance of prostate cancer is an approach to monitor early or localized prostate cancer. It is about close monitoring instead of getting started with the treatments right away.

diseases.name: Acute Abdomen - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute abdomen is a term used to describe a sudden onset of severe abdominal pain that may indicate a serious underlying medical condition. This condition is significant because it often requires immediate medical attention to prevent complications or even death. Understanding acute abdomen is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely diagnosis and treatment can be life-saving.
symptoms: The symptoms of acute abdomen can vary widely depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Severe Abdominal Pain: This is the hallmark symptom and can be localized or diffuse.
Nausea and Vomiting: Many patients experience gastrointestinal upset.
Fever: A sign of infection or inflammation.
Changes in Bowel Habits: Diarrhea or constipation may occur.
Abdominal Distension: Swelling of the abdomen can indicate fluid accumulation or obstruction.

diseases.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) is a term that encompasses a range of conditions associated with sudden, reduced blood flow to the heart. It is a critical medical emergency that can lead to severe complications, including heart attacks and even death. Understanding ACS is vital for recognizing its symptoms, knowing the risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Acute Coronary Syndrome, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and preventive measures.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of ACS is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain or Discomfort: Often described as a feeling of pressure, squeezing, or fullness in the center or left side of the chest.
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate to the arms, back, neck, jaw, or stomach.
Shortness of Breath: This may occur with or without chest discomfort.
Nausea or Vomiting: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal symptoms.
Sweating: Profuse sweating, often described as "cold sweat," can occur.
Lightheadedness or Dizziness: Feeling faint or weak can be a sign of reduced blood flow to the heart.

diseases.name: Acute Cystitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute cystitis is a common yet often overlooked condition that affects many individuals, particularly women. It is characterized by inflammation of the bladder, typically caused by a bacterial infection. Understanding acute cystitis is crucial not only for those who experience its symptoms but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of acute cystitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Individuals with acute cystitis may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Frequent Urination: A strong, persistent urge to urinate, often resulting in little urine being passed.
Burning Sensation: A painful or burning feeling during urination.
Cloudy or Strong-Smelling Urine: Changes in urine appearance or odor can indicate infection.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pressure in the lower abdomen or pelvic area.
Blood in Urine: Hematuria, or blood in the urine, may occur in some cases.

diseases.name: Acute Encephalitis Syndrome (AES) - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: AES (Acute Encephalitis Syndrome) is a critical public health concern in India. Also known as ‘Chamki Fever’ or Litchi Virus , AES is a health condition that mainly affects young adults and children and causes inflammation, irritation, or swelling of the brain. Most importantly, it can lead to a significant number of deaths. The chief cause of acute encephalitis syndrome in India is the Japanese Encephalitis Virus (JEV) . Besides, Influenza A virus, Herpes simplex virus, Parvovirus B4, dengue, Epstein-Barr virus, Chandipura virus, S. pneumoniae, etc., are responsible for the sporadic spread of the disease in the country. The first case of JEV-induced AES was recorded in India in 1955 in Tamil Nadu (formerly called the State of Madras). According to the National Vector Borne Diseases Control Program (NVBDCP), over 10,400 cases of AES and more than 630 deaths were recorded from seventeen states in India in 2018. Jharkhand, Bihar, Assam, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Tripura, Meghalaya, Manipur, and Tamil Nadu add to the maximum number of cases. Apart from sources like fungus, bacteria, chemicals, parasites, toxins, and spirochetes reported to be the cause of Acute Encephalitis Syndrome over the past few decades, viruses have also been attributed mainly to be the cause of Acute Encephalitis Syndrome in India. In addition to viral encephalitis, severe forms of toxoplasmosis and leptospirosis can cause the Infections. Apart from this, the causative agent of encephalitis syndrome varies with geographical location and season.

diseases.name: Acute Fatty Liver Of Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy (AFLP) is a rare but serious condition that can occur during the third trimester of pregnancy. It is characterized by the accumulation of fat in the liver, which can lead to liver failure and other severe complications for both the mother and the fetus. Understanding AFLP is crucial for expectant mothers, healthcare providers, and families, as early recognition and management can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of AFLP, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of AFLP can vary but often include:
Nausea and Vomiting: Persistent nausea and vomiting that may not respond to typical remedies.
Abdominal Pain: Pain in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen, which may be severe.
Fatigue: Extreme tiredness or weakness that is disproportionate to normal pregnancy fatigue.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, indicating liver dysfunction.
Dark Urine: Urine that appears darker than usual, often a sign of liver issues.
Pale Stools: Stools that are lighter in color, which can indicate a lack of bile.

diseases.name: Acute Heart Attack - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The heart attack may manifest with a sudden onset of severe central chest pain described as heavy, compressing pain, which can radiate to the left hand, jaw or to the back. It is often associated with profuse sweating and weakness. The presentation can be so sudden that the patient suddenly collapses and becomes unresponsive with profuse sweating and cold peripheries. A patient with the above mentioned symptoms has to be rushed to the nearest hospital equipped with ECG facilities and a physician / cardiologists on call. Emergency measures include supplemental oxygen through a face mask, pain relief with strong analgesics, intravenous access and initial dose of aspirin and statins (lipid lowering drug). Once the diagnosis of heart attack is confirmed, the treatment is initiated.

diseases.name: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a fast-growing cancer of the blood and bone marrow. It affects the white blood cells called lymphoblasts (immature lymphocytes), which are meant to help fight infection. In ALL, these immature cells grow out of control and crowd out healthy blood cells. While ALL is an urgent and serious diagnosis, modern treatments are highly effective—especially when started early—and many children and adults go on to live full lives.
symptoms: Symptoms typically develop over days to weeks, reflecting low blood counts and high leukemia burden. Seek medical care promptly if these signs persist or worsen.
Common early signs:
Fatigue, weakness, or pale skin (from anemia)
Fevers or frequent infections that are hard to clear
Easy bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or tiny red spots under the skin (petechiae)
Additional symptoms:
Bone or joint pain, especially in children
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck, armpits, or groin
Abdominal fullness or discomfort from an enlarged spleen or liver
Shortness of breath, chest discomfort, or facial swelling if there is a chest mass (more common in T-ALL)
Headaches, vision changes, or vomiting if the central nervous system (CNS) is involved
Symptoms vary. Many are caused by conditions other than leukemia, but rapid evaluation is essential to rule out ALL and start treatment if needed.

diseases.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is an aggressive type of blood cancer that starts in the bone marrow and affects the production of healthy blood cells. Because it develops quickly, early recognition and treatment are important. This guide provides clear and reliable information about AML—its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, available treatment options, and what patients and families can expect. Understanding the condition can help you feel more prepared and supported as you navigate the steps ahead.
symptoms: The symptoms of AML often develop quickly, over a period of days or weeks. They are a direct result of the shortage of healthy blood cells. It is crucial to see a doctor promptly if you experience any of these symptoms.
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Swollen Gums: Some types of AML can cause the gums to swell and bleed.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: You may have painless, swollen lymph nodes in your neck, armpit, or groin.
A Feeling of Fullness: An enlarged spleen or liver, where leukemia cells can collect, may cause a feeling of fullness or discomfort in your abdomen.
Neurological Symptoms: In rare cases where leukemia cells have spread to the brain and spinal cord, it can cause headaches, vision problems, or seizures.
If you are at high risk for AML (e.g., a history of smoking or previous cancer treatment) and experience any of these symptoms, it is crucial to consult a doctor right away for an accurate diagnosis.

diseases.name: Acute Pericarditis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute pericarditis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the pericardium, the thin sac-like membrane surrounding the heart. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and, in some cases, serious complications if not properly managed. Understanding acute pericarditis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can significantly improve patient outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding acute pericarditis.
symptoms: The symptoms of acute pericarditis can vary in intensity and may include:
Chest Pain: The most common symptom, often described as sharp or stabbing, and may worsen with deep breathing, coughing, or lying down.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may occur, especially when lying flat.
Fever: A mild fever may accompany the inflammation.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness and malaise are common.
Palpitations: Some individuals may experience an irregular heartbeat or a sensation of fluttering in the chest.

diseases.name: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL) is a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) characterized by the rapid proliferation of promyelocytes in the bone marrow and blood. This rare but significant form of leukemia is notable for its unique genetic features and the potential for effective treatment, particularly with the advent of targeted therapies. Understanding APL is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers, as early detection and treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of APL can vary widely but often include:
Fatigue: A common symptom due to anemia caused by a lack of healthy red blood cells.
Frequent Infections: Resulting from a decrease in white blood cells, which are crucial for fighting infections.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: Due to low platelet counts, patients may experience unexplained bruising, nosebleeds, or bleeding gums.
Fever: Often a sign of infection or the body’s response to leukemia.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can occur due to the disease's impact on metabolism and appetite.
Bone Pain: Patients may experience pain in the bones or joints as the bone marrow becomes crowded with abnormal cells.

diseases.name: Acute Renal Failure : Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Acute Renal Failure is a rapid condition (almost less than 2 days) when the kidneys fail in their ability to filter/remove waste from the blood and in maintaining fluid and electrolyte balance in the body.
symptoms: There are times when lab tests are required to detect acute renal failure for lack of signs and symptoms. However, the following signs and symptoms are not hard to miss –
Irregular urine output – excessive to little/no urine at times
Bad breath and a weird taste of metal in the mouth
Frequent mood swings and confusion
Hiccups, Seizures, hand tremor or coma in severe cases
Poor appetite
Tiredness and drowsiness
Fluid retention and decreased sensation in the limbs
Chest pain and flank pain (between the ribs and the hips)
High blood pressure and shortness of breath
Nausea or vomiting that may run for days
Nose-bleeding besides bruising easily
Trace of blood in the stool

diseases.name: Acute Stress Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Stress Disorder (ASD) is a psychological condition that can occur in response to a traumatic event. It is characterized by a range of symptoms that can significantly impact an individual's daily life. Understanding ASD is crucial, as it can lead to more severe mental health issues if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Acute Stress Disorder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Acute Stress Disorder presents a variety of symptoms that can affect an individual's emotional and physical well-being. Common symptoms include:
Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary memories of the traumatic event.
Avoidance: Efforts to avoid reminders of the trauma, including people, places, or activities.
Negative Mood: Persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or emotional numbness.
Dissociation: A sense of detachment from oneself or the environment, feeling as if the event is happening again.
Heightened Arousal: Symptoms such as irritability, difficulty sleeping, hypervigilance, and exaggerated startle response.

diseases.name: Acute Tubular Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Tubular Necrosis (ATN) is a serious medical condition that affects the kidneys, specifically the tubules, which are tiny structures responsible for filtering waste and excess substances from the blood. Understanding ATN is crucial because it can lead to acute kidney injury (AKI), a potentially life-threatening condition that requires immediate medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Acute Tubular Necrosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Acute Tubular Necrosis can vary depending on the severity of the condition but may include:
Decreased Urine Output: A significant reduction in urine production is often one of the first signs of ATN.
Swelling: Fluid retention can lead to swelling in the legs, ankles, and face.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness may occur due to the buildup of toxins in the body.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms can arise as the kidneys fail to filter waste effectively.
Confusion: Accumulation of toxins can affect mental clarity and cognitive function.

diseases.name: Addison's Disease
diseases.description: Addison’s disease, also known as ‘adrenal insufficiency’ is a rare disorder where the adrenal glands do not produce certain hormones that are essential for healthy living. It may occur at any age in both men and women.
symptoms: Addison’s disease symptoms may develop over several months, which may include the following:
Extreme fatigue
Darkening of your skin (hyperpigmentation)
Weight loss and decreased appetite
Salt craving
Low blood pressure, even fainting
Nausea, diarrhea or vomiting
Abdominal pain
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
Muscle or joint pains
Irritability
Depression
Body hair loss or sexual dysfunction can be seen in women

However, some of the symptoms may occur immediately in case of acute adrenal gland failure. These symptoms may include pain in your lower back, abdomen or legs, low blood pressure, severe vomiting and diarrhea, leading to dehydration, low sodium (hyponatremia) and loss of consciousness.

diseases.name: ADEM: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, or ADEM, is a rare neurological condition. Anyone can get affected by ADEM, but it mostly affects children. It usually develops after a bacterial or viral infection.
symptoms: You may develop acute disseminated encephalomyelitis two to three weeks after a viral or bacterial upper respiratory tract infection or another form of infection in the body.
The onset of the symptoms is sudden and worsens quickly. The following are the symptoms:
Fever
Headache
Stiffness in the neck
A sensation of weakness, numbness, and tingling in the arms and legs
Problems in the balance
Lethargy
Optic neuritis (you may experience blurred or doubled vision as the disorder causes inflammation of the optic nerve)
Swallowing and speaking problems
Issues in the bladder and bowel
Changes in behavior, such as confusion and crankiness
In rare cases, seizures or coma
Paralysis on one side of the body

diseases.name: Adenocarcinoma (Stomach Cancer) - Stages, Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: Adenocarcinoma of the stomach is a type of stomach cancer or gastric cancer. It is an accumulation of abnormal cells that creates a mass in your stomach.
symptoms: ● Losing appetite.
● Difficulty in swallowing.
● Feeling bloated after meals.
● Frequent burping or hiccups.
● Feeling of heartburn .
● Unresolved indigestion.
● Constant stomach ache.
● Soreness in the breastbone.
● Irritable bowel syndrome (trapped wind).
● Persistent vomiting, sometimes excreting blood.
● Unexplained nausea .

As these symptoms are extremely common in other medical conditions, diagnosis without biopsy is not possible. So, if you have swallowing difficulties along with the above-mentioned symptoms, it is better to get a medical assessment.
● Anemia (low hemoglobin).
● Fluid buildup.
● Black or blood contains stools.
● Lethargy.
● Loss of appetite.
● Unexplained weight loss.

diseases.name: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma (ACC) is a rare type of cancer that primarily affects the salivary glands, though it can also occur in other areas such as the breast, skin, and respiratory tract. This malignancy is characterized by its slow growth and tendency to invade surrounding tissues, making it a significant concern for patients and healthcare providers alike. Understanding ACC is crucial for early detection, effective treatment, and improved patient outcomes.
symptoms: Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the tumor's location. Common symptoms include:
Swelling or a lump: Often in the salivary glands, neck, or mouth.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the affected area.
Numbness or weakness: If the tumor affects nearby nerves.
Difficulty swallowing or speaking: Particularly if the tumor is located in the throat or mouth.
Changes in saliva production: Such as dry mouth or difficulty in swallowing.

diseases.name: Adenomyosis: Symptoms, Causes, and Treatments
diseases.description: Adenomyosis is a medical condition where the inner tissue lining the uterus, also known as endometrium, starts to grow into the muscular wall of uterus. The causes of adenomyosis are not known yet, but the condition usually resolves on its own after menopause. It often develops in middle-aged women.The displaced tissue continues acting normally (thickening, breaking down as well as bleeding) during each menstrual cycle. This can result in an enlarged uterus and painful, heavy periods.
symptoms: Adenomyosis can cause:
● Heavy menstrual bleeding.
● Dysmenorrhea – Severe menstrual cramps.
● Dyspareunia – Painful sexual intercourse.
● Bloating.
● Abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Adjustment Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Adjustment Disorder is a mental health condition that arises when an individual experiences difficulty coping with a significant life change or stressor. This disorder can manifest in various ways, affecting emotional well-being and daily functioning. Understanding Adjustment Disorder is crucial, as it can lead to more severe mental health issues if left unaddressed. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Adjustment Disorder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Adjustment Disorder can manifest in various emotional and behavioral symptoms, including:
Sadness: Persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness.
Anxiety: Increased levels of anxiety or worry about the future.
Irritability: Heightened irritability or frustration over minor issues.
Social Withdrawal: Avoidance of social interactions and activities once enjoyed.
Difficulty Concentrating: Trouble focusing on tasks or making decisions.
Changes in Sleep Patterns: Insomnia or excessive sleeping.
Changes in Appetite: Significant weight loss or gain due to changes in eating habits.

diseases.name: Adrenal Adenoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Adrenal adenoma is a benign tumor that arises from the adrenal glands, which are small glands located on top of each kidney. These glands play a crucial role in producing hormones that regulate various bodily functions, including metabolism, immune response, and blood pressure. While adrenal adenomas are often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally during imaging studies for other conditions, their significance lies in their potential to disrupt hormonal balance and lead to various health issues. Understanding adrenal adenomas is essential for early detection, effective management, and improved patient outcomes.
symptoms: Adrenal adenomas are often asymptomatic, but when they do produce hormones, they can lead to various symptoms, including:
Cushing's Syndrome: Symptoms may include weight gain, particularly around the abdomen and face, thinning skin, easy bruising, and muscle weakness.
Hyperaldosteronism: This condition can cause high blood pressure, low potassium levels, and muscle cramps.
Adrenal Insufficiency: In some cases, adrenal adenomas can disrupt normal hormone production, leading to fatigue, weakness, and low blood pressure.

diseases.name: Adrenal Crisis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Adrenal crisis is a life-threatening condition that arises from insufficient levels of cortisol, a vital hormone produced by the adrenal glands. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe health complications, including shock and even death, if not promptly recognized and treated. Understanding adrenal crisis is crucial for individuals with adrenal insufficiency, healthcare providers, and caregivers, as timely intervention can save lives.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of an adrenal crisis is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Severe Fatigue: An overwhelming sense of tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Weakness: Muscle weakness that can affect daily activities.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal distress that may lead to dehydration.
Abdominal Pain: Often described as severe and cramp-like.
Low Blood Pressure: Hypotension can lead to dizziness or fainting.
Confusion or Altered Mental Status: Changes in consciousness or cognitive function.
Skin Changes: Darkening of the skin, particularly in areas exposed to sunlight.

diseases.name: Adrenal Gland Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: The adrenal glands are two small organs that sit on top of the kidneys. Despite their size, they play a major role in controlling hormones that regulate blood pressure, metabolism, stress response, and other essential body functions. An adrenal gland tumor is an abnormal growth in one or both adrenal glands. Adrenal gland tumors may be non-cancerous (benign) or cancerous (malignant). Most are found by chance on scans for other reasons. The aggressive form, called adrenocortical carcinoma, is very rare but needs urgent treatment.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on whether the tumor is functional (producing hormones) or non-functional (not producing hormones).
Excess hair growth (especially in women)
Deepening of the voice in women
Irregular menstrual cycles
Muscle cramps or weakness
Easy bruising or stretch marks on the skin
Diabetes or worsening blood sugar control
Because symptoms can mimic common conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, adrenal tumors may go unnoticed until they grow larger.

diseases.name: Adrenocortical Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare and aggressive cancer that originates in the adrenal glands, which are located on top of each kidney. These glands are responsible for producing hormones that regulate various bodily functions, including metabolism, immune response, and blood pressure. The significance of ACC lies in its potential to disrupt hormonal balance and its aggressive nature, which can lead to severe health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of adrenocortical carcinoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Adrenocortical carcinoma can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the tumor's size and the hormones it produces. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Persistent pain in the abdomen may indicate the presence of a tumor.
Weight Changes: Unexplained weight loss or gain can occur due to hormonal imbalances.

Hormonal Symptoms: Overproduction of hormones can lead to symptoms such as: Cushing's syndrome (weight gain, high blood pressure, diabetes) Virilization (development of male characteristics in women) Feminization (development of female characteristics in men)
Cushing's syndrome (weight gain, high blood pressure, diabetes)
Virilization (development of male characteristics in women)
Feminization (development of female characteristics in men)
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue may result from hormonal imbalances or the cancer itself.
Changes in Appetite: A noticeable increase or decrease in appetite can occur.

symptoms: The symptoms of Adult attention deficit hyperactivity disorder depend on the person’s age. Most of the time persons with ADHD are not aware of the disorder in themselves.
The symptoms of Adult attention deficit hyperactivity disorder include:
Impulsiveness and restlessness
Difficulty in organizing and prioritizing things
Difficulty on focusing on work and completing tasks

Difficulty in multitasking things

diseases.name: Adult Still's Disease: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Risk Factors
diseases.description: Adult-onset Still’s disease is also known as Wissler-Fanconi syndrome. It is a form of a rare type of inflammatory arthritis with no known cause. This condition causes high fever , swelling in the joints, organs, lymph nodes , and tissues, and rashes . Some patients with Still’s disease may experience only one episode. However, for a few others, the condition may persist or recur. The inflammation may destroy joints that are affected, particularly the wrists. The treatment involves medications such as prednisone that help control inflammation.
symptoms: The most common symptom of Adult Still’s disease is a fever that lasts for many days and peaks (spikes) at the same time every day. For some people, the fever can spike twice a day, at the same time each day. The patient may also notice a quick-changing salmon-pink rash on the skin that can look similar to hives. Usually, the rash appears on your trunk, arms or legs. Unlike hives, the rash is not itchy .
Sore throat
Swelling in the knee and tender joints
Muscle pain
Abdominal pain
Weight loss
Inflamed or swollen lymph nodes
Pain associated with deep breathing

The liver or spleen can become enlarged in rare cases. The tissues around major organs such as the heart and lungs can also be inflamed. A rare complication of this disease is macrophage activation syndrome (MAS), which can lead to serious, sometimes life-threatening, inflammation in the body.
The signs and symptoms of this condition mimics those of other disorders, including lupus and lymphoma , a type of cancer.

diseases.name: Aerophagia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aerophagia , a term derived from the Greek words "aero" meaning air and "phagia" meaning to eat, refers to the excessive swallowing of air. While it may seem like a trivial issue, aerophagia can lead to significant discomfort and may indicate underlying health problems. Understanding aerophagia is essential for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can affect quality of life and may require medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of aerophagia can vary in severity and may include:
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Belching: Frequent burping as a result of excess air in the stomach.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or cramping in the abdominal area.
Flatulence: Increased gas production leading to passing gas.

diseases.name: Afib (Atrial Fibrillation): Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Atrial fibrillation (Afib), is an abnormal and often rapid heart rate seen in most Indians Many with Atrial fibrillation are unaware that it increases the risk of stroke, heart failure, and other complicated heart conditions. While there is no proper data, most of the studies in Indian point that a maximum of six per every 1000 suffers from this condition. Often, atrial fibrillation symptoms include weakness, irregular heartbeat ,heart palpitations and shortness of breath.
symptoms: There are examples of people who suffer from atrial fibrillation but does not show any sign until it is found in a physical examination. But, most of the others suffering from it may show symptoms including:
Chest pain
Weakness
Dizziness
Lightheadedness
Decreased ability to exercise
Fatigue
Shortness of breath
Confusion
Palpitations (flip-flopping, irregular heartbeat, sensations of racing in the chest)

diseases.name: Agnosia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Agnosia is a fascinating yet complex neurological condition that affects an individual's ability to recognize and interpret sensory information. This impairment can manifest in various forms, impacting how a person perceives objects, sounds, or even faces. Understanding agnosia is crucial not only for those directly affected but also for caregivers, healthcare professionals, and the general public. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of agnosia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Agnosia presents a range of symptoms depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Visual Agnosia: Inability to recognize familiar objects, faces, or places despite normal vision.
Auditory Agnosia: Difficulty recognizing sounds, such as music or spoken words, even though hearing is intact.
Tactile Agnosia: Inability to identify objects by touch, despite normal sensory function.
Prosopagnosia: A specific type of visual agnosia where individuals cannot recognize familiar faces.

diseases.name: Agoraphobia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Agoraphobia is a complex anxiety disorder that significantly impacts the lives of those who suffer from it. It is characterized by an intense fear of situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable in the event of a panic attack or other incapacitating symptoms. This fear can lead individuals to avoid public places, crowded areas, or even leaving their homes altogether. Understanding agoraphobia is crucial not only for those affected but also for their families, friends, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of agoraphobia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Agoraphobia manifests through various symptoms, which can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Intense Fear or Anxiety: A persistent fear of being in situations where escape may be difficult.
Panic Attacks: Sudden episodes of intense fear that may include heart palpitations, sweating, trembling, and feelings of impending doom.
Avoidance Behavior: Actively avoiding places or situations that may trigger anxiety, leading to significant lifestyle changes.
Physical Symptoms: Nausea, dizziness, shortness of breath, and a sense of detachment from reality.

diseases.name: Agranulocytosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Agranulocytosis is a medical condition characterized by an extremely low level of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell essential for fighting off infections. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe infections, making it a critical health concern that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment. Understanding agranulocytosis is vital for both patients and healthcare providers, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of agranulocytosis can vary but often include:
Fever: A common sign of infection, which may be the first indication of agranulocytosis.
Chills: Accompanying fever, chills can indicate the body’s response to infection.
Sore Throat: Infections can lead to inflammation and pain in the throat.
Mouth Ulcers: Painful sores may develop in the mouth due to a weakened immune system.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness can occur as the body struggles to fight infections.
Rapid Heart Rate: The body may respond to infection with an increased heart rate.

diseases.name: Aicardi Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aicardi Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects females and is characterized by a unique combination of neurological and developmental issues. First described in 1965 by Dr. Jean Aicardi, this syndrome is significant not only for its clinical manifestations but also for its implications on the lives of affected individuals and their families. Understanding Aicardi Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those impacted.
symptoms: Aicardi Syndrome presents a range of symptoms that can vary significantly among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Seizures: These can be frequent and may vary in type, including tonic-clonic and absence seizures.
Developmental Delays: Affected individuals often experience delays in reaching developmental milestones, such as walking and talking.
Intellectual Disability: Many individuals with Aicardi Syndrome have varying degrees of cognitive impairment.
Vision Problems: Chorioretinal lacunae can lead to visual impairments, including blindness in severe cases.
Motor Dysfunction: Muscle tone abnormalities, such as spasticity or hypotonia, can affect movement and coordination.

diseases.name: AIDS/HIV
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms vary depending on the stages of infection such as primary infection (acute HIV), clinical latent infection (chronic HIV) and early symptomatic HIV infection.

A person infected by HIV may suffer from flu, fever, headache, joint pain, sore throat and swollen glands within two months after contracting the virus. Often referred to as ‘primary or acute HIV infection’, it may go unnoticed. But the virus spreads fast and efficiently during this stage.

In some cases, person suffers from consistent swelling of lymph glands in the chronic HIV stage. This condition lasts for almost 10 years if the person is not taking up antiretroviral therapy. The phase can continue for decades if the person takes antiretroviral medicine. In few cases, the person may progress to severe stage.

As the virus further develops and continues damaging the immune system, a person may suffer from fever, fatigue, weight loss, oral yeast infection , diarrhea and shingles. Other symptoms of AIDS include :
Rashes on skin or bumps
Night sweats
Persistent fever
White spots or unusual wounds on tongue or mouth

diseases.name: Akathisia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Akathisia is a complex and often misunderstood condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Characterized by an overwhelming sense of restlessness and an uncontrollable urge to be in constant motion, akathisia can be distressing for those who experience it. This article aims to provide a thorough understanding of akathisia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. By shedding light on this condition, we hope to empower individuals and their families to recognize and seek appropriate care.
symptoms: The symptoms of akathisia can vary in intensity and may include:
Restlessness: A constant urge to move, often described as an inability to sit still.
Anxiety: Feelings of unease or agitation that accompany the restlessness.
Irritability: Increased frustration or mood swings.
Difficulty Concentrating: Challenges in focusing on tasks due to the overwhelming need to move.
Sleep Disturbances: Trouble falling or staying asleep, often due to restlessness.

diseases.name: Albinism: Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: One can say a person has Albinism if their skin, hair, or eyes are unusually lighter than their family members or ethnic groups.
symptoms: People with Albinism may have the following symptoms:
Ashen skin, hair, or eyes
Unusually lighter skin, hair, or eyes
Patches of skin have a lighter pigmentation than other body parts.
Albinism with vision problems shows symptoms such as
Crossed eyes
Photophobia, or sensitivity to light
Involuntary rapid eye movements
Impaired vision or blindness

diseases.name: Alcohol Poisoning - Symptoms, Causes, Risk Factors and Treatment Options
diseases.description: Alcohol Poisoning is a potentially fatal condition that arises as a consequence of drinking an excessive amount of alcohol within a short period of time. When the level of alcohol in blood increases over the recommended maximum level, an individual is at risk of alcohol poisoning. The person then starts showing the symptoms of disorientation, labored breathing, decreased temperature, or can even slip into a coma.
symptoms: Blood Alcohol Concentration or BAC is the measure of alcohol levels in the blood of an individual. A sober person would have a BAC of 0.0, while a BAC of 0.08 is considered to be intoxicated. BAC of 0.40 can be fatal.
Symptoms of mild alcohol poisoning include:
Disorientation.
Confusion.
A sudden drop in body temperature.
Abnormal or slow breathing.
Vomiting.
Stupor.
Symptoms of severe alcohol poisoning include:
Heart attack .
Severe lung infections.
Dehydration that may potentially lead to brain damage
Seizures due to a sudden drop in glucose levels.
Might stop breathing.
Pale skin with a blue tinge.
BAC of 0.40 or higher can potentially lead to the onset of coma.
If any of the above-mentioned symptoms are detected in a person, it is advisable to seek medical help immediately.

diseases.name: Alcoholic Liver Disease
diseases.description: The liver is the largest organ in our body which plays a central role in metabolic processes. Alcohol can damage the liver and its functioning. Over the years, the number of alcohol-related diseases and death is increasing. Young people between the age group of 25 – 34 are more affected at a prime period of life.

diseases.name: Alcoholism

symptoms: The symptoms of alcoholism are based on the person’s behavior which can be mild, moderate or severe. These symptoms include:
Not being able to keep a tab on the amount of alcohol a person drinks

Spending too much of time drinking alcohol
Showing no interest in social, occupational and recreational activities
Always finding a reason to drink

The symptoms of alcoholism also include alcohol intoxication and alcohol withdrawal.
Alcohol intoxication leads to several behavioral problems such as mood swings, lack of coordination, slurred speech and impaired memory.

diseases.name: Alexander Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Alexander Disease is a rare and progressive neurological disorder that primarily affects the brain's white matter. It is classified as a type of leukodystrophy, which refers to a group of disorders characterized by the abnormal development or destruction of the myelin sheath that insulates nerve fibers. This condition is significant not only due to its impact on the affected individuals and their families but also because it highlights the complexities of genetic disorders and the importance of early diagnosis and intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of Alexander Disease can vary widely depending on the age of onset. Common symptoms include:
Developmental Delays: Children may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones.
Seizures: Frequent seizures can occur, particularly in infants.
Muscle Weakness: Weakness in the limbs and trunk can lead to difficulties with movement and coordination.
Cognitive Impairment: Affected individuals may experience learning difficulties and cognitive decline.
Speech and Language Delays: Delays in speech development are common.
Behavioral Changes: Changes in behavior, including irritability and mood swings, may be observed.

diseases.name: Allergic Shiners - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Allergic shiners are a common yet often overlooked symptom of allergies, particularly in children and young adults. Characterized by dark circles under the eyes, these shiners are not merely cosmetic concerns; they can indicate underlying allergic reactions that may require medical attention. Understanding allergic shiners is crucial for effective management and improving the quality of life for those affected. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of allergic shiners.
symptoms: The primary symptom of allergic shiners is the presence of dark circles under the eyes. Other associated symptoms may include:
Itchy Eyes: Often accompanied by redness and swelling.
Sneezing: Frequent sneezing can occur due to nasal irritation.
Runny or Stuffy Nose: Nasal congestion is common in individuals with allergies.
Postnasal Drip: Mucus dripping down the throat can lead to coughing and throat irritation.

diseases.name: Allergies - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Allergies are a common health issue affecting millions of people worldwide. They occur when the immune system reacts to a foreign substance, known as an allergen, as if it were a harmful invader. This inappropriate immune response can lead to a range of symptoms, from mild discomfort to severe, life-threatening reactions. Understanding allergies is crucial not only for those who suffer from them but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of allergies, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Allergic reactions can manifest in various ways, depending on the type of allergen and the individual's sensitivity. Common symptoms include:
Respiratory Symptoms: Sneezing, runny or stuffy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and coughing.
Skin Reactions: Hives, eczema, or rashes.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain, particularly in food allergies.
Anaphylaxis: A severe, life-threatening reaction that can cause difficulty breathing, swelling of the throat, rapid pulse, and loss of consciousness.

diseases.name: Alopecia Areata
diseases.description: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease that causes hair loss on the scalp, face, and sometimes other areas of the body. The immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, disrupting the normal hair formation cycle. The condition can affect anyone regardless of age or gender, but often begins in childhood.
symptoms: Patchy hair loss on scalp
Hair loss on face (beard, eyebrows, eyelashes)
Nail changes (pitting, ridging)
Hair loss may affect entire scalp (alopecia totalis) or entire body (alopecia universalis)
Tingling or itching before hair loss

diseases.name: Alpha Gal Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Alpha Gal Syndrome (AGS) is a relatively new and increasingly recognized condition that has garnered attention in the medical community and among the general public. This syndrome is characterized by an allergic reaction to a carbohydrate called galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose, commonly referred to as alpha-gal. The significance of Alpha Gal Syndrome lies in its unique association with tick bites, particularly from the Lone Star tick, and its potential to cause severe allergic reactions to red meat and other mammalian products. As awareness of AGS grows, understanding its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies becomes crucial for those affected and healthcare providers alike.
symptoms: The symptoms of Alpha Gal Syndrome can vary widely among individuals and may include:
Hives or Rash: Itchy, raised welts on the skin.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain.
Respiratory Issues: Difficulty breathing, wheezing, or nasal congestion.
Anaphylaxis: A severe, life-threatening allergic reaction that can cause swelling of the throat, difficulty breathing, rapid heartbeat, and a drop in blood pressure.

symptoms: Depending on the degree of altitude sickness one may experience, the symptoms may be the following:
