diseases.name: Alzheimer’s Disease: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Alzheimer’s is a slowly progressing neurological condition. It results in the death of brain cells and the shrinking of the brain. Patients with Alzheimer’s go through multiple stages that affect memory, thinking, cognitive behavior, and simple life skills. The progressive loss of memory (dementia) is the most notable of all Alzheimer’s symptoms. Alzheimer’s disease causes slow and consistent loss of memory. Interestingly, patients with Alzheimer’s disease can remember incidences of the distant past but experience difficulty remembering recent events in the initial stages. Alzheimer’s disease causes extensive degeneration of brain cells with time and results in severe impairment of memory. The individual will lose the ability to carry out routine activities. It may result in death because of severe dehydration , malnutrition, infections, and bedsores. Alzheimer’s has neither any cure nor any remedy to slow down or arrest the disease progression. Alzheimer’s is a multi-factorial disease affecting the function of the brain. AD results due to People who have Alzheimer’s disease are older. However, the condition is not a normal part of aging. Scientists do not know why some people get this disease and why some do not. However, the causes come from two kinds of nerve damage:
symptoms: Most people experience occasional memory lapses, but that does not indicate they have Alzheimer’s. People with Alzheimer’s may:
Forget appointments, conversations, or events.
Repeat the same questions and statements multiple times.
Get lost in familiar locations.
Misplace possessions routinely.
Have trouble expressing thoughts or participating in conversations.
Have issues in planning and executing familiar tasks.

Routine activities or those requiring proper planning, such as playing a mind game or cooking a meal, become difficult as the disease progresses. Gradually, people at an advanced stage of the illness forget to perform basic tasks such as bathing and dressing.
With the progress of the disease, the mood and behavior of the person gets affected to a great extent. This may include –
Social withdrawal
Depression
Wandering
Mood swings
Loss of inhibitions
Delusions
Aggressiveness and irritability
Preserved Skills

Even as the disease worsens, many important skills such as drawing, dancing, craftwork, singing, listening to music, etc., are forgotten. These skills are affected at an advanced stage of the disease.

diseases.name: Amenorrhea: Lack of periods and how to tackle it
diseases.description: Amenorrhea mainly refers to either missed menstrual period on one or more occasions or the entire absence of menstruation. Women missing a minimum of three menstrual periods consecutively, or young girls who have not started to menstruate by the age of 15 years are diagnosed as having amenorrhea.
symptoms: The absence of menstruation is amenorrhea. The other symptoms will depend upon the underlying reason for a missed period; however, here are the symptoms and signs that you might experience besides the absence of periods:
● Loss of hair
● Milky discharge from nipples
● Change in vision
● Headache
● Pain in the pelvic region
● Acne outbreak
● Excessive facial hair

diseases.name: Amnesia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Amnesia is a condition that affects memory, leading to difficulties in recalling past events or forming new memories. It can significantly impact an individual's daily life, relationships, and overall well-being. Understanding amnesia is crucial not only for those who may experience it but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of amnesia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of amnesia can vary widely depending on the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Inability to recall past events: This can range from forgetting recent conversations to losing memories from childhood.
Difficulty forming new memories: Individuals may struggle to remember new information or experiences.
Confusion: Some may experience disorientation regarding time and place.
Emotional changes: Anxiety, depression, or frustration can accompany memory loss.

diseases.name: Amoebic Dysentery - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Amoebic dysentery, also known as amoebiasis, is a severe intestinal infection caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica . This condition is significant not only due to its impact on individual health but also because it poses a public health challenge, particularly in developing countries. Understanding amoebic dysentery is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective treatment, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated.
symptoms: The symptoms of amoebic dysentery can vary from mild to severe and may include:
Diarrhea: Often watery and may contain blood or mucus.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping and discomfort in the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Feelings of sickness and the urge to vomit.
Fever: A mild to moderate fever may accompany the infection.
Fatigue: General weakness and tiredness due to dehydration and nutrient loss.

diseases.name: Amyloidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Amyloidosis is a rare but serious condition characterized by the abnormal accumulation of amyloid proteins in various tissues and organs. This buildup can disrupt normal function and lead to severe health complications. Understanding amyloidosis is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and the general public. Early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes, making awareness of this disease essential.
symptoms: The symptoms of amyloidosis can vary widely depending on the organs affected. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Swelling: Particularly in the legs and ankles due to fluid retention.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Numbness or Tingling: Often in the hands and feet, indicating nerve involvement.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Sudden weight loss without a clear reason.
Diarrhea or Constipation: Gastrointestinal symptoms can occur due to amyloid deposits in the digestive tract.

diseases.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS): Types, Causes, Symptoms, Treatment
diseases.description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is one of the motor neuron diseases. It is a progressive, neurodegenerative disease that affects the brain and the spinal cord, resulting in the loss of muscle control. It causes difficulty in walking, swallowing, and moving. Gradually, it ends up making breathing difficult. There is no cure for the disease, and the cause is unknown. But there are a few cases that are inherited.
symptoms: The symptoms of ALS vary from person to person, and the neurons are affected. The typically begins with muscle weakness that spreads to other body parts and worsens over time. During the initial stages, the symptoms may sometimes look like symptoms of other medical conditions. The following are the symptoms of ALS:
Trouble in walking and performing daily activities
Stumbling and falling
Weakness in the leg, feet, and ankles
Weakness in the hand that leads to clumsiness
Impaired speech or difficulty in swallowing.
An inappropriate emotional outburst, such as crying, laughing or yawning
Cognitive and behavioural changes
Uncontrolled rhythmic muscle contraction, known as clonus
Muscle spasticity
Overactive reflexes
As ALS progresses, the symptoms worsen. The following are the symptoms:
Frequent muscle cramps and twitching in the arms, shoulder, and tongue
Muscle cramps and twitching, particularly in the hands and feet
Struggle to use arms and legs
Thick speech and challenge to project the voice
Weakness and fatigue
Weight loss
Muscle atrophy
Constant twitching
The symptoms of severe ALS are as follows:
Shortness of breath
Troubled breathing, chewing, and eating
Unable to independently stand or walk
ALS patients burn calories at a faster rate. Therefore there is tremendous weight loss
Depression and anxiety
As the disease further progresses, the following are the symptoms:
Troubled breathing and swallowing
Paralysis

diseases.name: Anal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Anal cancer is a relatively uncommon cancer that develops in the tissues of the anus (the opening where stool leaves the body). While it is not as common as colon or rectal cancer, the number of new cases has slowly been rising. With early detection and treatment, many patients do very well. According to global cancer statistics, thousands of new cases are diagnosed each year, with women being slightly more affected than men.
symptoms: In its early stages, anal cancer may not cause noticeable symptoms. However, some early signs include:
Bleeding from the anus or rectum (often mistaken for hemorrhoids).
Pain, itching, or burning in the anal area.
A lump or growth near the anus.
Changes in bowel habits, such as narrowing of stool.
Advanced symptoms may include: Swelling of lymph nodes in the groin. Persistent anal pain or pressure. Incontinence (difficulty controlling bowel movements).
Swelling of lymph nodes in the groin.
Persistent anal pain or pressure.
Incontinence (difficulty controlling bowel movements).
Many people mistake rectal bleeding for piles (hemorrhoids), but persistent bleeding should always be checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Anal Fissures - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: A small tear in the inner mucosal wall of the lower anal canal is called anal fissure or fissure-in-anus. It is an oval-shaped tear usually present at the anal opening. Anal fissures cause pain as well as bleeding with bowel movements. Sometimes, the tear or ulcer can be large enough to expose the underneath muscle or tissue.
symptoms: There are some signs and symptoms that you may notice that signifies you might have developed a fissure:
A small tear or a visible ulcer around the anal region
Throbbing pain around the anal region which worsen during bowel movements
Streaks of blood while passing stools, which are bright red. In Hemorrhoid’s , the characteristic feature of bleeding is a splash in the pan
Development of a skin tag or a lump of tissue around the tear
Itchy or burning sensation around the anal region

diseases.name: Anal Fistula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anal fistula is a medical condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. It is characterized by an abnormal connection between the anal canal and the skin surrounding the anus. This condition can lead to discomfort, pain, and recurrent infections, making it essential for individuals to understand its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. In this article, we will explore anal fistula in detail, providing a comprehensive overview that is easy to understand for a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of anal fistula can vary from person to person but often include:
Pain and Discomfort: Many individuals experience pain around the anus, especially during bowel movements.
Swelling and Redness: The area around the fistula may appear swollen and red.
Drainage: Persistent drainage of pus or blood from the opening of the fistula is common.
Itching: The area may become itchy due to irritation from drainage.
Foul Odor: The drainage can have an unpleasant smell.

diseases.name: Anal Stenosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anal stenosis is a medical condition characterized by the narrowing of the anal canal, which can lead to various complications and discomfort. This condition is significant because it can affect bowel movements, cause pain, and lead to other gastrointestinal issues. Understanding anal stenosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring a better quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of anal stenosis can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Difficulty Passing Stool: Individuals may experience straining or pain during bowel movements.
Narrowed Stool: The stool may appear thin or ribbon-like due to the narrowed passage.
Pain or Discomfort: Pain during bowel movements or a constant feeling of discomfort in the anal area.
Bleeding: Some individuals may notice blood in their stool or on toilet paper.
Itching or Irritation: The anal area may become itchy or irritated due to inflammation.

diseases.name: Anal Warts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anal warts, also known as anal condylomas, are benign growths that occur in the anal region due to infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). While they are not life-threatening, their presence can lead to discomfort, embarrassment, and complications if left untreated. Understanding anal warts is crucial for early detection, effective treatment, and prevention of further complications. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of anal warts, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Anal warts may not always cause noticeable symptoms, but when they do, they can include:
Small, flesh-colored or gray growths around the anus
Itching or irritation in the anal area
Bleeding during bowel movements
Discomfort or pain in the anal region

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment, Diagnose and Prevention
diseases.description: Certain people have a genetic predisposition to allergy to some materials, since birth. Anaphylaxis is a condition which involves severe, life-threatening allergic reactions. This blog is a comprehensive guide to anaphylaxis, its symptoms, causes, diagnosis and treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of anaphylaxis start appearing within a few minutes or hours of exposure to the triggers. In certain cases, it can take up to 30 minutes for the body to react to triggers. Some of the most common symptoms of anaphylaxis include:
Skin reaction, rashes , and flushed skin
Low blood pressure
Narrowed airways, swollen tongue or throat
Wheezing
Nausea
Diarrhea
Dizziness or fainting
Weak or rapid pulse
Hives
Vomiting

diseases.name: Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL) is a rare and aggressive form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a type of cancer that originates in the lymphatic system. This disease is characterized by the proliferation of large, abnormal lymphocytes, which can lead to various symptoms and complications. Understanding ALCL is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma can vary widely depending on the extent of the disease and the organs affected. Common symptoms include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Painless swelling in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Fever: Unexplained fevers that may come and go.
Night Sweats: Excessive sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss without changes in diet or exercise.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness or lack of energy.
Skin Lesions: In cases of cutaneous ALCL, patients may develop red or purple nodules or plaques on the skin.

diseases.name: Anasarca - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anasarca is a medical condition characterized by widespread swelling of the body due to the accumulation of fluid in the tissues. This condition is significant because it can be a symptom of underlying health issues, ranging from mild to severe. Understanding anasarca is crucial for early detection and management, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding anasarca.
symptoms: The primary symptom of anasarca is generalized swelling, which may be accompanied by:
Weight Gain: Rapid weight gain due to fluid retention.
Stiffness: A feeling of tightness or stiffness in the swollen areas.
Skin Changes: The skin may appear stretched, shiny, or discolored.
Difficulty Breathing: In severe cases, fluid accumulation in the lungs can lead to shortness of breath.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue or weakness may occur due to the body’s increased effort to manage fluid balance.

diseases.name: Anastomotic Leak - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anastomotic leak is a serious medical condition that can occur after surgical procedures involving the connection of two hollow organs, such as the intestines or blood vessels. This complication can lead to significant morbidity and mortality if not identified and managed promptly. Understanding anastomotic leaks is crucial for patients undergoing surgeries that involve anastomosis, as well as for healthcare providers who must monitor for this potential complication.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of an anastomotic leak is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: This may be localized or diffuse and can range from mild to severe.
Fever: A sudden onset of fever may indicate an infection related to the leak.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur due to the body's response to the leak and potential infection.
Changes in Bowel Habits: Diarrhea or constipation may occur, depending on the location of the leak.
Signs of Sepsis: Rapid heart rate, low blood pressure, and confusion can indicate a severe systemic response to infection.

diseases.name: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS) is a rare genetic condition that affects sexual development in individuals with XY chromosomes, typically associated with male biological characteristics. Despite having male chromosomes, individuals with AIS may develop female physical traits due to the body's inability to respond to androgens, the hormones responsible for male characteristics. Understanding AIS is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, families, and society at large, as it highlights the complexities of gender identity and biological development.
symptoms: The symptoms of Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome can vary significantly based on the type and severity of the condition.

Complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (CAIS): Female external genitalia Absence of menstruation (primary amenorrhea) Normal breast development Shortened or absent vagina Testes may be present in the abdomen or inguinal canal
Female external genitalia
Absence of menstruation (primary amenorrhea)
Normal breast development
Shortened or absent vagina
Testes may be present in the abdomen or inguinal canal
Partial Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (PAIS): Ambiguous genitalia Hypospadias (urethra opening on the underside of the penis) Variable degrees of breast development Possible infertility
Ambiguous genitalia
Hypospadias (urethra opening on the underside of the penis)
Variable degrees of breast development
Possible infertility

diseases.name: Anemia
diseases.description: Anemia (anaemia) is a condition in which the number of red blood cells or the hemoglobin they contain is lower than normal, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen to tissues.
symptoms: Tiredness or low energy
Dizziness or light-headedness
Shortness of breath on exertion
Headache
Cold hands and feet
Pale skin or pale inner eyelids

diseases.name: Anemia – Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis & Treatment
diseases.description: Anemia is a condition in which the oxygen supply to tissues in the body is reduced due to an inadequate amount of healthy red blood cells in the blood. The condition reduces the capacity of blood to transport enough oxygen and causes multiple symptoms of Anemia that make the individual feel weak and exhausted. Hemoglobin is a protein, a highly essential constituent of red blood cells. It is a vehicle for carrying and delivering oxygen to the cells throughout the body. There are different types of Anemia . Iron deficiency Anemia is the most common type that mainly affects women. The condition can lead to complications during pregnancy because of the higher requirement of blood. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), it is said that approximately two billion people around the world have Anemia, making this the most common nutritional disorder worldwide.
symptoms: There are different signs and symptoms based on the types of Anemia . The symptom of mild Anemia is almost untraceable, but the symptoms become prominent as Anemia worsens. Some common symptoms are pale lips and nails, weakness, dizziness, fatigue, cramps in legs, breathing difficulty, and headaches .
Anemia because of a deficiency of iron – Nail curving like a spoon, cravings for strange things like mud or paper, and cracks and sores in the mouth.
Anemia because of lack of Vitamin B12 – Numbness or a tingling sensation in extremities, muscle stiffness in arms and legs, momentary loss of memory .
Sickle cell Anemia – Pain in joints, stomach, and legs, delay in growth milestones in kids, frequent infections.
Chronic destruction of blood cells – Dark color of urine, symptoms of jaundice or gallstones.

If you are getting tired quickly or have fatigue without any exertion, these might be symptoms of Anemia. Also, if your blood test displays low hemoglobin , it is advisable to see a doctor. Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment
Family history of blood disorders – Discussing hereditary factors with your gynecologist is necessary before planning a child.

Planning a pregnancy – Visiting a doctor is necessary if you are considering pregnancy. Anemic conditions can be harmful to the expectant mother and the fetus. Anemia can also affect the growth of the fetus and may cause complications during childbirth.
Changes in heart rate – Any change in your heartbeat may be a sign of Anemia. Visit the doctor immediately if you experience shortness of breath because of minor physical work.
Significant blood loss during periods – Heavy periods can cause a sudden fall in your hemoglobin levels. Your doctor can recommend treatment to control the blood loss.

Medical conditions that cause blood loss – Anemia is common in individuals with hemorrhoids , cancer of the colon or rectum, and ulcers. Visit a doctor for an assessment of your blood for timely treatment.

Nutritional deficiencies – There is a possibility of Anemia if your diet lacks essential nutrients such as minerals and vitamins. Visit a doctor or a nutritionist for advice and correction of nutritional status.
A regular blood test to check hemoglobin is necessary for every woman from the time she attains puberty. Anemia is a silent disorder, and you may miss the symptoms.

diseases.name: Anencephaly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anencephaly is a severe congenital condition that affects the development of the brain and skull in a fetus. It is classified as a type of neural tube defect (NTD), which occurs when the neural tube, the structure that eventually forms the brain and spinal cord, fails to close completely during early pregnancy. This condition is significant not only because of its profound impact on the affected individuals and their families but also due to its implications for prenatal care and public health. Understanding anencephaly is crucial for expectant parents, healthcare providers, and society as a whole, as it raises important questions about prevention, management, and support for those affected.
symptoms: Infants born with anencephaly typically exhibit several characteristic symptoms, including:
Absence of a Major Portion of the Brain: The most defining feature is the lack of a significant part of the brain, particularly the cerebrum and cerebellum.
Exposed Brain Tissue: The brain may be partially exposed due to the absence of the skull.
Facial Abnormalities: Some infants may have facial deformities, including a flattened forehead and wide-set eyes.
Lack of Response: Infants with anencephaly often do not respond to stimuli and may exhibit limited movement.

diseases.name: Aneuploidy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aneuploidy is a genetic condition characterized by an abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell. This condition can have significant implications for an individual's health, development, and overall well-being. Understanding aneuploidy is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, as it can influence treatment decisions and management strategies. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding aneuploidy.
symptoms: The symptoms of aneuploidy can vary widely depending on the specific type of chromosomal abnormality. Some common symptoms associated with specific aneuploidies include:
Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21): Characteristic facial features, developmental delays, and increased risk of heart defects.
Turner Syndrome (Monosomy X): Short stature, delayed puberty, and infertility.
Klinefelter Syndrome (XXY): Taller than average height, reduced testosterone levels, and potential learning difficulties.

diseases.name: Anger Management - Importance and Benefits
diseases.description: Anger management deals with recognizing the signs of anger and trying to calm down and deal with it in a healthy, wholesome manner.

diseases.name: Angina: Symptoms, Causes, Types & Treatment for Chest Pain
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Pain and discomfort which usually starts behind the breastbone, arms, shoulders, neck, jaw, throat or the back
Heart burn and Indigestion-like pain in the abdomen
Pressure, squeezing, burning, or tightness in the chest
Nausea (feeling sick to your stomach)
Fatigue and weakness
Shortness of breath and sweating
Light-headedness, dizziness and confusion
Stable angina is usually brought on by exertion and stops with rest. It is usually predictable, short and goes away with angina medication.

Unstable angina on the other hand is a medical emergency which can occur at rest also, is unusual in pattern, comes on suddenly, more severe, may not disappear with angina medicines and may evolve into a heart attack.

diseases.name: Angioedema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angioedema is a medical condition characterized by the rapid swelling of the deeper layers of the skin, often around the eyes and lips, and sometimes the throat. This condition can be alarming and potentially life-threatening, especially when it affects the airways. Understanding angioedema is crucial for timely diagnosis and treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of angioedema, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of angioedema can vary widely depending on the severity and location of the swelling. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: Rapid swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, or extremities.
Pain or Discomfort: The affected area may be painful or tender to the touch.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Some individuals may experience itching or a burning sensation in the swollen areas.
Difficulty Breathing: If the throat or airways are affected, individuals may experience shortness of breath or wheezing.

diseases.name: Angioid Streaks - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angioid streaks are a rare but significant ocular condition that can lead to serious vision problems. These streaks are irregular lines that appear in the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. Understanding angioid streaks is crucial for early detection and management, as they can be associated with various underlying health issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of angioid streaks, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Angioid streaks themselves may not present noticeable symptoms. However, they can lead to complications that affect vision. Common symptoms associated with these complications include:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty seeing clearly, especially at a distance.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent.
Blind Spots: Areas of vision may be missing or obscured.
Difficulty with Color Perception: Colors may appear less vibrant or altered.

diseases.name: Angiokeratoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angiokeratoma is a benign skin condition characterized by the presence of small, dark red to blue lesions that can appear on various parts of the body. While these growths are generally harmless, they can sometimes cause concern due to their appearance and potential for misdiagnosis. Understanding angiokeratoma is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ensuring that individuals can seek appropriate medical advice when necessary.
symptoms: Angiokeratomas typically present as:
Small, raised lesions that are dark red, blue, or purple in color.
Lesions that may be flat or slightly elevated.
A rough or scaly surface, particularly in older lesions.

diseases.name: Angiolipoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angiolipoma is a benign tumor that primarily consists of fat cells and blood vessels. While it is not cancerous, its presence can lead to discomfort and may require medical attention. Understanding angiolipoma is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding angiolipoma.
symptoms: Angiolipomas can present with various symptoms, including:
Soft, movable lumps: These tumors are usually soft to the touch and can be moved slightly under the skin.
Tenderness: Angiolipomas are often painful, especially when pressure is applied.
Swelling: In some cases, the area around the angiolipoma may appear swollen or inflamed.

diseases.name: Angiomyolipoma Of The Kidney - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angiomyolipoma of the kidney is a benign tumor that consists of blood vessels, smooth muscle, and fat. While it is generally non-cancerous, its presence can lead to significant health issues, particularly if it grows large enough to cause complications. Understanding angiomyolipoma is crucial for early detection and management, as it can affect kidney function and overall health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of angiomyolipoma of the kidney, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Angiomyolipomas may not cause any symptoms, especially when they are small. However, as they grow, they can lead to various symptoms, including:
Flank Pain: Discomfort or pain in the side or back, often due to pressure on surrounding tissues.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which can be a sign of bleeding from the tumor.
Palpable Mass: In some cases, a large angiomyolipoma may be felt as a lump in the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur if the tumor causes kidney dysfunction or bleeding.

diseases.name: Angiosarcoma : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Cancers are of numerous types. But each of them has its specific symptoms which you can look out for. It is vital to remain aware of the signs that the body may give and the treatment options available in healthcare so that you know what to do at the incidence of the condition. This blog is a comprehensive guide on angiosarcoma, its symptoms, causes, and treatment options available.
symptoms: The symptoms of the condition depend upon the location of the cancer. The most typical symptoms are mainly shown on your skin. They are:
A purple patch that resembles a bruise
Persistent sore that gets worse over time
A region that bleeds when touched or jolted
A soft mass that is visible or can be felt

The symptoms are less visible if the angiosarcoma is in the deep tissue, such as your liver or heart. But the pain could be experienced when it grows beyond a particular level. A physician may be able to feel the growth as it grows.

diseases.name: Angle Closure Glaucoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angle Closure Glaucoma (ACG) is a serious eye condition that can lead to irreversible vision loss if not diagnosed and treated promptly. It occurs when the drainage angle of the eye becomes blocked, causing a rapid increase in intraocular pressure (IOP). This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause blindness but also due to its sudden onset, which can be alarming for those affected. Understanding ACG is crucial for early detection and effective management, ensuring better outcomes for patients.
symptoms: The symptoms of Angle Closure Glaucoma can vary, but common signs include:
Severe Eye Pain: Often described as a throbbing or aching sensation.
Headache: Accompanied by eye pain, it can be intense and persistent.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to the severe pain.
Blurred Vision: Sudden changes in vision clarity.
Halos Around Lights: A common visual disturbance during an acute attack.
Redness of the Eye: Due to increased pressure and inflammation.

diseases.name: Angular Cheilitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Angular cheilitis, also known as angular stomatitis or cheilosis, is a common condition characterized by inflammation and cracking at the corners of the mouth. While it may seem like a minor issue, angular cheilitis can significantly impact a person's quality of life, causing discomfort, pain, and difficulty in eating or speaking. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective management and prevention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of angular cheilitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of angular cheilitis can vary in severity but typically include:
Redness and Swelling: Inflammation at the corners of the mouth.
Cracks or Fissures: Painful splits that may bleed or ooze.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Discomfort that can worsen with movement.
Dryness: Flaky or peeling skin around the affected area.

diseases.name: Anisocoria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anisocoria is a condition characterized by unequal pupil sizes in the eyes. While it may seem like a minor issue, anisocoria can be a significant indicator of underlying health problems. Understanding this condition is crucial for recognizing potential medical emergencies and ensuring timely intervention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding anisocoria.
symptoms: The primary symptom of anisocoria is the noticeable difference in pupil size. However, depending on the underlying cause, other symptoms may accompany this condition, including:
Blurred vision
Eye pain
Headaches
Sensitivity to light
Changes in vision

diseases.name: Ankle Injuries - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ankle injuries are among the most common musculoskeletal injuries, affecting individuals of all ages and activity levels. They can range from mild sprains to severe fractures, significantly impacting mobility and quality of life. Understanding ankle injuries is crucial not only for effective treatment but also for prevention, allowing individuals to maintain an active lifestyle without the fear of injury. This comprehensive guide will delve into the various aspects of ankle injuries, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of ankle injuries can vary depending on the type and severity of the injury. Common symptoms include:
Pain: This can range from mild discomfort to severe pain, especially when bearing weight on the affected ankle.
Swelling: Swelling around the ankle is a common response to injury.
Bruising: Discoloration may appear around the injury site due to bleeding under the skin.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the ankle or foot may occur, particularly in severe injuries.
Instability: A feeling of the ankle giving way or being unstable can indicate ligament damage.

diseases.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
diseases.description: Ankylosing spondylitis is a type of arthritis that primarily affects the spine. It causes inflammation of the spinal joints (vertebrae) that can lead to severe, chronic pain and discomfort. In more advanced cases, this inflammation can cause new bone to form on the spine, causing the spine to fuse in a fixed, immobile position, sometimes creating a hunched-forward posture.
symptoms: Pain and stiffness in the lower back and hips, especially in the morning and after periods of inactivity
Neck pain
Fatigue
Pain and swelling in other joints such as the shoulders, hips, knees, and feet
Vision problems and eye pain (uveitis)
Skin rashes

diseases.name: Anodontia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anodontia is a rare dental condition characterized by the complete absence of teeth. While it may seem like a minor issue, the implications of anodontia extend far beyond aesthetics. This condition can significantly impact an individual's ability to eat, speak, and maintain proper oral hygiene, leading to various health complications. Understanding anodontia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that those affected can lead healthy, fulfilling lives.
symptoms: The primary symptom of anodontia is the absence of teeth. However, individuals may also experience:
Difficulty chewing and swallowing food
Speech difficulties, such as slurred or unclear speech
Changes in facial appearance, leading to a sunken or aged look
Increased risk of gum disease and other oral health issues

diseases.name: Anorectal Malformation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anorectal malformation (ARM) is a congenital condition that affects the development of the anus and rectum. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated early. ARM can vary in severity, affecting not only the anus but also the surrounding structures, and it can have a profound impact on a child's quality of life. Understanding anorectal malformation is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of anorectal malformation can vary widely depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Absence of an anal opening: In severe cases, the anus may not be present at all.
Misplaced anus: The anus may be located in an abnormal position, such as too high on the body.
Difficulty passing stool: Infants may struggle to have bowel movements, leading to constipation or abdominal distension.
Fecal incontinence: Older children may experience difficulty controlling bowel movements.
Signs of infection: Symptoms such as fever, swelling, or redness around the anal area may indicate an infection.

diseases.name: Anorexia : Symptoms, Diet and Treatment
diseases.description: Anorexia nervosa or anorexia is a severe psychological condition and one of the most life-threatening eating disorders. People who have anorexia starve themselves and suffer from an intense fear (phobia) of gaining weight or becoming obese. Their perception of body weight is unrealistic, which makes them focus on keeping a check on their weight relentlessly. To ensure that they look thin and skinny, they tend to compromise with their health and quality of life to a great extent.

diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Since anorexia is looked at more of a mental disorder, symptoms are both physical as well as emotional and behavioural.
Weight loss of extreme nature
Thin appearance

diseases.name: Anosmia - Loss of Smell
diseases.description: The medical term for loss of smell is Anosmia or Hyposmia in case of partial loss of smell. The condition is also called smell blindness and is defined as the loss of the ability to detect smells.
symptoms: Cough
Running nose
Fever
Headache
Sneezing
Pain
Swelling
Difficulty breathing
Numbness on one side of the body
Speech difficulty
Issues with vision

diseases.name: Anovulation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anovulation is a condition that affects many women at different stages of their lives, often without them even realizing it. It refers to the absence of ovulation, which is a crucial part of the menstrual cycle where an ovary releases an egg. Understanding anovulation is significant not only for those trying to conceive but also for overall reproductive health. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of anovulation, providing a comprehensive resource for anyone seeking to understand this condition.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of anovulation is crucial for early diagnosis and treatment. Common symptoms include:
Irregular Menstrual Cycles: This can manifest as missed periods or cycles that are longer or shorter than usual.
Heavy or Light Menstrual Bleeding: Changes in menstrual flow can indicate hormonal imbalances.
Infertility: Difficulty conceiving after trying for a year or more can be a sign of anovulation.
Hormonal Symptoms: These may include acne, excessive hair growth (hirsutism), and weight gain.

diseases.name: Anterior Placenta - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The placenta is a vital organ that develops during pregnancy, providing essential nutrients and oxygen to the growing fetus while also removing waste products. One of the various positions the placenta can adopt is the anterior position, which means it is located on the front wall of the uterus. Understanding the significance of an anterior placenta is crucial for expectant mothers and healthcare providers alike, as it can influence pregnancy management, delivery, and maternal-fetal health.
symptoms: Most women with an anterior placenta do not experience any specific symptoms related to the placental position. However, some may notice:
Decreased fetal movement: Anterior placentas can cushion the fetus, making movements less noticeable.
Abdominal discomfort: Some women may experience mild discomfort as the uterus expands.

diseases.name: Anterograde Amnesia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anterograde amnesia is a condition that affects an individual's ability to form new memories after the onset of the disorder. This type of amnesia can significantly impact daily life, relationships, and overall well-being. Understanding anterograde amnesia is crucial not only for those affected but also for their families and caregivers. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding anterograde amnesia.
symptoms: The primary symptom of anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories. Individuals may struggle to remember recent conversations, events, or information learned after the onset of the condition. Other symptoms may include:
Difficulty recalling new information
Repeatedly asking the same questions
Confusion about time and place
Inability to recognize familiar faces or places

diseases.name: Anteverted Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: An anteverted uterus is a common anatomical variation in which the uterus tilts forward towards the bladder. This positioning is considered normal and is found in a significant portion of the female population. Understanding the anteverted uterus is essential for women’s health, as it can influence various aspects of reproductive health, including menstruation, pregnancy, and gynecological examinations. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the anteverted uterus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: An anteverted uterus typically does not cause any symptoms. However, some women may experience symptoms related to underlying conditions that can affect the uterus. Common symptoms include:
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort in the pelvic region may occur, especially if there are underlying conditions such as endometriosis or fibroids.
Menstrual Irregularities: Some women may experience changes in their menstrual cycle, which may not be directly related to the anteverted position but rather to other gynecological issues.
Pain During Intercourse: Some women may experience discomfort during sexual activity, which could be linked to underlying conditions rather than the uterine position itself.

diseases.name: Anthropophobia : Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: The dread of people is known as Anthropophobia. It isn’t a clinical diagnosis in the traditional sense. Anthropophobia is a fear or worry that people experience when they are in the presence of other people. Anthropophobia, unlike other social anxiety disorders, is a fear of people, not of social circumstances.
symptoms: ‘Anticipatory anxiety is a common symptom of Anthropophobia. Anticipatory anxiety is a feeling of dread, worry, or terror over something that is going to happen. People with Anthropophobia may be very concerned about being among other people.
Physical symptoms are frequently associated with anxiety. People may have the following experiences:
Hyperventilation
Flushed skin
Vomiting or nausea
Heart palpitations or a rapid heartbeat
Sweating
Tremors

diseases.name: Anti-Social Personality Disorder
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of antisocial personality disorder include:
Disregard for social rules
Failing to meet responsibility at work, school or home
Being disrespectful and arrogant
Lying & exploiting others
A careless attitude towards safety of others as well as themselves
Showing no signs of guilt or remorse
Violating laws
Abusive, impulsive, and irritable behavior

diseases.name: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)
diseases.description: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an autoimmune disorder in which the immune system produces abnormal antibodies against phospholipids — a type of fat — in the blood. APS can cause blood clots to form in arteries and veins, as well as pregnancy complications such as miscarriages and preterm births. It may occur alone or with another autoimmune disease such as lupus.
symptoms: Blood clots in legs (DVT)
Blood clots in lungs (pulmonary embolism)
Stroke
Repeated miscarriages
Low platelet count (thrombocytopenia)
Lacy, net-like purplish skin rash (livedo reticularis)
Headaches or migraines

diseases.name: Antisynthetase Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Antisynthetase Syndrome (ASS) is a rare autoimmune condition characterized by the presence of specific autoantibodies that target aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, enzymes crucial for protein synthesis. This syndrome is significant not only for its clinical manifestations but also for its association with various complications, including interstitial lung disease and muscle weakness. Understanding Antisynthetase Syndrome is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for affected individuals.
symptoms: Antisynthetase Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Weakness: This is often one of the first symptoms, affecting the proximal muscles (those closest to the center of the body).
Interstitial Lung Disease: Patients may experience shortness of breath, cough, and reduced exercise tolerance due to lung involvement.
Skin Rashes: Some individuals may develop skin manifestations, such as a heliotrope rash (a purplish rash on the eyelids) or Gottron's papules (red or purple bumps on the knuckles).
Joint Pain: Arthralgia or joint pain is common and can affect mobility.
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue is a prevalent symptom that can significantly impact daily activities.

diseases.name: Antral Gastritis - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Prevention and Treatments
diseases.description: Antral Gastritis: Gastritis refers to inflammation of the inner stomach lining. Gastritis can develop quickly (acute gastritis) or gradually over time (chronic gastritis). It can lead to ulcers and may also increase the risk of developing stomach cancer.
symptoms: The primary symptom of antral gastritis is inflammation or feeling a burning sensation inside your stomach.
Other symptoms associated with antral gastritis are:
Feeling full or bloated during or after a meal
Loss of appetite
Stomach ulcers
Pain or discomfort in the upper abdomen
Nausea

diseases.name: Anuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Anuria is a medical condition characterized by the absence of urine production, defined as the output of less than 100 milliliters of urine in a 24-hour period. This condition is significant because it can indicate severe underlying health issues, including kidney failure, dehydration, or urinary obstruction. Understanding anuria is crucial for early detection and treatment, as it can lead to serious complications if left unaddressed.
symptoms: The primary symptom of anuria is the significant reduction or complete cessation of urine output. Other associated symptoms may include:
Swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet due to fluid retention.
Fatigue or weakness.
Nausea or vomiting.
Confusion or altered mental status.

diseases.name: Anxiety: Understanding It, Managing It, and Getting Help
diseases.description: Anxiety is a natural human response to stress or danger. It is a feeling of fear, worry, or uneasiness that can range from mild to severe. Everyone feels anxious from time to time, before a job interview, during an exam, or while waiting for medical results. However, when anxiety becomes constant, overwhelming, and interferes with daily life, it may be a sign of an anxiety disorder.
symptoms: Anxiety can show up in the body, mind, and behavior. Common symptoms include:
Rapid heartbeat
Sweating
Shortness of breath
Muscle tension
Headaches
Fatigue or insomnia
Upset stomach or nausea
Constant worry or dread
Feeling restless or on edge
Difficulty concentrating
Irritability
Avoiding situations that cause fear
Panic attacks
Not everyone experiences the same symptoms. Some people may only have physical symptoms, while others may struggle with constant negative thoughts.

diseases.name: Aortic Dissection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aortic dissection is a serious medical condition that occurs when the inner layer of the aorta, the large blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body, tears. This tear allows blood to flow between the layers of the aorta, leading to a separation or dissection of the vessel wall. Aortic dissection is significant because it can lead to life-threatening complications, including rupture of the aorta, which can result in massive internal bleeding and death. Understanding aortic dissection is crucial for early recognition and treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of aortic dissection can vary depending on the location and extent of the dissection. Common symptoms include:
Sudden, severe chest pain: Often described as a tearing or ripping sensation, this pain may radiate to the back, neck, or abdomen.
Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing may occur if the dissection affects blood flow to the lungs.
Weakness or paralysis: If blood flow to the brain is compromised, neurological symptoms may arise.
Cold or numb extremities: Reduced blood flow can lead to coldness or numbness in the arms or legs.

diseases.name: Aortic Stenosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aortic stenosis is a serious heart condition that affects the aortic valve, which is responsible for regulating blood flow from the heart to the rest of the body. This condition can lead to significant health complications if left untreated, making it crucial for individuals to understand its implications, symptoms, and treatment options. In this comprehensive article, we will explore aortic stenosis in detail, providing insights into its causes, risk factors, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Aortic stenosis may not present noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or even at rest.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, often described as pressure or tightness.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy, especially during exertion.
Dizziness or Fainting: Lightheadedness or fainting spells, particularly during physical activity.
Heart Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.

diseases.name: Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease (AIOD) is a significant vascular condition that affects blood flow in the lower body. It occurs when the aorta, the main artery supplying blood to the lower extremities, becomes narrowed or blocked, typically due to atherosclerosis. This condition can lead to serious complications, including limb ischemia and cardiovascular events. Understanding AIOD is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease can vary in severity and may include:
Claudication: Pain or cramping in the legs or buttocks during physical activity, which typically resolves with rest.
Weak or Absent Pulses: Reduced blood flow may lead to weak or absent pulses in the legs or feet.
Coldness in the Lower Extremities: Affected limbs may feel colder than the rest of the body.
Skin Changes: Changes in skin color, texture, or temperature may occur.
Non-Healing Wounds: Ulcers or sores on the feet or legs that do not heal properly.

diseases.name: Aphakia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aphakia is a condition characterized by the absence of the eye's natural lens, which can significantly impact vision. This condition can arise from various causes, including surgical removal of the lens due to cataracts, trauma, or congenital factors. Understanding aphakia is crucial, as it can lead to various visual impairments and complications if not properly managed. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of aphakia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Individuals with aphakia may experience a range of visual symptoms, including:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty focusing on objects at various distances.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to bright lights, often leading to discomfort.
Glare and Halos: Difficulty seeing in bright conditions, with halos around lights.
Reduced Depth Perception: Challenges in judging distances accurately.

diseases.name: Aphasia - Types, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Aphasia is a common condition that affects millions of people worldwide. A person living with aphasia will face difficulty in speaking, reading, or trying to communicate with others. Even though the person’s intellect is intact, an individual will find it difficult to put his thoughts into words. Aphasia can either occur suddenly or develop gradually over the years, but the patient will have to face difficulties in performing daily activities and tasks.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms are different according to the areas of the brain affected . Some changes or issues in daily activities help us to identify as the symptoms of aphasia which are : ● Difficulty in distinguishing the name of any objects, known persons, places, and any incidents. ● Difficulty finding the correct or appropriate words when reading, writing and speaking. ● Facing trouble while pronouncing the words which is also termed as Dysarthria . ● Chances of skipping common or small words such as was, the, of, while talking. There is a lack of grammatical correctness in speech. ● Low level of understanding of the conversation, with a poor quality of talk. ● Inability to set the words in an arranged form. ● Lack of awareness about their fault in their own spoken speech. ● Limited speech with more effort or sometimes repeating the same words and phrases over again and again. ● Difficulty in performing simple mathematical solutions. ● Presence of nonsensical speech. For example, saying “blem” for “ball”.

diseases.name: Aplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aplasia is a medical term that refers to the absence or failure of an organ or tissue to develop properly. This condition can affect various parts of the body, including the bone marrow, which is crucial for producing blood cells. Understanding aplasia is significant because it can lead to serious health complications, including anemia, increased risk of infections, and bleeding disorders. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of aplasia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of aplasia can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Due to a lack of red blood cells, individuals may experience extreme tiredness.
Frequent Infections: A decrease in white blood cells can lead to a weakened immune system, making individuals more susceptible to infections.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: A low platelet count can result in easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from cuts, or spontaneous bleeding.
Pale Skin: Anemia can cause paleness due to reduced hemoglobin levels.

diseases.name: Aplastic Anemia - Symptoms, Complications, Diet and Treatment
diseases.description: Aplastic anemia, also known as hypoplastic anemia, is a rare and serious condition when the body stops producing blood cells, causing fatigue. This condition can occur at any age in varying degrees of severity. Its onset can be sudden or begin gradually and worsen over time. While aplastic anemia can be severe with serious life-threatening consequences like bleeding or infections, it is also very treatable.
symptoms: A person could have a condition like aplastic anemia without showing any symptoms. However, when they do showcase symptoms, they will most likely experience the following:
Fatigue
Prolonged bleeding from any cuts
Bleeding gums or nosebleeds
Increased frequency of infections
Dizziness
Rashes on the skin
Shortness of breath even after minimal exertion
Fever and/or headache
Susceptible to easy bruising
Pale skin
Complications or Risk factors Aplastic anemia is a rare condition. Some risk factors for the condition include:
Chemotherapy
Exposure to toxic chemicals
Blood diseases or autoimmune diseases
Use of certain prescription drugs or gold compounds
Pregnancy
Treatment The treatment for aplastic anemia depends entirely upon the severity of the condition and the age of the patient. Your doctor might prescribe one or more of the following treatments:

Antibiotics: People with aplastic anemia are more prone to infections since they are no longer producing white blood cells that are responsible for fighting off germs. Your doctor might recommend antibiotics to help boost your immune system.

Blood transfusion : While this is a temporary fix, a blood transfusion will help restore the blood cell numbers. This line of treatment prevents excessive bleeding. However, there is a limit to the number of transfusions a person can have during their lifetime. There can be severe complications with increased transfusions.

Immunosuppressants: In some cases of aplastic anemia, the condition is caused by an autoimmune disease. This is where the body’s immune system starts to attack the body. Here, immunosuppressants are administered to suppress the body’s natural immune system and prevent it from attacking the patient’s bone marrow. These drugs need to be taken for life, and the patient will have to be cautious about contracting other infections.

Growth Factors: Some drugs which mimic naturally occurring hormones can be used to signal to your bone marrow that they need to produce blood cells. This treatment is effective in patients who have bone marrow failure diseases.

Stem Cell transplant: This treatment is the most intensive of all your options. It is generally recommended for aplastic anemia patients who are young. In this treatment, the failed bone marrow is depleted through radiation or chemotherapy. Then matching donor stem cells are injected into the patient. These stem cells transfer to the bone marrow cavities and produce new blood cells. The patient will have to use immunosuppressants in order to prevent rejection of the stem cells.

Precautions The condition can cause a range of complications depending on its severity. Anyone who has been diagnosed with aplastic anemia must take the following precautions in order to keep their risks to a minimum.

Rest whenever you feel the need. Since the number of red blood cells in your body are severely reduced, you will experience shortness of breath and fatigue . So, it is vital that you rest whenever your body signals to you that it is tired.

Avoid situations where you can get hurt like contact sports. You do not want to be in a situation where you will experience bleeding as it can be difficult to control. It is not just cut that you have to be wary of; you should also be aware that you can suffer from internal bleeding.

Wash your hands regularly and practice safe hygiene practices to stave off any potential infections. The lack of white blood cells makes it difficult to fight off infections. Help your body by avoiding people who have infections or large crowded spaces.

diseases.name: Aplastic Crisis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aplastic crisis is a serious medical condition characterized by a sudden and severe decrease in the production of red blood cells, leading to anemia. This condition is particularly significant because it can occur in individuals with underlying health issues, such as sickle cell disease or thalassemia, and can lead to life-threatening complications if not promptly addressed. Understanding aplastic crisis is crucial for early recognition and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of aplastic crisis can vary but often include:
Fatigue: A significant drop in red blood cells can lead to extreme tiredness and weakness.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin due to reduced hemoglobin levels.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity, can occur as the body struggles to deliver oxygen.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may beat faster to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Insufficient blood flow can lead to feelings of faintness.

diseases.name: Appendiceal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Appendiceal cancer is a rare cancer that starts in the appendix---a small pouch attached to the large intestine. It affects only 1--2 people in a million each year, so most people have never heard of it until diagnosis. Because of its rarity, many people are not aware of it until they or a loved one is diagnosed.
symptoms: Early appendiceal cancer often causes no symptoms. When symptoms do appear, they may mimic appendicitis or other abdominal conditions. Signs and symptoms include:
Pain in the lower right side of the abdomen
Bloating or swelling
Changes in bowel habits (constipation or diarrhea)
Unexplained weight loss
A feeling of fullness
Advanced Symptoms: A palpable abdominal mass Ascites (fluid buildup in the abdomen) Widespread abdominal pain Gastrointestinal bleeding (in rare cases)
A palpable abdominal mass
Ascites (fluid buildup in the abdomen)
Widespread abdominal pain
Gastrointestinal bleeding (in rare cases)
Because these symptoms are non-specific, appendiceal cancer is often found incidentally during surgery or imaging for another condition.

diseases.name: Appendicitis - Signs and Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The appendix is a finger-like pouch attached at the beginning of the large intestine and has no known purpose in the human body. Appendicitis is the corresponding condition of an inflamed appendix filled with pus that causes unbearable pain. The pain is concentrated in the lower right abdomen. In certain cases, it starts around the navel. As the inflammation increases, the pain becomes severe, and appendicitis turns acute. Most of these people affected by this condition are between the ages of 10 and 30. So, let us take a closer look at what appendicitis really is.
symptoms: Appendicitis symptoms form a classic triad of stomach pain, vomiting, and fever. But this typical presentation may not be presented in all cases.

Abdominal pain is the most common symptom of appendicitis. Typically, the pain starts in the middle of the abdomen and later shifts to the lower right side, where the appendix is usually located. The pain may worsen if the area where the appendix is located is pressed or while coughing or walking. In acute appendicitis, the affected individual experiences excruciating pain that causes him to bend his body by folding his legs to the chest.

The anatomic position of the appendix varies considerably between individuals. The location of the pain associated with appendicitis and the associated symptoms can also vary accordingly. An inflamed appendix near the urinary bladder may irritate the bladder and cause painful urination. If the appendix extends behind, inflammation can irritate the nerves and muscles behind and cause difficulty while walking.
Fever
Nausea and vomiting
Loss of appetite
Pain around the navel
Bloating
Frequent and painful urination

Appendicitis symptoms vary in different individuals, and the duration of the inflammation also causes the symptoms to vary. Depending on the duration of the symptoms and the presence of complications, appendicitis may be classified as acute, chronic, recurrent, or complicated.

diseases.name: Appendicolith - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Appendicolith , often referred to as an appendiceal stone, is a calcified deposit that can form in the appendix, a small pouch connected to the large intestine. While appendicoliths are not always symptomatic, they can lead to significant complications, including appendicitis, if left untreated. Understanding appendicoliths is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as they can pose serious health risks. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of appendicoliths, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Many individuals with appendicoliths may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Abdominal Pain: Often starting around the navel and then shifting to the lower right abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Accompanying the abdominal pain, these symptoms may indicate inflammation.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat can occur due to discomfort.
Fever: A low-grade fever may develop as the body responds to inflammation.

diseases.name: Aquagenic Urticaria : Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, Prevention and More
diseases.description: Water is essential for human beings. And for most people, it does not cause any adverse reaction. However, it is not the case for individuals with a rare condition called Aquagenic Urticaria. People suffering from this condition develop hives and rashes rapidly when their skin comes in contact with water.
symptoms: Aquagenic hive is a rare condition that might cause an itchy, painful rash when the skin comes in contact with water. The rash may appear anywhere on the body. But it commonly appears on the neck, arms, and chest. These symptoms disappear within 30 to 60 minutes after the skin dries. Within minutes of being exposed to water, people with this condition might experience:
Reddening of the skin
Burning sensation
Lesions
Welts
Inflammation
In more severe cases, drinking water can also cause people to experience symptoms including:
Rash around the mouth
Difficulty swallowing, breathing
Wheezing
Sometimes, a person may get other symptoms such as headaches , shortness of breath, dizziness, and fainting.

diseases.name: Arachnoid Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arachnoid cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form in the arachnoid membrane, one of the three layers of tissue that cover the brain and spinal cord. While many individuals with arachnoid cysts may remain asymptomatic, these cysts can sometimes lead to significant neurological issues, making their understanding crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of arachnoid cysts, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Arachnoid cysts can be asymptomatic, meaning many individuals may not experience any noticeable symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can vary based on the cyst's size and location. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Persistent or severe headaches may occur, particularly if the cyst exerts pressure on surrounding brain structures.
Seizures: Some individuals may experience seizures, especially if the cyst is located in the temporal lobe.
Neurological Deficits: Depending on the cyst's location, symptoms may include weakness, numbness, or coordination problems.
Vision or Hearing Changes: Cysts near the optic or auditory pathways may lead to visual or hearing disturbances.

diseases.name: Arachnoiditis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arachnoiditis is a rare but serious condition that affects the arachnoid mater, one of the three membranes that surround and protect the brain and spinal cord. This condition can lead to significant pain and neurological issues, impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding arachnoiditis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can result from various causes and may lead to long-term complications if not addressed properly.
symptoms: The symptoms of arachnoiditis can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Chronic Pain: This is the most common symptom, often described as burning, stabbing, or aching pain in the lower back, legs, or feet.
Numbness and Tingling: Many patients report sensations of numbness or tingling in the extremities.
Muscle Weakness: Weakness in the legs or other areas may occur, affecting mobility.
Bladder and Bowel Dysfunction: Some individuals may experience issues with bladder control or bowel function.
Neurological Symptoms: These can include difficulty walking, coordination problems, and changes in reflexes.

diseases.name: Arcuate Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arcuate uterus is a congenital uterine anomaly characterized by a slight indentation at the top of the uterine cavity. While it is considered one of the least severe forms of uterine malformations, understanding its significance is crucial for women’s reproductive health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of arcuate uterus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many women with an arcuate uterus may not experience any symptoms. However, some may report:
Irregular menstrual cycles
Painful periods (dysmenorrhea)
Difficulty in conceiving (though this is rare)

diseases.name: ARDS - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is a serious medical condition characterized by rapid onset of widespread inflammation in the lungs. It is a critical illness that can lead to severe respiratory failure and is often associated with high mortality rates. Understanding ARDS is crucial not only for healthcare professionals but also for the general public, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ARDS, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of ARDS can develop rapidly, often within hours to days after the initial injury or illness. Common symptoms include:
Severe Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate as the body attempts to get more oxygen.
Cough: A persistent cough that may produce sputum.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Confusion or Fatigue: Due to low oxygen levels affecting brain function.

diseases.name: Are You Prone to High Blood Pressure?
diseases.description: About 60 percent of your health issues occur between the age of 30 to 45 and about 70 percent of those health problems can be prevented, if diagnosed on time. Most of the global studies identified three avoidable risk factors like smoking, high blood pressure (Hypertension or High BP), obesity or high BMI (body, mass index) for disease and death among adults. And, almost 50 percent of deaths are attributed to High BP. High BP is considered a silent killer as it is a serious condition that may lead to stroke, heart disease , heart and/or kidney failure, including other complications. It can be identified if regular body check-ups are done. Most people are under the impression that if you don’t smoke and your BMI is in control, you cannot have high blood pressure . That certainly is not enough. Constant stress for a long time and having a family history of high blood pressure can trigger high BP. This means you can still be a victim of high blood pressure. If the above figures and risk factors are telling you about your own health, read on to know more about High Blood Pressure and its effect on your life.

diseases.name: Are You Suffering From Painful Periods?
diseases.description: You must have heard from people saying painful periods is normal and they also tell young girls nothing to worry and once you get married or have children, this will subside. This is a myth and if you have painful period, make sure you see your gynecologist and rule out endometriosis. Mild pain can be primary dysmenorrhea and doesnot need intervention but if it is severe needs treatment and it should start early to stop the progression of the disease
symptoms: Surgery to remove uterus and ovaries was once considered the permanent treatment for endometriosis but now it’s clear with research that it’s no more the permanent cure. Having your ovaries removed results in menopause. The lack of hormones produced by the ovaries may improve endometriosis pain for some women, but for others, endometriosis that remains after surgery continues to cause symptoms. You must ask your gynecologist about excision surgery if you are getting operated for pain or infertility due to endometriosis. Partial clearance may not help you always. Ladies, please do not avoid period pains. It may look normal to you but there can be something really serious about it which you may not know. Consult the best doctors near you as soon as possible. Book online appointment with the best gynecologist in your city, Visit the links below to get a complete list of doctors Best Gynecologist in Bangalore Best Gynecologist in Chennai gynecologist Best Gynecologist in Kolkata Best Gynecologist in Delhi Best Gynecologist in Mumbai

diseases.name: Areflexia: Definition, Detrusor, Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: When a person gets a gentle tap on the knee, ankle, or fingers to elicit a reflex, but the tendons in those regions do not react to the stimuli and produce normal reflexes, it indicates a neurological disorder known as areflexia. Areflexia patients do not exhibit typical body reflexes, such as the knee-jerk reaction.
symptoms: A complete absence of reflexes is the leading symptom of areflexia due to nerve damage. Other symptoms depend on underlying causes. However, other common symptoms may include the following:
Tingling or numbness in the hands or feet
Irregular muscle coordination
Weakness in the muscle
Lack of muscle coordination resulting in clumsiness and frequent dropping of things from hands or falling
Lack of sexual desire, particularly in men
Constipation
Problems in digestion
Detrusor areflexia
Complete or partial paralysis
Respiratory failure
Loss of sensitivity to touch in fingers or toes
Unexplained pain

diseases.name: Argyria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Argyria is a rare condition characterized by a bluish-gray discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes, resulting from the accumulation of silver in the body. While it is not life-threatening, argyria can have significant psychological and social implications for those affected. This article aims to provide a thorough understanding of argyria, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of argyria is a bluish-gray discoloration of the skin, particularly in areas exposed to sunlight. Other symptoms may include:
