Mucous Membrane Discoloration: The gums and other mucous membranes may also exhibit a grayish hue.
Photosensitivity: Individuals may experience increased sensitivity to sunlight, leading to skin irritation or rashes.
Eye Discoloration: In some cases, the sclera (the white part of the eye) may take on a bluish tint.

diseases.name: Armpit Yeast Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Armpit yeast infection, also known as axillary candidiasis, is a fungal infection that occurs in the warm, moist environment of the armpits. This condition is caused by an overgrowth of yeast, particularly Candida albicans , which is a type of fungus that naturally resides on the skin and in the body. While often overlooked, armpit yeast infections can lead to discomfort, itching, and skin irritation, significantly impacting an individual's quality of life. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and preventive measures is crucial for effective management and recovery.
symptoms: The symptoms of an armpit yeast infection can vary in severity but typically include:
Itching: A persistent and intense itching sensation in the armpit area.
Redness and Inflammation: The skin may appear red, swollen, and irritated.
Rash: A rash may develop, often characterized by small red bumps or patches.
Odor: An unpleasant odor may arise due to the infection.
Discomfort: General discomfort, especially when moving the arms or wearing clothing.

diseases.name: Arnold Chiari Malformation: Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: When the skull is smaller than usual or misshapen , it presses on the brain and forces it downwards into the spinal canal is known as a Chiari malformation. It typically affects the region of the brain called the cerebellum, which is responsible for controlling balance.
symptoms: Every person’s symptoms vary from each other. Some may experience mild symptoms, while others develop severe symptoms. Some symptoms present at birth, while others may appear in late childhood or adulthood. Some of the common symptoms are as follows:

Headache: It is a common symptom. Headache may start or worsen after the person coughs, sneezes, or strains, often developing at the back of the head. However, the ache may spread to the neck and shoulder. Patients describe the pain as throbbing, stabbing, or sharp.

Balance and movement issues: Chiari malformation may cause weakness in the muscles, lack of coordination, and numbness in the limbs, causing a lack of fine motor skills. It can also result in dizziness, vertigo , and balance issues.

Issues in hearing and vision: Some patients experience buzzing or ringing sounds in the ear and have trouble hearing. They also experience double vision, blurred vision, abnormal eye movements, and sensitivity to light.

Problems with eating, drinking and speaking: Swallowing becomes difficult. Some babies with Chiari malformation may experience vomiting , gagging, or drooling, in addition to difficulty eating and may struggle to put on weight for proper development.
Scoliosis: Curvature of the spine, known as scoliosis , is seen in some people with Chiari malformation.
Sleep-related issues: Patients may also experience insomnia due to headaches, while others may also experience sleep apnea.
Problems with bladder and bowel: Chiari malformation may also cause bladder and bowel control issues.
Other symptoms: Chronic fatigue, palpitations, fainting spells, and tingling or burning sensations in the fingers, toes, or lips are some of the other symptoms.
Irrespective of the type or severity of the condition, the following are the symptoms in an infant:
Problems swallowing
Excessive drooling, gagging, or vomiting
Irritability while eating or feeding
Breathing difficulties
Developmental delays
Stiff neck
Problems gaining weight
Lack of arm strength
If the infant is suffering from Chiari malformation type 2 with excess fluid in the brain, the following are some of the additional symptoms to look out for:
A large head
Vomiting
Seizures
Irritability
Delay in development
If the symptoms are developed rapidly, they may require emergency treatment.

diseases.name: Arrhythmia
diseases.description: Regular heartbeats occur because of internal electrical signals that cause the heart to contract and relax. This internal electrical system controls the rhythm and rate of our heartbeats. When that electrical system goes awry, your heart may either beat too fast, too slowly or irregularly.

diseases.name: Arsenic Poisoning - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arsenic poisoning is a serious health concern that arises from exposure to arsenic, a toxic element found in the environment. This condition can lead to severe health complications and even death if not addressed promptly. Understanding arsenic poisoning is crucial for prevention, early detection, and effective treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of arsenic poisoning, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of arsenic poisoning can vary depending on the level and duration of exposure. Common symptoms include:
Nausea and Vomiting: Often the first signs of acute poisoning.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping and discomfort in the stomach area.
Diarrhea: Frequent loose or watery stools.
Headaches: Persistent or severe headaches.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or weakness.
Skin Changes: Rashes, discoloration, or lesions on the skin.
Neurological Symptoms: Confusion, dizziness, or numbness in extremities.

diseases.name: Arterial Embolism
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: An embolism has different stages and each of these stages have symptoms depending on the extent of damage already caused. Depending on where the clot forms, arterial thrombosis and embolism can cause several serious conditions, including:
Heart Attack when the flow of blood to the heart is unexpectedly clogged
Stroke when blood flow to the brain is cut off
Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD), alternatively known as peripheral vascular disease (PVD) when a build-up of fatty deposits in the arteries curbs the supply of blood to leg muscles
Shivering
Lack of movement
Lack of pulse
Feeling of numbness
Muscle pain or spasm
Pale skin
Weakness
These symptoms will most likely be asymmetrical which means they will only appear on the side of your body with the embolism.
Ulcers
Signs of shedding skin
Tissue death
If you feel some/any/all of the above symptoms, prompt medical attention is highly advised

diseases.name: Arteriosclerosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arteriosclerosis is a term that encompasses a group of conditions characterized by the thickening and hardening of the arterial walls. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes. Understanding arteriosclerosis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, risk factors, and treatment options, ultimately empowering individuals to take proactive steps in managing their cardiovascular health.
symptoms: Arteriosclerosis may not present noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Chest Pain (Angina): A feeling of pressure or tightness in the chest, often triggered by physical activity or stress.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical exertion or at rest.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness, especially during physical activity.
Leg Pain: Pain or cramping in the legs during exercise, known as claudication.

diseases.name: Arteriovenous Fistula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is a medical condition characterized by an abnormal connection between an artery and a vein. This condition can have significant implications for an individual's health, particularly in the context of kidney disease and dialysis. Understanding arteriovenous fistulas is crucial for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers alike, as it plays a vital role in managing chronic conditions and ensuring effective treatment options.
symptoms: The symptoms of an arteriovenous fistula can vary depending on its size and location. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: The affected area may become swollen due to increased blood flow.
Pain: Patients may experience pain or discomfort near the fistula site.
Skin Changes: The skin over the fistula may appear discolored or feel warm to the touch.
Pulse Changes: A noticeable pulse may be felt over the fistula due to the high blood flow.

diseases.name: Arthritis
diseases.description: Arthritis is a broad term that refers to inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain, swelling, stiffness, and limited range of motion. There are more than 100 different types of arthritis. The most common forms are osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Arthritis is a leading cause of disability in the United States.
symptoms: Joint pain
Swelling in one or more joints
Stiffness in the morning or after sitting still
Decreased range of motion
Redness of the skin around the joint
Fatigue

diseases.name: Arthus Reaction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The Arthus reaction is a localized immune response that occurs when an individual is exposed to a specific antigen after having previously developed antibodies against that antigen. This phenomenon is significant in the field of immunology and vaccine development, as it can provide insights into how the immune system reacts to certain stimuli. Understanding the Arthus reaction is crucial for healthcare professionals, researchers, and patients alike, as it can influence vaccination strategies and the management of allergic reactions.
symptoms: The symptoms of an Arthus reaction can vary depending on the severity of the response and the location of the immune complex deposition. Common symptoms include:
Localized Swelling: This is often the most noticeable symptom, occurring at the site of antigen exposure or injection.
Redness and Warmth: The affected area may appear red and feel warm to the touch due to increased blood flow and inflammation.
Pain or Discomfort: Individuals may experience pain or tenderness in the affected area.
Itching or Rash: Some may develop an itchy rash or hives around the injection site.

diseases.name: Articulation Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Articulation disorder is a speech disorder that affects an individual's ability to produce sounds correctly, leading to difficulties in communication. This condition can significantly impact a person's social interactions, academic performance, and overall quality of life. Understanding articulation disorder is crucial for parents, educators, and healthcare providers, as early identification and intervention can lead to better outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Common symptoms of articulation disorder include:
Difficulty pronouncing specific sounds (e.g., "s," "r," "l").
Substituting one sound for another (e.g., saying "w" for "r").
Omitting sounds in words (e.g., saying "ca" instead of "cat").
Distorting sounds, making them unclear.
Difficulty being understood by peers or adults.

diseases.name: Asbestosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Asbestosis is a serious lung condition caused by the inhalation of asbestos fibers, which can lead to significant health complications. This disease is particularly significant due to its association with occupational exposure, especially in industries that historically used asbestos extensively. Understanding asbestosis is crucial for those at risk, as early detection and management can significantly impact quality of life and long-term health outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of asbestosis may not appear until many years after exposure. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Initially occurring during physical activity, it may progress to breathlessness at rest.
Persistent Cough: A dry cough that does not go away can be an early sign.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest may occur, especially during deep breaths.
Clubbing of Fingers: Enlargement of the fingertips or toes can develop over time.

diseases.name: Ascites - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ascites is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of fluid in the abdominal cavity. This condition can be a significant indicator of underlying health issues, often related to liver disease, heart failure, or cancer. Understanding ascites is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers and healthcare professionals, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ascites, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of ascites can vary depending on the underlying cause and the amount of fluid present. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Swelling: A noticeable increase in the size of the abdomen due to fluid accumulation.
Discomfort or Pain: Patients may experience a feeling of fullness or pressure in the abdomen.
Shortness of Breath: Fluid buildup can press against the diaphragm, making it difficult to breathe.
Weight Gain: Sudden weight gain can occur due to fluid retention.
Changes in Bowel Habits: Some individuals may experience constipation or changes in appetite.

diseases.name: Ashermans Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Asherman's Syndrome is a rare but significant medical condition that affects women's reproductive health. Characterized by the formation of scar tissue in the uterus, this syndrome can lead to a range of complications, including infertility, menstrual irregularities, and complications during pregnancy. Understanding Asherman's Syndrome is crucial for women who may be experiencing unexplained reproductive issues, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Asherman's Syndrome can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Menstrual Irregularities: Women may experience lighter periods, missed periods, or even amenorrhea (absence of menstruation).
Infertility: Difficulty conceiving is a significant concern for women with this condition.
Pelvic Pain: Some women may experience chronic pelvic pain or discomfort.
Recurrent Miscarriages: Women with Asherman's Syndrome may face challenges in maintaining a pregnancy.

diseases.name: Asperger Syndrome
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms for Asperger syndrome differ from person to person. It also depends on a person’s age. In children, for example, there develops an obsessive focus on one idea or item or topic of interest. This can be the case even in adults and more often than not, it results in one-sided conversations and social awkwardness.

A person with Asperger syndrome cannot acknowledge another person’s attempt to change a topic of conversation. They also suffer in situations where there needs to be social interaction. They often have trouble making eye contact with others and also find it hard to recognize another person’s feelings.
Children with Asperger may have difficulty with motor skills such as riding, running or walking.

diseases.name: Aspergillosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aspergillosis is a term that encompasses a range of diseases caused by the Aspergillus species, a type of mold commonly found in the environment. This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause serious health issues, particularly in immunocompromised individuals, but also due to its increasing prevalence in various populations. Understanding Aspergillosis is crucial for early detection, effective treatment, and prevention of complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of Aspergillosis can vary widely depending on the type of infection:
Allergic Aspergillosis: Symptoms may include wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, often resembling asthma.
Chronic Pulmonary Aspergillosis: This form may present with a persistent cough, chest pain, fatigue, and weight loss.
Invasive Aspergillosis: Symptoms can be severe and include fever, cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing, often accompanied by a rapid decline in health.

diseases.name: Asphyxiation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Asphyxiation is a critical medical condition that occurs when the body is deprived of oxygen, leading to severe physiological consequences. This condition can arise from various causes, including choking, drowning, or exposure to toxic gases. Understanding asphyxiation is vital not only for medical professionals but also for the general public, as timely recognition and intervention can save lives. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of asphyxiation.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of asphyxiation is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling like you can't get enough air.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially around the lips and fingertips, indicating low oxygen levels.
Confusion or Disorientation: Lack of oxygen can affect cognitive function, leading to confusion.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may race as the body attempts to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Loss of Consciousness: In severe cases, asphyxiation can lead to fainting or loss of consciousness.

diseases.name: Aspiration Pneumonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Aspiration pneumonia is a serious condition that arises when food, liquid, or other foreign materials are inhaled into the lungs, leading to infection and inflammation. This condition is significant not only because of its potential severity but also due to its prevalence among certain populations, particularly the elderly and those with swallowing difficulties. Understanding aspiration pneumonia is crucial for both prevention and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of aspiration pneumonia can vary but often include:
Cough: A persistent cough, which may produce phlegm or pus.
Fever: A high temperature indicating infection.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or rapid breathing.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, especially when breathing deeply or coughing.
Fatigue: General tiredness and weakness.

diseases.name: Assistive Technology for Spinal Cord Injury: Types and Benefits
diseases.description: Assistive technology helps or assists people with disabilities in living a better life and reducing the burden of the disorder. Most people suffer from spinal cord injuries caused by falls, crashes, and road accidents.

diseases.name: Asterixis: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment, Diagnosis, Risk Factors
diseases.description: Several neurological problems cause motor issues in human beings. Asterixis is one such neurological disorder affecting the motor functions of particular body parts.
symptoms: The fluttering tremor of the hands, fingers, and wrists is the most noticeable sign of Asterixis. Since this flapping is unintentional, one has no control over it. Asterixis, which most frequently manifests as hand tremors, can also affect other body portions. In addition, the underlying reasons for the tremors may cause other symptoms. ‌These other symptoms may differ depending on whether liver, renal, cardiac, or metabolic disorders influence the brain. ‌

diseases.name: Asteroid Hyalosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Asteroid hyalosis is a fascinating yet often misunderstood ocular condition characterized by the presence of small, white, opalescent bodies within the vitreous humor of the eye. While it is generally considered benign and does not typically lead to significant vision impairment, understanding its implications is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of asteroid hyalosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Asteroid hyalosis is often asymptomatic, meaning many individuals may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some common symptoms include:
Floaters: Patients may notice small, moving spots or strands in their field of vision.
Visual Disturbances: Some individuals may experience blurred vision or difficulty focusing, particularly in bright light.
Light Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to light may occur in some cases.

diseases.name: Asthma
diseases.description: Asthma is a chronic condition that inflames and narrows the airways, making it harder to breathe. Symptoms can come and go and are often triggered by infections, allergens, or exercise.
symptoms: Wheezing, especially when breathing out
Coughing at night or early morning
Shortness of breath
Chest tightness

diseases.name: Astigmatism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Astigmatism is a common refractive error that affects how the eye focuses light. It can lead to blurred or distorted vision, making everyday activities challenging. Understanding astigmatism is crucial not only for those who experience its symptoms but also for anyone interested in maintaining optimal eye health. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of astigmatism, providing a thorough understanding of this condition.
symptoms: Individuals with astigmatism may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Blurred or distorted vision at all distances
Difficulty seeing at night
Eye strain or discomfort
Headaches, especially after prolonged visual tasks
Squinting to see clearly

diseases.name: Astraphobia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Astraphobia, commonly known as the fear of thunder and lightning, is a specific phobia that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. While many people may feel uneasy during thunderstorms, those with astraphobia experience intense fear and anxiety that can lead to avoidance behaviors and distress. Understanding this condition is crucial for those affected and their loved ones, as it can help in seeking appropriate treatment and support.
symptoms: Individuals with astraphobia may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Intense Fear: An overwhelming sense of dread or panic when thunder or lightning occurs.
Physical Reactions: Symptoms such as rapid heartbeat, sweating, trembling, and shortness of breath during storms.
Avoidance Behavior: Actively avoiding situations where thunderstorms may occur, such as staying indoors or canceling outdoor plans.
Anxiety: Persistent worry about future thunderstorms, leading to increased anxiety levels even when storms are not imminent.

diseases.name: Astrovirus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Astrovirus is a viral pathogen that primarily affects the gastrointestinal tract, leading to gastroenteritis, particularly in young children and immunocompromised individuals. While it is often overshadowed by more well-known viruses like norovirus and rotavirus, astrovirus is significant due to its prevalence and potential to cause outbreaks, especially in settings such as daycare centers, nursing homes, and hospitals. Understanding astrovirus is crucial for effective prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, making it an important topic for both healthcare professionals and the general public.
symptoms: Astrovirus infections typically present with mild to moderate gastroenteritis symptoms. Common symptoms include:
Diarrhea: Watery stools are the most common symptom.
Vomiting: This may occur but is less frequent than with other viral gastroenteritis.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping and discomfort are common.
Fever: A mild fever may accompany the infection.
Nausea: Patients often report feelings of nausea.

diseases.name: Asymptomatic Bacteriuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Asymptomatic bacteriuria (ABU) is a medical condition characterized by the presence of bacteria in the urine without any accompanying symptoms of a urinary tract infection (UTI). While it may sound alarming, ABU is surprisingly common, especially among certain populations, such as the elderly and pregnant women. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can have significant implications for both individual health and public health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of asymptomatic bacteriuria, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Asymptomatic bacteriuria is defined as the isolation of a specified number of bacteria in the urine of a person who does not exhibit any symptoms of a urinary tract infection. Typically, this is defined as the presence of 100,000 colony-forming units (CFUs) of bacteria per milliliter of urine in a clean-catch sample. It is important to note that ABU is distinct from symptomatic urinary tract infections, which present with symptoms such as pain during urination, frequent urination, and abdominal discomfort.
As the name suggests, asymptomatic bacteriuria does not present with any noticeable symptoms. However, it is essential to differentiate ABU from symptomatic urinary tract infections, which can cause:
Pain or burning sensation during urination
Frequent urge to urinate
Cloudy or foul-smelling urine
Lower abdominal pain or discomfort
While asymptomatic bacteriuria is often benign, untreated cases can lead to complications, particularly in vulnerable populations. Potential complications include:
Progression to Symptomatic UTI: Bacteria may multiply and lead to a symptomatic urinary tract infection, causing discomfort and requiring treatment.
Kidney Infections: In some cases, bacteria can ascend to the kidneys, resulting in pyelonephritis, which can be serious and require hospitalization.
Sepsis: In rare instances, untreated infections can lead to sepsis, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate medical attention.
Preventing asymptomatic bacteriuria involves adopting healthy lifestyle practices and hygiene measures. Here are some strategies:
Stay Hydrated: Drinking adequate fluids helps flush bacteria from the urinary tract.
Practice Good Hygiene: Regularly washing the genital area and wiping from front to back can reduce bacterial entry.
Urinate After Intercourse: This practice can help eliminate bacteria that may have entered the urinary tract during sexual activity.
Dietary Modifications: Consuming foods rich in antioxidants and probiotics can support urinary tract health.
Regular Medical Check-ups: Routine screenings and check-ups can help identify and manage any underlying health issues.

diseases.name: Ataxia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ataxia is a term that refers to a lack of voluntary coordination of muscle movements, which can affect various parts of the body, including the limbs, eyes, and speech. This condition can significantly impact an individual's ability to perform everyday tasks, leading to challenges in mobility, balance, and overall quality of life. Understanding ataxia is crucial not only for those who may be affected by it but also for caregivers, healthcare providers, and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ataxia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Ataxia can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the underlying cause and the areas of the nervous system affected. Common symptoms include:
Unsteady Gait: Difficulty walking or maintaining balance, often described as a "drunken" walk.
Coordination Problems: Difficulty with fine motor skills, such as writing or buttoning a shirt.
Speech Difficulties: Slurred speech or changes in voice quality, known as dysarthria.
Vision Problems: Blurred or double vision, or difficulty with eye movements (nystagmus).
Tremors: Involuntary shaking or trembling of the limbs.

diseases.name: Ataxia Telangiectasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ataxia Telangiectasia (A-T) is a rare, inherited disorder that affects multiple systems in the body, leading to a range of neurological and immunological challenges. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the individuals affected but also due to its implications for family members and healthcare providers. Understanding A-T is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those living with this condition.
symptoms: Ataxia Telangiectasia presents a variety of symptoms that can vary in severity among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Ataxia: Loss of coordination and balance, leading to difficulty walking and performing fine motor tasks.
Telangiectasia: Small, dilated blood vessels visible on the skin, particularly on the face and eyes.
Immunodeficiency: Increased susceptibility to infections due to a weakened immune system.
Neurological Issues: Cognitive decline, learning disabilities, and speech difficulties.
Growth Retardation: Delayed growth and development in children.
Increased Cancer Risk: Higher likelihood of developing certain cancers, particularly lymphomas and leukemias.

diseases.name: Atelectasis - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Atelectasis is a condition when there is a complete or partial collapse of the entire lung or area (lobe) of the lung. It occurs when the tiny air sacs (alveoli) within the lungs become deflated or possibly filled with alveolar fluid.
symptoms: Some of the most common atelectasis symptoms include:
Difficulty breathing
Shallow breathing
Rapid breathing
Cough
Wheezing
Some patients can experience severe atelectasis symptoms, like pain in the chest region while breathing, due to the severity of the condition leading to a lung collapse.

diseases.name: Atherosclerosis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Atherosclerosis shows no symptoms at a younger age, but only in the middle and older age groups.
The common symptoms of Atherosclerosis include:
Chest pain or angina
Pain in parts of the body where an artery might be blocked
Shortness of breath
Fatigue
Confusion due to blocked circulation
Weakening of leg muscles

diseases.name: Athetosis: Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Movement disorders are many. But some are more severe than others. Understanding the signs and causes of various disorders allows a patient to seek early medical intervention for a better quality of life. This blog delves deep into the movement disorder Athetosis, its symptoms, causes and available treatment options.
symptoms: The signs or symptoms that may indicate athetosis are:
Erratic and unpredictable variations in muscular motion aggravate symptoms when attempting to control the movement
Sluggish, writhing, involuntary muscle motions
Symptoms worsen as one tries to stand up straight
Difficulty talking
Muscle overflow may also occur in those with athetosis. This is when one tries to control one muscle or muscle group, and another muscle group moves uncontrollably.

diseases.name: Athlete’s Foot - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Athlete’s foot, also known as tinea pedis, is a form of fungal infection. The fungal skin infection begins in between your toes. The fungal infection will appear if you wear very tight-fitting shoes for the major part of the day. The Athlete’s foot is similar to other fungal skin infections, but it can recur again and again if not treated properly and on time.
symptoms: The symptoms of Athlete’s foot include
● Rash: You will notice red, scaly, itchy rashes in between your toes.
● Blisters: You can get blisters in between your toes or on your soles.
● Dryness and scaling: You can experience dryness and scaling on the soles and sides of your sole if suffering from Athlete’s foot.
● Ulcers: Athlete’s foot can lead to painful ulcers or sores. The sores can be full of pus.

diseases.name: Atonic Seizure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atonic seizures, often referred to as "drop attacks," are a type of seizure characterized by a sudden loss of muscle tone, leading to a collapse or fall. These seizures can be particularly dangerous due to the risk of injury from falls. Understanding atonic seizures is crucial for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers, as early recognition and appropriate management can significantly improve quality of life and reduce the risk of complications.
symptoms: The hallmark of an atonic seizure is a sudden loss of muscle tone, which can manifest as:
Dropping of the head: The head may suddenly drop forward or to the side.
Collapse: The individual may fall to the ground without warning.
Brief duration: Atonic seizures typically last only a few seconds.

diseases.name: Atopic Dermatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that affects millions of people worldwide. It is characterized by dry, itchy skin and can significantly impact the quality of life for those who suffer from it. Understanding atopic dermatitis is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of atopic dermatitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Atopic dermatitis symptoms can vary widely among individuals but commonly include:
Dry, sensitive skin: The skin may feel rough and tight.
Intense itching: This can be severe, leading to scratching and further irritation.
Red or brownish-gray patches: These can appear on various parts of the body, including the hands, feet, ankles, wrists, neck, upper chest, eyelids, and inside the bend of the elbows and knees.
Thickened, cracked skin: Chronic scratching can lead to lichenification, where the skin becomes thick and leathery.
Small, raised bumps: These may leak fluid and crust over when scratched.

diseases.name: Atrial Fibrillation With Rvr - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (AF with RVR) is a significant cardiac condition that affects millions of people worldwide. It is characterized by an irregular and often rapid heart rate, which can lead to various complications if not managed properly. Understanding AF with RVR is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of AF with RVR, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Individuals with AF with RVR may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Palpitations: A sensation of a racing or fluttering heart.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A feeling of faintness or unsteadiness.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.

diseases.name: Atrial Septal Defect
diseases.description: Atrial septal defect can be defined as a hole between the walls of the two upper chambers of the heart. Such a defect is congenital and may sometimes go away during early childhood itself. This defect allows oxygen-rich blood to leak into the oxygen-poor blood chambers in the heart. ASD is a defect in the septum between the heart’s two upper chambers (atria). The septum is a wall that separates the heart’s left and right sides. If the hole is small, it may have minimal effect on heart function. When a large defect exists between the atria, a large amount of oxygen-rich (red) blood leaks from the heart’s left side back to the right side. Then this blood is pumped back to the lungs, despite already having been refreshed with oxygen. Unfortunately this creates more work for the right side of the heart. This extra amount of blood flow in the lung arteries can also cause gradual damage. A large ASD is usually closed in early childhood, even in patients with few symptoms, to prevent complications later. The prognosis after ASD closure during childhood is excellent and late complications are uncommon. If the opening is small, surgery or other treatments may not be needed.
symptoms: Some patients with ASD have no symptoms. If the opening is small, it won’t cause symptoms because the additional work done by the heart and lungs is minimal. If the opening is large, it may cause mild shortness of breath, especially with exercise. The increased blood in the lung may increase a patient’s susceptibility to pneumonia and bronchitis. On physical examination, the only abnormal finding may be a murmur (noise heard with a stethoscope) and other abnormal heart sounds. However, with progressive damage to the lung vessels, the pressures in the lung may rise, and the patient can become more severely limited, eventually developing Eisenmenger’s syndrome. ASD may present as:
Stroke
Frequent lung infections
Fatigue
Heart murmurs
Shortness of breath
Swelling in legs or abdomen
Heart palpitations

diseases.name: Atrioventricular Canal Defect - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atrioventricular Canal Defect (AV Canal Defect) is a congenital heart condition that affects the heart's structure and function. It is characterized by a combination of atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD), leading to a single common atrioventricular valve instead of separate mitral and tricuspid valves. This defect can significantly impact blood flow and oxygenation in the body, making it a critical condition that requires timely diagnosis and management. Understanding AV Canal Defect is essential for parents, caregivers, and patients, as early intervention can lead to better health outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Atrioventricular Canal Defect can vary based on the severity of the defect and the age of the child. Common symptoms include:
Rapid Breathing: Infants may exhibit fast or labored breathing due to increased blood flow to the lungs.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty in feeding or poor weight gain can occur as a result of the heart's inefficiency.
Fatigue: Children may tire easily during physical activities or play.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, lips, or nails may indicate low oxygen levels in the blood.
Frequent Respiratory Infections: Increased blood flow to the lungs can lead to recurrent lung infections.

diseases.name: Atrophic Gastritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atrophic gastritis is a chronic condition characterized by the thinning of the stomach lining, which can lead to various gastrointestinal issues. This condition is significant because it can affect nutrient absorption, increase the risk of stomach cancer, and lead to other serious health complications. Understanding atrophic gastritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring better health outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Atrophic gastritis may present with a variety of symptoms, which can range from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain : Discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting : Feelings of nausea and occasional vomiting.
Loss of Appetite : A decreased desire to eat, which can lead to weight loss.
Bloating and Gas : Increased bloating and flatulence after meals.
Indigestion : Difficulty digesting food, often accompanied by heartburn.

diseases.name: Atrophic Rhinitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atrophic rhinitis is a chronic nasal condition characterized by the thinning and inflammation of the nasal mucosa, leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This condition is often overlooked, yet it can cause discomfort and complications if not properly managed. Understanding atrophic rhinitis is essential for both patients and healthcare providers, as early recognition and treatment can help alleviate symptoms and prevent further complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of atrophic rhinitis can vary in severity and may include:
Nasal Obstruction: Difficulty breathing through the nose due to swelling and crusting.
Nasal Crusting: Formation of dry, crusty material in the nasal passages.
Foul Odor: A distinct, unpleasant smell emanating from the nasal cavity, often due to bacterial overgrowth.
Nasal Bleeding: Frequent nosebleeds due to the dryness and fragility of the nasal mucosa.
Altered Sense of Smell: Reduced or distorted sense of smell (hyposmia or dysosmia).

diseases.name: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: ADHD is a neurodevelopment disorder that negatively affects millions of children and adolescents’ social interaction capabilities and often lasts into adulthood. ADHD is characterized by a number of persistent difficulties, including difficulty in focusing, hyperactivity, and impulsive behavior.
symptoms: At some point in their life, most youngsters will have difficulties focusing and behaving. Children with ADHD on the other hand, do not simply grow out of their behaviours. The symptoms might last for weeks or months, causing difficulty at school, at home, and with friends.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

Having trouble focusing, sitting still, and remaining organized are common symptoms of ADHD. Many children show signs of this condition before they reach the age of seven, while some go undetected until they reach adulthood. The way the illness appears in men and women differs significantly. This may have an impact on how ADHD is identified and diagnosed.

According to the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, men are three times more likely than women to be diagnosed with ADHD. This gap isn’t always due to women’s lower susceptibility to the illness. It’s more than likely due to the fact that women’s ADHD symptoms differ from men. The symptoms are frequently milder, making them more difficult to detect.

diseases.name: Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia (ADH) is a condition that affects the breast tissue and is often discovered during routine mammograms or breast biopsies. While it is not breast cancer, ADH is considered a marker for an increased risk of developing breast cancer in the future. Understanding ADH is crucial for women, as it can influence screening practices and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia often does not present any noticeable symptoms. Many women are unaware they have the condition until it is discovered during a routine screening or biopsy. However, some potential symptoms may include:
Breast Lumps: A lump in the breast may be felt, but this is not always the case.
Changes in Breast Shape or Size: Some women may notice changes in the appearance of their breasts.
Nipple Discharge: Unusual discharge from the nipple may occur, although this is not common.

diseases.name: Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia (AEH) is a condition characterized by the abnormal thickening of the endometrium, the lining of the uterus, due to an overgrowth of cells. This condition is significant because it can be a precursor to endometrial cancer, making early detection and management crucial for women's health. Understanding AEH is essential for women, especially those at risk, as it can lead to serious health complications if left untreated.
symptoms: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: This is the most common symptom, which may include heavy periods, bleeding between periods, or postmenopausal bleeding.
Pelvic Pain: Some women may experience discomfort or pain in the pelvic region.
Menstrual Irregularities: Changes in the regularity or heaviness of menstrual cycles can occur.

diseases.name: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS) is a rare but serious condition that primarily affects the kidneys and can lead to life-threatening complications. It is characterized by the triad of hemolytic anemia, acute kidney injury, and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count). Understanding aHUS is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and the general public, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of aHUS, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of aHUS can vary widely but typically include:
Hemolytic Anemia: Fatigue, weakness, and pallor due to the destruction of red blood cells.
Thrombocytopenia: Easy bruising, bleeding gums, or petechiae (small red or purple spots on the skin).
Acute Kidney Injury: Decreased urine output, swelling in the legs and ankles, and elevated blood pressure.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain may occur, particularly during acute episodes.

diseases.name: Auditory Processing Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Auditory Processing Disorder (APD) is a complex condition that affects how the brain processes auditory information. It is significant because it can impact an individual's ability to understand spoken language, follow directions, and communicate effectively. This disorder can lead to challenges in academic performance, social interactions, and overall quality of life. Understanding APD is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly improve outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Individuals with APD may exhibit a range of symptoms, including:
Difficulty understanding spoken language, especially in noisy environments.
Trouble following multi-step directions.
Frequent requests for repetition or clarification.
Difficulty distinguishing between similar-sounding words.
Problems with reading and spelling.
Challenges in social situations due to misunderstandings.

diseases.name: Autism
diseases.description: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder. It belongs to a group of diseases called pervasive developmental disorders (PDD). It is characterized by impaired development in communication, social interaction, and behavior. Patients often exhibit repetitive, restricted and stereotyped behavior patterns/interests. It commonly manifests in childhood. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), boys are more affected than girls with autism and a 5:1 male to female ratio is observed. The cause of autism is unknown. Autism spectrum disorders include autism and related disorders. The degree of autism may vary from mild to severe. Profound intellectual disability is often seen in severely afflicted persons. The mortality rate is high in individuals with autism than normal average individuals, especially when they have diseases like seizures and co-existing infections. Autism has been confused with childhood psychosis previously and may have been misunderstood as a personality disorder in some adults. Both in adults and in children, vocational or educational programs are designed for optimal treatment of autism respectively. Unique mental-health and medical needs of people with autism are to be addressed so that they can have a good quality of life. Autism can cause stress for parents and family members, and financial, emotional and social challenges in a family. Educating the siblings and family members about autism will help the child to fare better at home or school.
symptoms: The period of normal development in a child, usually does not extend beyond six years of age. Autism symptoms typically become evident between 24 months and six years of age according to the Autism Society. The symptoms of autism may range from mild to severe. Some patients who have autism can manage to have a healthy functioning life without any setbacks. While in other severely affected individuals, a great impact can be observed in their lives.
Abnormal or impaired development of communication,
Marked delay in language and cognitive development,
Impaired social interaction,
The repeat of restricted activities, behaviors, and interests,
Signs of obsessive or antisocial behavior can also be seen.
If any of the below signs are seen in a child, the physician has to be contacted immediately for evaluation:
When no joyful expressions or smiles are seen, by six months or later
When facial expressions, smiles, and sounds are not perceived by nine months of age,
When no gestures such as pointing, showing, reaching or waving by 12 months of age,
The child does not respond when the child’s name is called or shouted,
The child does not respond to a sudden clap or sound,
When the child does not speak any words by 16 months of age,
When the child does not repeat or mimic by 24 months of age,
Loss of speech and social skills at any age of the child.
Autism Spectrum Diseases: Individuals with ASD may exhibit at least two of the following behavioral difficulties:
Insistence on sameness in routine or environment
Interests that are inflexible
Increased or decreased reactions to sensory stimuli
Repetitive sensory and motor behaviors
Asperger syndrome: This may be referred to as “high functioning autism.” In this, syndrome the patient usually lacks the cognitive problems and primary communication that characterize classic autism.

diseases.name: Autoimmune Disease: Types, Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The human body is like a fortress, and the immune system is the army that protects the fort from invaders such as bacteria and viruses. But when the army fails to identify the enemy, it starts attacking the fortress. Thus, the human body develops numerous diseases, such as lupus , multiple sclerosis , rheumatoid arthritis , psoriasis and many more. Such diseases are called autoimmune diseases. Patients with autoimmune diseases experience pain, fatigue , dizziness, rashes, depression , and other symptoms.
symptoms: Although there are various types of autoimmune diseases, most of them have common symptoms, such as the following:
Tiredness
Pain and inflammation of the joints
Skin issues
Pain in the abdominal and digestive issue
Recurring fever
Inflammation of the glands
Skin rashes
Difficulty concentrating
The symptoms of autoimmune hepatitis are as follows:
Tiredness, exhaustion, and lack of motivation
Yellowing of the skin
Pain in the joint and upper abdomen
Rashes, acne , and other skin conditions
Low appetite
Dark urine and light-coloured stools
Nausea and vomiting
Patients of Celiac disease experience the following symptoms:
Diarrhoea
Extreme pain in the joints, bones, and stomach
Excessive gas
If a person has Crohn’s disease, they may develop the following symptoms:
Low red blood cell count
Cramping and pain in the stomach
Extreme weight loss
Fever
Nausea
Pain in the joint and eye
Red, bumpy skin rashes
The symptoms of Grave’s disease are as follows:
Arrhythmia
Anxiety
Weight loss
Extreme sense of feeling hot
Increased sweating
Tiredness and muscle weakness
Hand tremors and shaking
Troubled sleeping
Hashimoto’s thyroiditis has the following symptoms:
Unexpected fatigue
Increased weight gain
Increased sense of feeling cold
Muscle cramps
Constipation
Stiffness in the joint
Hair loss
Heavy or irregular menstrual cycle
Slow heartbeat
Hives
Infertility
Multiple Sclerosis patients experience the following:
Weakness, numbness, and tingling
A sudden sensation of electrical shocks in the limbs and back
Dizziness
Issues with the vision
Troubled walking
Pernicious anaemia symptoms are as follows:
Pale skin
Depression
Cold, tingling, or numbness in the hands and feet
A red and swollen tongue
Cognitive disability
Diarrhea , bloating, and heartburn
Rheumatoid arthritis presents the following symptoms:
Fatigue
Pain in the muscles and joints
Low-grade fever
The symptoms of Sjogren’s syndrome are as follows:
Dryness in lips, skin, nasal passages, throat, and vagina
Inflammation in the salivary glands
Trouble swallowing
Changes in the sense of taste and smell
Headaches and stomach aches
Increase in dental activities
Eye infections
The symptoms of systemic lupus erythematosus are as follows:
Increased hair loss
Butterfly-shaped rashes across cheeks, nose, and eyelids
Lung and kidney issues
Inflammation and pain in the joints and muscles
Dry mouth , dry eyes, and painful mouth sores
Blood clots
The following are the symptoms of type 1 diabetes:
Frequent urination
Excessive thirst
Blurred vision
Unexplained and sudden weight loss
Increased hunger
Numbness and tingling in hands and feet
Dry skin
Sores
Increased infection
Patients of autoimmune hepatitis experience the following symptoms:
Discomfort in the abdomen
Enlarged liver and jaundice
Rashes on the skin
Unusual blood vessels
Minimal menstrual period
Joint pains

diseases.name: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA) is a rare but significant blood disorder characterized by the premature destruction of red blood cells due to the body's immune system mistakenly attacking them. This condition can lead to a variety of health issues, including fatigue, weakness, and more severe complications if left untreated. Understanding AIHA is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of AIHA can vary in severity and may include:
Fatigue: A common symptom due to reduced oxygen delivery to tissues.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin and mucous membranes.
Shortness of Breath: Especially during physical activity, due to decreased oxygen levels.
Rapid Heartbeat: The heart compensates for low red blood cell counts by beating faster.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to the buildup of bilirubin from the breakdown of red blood cells.
Dark Urine: Caused by the presence of hemoglobin or bilirubin.
Splenomegaly: Enlargement of the spleen, which may occur as it works harder to filter out damaged red blood cells.

diseases.name: Autonomic Neuropathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Autonomic neuropathy is a condition that affects the autonomic nervous system (ANS), which controls involuntary bodily functions such as heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and temperature regulation. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to a range of symptoms that can be both uncomfortable and debilitating. Understanding autonomic neuropathy is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can be associated with various underlying health issues, particularly diabetes.
symptoms: The symptoms of autonomic neuropathy can vary widely depending on which part of the autonomic nervous system is affected. Common symptoms include:
Cardiovascular Symptoms: Dizziness or fainting upon standing (orthostatic hypotension), rapid heart rate, or irregular heartbeats.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation.
Urinary Symptoms: Difficulty in bladder control, urinary retention, or frequent urination.
Sexual Dysfunction: Erectile dysfunction in men and decreased libido or vaginal dryness in women.
Sweating Abnormalities: Excessive sweating or lack of sweating.

diseases.name: Avascular Necrosis (Osteonecrosis)
diseases.description: Avascular necrosis, also called osteonecrosis, is bone death caused by reduced blood flow to the bone. When blood doesn't reach bone tissue, the bone begins to die and may eventually collapse. The hip is the most commonly affected joint, but avascular necrosis can also occur in the knee, shoulder, ankle, and wrist.
symptoms: Pain in the joint that may be mild at first and progressively worsens
Pain only when putting weight on the affected joint
Limited range of motion
Groin pain spreading to knee or buttock
Limping (if hip or knee affected)

diseases.name: Avascular Necrosis of Femoral Head - Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Bone is a living tissue and it needs blood supply to survive. If there is damage to one of the blood supply, bone may depend on the accessory blood supply for the survival. But certain bones in our body have precarious unidirectional blood supply like Head of femur, scaphoid, and talus.

diseases.name: Avnrt - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) is a common type of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) that affects the heart's electrical system. It is characterized by a rapid heart rate due to a reentrant circuit involving the atrioventricular (AV) node. While AVNRT is generally not life-threatening, it can significantly impact a person's quality of life and may lead to more serious complications if left untreated. Understanding AVNRT is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to lead healthier lives.
symptoms: The symptoms of AVNRT can vary in intensity and may include:
Palpitations: A sensation of a rapid or fluttering heartbeat.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Due to reduced blood flow during episodes of rapid heart rate.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain or Discomfort: May occur during episodes of tachycardia.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.

diseases.name: Avoidant Personality Disorder
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of Avoidant personality disorder include:
Low self esteem
Self-isolation
Sensitivity towards criticism and rejection
Feeling inferior and inadequate
Avoiding work and relationship that requires interaction
Social inhibition and shyness

diseases.name: Avulsed Tooth - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: An avulsed tooth is a dental emergency that occurs when a tooth is completely knocked out of its socket. This condition is significant not only because it can lead to immediate pain and discomfort but also because it can have long-term implications for oral health if not managed properly. Understanding the causes, symptoms, and treatment options for an avulsed tooth is crucial for anyone, as it can happen to anyone at any age, often due to accidents or sports injuries. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of avulsed teeth, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Immediate Pain: The most noticeable symptom is often severe pain at the site of the injury.
Bleeding: There may be bleeding from the socket where the tooth was located.
Swelling: The surrounding gum tissue may become swollen and tender.
Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to temperature changes or pressure may occur.

diseases.name: Avulsion Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Avulsion fractures are a specific type of bone injury that occurs when a fragment of bone is pulled away from the main bone mass by a tendon or ligament. This injury is significant because it can lead to pain, limited mobility, and long-term complications if not treated properly. Understanding avulsion fractures is crucial for athletes, active individuals, and anyone at risk of injury, as early recognition and appropriate management can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Pain: Sudden and severe pain at the site of the injury is the most common symptom.
Swelling: The affected area may become swollen and tender to the touch.
Bruising: Discoloration may occur around the injury site.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty moving the affected joint or limb is common.
Deformity: In some cases, the area may appear deformed or out of alignment.

diseases.name: Axenfeld Rieger Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Axenfeld Rieger Syndrome (ARS) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the development of the eyes, teeth, and facial structures. It is characterized by a range of ocular anomalies, including glaucoma, and can also lead to various systemic issues. Understanding ARS is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and families, as early detection and management can significantly improve quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Axenfeld Rieger Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Axenfeld Rieger Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but may include:

Ocular Symptoms: Glaucoma: Increased pressure in the eye, which can lead to vision loss if untreated. Anterior segment dysgenesis: Abnormal development of the eye's front structures, including the cornea and iris. Iridocorneal adhesions: Abnormal connections between the iris and cornea. Coloboma: A gap or defect in the eye structure.
Glaucoma: Increased pressure in the eye, which can lead to vision loss if untreated.
Anterior segment dysgenesis: Abnormal development of the eye's front structures, including the cornea and iris.
Iridocorneal adhesions: Abnormal connections between the iris and cornea.
Coloboma: A gap or defect in the eye structure.
Dental Anomalies: Missing teeth or abnormal tooth development. Malocclusion or misalignment of teeth.
Missing teeth or abnormal tooth development.
Malocclusion or misalignment of teeth.
Facial Features: Distinctive facial features, such as a flat nasal bridge or widely spaced eyes. Other craniofacial anomalies may also be present.
Distinctive facial features, such as a flat nasal bridge or widely spaced eyes.
Other craniofacial anomalies may also be present.

diseases.name: Azoospermia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Azoospermia is a medical condition characterized by the absence of sperm in a man's ejaculate. This condition is significant as it is one of the leading causes of male infertility, affecting approximately 1% of the male population and up to 15% of infertile men. Understanding azoospermia is crucial for couples trying to conceive, as it can impact their reproductive options and emotional well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of azoospermia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Azoospermia itself may not present with obvious symptoms, as many men may not experience any noticeable signs. However, some men may encounter symptoms related to underlying conditions, such as:
Hormonal Imbalances: Changes in libido, erectile dysfunction, or gynecomastia (enlarged breast tissue).
Testicular Issues: Swelling, pain, or lumps in the testicular area.
Sexual Dysfunction: Difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection.

diseases.name: Azotemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Azotemia is a medical condition characterized by an elevated level of nitrogenous waste products, particularly urea and creatinine, in the blood. This condition is significant because it often indicates underlying kidney dysfunction, which can lead to serious health complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding azotemia is crucial for early detection and management, as it can serve as a warning sign for more severe renal issues, including acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease.
symptoms: Azotemia may not present with noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms can occur due to the buildup of toxins in the blood.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat can be a result of nausea or changes in metabolism.
Swelling: Fluid retention may lead to swelling in the legs, ankles, or around the eyes.
Changes in Urination: This may include decreased urine output or changes in urine color.

diseases.name: B Cell Lymphoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: B Cell Lymphoma is a type of cancer that originates in the B cells, which are a crucial part of the immune system. These cells are responsible for producing antibodies that help the body fight infections. B Cell Lymphoma is significant not only because of its impact on the immune system but also due to its varying forms, which can range from indolent (slow-growing) to aggressive (fast-growing). Understanding B Cell Lymphoma is essential for early detection, effective treatment, and improving patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of B Cell Lymphoma can vary widely depending on the type and stage of the disease. Common symptoms include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Painless swelling in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Fever: Unexplained fevers that may come and go.
Night Sweats: Profuse sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss without changes in diet or exercise.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Itching: Generalized itching without a rash.

diseases.name: Baby Acne - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Baby acne, also known as neonatal acne, is a common skin condition that affects many infants in their first few months of life. While it can be concerning for new parents, it is generally harmless and often resolves on its own. Understanding baby acne is essential for parents to differentiate it from other skin conditions and to know when to seek medical advice. This article will provide a detailed overview of baby acne, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of baby acne are usually mild and include:
Small red or white bumps on the face, particularly on the cheeks, forehead, and chin.
Pustules or papules that may resemble teenage acne.
No associated itching or discomfort for the infant.

diseases.name: Back Pain
diseases.description: Back pain is one of the most common medical problems, affecting most people at some point in their lives. It can range from a dull, constant ache to a sudden, sharp sensation that leaves a person incapacitated. Pain can be classified as acute (less than 6 weeks), sub-chronic (6–12 weeks), or chronic (more than 12 weeks). Most back pain is mechanical in nature.
symptoms: Muscle ache
Shooting or stabbing pain
Pain that radiates down your leg
Pain that worsens with bending, lifting, standing, or walking
Pain that improves with reclining
Numbness or tingling
Leg weakness

diseases.name: Back Spasms: Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: A back spasm is an involuntary contraction or straining of the muscles in the lower back. This condition varies from infrequent spasms with mild discomfort to chronic spasms with severe pain making it difficult to move.

diseases.name: Bacteremia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bacteremia is a medical condition characterized by the presence of bacteria in the bloodstream. While it may sound alarming, it is essential to understand its significance, causes, symptoms, and treatment options. Bacteremia can lead to severe health complications, including sepsis, if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bacteremia, making it accessible for a general audience while ensuring medical accuracy.
symptoms: The symptoms of bacteremia can vary widely, but common signs include:
Fever: A high fever is often one of the first signs of bacteremia.
Chills: Patients may experience chills or shivering.
Rapid Heart Rate: An increased heart rate can occur as the body responds to infection.
Fatigue: Generalized weakness and fatigue are common.
Nausea and Vomiting: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal symptoms.

diseases.name: Bacterial Meningitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bacterial meningitis is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition that affects the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, known as the meninges. This infection can lead to severe complications, including brain damage, hearing loss, and even death if not treated promptly. Understanding bacterial meningitis is crucial for early detection and effective management, making it a significant public health concern.
symptoms: The symptoms of bacterial meningitis can develop rapidly, often within hours to a few days. Common symptoms include:
Fever : A high fever is often one of the first signs.
Severe Headache : A sudden and intense headache that may be different from typical headaches.
Stiff Neck : Difficulty bending the neck forward, often accompanied by pain.
Nausea and Vomiting : These symptoms may occur alongside headaches.
Sensitivity to Light : Photophobia, or discomfort in bright light, is common.
Altered Mental Status : Confusion, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating may occur.

diseases.name: Bacterial Vaginosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bacterial Vaginosis (BV) is a common vaginal condition that affects many women worldwide. It occurs when there is an imbalance in the normal bacteria found in the vagina, leading to an overgrowth of certain types of bacteria. While BV is not classified as a sexually transmitted infection (STI), it can have significant implications for women's health, including increased susceptibility to STIs, complications during pregnancy, and potential impacts on overall reproductive health. Understanding BV is crucial for effective management and prevention, making it essential for women to be informed about this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of Bacterial Vaginosis can vary, but common signs include:
Unusual Vaginal Discharge: This may be thin, gray, or white in color and can have a fishy odor, especially after sexual intercourse.
Vaginal Odor: A strong, fishy smell is often associated with BV, particularly after sexual activity.
Itching or Irritation: Some women may experience discomfort or itching in the vaginal area.

diseases.name: Bakers Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A Baker's cyst, also known as a popliteal cyst, is a fluid-filled sac that forms behind the knee. It is often associated with knee joint conditions, such as arthritis or meniscus tears, and can lead to discomfort and mobility issues. Understanding Baker's cyst is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Common symptoms of a Baker's cyst include:
Swelling: A noticeable bulge behind the knee, which may feel soft or firm.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the knee, especially when bending or straightening the leg.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the knee joint.
Tightness: A feeling of tightness or pressure behind the knee.

diseases.name: Balanitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Balanitis is a medical condition that affects the glans (the head) of the penis, leading to inflammation and discomfort. While it may not be a widely discussed topic, its significance lies in its potential to cause pain, discomfort, and complications if left untreated. Understanding balanitis is crucial for both men and their partners, as it can impact sexual health and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of balanitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of balanitis can vary in severity and may include:
Redness and Swelling: The glans may appear inflamed and swollen.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many individuals report discomfort, especially during urination or sexual activity.
Pain: Pain may be localized to the glans or may radiate to the surrounding areas.
Discharge: There may be a discharge from the penis, which can be clear, cloudy, or purulent.
Foul Odor: An unpleasant smell may accompany the discharge.

diseases.name: Balanoposthitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Balanoposthitis is a medical condition that affects the male genital area, specifically the glans (the head of the penis) and the foreskin. This inflammation can lead to discomfort, pain, and various other symptoms that can significantly impact a man's quality of life. Understanding balanoposthitis is crucial not only for those who may experience it but also for healthcare providers who need to recognize and treat this condition effectively. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of balanoposthitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of balanoposthitis can vary in severity and may include:
Redness and Swelling: Inflammation of the glans and foreskin.
Pain or Discomfort: Pain during urination or sexual activity.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Commonly reported by those affected.
Discharge: A thick, white discharge (smegma) may be present.
Foul Odor: An unpleasant smell can arise from the accumulation of smegma or infection.

diseases.name: Band Keratopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Band keratopathy is a condition that affects the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. It is characterized by the deposition of calcium in the cornea, leading to a band-like appearance. This condition can significantly impact vision and quality of life, making it essential for individuals to understand its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. In this article, we will explore band keratopathy in detail, providing a comprehensive overview that is easy to understand for the general audience.
symptoms: Individuals with band keratopathy may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Blurred Vision: The calcium deposits can interfere with light entering the eye, leading to blurred or distorted vision.
Eye Discomfort: Some individuals may experience a sensation of grittiness or discomfort in the eye.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to bright lights or glare is common.
Redness: The eye may appear red or inflamed due to irritation.

diseases.name: Barotrauma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Barotrauma is a medical condition that occurs when there is a significant difference between the pressure inside a body cavity and the external environment. This condition is particularly relevant for individuals who engage in activities that involve rapid changes in pressure, such as scuba diving, flying, or even certain medical procedures. Understanding barotrauma is crucial, as it can lead to serious complications if not recognized and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of barotrauma, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of barotrauma can vary depending on the affected area but commonly include:
Ear Pain: A feeling of fullness or pressure in the ears, often accompanied by sharp pain.
Hearing Loss: Temporary or permanent hearing impairment may occur due to damage to the eardrum or inner ear structures.
Nasal Congestion: Difficulty breathing through the nose, often due to swollen nasal passages.
Sinus Pain: Discomfort or pain in the forehead, cheeks, or around the eyes.
Coughing or Wheezing: Respiratory symptoms may arise if the lungs are affected.
Gastrointestinal Distress: Nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain can occur if the gastrointestinal tract is involved.

diseases.name: Barrett's Esophagus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Barrett's Esophagus is a condition that affects the lining of the esophagus, the tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach. This condition is significant because it can increase the risk of developing esophageal cancer, a serious and often deadly disease. Understanding Barrett's Esophagus is crucial for early detection and management, which can significantly improve outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Many individuals with Barrett's Esophagus may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some common symptoms include:
Heartburn: A burning sensation in the chest, often after eating.
Regurgitation: The sensation of acid backing up into the throat or mouth.
Difficulty Swallowing: A feeling that food is stuck in the throat or chest.
Chest Pain: Discomfort that may mimic heart-related issues.

diseases.name: Bartholin Abscess: Causes, Diagnosis, and Treatments
diseases.description: The Bartholin glands are present on each side of the vaginal entrance. These glands produce a lubricating fluid that helps to keep the vaginal area lubricated. These glands’ openings can become clogged, allowing fluid to back up into the gland. This causes a bartholin’s CYST which is painless.
symptoms: The cyst usually occurs on only one side of the vaginal opening. Once the cyst grows, a lump or mass appears in the opening of the vaginal. The cyst can get infected in a few days. A cyst infection shows the following symptoms:
Painful and tender lump near the vaginal opening
Causes discomfort while walking and sitting
Pain during intercourse
Fever

diseases.name: Bartholin Cysts – All you wanted to Know
diseases.description: Our body consists of multiple glands and ducts that secrete fluids. A cyst is formed when these ducts get blocked leading to fluid obstruction. Bartholin Cyst usually results due to obstruction of Bartholin glands.
symptoms: The sign and symptoms depend on the shape and size of the cysts. It may be initially small and can later increase in size (size of a golf ball).
