At first, you might feel a slightly enlarged swelling or a lump around the vaginal opening. It can be somewhat tender to touch but is usually painless. Later cysts may get infected and painful.
On examination, there is usually:
● Tender and painful mass near vaginal pillars
● High-grade fever
● General discomfort
● Inability to sit

diseases.name: Barton Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Barton Fracture is a specific type of wrist fracture that occurs at the distal end of the radius, characterized by a fracture that extends into the joint surface of the wrist. This injury is significant not only because of its impact on wrist function but also due to its potential complications if not treated properly. Understanding Barton Fracture is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely diagnosis and appropriate management can lead to better outcomes.
symptoms: Severe Pain: Immediate and intense pain in the wrist area.
Swelling: Noticeable swelling around the wrist joint.
Bruising: Discoloration may appear due to bleeding under the skin.
Deformity: The wrist may appear deformed or out of alignment.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the wrist or hand.

diseases.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common type of skin cancer, usually developing in areas exposed to the sun such as the face, ears, and neck. While it tends to grow slowly and rarely spreads, early detection and treatment are key to preventing complications. This guide provides clear and reliable information about BCC—its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what you can expect along the way. Written in simple, patient-friendly language, our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and confident as you take steps to manage your skin health.
symptoms: The symptoms of basal cell carcinoma can be subtle and are often mistaken for other common skin conditions. A key characteristic to look for is a spot that does not heal, or that bleeds and then scabs over and then bleeds again.

diseases.name: Basophilia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Basophilia is a medical condition characterized by an elevated level of basophils, a type of white blood cell, in the bloodstream. Basophils play a crucial role in the immune system, particularly in allergic reactions and responses to parasitic infections. Understanding basophilia is significant because it can be an indicator of underlying health issues, ranging from benign conditions to more serious diseases. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of basophilia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Basophilia itself may not present specific symptoms, but it can be associated with various underlying conditions. Common symptoms may include:
Allergic Reactions: Symptoms such as itching, hives, or swelling may occur in response to allergens.
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue can be a symptom of underlying conditions associated with basophilia.
Fever: Infections that lead to basophilia may cause fever as part of the body’s immune response.
Respiratory Issues: Conditions like asthma or allergic rhinitis may present with respiratory symptoms.

diseases.name: Batten Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Batten Disease, also known as neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL), is a rare and progressive neurological disorder that primarily affects children. It is characterized by the accumulation of lipopigments in the body's tissues, leading to a decline in cognitive and motor functions. The significance of Batten Disease lies not only in its devastating impact on affected individuals and their families but also in the challenges it presents to medical professionals in terms of diagnosis and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Batten Disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Batten Disease symptoms can vary depending on the specific type and the age of onset. Common symptoms include:
Vision Loss: One of the earliest signs, often leading to blindness.
Seizures: Frequent seizures can occur as the disease progresses.
Cognitive Decline: Affected children may experience learning difficulties, memory loss, and behavioral changes.
Motor Skills Deterioration: Loss of coordination and motor skills, leading to difficulty walking and performing daily activities.
Speech Difficulties: Children may struggle with speech and language development.
Personality Changes: Mood swings, irritability, and changes in behavior are common.

diseases.name: Beckwith Wiedemann Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome (BWS) is a complex genetic disorder that affects various aspects of growth and development in children. It is characterized by a range of physical features and an increased risk of certain medical conditions. Understanding BWS is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary significantly from one individual to another. Common symptoms include:
Macrosomia: Increased birth weight and length.
Macroglossia: An enlarged tongue, which can affect feeding and speech.
Omphalocele: A condition where abdominal organs protrude through the abdominal wall.
Hemihyperplasia: Asymmetrical growth of one side of the body.
Facial Features: Distinctive facial features, such as a prominent forehead and ear abnormalities.
Increased Risk of Tumors: Particularly Wilms tumor (kidney cancer) and hepatoblastoma (liver cancer).

diseases.name: Bed Sores (Pressure Ulcers): Causes, Stages, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Bed sores, also called pressure ulcers or decubitus ulcers, are painful injuries to the skin and underlying tissue caused by prolonged pressure on a particular area of the body. They typically develop on bony areas like the hips, tailbone, heels, elbows, and back—especially in people who are bedridden, immobile, or spend long periods sitting or lying down.
symptoms: Recognizing the early warning signs can prevent complications. Watch out for:
Unusual redness or discoloration of the skin
Skin that feels warmer or cooler than the surrounding area
Pain, burning, or itching over pressure points
Swelling or hard patches on the skin
Open sores, blisters, or pus-filled wounds in later stages
For patients who are non-verbal or unconscious, it’s especially important that family members or nurses inspect the skin daily.

diseases.name: Behçet's Disease
diseases.description: Behçet's disease is a rare disorder that causes blood vessel inflammation throughout the body. This can lead to numerous signs and symptoms that can seem unrelated at first. The disease can cause mouth sores, eye inflammation, skin rashes, and lesions, and genital sores. It is also known as Behçet's syndrome or Silk Road disease.
symptoms: Mouth sores (canker sores)
Skin lesions
Genital sores
Eye inflammation (uveitis)
Joint pain and swelling
Blood clots
CNS symptoms (headache, dizziness)

diseases.name: Belly Button Yeast Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Belly button yeast infections, while not commonly discussed, can be a source of discomfort and concern for many individuals. These infections occur when an overgrowth of yeast, typically Candida , develops in the belly button area. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can lead to various symptoms and complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of belly button yeast infections, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of a belly button yeast infection can vary in severity but often include:
Itching: A persistent itch around the belly button area.
Redness and Inflammation: The skin may appear red and swollen.
Discharge: A thick, white discharge may be present, resembling cottage cheese.
Odor: An unpleasant odor may emanate from the affected area.
Pain or Discomfort: Some individuals may experience pain, especially when touching the area.

diseases.name: Bell’s Palsy - Symptoms, Causes, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: Bell’s Palsy is commonly known as Idiopathic Facial Palsy. It is a condition that causes paralysis and temporary weakness on one side of the face.
symptoms: The onset of Bell’s Palsy symptoms is sudden, and you might notice them when you wake up in morning or when you try to eat or drink.

The primary symptom of the condition is drooping, along with difficulty in opening or closing the eye of the side that is affected. Other signs or symptoms of Bell’s Palsy that you must look out for include:
Facial weakness
Dry mouth or eye
Sound sensitivity
Headache
Difficulty drinking or eating
Inability to make or change facial expressions
Drooling
Eye irritation
Twitching of the facial muscles

If you are experiencing any of these symptoms, you must get immediate medical attention. Many of these symptoms overlap with those of a stroke or brain tumor . These conditions are more serious and life-threatening.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Benign Blood Disorders - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Benign (non-cancerous) blood disorders are conditions that affect the blood but are not classified as cancer. Unlike many other illnesses, these disorders may not cause obvious symptoms right away and are sometimes discovered during routine check-ups. This guide provides clear and reliable information about benign blood disorders---their types, common symptoms, how they are diagnosed, and the treatment options available. Understanding these conditions can help patients and families feel more informed and better prepared to manage them.
symptoms: The symptoms of benign blood disorders can vary widely depending on the specific condition. In many cases, a person may have no symptoms, and the condition is only discovered during a routine blood test. When symptoms do appear, they are often a result of a shortage of healthy blood cells.
Fatigue and Weakness: The most common symptom, caused by a lack of oxygen being carried to the body's tissues.
Pale Skin (Pallor): A lack of red blood cells can make your skin look pale or "washed out."
Shortness of Breath: Feeling winded after minimal exertion.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness
Cold Hands and Feet
Headaches
Irregular Heartbeat
Easy Bruising: Unexplained or large bruises.
Frequent Nosebleeds
Bleeding Gums
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding
Tiny, Red Pinprick Spots Under the Skin (Petechiae)
Swelling, Pain, or Tenderness in a Leg or Arm
Shortness of Breath or Chest Pain (if a blood clot travels to the lungs)
If you have any of these persistent symptoms, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.

diseases.name: Benign Fasciculation Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Benign Fasciculation Syndrome (BFS) is a neurological condition characterized by involuntary muscle twitches, known as fasciculations. While the term "benign" suggests that the condition is not harmful, it can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected. Understanding BFS is crucial for patients and their families, as it helps demystify the symptoms and provides a pathway for effective management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of BFS, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of BFS is muscle twitching, which can occur in any muscle group but is most commonly observed in the arms, legs, and eyelids. Other symptoms may include:
Muscle Cramps: Sudden, involuntary contractions of muscles.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Anxiety: Many individuals with BFS report heightened anxiety levels, which can further exacerbate symptoms.
Numbness or Tingling: Some may experience sensations of pins and needles in affected areas.

diseases.name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), its Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Most individuals have experienced dizziness at least once in their lives. It can be due to various reasons, including changes in blood pressure, exhaustion, and other underlying medical conditions. However, one of the common causes of dizziness is benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). The disorder of the inner ear causes a sudden spinning sensation whenever a person moves their head. It is not a severe health condition. If it does not resolve on its own, a simple outpatient procedure can alleviate the symptoms.
symptoms: The symptoms can occur any time of the day, whenever a person changes the position of their head. Also, the symptoms may occur periodically and last for less than a minute. The most common symptom is dizziness which may lead to loss of balance and falls. The other symptoms may include the following:
A sensation that the surrounding is spinning
Nausea
Vomiting
Unsteadiness
Light-headedness
Vertigo
Blurred vision
Dehydration , in severe cases
Rapid and involuntary eye movement

diseases.name: Benign Tumor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Benign tumors are non-cancerous growths that can develop in various tissues throughout the body. While they are generally not life-threatening, their presence can lead to discomfort, complications, or even significant health issues depending on their size and location. Understanding benign tumors is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their health and well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of benign tumors can vary widely depending on their location and size. Common symptoms may include:
Lumps or Masses: Noticeable growths under the skin or in organs.
Pain or Discomfort: Pressure on surrounding tissues can cause pain.
Changes in Function: Tumors in organs may disrupt normal function, leading to symptoms like difficulty breathing or digestive issues.

diseases.name: Beriberi : Types, Symptoms, Diagnosis And Treatment
diseases.description: Healthy food nourishes our bodies. It protects us from diseases and illnesses. But, sometimes, people may not get the required nutrition for numerous reasons. A deficiency in vitamins, proteins, minerals, and other nutrients may lead to disorders. One such disorder is Beriberi – caused due to vitamin B-1 deficiency.
symptoms: The symptoms of dry Beriberi are different than that of wet Beriberi. The symptoms of dry Beriberi are as follows:
Troubled walking
Loss of sensation in the hands and feet
Decrease muscle function or paralysis of the lower legs
Confusion or speech impairment
Extreme pain
Bizarre eye movements
Tingling sensations
Vomiting
paralysis
The symptoms of wet Beriberi include the following:
Suddenly getting up at night with shortness of breath
Increased heart rate
Shortness of breath when performing activities
Swollen lower legs
In severe cases, Beriberi is linked to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, two different types of brain damage resulting from thiamine deficiency.
Wernicke encephalopathy is responsible for damaging brain regions known as the thalamus and hypothalamus. It can lead to:
Confusion
Loss of memory
Decreased muscle coordination
Vision issues such as double vision or rapid eye movement
Korsakoff syndrome is due to the permanent damage caused to the region of the brain where memories are formed. It causes the following:
Memory loss
Inability to create and develop new memories
hallucinations

diseases.name: Bernard Soulier Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bernard Soulier Syndrome (BSS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot properly. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious health complications, including excessive bleeding and bruising. Understanding BSS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected. In this article, we will explore the various aspects of Bernard Soulier Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Bernard Soulier Syndrome can vary in severity and may include:
Easy Bruising: Individuals may notice unexplained bruises on their skin.
Frequent Nosebleeds: Recurrent nosebleeds can occur without any apparent cause.
Prolonged Bleeding: Cuts or injuries may take longer to stop bleeding than in individuals without the disorder.
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Women may experience heavier than normal menstrual periods (menorrhagia).
Gum Bleeding: Bleeding from the gums, especially during brushing or flossing, is common.

diseases.name: Beta Thalassemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Beta Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder that affects the body’s ability to produce hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen throughout the body. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on individual health but also due to its prevalence in certain populations. Understanding Beta Thalassemia is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Beta Thalassemia can vary widely depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Due to anemia, individuals often feel tired and weak.
Pale Skin: A lack of red blood cells can lead to paleness.
Shortness of Breath: Reduced oxygen transport can cause difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes may occur due to increased breakdown of red blood cells.
Enlarged Spleen or Liver: The body may work harder to produce red blood cells, leading to organ enlargement.
Bone Deformities: In severe cases, the bone marrow expands, leading to changes in bone structure.

diseases.name: Bicep Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bicep tendonitis is a common condition that affects the tendons connecting the biceps muscle to the shoulder and elbow. This condition can lead to pain, discomfort, and reduced mobility, significantly impacting daily activities and quality of life. Understanding bicep tendonitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their normal routines with minimal disruption.
symptoms: Pain: A dull ache in the front of the shoulder, which may worsen with overhead activities or lifting.
Tenderness: Sensitivity in the biceps tendon area, especially when pressure is applied.
Swelling: Mild swelling around the shoulder joint may occur.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty in moving the arm, particularly when lifting or reaching overhead.
Crepitus: A crackling or popping sensation during shoulder movement.

diseases.name: Bicornuate Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A bicornuate uterus is a congenital uterine anomaly characterized by a uterus that has two distinct horns instead of a single, pear-shaped cavity. This condition arises during fetal development when the Müllerian ducts, which form the female reproductive tract, fail to fuse completely. Understanding a bicornuate uterus is crucial for women’s health, as it can impact fertility, pregnancy outcomes, and overall reproductive health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bicornuate uterus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many women with a bicornuate uterus may not experience any symptoms. However, some common symptoms can include:
Irregular Menstrual Cycles: Some women may experience changes in their menstrual patterns.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic region may occur, particularly during menstruation.
Reproductive Challenges: Difficulties in conceiving, recurrent miscarriages, or preterm labor may be experienced by some women.

diseases.name: Bicuspid Aortic Valve - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The heart is a complex organ with several components working in harmony to ensure proper blood circulation throughout the body. One of these components is the aortic valve, which plays a crucial role in regulating blood flow from the heart to the aorta and, subsequently, to the rest of the body. A common condition affecting this valve is known as a bicuspid aortic valve. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bicuspid aortic valve, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many individuals with a bicuspid aortic valve may not experience symptoms until complications arise. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or at rest.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may be mistaken for angina.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy, especially during exertion.
Heart Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.
Dizziness or Fainting: Lightheadedness or loss of consciousness, particularly during physical activity.

diseases.name: Bifascicular Block - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bifascicular Block (BFB) is a type of heart conduction disorder that affects the electrical pathways in the heart. It is characterized by a delay or blockage in the conduction of electrical impulses through two of the three main fascicles of the heart's conduction system. This condition is significant because it can lead to various cardiac complications, including arrhythmias and heart failure, if not properly managed. Understanding Bifascicular Block is crucial for early detection and treatment, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Bifascicular Block may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Due to irregular heartbeats, patients may feel faint or dizzy.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats can be a common symptom.
Fatigue: Reduced cardiac efficiency may lead to feelings of tiredness or exhaustion.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during exertion, can occur.
Chest Pain: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the chest.

diseases.name: Bifid Uvula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bifid uvula is a condition characterized by a split or forked uvula, the small, fleshy structure that hangs at the back of the throat. While it may seem like a minor anatomical variation, bifid uvula can have significant implications for an individual's health, particularly concerning speech, swallowing, and the risk of certain medical conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bifid uvula, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: In many cases, bifid uvula does not present any noticeable symptoms. However, some individuals may experience:
Speech Difficulties: A bifid uvula can affect the articulation of certain sounds, leading to speech delays or disorders.
Swallowing Issues: Some individuals may have difficulty swallowing, particularly if the bifid uvula is associated with other palate abnormalities.
Increased Risk of Infections: A bifid uvula may be linked to a higher incidence of ear infections or respiratory issues.

diseases.name: Bile Acid Malabsorption - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bile Acid Malabsorption (BAM) is a condition that affects the body's ability to properly absorb bile acids, which are crucial for the digestion and absorption of fats and fat-soluble vitamins in the intestines. This condition can lead to a range of gastrointestinal symptoms and can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding BAM is essential for both patients and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can alleviate symptoms and prevent complications.
symptoms: Bile Acid Malabsorption can manifest through various symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Chronic Diarrhea: Frequent, watery stools are the hallmark of BAM.
Abdominal Pain and Cramping: Discomfort in the abdomen can occur, often associated with bowel movements.
Bloating and Gas: Increased gas production and a feeling of fullness can accompany BAM.
Fatty Stools (Steatorrhea): Stools may appear greasy or float due to undigested fats.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to malabsorption of nutrients.

diseases.name: Bile Duct Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Bile duct cancer, also known as cholangiocarcinoma, is a rare but serious type of cancer. It develops in the tubes that carry bile (a fluid helping digest fats) from the liver and gallbladder to the small intestine. Because it often causes no symptoms early, it is usually detected late.
symptoms: Early stages may show no clear warning signs. As the disease progresses, symptoms become more noticeable:
Unexplained weight loss
Loss of appetite
Fatigue and weakness
Fever and night sweats
Enlarged liver or gallbladder felt during an exam
Since many of these symptoms overlap with other liver or gallbladder conditions, it is important not to ignore them and consult a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Bile Reflux - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bile reflux is a condition that occurs when bile, a digestive fluid produced by the liver, flows back into the stomach and esophagus. This can lead to a range of uncomfortable symptoms and may significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding bile reflux is crucial, as it can be mistaken for other gastrointestinal disorders, such as acid reflux or gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bile reflux, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Bile reflux can manifest through various symptoms, including:
Nausea: A frequent feeling of wanting to vomit.
Vomiting: This may include bile, which is a yellow-green fluid.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen.
Heartburn: A burning sensation in the chest, often mistaken for acid reflux.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Loss of Appetite: Reduced desire to eat, often due to nausea or discomfort.

diseases.name: Biliary Stricture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Biliary stricture is a medical condition that involves the narrowing of the bile ducts, which are essential for transporting bile from the liver to the small intestine. This condition can lead to significant health issues, including jaundice, infections, and liver damage. Understanding biliary stricture is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life and overall health.
symptoms: Biliary stricture can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels.
Dark Urine: A result of excess bilirubin being excreted through urine.
Pale Stools: Lack of bile reaching the intestines can lead to lighter-colored stools.
Itching: Accumulation of bile salts in the bloodstream can cause itching.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper right abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Digestive disturbances may occur due to bile obstruction.

diseases.name: Binder Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Binder Syndrome, also known as Binder's Syndrome or Binder's malformation, is a rare congenital condition that primarily affects the development of the facial structure. This syndrome is significant not only because of its physical manifestations but also due to its psychological and social implications for those affected. Understanding Binder Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for individuals living with this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of Binder Syndrome can vary widely among individuals, but common features include:
Flat Nasal Bridge: One of the hallmark signs of Binder Syndrome is a noticeably flat nasal bridge, which can affect facial aesthetics.
Underdeveloped Maxilla: The upper jaw may be smaller than normal, leading to dental and alignment issues.
Facial Asymmetry: Some individuals may exhibit asymmetrical facial features.
Dental Anomalies: Malocclusion or other dental issues may arise due to the underdevelopment of the jaw.
Hearing Impairment: In some cases, individuals may experience hearing loss due to structural abnormalities in the ear.

diseases.name: Bipolar Disorder: Types, Causes, Symptoms, Treatment
diseases.description: Fluctuations in moods like feeling sad, happy or anxious are normal. But it becomes a cause of concern when mood swings happen frequently and intensely. These mood swings define bipolar disorder, and it is essential to identify which ones are natural and which need medical attention. This blog is a comprehensive guide on bipolar disorder, its symptoms, causes and treatment options available.
symptoms: A person who experiences bipolar disorder may feature high levels of energy, impulsivity, and enthusiasm, although hypomania is seen as less severe than mania. Mania symptoms can interfere with daily activities and cause issues at work or home. But this may not happen for patients with hypomania. Mania, hypomania, and depression are the three primary signs and symptoms of bipolar illness. These symptoms can appear in various ways in different bipolar disorder types.

Bipolar I: In this case, the patient may have experienced a minimum of one manic episode, which may be preceded or followed by severe depression or hypomanic episodes. Mania may occasionally make the patients dissociate from reality, also known as psychosis.
Bipolar II : Patients with bipolar II disorder may not have experienced multiple manic episodes. Instead, they must have had a minimum of one episode of major depression and one hypomanic episode.
Cyclothymic disorder : Patients with this type of disorder must have experienced numerous less severe hypomania symptoms and periods of depressive episodes for at least two years.

Other kinds of disorders : Bipolar illness and other associated disorders can also be brought on by certain drugs, alcohol or by a physical condition such as multiple sclerosis , stroke or Cushing’s disease.

It is difficult to spot signs of bipolar disorder in children. It can be challenging to determine whether these mood swings are typical of their growth, the effect of stress or trauma , or an indication of a mental health issue.

Major depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes may differ in children and teenagers, although the pattern may vary from that in adults with bipolar disorder. And while having an episode, feelings can change quickly. Between episodes, some kids may even have a period without mood problems.
So, identifying severe mood swings that differ from their typical mood swings is one of the ways of identifying bipolar disorder in children and teenagers.

diseases.name: Bird Flu (Avian Influenza) Infection – Symptoms, Causes, and Diagnosis
diseases.description: As the country still grapples with the COVID-19 pandemic including its recent new variant, another health issue seems to have taken hold , as cases of bird flu have been confirmed (on 5 th Jan’ 2021) in four Indian states so far: Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh. The bird flu is a disease which can be transmitted to human beings and become fatal.
symptoms: The reported symptoms of bird flu (avian influenza ) infection in humans have ranged from mild to severe and may start within two to seven days, depending on the type. In most cases, symptoms resemble those of common flu, like:
Sore throat
Cough
Headache
Muscle aches
Fever

Some people may also experience diarrhea , nausea , vomiting , abdominal pain , or severe respiratory complications like pneumonia difficulty breathing , acute , respiratory distress , respiratory failure , etc.
And in certain cases, conjunctivitis (a mild eye infection) may be the only indication of this disease.

diseases.name: Black Hairy Tongue - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Black hairy tongue , medically known as lingua villosa, is a benign condition characterized by an abnormal appearance of the tongue. This condition can be alarming for those who experience it, as it often presents with a dark, hairy appearance due to the elongation of the filiform papillae on the tongue's surface. While it is not a serious health concern, understanding its significance, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for effective management and prevention.
symptoms: The primary symptom of black hairy tongue is the appearance of the tongue itself. It may appear dark, brown, or black, with a hairy texture. Other symptoms may include:
Bad Breath: The accumulation of bacteria can lead to halitosis.
Altered Taste: Some individuals may experience changes in their sense of taste.
Discomfort: While not typically painful, some may feel a sensation of fullness or discomfort on the tongue.

diseases.name: Blackheads - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Blackheads are a common skin concern that affects individuals of all ages, genders, and ethnicities. They are a type of acne that occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil, dead skin cells, and bacteria. While blackheads are not harmful, they can be a source of frustration and embarrassment for many people. Understanding blackheads, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for effective management and prevention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of blackheads, helping readers gain insight into this prevalent skin condition.
symptoms: The primary symptom of blackheads is the presence of small, dark bumps on the skin. These bumps may vary in size and can appear on various parts of the body, including the face, neck, back, and shoulders. Blackheads are typically painless and do not cause inflammation, unlike other forms of acne.

diseases.name: Bladder cancer – Symptoms and Causes
diseases.description: Bladder cancer is one of the most common cancers among both men and women. It occurs when the cells of your urinary bladder grow uncontrollably. It can be seen commonly in people who are over 55 years of age, making up about 90% of diagnosed cases. Bladder cancer often spreads to various other regions of the body like lungs, bones, and liver. Here are some of the symptoms and causes of bladder cancer.
symptoms: The first sign of bladder cancer is blood in the urine with no pain while urinating. Numerous symptoms exist as an indication for bladder cancer like fatigue, weight loss, and bone tenderness. However, the following are more specific symptoms:
Blood in the urine ( hematuria )
Painful urination
Urgent urination
Urinary incontinence
Pain in the abdominal area
Pain in the lower back
Blood or blood clots in the urine
Pain or burning sensation during urination
Frequent urination
lynch syndrome
Sensing the need to urinate throughout the night
Not being able to pass urine
Lower back pain on 1 side of the body
If your bladder cancer advances, you may also experience some other symptoms including:
Swelling of the lower legs
Pain in the lower back in the area near the kidneys
Pelvic growths in the area of the bladder
You may also sense some other symptoms when your bladder cancer has spread throughout the body.
Pain in the bones
Pain in the pelvic, anal cancer, or rectal areas.
Anemia
Weight loss
If you experience any of the above symptoms especially blood in your urine make an online appointment with Medical Professional to get it checked out.

diseases.name: Bladder Exstrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bladder exstrophy is a rare congenital condition that affects the urinary system, specifically the bladder. It occurs when the bladder fails to form properly during fetal development, resulting in the bladder being exposed outside the body. This condition is significant not only because of its physical implications but also due to the psychological and social challenges it poses for affected individuals and their families. Understanding bladder exstrophy is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of bladder exstrophy can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Visible Bladder: The most apparent symptom is the presence of the bladder outside the body, often accompanied by a split in the abdominal wall.
Urinary Incontinence: Children with bladder exstrophy may experience difficulty controlling urination.
Abnormal Urethra: The urethra may be malformed, leading to further complications.
Pelvic Bone Abnormalities: Some children may have associated skeletal issues, such as pelvic bone malformations.

diseases.name: Bladder Stones - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bladder stones, also known as vesical calculi, are hard mineral deposits that form in the bladder. They can vary in size and shape, ranging from tiny grains to large stones that can cause significant discomfort and complications. Understanding bladder stones is crucial, as they can lead to urinary tract infections, bladder damage, and other serious health issues if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bladder stones, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Bladder stones can present a variety of symptoms, including:
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen or back.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little urine output.
Painful Urination: A burning sensation during urination.
Blood in Urine: Hematuria, or blood in the urine, can occur.
Cloudy or Foul-Smelling Urine: Changes in urine appearance or odor may indicate infection or stone presence.

diseases.name: Bleeding Diathesis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bleeding diathesis is a term that refers to a group of disorders characterized by an increased tendency to bleed. This condition can arise from various underlying causes, including genetic factors, environmental influences, and lifestyle choices. Understanding bleeding diathesis is crucial, as it can lead to serious health complications if not properly managed. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of bleeding diathesis, providing a comprehensive overview for patients and caregivers.
symptoms: The symptoms of bleeding diathesis can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Easy Bruising: Unexplained bruises that appear without significant trauma.
Prolonged Bleeding: Extended bleeding from cuts or injuries.
Spontaneous Bleeding: Bleeding from the gums, nose, or in urine or stool.
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Women may experience unusually heavy periods (menorrhagia).
Joint Bleeding: Swelling and pain in joints due to bleeding into the joint spaces.

diseases.name: Blepharitis (Eyelid Inflammation): Causes & Treatment
diseases.description: Blepharitis often affects both the eyes and rarely disappears entirely. Blepharitis – a condition of eyelid swelling that demands efforts daily. It is comparatively easy to treat but difficult to cure. Blepharitis is the inflammation of the eyelids, which leads to eye swelling too. This primarily occurs due to the blockage of oil glands present adjacent to the base of eyelids. This causes redness and irritation. This condition is difficult to cure but in hand to manage. It does not cause any permanent damage and cannot spread from a person to another person (non-contagious). If you witness any eyelid swelling or eye swelling despite proper hygiene, it is mandatory to make an appointment with your eyelid doctor.
symptoms: The most commonly witnessed symptoms of Blepharitis include the following –
Red and watery eyes
A grainy or rough, and a burning sensation in your eyes
Oily and itchy eyelids
Swollen or inflamed eyelids
Eye covered with crust and stuck together early morning as soon as you wake up
Increased blinking of the eye due to light sensitivity
Blurring of the vision in some cases
Consult your doctor immediately if these symptoms appear even after regular cleaning of the affected area.

diseases.name: Blighted Ovum: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: When a fertilized egg implants in the uterus but fails to develop into an embryo, a placenta and embryonic sac are formed but remain empty. The condition is also described as anembryonic pregnancy, meaning no embryo. The cause of blighted ovum is unknown. However, it may occur due to chromosomal abnormalities in the fertilized egg. As this happens early in pregnancy, most women are unaware of their pregnancy. It is also the leading cause of miscarriage and early pregnancy failure. It also is the cause of one out of two miscarriages in the first trimester of pregnancy. The condition results in a miscarriage as it is not a viable pregnancy.
symptoms: A woman with a blighted ovum may experience pregnancy-related symptoms, including breast tenderness, missed periods, morning sickness, nausea , vomiting, and a positive pregnancy test. However, when the embryo fails to develop, the hormone levels gradually decrease, and pregnancy symptoms reduce.
When this occurs, a pregnant woman may also experience symptoms of miscarriage, such as the following:
Vaginal bleeding or spotting
Abdominal cramping
An unusually heavy period
A doctor can confirm a miscarriage with an ultrasound scan.

diseases.name: Blind Loop Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Blind Loop Syndrome (BLS) is a gastrointestinal disorder that arises when a segment of the small intestine becomes obstructed or disconnected from the normal flow of digestive contents. This condition can lead to a variety of complications, including malabsorption of nutrients, bacterial overgrowth, and significant gastrointestinal distress. Understanding Blind Loop Syndrome is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly improve quality of life and prevent serious complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of Blind Loop Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the abdominal area is common.
Bloating and Gas: Increased gas production due to bacterial overgrowth can lead to significant bloating.
Diarrhea: Frequent, watery stools may occur as a result of malabsorption.
Nutritional Deficiencies: Symptoms related to deficiencies in vitamins and minerals, such as fatigue, weakness, and anemia, may develop over time.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can occur due to malabsorption of nutrients.

diseases.name: Blind Pimple - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Blind pimples, often referred to as cystic acne, are a common skin condition that can be both painful and frustrating. Unlike regular pimples that have a visible head, blind pimples are deeper within the skin, making them harder to treat and often more uncomfortable. Understanding blind pimples is essential for effective management and prevention. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of blind pimples, providing a thorough understanding of this condition.
symptoms: Blind pimples can present with various symptoms, including:
Painful Bump: A firm, swollen bump beneath the skin that may be tender to the touch.
Redness and Inflammation: The surrounding skin may appear red and inflamed.
Heat: The area may feel warm due to increased blood flow and inflammation.

diseases.name: Blocked Hair Follicles - Symptoms, Causes, Treatment
diseases.description: Blocked hair follicles, also known as hidradenitis suppurativa or acne inversa , refers to a chronic inflammatory skin condition. The follicles, i.e., the shafts through which hair grows out of the skin get blocked causing breakouts, or pimples or boils. These blocks are present where the skin rubs together, like the armpits or groin.
symptoms: Symptoms of blocked hair follicles differ in various cases. Pimple-like bumps or deep cysts can form in the affected area. Before noticing a lump, you will feel a sensation in the skin area where the lump will appear. People may also experience skin burns, itches, or excessive sweating.
If the condition is left untreated for a long duration, the symptoms can worsen and develop into the following condition:
Blackheads . Pairs of tiny black bumps resembling blackheads appear in the advanced stages of this condition.
Growing Lumps . Blocked hair follicles symptoms begin with a lump that gradually becomes painful. Lumps can either form in one spot or multiple areas of the body and persist for weeks or months.
Abscesses . As the lumps grow and fuse, they get filled up with fluid that becomes painful abscesses.
Odor. When an abscess breaks open, it will secrete blood and pus. These fluids can collect in clothes and cause a foul odor.

Scars. Usually, abscesses do not heal easily, but if they do, the process is slow, and they will mostly return. The condition’s recurrence causes ‘tunnels’ to form underneath the skin and leads to permanent scars.

diseases.name: Blood Clot in the Brain: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The brain is considered to be one of the most vital organs in the human body. The human brain serves as the nervous system’s command center. This organ is the seat of intelligence, thoughts interpreter of the senses, initiator of body movement, and controller of behavior. Blood clot in the brain could affect these functions.
symptoms: Here is a checklist of symptoms that can help you identify if a person has experienced brain stroke in the past, or is at a higher risk of suffering from one in the near future:
Blurry and darkened vision: Blurred vision is one of the earliest signs of a brain stroke. In this scenario, the person is prone to suffer from double vision.

Slurred speech: Difficulty in speaking is another common symptom of an imminent brain stroke or attack. The patient may be unable to communicate or have slurred speech that is difficult to comprehend.
Numbness: Prolonged numbness on either side of the face can be a sign of an impending brain stroke. If you are experiencing this symptom, you must consult your Apollo doctor immediately.

Acute paralysis: Blood clots in the brain can cause partial paralysis on either side of the patient’s body. Paralysis usually affects the limbs, and in some cases, can also impact one side of the face.

Trouble walking: Brain stroke can cause an individual to lose balance or coordination of their arms and legs. It can also cause sudden bouts of dizziness. This makes walking a difficult task for the afflicted patient.

Visual agnosia: In certain instances of brain stroke, when there’s damage along the pathways that connect the occipital lobe of the brain to the temporal lobe, the person may end up suffering from visual agnosia. Visual agnosia is the inability to recognize a large number of objects placed in front of you. You may suddenly have blurred or blackened vision in one or both eyes, or you may see double.
Headache. A sudden, severe headache , which may be accompanied by vomiting , dizziness or altered consciousness, may indicate that you’re having a stroke.

diseases.name: Blood Clots
diseases.description: Blood clot help heal both internal and external wounds in the body. However, they can be risky when they form inappropriately inside the veins and disrupt the blood flow. Read on to know more about blood clots, their symptoms, causes, and if they pose any risk to your health.
symptoms: Prolonged sitting and bed rest, smoking, obesity , cancer, long periods, birth control, or hormonal pills are few causes of developing blood clots. You cannot find out if you have a blood clot without medical intervention. However, few noticeable and visible symptoms are present in the human body that can indicate the existence of such clots, such as:
Discoloration in a specific area of your skin accompanied by swelling, pain, a warm sensation, and tenderness are the symptoms of a blood clot in the leg or arms.

Shortness of breath, lightheadedness, and feeling a heaviness on your chest are the symptoms of blood clots in your heart. This kind of clot is dangerous because it can cause a massive heart attack if not treated immediately.
Abdominal pain, cramps, and swelling could be the symptoms of blood clots in your abdomen. However, these are also the symptoms of food poisoning or gastrointestinal infection.

Sudden difficulty in your vision and talking ability, with severe headache can indicate that you might have a blood clot in the brain . These clots can also be potentially dangerous because they can lead to strokes.

Breathing problems, coughing up blood , sudden shortness of breath (without physical activity), palpitations, chest pain, and rapid heart rate are the symptoms of blood clots in your lungs. It is called pulmonary embolism .

diseases.name: Blood in your stool? Home Remedies to Relieve Yourself from Hemorrhoids
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids, commonly known as piles , are swollen veins in your rectum and anal region. Due to the increased pressure in the lower rectum region, the veins in this area gets swollen, resulting in hemorrhoids. In some cases, it may even cause bleeding. But not every case of rectal bleeding is due to hemorrhoids. Changes in your bowel habits or discoloration of the stool can also cause rectal bleeding . Anal cancer and colorectal cancer may also cause rectal bleeding.
symptoms: Different types of hemorrhoids show different signs and symptoms.
Internal Hemorrhoids

Internal hemorrhoids are found deep inside the rectum. You can’t see or feel them. Generally, they don’t hurt as much because of a few pain-sensing nerves present there. You may notice these symptoms:
Painless bleeding when you pass a stool
Pain or irritation when you pass a stool
Bloodstains on the toilet bowl or toilet paper
External Hemorrhoids
External hemorrhoids are found under the skin around your anus. These hemorrhoids hurt more because several pain-sensing nerves are present in this region. The signs and symptoms include:
Bleeding
Irritation or itching in your anus
Discomfort or pain
Swelling around the anus region
Thrombosed Hemorrhoids
Sometimes, external hemorrhoids turn into a blood clot or a thrombus. It is called a thrombosed hemorrhoid. You may notice symptoms such as:
Inflammation
Itching
Severe pain
Swelling
A hard lump in the anus region
If you notice any of these symptoms, visit a doctor to get yourself checked.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: Bloom Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bloom Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterized by a heightened sensitivity to sunlight, growth deficiencies, and an increased risk of developing various cancers. This condition is significant not only due to its clinical manifestations but also because it serves as a model for understanding the complexities of genetic disorders and their implications on health. Individuals with Bloom Syndrome face unique challenges, and understanding this condition is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support.
symptoms: Bloom Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity among affected individuals. Common symptoms include:
Short Stature: Individuals with Bloom Syndrome often have a significantly shorter height compared to their peers.
Skin Changes: A butterfly-shaped rash may develop on the face, particularly after sun exposure. Other skin issues may include photosensitivity and telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels).
Immune Deficiencies: Affected individuals may experience recurrent infections due to compromised immune function.
Fertility Issues: Males may have reduced fertility, while females may experience complications during pregnancy.
Increased Cancer Risk: There is a heightened risk of developing various cancers, including leukemia, lymphoma, and solid tumors.

diseases.name: Blounts Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Blount's disease, also known as tibia vara, is a growth disorder that affects the bones of the lower leg, particularly the tibia (shinbone). This condition is characterized by an abnormal curvature of the tibia, leading to a bowing of the legs. Blount's disease is significant not only because of its impact on physical appearance and mobility but also due to its potential long-term effects on joint health and function. Early diagnosis and appropriate management are crucial to prevent complications and ensure optimal outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of Blount's disease can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Bowing of the Legs: The most noticeable symptom is the outward curvature of the legs, which may become more pronounced with age.
Knee Pain: Children may experience discomfort or pain in the knees, particularly during physical activities.
Gait Abnormalities: Affected individuals may have an altered walking pattern, which can lead to further complications.
Uneven Leg Length: In some cases, one leg may appear shorter than the other due to the curvature.

diseases.name: Blue Baby Syndrome : Symptoms, Causes and Treatments
diseases.description: Blue baby syndrome is a condition some babies are born with or develop early in life. It’s characterized by an overall skin colour with a blue or purple tinge, called cyanosis. The baby can be born with it or develop the condition during an early period of its life.
symptoms: The following are some of the symptoms of the blue baby syndrome.
Skin turns blue
Irritability
Rapid breath or heartbeat
Baby refuses to feed
Low weight gain
Lethargy

diseases.name: Body Dysmorphic Disorder
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: A person suffering from BDD may display the following warning signs due to the perceived defect:
Repetitive behaviors like being obsessed with checking oneself in the mirror
Touching the skin and trying to hide the perceived defect
Suffering from lack of concentration
Unable to cope with school, work or relationship
Asking for constant reassurance
Always feeling self-conscious or anxious when around other people
Repeatedly consulting medical specialists to improve their appearance

diseases.name: Body-Focused Repetitive Behavior (BFRB): Causes & Diagnosis
diseases.description: Body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) are intense urges such as picking, pulling and biting, which can cause damage to the body.Some common behaviors that a lot of individuals show include skin chewing, skin pinching, and nail-biting.

diseases.name: Boerhaave Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Boerhaave Syndrome is a rare but serious medical condition characterized by the spontaneous rupture of the esophagus. Named after the Dutch physician Hermann Boerhaave, who first described the condition in the 18th century, this syndrome is significant due to its high mortality rate if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding Boerhaave Syndrome is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early recognition and intervention can be life-saving.
symptoms: The symptoms of Boerhaave Syndrome can vary but often include:
Severe Chest Pain: Sudden, intense pain in the chest, often described as sharp or stabbing.
Vomiting: This may be accompanied by blood or a foul-smelling substance.
Difficulty Swallowing: Patients may experience dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) due to esophageal obstruction.
Fever: A high fever may indicate infection or inflammation.
Rapid Heart Rate: Tachycardia can occur as the body responds to pain and potential infection.

diseases.name: Boils And Carbuncles - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Boils and carbuncles are common skin conditions that can cause discomfort and distress. While they may seem like minor nuisances, they can lead to significant complications if not properly managed. Understanding these conditions is crucial for effective treatment and prevention. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of boils and carbuncles, including their definitions, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: Pain and Tenderness: The affected area is often painful and tender to the touch.
Redness and Swelling: The skin around the boil or carbuncle may appear red and swollen.
Pus Formation: Boils typically contain pus, which may drain from the center of the bump.
Fever: In some cases, individuals may experience fever or chills, indicating a more severe infection.

diseases.name: Bone Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Bone cancer occurs when abnormal cells in the bone begin to grow uncontrollably, which can lead to pain, swelling, and fractures. Although it is relatively rare compared to other cancers, understanding the condition is important for effective management and treatment. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about bone cancer—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what you can expect throughout the journey. Our aim is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of bone cancer can be vague and are often mistaken for other, more common conditions like sports injuries or growing pains. However, if you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
Common Early Signs:
Bone Pain or Tenderness: The most common symptom is a persistent pain in the affected bone. The pain may come and go at first, but it can become constant and may get worse at night or with activity.
A Lump or Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling may appear in the affected area, which may or may not be painful.
Problems with Movement: If the cancer is near a joint, it may cause a limp or make it difficult to move the joint.
Unexplained Broken Bone (Fracture): In rare cases, a bone can become so weakened by the cancer that it breaks after a minor fall or injury.
Advanced Symptoms:
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Fever: A persistent, unexplained fever.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
If you or a loved one has a persistent bone pain that doesn't go away, especially if it is worse at night, it is crucial to consult a doctor right away for an accurate diagnosis.

diseases.name: Bone marrow failure syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome (BMFS) refers to a collection of disorders that impair the bone marrow's ability to produce healthy blood cells. This is a rare but serious medical condition that can affect individuals of all ages. Bone marrow failure may lead to severe anemia, infections, and uncontrolled bleeding. Early detection and treatment are critical to prevent complications and improve the quality of life for patients.
symptoms: The symptoms of BMFS vary depending on the severity of bone marrow dysfunction and the type of blood cell affected. Below are the common symptoms:
Fatigue and Weakness: Due to the lack of red blood cells, individuals with BMFS often experience extreme fatigue, weakness, and paleness.
Frequent Infections: A reduced number of white blood cells compromises the immune system, making individuals more susceptible to infections.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: A lack of platelets can lead to easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, or spontaneous bleeding (e.g., nosebleeds or gum bleeding).
Paleness and Shortness of Breath: Anemia can lead to paleness of the skin, as well as shortness of breath, even with minimal physical activity.
Unexplained Fever or Weight Loss: In some cases, BMFS can present with unexplained fever, weight loss, and other systemic signs that may be confused with other illnesses.

diseases.name: Borderline Personality Disorder - Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Borderline Personality Disorder, or BPD, is a mental health disorder that affects the way you feel about yourself and other people in your life. People who have experienced it defines it as a rollercoaster ride full of unstable emotions, relationships, and a wavering sense of self. BPD can cause frequent changes in personality, self-image, and even likes and dislikes.
symptoms: Borderline Personality Disorder has several signs and symptoms. For diagnosis, mental health professionals have grouped the symptoms into 9 categories. A person who shows at least 5 of these symptoms for a long duration is diagnosed as suffering from BPD. The following are the signs and symptoms of BPD:
Fear of abandonment

One of the most prominent signs of BPD is a fear of abandonment. People with BPD are always scared of being left alone by loved ones. Something as simple as a family member coming home late from work can trigger intense reactions. As a result, individuals suffering from BPD put frantic efforts into keeping family and friends close.

While this kind of behavior feels normal to a person with borderline personality disorder, it looks scary to the person on the other side. Therefore, an attempt to keep everyone close has the opposite effect and scares people away. This is why people suffering from BPD often find themselves alone, and their feeling of emptiness only deepens with every failed relationship.
Unstable relationships

People with BPD fall quickly in love and then get easily disappointed and fall out of love. More often than not, they enter a relationship hoping that the new person will give them some comfort from their constant worries and insecurities. When that does not happen, the relationship goes from bad to worse in no time. For people with BPD, relationships are either perfect or horrible; there is nothing in between.
Unclear self-image

Self-image is a perception of self that defines how much you like yourself. With BPD, individuals struggle to keep a stable perception. They go from loving themselves one day to absolutely hating themselves the next day. Such people do not have an idea of who they are and what they want in life. Their ambitions and goals change with their mood, and this is why they end up changing friends, jobs, values, goals, and even religion or sexual identity.
Self-destructive behavior

Self-destructive behavior and impulsiveness are two of the most prominent signs of BPD. People with this disorder tend to behave in self-destructive ways like driving recklessly, shoplifting, overdoing alcohol or drugs, overspending money, etc. Risky behavior helps them feel good in the moment, but it causes lasting damage to a person’s health, finances, and personal relationships.
Self-harm

After self-destruction comes self-harm. Individuals suffering from BPD do not hesitate from harming themselves. They may easily cut themselves or burn themselves and may also take a step with the intent of suicide. Cutting and burning are the most common forms of self-harm, but they may find other ways of hurting themselves. People with BPD are always in danger of taking a drastic step. Loved ones have to be vigilant at all times and on the lookout for suicidal thoughts .
Mood swings

BPD causes extreme mood swings that can go from happy-go-lucky today to despondent and suicidal tomorrow. This symptom is caused by the fact that individuals with BPD get triggered by the smallest things in life and go into an emotional tailspin. Their mood swings are intense but may also pass quickly. Mood swings of individuals with BPD last just a few minutes or hours.
Feeling of emptiness

Individuals with BPD suffer from a chronic feeling of emptiness. They often feel like “nobody” and have this uncomfortable void that they try to fill with the help of extreme and risky behaviors. People with BPD may get involved in drugs, bingeing on food, or even risky sex arrangements to feel better. This feeling of emptiness is what triggers all their behaviors and reactions. Their relationships, their jobs, and even their aggressiveness are built around this void that they want to fill.
Explosive anger

BPD causes impulsiveness, which often results in explosive anger. It also results in a short temper that comes out even at the slightest of disagreements. Explosive anger may be accompanied by behavior like throwing things or screaming (even in public places). According to mental health practitioners, the anger may not necessarily be directed outwards always. People with BPD may hold it inside for a long time and may express it in the form of self-harm.
Paranoia or suspicion

Individuals with BPD often struggle with paranoia. They get suspicious about other people’s intentions and may give a tough time to their spouse with their foggy and spaced out beliefs and thoughts. Patients of BPD often lose touch with reality when under stress and cause distress to their family and friends with their words and actions.
