diseases.name: Boutonniere Deformity: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Boutonnière deformity is a medical condition caused by an injury to the tendons that straighten your finger’s middle joint. For those who are afflicted by this condition, the middle joint of your finger bends in, and the outermost joint bends out.
symptoms: The initial signs of a Boutonniere deformity can appear either immediately after an accident or manifest after a period of time. If the underlying cause of the deformity is arthritis , then it usually develops gradually over time. You will first notice that you are unable to straighten your fingers completely. In addition, the tip of your finger does not bend in toward the palm of your hand, no matter how hard you try. Swelling or soreness is also possible.

diseases.name: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE)
diseases.description: Numerous diseases are contracted from animals to humans. Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) is a disease transmitted from cattle to humans. Many lives have succumbed to bovine spongiform encephalopathy during the past few years. This blog is a comprehensive guide on bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), its symptoms, causes and treatment options. Let’s be aware and fight it.
symptoms: All age groups are susceptible to the condition, making it difficult to identify until it has almost entirely progressed. People with vCJD experience symptoms linked to the nervous system, such as depression and loss of coordination in the early stages of the disease. Dementia sets in later on during the illness. Some other symptoms of bovine spongiform encephalopathy are:
Vision problems
Inability to walk
Stinging or electric shock sensation in nerves
Jerking in muscles
Psychotic episodes
Coma
But MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) cannot reveal abnormalities in the brain unless the disease is far along. Within 13 months after the commencement of symptoms, vCJD becomes fatal.

diseases.name: Bowen’s Disease: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment, Prevention, Risks Factors
diseases.description: Bowen’s disease is an early form of skin cancer. It is also known as squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in situ, a skin cancer, as it is formed on the top layer of the skin. It is a slow-progressing cancer. It is often confused with other skin conditions, including eczema or psoriasis .
symptoms: For most people, symptoms show up as a single lesion. But some people have more than one lesion. These lesions are often found on your head, neck, palms of your hands, and soles of your feet. If you have skin patches you may experience the following:
Red scaling sometimes may appear as yellow or white
Moist pinkness or redness under the patch
Itching
Crusty lesions
Slow growth
Pus, if infected
Defined borders
The size may be a few millimeters to a few centimeters
Flat or raised lesions

These lesions may take 2 to 40 years to reach their full size. Therefore it is vital to identify the disease early and get prompt treatment. Sometimes, you may be asymptomatic. In rare cases, you may develop lesions around your genitals.

diseases.name: Bowlegs - Symptoms, Causes & Treatment
diseases.description: Bow legs is a type of knee malformation that can afflict individuals at any stage of the growing process but is more common amongst toddlers and adolescents. This disease is also referred to as bandy-leg, varus deformity, genu varum, and tibia vara. The treatment of the disease depends on multiple factors such as the patient’s age, stage of the disease, severity of the bone deformation and more.
symptoms: Here is a checklist of common symptoms that signal that the patient is potentially suffering from bowlegs:
The most prominent and common symptom of this affliction is a visible bowing of the legs.
Patients also tend to display abnormal walking patterns.
Consistent bowing during adolescence can create discomfort in the hips, knees, and/or ankles due to the unnatural tension that the curved legs place on these joints.
Instability while walking is common among adolescents suffering from this disease.

diseases.name: Boxers Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Boxers Fracture is a common injury that affects the hand, specifically the fifth metacarpal bone, which is located in the palm and connects to the little finger. This type of fracture is often associated with punching an object, hence the name "Boxers Fracture." Understanding this injury is crucial not only for athletes but also for anyone who may inadvertently sustain such an injury in everyday life. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Boxers Fracture.
symptoms: Pain: Intense pain in the hand, particularly around the little finger.
Swelling: Swelling and bruising may develop around the fracture site.
Deformity: The hand may appear misshapen, especially if the fracture is displaced.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty in moving the little finger or making a fist.

diseases.name: BPH (Enlarged Prostate)
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: BPH symptoms usually start after the age of 50. They can include:
Trouble starting a urine stream or making more than a dribble
Passing urine often, especially at night
Feeling that the bladder has not fully emptied
A strong or sudden urge to pass urine
Weak or slow urine stream
Stopping and starting again several times while passing urine
Pushing or straining to begin passing urine
At its worst, BPH can lead to:
A weak bladder
Backflow of urine causing bladder or kidney infections
Complete block in the flow of urine
Kidney failure

BPH affects most men as they get older. It can lead to urinary problems like those with prostatitis. By age 60, many men have signs of BPH. By age 70, almost all men have some prostate enlargement. The prostate starts out about the size of a walnut. By the time a man is 40, it may have grown slightly larger, to the size of an apricot. By age 60, it may be the size of a lemon. As a normal part of aging, the prostate enlarges and can press against the bladder and the urethra. This can slow down or block urine flow. Some men might find it hard to start a urine stream, even though they feel the need to go. Once the urine stream has started, it may be hard to stop. Other men may feel like they need to pass urine all the time or are awakened during sleep with the sudden need to pass urine. Early BPH symptoms take many years to turn into bothersome problems. These early symptoms are a cue to see your doctor. Urine flow of normal (left) and enlarged prostate (right). In diagram on the left, urine flows freely. On the right, urine flow is affected because of the prostate pressing on the bladder and urethra.

diseases.name: Brachydactyly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brachydactyly is a term that may not be familiar to many, but it refers to a condition that affects the length of fingers and toes. This condition is characterized by the shortening of one or more digits, which can have significant implications for an individual's daily life and overall well-being. Understanding brachydactyly is essential not only for those who may be affected by it but also for healthcare providers and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of brachydactyly, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of brachydactyly is the noticeable shortening of one or more fingers or toes. The severity and specific digits affected can vary widely among individuals. Other potential symptoms may include:
Difficulty gripping or holding objects due to shortened fingers.
Altered hand or foot function, which may affect daily activities.
Aesthetic concerns related to the appearance of the hands or feet.

diseases.name: Bradyarrhythmia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bradyarrhythmia is a medical condition characterized by an abnormally slow heart rate, typically defined as fewer than 60 beats per minute. While the heart rate can vary significantly among individuals, bradyarrhythmia can lead to various health complications if not properly managed. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can affect anyone, regardless of age or health status. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bradyarrhythmia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Bradyarrhythmia may present with a variety of symptoms, which can range from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A sensation of spinning or feeling faint, especially when standing up quickly.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded during normal activities.
Chest Pain or Discomfort: A feeling of pressure or tightness in the chest.
Confusion or Memory Problems: Difficulty concentrating or experiencing memory lapses.

diseases.name: Bradycardia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bradycardia is a medical condition characterized by an unusually slow heart rate, typically defined as fewer than 60 beats per minute in adults. While a slow heart rate can be normal for some individuals, particularly athletes, bradycardia can also indicate underlying health issues that may require medical attention. Understanding bradycardia is crucial, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bradycardia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Bradycardia may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when it does, they can include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A sensation of feeling faint or unsteady.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Confusion: Difficulty concentrating or confusion, particularly in older adults.

diseases.name: Brain Abscess - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A brain abscess is a localized collection of pus within the brain tissue, typically caused by an infection. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe neurological complications, including seizures, cognitive deficits, and even death if not treated promptly. Understanding brain abscesses is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of a brain abscess can vary depending on the size and location of the abscess, as well as the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Headache: Often severe and persistent, headaches are one of the most common symptoms.
Fever: A low-grade fever may be present, indicating an underlying infection.
Neurological Deficits: Symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking may occur, depending on the area of the brain affected.
Seizures: Seizures can occur due to irritation of the brain tissue.
Altered Mental Status: Confusion, drowsiness, or changes in behavior may be observed.

diseases.name: Brain Aneurysms - Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: When most of us think about the word aneurysm, we think about chaotic scenes from movies where someone is being rushed into an operation theatre with a whole lot of doctors and nurses following, or the character stops mid-speech to fall dead within a second. All of these project aneurysm as a very scary and fatal condition. But let’s stop to consider what really makes an brain aneurysm, and understand when you should be concerned and when to take it easy.
symptoms: Usually, small aneurysms do not show any symptoms and may not be worrisome. However, large aneurysm and ruptured or leaking aneurysms are dangerous and need immediate medical attention.

A large unruptured aneurysm can press on nearby nerves and brain tissue and can cause unilateral headaches , pain above or behind the eye, dizziness, difficulty in speaking, moving, unilateral numbness or weakness.
However, a ruptured or leaking aneurysm can occur with:
A sudden extremely severe headache
Insensitivity to light
Nausea
Neck stiffness
Sudden blurring of vision
difficulty in speaking
Loss of consciousness
Seizures
Confusion
Drooping eyelid
If you or your loved ones develops any of the above symptoms, you should seek medical help as an emergency.

diseases.name: Brain Atrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brain atrophy, a term that may sound alarming, refers to the loss of neurons and the connections between them in the brain. This condition can lead to a decrease in brain mass and is often associated with various neurological disorders. Understanding brain atrophy is crucial, as it can significantly impact cognitive functions, memory, and overall quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of brain atrophy, providing a comprehensive overview for readers seeking to understand this complex condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of brain atrophy can vary depending on the areas of the brain affected. Common symptoms include:
Memory Loss: Difficulty remembering recent events or learning new information.
Cognitive Decline: Challenges with problem-solving, planning, and decision-making.
Language Difficulties: Trouble finding words or understanding language.
Changes in Mood or Behavior: Increased irritability, depression, or anxiety.
Motor Skill Impairment: Difficulty with coordination and balance.

diseases.name: Brain Cancer
diseases.description: In the last hundred years, medicine has seen advances that have not been witnessed in human history. As a result, today we are healthier and live longer than at any time in the past. Diseases such as smallpox that have killed millions have now been completely eradicated, thanks to vaccinations and the dreaded scourge of tuberculosis are now treated successfully with antibiotics. Healthy eating and active lifestyles have contributed to lower morbidity and mortality from diabetes , heart attacks and stroke.

diseases.name: Brain Death - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brain death is a critical medical condition that signifies the irreversible loss of all brain function, including the brainstem. It is a legal and clinical definition of death that has profound implications for patients, families, and healthcare providers. Understanding brain death is essential not only for medical professionals but also for the general public, as it raises ethical, emotional, and practical questions about end-of-life care, organ donation, and the nature of life itself.
symptoms: Brain death is characterized by the absence of all brain activity. Symptoms may include:
Unresponsiveness: The individual does not respond to stimuli, including pain.
Absence of Reflexes: There are no reflexive movements, such as blinking or withdrawal from pain.
No Breathing: The individual cannot breathe independently and requires mechanical ventilation.
Fixed Pupils: The pupils do not react to light.

diseases.name: Brain Fog: Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Have you ever faced a situation where you have difficulty processing a thought or have fuzzy thinking? Then, you might be suffering from brain fog.
symptoms: Brain fog acts differently in people. It can affect all age groups starting from a school going child to a full-grown adult, and in old age as well. A person suffering from brain fog may have either one symptom or may have multiple symptoms together that are associated with the conditions’ severity. Mentioned below are a few common symptoms of brain fog:
Decreased concentration
Memory impairment
Hazy or faded thoughts
Extreme tiredness and feeling sleepy
Feeling demotivated
Low self-esteem
Poor performance at school and work
Depressed mood
Unable to create sentences using words or inability to understand a simple sentence
Cannot focus on a single target
Unable to execute a plan, solve a problem, or organize stuff

diseases.name: Brain Lesions - Symptoms, Causes, Types and Treatment
diseases.description: A brain lesion is a damaged area in the brain tissue. It can happen due to a traumatic injury , infection, or destruction of the brain cells. The initial stages of a brain lesion may not show any symptoms. However, as the lesions progress over time, they can cause mental and physical changes. There are numerous types of brain lesions that can range from large to small, few to many, and from relatively harmless to life threatening.
symptoms: You may experience symptoms depending on the location, severity, and type of brain lesion. Headaches are usually the first symptoms you develop when you get brain lesions. You may experience a sudden headache which may worsen over time.
Along with headache, some of the other symptoms that you can experience are:
Lack of appetite, nausea, and vomiting
Lack of concentration
Memory loss or confusion
Pain or stiffness in the neck
Seizures
Impaired hearing, delayed speech , or blurred vision
Involuntary movement of body parts

diseases.name: Brain Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: A brain tumor is an abnormal growth of cells in the brain or nearby structures. Some tumors grow slowly and are not cancer (benign), while others grow faster and may be cancer (malignant). Even non-cancerous tumors can cause problems because the brain is such a delicate and important organ. Both types can cause serious health issues because the brain controls essential functions like movement, speech, memory, and breathing.
symptoms: Brain tumor symptoms vary depending on size, location, and growth rate.
Common early signs include:
Persistent headaches, especially worse in the morning
Nausea or vomiting without a clear cause
Blurred or double vision
Memory problems and difficulty concentrating
Advanced symptoms may include:
Seizures
Difficulty with balance and coordination
Speech problems
Weakness or numbness in limbs
Personality or behavior changes
These symptoms do not always mean cancer, but if persistent, they should be evaluated by a doctor.

diseases.name: Brain Tumour
diseases.description: A brain tumour is an abnormal growth of cells (mass of unnecessary cells) in the brain, which upon enlargement exerts pressure on normal brain tissue and vital nerves inside the skull leading to a set of symptoms and signs.

diseases.name: Brain-Eating Amoeba : Symptoms, Diagnosis, Cure and Prevention
diseases.description: If you are one of those students who paid attention in biology classes in school, you would know that there is a single-celled organism called an amoeba. But do you also know a species of amoeba known as the brain-eating amoeba? Only a few know about it. It was first identified in 1965 in Australia and is scientifically called Naegleria fowleri.
symptoms: PAM does not have specific symptoms. It may first resemble viral meningitis. The signs include
nausea and vomiting
loss of appetite
fever
changed state of mind
seizures
coma
You could also experience hallucinations, drooping eyelids, blurred visions, and a loss of taste.

diseases.name: Branchial Cleft Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Branchial cleft cysts are congenital anomalies that arise from the incomplete closure of the branchial apparatus during embryonic development. These cysts are significant not only because they can lead to discomfort and complications but also due to their potential to mimic other conditions. Understanding branchial cleft cysts is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring better outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: Branchial cleft cysts may present with various symptoms, including:
Neck Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling on the side of the neck, which may fluctuate in size.
Pain or Discomfort: The cyst may become painful, especially if infected.
Redness or Warmth: Signs of infection may include redness and warmth over the cyst.
Drainage: Infected cysts may drain pus or fluid, leading to foul-smelling discharge.

diseases.name: Breaking the Stigma around HPV: All You Need to Know
diseases.description: HPV infection is caused by the Human Papilloma Virus and is a common infection that affects millions of people around the world each year. The infection is usually passed from one person to the other through skin-to-skin contact. There are about 100 or more varieties of this virus, and nearly 40 of them are said to be transmitted through sexual contact. HPV (Human papillomavirus) is said to be the most common Sexually Transmitted Infection or Disease, and many sexually active individuals do get exposed to this virus sometime during their lives. HPV infection There is significant fear and stigma associated with developing the HPV infection. The main reason for this is that most people believe an HPV infection leads to cancer. However, there is more to this that we need to understand. In some people, human papillomavirus infection causes the development of warts, but in others, it can cause cancer. But, this doesn’t mean that all HPV infections lead to cancer. The human papillomavirus infection results in cancers of uterus, vagina, penis, vagina, vulva, and even oropharyngeal cancer. Though there is no treatment for this viral infection, it can now be prevented by the HPV vaccine . Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment Signs and symptoms HPV (human papillomavirus) Most people are usually asymptomatic when infected by the virus, and their body successfully hold off the infection over a period of a few months to years. But, such individuals may still be harbouring the virus and end up transmitting it to another person. Your body usually fights the HPV before it results in the formation of warts– the first sign of the disease, and some commonly observed warts caused by the virus include:

diseases.name: Breast Calcifications - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Breast calcifications are tiny deposits of calcium in the breast tissue. These are more commonly found in women above the age of 50 years. Typically, breast calcifications are benign or noncancerous. However, some of them may indicate the early stages of breast cancer .
symptoms: Usually, breast calcifications do not show any symptoms. It is because they are too small to be felt or noticed during your routine breast examinations.

diseases.name: Breast Cancer - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Breast cancer is the second largest cancer occurring in Indian women. It has been estimated that 1 in 20 women will be affected by breast cancer sometime in their life. Breast cancer is a malignant tumour, which begins in the cells of the breast. It is found mostly in women, but men can also get affected.

diseases.name: Breast Cancer Treatment in Hyderabad
diseases.description: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women worldwide. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), it has become the most frequently diagnosed cancer globally, with approximately 2.3 million new cases each year. Early detection and access to specialised oncology care can significantly improve outcomes.

diseases.name: Breast Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Breast cysts are fluid-filled sacs that can develop in the breast tissue. While they are often benign (non-cancerous), their presence can cause anxiety and concern among those affected. Understanding breast cysts is crucial for women, as it empowers them to recognize symptoms, seek appropriate medical care, and make informed decisions about their health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of breast cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Breast cysts may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when they do, they can include:
Lump or Mass: A palpable lump in the breast that may feel smooth and firm.
Pain or Discomfort: Some women experience tenderness or pain in the area of the cyst, especially before menstruation.
Changes in Size: Cysts may fluctuate in size with the menstrual cycle, often becoming larger and more tender before menstruation.

diseases.name: Breast Eczema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Breast eczema, also known as eczema of the breast or nipple eczema, is a skin condition that affects many individuals, particularly women. It can cause discomfort, embarrassment, and distress, impacting the quality of life. Understanding breast eczema is crucial for effective management and prevention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of breast eczema, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and preventive measures.
symptoms: Breast eczema can manifest in various ways, including:
Redness: The skin may appear inflamed and red.
Itching: Intense itching is a hallmark symptom, often leading to scratching and further irritation.
Dryness and Flaking: The affected skin may become dry, flaky, or scaly.
Oozing or Crusting: In severe cases, the skin may ooze fluid or develop crusts.
Thickened Skin: Chronic eczema can lead to lichenification, where the skin becomes thick and leathery.

diseases.name: Breast Engorgement - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Breast engorgement is a common condition that many individuals experience, particularly during the early stages of breastfeeding. It occurs when the breasts become overly full with milk, leading to discomfort and potential complications if not managed properly. Understanding breast engorgement is crucial for new mothers, healthcare providers, and anyone interested in maternal health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of breast engorgement, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: Breast engorgement can present with various symptoms, including:
Swelling: The breasts may appear larger and feel firm to the touch.
Pain or Discomfort: Many individuals experience tenderness or aching in the breasts.
Warmth: The skin over the breasts may feel warm or hot.
Nipple Changes: The nipples may become flat or inverted, making breastfeeding more challenging.
Difficulty Feeding: Babies may struggle to latch onto engorged breasts, leading to frustration for both mother and child.

diseases.name: Breast Implant-Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) is a rare type of lymphoma (cancer of the immune system) that can develop in the scar tissue and fluid surrounding a breast implant. It is not a breast carcinoma but a rare T-cell lymphoma that arises in the capsule and fluid surrounding the implant. Most reported cases are associated with textured implants, with a latency period typically of 7–10 years, though cases as early as 2 years and as late as >20 years have been described. When detected early and treated with the right approach, outcomes are generally very good. This comprehensive article explains BIA-ALCL, including what it is, symptoms to watch for, how it is diagnosed and treated, recovery, and prevention tips at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms typically develop gradually and may affect only one breast:
Unexplained breast swelling, tightness, or sudden size increase
Fluid build-up around the implant (seroma)
A lump on or near the implant or in the armpit (lymph node)
Breast pain, asymmetry, or firmness (capsular contracture)
Cutaneous rash is rare and usually reflects local inflammation rather than lymphoma itself
General symptoms such as fatigue, fever, and weight loss are uncommon but can occur in more advanced disease
Any new change in a breast with an implant—especially late-onset swelling—should be evaluated promptly. Early assessment allows for simpler treatment and better outcomes.

diseases.name: Breast Milk Jaundice - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Breast milk jaundice is a type of jaundice that occurs in neonates due to breastfeeding. It happens within the first week of life due to the abnormal accumulation of bilirubin. Jaundice is a condition in which the skin and eyes turn yellow. It is common in newborns . Many infants get jaundice within a few days or weeks after birth. Jaundice occurs when the bilirubin content in the blood is higher than usual. Bilirubin is produced during the breakdown of red blood cells. This bilirubin releases into the intestinal tract after passing through the liver. Since the liver in infants is not fully developed, it is difficult for their liver to remove the bilirubin from the blood. Due to the excess amount of bilirubin in the blood, the skin and eyes appear yellow.
symptoms: Infants generally show symptoms of breast milk jaundice one week after birth. They are:
Yellow pigmentation of the skin and eyes
Poor weight gain
High-pitched crying
Fatigue

diseases.name: Breast Pain
diseases.description: What is mastalgia?

diseases.name: Breech Baby - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A breech baby refers to a fetus that is positioned in the womb with its buttocks or feet facing down toward the birth canal, rather than the head. This position can complicate the delivery process and may pose risks to both the mother and the baby. Understanding the implications of a breech presentation is crucial for expectant parents, as it can influence delivery methods and overall pregnancy management. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding breech babies.
symptoms: Most women may not experience specific symptoms indicating a breech baby, as the position of the fetus is often discovered during routine prenatal check-ups. However, some signs may include:
Unusual Fetal Movement: Feeling kicks or movements in the upper abdomen rather than the lower.
Pelvic Pressure: Increased pressure in the pelvic area as the baby’s head is not engaged.
Back Pain: Discomfort in the lower back due to the baby's position.

diseases.name: Brief Psychotic Disorder - Treatment, Prognosis and Symptoms
diseases.description: A brief psychotic disorder (BPD) is a psychiatric condition that may occur suddenly and for a brief period of time, accompanied by symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, and confusion. As the name suggests, these symptoms may last for a day or for as long as a month. The symptoms may feel realistic enough to the patient to the extent that they may trigger violent behaviour or increase their risk of committing suicide .
symptoms: Signs and symptoms usually begin suddenly and might last for 1 month or less. A person with BPD may experience any of the following:

Delusional episodes : During this episode, one may believe that something is true or right when it is not. These false beliefs do not go away even if there is proof that they are untrue. One may even believe someone is constantly following, looking, or manipulating their mind. They may also feel there is something wrong with how their body functions.

Disoriented speech : Here, the person affected usually talks senselessly, uses made-up words and utters disturbing sounds, and may suddenly switch between subjects with no logical connection between them.
Disorganized behaviour : The person may behave differently than normal, wear different clothes, get mood swings, and have trouble remembering things.

Hallucinations : The person may imagine things that are not there. Auditory hallucinations are one of the most common types of hallucinations. In this, one may even believe someone is telling them to do things or threatening them.

diseases.name: Brittle Diabetes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brittle diabetes , also known as labile diabetes, is a rare and complex form of diabetes characterized by extreme fluctuations in blood glucose levels. This condition poses significant challenges for those affected, as it can lead to severe hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) or hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) that can be life-threatening. Understanding brittle diabetes is crucial for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers, as it requires a tailored approach to management and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of brittle diabetes, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of brittle diabetes can vary widely due to the unpredictable nature of blood sugar levels. Common symptoms include:
Severe Hypoglycemia: Symptoms may include sweating, shaking, confusion, irritability, and fainting.
Severe Hyperglycemia: Symptoms may include excessive thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, and blurred vision.
Mood Swings: Rapid changes in blood sugar levels can lead to emotional instability, anxiety, and depression.
Physical Symptoms: Individuals may experience headaches, dizziness, and weakness.

diseases.name: Broken Heart Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Broken Heart Syndrome , medically known as Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy, is a temporary heart condition that mimics the symptoms of a heart attack. It is often triggered by extreme emotional or physical stress, leading to a sudden weakening of the heart muscle. This condition is significant not only because of its striking presentation but also due to its implications for heart health and emotional well-being. Understanding Broken Heart Syndrome is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, seeking timely treatment, and preventing potential complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of Broken Heart Syndrome can be similar to those of a heart attack and may include:
Chest Pain: Sudden, intense chest pain is the most common symptom.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or emotional stress.
Palpitations: A feeling of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or weakness, even with minimal exertion.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady.

diseases.name: Bronchiectasis
diseases.description: Bronchiectasis is a condition wherein the bronchial tubes of the lungs are enlarged and permanently damaged, giving way for excess mucus and bacteria to build up in the lungs, causing infections.
symptoms: Symptoms of bronchiectasis do not develop overnight. Depending on the severity, symptoms can occur over weeks, months or even years. The following are the most usual symptoms of this condition:
Chest pains
Shortness of breath
Bad breath
Chronic coughing
Blood in the sputum
Wheezing in the chest
Fatigue
Weight loss
Thickening of the skin under toes and nails
Excessive coughing up of mucus
If you have any/some/all of the above symptoms, seek your doctor’s counsel immediately.

diseases.name: Bronchiolitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bronchiolitis is a common respiratory condition that primarily affects infants and young children. It is characterized by inflammation of the small airways in the lungs, known as bronchioles. This condition is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its potential to lead to serious respiratory complications. Understanding bronchiolitis is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of bronchiolitis typically develop over a few days and may include:
Cough: A persistent cough that may worsen at night.
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, which may be accompanied by rapid breathing.
Fever: Mild to moderate fever may be present.
Nasal Congestion: Stuffy or runny nose.

diseases.name: Bronchiolitis in Children - Symptoms, Causes, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Bronchiolitis is a common lung infection in infants and young children. The disease can cause difficulty in breathing, coughing, and wheezing. Most cases of bronchiolitis are treatable at home. In severe cases, you may need to hospitalize the child. Bronchiolitis is also one of the most common reasons for admissions of infants and children to a hospital.
symptoms: The initial symptoms look a lot like that of a common cold. Your child may present with the following symptoms:
Fever
Cough
Runny nose
Stuffy nose
Loss of appetite
These symptoms may get worse with time. Your child may show severe symptoms such as:
Rapid breathing (over 60 breaths in a minute)
Vomiting
Wheezing (a high-pitched, whistling sound while exhaling)
Constant coughing
Tired or lethargic appearance
Labored breathing
Difficulty in swallowing, drinking, and sucking.
Signs of dehydration including crying without tears, dry mouth, and reduced urination
During bronchiolitis, infants may also experience an ear infection, known as otitis media .
If you notice your child presenting with these symptoms, immediately seek medical assistance.

diseases.name: Bronchitis
diseases.description: Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchial tubes, often causing cough with mucus. It can be acute (short-term) or chronic.
symptoms: Cough with mucus
Wheezing
Shortness of breath
Chest tightness
Low-grade fever

diseases.name: Bronchogenic Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bronchogenic cysts are congenital anomalies that arise from the abnormal development of the bronchial tubes during fetal development. These cysts are typically located in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavity, and can vary in size and presentation. While often asymptomatic, bronchogenic cysts can lead to significant health issues if not diagnosed and managed appropriately. Understanding bronchogenic cysts is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Bronchogenic cysts are often asymptomatic, especially when small. However, larger cysts or those that become infected can present with various symptoms, including:
Cough: A persistent cough may occur, particularly if the cyst is compressing the airways.
Chest Pain: Patients may experience discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Shortness of Breath: Larger cysts can obstruct airflow, leading to difficulty breathing.
Fever: If a cyst becomes infected, fever may be present.
Wheezing: This may occur due to airway obstruction.

diseases.name: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) is a serious lung condition primarily affecting premature infants. It is characterized by inflammation and scarring in the lungs, leading to breathing difficulties. BPD is significant not only because of its immediate impact on the health of newborns but also due to its potential long-term effects on respiratory health and overall development. Understanding BPD is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia can vary in severity and may include:
Rapid Breathing: Infants may exhibit tachypnea, or rapid breathing, as their lungs struggle to provide adequate oxygen.
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing can indicate airway obstruction.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially around the lips and fingertips, may signal low oxygen levels.
Poor Feeding: Infants with BPD may have difficulty feeding due to respiratory distress.
Frequent Respiratory Infections: Increased susceptibility to infections can occur due to compromised lung function.

diseases.name: Bronchospasm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bronchospasm is a medical condition characterized by the sudden constriction of the muscles surrounding the airways, leading to difficulty in breathing. This phenomenon is significant because it can be a symptom of various underlying health issues, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and allergic reactions. Understanding bronchospasm is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely recognition and management can prevent severe complications and improve quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of bronchospasm can vary in intensity and may include:
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing, especially when exhaling.
Coughing: A persistent cough that may worsen at night or during physical activity.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of tightness in the chest.
Chest Tightness: A sensation of pressure or constriction in the chest area.

diseases.name: Brown Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brown Syndrome is a rare eye condition that affects the movement of the eye, specifically the ability to elevate the eye in certain positions. This condition can significantly impact a person's vision and quality of life, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options. In this article, we will explore Brown Syndrome in detail, providing a comprehensive overview for those seeking to learn more about this condition.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Brown Syndrome is the inability to elevate the affected eye, particularly when looking inward. Other symptoms may include:
Strabismus: Misalignment of the eyes, often leading to double vision.
Head Tilt: Individuals may tilt their head to compensate for the restricted eye movement.
Eye Fatigue: Prolonged use of the affected eye may lead to discomfort or fatigue.

diseases.name: Brugada Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Brugada Syndrome is a rare but significant cardiac condition that can lead to life-threatening arrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. Named after the Brugada brothers who first described it in the 1990s, this syndrome is characterized by specific changes in the heart's electrical activity. Understanding Brugada Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and management, as it can affect individuals without any prior heart issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Brugada Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Brugada Syndrome may not present any symptoms in many individuals, making it particularly insidious. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Syncope: Fainting or loss of consciousness, often triggered by arrhythmias.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may be mistaken for a heart attack.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical exertion.

diseases.name: Bruxism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bruxism is a condition characterized by the involuntary grinding or clenching of teeth, often occurring during sleep or while awake. While it may seem like a benign habit, bruxism can lead to significant dental and health issues if left untreated. Understanding bruxism is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early intervention can prevent complications and improve quality of life.
symptoms: Bruxism can manifest through various symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Teeth Grinding: The most obvious sign, often reported by partners or family members.
Jaw Pain: Discomfort or pain in the jaw muscles, particularly upon waking.
Headaches: Frequent tension headaches, especially in the temples.
Tooth Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to hot or cold due to enamel wear.
Facial Pain: General discomfort in the face or neck.
Earaches: Pain in the ears, which may be mistaken for an ear infection.

diseases.name: Bubonic Plague - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bubonic plague, often referred to simply as the plague, is a severe infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis . Historically notorious for causing pandemics, including the Black Death in the 14th century, bubonic plague remains a significant public health concern in certain regions of the world today. Understanding this disease is crucial not only for historical context but also for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bubonic plague, making the information accessible to a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of bubonic plague typically appear within 2 to 6 days after exposure to the bacterium. Common symptoms include:
Fever and Chills: Sudden onset of high fever and chills is often the first sign.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Painful, swollen lymph nodes (buboes) are characteristic of bubonic plague and usually appear in the groin, armpit, or neck.
Headache: Many patients experience severe headaches.
Fatigue: General weakness and fatigue are common.
Muscle Aches: Body aches and muscle pain may occur.

diseases.name: Bucket Handle Meniscus Tear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A bucket handle meniscus tear is a specific type of injury to the meniscus, a C-shaped cartilage in the knee that acts as a cushion between the thigh bone (femur) and the shin bone (tibia). This injury is significant because it can lead to pain, swelling, and limited mobility, affecting daily activities and overall quality of life. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for a bucket handle meniscus tear is crucial for anyone who may be at risk or experiencing knee pain.
symptoms: Knee Pain: Pain is often localized to the inner side of the knee and may worsen with movement.
Swelling: Swelling may develop within hours of the injury due to inflammation.
Stiffness: The knee may feel stiff, making it difficult to fully extend or flex the joint.
Locking or Catching: A characteristic symptom of a bucket handle tear is the sensation of the knee locking or catching during movement.
Reduced Range of Motion: Individuals may find it challenging to move their knee through its full range of motion.

diseases.name: Buckle Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A buckle fracture, also known as a torus fracture, is a common type of bone injury, particularly in children. It occurs when one side of the bone buckles or compresses without breaking completely. This type of fracture is significant because it often indicates a less severe injury compared to complete fractures, allowing for a more straightforward treatment and quicker recovery. Understanding buckle fractures is essential for parents, caregivers, and anyone involved in the care of children, as early recognition and appropriate management can lead to better outcomes.
symptoms: Pain: Localized pain at the site of the injury, which may worsen with movement.
Swelling: Swelling around the affected area, often accompanied by tenderness.
Bruising: Discoloration of the skin may occur due to bleeding under the skin.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty using the affected limb, particularly in children who may refuse to use the injured arm or leg.

diseases.name: Bulimia Nervosa - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bulimia Nervosa is a serious eating disorder characterized by a cycle of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, excessive exercise, or the misuse of laxatives. This condition is not just about food; it often reflects deeper emotional struggles and societal pressures. Understanding Bulimia Nervosa is crucial, as it can lead to severe health complications and significantly impact an individual's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Bulimia Nervosa, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Bulimia Nervosa can be both physical and psychological. Common symptoms include:
Binge Eating: Consuming large quantities of food in a short time, often feeling a loss of control during these episodes.
Compensatory Behaviors: Engaging in self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or misuse of laxatives.
Preoccupation with Weight and Body Image: An intense focus on body shape and weight, often leading to distorted self-image.
Physical Signs: Dental erosion, swollen glands, and gastrointestinal issues can occur due to repeated vomiting.

diseases.name: Bullous Emphysema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bullous emphysema is a specific form of emphysema, a chronic lung condition that affects the air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs. This condition is characterized by the formation of large air-filled spaces, known as bullae, which can significantly impair lung function. Understanding bullous emphysema is crucial, as it can lead to serious health complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of bullous emphysema, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of bullous emphysema can vary in severity but often include:
Shortness of Breath: This is the most common symptom, especially during physical activity.
Chronic Cough: A persistent cough that may produce mucus.
Wheezing: A whistling sound when breathing, indicating narrowed airways.
Chest Tightness: A feeling of pressure or constriction in the chest.
Fatigue: General tiredness due to the increased effort required to breathe.

diseases.name: Bullous Myringitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bullous myringitis is a medical condition that affects the eardrum, characterized by the formation of fluid-filled blisters (bullae) on the tympanic membrane. This condition is significant because it can lead to pain, hearing loss, and potential complications if not properly managed. Understanding bullous myringitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, ensuring better outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of bullous myringitis can vary in severity but commonly include:
Ear Pain: Often severe and sharp, this is the most prominent symptom.
Hearing Loss: Temporary hearing impairment may occur due to fluid buildup.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ear can accompany the condition.
Fever: A mild fever may be present, especially if an infection is involved.
Fluid Drainage: In some cases, fluid may drain from the ear if the blisters rupture.

diseases.name: Bulls Eye Maculopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Bulls Eye Maculopathy is a significant ocular condition that primarily affects the macula, the central part of the retina responsible for sharp, detailed vision. This condition is characterized by a distinctive pattern of retinal damage that resembles a bull's eye, hence the name. Understanding Bulls Eye Maculopathy is crucial, as it can lead to severe vision impairment if not diagnosed and managed promptly. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Bulls Eye Maculopathy, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Bulls Eye Maculopathy can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty seeing fine details, especially when reading or recognizing faces.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent, a phenomenon known as metamorphopsia.
Color Perception Changes: Difficulty distinguishing between colors, particularly in the central visual field.
Dark or Empty Spots: Areas of vision may appear dark or missing, known as scotomas.

diseases.name: Bunion – Symptoms, Cause and Remedies
diseases.description: A bunion is a ‘bony bump’ seen at the joint of the base of the big toe. It usually occurs due to displacement of the other bones at the front of the foot, causing the big toe to be pulled towards to the smaller toes while moving the joint in the opposite direction causing it to protrude. This leads to redness and the feeling of the skin being sore over the protruding part of the joint.
symptoms: The symptoms of bunions are:
Swelling, soreness, and redness at the outer part of the base of the big toe
Calluses or corns where the first and second toes run against each other
Pain
Limited movement observed of the big toe

diseases.name: Buphthalmos - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Buphthalmos is a medical term that refers to an abnormal enlargement of the eyeball, primarily seen in children. This condition is often associated with congenital glaucoma, a serious eye disorder that can lead to vision loss if not treated promptly. Understanding buphthalmos is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early detection and intervention can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding buphthalmos.
symptoms: The symptoms of buphthalmos can vary, but common signs include:
Enlarged Eye: The most noticeable symptom is the abnormal enlargement of one or both eyes.
Corneal Clouding: The cornea may appear cloudy or hazy due to increased pressure.
Photophobia: Sensitivity to light is common, causing discomfort in bright environments.
Tearing: Excessive tearing may occur as a response to irritation.
Squinting: Affected individuals may squint or close their eyes to reduce light exposure.

diseases.name: Burkitt Lymphoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: A diagnosis of Burkitt lymphoma can be an overwhelming experience, filled with questions about a disease you may have never heard of. This comprehensive guide is designed to provide clear, compassionate, and authoritative information to help you understand what Burkitt lymphoma is, how it is diagnosed and treated, and what to expect on your journey. We will use simple, patient-friendly language to ensure you feel informed and empowered to navigate this challenge with confidence and hope.
symptoms: Because Burkitt lymphoma grows so quickly, its symptoms tend to appear suddenly and can worsen rapidly. The symptoms depend on where the cancer is located.
Abdominal Pain and Swelling: This is the most common symptom, caused by a rapidly growing mass in the abdomen.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and a feeling of fullness after eating a small amount of food.
Bowel Obstruction: If the tumor blocks the bowel, it can be a medical emergency.
Jaw or Facial Swelling: A rapidly growing mass in the jaw or face.
Swelling Around the Eyes: This can also be a symptom of cancer.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck, armpit, or groin.
Fever: An unexplained fever that comes and goes.
Night Sweats: Drenching night sweats.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
It is crucial to seek immediate medical attention if you notice a rapidly growing lump or mass, especially if it is accompanied by other symptoms.

diseases.name: Burning Mouth Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Burning Mouth Syndrome (BMS) is a complex and often perplexing condition characterized by a burning sensation in the mouth without an obvious cause. This syndrome can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to discomfort, anxiety, and difficulty in eating or speaking. Understanding BMS is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can often be misdiagnosed or overlooked. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Burning Mouth Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Burning Mouth Syndrome is a persistent burning sensation in the mouth, which can vary in intensity. Other common symptoms include:
Dry mouth (xerostomia)
Altered taste sensations (bitter or metallic taste)
Tingling or numbness in the tongue or lips
Increased sensitivity to spicy or acidic foods

diseases.name: Burnout - Stages, Signs, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Are you so worn out or burnout that even moving a muscle feels challenging? Do you have to drag yourself out of bed to work? Does depressing news make you upset for a long time?

diseases.name: Burns - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Burns are a common yet serious injury that can affect anyone, regardless of age or background. They can result from various sources, including heat, chemicals, electricity, and radiation. Understanding burns is crucial not only for prevention but also for effective treatment and recovery. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of burns, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of burns vary depending on the severity:
First-Degree Burns: Redness, minor swelling, and pain.
Second-Degree Burns: Blisters, swelling, and severe pain.
Third-Degree Burns: White, charred skin, and a lack of pain in the burned area due to nerve damage.

diseases.name: Bursitis
diseases.description: Bursitis is a painful condition that affects the small, fluid-filled sacs called bursae that cushion the bones, tendons, and muscles near joints. Bursitis occurs when bursae become inflamed. The most common locations are the shoulder, elbow, and hip. Bursitis often occurs near joints that perform frequent repetitive motion.
symptoms: Achy or stiff joint
Pain that worsens with movement or pressure
Swelling and redness
Limited range of motion

diseases.name: Cafe Au Lait Spots - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cafe Au Lait spots are flat, pigmented birthmarks that can appear on the skin of individuals from various backgrounds. Named after the French term for "coffee with milk," these spots can range in color from light brown to dark brown and can vary in size. While they are generally harmless, their presence can sometimes indicate underlying medical conditions, making it essential for individuals and healthcare providers to understand their significance. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Cafe Au Lait spots.
symptoms: Cafe Au Lait spots are typically asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause pain or discomfort. They are characterized by:
Flat, smooth lesions on the skin
Color ranging from light brown to dark brown
Size varying from small (a few millimeters) to large (several centimeters)

diseases.name: Can Acromegaly be Life-Threatening?
diseases.description: Acromegaly is a condition that happens when the pituitary gland produces excess growth hormone that affect many parts of your body. The onset of this condition is slow and can be challenging to diagnose early. Though acromegaly can cause life-threatening complications, it can be managed.
symptoms: Most of the symptoms of acromegaly are visually apparent. However, these symptoms can vary from person to person. Some of the more common visual acromegaly symptoms include:
● Thick, coarse, and oily skin
● Deeper voice
● A more prominent nose, lips, and tongue
● Hands and feet become bigger.
● Increased body odor and sweating
● More extensive and darker skin tags
● Brow bone or jaw may jut out.
● Increased spacing between the teeth
● muscle weakness and fatigue
● Severe snoring issues due to obstruction of upper airway
● Headaches
● Impaired vision
● Pain & limited joint mobility
● Menstrual cycle irregularities in women
● Erectile dysfunction in men
● Enlarged organs like the heart
● Loss of interest in sex
Non-visual acromegaly symptoms include:
● Joint aches
● Vision problems

diseases.name: Can Gallbladder Stones Go Away Without Surgery?
diseases.description: The gallbladder is a small-sized organ located in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen, below the liver. Its main function is to store bile juice that assists digestion. Gallbladder stones is a medical condition wherein hardened deposits of cholesterol and bilirubin develop and sometimes get lodged in the gallbladder or bile ducts. The size of these stones may vary from the size of a golf ball to a grain of rice. Many stones may develop simultaneously. These stones can leave the gallbladder and get stuck along the way.
symptoms: Usually, gallbladder stones do not exhibit any symptoms. However, if these stones lodge in the bile duct, it might lead to :
Sudden and rapidly growing pain in the upper right part of your abdomen
Sudden and rapidly increasing pain in the centre of your abdomen, just below your breastbone
Back pain between your shoulder blades
Pain in your right shoulder
Nausea or vomiting

diseases.name: Can Peripheral Neuropathy Be Reversed?
diseases.description: The peripheral nervous system is responsible for sending information from the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) to your organs and limbs. The central nervous system also receives sensory information from the peripheral nerves. Neuropathy affects these peripheral nerves. In this condition, a person may feel pain, numbness, and weakness in the affected area.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of peripheral neuropathy that affect motor and sensory nerves include:
Numbness and tingling of the feet and hands, which gradually moves up the arms and legs.
Sensitivity to touch.
Decreased coordination and a tendency to fall.
Weakness of the muscles.
Partial or total paralysis .
Sharp, throbbing pain or burning sensation in the feet and hands.
If your autonomic nerves are affected, then you will experience the following symptoms:
Excessive or no sweating.
Intolerance for heat.
Variance in blood pressure .
Dizziness or light-headedness.
Digestive, bowel, or bladder issues.

diseases.name: Cancer remission - Types, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: If you or your loved one has been diagnosed with cancer, the first thing that comes to mind is, “Is this cancer curable?” Cancer is a complex disease . One of the primary goals of the treatment of most cancers is remission.

diseases.name: Candida Albicans - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Candida albicans is a type of yeast that is commonly found in the human body, particularly in the mouth, gut, and vaginal area. While it usually coexists harmlessly with other microorganisms, it can become pathogenic under certain conditions, leading to infections known as candidiasis. Understanding Candida albicans is crucial not only for recognizing its potential health implications but also for implementing effective prevention and treatment strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Candida albicans infections can vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include:
Oral Thrush: White patches in the mouth, soreness, and difficulty swallowing.
Vaginal Yeast Infections: Itching, burning, and a thick, white discharge.
Skin Infections: Red, itchy rashes, often in warm, moist areas of the body.
Invasive Candidiasis: Fever, chills, and symptoms related to the affected organs.

diseases.name: Candida Auris - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Candida auris is a type of fungus that has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its alarming ability to cause severe infections, particularly in healthcare settings. First identified in 2009, this organism has emerged as a global health threat, primarily affecting individuals with weakened immune systems. Its significance lies not only in its resistance to multiple antifungal medications but also in its potential to spread rapidly in hospitals and nursing homes, leading to outbreaks that can be difficult to control. This article aims to provide a thorough understanding of Candida auris, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Candida auris infections can vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include:
Fever and chills: Often the first signs of a bloodstream infection.
Wound infections: Redness, swelling, and discharge from the infected area.
Ear infections: Pain, itching, and discharge from the ear.
Respiratory symptoms: Cough, difficulty breathing, and chest pain if the lungs are involved.

diseases.name: Candida Parapsilosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Candida parapsilosis is a type of yeast that is part of the normal flora of the human body, particularly found on the skin and mucous membranes. While it is typically harmless in healthy individuals, it can become pathogenic, leading to infections, especially in immunocompromised patients. Understanding Candida parapsilosis is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as it can have significant implications for health, particularly in hospital settings where vulnerable populations are present.
symptoms: The symptoms of Candida parapsilosis infections can vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include:
Skin Infections: Redness, itching, and rash, often in warm, moist areas of the body.
Nail Infections: Discoloration, thickening, and separation of the nail from the nail bed.
Systemic Infections: Fever, chills, and malaise, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.

diseases.name: Canker Sores - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Canker sores, also known as aphthous ulcers, are small, painful lesions that develop in the mouth. They can make eating, drinking, and speaking uncomfortable, significantly impacting a person's quality of life. While canker sores are not contagious, their presence can be distressing and may indicate underlying health issues. Understanding canker sores, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for effective management and prevention.
symptoms: Canker sores can cause a range of symptoms, including:
Painful Ulcers: The primary symptom is the presence of painful sores in the mouth, which can make eating, drinking, and speaking uncomfortable.
Burning Sensation: Many individuals report a burning or tingling sensation in the area before the sore appears.
Swelling: Surrounding tissues may become swollen and red.
Difficulty Eating or Drinking: The pain associated with canker sores can lead to difficulty consuming food and beverages.

diseases.name: Capillary Leak Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS) is a rare but significant medical condition characterized by the sudden and severe leakage of fluid from the capillaries into surrounding tissues. This phenomenon can lead to a range of serious health issues, including swelling, low blood pressure, and organ dysfunction. Understanding CLS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve patient outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Capillary Leak Syndrome.
symptoms: The symptoms of Capillary Leak Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the arms, legs, and abdomen due to fluid accumulation.
Low Blood Pressure: A significant drop in blood pressure can lead to dizziness, fainting, or shock.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may beat faster in an attempt to compensate for low blood volume.
Fatigue: Generalized weakness and fatigue are common as the body struggles to maintain adequate circulation.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may occur due to fluid shifts and decreased blood flow to the digestive system.

diseases.name: Caput Succedaneum: Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: One may come across a newborn with a cone-shaped head and wonder about the reasons for this occurrence. This may be caput succedaneum.
symptoms: One of the main symptoms of caput succedaneum is swelling of the scalp. The skin is swollen and soft; pressing it creates a dimple. The scalp swells either on one side of the skull or may extend across the midline of the scalp.

The swelling usually happens on that part of the skull that was the first to come down the birth canal. Discolouration or bruising is also normal in this case but not as extensive as in cephalohematoma.

Once the swelling reduces, one may notice that the baby’s head is slightly pointed due to the pressure on the bones of the head, which is called moulding. It gradually goes away over time since the bones of the head of the baby aren’t fused and can remould without damage. This condition can be diagnosed with a physical exam .

diseases.name: Carcinoid Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carcinoid Syndrome is a complex medical condition that arises from neuroendocrine tumors, primarily affecting the gastrointestinal tract and lungs. These tumors secrete hormones and other substances that can lead to a variety of symptoms, significantly impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding Carcinoid Syndrome is crucial not only for patients but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and management can lead to better outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Carcinoid Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Carcinoid Syndrome manifests through a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity and frequency. Common symptoms include:
Flushing: Sudden reddening of the skin, often accompanied by a feeling of warmth.
Diarrhea: Frequent, watery stools that can lead to dehydration and electrolyte imbalances.
Wheezing: Difficulty breathing due to bronchoconstriction, which can mimic asthma.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the abdomen, often related to gastrointestinal disturbances.
Heart Issues: Some patients may develop carcinoid heart disease, leading to valve dysfunction.

diseases.name: Carcinoma : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The most common type of cancer is carcinoma. It accounts for nearly 90% of all cancer diagnoses. Carcinomas form on the tissues that protect your organs, internal passageways in your body, and skin and also in organs like lungs, breasts, prostate, colon, kidneys, pancreas, and other organs. This type of cancer creates abnormal cells that uncontrollably divide and spread to the other body parts. It is essential to note that not all cancers are carcinomas.
symptoms: Each carcinoma exhibits different symptoms. They are as follows.
Adenocarcinoma symptoms:
If you have breast cancer, you experience a lump in the breast and nipple discharge
In the case of lung cancer , you show signs of coughing bloody mucus, chest pain , and breathing issues
Pancreatic cancer causes jaundice , dark urine, weight loss, back or stomach pain
When you have colon cancer , you experience issues in the bowel movement, rectal bleeding, stomach pain, and unexplained weight loss
Invasive ductal carcinoma symptoms:
Lumps in the breast
Skin darkening
Swelling
Dimpling around the nipple
Nipple discharge
Lumps in the armpit
Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) symptoms:
Small lumps in the breast
Discharge from the nipples
Renal cell carcinoma symptoms:
Loss of appetite
Unexplained weight loss
Extreme pain in the side of the body
A lump in the abdomen
Blood when urinating
Anemia
Squamous cell carcinoma symptoms:
Skin patches that are scaly and dark
Open sores with raised borders
Firm growths
Spots that are similar to age spots
Wart-like and horn-like growths
Sores on the scars
Basal cell carcinoma symptoms:
Open sores that do not heal
Dark patches of skin
Shiny bumps
Raised scar-like areas

diseases.name: Cardiac Amyloidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiac amyloidosis is a rare but serious condition that affects the heart's ability to function properly. It occurs when abnormal proteins, known as amyloid, build up in the heart tissue, leading to stiffening and impaired function. This condition is significant because it can lead to heart failure and other serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding cardiac amyloidosis is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of cardiac amyloidosis can vary widely but often include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or when lying down.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or weakness that does not improve with rest.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen due to fluid retention.
Irregular Heartbeat: Palpitations or a feeling of a racing heart.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may mimic angina.

diseases.name: Cardiac Arrest
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Cardiac Arrest Symptoms are very immediate and drastic, and come without any warning:
Sudden collapse
No pulse
No breathing
Loss of consciousness
Fatigue and weakness
Fainting, blackouts, dizziness
Chest pain, shortness of breath and palpitations
Vomiting

diseases.name: Cardiac Cachexia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiac cachexia is a serious condition that affects individuals with heart disease, leading to significant weight loss, muscle wasting, and a decline in overall health. It is often overlooked but is crucial to recognize due to its impact on the quality of life and prognosis of patients with heart failure. Understanding cardiac cachexia is essential for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of cardiac cachexia can vary but often include:
Unintentional Weight Loss: Significant weight loss over a short period, often more than 5% of body weight in six months.
Muscle Wasting: Noticeable loss of muscle mass, particularly in the arms and legs.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy, making daily activities challenging.
Weakness: Generalized weakness and reduced physical strength.
Loss of Appetite: Decreased desire to eat, leading to further weight loss.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen due to fluid retention.

diseases.name: Cardiac Sarcoidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiac sarcoidosis is a rare but significant condition that affects the heart, characterized by the formation of small clusters of inflammatory cells known as granulomas. These granulomas can disrupt the normal functioning of the heart, leading to various complications. Understanding cardiac sarcoidosis is crucial, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cardiac sarcoidosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of cardiac sarcoidosis can vary widely among individuals. Some may experience no symptoms, while others may have significant heart-related issues. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or at rest.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of a racing heart.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Dizziness or Fainting: Lightheadedness or loss of consciousness, especially during exertion.

diseases.name: Cardiac Tamponade - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiac tamponade is a serious medical condition that occurs when fluid accumulates in the pericardial sac surrounding the heart, leading to increased pressure on the heart and impaired function. This condition can be life-threatening if not recognized and treated promptly. Understanding cardiac tamponade is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding cardiac tamponade.
symptoms: The symptoms of cardiac tamponade can vary depending on the severity and speed of fluid accumulation. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially when lying down, is a common symptom.
Chest Pain or Discomfort: Patients may experience pressure or pain in the chest.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may beat faster in an attempt to compensate for reduced cardiac output.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness can occur.
Swelling: Fluid retention may lead to swelling in the legs, abdomen, or other areas.

diseases.name: Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema (CPE) is a serious medical condition characterized by the accumulation of fluid in the lungs due to heart failure. This condition can lead to severe respiratory distress and requires immediate medical attention. Understanding CPE is crucial not only for those at risk but also for the general public, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
symptoms: Shortness of Breath: Often worsens with exertion or when lying flat.
Coughing: May produce frothy or pink-tinged sputum.
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing.
Chest Pain: May occur if there is an underlying heart condition.
