Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate as the body attempts to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Feeling of Suffocation: A sense of panic or anxiety due to difficulty breathing.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen may be present.

diseases.name: Cardiogenic Shock - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiogenic shock is a critical medical condition that occurs when the heart is unable to pump enough blood to meet the body's needs. This condition can lead to severe complications and even death if not treated promptly. Cardiogenic shock is significant because it often arises from underlying heart problems, such as a heart attack, and requires immediate medical intervention. Understanding cardiogenic shock, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is essential for both patients and caregivers.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of cardiogenic shock is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart beats faster in an attempt to compensate for reduced blood flow.
Low Blood Pressure: Blood pressure drops significantly, leading to inadequate perfusion of organs.
Cold, Clammy Skin: Reduced blood flow can cause the skin to feel cool and sweaty.
Weakness or Fatigue: Patients may feel unusually weak or tired due to insufficient blood flow.
Confusion or Altered Mental State: Lack of oxygen to the brain can lead to confusion or disorientation.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may occur due to fluid accumulation in the lungs.

diseases.name: Cardiomyopathy
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Cardiomyopathy symptoms or signs cannot be detected in the early stages. But as the condition advances or worsens, the following symptoms are usually seen:
Bloating of the abdomen due to fluid buildup
Breathlessness due to exertion or even at rest
Chest pain
Coughing while lying down
Dizziness, lightheadedness and fainting
Fatigue
Irregular heartbeats
Swelling of the legs, ankles and feet

diseases.name: Cardiorenal Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cardiorenal Syndrome (CRS) is a complex medical condition that highlights the intricate relationship between the heart and kidneys. This syndrome occurs when dysfunction in one organ leads to dysfunction in the other, creating a vicious cycle that can significantly impact a patient's overall health. Understanding Cardiorenal Syndrome is crucial, as it affects millions of people worldwide and can lead to severe complications if not properly managed. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Cardiorenal Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Cardiorenal Syndrome can vary depending on which organ is primarily affected. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Often due to fluid overload from heart failure.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen due to fluid retention.
Fatigue: Generalized weakness and tiredness from reduced organ function.
Nausea and Vomiting: Can occur due to kidney dysfunction.
Chest Pain: May indicate heart issues or fluid overload.

diseases.name: Caring for a Baby With Marfan Syndrome
diseases.description: Marfan syndrome or MFS is a genetic condition that affects the connective tissue of the body. Connective tissue provides support, elasticity, and strength to your body while securing the organs and other vital parts (including cartilage, tendons, blood vessels, and heart valves, among others) together. This syndrome affects your skeleton, eyes, heart, and blood vessels.
symptoms: The symptoms of Marfan disease differ from one person to the other and even amongst family members. Some show mild Marfanoid features, while some suffer from life-threatening conditions. However, this genetic abnormality worsens with age, in most cases.
Some of the common signs and symptoms of this disease include the following:
● Tall and slim stature.
● Flat feet.
● Unreasonably long legs, arms, and fingers
● Breastbone protruding outward or sinking inward.
● Heart murmurs.
● Crowded teeth.
● Arched and high palate.
● Abnormally arched spine.
● Severe nearsightedness.

In case you, your child, or any of your family members exhibit the features, get in touch with your doctor. If your doctor feels that there is a problem, they are likely to refer you to a specialist for detailed evaluation.

diseases.name: Carney Complex - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carney Complex is a rare genetic disorder that significantly impacts multiple organ systems, leading to a variety of tumors and other health issues. Understanding Carney Complex is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Carney Complex, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Carney Complex can vary widely among individuals, but common manifestations include:
Cardiac Myxomas: These are the most common tumors associated with Carney Complex and can lead to heart murmurs, palpitations, or even heart failure.
Skin Tumors: Individuals may develop pigmented lesions, such as lentigines or blue nevi.
Endocrine Tumors: These can include adrenal tumors, which may cause hormonal imbalances leading to symptoms like weight gain, high blood pressure, or changes in menstrual cycles.
Other Tumors: Tumors may also develop in the breast, pancreas, or other organs.

diseases.name: Caroli Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Caroli Disease is a rare congenital disorder that primarily affects the bile ducts within the liver. It is characterized by the dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts, leading to a range of complications that can significantly impact liver function and overall health. Understanding Caroli Disease is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers, as early detection and management can greatly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Caroli Disease, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Caroli Disease can vary widely among individuals, but common manifestations include:
Abdominal Pain: Often located in the upper right quadrant, this pain can be intermittent or persistent.
Jaundice: A yellowing of the skin and eyes due to bile accumulation.
Fever and Chills: These may indicate an infection, such as cholangitis, which is an inflammation of the bile ducts.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur due to bile duct obstruction or infection.
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue may result from liver dysfunction.

diseases.name: Carotid Artery Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carotid Artery Disease (CAD) is a significant health concern that affects millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the carotid arteries, which supply blood to the brain, become narrowed or blocked due to a buildup of fatty deposits, known as plaque. This condition can lead to serious complications, including stroke, which is one of the leading causes of death and disability globally. Understanding CAD is crucial for early detection, effective management, and prevention of its potentially life-threatening consequences.
symptoms: Carotid Artery Disease can often be asymptomatic, especially in its early stages. However, as the disease progresses, individuals may experience various symptoms, including:

Transient Ischemic Attacks (TIAs): Often referred to as "mini-strokes," TIAs can cause temporary symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking. These episodes typically resolve within a few minutes to hours but indicate a higher risk of a full-blown stroke.
Stroke Symptoms: Sudden onset of severe headache, confusion, difficulty walking, or loss of coordination may indicate a stroke, requiring immediate medical attention.
Vision Problems: Sudden loss of vision in one eye or double vision can occur due to reduced blood flow to the brain.

diseases.name: Carotid Body Tumors - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carotid body tumors, also known as carotid body paragangliomas, are rare neoplasms that arise from the carotid body, a small cluster of chemoreceptor cells located at the bifurcation of the common carotid artery. These tumors are significant due to their potential to cause serious health complications, including vascular and neurological issues, if left untreated. Understanding carotid body tumors is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Carotid body tumors may not present symptoms in their early stages. However, as they grow, they can cause various symptoms, including:
Painless Neck Mass: The most common presentation is a palpable mass in the neck, often located near the angle of the jaw.
Difficulty Swallowing: Compression of the esophagus can lead to dysphagia.
Hoarseness: Tumors may affect the recurrent laryngeal nerve, leading to voice changes.
Headaches: Increased intracranial pressure or nerve involvement can cause headaches.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Vascular compression may lead to symptoms of reduced blood flow.

diseases.name: Carpal Boss - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carpal Boss is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it represents a significant condition affecting the wrist and hand. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Carpal Boss, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. Understanding this condition is crucial for those who may be experiencing symptoms or are at risk, as early intervention can lead to better outcomes.
symptoms: Bony Growth: A noticeable bump on the back of the wrist.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the wrist, especially during movement.
Swelling: Mild swelling around the affected area.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty in fully extending or flexing the wrist.

diseases.name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
diseases.description: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common condition that causes pain, numbness, and tingling in the hand and arm. The condition occurs when one of the major nerves to the hand — the median nerve — is squeezed or compressed as it travels through a narrow passageway in the wrist called the carpal tunnel.
symptoms: Numbness, tingling, or pain in the thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers
Occasional shock-like sensations that radiate to the thumb and index, middle, and ring fingers
Pain or tingling that may travel up the forearm toward the shoulder
Weakness and clumsiness in the hand
Dropping things

diseases.name: Carpenter Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Carpenter Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects various aspects of physical development. It is characterized by a combination of craniosynostosis (premature fusion of skull bones), obesity, and distinctive facial features. Understanding Carpenter Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for healthcare providers, families, and communities. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Carpenter Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Carpenter Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Craniosynostosis: Premature fusion of skull bones leading to an abnormal head shape.
Obesity: Many individuals with Carpenter Syndrome experience obesity due to metabolic issues.
Distinctive Facial Features: These may include a broad forehead, wide-set eyes, and a flat nasal bridge.
Skeletal Abnormalities: This can include fusion of fingers or toes (syndactyly) and other limb deformities.
Cognitive Challenges: Some individuals may experience developmental delays or learning difficulties.

diseases.name: Caseous Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Caseous necrosis is a specific type of tissue death characterized by the formation of a cheese-like (caseous) appearance in affected tissues. This phenomenon is most commonly associated with certain infections, particularly tuberculosis, and can have significant implications for health. Understanding caseous necrosis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, as well as for preventing potential complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of caseous necrosis can vary depending on the underlying cause and the location of the necrotic tissue. Common symptoms may include:
Cough: A persistent cough, often with sputum production, is common in pulmonary tuberculosis.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest may occur, especially if the lungs are affected.
Fever: Low-grade fever is often present, indicating an ongoing infection.
Night Sweats: Excessive sweating during the night is a classic symptom of tuberculosis.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can occur due to chronic infection and metabolic changes.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue and weakness are common in individuals with chronic infections.

diseases.name: Cataract
diseases.description: A cataract is formed due to clouding of the area around the lens of the eye. It blocks the passage of light into the retina. Hence, it causes problems in vision.
symptoms: Cataract symptoms include:
Dim, clouded or blurred vision
Fading of colors
Double vision in affected eye
Problem with light and glare
Visualizing a halo effect around a light source

diseases.name: Catatonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Catatonia is a complex neuropsychiatric condition characterized by a range of motor and behavioral symptoms. It can manifest as a state of unresponsiveness, excessive movement, or a combination of both. Understanding catatonia is crucial, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and may indicate underlying medical or psychiatric disorders. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of catatonia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Catatonia can present with a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Stupor: A state of unresponsiveness where the individual does not react to external stimuli.
Mutism: Lack of verbal communication despite the ability to speak.
Posturing: Maintaining a fixed position for an extended period, often in an unusual posture.
Rigidity: Increased muscle tone leading to stiffness and resistance to movement.
Agitation: Excessive movement or restlessness, often without a clear purpose.
Echolalia: Repeating words or phrases spoken by others.
Echopraxia: Imitating the movements of others.

diseases.name: Catatonic Schizophrenia - Symptoms, Causes, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: Catatonic schizophrenia is a serious mental illness and a subset of schizophrenia . An individual who is afflicted with schizophrenia and is also diagnosed with catatonia at the same time is said to be suffering from catatonic schizophrenia.
symptoms: Catatonia may show up in a variety of ways. A commonly observed symptom in individuals with catatonic schizophrenia is limited motor movements even though they are physically capable of mobility. The doctor may diagnose catatonia (or catatonic schizophrenia), if you display at least three of the below 12 features, You:
You stay silent (mute)
Stupor: React very little or are unmoving to what is happening around you
Mannerisms: Make odd gestures or movements
Posturing: Hold your leg up or keep other uncomfortable positions for a longer time
Waxy flexibility: Stay locked in an awkward position for a longer time and resist any attempt to move you
Echopraxia: Mimic someone else’s movements
Echolalia: Mimic someone else’s speech
Passively let other individuals position your limbs or other parts or body
Ignore requests or instructions
Are agitated or hyperactive for no reason
Stereotypy: Repeat senseless gestures, such as rocking, shrugging and waving
Contort your face into a grimace

diseases.name: Caudal Regression Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Caudal Regression Syndrome (CRS) is a rare congenital disorder that primarily affects the development of the lower spine and associated structures. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on physical health but also due to the challenges it poses for affected individuals and their families. Understanding CRS is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Caudal Regression Syndrome can vary significantly from one individual to another, depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Lower Limb Malformations: This may include clubfoot, absence of toes, or underdeveloped legs.
Spinal Anomalies: Individuals may have a shortened or malformed spine, leading to issues with posture and mobility.
Bowel and Bladder Dysfunction: Many individuals with CRS experience difficulties with bowel and bladder control, which can lead to incontinence.
Skeletal Abnormalities: Some may have additional skeletal issues, such as scoliosis or hip dislocation.
Neurological Issues: In severe cases, neurological complications may arise due to spinal cord involvement.

diseases.name: Cauliflower Ear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cauliflower ear is a condition that affects the outer ear, resulting in a distinctive, swollen appearance resembling a cauliflower. This deformity is not just a cosmetic issue; it can lead to significant complications if left untreated. Understanding cauliflower ear is essential for athletes, particularly those involved in contact sports like wrestling, boxing, and rugby, where the risk of ear trauma is heightened. This article will explore the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for cauliflower ear, providing a comprehensive overview for those seeking to understand this condition.
symptoms: Swelling: The most noticeable symptom is swelling of the outer ear, which may appear red or bruised.
Pain: There may be tenderness or pain in the affected area, especially if the ear is touched.
Deformity: Over time, the ear may take on a lumpy, irregular shape.
Warmth: The area may feel warm to the touch, indicating inflammation.

diseases.name: Causes and Symptoms of Rheumatoid Arthritis
diseases.description: When our joints ache, we often chalk it up to an old injury or osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis — the wearing away of cartilage, which is common as people age, but aching joints could be even due to rheumatoid arthritis- the most severe, unremitting form of arthritis that continues for decades and causes debilitating joint damage.
symptoms: Unlike osteoarthritis , which is limited to the joints and can be treated with mild pain relievers or even exercise or can be resolved with joint replacement surgery. RA is a progressive disease that can damage the joints, tendons, and bones and affect the whole body, including vital organs such as the heart, lungs, and eyes. The most prominent tip-off to RA is the presence of persistent swelling in multiple joints that don’t occur in other types of joint pain. Other classic symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis include joint pain that gets worse in the morning and gets better with movement, the presence of lumps or rheumatoid nodules below the skin and persistent fatigue . While some uncommon symptoms include fever, weight loss, anemia , and depression . Also Read About: Swelling in The Knee

diseases.name: Causes and treatment for Muscular Dystrophy
diseases.description: Muscular dystrophy refers to a group of inherited diseases which damage and weaken your muscles over time. They cause loss of muscle mass and lack of the dystrophin protein which is required for normal muscle function. Mutations take place and abnormal genes interfere with the normal production of proteins that are needed to form and maintain healthy muscles. It can occur at any age, but most cases are diagnosed at childhood. Muscular dystrophy is a rare medical condition. So, it is important for us to learn more about this progressive muscular weakness disease.
symptoms: There are more than 30 types of muscular dystrophy, all of which vary in their symptoms and severity. For diagnosis, there are nine different categories referred to. Specific signs start at different ages, in different muscle groups, depending on the type. Here are the common symptoms for the general categories:

Duchenne type This is the most common form. It is much more prevalent in boys. Signs and symptoms include difficulty in running and jumping, frequent falls, waddling gait, large calf muscles, trouble getting up from lying or sitting position, muscle pain, stiffness and learning disabilities.

diseases.name: Cavernous Hemangioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cavernous hemangioma is a type of benign vascular tumor that primarily consists of a mass of blood vessels. These tumors can occur in various parts of the body, including the skin, liver, and brain. While they are generally non-cancerous and often asymptomatic, their presence can lead to complications depending on their size and location. Understanding cavernous hemangiomas is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals receive appropriate care when necessary.
symptoms: Cavernous hemangiomas can be asymptomatic, especially when they are small. However, larger lesions or those located in critical areas may present various symptoms, including:
Visible Lesions: A raised, reddish-blue mass on the skin or mucous membranes.
Pain or Discomfort: Depending on the location, individuals may experience pain or discomfort.
Bleeding: In some cases, cavernous hemangiomas can bleed, especially if they are located in areas prone to trauma.
Neurological Symptoms: Hemangiomas in the brain may lead to headaches, seizures, or neurological deficits.

diseases.name: Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: When blood clots in the cavernous sinuses, it is known as cavernous sinus thrombosis. The cavernous sinus is a hollow space behind each eye socket and underneath the brain. It is a life-threatening condition that needs immediate medical attention and can affect adults and children equally. In nearly 30% of cases of Cavernous sinus thrombosis , it causes death.
symptoms: Cavernous sinus thrombosis symptoms may include:
Swelling, irritation or redness around one or both the eyes
Severe headache accompanied often by tearing
Inability to move the eye
Drooping eyelids
Fatigue
High fever
Seizures
Altered mental status, which may range from confusion to coma
Numbness or pain around the face or eyes
Double vision or vision loss
As cavernous sinus thrombosis affects the eyes, the patient may experience the following symptoms:
Swelling and bulging of the eyes starts from one eye and moves to the other eye as well
Severe pain in the eye
Red eyes
Vision issues, such as double or blurred vision
Difficulty moving eyes
Droopy eyelids
Pain and numbness in the face and eyes
The other symptoms of cavernous sinus thrombosis are as follows:
Sudden onset of high fever
Vomiting
Change in the mental state, such as confusion
Severe headache accompanied by tearing
Pain
If left untreated, the infection can spread throughout the body. Patients may experience drowsiness and slip into a coma. Death may also follow.

diseases.name: Cavities - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cavities, also known as dental caries or tooth decay, are one of the most common dental problems affecting people of all ages. They occur when the hard surface of a tooth is damaged, leading to the formation of holes or openings. Cavities can cause pain, infection, and even tooth loss if left untreated. Understanding cavities is crucial not only for maintaining oral health but also for overall well-being, as dental issues can impact nutrition, self-esteem, and quality of life.
symptoms: Cavities may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in the early stages. However, as they progress, individuals may experience:
Tooth Sensitivity: Pain or discomfort when consuming hot, cold, or sweet foods and beverages.
Visible Holes or Pits: Noticeable holes in the teeth, which may be dark or discolored.
Toothache: Persistent pain in the affected tooth, which can range from mild to severe.
Bad Breath: Foul-smelling breath that does not improve with brushing.
Swelling or Redness: Inflammation of the gums surrounding the affected tooth.

diseases.name: Celiac Disease - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Celiac disease is a digestive disorder resulting from an abnormal immune reaction to gluten.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of celiac disease in children and adults are different. Some of the symptoms seen in children are:
Diarrhea
Fatigue
Weight loss
Bloating and gas
Abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting
Constipation
Anemia , typically from iron deficiency
Depletion of bone density ( osteoporosis ) or softening of the bone (osteomalacia)
Itchy, blistery skin rash (dermatitis herpetiformis)
Mouth ulcers
Headaches and fatigue
Nervous system injury, as well as numbness and tingling in the feet and hands, potential problems with balance, and cognitive impairment
Joint pain
Decreased spleen functioning (hyposplenism)
The lack of ability to absorb nutrients in children can lead to:
Failure to thrive for infants
Damage to tooth enamel
Anemia
Irritability
Short stature
Delayed puberty
Neurological symptoms, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), headaches, learning disabilities, insufficient muscle coordination, and seizures

diseases.name: Cellulite - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cellulite is a common skin condition that affects a significant portion of the adult population, particularly women. Characterized by a dimpled, lumpy appearance on the skin, cellulite can be a source of concern for many individuals. While it is not a medical condition that poses health risks, its aesthetic implications can lead to psychological distress and affect self-esteem. Understanding cellulite, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for those seeking to manage its appearance effectively.
symptoms: The primary symptom of cellulite is the dimpled appearance of the skin, which can vary in severity. Other symptoms may include:
Skin Texture Changes: The skin may feel rough or uneven to the touch.
Fatigue: Some individuals report a feeling of heaviness in the affected areas.
Discomfort: In rare cases, cellulite may cause mild discomfort or tenderness.

diseases.name: Cellulitis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The possible cellulitis symptoms are:
Blisters
Fever
Pain
Red spots
Skin dimpling
Swelling of arms and legs
Tenderness
Warmth
Nausea
Obesity
It is better to seek immediate medical help if the patient has a high fever, vomiting, increased pain, or numbness in the area when touched.

diseases.name: Central Nervous System (CNS) Lymphoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma is a rare cancer that starts in or spreads to the brain, spinal cord, eyes (vitreoretinal lymphoma), or the coverings of the brain and spinal cord (meninges). It is most often a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). While the diagnosis can feel overwhelming, timely, coordinated care has significantly improved outcomes. This article explains CNS lymphoma - what it is, who gets it, symptoms to watch for, how it's diagnosed and treated, recovery and follow-up at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the tumor's location and size, and whether the brain, spinal cord, eyes, or meninges are involved. They can develop over days to weeks.
Persistent headaches, worse in the morning or with coughing/straining
Nausea, vomiting, or new seizures
Weakness or numbness on one side of the body
Changes in speech, vision, balance, or coordination
Personality changes, confusion, memory loss, or slowed thinking
Back pain, limb weakness, numbness, or tingling
Bowel or bladder changes
Neck stiffness or sensitivity to light (meningeal irritation)
Blurry vision, floaters, sensitivity to light
Eye pain or redness in some cases
Any new, persistent neurological symptom—especially if worsening—should be evaluated promptly. Early imaging and specialist assessment are crucial.

diseases.name: Central Serous Retinopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Central Serous Retinopathy (CSR) is a condition that affects the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. It is characterized by the accumulation of fluid under the retina, leading to visual disturbances. CSR is significant not only because of its impact on vision but also due to its association with various lifestyle factors and underlying health conditions. Understanding CSR is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can help preserve vision and improve quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Central Serous Retinopathy can vary in severity and may include:
Blurred Vision: A common symptom where objects appear out of focus.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent.
Dark or Empty Areas: Patients may notice dark spots or areas in their central vision.
Color Perception Changes: Colors may appear less vibrant or altered.

diseases.name: Cephalopelvic Disproportion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cephalopelvic Disproportion (CPD) is a significant obstetric condition that occurs when a baby's head is too large to fit through the mother's pelvis during childbirth. This condition can lead to complications during labor and delivery, making it a critical topic for expectant parents and healthcare providers alike. Understanding CPD is essential for ensuring safe delivery and minimizing risks to both mother and child.
symptoms: Prolonged Labor: One of the most common signs of CPD is a labor that lasts significantly longer than expected.
Failure to Progress: The cervix may not dilate adequately despite strong contractions.
Fetal Distress: Changes in the baby's heart rate may indicate distress, often due to prolonged labor.
Pelvic Pain: Mothers may experience significant discomfort or pain in the pelvic region during labor.

diseases.name: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) is a condition characterized by the accumulation of amyloid protein in the walls of the blood vessels in the brain. This buildup can lead to a range of neurological issues, including strokes and cognitive decline. Understanding CAA is crucial, as it significantly impacts the health and quality of life of affected individuals, particularly the elderly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of CAA, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of CAA can vary widely, but common manifestations include:
Headaches: Often described as severe and sudden, these headaches may be indicative of bleeding in the brain.
Cognitive Decline: Memory loss, confusion, and difficulty concentrating can occur as the disease progresses.
Seizures: Some individuals may experience seizures, particularly if there is significant brain damage.
Stroke Symptoms: Sudden weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking can indicate a stroke, which may be caused by CAA.

diseases.name: Cerebral Hypoxia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cerebral hypoxia is a medical condition characterized by a deficiency of oxygen in the brain. This condition can have serious implications for brain function and overall health. Understanding cerebral hypoxia is crucial, as it can lead to irreversible brain damage if not addressed promptly. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of cerebral hypoxia, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of cerebral hypoxia is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Confusion or Disorientation: Individuals may experience difficulty thinking clearly or may seem confused.
Headaches: Persistent or severe headaches can indicate reduced oxygen supply to the brain.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A feeling of faintness or unsteadiness can occur due to inadequate oxygen.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may accompany cerebral hypoxia, especially if it is related to respiratory issues.
Loss of Consciousness: In severe cases, individuals may faint or lose consciousness.

diseases.name: Cerebral Infarction- Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: A cerebral infarction is a medical condition that occurs when the blood flow to the brain is disrupted due to issues with the arteries that supply it. A lack of sufficient blood supply to brain cells deprives them of oxygen and critical nutrients, potentially leading to the death of brain cells. This condition is also called an ischemic stroke.
symptoms: Contralateral hemiparesis is a symptom that occurs when an infarct occurs in the primary motor cortex.
Infarctions also cause weakness and loss of sensation. On physical examination, the following are discovered:
Sudden confusion
Sudden trouble in speaking or difficulty in understanding speech
Sudden weakness, or numbness in the face, arm or leg, specifically on one side of the body
Sudden trouble in visibility – in one or both eyes.
Sudden dizziness, loss of balance, trouble walking or lack of coordination.

diseases.name: Cerebral Palsy - Causes, Symptoms, Types, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Cerebral palsy (CP) refers to a group of neurological disorders that appear in infancy or the early childhood and permanently affect the body movement, muscle tone, posture and coordination. Cerebral palsy (CP) is caused by abnormalities inside or damage to the developing brain which disrupt the ability of our brain to control the movement and maintain posture as wells balance. The term cerebral refers to the brain; palsy refers to the loss or impairment of motor function.
symptoms: Cerebral palsy symptoms vary and can be found in early childhood. The ones affected by cerebral palsy may face movement problems such as:
Stiff and floppy muscles
Rigidity in movement of muscles
Involuntary movements
Excessive swallowing or drooling
Difficulty in speaking
Difficulty in holding objects
Difficulty in walking
Difficulty in writhing movements
Other abnormalities with cerebral palsy lead to neurological problems. Persons having cerebral palsy may also suffer from:
Blindness
Deafness
Oral problems
Intellectual disability
Seizures
Psychiatric health problems

diseases.name: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis (CVST) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that occurs when a blood clot forms in the brain's venous sinuses. These sinuses are responsible for draining blood from the brain, and when they become blocked, it can lead to increased intracranial pressure, brain swelling, and even stroke. Understanding CVST is crucial, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of CVST, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of CVST can vary widely depending on the location and extent of the clot. Common symptoms include:
Headache: Often described as the worst headache ever experienced, it may be sudden and severe.
Vision Changes: Blurred or double vision can occur due to increased pressure on the optic nerve.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may arise from increased intracranial pressure.
Seizures: Some individuals may experience seizures as a result of brain swelling.
Neurological Deficits: Weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking may occur, depending on the affected brain area.

diseases.name: Cervical Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Cervical cancer starts in the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina. In most cases, it develops slowly from precancerous changes of the cervix (called CIN1–3), which can be treated before they turn into cancer. With regular screening and timely treatment, cervical cancer is one of the most preventable and curable cancers. This comprehensive, patient-friendly article explains what cervical cancer is, how it's diagnosed, modern treatments, recovery, and prevention, so informed, confident decisions are easier at every step.
symptoms: Early cervical cancer often causes no symptoms, which is why screening is essential. When symptoms do occur, they can be subtle at first.
Pelvic or lower back pain
Painful urination or blood in urine
Swelling of the legs (if lymph drainage is blocked)
Fatigue, weight loss, or loss of appetite
Any unusual bleeding or discharge should be evaluated promptly, especially after menopause or after sexual intercourse.
Pap test (Pap smear): looks for precancerous and cancerous cells on the cervix.
HPV test: detects high-risk HPV types; a positive result may lead to closer follow-up.
Co-testing: Pap + HPV together at defined intervals (varies by age and region-specific guidelines).
Colposcopy: a magnified exam of the cervix using a special microscope; highlights abnormal areas.
Biopsy: small tissue samples taken during colposcopy to confirm precancer or cancer.
Endocervical sampling: evaluates the canal if needed.

Early stages often have no symptoms. When present, early signs include abnormal vaginal bleeding (between periods, after sex, or after menopause) and unusual discharge. Any abnormal bleeding should be evaluated promptly.

diseases.name: Cervical Dystonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical dystonia, also known as spasmodic torticollis, is a neurological movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions in the neck, leading to abnormal head positions and movements. This condition can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, affecting daily activities, social interactions, and emotional well-being. Understanding cervical dystonia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing those affected to lead more fulfilling lives.
symptoms: Cervical dystonia presents a range of symptoms, which can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Involuntary Neck Movements: These may include twisting, tilting, or turning of the head.
Muscle Spasms: Sudden, painful contractions of the neck muscles can occur.
Pain and Discomfort: Many individuals experience neck pain, headaches, or shoulder discomfort.
Difficulty with Head Control: Maintaining a stable head position can be challenging.

diseases.name: Cervical Ectropion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical ectropion, also known as cervical erosion, is a condition that affects the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina. This condition occurs when the cells that normally line the inside of the cervical canal (glandular cells) extend outward onto the surface of the cervix, which is typically lined with squamous cells. While cervical ectropion is often benign and may not cause any symptoms, it can lead to various complications if left untreated. Understanding cervical ectropion is crucial for women’s health, as it can impact reproductive health and overall well-being.
symptoms: Cervical ectropion may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Abnormal Vaginal Discharge: Women may notice an increase in vaginal discharge, which can be clear, yellow, or even blood-tinged.
Intermenstrual Bleeding: Some women may experience bleeding between menstrual periods, which can be alarming.
Postcoital Bleeding: Bleeding after sexual intercourse is a common symptom associated with cervical ectropion.
Pelvic Pain: Although less common, some women may experience discomfort or pain in the pelvic region.

diseases.name: Cervical Kyphosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical kyphosis is a medical condition characterized by an abnormal curvature of the cervical spine, which is the section of the spine located in the neck. This condition can lead to a range of symptoms and complications, significantly impacting an individual's quality of life. Understanding cervical kyphosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can affect mobility, posture, and overall health. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of cervical kyphosis.
symptoms: Cervical kyphosis can present a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Neck Pain: Persistent discomfort or pain in the neck region.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the neck, making it difficult to turn the head.
Headaches: Tension headaches may arise due to muscle strain from abnormal posture.
Numbness or Tingling: Radiating sensations in the arms or hands, indicating nerve compression.
Fatigue: General tiredness due to the body compensating for poor posture.

diseases.name: Cervical Myelopathy
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of cervical myelopathy are as follows:
Tingling sensation in legs and arms
Difficulty in balancing while walking
Difficulty in flexing the neck
Difficulty in motor functions like buttoning shirt
Weakness in muscles and limbs
Pain in arms and shoulders
Loss of position sense

When there is narrowing of the spinal canal, the bony tube through which the spinal cord runs, the whole spinal cord may be affected. This is different than when the bone spurs only narrow one of the foramen – the openings where the nerve roots exit. The symptoms are much different. A pinched nerve from either a herniated disc or a bone spur rarely affects the legs. Cervical myelopathy can affect both the arms and the legs.

The other factors that increase the risk of cervical myelopathy include ischemia, over stretching of spine, medical history of back and bone injuries, vascular disease, having narrow spinal canal since birth and so on.

diseases.name: Cervical Polyp - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical polyps are small, benign growths that develop on the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that connects to the vagina. While they are often harmless and may not cause any symptoms, their presence can sometimes indicate underlying health issues. Understanding cervical polyps is crucial for women’s health, as they can affect reproductive health and may require medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cervical polyps, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Many women with cervical polyps may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Abnormal Vaginal Bleeding: This may include bleeding between periods, after sexual intercourse, or after menopause.
Increased Vaginal Discharge: Some women may notice a change in the amount or consistency of vaginal discharge.
Pelvic Pain: Although less common, some women may experience discomfort or pain in the pelvic area.

diseases.name: Cervical Radiculopathy
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of cervical radiculopathyare as follows:
Pain in shoulder, arm, neck, upper backand chest
Weakness, numbness and tingling sensation in hands and fingers
Lack of co-ordination, mostly in hands

diseases.name: Cervical Rib - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical rib is a rare anatomical variation that can have significant implications for an individual's health. It refers to an extra rib that develops above the first rib, arising from the cervical vertebrae in the neck. While many people with a cervical rib may remain asymptomatic, others can experience a range of symptoms due to compression of nearby nerves and blood vessels. Understanding cervical rib is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, especially for those who may experience complications.
symptoms: Many individuals with cervical ribs are asymptomatic, but when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Neck Pain: Discomfort or pain in the neck region, often exacerbated by certain movements.
Shoulder Pain: Pain that radiates to the shoulder or upper back.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations in the arms or hands due to nerve compression.
Weakness: Muscle weakness in the upper extremities.
Coldness or Color Changes: Altered blood flow can lead to coldness or changes in color in the hands.

diseases.name: Cervical Spondylosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical spondylosis is a degenerative condition affecting the cervical spine, which is the portion of the spine located in the neck. As people age, the wear and tear on the spinal discs and joints can lead to this condition, which is often characterized by pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility. Understanding cervical spondylosis is significant not only for those experiencing symptoms but also for the general population, as it highlights the importance of spinal health and proactive management of age-related changes.
symptoms: Common symptoms of cervical spondylosis include:
Neck pain and stiffness
Headaches, often starting from the neck
Numbness or tingling in the arms or hands
Weakness in the arms or hands
Difficulty with balance or coordination

diseases.name: Cervical Vertigo - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervical vertigo is a condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, often leading to confusion and distress. It is characterized by dizziness or a sensation of spinning that arises from issues related to the cervical spine, particularly the neck. Understanding cervical vertigo is crucial, as it can be mistaken for other forms of vertigo or balance disorders. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cervical vertigo, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Cervical vertigo can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Dizziness: A sensation of spinning or lightheadedness.
Nausea: Often accompanying dizziness, leading to discomfort.
Imbalance: Difficulty maintaining balance, especially when moving the head.
Neck Pain: Discomfort or stiffness in the neck region.
Headaches: Tension-type headaches may occur alongside cervical vertigo.

diseases.name: Cervicitis – Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Cervicitis is an inflammation of the cervix, the lower, narrow end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.
symptoms: Cervicitis sometimes occurs with no symptoms, and the patient can discover it only when a pelvic check is performed for another reason. The patient experiences the following signs and symptoms:
Excessive vaginal discharge that is greyish or pale yellow
Urination that is frequent, difficult, and painful
Excessive pain during intercourse
Bleeding in-between menstrual cycles.
Vaginal bleeding after sex that is unrelated to a menstrual cycle

diseases.name: Cervicogenic Headache - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cervicogenic headache is a type of secondary headache that originates from the cervical spine or the surrounding structures. Unlike primary headaches, such as migraines or tension-type headaches, cervicogenic headaches are caused by underlying issues in the neck. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cervicogenic headaches, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Cervicogenic headaches present with a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Pain: Typically unilateral (one-sided) and may radiate from the neck to the forehead, temples, or behind the eyes.
Neck Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the neck, often accompanied by muscle tightness.
Referred Pain: Pain may be felt in the shoulders, upper back, or arms.
Nausea: Some individuals may experience mild nausea, particularly during severe headache episodes.
Sensitivity to Light and Sound: Similar to migraines, some cervicogenic headache sufferers may be sensitive to light and sound.

diseases.name: Chagas Disease
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms pretty much range from mild and acute to severe, and patients usually do not detect symptoms till the disease hits a long-lasting chronic stage. Acute phase – this usually lasts for weeks or months, almost symptom free. Typical but mild symptoms that may show up include the following:
Fever
Swelling around the infection, eyelids and glands
Fatigue
Body ache and headache
Rashes
Loss of appetite
Nausea and vomiting
Diarrhea
Enlarged liver or spleen

Acute symptoms usually go away on their own but in some cases if left untreated, they advance to the chronic phase. Chronic phase – this phase may never show up or may show up 10 to 20 years after the first infection. Typical symptoms in severe cases include the following:
Irregular heartbeat
Congestive heart failure and sudden cardiac arrest
Abdominal pain or constipation due to enlarged colon
Difficulty in swallowing food due to enlarged esophagus

diseases.name: Charcot Foot - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Charcot Foot is a serious condition that affects the bones, joints, and soft tissues of the foot, leading to significant deformity and disability if not properly managed. It is often associated with neuropathy, particularly in individuals with diabetes, and can result in severe complications if left untreated. Understanding Charcot Foot is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Charcot Foot can vary widely but typically include:
Swelling: The affected foot may appear swollen and puffy.
Redness and Warmth: The skin may become red and feel warm to the touch.
Deformity: Over time, the foot may develop a noticeable deformity, such as a collapsed arch or misaligned toes.
Pain: While some individuals may not experience pain due to nerve damage, others may have significant discomfort.
Instability: The foot may feel unstable, making walking difficult.

diseases.name: Charcot Marie Tooth Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Charcot Marie Tooth Disease (CMT) is a group of inherited neurological disorders that affect the peripheral nerves, which are responsible for transmitting signals between the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body. This condition is significant not only because of its prevalence—affecting approximately 1 in 2,500 people—but also due to its impact on mobility and quality of life. Understanding CMT is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the lives of those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Charcot Marie Tooth Disease can vary widely depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Weakness: Often begins in the feet and legs, leading to difficulty walking and frequent tripping.
Muscle Atrophy: Wasting away of muscle tissue, particularly in the lower legs and feet.
Foot Deformities: High arches (pes cavus) or flat feet can develop due to muscle imbalances.
Numbness and Tingling: Affected individuals may experience sensory loss or abnormal sensations in the feet and hands.
Difficulty with Fine Motor Skills: Problems with tasks requiring hand coordination, such as buttoning shirts or writing.

diseases.name: Charge Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: CHARGE Syndrome is a complex genetic condition that significantly impacts the lives of those affected and their families. It is characterized by a unique combination of physical and developmental challenges, making early diagnosis and intervention crucial for improving outcomes. This article aims to provide a thorough understanding of CHARGE Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Individuals with CHARGE Syndrome may present a variety of symptoms, which can include:
Coloboma: A gap or defect in one or both eyes, which can affect vision.
Heart Defects: Congenital heart issues, such as ventricular septal defects or tetralogy of Fallot.
Atresia of the Choanae: Blockage of the nasal passages, which can lead to breathing difficulties.
Hearing Loss: Ear abnormalities can result in varying degrees of hearing impairment.
Growth and Development Delays: Children may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones.
Genital Abnormalities: This may include undescended testicles in males or abnormalities in the reproductive organs in females.

diseases.name: Charles Bonnet Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Charles Bonnet Syndrome (CBS) is a condition that affects individuals with significant vision loss, leading to vivid visual hallucinations. These hallucinations can be distressing and confusing for those who experience them, often causing fear and anxiety. Understanding CBS is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers and healthcare providers, as it can significantly impact the quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Charles Bonnet Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark of CBS is the presence of visual hallucinations. These can include:
Simple Patterns: Such as grids, stripes, or geometric shapes.
Complex Images: Including people, animals, or scenes that may appear vividly.
Movement: Hallucinations may involve moving objects or figures.

diseases.name: Chauffeur Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chauffeur fracture , also known as a radial styloid fracture, is a specific type of wrist fracture that occurs at the base of the thumb. This injury is significant not only because of its impact on wrist function but also due to its association with various activities, particularly those involving repetitive wrist motion or trauma. Understanding chauffeur fractures is essential for both prevention and effective management, as they can lead to long-term complications if not treated properly.
symptoms: Common symptoms of a chauffeur fracture include:
Pain: Localized pain at the base of the thumb or wrist, especially when moving the wrist or thumb.
Swelling: Swelling around the wrist joint.
Bruising: Discoloration may appear around the injury site.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty in moving the wrist or thumb.
Tenderness: Increased sensitivity when pressure is applied to the affected area.

diseases.name: Chemical Burns - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chemical burns are injuries caused by exposure to corrosive substances, which can lead to significant damage to the skin and underlying tissues. These burns can occur in various settings, including workplaces, homes, and even during medical procedures. Understanding chemical burns is crucial, as they can result in severe pain, long-term complications, and even life-threatening situations if not treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of chemical burns, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of chemical burns can vary based on the severity of the injury and the type of chemical involved. Common symptoms include:
Redness and Swelling: The affected area may become red and swollen shortly after exposure.
Pain and Discomfort: Chemical burns can be extremely painful, often described as a burning or stinging sensation.
Blistering: Severe burns may lead to the formation of blisters filled with fluid.
Peeling Skin: As the burn heals, the skin may begin to peel away.
Discoloration: The skin may appear white, brown, or black, depending on the severity of the burn.

diseases.name: Chiari Malformation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chiari Malformation is a neurological condition that affects the brain and spinal cord, often leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding Chiari Malformation is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Chiari Malformation, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Chiari Malformation can present a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Often described as severe and occurring at the back of the head, headaches are one of the most common symptoms.
Neck Pain: Pain in the neck region can accompany headaches and may worsen with certain movements.
Balance Issues: Difficulty with coordination and balance can occur, affecting daily activities.
Dizziness: Some individuals may experience episodes of dizziness or vertigo.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations of numbness or tingling in the arms or legs may occur due to nerve compression.
Vision Problems: Blurred or double vision can be a symptom of Chiari Malformation.
Difficulty Swallowing: Some individuals may experience swallowing difficulties, known as dysphagia.
Sleep Apnea: Chiari Malformation can lead to breathing difficulties during sleep.

diseases.name: Chickenpox (Varicella)
diseases.description: Chickenpox is a highly contagious infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus, marked by an itchy blister-like rash.
symptoms: Fever
Tiredness
Loss of appetite
Itchy rash with fluid-filled blisters

diseases.name: Chickenpox - How does it spread, Stages, Symptoms, Risks and Treatment Options
diseases.description: Chicken pox, once a common rite of passage in childhood, has become less frequent due to vaccinations, yet it still poses a significant health concern in India. Whether you’re a parent, teacher, or adult worried about catching or caring for someone with chicken pox, understanding every aspect of this disease is essential for effective management and peace of mind. This comprehensive guide addresses the symptoms, spread, prevention, treatment, and frequently asked questions about chicken pox, tailored especially for the Indian context.
symptoms: Classic Chickenpox symptoms include:
Itchy red rash: Begins on the face, chest, and back, then spreads to other body parts, including inside the mouth, eyelids, or genital area.
Fever: Usually mild to moderate (38–39°C), but can be higher in adults.
Body aches, headache, tiredness, and loss of appetite.
Blisters: Filled with clear fluid, break open before crusting over.
Severity notes (especially for Indian readers): In hot, humid climates, rash and blisters may be more intense and secondary skin infections (due to scratching) more common.

diseases.name: Chikungunya
diseases.description: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral illness that causes sudden fever and severe joint pain. Joint pain can be debilitating and may last for weeks or longer.
symptoms: Sudden high fever
Severe joint pain
Joint swelling
Muscle pain
Headache
Nausea
Fatigue
Skin rash

diseases.name: Chilblains: Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Chilblains refer to inflammation of the blood capillaries in your skin resulting from cold exposure. This condition commonly affects your feet or hands. These occur when you are exposed to cold temperatures for a considerable time. Also termed as chill burns and pernio, chilblains can cause swelling of the affected area, the formation of red patches and blisters, and itchiness.
symptoms: The telltale signs and symptoms of chilblains include the following:
Inflammation of the skin.
The appearance of small and red itchy patches on the skin, especially on your hands and feet
Skin ulcers or blisters
Discoloration of skin
Changes in the color of your skin (red to dark blue) along with pain
Burning sensation on your skin

diseases.name: Childhood Arthritis (Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis)
diseases.description: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), formerly known as juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, is the most common type of arthritis in children under 16. JIA can cause persistent joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. Some children may experience symptoms for only a few months, while others have symptoms for the rest of their lives.
symptoms: Pain, swelling, and stiffness in joints
Fever
Rash
Eye inflammation (uveitis)
Lymph node swelling
Limping
Fatigue

diseases.name: Childhood Blood Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Childhood blood cancer refers to cancers that start in the blood and bone marrow—the soft tissue inside bones where new blood cells are made. While the term sounds alarming, many children with blood cancers respond very well to modern treatments and go on to lead healthy, active lives. Early detection, expert pediatric oncology care, and compassionate support make a powerful difference. This comprehensive article explains childhood blood cancer in clear - what it is, how it’s diagnosed, treatment options, recovery at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms can develop over days to weeks and sometimes resemble common infections. Seek medical evaluation if symptoms are persistent, unusual, or worsening.
Common early signs:
Fatigue, pale skin, shortness of breath (from anemia)
Fevers that don’t settle, repeated infections
Easy bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or tiny red spots on the skin (petechiae)
Bone or joint pain, limping without injury
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck, armpits, or groin
Additional or advanced symptoms:
Abdominal fullness (enlarged liver or spleen)
Headaches, vomiting, vision changes, or seizures (CNS involvement—less common)
Persistent cough or chest discomfort (lymph nodes in the chest)
Unintentional weight loss or night sweats (more common in lymphomas)
Any sudden behavior change, constant tiredness, or repeated infections that don’t improve should prompt a pediatric checkup.

diseases.name: Childhood Brain Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Childhood brain tumors are among the most challenging and rare types of cancer, developing from abnormal cell growth in a child’s brain or spinal cord. Their symptoms—such as headaches, nausea, or changes in behavior—can often be mistaken for other common childhood conditions, making early understanding especially important. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about childhood brain tumors—covering their symptoms, how they are diagnosed, treatment options, and what to expect throughout the journey. Our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of a childhood brain tumor can be vague and are often mistaken for other common childhood illnesses. However, if you notice these symptoms, especially if they are persistent or getting worse, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation. The symptoms depend on the tumor's location, size, and growth rate.

diseases.name: Childhood Germ Cell Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Childhood germ cell tumors (GCTs) are rare cancers that start in cells meant to become eggs (in ovaries) or sperm (in testes). Because germ cells form very early in development, they can sometimes settle in other parts of the body, leading to tumors in areas such as the tailbone (sacrococcygeal region), chest (mediastinum), abdomen, brain, or pelvis. The good news: most childhood GCTs are highly treatable—and many are curable—especially when diagnosed early. Five-year survival rates are very high, often above 85–90% in many subtypes, especially when found early.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the tumor's location, size, and whether it produces hormones or raises tumor markers.

diseases.name: Childhood Melanoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Childhood melanoma is a rare form of skin cancer that starts in melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells that give skin, hair, and eyes their color. Although melanoma is far less common in children than in adults, it can occur at any age, including infancy. The reassuring news: when melanoma is found early and treated promptly by an experienced, multidisciplinary team, outcomes are often excellent. This article explains what childhood melanoma is, how common it is, what symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, current treatments (surgery, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiation when needed), expected prognosis, prevention tips.
symptoms: Melanoma in children may look different than in adults. While the adult "ABCDE" rule is still helpful, pediatric signs can include new or changing lesions that are amelanotic (less pigmented), red, or pink.

diseases.name: Childhood Obesity
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: There are no visible symptoms of obesity in children apart from excess body weight. Moreover, not all children who carry extra pounds are regarded as obese or overweight. Some children have bigger body proportions and normally bear different proportions of body fat.

diseases.name: Childhood Rhabdomyosarcoma (Soft Tissue Sarcoma) - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Childhood rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents. It begins in cells that are meant to become skeletal muscle (the muscles used for movement), but it can arise almost anywhere in the body—even in areas with little muscle, such as around the eye or in the urinary tract. While a cancer diagnosis is frightening, modern treatments are highly effective, especially when started early and delivered by a specialized pediatric oncology team. This comprehensive article explains what RMS is, who is affected, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, the latest treatments, and recovery at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the tumor's size and location. Because RMS can arise almost anywhere, signs vary widely.
Painful lump, rapid growth, or skin color changes over a mass
Breathing difficulty (if chest wall or airway is involved)
Unintentional weight loss, fatigue, or fever (less common as first signs)
Any persistent, unexplained lump or site-specific symptom should be evaluated promptly. Early imaging and specialist referral are key.

diseases.name: Chlamydia: Symptoms, Diagnosis, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Chlamydia is a sexually transmitted bacterial disease, which is contracted during sexual contact. It affects both males and females. Often, Chlamydia produces no symptoms, but it can lead to fertility problems. However, effective treatment is available. Therefore, it is essential to undergo regular screening to prevent the spread of the disease.
symptoms: Men

Since most men do not show symptoms of Chlamydia, they fail to notice it. The symptoms usually appear two or three weeks after the transmission. The most common symptoms in men after the transmission include :
Burning sensation while urinating
Yellow or green discharge from the penis
Pain in the lower abdomen
Pain in the testicle

Sometimes the infection can also occur in the anus. The symptoms during such cases are discharge, pain, and bleeding. If the person has oral intercourse with someone with the virus, they are more likely to get Chlamydia in the throat. A sore throat , cough, or fever are some symptoms of throat chlamydia.
Women
It may take many weeks for a woman to develop symptoms after contracting the STI.
The following are the most prevalent chlamydia symptoms in women:
Painful sexual intercourse
Excessive vaginal discharge
Burning sensation during urination
Bleeding between periods
The infection can spread to the fallopian tubes in some women, resulting in a life-threatening condition known as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

diseases.name: Choanal Atresia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Choanal Atresia is a congenital condition that affects the nasal passages, specifically the connection between the nasal cavity and the throat. This condition can significantly impact a newborn's ability to breathe, feed, and thrive. Understanding Choanal Atresia is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can lead to better outcomes for affected infants. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Choanal Atresia.
symptoms: The symptoms of Choanal Atresia can vary depending on whether the condition is unilateral or bilateral. Common symptoms include:
Difficulty Breathing: Infants may exhibit labored breathing, especially when feeding or crying.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, particularly around the lips and face, may occur due to low oxygen levels.
Nasal Congestion: Persistent nasal blockage can lead to difficulty in breathing through the nose.
Feeding Difficulties: Infants may struggle to feed due to respiratory distress, leading to poor weight gain.
Foul Smell: In cases of unilateral Choanal Atresia, a foul-smelling discharge may be present from the affected nostril.

diseases.name: Choking - Symptoms, Risks, First Aid, Diagnosis and Treatment.
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: If a person is choking, look for these very obvious signs so that you can provide first-aid immediately:
Difficulty in breathing
Unconsciousness
Inability to talk
Inability to cough
Skin, lips or nails turning blue
Symptoms of asphyxia are more serious and in addition to the above, one may also experience:
High blood pressure
Hastened pulse rate
Convulsions
Paralysis
If you see any of these symptoms in a person, you can help by giving:
5 back-blows
5 abdominal thrusts and
alternating between the two till the obstruction is cleared

diseases.name: Cholangiocarcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cholangiocarcinoma, often referred to as bile duct cancer, is a rare and aggressive form of cancer that arises from the bile ducts, which are the tubes that carry bile from the liver to the gallbladder and small intestine. This type of cancer is significant due to its challenging diagnosis, often late-stage presentation, and poor prognosis. Understanding cholangiocarcinoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can significantly impact the quality of life and survival rates of affected individuals.
symptoms: Cholangiocarcinoma often presents with nonspecific symptoms, which can make early diagnosis challenging. Common symptoms include:
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to bile duct obstruction.
Itching: Often accompanies jaundice and results from bile salts accumulating in the bloodstream.
Abdominal Pain: Typically located in the upper right quadrant, this pain can be persistent or intermittent.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to decreased appetite or metabolic changes.
Fatigue: A common symptom in many cancers, fatigue can be debilitating.
Dark Urine and Pale Stools: Changes in urine and stool color can indicate bile duct obstruction.

diseases.name: Cholangitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cholangitis is a serious medical condition that affects the bile ducts, which are essential for the digestion of fats and the elimination of waste from the liver. This infection can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding cholangitis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions about cholangitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of cholangitis can vary but often include:
Fever: A high fever is a common sign of infection.
Chills: Patients may experience chills along with fever.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes occurs due to the buildup of bilirubin when bile flow is obstructed.
Abdominal Pain: Pain, particularly in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen, is common.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may accompany abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Cholecystitis - Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: In order to understand what cholecystitis is, we must first understand how the gallbladder functions. The gallbladder is a digestive organ located near the liver. Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder which is caused when the flow of bile (a fluid that passes from the gallbladder into the small intestine) is blocked, causing swelling and pain in the gall bladder. Other causes of cholecystitis include bile duct problems and tumors. If left untreated, cholecystitis can lead to serious, sometimes life-threatening complications, such as a gallbladder rupture. Treatment for cholecystitis often involves gallbladder removal
symptoms: There are a number of symptoms that are indicative of Cholecystitis. These may include:
Pain the upper right abdomen
Fever
Nausea
Pain while breathing
Tenderness in the right abdomen
Long-lasting pain after meals

diseases.name: Choledocholithiasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Choledocholithiasis is a medical condition characterized by the presence of gallstones in the common bile duct. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications, including infections, pancreatitis, and liver damage if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding choledocholithiasis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ultimately leading to better health outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of choledocholithiasis can vary in severity and may include:
Abdominal Pain: Often located in the upper right quadrant, this pain can be severe and may radiate to the back or shoulder.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes occurs when bile flow is obstructed.
Dark Urine and Pale Stools: Changes in urine and stool color can indicate bile duct obstruction.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may accompany abdominal pain.
Fever and Chills: These can indicate an infection, such as cholangitis.

diseases.name: Cholera
diseases.description: Cholera is an acute diarrheal infection caused by Vibrio cholerae from contaminated food or water. It can cause severe dehydration if not treated quickly.
symptoms: Severe watery diarrhea
Vomiting
Leg cramps
Rapid dehydration
Thirst and dry mouth

diseases.name: Cholestasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cholestasis is a medical condition characterized by the impairment of bile flow from the liver. This disruption can lead to a buildup of bile acids in the liver and bloodstream, resulting in various health issues. Understanding cholestasis is crucial, as it can indicate underlying liver disease or other serious health conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cholestasis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Cholestasis can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the underlying cause and severity of the condition.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to the accumulation of bilirubin.
Itching (Pruritus): A common symptom caused by bile acid buildup in the bloodstream.
Dark Urine: Caused by excess bilirubin being excreted through urine.
Pale Stools: Resulting from a lack of bile reaching the intestines.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen.
Fatigue: Generalized tiredness and lack of energy.
Nausea and Vomiting: Digestive disturbances may occur.

diseases.name: Cholestasis Of Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cholestasis of pregnancy is a liver condition that can occur during the later stages of pregnancy, affecting both the mother and the developing fetus. It is characterized by the impairment of bile flow, leading to a buildup of bile acids in the liver and bloodstream. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications, including preterm birth and fetal distress. Understanding cholestasis of pregnancy is crucial for expectant mothers, healthcare providers, and families to ensure proper management and care.
symptoms: Cholestasis of pregnancy presents with a range of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Itching (Pruritus): The most prominent symptom, often starting on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet, and can spread to other areas.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, indicating elevated bile acids in the bloodstream.
Dark Urine: A result of excess bile acids being excreted through urine.
Pale Stools: Due to reduced bile flow into the intestines.
Fatigue: General tiredness and lack of energy.

diseases.name: Cholesteatoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
