diseases.description: Cholesteatoma is a condition that affects the ear, often leading to significant complications if left untreated. It is characterized by the abnormal growth of skin cells in the middle ear and the mastoid process, which can result in hearing loss, infections, and other serious health issues. Understanding cholesteatoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can have a profound impact on an individual's quality of life.
symptoms: Cholesteatoma can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Hearing Loss: Often the first noticeable symptom, which can range from mild to profound.
Ear Discharge: A foul-smelling discharge from the ear is common.
Ear Pain: Discomfort or pain in the ear may occur, especially during infections.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ear can be a symptom.
Dizziness or Balance Issues: As the condition progresses, it may affect balance.

diseases.name: Cholinergic Urticaria: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Cholinergic urticaria is a condition that causes skin rashes known as hives in people when their body gets too warm and when they sweat. Typically, the rash swiftly develops after an increase in body temperature.
symptoms: Cholinergic urticaria tends to arise very quickly after people begin to sweat or when their body temperature increases. The typical signs and symptoms of the rash include any combination of the following:
Wheals (tiny, raised bumps on skin)
Itching
Redness around the bumps
Typically, these bumps develop within first six minutes of workout. Symptoms can get worse for the next 12 to 25 minutes.
Wheals often begin on the chest and neck first. They can then spread out to other areas. Other symptoms include:
abdominal pain
diarrhea
nausea
vomiting
hypersalivation
However, cholinergic urticaria is not a serious condition. The rashes may disappear on their own within an hour of their appearance.

Exercise-induced anaphylaxis is a severe type of CU with more severe allergic reaction to exercise. The symptoms of this condition can be life-threatening and need immediate medical attention. They include :
wheezing
difficulty breathing
headache

diseases.name: Chondroblastoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chondroblastoma is a rare type of benign bone tumor that primarily affects the cartilage of the bones. While it is not cancerous, its presence can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not properly managed. Understanding chondroblastoma is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of chondroblastoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Chondroblastoma can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in intensity. Common symptoms include:
Localized Pain: Often the first symptom, pain may be persistent and worsen with activity.
Swelling: The area around the tumor may become swollen or tender.
Limited Range of Motion: Depending on the tumor's location, patients may experience difficulty moving the affected joint.
Joint Stiffness: Stiffness may occur, particularly after periods of inactivity.

diseases.name: Chondromalacia Patella (Runner's Knee)
diseases.description: Chondromalacia patella refers to the softening and breakdown of the cartilage on the underside of the kneecap (patella). It is one of the most common causes of chronic knee pain, especially in young athletes. The condition develops when the kneecap rubs abnormally against the thigh bone, causing irritation of the cartilage.
symptoms: Dull aching pain around or behind the kneecap
Pain that worsens when climbing stairs, kneeling, or squatting
Pain after sitting for a long time with bent knees
Grinding or cracking sound when the knee is flexed
Knee swelling

diseases.name: Chorioamnionitis : Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, Risk Factors
diseases.description: Chorioamnionitis is a severe health condition in pregnant women. This condition occurs when bacteria infect the membranes that surround the fetus and also affect the amniotic fluid. If left untreated, chorioamnionitis can cause severe complications in the mother and baby.
symptoms: Though chorioamnionitis does not always cause symptoms, some women with this condition may experience:
Sweating
High temperature and fever
Rapid heartbeat (the fetus can also have a fast heartbeat)
Uterine tenderness
Discolored, foul-smelling amniotic fluid

diseases.name: Choriocarcinoma Cancer: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Choriocarcinoma is a rapidly growing cancer that develops in the uterus of women. It is a rare type of cancer in which abnormal cells starts to grow in the cells that remain after pregnancy. Choriocarcinoma is one of the forms of gestational trophoblastic disease. In most cases, it is a curable disease. However, it can metastasize to other body parts.
symptoms: The American Cancer Society mentions that choriocarcinoma does not always show symptoms. However, you may experience:
Irregular bleeding from the vagina
Extreme pain due to vaginal bleeding or enlargement of ovaries
Infection that may result in vaginal discharge , pelvic cramps, and fever
Inflammation in the abdominal area
However, if cancer has metastasized to other body parts, you may suffer from the following:
Dry cough
Difficulty breathing
Coughing blood
Chest pain
Headache
Lightheadedness

diseases.name: Chorioretinitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chorioretinitis is a significant ocular condition that affects the choroid and retina, two critical components of the eye responsible for vision. This inflammation can lead to serious complications, including vision loss, if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding chorioretinitis is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ultimately empowering individuals to seek timely medical intervention.
symptoms: Chorioretinitis can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the severity of the inflammation. Common symptoms include:
Blurred Vision: A common early sign, often affecting central vision.
Floaters: Small spots or lines that appear in the field of vision.
Flashes of Light: Sudden flashes may indicate retinal involvement.
Blind Spots: Areas of vision loss can occur.
Eye Pain: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the affected eye.
Redness: The eye may appear red or inflamed.

diseases.name: Choroid Plexus Cyst : Causes, Complication and Treatment
diseases.description: The choroid plexus is the part of the brain which makes cerebrospinal fluid. Cerebrospinal fluid normally bathes and protects the spinal column and brain. In about 1 – 2 per cent of normal babies (1 out of 50 – 100), a tiny bubble of fluid is pinched off as choroid plexus forms. This looks like a cyst inside choroid plexus at the time of the ultrasound .

diseases.name: Chronic fatigue syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) is a medical condition characterized by extreme weariness or fatigue that does not go away with rest and is not caused by a specific medical illness. CFS is also known as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) or Systemic Exertion Intolerance Disease (SEID).
symptoms: CFS symptoms vary depending on the person and the severity of the disorder.
Fatigue that is severe enough to impede everyday activities is the most prevalent symptom.
A considerably diminished capacity to perform typical daily activities with fatigue for at least 6 months to diagnose CFS. The fatigue does not reduce with rest.
The patient may also feel extremely tired after engaging in physical or mental activities, known as post-exertional malaise (PEM). This can linger for up to 24 hours after the activity is completed.
Feeling unrefreshed after a night’s sleep
Chronic insomnia
Muscle or joint discomfort
Headaches
A sore throat
Swollen glands
Trouble thinking, remembering, or focusing
Flu-like symptoms
Dizziness or sickness
Fast or irregular heartbeats ( heart palpitations )
Intolerance to orthostatic pressure (going from lying or seated to standing positions makes the patient light-headed, dizzy, or faint)
According to the majority of people, overexercising exacerbates their symptoms. Symptoms might fluctuate in severity from day to day, or even within a single day.
Because the symptoms of CFS are similar to those of other conditions, it’s important to consult a doctor to get a proper diagnosis.
Some people are affected by CFS in cycles, with times of feeling worse followed by periods of feeling better.
Symptoms may even go away completely in certain cases, and the condition is known as remission. It’s still conceivable that symptoms will return later, which is known as a relapse.
It can be tough to control the symptoms in this cycle of remission and relapse, but it is achievable.
PEM is when even moderate physical, mental, or emotional exertion causes CFS symptoms to worsen
Worsening symptoms typically appear 12 to 48 hours after the activity and might continue for days or even weeks.

Activity management, also known as pacing, can help prevent PEM flare-ups by balancing rest and activity. To stay inside the particular boundaries for mental and physical tasks, the patient will need to identify them, schedule them, and then rest.
The “energy envelope” is a term used by certain clinicians to describe staying within these parameters. Keeping a journal of the activities can assist the patient in determining personal boundaries.
It’s crucial to remember that, while intensive aerobic activity is beneficial for most chronic diseases, it’s not tolerated by patients with CFS.

diseases.name: Chronic Granulomatous Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the immune system, making individuals more susceptible to infections. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on health but also due to the challenges it presents in diagnosis and management. Understanding CGD is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and effective treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of Chronic Granulomatous Disease can vary widely among individuals but commonly include:
Frequent infections : Recurrent bacterial and fungal infections, particularly in the lungs, skin, and lymph nodes.
Granulomas : Chronic inflammation leading to the formation of granulomas, which can cause obstruction in various organs.
Fever : Persistent or recurrent fevers due to infections.
Fatigue : Generalized weakness and fatigue from chronic infections.
Skin lesions : Abscesses or other skin infections that are slow to heal.

diseases.name: Chronic Hives - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chronic hives, also known as chronic urticaria, is a condition characterized by the recurrent appearance of itchy welts or hives on the skin that persist for six weeks or longer. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to discomfort, sleep disturbances, and emotional distress. Understanding chronic hives is essential for effective management and treatment, as well as for improving the overall well-being of those affected.
symptoms: The primary symptom of chronic hives is the appearance of raised, itchy welts on the skin. These welts can vary in size and may change shape or location over time. Other common symptoms include:
Itching: The welts are often intensely itchy, leading to discomfort and scratching.
Swelling: In some cases, the hives may be accompanied by swelling of the skin, known as angioedema, which can affect the face, lips, or throat.
Flushing: Some individuals may experience redness or flushing of the skin.

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
diseases.description: Also known as chronic kidney failure, Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is the gradual loss of kidney function which involves filtering wastes and excess fluids from the blood, which gets excreted in your urine.
symptoms: The following signs and symptoms of chronic kidney disease are so non-specific that they may not appear until at an irreversible stage:
Nausea and vomiting
Loss of appetite, sleep, weight and interest in sex
Tiredness and weakness
Excessive thirst
Blood in stools and irregular urine output
Poor mental agility, confusion and drowsiness
Loss of muscle mass, twitches and cramps and aches in bones
Restless leg syndrome and numbness in hands and feet
Brittle hair and nails
Hiccups
Periorbital edema – inflammation around the eyes
Pedal edema – Inflammation of ankles and feet
Urine-like bad breath
Persistent itching
Chest pain in case of a fluid build-up around the lining of the heart
Shortness of breath in case of a fluid build-up in the lungs
Uremic frost – Unusual dark, ashen or light skin prone to bruises and bleeding
Uncontrollable High blood pressure (hypertension)

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.description: Chronic kidney disease means the kidneys are damaged and cannot filter blood properly over time.
symptoms: Often no symptoms early on
Swelling of feet or ankles
Fatigue
Nausea or poor appetite

diseases.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) is a type of blood cancer that develops slowly and often does not require immediate treatment. This slow progression can make the condition feel uncertain and raise many questions for patients and families. This guide provides clear and reliable information about CLL—what it is, the symptoms to look for, how it is diagnosed, and the treatment approaches available. By understanding the condition, you can feel more prepared and supported as you move forward.
symptoms: One of the most unique aspects of CLL is that many people do not have any symptoms at the time of diagnosis. It is often found by chance during a routine blood test for an unrelated condition. When symptoms do appear, they are often vague and can be mistaken for other, less serious conditions.
As the number of leukemia cells increases and crowds out healthy blood cells, a person may experience:
Frequent Infections: A shortage of healthy white blood cells makes it difficult for your body to fight off infections.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: A shortage of platelets can lead to easy bruising and bleeding from the gums or nose.
Anemia: A shortage of red blood cells can cause fatigue, paleness, and shortness of breath.
Pain or a Feeling of Fullness in the Abdomen: This can be caused by an enlarged spleen, which is a common occurrence in CLL.
If you have any of these persistent symptoms, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.

diseases.name: Chronic Migraine - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chronic migraine is a debilitating neurological condition that affects millions of people worldwide. Characterized by recurrent headaches that can significantly impair daily functioning, chronic migraine is more than just a headache; it is a complex disorder that can lead to severe physical and emotional distress. Understanding chronic migraine is crucial for effective management and improving the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of chronic migraine, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Chronic migraine symptoms can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Severe Headache: Often described as a throbbing or pulsating pain, usually on one side of the head.
Nausea and Vomiting: Many individuals experience gastrointestinal symptoms during an attack.
Sensitivity to Light and Sound: Increased sensitivity to sensory stimuli is common during migraine episodes.
Aura: Some individuals may experience visual disturbances, such as flashing lights or blind spots, before the onset of a headache.

diseases.name: Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), also called chronic myeloid leukemia, is a blood cancer that starts in the bone marrow—the soft, spongy tissue inside bones where blood cells are made. CML is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of myeloid cells (a type of white blood cell). The hallmark of CML is a genetic change called the Philadelphia chromosome, which creates an abnormal BCR-ABL1 gene that drives the disease. The good news is that with modern targeted medicines, most people with CML live long, active lives, and many achieve deep, long-term remissions. This comprehensive article explains what it is, how it is diagnosed and monitored, the latest treatments at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Many people have few or no symptoms, and CML is often found on routine blood tests. When symptoms occur, they may include:
Fatigue and weakness
Unexplained weight loss or night sweats
Fullness or discomfort on the left side of the abdomen (enlarged spleen)
Easy bruising or bleeding (less common in chronic phase)
Bone pain or feeling "unwell"
Frequent infections are more typical in advanced phases; many patients in chronic phase are asymptomatic or present only with fatigue, weight loss, or splenomegaly.
Because symptoms are non-specific, persistent issues should be checked. A simple blood count can be the first clue.

diseases.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
diseases.description: COPD is a chronic lung disease that causes airflow limitation and breathing difficulty, commonly due to long-term exposure to lung irritants such as tobacco smoke.
symptoms: Shortness of breath, especially with activity
Chronic cough
Cough with mucus (sputum)
Wheezing
Chest tightness
Fatigue

diseases.name: Chronic Pharyngitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chronic pharyngitis is a condition that affects many individuals, often leading to discomfort and a significant impact on quality of life. It is characterized by persistent inflammation of the pharynx, the part of the throat located behind the mouth and nasal cavity. Understanding chronic pharyngitis is crucial, as it can be a symptom of underlying health issues and may require medical intervention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of chronic pharyngitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Chronic pharyngitis presents a range of symptoms, which may vary in intensity. Common symptoms include:
Persistent Sore Throat: A constant feeling of discomfort or pain in the throat.
Dry Throat: A sensation of dryness that may worsen at night or in dry environments.
Difficulty Swallowing: Pain or discomfort when swallowing food or liquids.
Hoarseness: Changes in voice quality, often becoming raspy or weak.
Cough: A chronic cough that may be dry or produce mucus.
Bad Breath: Halitosis can occur due to chronic inflammation.

diseases.name: Chylothorax - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chylothorax is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of lymphatic fluid, known as chyle, in the pleural cavity—the space between the lungs and the chest wall. This condition can lead to significant respiratory issues and may indicate underlying health problems. Understanding chylothorax is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can arise from various causes and may have serious implications if left untreated.
symptoms: The symptoms of chylothorax can vary depending on the amount of fluid accumulation and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing due to pressure on the lungs.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area, often worsening with deep breaths.
Coughing: A persistent cough that may be dry or produce sputum.
Fatigue: General tiredness and weakness due to reduced oxygen levels.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to malabsorption of nutrients.

diseases.name: Chyluria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Chyluria is a medical condition characterized by the presence of chyle, a milky bodily fluid, in the urine. This condition can be alarming for patients and may indicate underlying health issues. Understanding chyluria is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers who may encounter this rare condition. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of chyluria, providing a comprehensive overview for a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of chyluria can vary, but the most notable sign is the appearance of milky urine. Other common symptoms may include:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the abdomen may occur due to underlying conditions affecting the lymphatic system.
Swelling: Lymphedema, or swelling due to lymphatic obstruction, may be present in the legs or other areas.
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue can result from the underlying causes of chyluria, particularly if there is an infection.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur, especially if the condition is related to a chronic infection or malabsorption.

diseases.name: Cirrhosis of the liver
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms of cirrhosis are often not prominent and are very dependent on the extent to which the liver is damaged. The most noticeable symptoms, however, include the following:
Itchy skin
Easily susceptible to bruises and bleeding
Fatigue
Yellow discolouration or jaundice
Fluid accumulation in the abdomen
Weight loss
Swollen legs
Loss of appetite
Spider-like blood vessels on the skin
Nausea

diseases.name: Claudication - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Claudication is a term that refers to pain, cramping, or heaviness in the legs or buttocks that occurs during physical activity, such as walking or climbing stairs, and typically resolves with rest. This condition is significant because it can be a warning sign of underlying vascular issues, particularly peripheral artery disease (PAD), which can lead to more severe complications if left untreated. Understanding claudication is crucial for early detection and management, allowing individuals to maintain their mobility and quality of life.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of claudication is muscle pain or cramping in the legs or buttocks during physical activity. Other symptoms may include:
Weakness or heaviness in the legs
Numbness or tingling in the legs
Coldness in the lower leg or foot compared to the other leg
Sores or wounds on the toes, feet, or legs that do not heal

diseases.name: Claustrophobia: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Claustrophobia is an anxiety disorder in which a panic episode is triggered by an illogical dread of being trapped or confined.
symptoms: Symptoms related to claustrophobia commonly occur during adolescence. Fears of running out of oxygen, not being able to breathe properly and distress at being confined can all be triggered by the thought of being in a closed environment.
When a person’s anxiety levels become high, they may begin to experience:
chills and sweating
lightheadedness, dizziness, and fainting
hyperventilation
bursts of heat
trembling or shivering, and a feeling of “butterflies” in the stomach
nausea
a choking sensation, chest tightness, and chest pain
an urge to use the restroom
confusion or disorientation

diseases.name: Claw Hand - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Claw hand is a condition that affects the hand's ability to function normally, leading to a characteristic deformity where the fingers curl inward, resembling a claw. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, affecting their ability to perform daily tasks, engage in work, and participate in social activities. Understanding claw hand is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can help mitigate its effects and improve overall hand function.
symptoms: The symptoms of claw hand can vary in severity but typically include:
Inward Curling of Fingers: The fingers bend inward, making it difficult to extend them fully.
Weak Grip: Individuals may struggle to grasp objects or perform tasks requiring fine motor skills.
Numbness or Tingling: Damage to the ulnar nerve can lead to sensations of numbness or tingling in the ring and little fingers.
Muscle Atrophy: Over time, the muscles in the hand may weaken and shrink, further impairing function.

diseases.name: Claw Toes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Claw toes are a common foot deformity that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. This condition is characterized by an abnormal bending of the toes, which can lead to discomfort, pain, and difficulty in walking. Understanding claw toes is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain mobility and overall foot health. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of claw toes.
symptoms: Individuals with claw toes may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Toe Deformity: The most noticeable symptom is the abnormal bending of the toes.
Pain and Discomfort: Many individuals report pain in the affected toes, especially when wearing shoes.
Calluses and Corns: The abnormal positioning can lead to friction against footwear, resulting in calluses or corns on the tops or sides of the toes.
Difficulty Walking: The altered toe position can affect balance and gait, making walking uncomfortable or challenging.

diseases.name: Cleft Palate - Causes, Symptoms, Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Cleft Palate/ lip usually occurs when the tissues of the lip/mouth are not formed properly during the early years of the baby. A connection between the nasal cavity and the mouth is observed in the form of a hole, which is known as the cleft palate.
symptoms: Generally, a split (separated) on the lip or the feeling of taste is quickly recognized during childbirth . Cleft palate and lip may show up as:
A split in the head of the mouth and the lip (feeling of taste) that impacts one or different sides of the face.
If there is a split in or near the lip that appears as a little indent in/near the lip or connects from the upper gum through the lip and feeling of taste into the lower part of the nose.
A split in the head of the mouth that doesn’t impact the presence of the face

It’s very rare that a cleft palate happens just in the area of the fragile feeling of taste, that is secured by the mouth’s covering and is generally at the head of the mouth. This sort of split habitually goes unnoticed during the birth and is not observed till the signs appear. Some of the symptoms of submucous cleft palate include:
Issue with feedings
Inconvenience in swallowing anything, which might result in liquids or food coming out of the nasal area.
Chronic ear disease

diseases.name: Cleidocranial Dysplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cleidocranial Dysplasia (CCD) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the development of bones and teeth. It is characterized by a range of skeletal abnormalities, particularly in the collarbone (clavicle) and skull. Understanding CCD is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers, families, and individuals who may be at risk. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Cleidocranial Dysplasia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Individuals with Cleidocranial Dysplasia may experience a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Underdeveloped or Absent Clavicles: This is one of the hallmark features of CCD, allowing the shoulders to come together.
Delayed Tooth Eruption: Many individuals with CCD experience delays in the eruption of their permanent teeth, leading to dental issues.
Skeletal Abnormalities: These may include a short stature, scoliosis, and other bone deformities.
Facial Features: Individuals may have a prominent forehead, wide-set eyes, and a flat nasal bridge.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals may experience conductive hearing loss due to middle ear abnormalities.

diseases.name: Cloacal Exstrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cloacal exstrophy is a rare and complex congenital condition that affects the development of the lower abdominal organs. It is characterized by a malformation of the cloaca, which is the common opening for the urinary, reproductive, and gastrointestinal tracts. This condition is significant not only due to its rarity but also because it presents numerous challenges for affected individuals and their families. Understanding cloacal exstrophy is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those impacted.
symptoms: Cloacal exstrophy presents a range of symptoms, which can vary significantly among individuals. Common symptoms include:
External Bladder and Intestinal Malformation: The bladder and intestines may be exposed outside the body.
Abnormal Genitalia: In males, the penis may be malformed, and in females, the vagina may be absent or malformed.
Urinary Issues: Difficulty in urination or urinary incontinence is common.
Gastrointestinal Problems: Issues such as constipation or fecal incontinence may occur due to the malformation of the intestines.
Spinal and Limb Anomalies: Some individuals may have associated spinal defects or limb malformations.

diseases.name: Clostridium Perfringens - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Clostridium perfringens is a type of bacteria that plays a significant role in both foodborne illnesses and serious medical conditions. This bacterium is known for its ability to produce toxins that can lead to various health issues, ranging from mild gastrointestinal disturbances to life-threatening infections. Understanding Clostridium perfringens is crucial for both prevention and treatment, as it can have serious implications for public health.
symptoms: The symptoms of Clostridium perfringens infections can vary depending on the type of illness. Common symptoms include:
Gastroenteritis: Symptoms may include abdominal cramps, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting, typically occurring within 6 to 24 hours after consuming contaminated food.
Gas Gangrene: This severe condition is characterized by sudden pain, swelling, and discoloration of the skin, along with fever and a foul-smelling discharge from the wound.
Necrotizing Enteritis: Symptoms may include severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea, which can lead to dehydration and shock.

diseases.name: Clubfoot - Signs, Exercises and Treatment
diseases.description: There are a host of congenital defects that can occur in children. Clubfoot is one such abnormality that is present since birth. It can be detected after birth or in the womb using ultrasound.

diseases.name: Cluster Headache - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cluster headaches are a debilitating form of primary headache disorder that can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected. Often described as one of the most painful types of headaches, cluster headaches occur in cyclical patterns or clusters, leading to intense pain that can last from 15 minutes to three hours. Understanding cluster headaches is crucial not only for those who suffer from them but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cluster headaches, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Cluster headaches are characterized by several hallmark symptoms, including:
Severe, Unilateral Pain: The pain is often described as sharp or burning and is typically located around one eye or one side of the head.
Duration: Attacks can last from 15 minutes to three hours and may occur multiple times a day.
Autonomic Symptoms: These may include nasal congestion, runny nose, tearing, and redness of the eye on the affected side.
Restlessness: Many individuals feel the need to move or pace during an attack, as sitting still can exacerbate the pain.

diseases.name: Coagulative Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Coagulative necrosis is a type of tissue death that occurs when cells are deprived of blood supply, leading to a loss of cellular structure and function. This condition is significant because it can result from various underlying health issues, including heart attacks, strokes, and other ischemic events. Understanding coagulative necrosis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, diagnosing the condition, and implementing effective treatment strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of coagulative necrosis can vary depending on the affected organ and the extent of tissue damage. Common symptoms may include:
Chest Pain: Often associated with myocardial infarction (heart attack).
Shortness of Breath: Can occur if the heart or lungs are affected.
Abdominal Pain: May indicate kidney or spleen involvement.
Weakness or Fatigue: Generalized weakness can result from systemic effects of tissue death.

diseases.name: Coarctation Of The Aorta - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Coarctation of the aorta is a congenital heart defect characterized by a narrowing of the aorta, the large blood vessel that carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the rest of the body. This condition can lead to serious health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding coarctation of the aorta is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of coarctation of the aorta can vary based on the severity of the condition and the age of the individual. Common symptoms include:
High Blood Pressure: Elevated blood pressure in the arms compared to the legs.
Weak or Absent Pulse: Reduced blood flow to the lower body can lead to weak or absent pulses in the legs.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, especially during physical activity.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, particularly during exertion.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lethargy, especially in infants and children.

diseases.name: Coats Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Coats Disease is a rare eye disorder that primarily affects the retina, leading to vision impairment and, in severe cases, blindness. This condition is characterized by abnormal blood vessel development in the retina, which can cause fluid accumulation and retinal detachment. Understanding Coats Disease is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers, as early detection and intervention can significantly impact the quality of life for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of Coats Disease can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Vision Changes: Blurred or distorted vision, particularly in one eye.
Leukocoria: A white or yellowish appearance of the pupil, often noticed by parents or caregivers.
Eye Pain: Discomfort or pain in the affected eye, especially in advanced cases.
Floaters: The presence of spots or lines in the field of vision.

diseases.name: Cobblestone Throat - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cobblestone throat is a term that describes a specific appearance of the throat characterized by swollen, bumpy, or irregularly shaped tonsils and pharyngeal tissue. This condition can be alarming for those who experience it, as it often accompanies other symptoms that may indicate an underlying health issue. Understanding cobblestone throat is essential for recognizing its significance, potential causes, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cobblestone throat, making it accessible for a general audience while ensuring medical accuracy.
symptoms: The symptoms of cobblestone throat can vary but often include:
Sore Throat: A persistent sore throat is a common complaint.
Swollen Tonsils: Enlarged tonsils that may appear bumpy or irregular.
Difficulty Swallowing: Pain or discomfort while swallowing.
Bad Breath: Foul-smelling breath due to inflammation or infection.
Cough: A persistent cough may accompany throat irritation.

diseases.name: Cohen Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cohen Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects multiple systems in the body, leading to a variety of physical and developmental challenges. This condition is significant not only because of its rarity but also due to the profound impact it can have on the lives of those affected and their families. Understanding Cohen Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for individuals living with this condition.
symptoms: Cohen Syndrome presents a range of symptoms that can vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Developmental Delays: Children may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones such as walking and talking.
Intellectual Disability: Many individuals with Cohen Syndrome have some degree of intellectual disability, which can affect learning and daily functioning.
Distinctive Facial Features: These may include a broad forehead, downturned corners of the mouth, and a prominent nose.
Vision Problems: Individuals may experience vision issues, including myopia (nearsightedness) and other eye conditions.
Hypotonia: Low muscle tone can lead to difficulties with movement and coordination.
Obesity: Many individuals with Cohen Syndrome may struggle with weight management due to metabolic issues.
Behavioral Challenges: Some may exhibit behavioral problems, including anxiety and social difficulties.

diseases.name: Cold Sores - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cold sores, also known as fever blisters, are small, painful blisters that typically appear on or around the lips. They are caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV), primarily HSV-1, although HSV-2 can also be responsible. Cold sores are not just a cosmetic concern; they can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, causing discomfort and emotional distress. Understanding cold sores is essential for effective management and prevention, especially since they are highly contagious and can recur throughout a person's life.
symptoms: Cold sores typically present with the following symptoms:
Tingling or Burning Sensation: This often occurs a day or two before the blisters appear.
Blisters: Small, fluid-filled blisters that usually cluster together.
Crusting: After a few days, the blisters break, ooze, and form a crust.
Pain or Itching: The affected area may be painful or itchy.

diseases.name: Cold Urticaria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cold urticaria is a rare but significant allergic reaction that occurs when the skin is exposed to cold temperatures. This condition can lead to uncomfortable and sometimes dangerous symptoms, making it essential for those affected to understand its implications. Cold urticaria can impact daily life, especially for individuals living in colder climates or those who enjoy outdoor activities during winter. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of cold urticaria, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of cold urticaria can vary in severity and may include:
Hives: Raised, itchy welts on the skin that develop after exposure to cold.
Redness: A flushed appearance in the affected areas.
Swelling: Localized swelling around the hives.
Burning Sensation: A feeling of warmth or burning in the affected areas.

diseases.name: Colic - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Colic is a term that often evokes concern among parents, caregivers, and even adults experiencing discomfort. While it is commonly associated with infants, colic can affect individuals of all ages. Understanding colic is crucial, as it can significantly impact quality of life and may indicate underlying health issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of colic, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of colic can vary depending on the age of the individual and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Severe Abdominal Pain: This is often described as cramp-like and may come in waves.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Gas: Increased flatulence or burping.
Changes in Bowel Movements: This may include diarrhea or constipation.
Crying and Fussiness in Infants: In infants, colic is often characterized by excessive crying, especially in the late afternoon or evening.

diseases.name: Colles Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A Colles fracture is a common type of wrist fracture that occurs when the distal radius bone in the forearm breaks just above the wrist. This injury is particularly significant because it often results from falls, especially among older adults, and can lead to long-term complications if not treated properly. Understanding Colles fractures is essential for both prevention and effective management, as they can impact daily activities and overall quality of life.
symptoms: Pain: Immediate and severe pain in the wrist area.
Swelling: Swelling around the wrist joint.
Deformity: A visible deformity, often described as a "dinner fork" appearance.
Bruising: Discoloration around the wrist due to bleeding under the skin.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty moving the wrist or hand.

diseases.name: Coloboma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Coloboma is a congenital eye condition that can affect various structures of the eye, including the iris, retina, and optic nerve. It occurs when a portion of the eye fails to develop properly during fetal growth, leading to a gap or defect. This condition can have significant implications for vision and overall eye health, making it essential for individuals and families to understand its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. In this article, we will explore coloboma in detail, providing a comprehensive overview that is accessible to a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of coloboma can vary widely depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Visual Impairment: Difficulty seeing clearly, especially in low light conditions.
Abnormal Pupil Shape: A keyhole or notched appearance of the pupil in cases of iris coloboma.
Light Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to bright lights (photophobia).
Strabismus: Misalignment of the eyes, which may occur in some individuals with coloboma.

diseases.name: Colon Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Colon cancer begins in the colon, the largest section of the large intestine. It usually starts as small, noncancerous growths called polyps that slowly develop into cancer over time. Because this process can take years, colon cancer is often preventable through early screening and removal of polyps before they become dangerous.
symptoms: In the early stages, colon cancer may cause few or no symptoms. That’s why screening is so important. When symptoms do appear, they may include:
Unexplained weight loss.
Fatigue and weakness, often from anemia due to hidden blood loss.
Severe abdominal pain or intestinal blockage.
If you experience any of these symptoms, it’s important to see a doctor right away.

diseases.name: Colon Infection : Symptoms And Treatments
diseases.description: The colon is a long, coiled, tubelike organ that reabsorbs or removes fluids from the digested food. The remaining solid waste, called stool, moves through the colon to the rectum and is finally expelled out of the body through the anus. The colon is a common site of infection by bacteria, viruses or parasites. Colon Infections can also be called as colitis or inflammation of the colon.
symptoms: If you have an inflamed or infected colon, you are likely to have the below symptoms.
Severe Stomach pain or cramping
Diarrhoea
Weight loss
Constant Fatigue
Bloating
Fever
Nausea
Abdominal pain and cramping
Loss of appetite
Tenderness in the abdomen
Frequent bowel movement which is as frequent as 10-15 times a day

diseases.name: Colon Polyps - Types, Symptoms, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Introduction

diseases.name: Colon Stricture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Colon stricture is a medical condition characterized by the narrowing of the colon, which can lead to significant gastrointestinal issues. This condition is significant because it can cause a range of symptoms, from mild discomfort to severe complications, including bowel obstruction. Understanding colon stricture is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, which can greatly improve a patient's quality of life.
symptoms: Abdominal Pain: Cramping or sharp pain in the abdomen is a common symptom.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Changes in Bowel Habits: This may include constipation, diarrhea, or alternating between the two.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur, especially if there is a blockage.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to malabsorption or reduced food intake.

diseases.name: Colorectal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Colorectal cancer starts in the large intestine (colon) or the rectum, which are the final parts of the digestive system. Together, these cancers are referred to as colorectal cancer.
symptoms: Colorectal cancer often develops silently at first. Early signs may be mild and easy to overlook.
Changes in bowel habits (diarrhea, constipation, or narrower stools).
Blood in the stool (bright red or dark).
Unexplained abdominal discomfort, cramps, or gas.
Feeling that the bowel does not empty completely.
Fatigue and weakness.
Unexplained weight loss.
Persistent abdominal pain.
Severe anemia (low red blood cells).
Bowel obstruction (blockage).

Many of these symptoms can also be caused by non-cancer conditions like piles or infections. But if they persist, it’s best to get checked early. If you notice these symptoms, seek medical advice promptly. Early treatment offers the best chance of cure.

diseases.name: Colorectal Polyp
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: People who have colorectal polyp may have the following symptoms:
Rectal bleeding
Blood in the stool or change of stool color
Constipation and diarrhea
Abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting
Anemia

diseases.name: Colpocephaly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Colpocephaly is a rare neurological condition characterized by the abnormal enlargement of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles in the brain. This condition is significant because it can lead to various developmental and cognitive challenges, impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding colpocephaly is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can help manage symptoms and improve outcomes for individuals with this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of colpocephaly can vary widely among individuals, depending on the severity of the condition and any associated anomalies. Common symptoms may include:
Developmental Delays: Children with colpocephaly may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones, such as walking or talking.
Cognitive Impairments: Some individuals may have learning disabilities or difficulties with attention and memory.
Seizures: Seizures can occur in some cases, particularly if colpocephaly is associated with other neurological conditions.
Motor Skill Challenges: Difficulty with coordination and fine motor skills may be present.

diseases.name: Coma : Causes, Types and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Coma is a term people know of or hear from movies and news. But most individuals may be unsure of the causes, diagnostic methods, and treatments available. This blog addresses all factors surrounding coma, its causes, and treatment options.

diseases.name: Comminuted Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A comminuted fracture is a type of bone fracture characterized by the bone being broken into multiple pieces. This type of fracture is significant not only because of the complexity of the injury but also due to the challenges it presents in terms of treatment and recovery. Understanding comminuted fractures is essential for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can lead to better management and outcomes.
symptoms: Severe Pain: Intense pain at the site of the fracture is common.
Swelling and Bruising: The area around the fracture may swell and become bruised.
Deformity: The affected limb may appear deformed or out of place.
Inability to Use the Limb: Patients often cannot move the affected limb or bear weight on it.

diseases.name: Common Cause of Sudden Cardiac Dysfunction
diseases.description: Sudden Cardiac Dysfunction/Arrest is probably one of the largest causes of natural death in the world. This kind of heart failure is known to occur most commonly in adults within the middle age range of mid 30s to middle 50s. This condition is seen twice as much in males than females. This dysfunction of the heart leads to the abrupt stoppage of the heart functions, loss of breathing and consciousness. It could lead to death if not treated immediately. So, let us take a closer look at what it actually is.
symptoms: In many cases, sudden cardiac arrests take place without any prior symptoms and signs. But sometimes there are drastic signs and symptoms, such as:
Dizziness
Shortness of breath
Palpitations
Sudden collapse
No pulse
Losing consciousness
Weakness
Rapid heartbeat

diseases.name: Common Causes of Ankle Pain
diseases.description: What Are the Possible Causes of Your Ankle Pain?

diseases.name: Common cold
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of common cold include:
Runny nose
Congestion
Sneezing
Coughing
Sore throat
Head and body aches
Low fever
Watery eyes
At times, fatigue can also be a symptom of common cold.

If the symptoms continue for more than 10 days, the person must see the doctor. In most cases high fever is accompanied by cough, chills and sweat, severe sinus pain and swollen glands. In children, the symptoms of common cold include fever, headache, vomiting, unusual sleepiness, ear pain, abdominal pain, cough and so on.

diseases.name: Common Neurological Emergencies
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE

diseases.name: Common spine problems and ways to deal with them
diseases.description: The spine forms the primary support structure of our body that helps us stay in an upright position. Our spine is a fragile structure that is protected by a vertical arrangement of vertebrae around it known as the vertebral column and various ligaments & muscles, rendering it flexible enough for multiple movements. Your spine is a part of the central nervous system extending from your neck up to your buttocks. Any abnormality in the spine tends to put pressure on the nerves resulting in back pain . Most of us face spinal issues at least once in our life irrespective of our age.
symptoms: The most common symptom that will awaken you towards your back issues is pain; it can be neck pain or back pain depending upon the part of your spine involved. Apart from this, you may experience: ● Tingling numbness in the back, arms, or legs. ● Weak arms and legs. ● In some instances, the pain in your back may extend down to your legs or even up to heels. ● Twitching of muscles of hands and legs. ● Difficulty in gripping objects

diseases.name: Commotio Cordis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Commotio Cordis is a medical term that refers to a specific type of cardiac arrest caused by a blunt impact to the chest, often occurring in sports or other physical activities. This condition is significant because it can lead to sudden cardiac death, particularly in young athletes. Understanding Commotio Cordis is crucial for athletes, coaches, parents, and medical professionals to recognize its symptoms, risk factors, and the importance of immediate medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of Commotio Cordis can be sudden and severe. They may include:
Loss of Consciousness: The individual may collapse immediately after the impact.
Irregular Heartbeat: This may be detected by a medical professional or through an automated external defibrillator (AED).
Chest Pain: Some individuals may report discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may occur, especially if the heart is not pumping effectively.

diseases.name: Compartment Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Compartment syndrome is a serious medical condition that occurs when pressure within a muscle compartment increases to dangerous levels. This pressure can impede blood flow, leading to muscle and nerve damage. Understanding compartment syndrome is crucial, as early recognition and treatment can prevent severe complications, including permanent disability. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of compartment syndrome, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of compartment syndrome can vary depending on the severity and duration of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Severe Pain: Often described as a deep, aching pain that does not improve with rest or pain medication.
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the affected area, which may feel tight or firm to the touch.
Numbness or Tingling: A sensation of pins and needles or loss of sensation in the affected limb.
Weakness: Difficulty moving the affected limb or muscle group.
Pale or Cool Skin: The skin may appear pale or feel cooler than the surrounding areas due to reduced blood flow.

diseases.name: Complete Heart Block (Third-degree Atrioventricular (AV) Block)
diseases.description: Heart block or AV Bundle Block is a disturbance in the heart’s electrical system. In heart block, your heart beats irregularly and very slowly, possibly stopping for about 20 seconds at a time. This can be because of an obstruction, disruption or delay along the pathway the electrical impulses travel through to make your heart beat. This condition can be due to damage or an injury to the heart valves or heart muscle. While heart block itself does not generally require direct treatment, the underlying related health conditions do.

diseases.name: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS)
diseases.description: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a chronic pain condition that most often affects a limb (arm, leg, hand, or foot) after an injury. CRPS is characterized by prolonged or excessive pain and changes in skin color, temperature, and/or swelling in the affected area. There are two types: CRPS-I (without confirmed nerve injury) and CRPS-II (with confirmed nerve injury, formerly called causalgia).
symptoms: Continuous burning or throbbing pain
Sensitivity to touch or cold (allodynia)
Swelling of the painful area
Changes in skin temperature (alternately sweaty and cold)
Changes in skin color (blotchy, purple, pale, or red)
Changes in skin texture
Hair and nail growth changes
Joint stiffness and swelling
Muscle spasms and weakness

diseases.name: Compound Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A compound fracture, also known as an open fracture, is a serious injury that occurs when a bone breaks and pierces through the skin. This type of fracture is significant not only because of the damage to the bone but also due to the potential for infection and other complications. Understanding compound fractures is crucial for both prevention and effective treatment, as they can lead to severe health issues if not managed properly.
symptoms: Visible Bone: The most obvious symptom is the visible protrusion of bone through the skin.
Severe Pain: Intense pain at the site of the fracture is common.
Swelling and Bruising: The area around the fracture may become swollen and bruised.
Inability to Move: The affected limb may be immobile or unable to bear weight.

diseases.name: Compression Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Compression fractures are a significant health concern, particularly among older adults. These fractures occur when a vertebra in the spine collapses due to excessive pressure, leading to pain, reduced mobility, and other complications. Understanding compression fractures is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Severe Back Pain: Often sudden and intense, this pain may worsen with movement or standing.
Decreased Height: A noticeable reduction in height over time can indicate vertebral compression.
Postural Changes: A stooped or hunched posture may develop as a result of multiple compression fractures.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty in bending, lifting, or performing daily activities can occur.

diseases.name: Concussion (Traumatic Brain Injury)
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Common symptoms of a traumatic brain injury are:
Blurry vision
Confusion
Delayed response to questions
Dizziness
Headache
Loss of consciousness
Loss of memory (amnesia)
Nausea and vomiting
Ringing in the ears
Slurred speech
Sleep disorders
Depression
In case of children, symptoms may include crying profusely, temper tantrums, lack of interest in playing, lack of learning new skills, loss of balance while walking and not paying attention.

diseases.name: Concussion: A First Aid Guide
diseases.description: A concussion is a head injury that affects the functioning of the brain. Concussions are mostly temporary, but their after-effects can last for a long time—however, most of the people who suffer a concussion recover well.

diseases.name: Conduct Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Conduct Disorder (CD) is a serious behavioral and emotional disorder that affects children and adolescents. It is characterized by a pattern of disruptive and violent behavior that violates societal norms and the rights of others. Understanding Conduct Disorder is crucial, as it can lead to significant challenges in a child's social, academic, and family life. Early identification and intervention can help mitigate the long-term effects of this disorder, making it essential for parents, educators, and healthcare providers to recognize its signs and symptoms.
symptoms: Conduct Disorder manifests through a range of symptoms that can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Aggression: Physical fights, bullying, or threatening behavior toward peers or animals.
Destruction of Property: Vandalism, arson, or other forms of property damage.
Deceitfulness: Lying, stealing, or manipulating others for personal gain.
Serious Rule Violations: Skipping school, running away from home, or engaging in illegal activities.

diseases.name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) is a group of inherited disorders affecting the adrenal glands, which are responsible for producing essential hormones. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on hormone levels but also due to its potential effects on growth, development, and overall health. Understanding CAH is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia can vary widely depending on the severity of the enzyme deficiency and the age of onset. Common symptoms include:
In Infants: Ambiguous genitalia in females, dehydration, low blood sugar, and electrolyte imbalances.
In Children: Early onset of puberty, rapid growth, and development of masculine traits in females (such as increased body hair).
In Adults: Irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, and symptoms of adrenal insufficiency, such as fatigue and low blood pressure.

diseases.name: Congenital Heart Disease
diseases.description: There are 150,000-200,000 children born each year with congenital heart disease in India. Many will die undiagnosed; some will be diagnosed but allowed to die anyway due to lack of medical facilities nearby or inability to afford medical treatment; and yet others will reach the appropriate hospital but at a stage too late to intervene. There is a dire need to create congenital heart disease awareness among people to help diagnose the condition and treat it.

diseases.name: Congenital Heart Diseases
diseases.description: What are birth defects in the heart?

diseases.name: Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis (CIPA) - What You Need To Know
diseases.description: Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis (CIPA) is a rare medical condition in which an individual cannot feel pain or temperature, and does not have the ability to sweat. Also known as hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type IV, this condition usually manifests during early infancy and can lead patients to suffer from repeated injuries.

diseases.name: Congenital Myopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Congenital myopathy is a group of rare muscle disorders that are present at birth and primarily affect skeletal muscles, which are responsible for movement. These conditions are characterized by muscle weakness and can lead to significant physical limitations. Understanding congenital myopathy is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and healthcare providers. Early diagnosis and intervention can significantly improve quality of life and functional outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of congenital myopathy can vary widely depending on the specific type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Weakness: Affected individuals may experience generalized muscle weakness, particularly in the proximal muscles (those closer to the center of the body).
Hypotonia: Decreased muscle tone is often observed in infants, leading to a "floppy" appearance.
Delayed Motor Milestones: Children with congenital myopathy may take longer to achieve developmental milestones such as sitting, crawling, or walking.
Respiratory Issues: Some individuals may experience breathing difficulties due to weakened respiratory muscles.
Skeletal Deformities: In some cases, congenital myopathy can lead to skeletal deformities, such as scoliosis or joint contractures.

diseases.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS) is a significant public health concern that arises when a pregnant woman contracts rubella, a viral infection, during the first trimester of her pregnancy. The implications of CRS can be severe, leading to a range of serious birth defects and health issues in the newborn. Understanding CRS is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective management, which can significantly improve outcomes for affected infants.
symptoms: The symptoms of CRS can vary widely, but common manifestations include:
Cardiac Defects: Congenital heart defects, such as patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and pulmonary artery stenosis.
Ocular Abnormalities: Cataracts, glaucoma, and retinopathy.
Hearing Impairment: Varying degrees of hearing loss, which can be profound in some cases.
Growth Retardation: Low birth weight and failure to thrive.
Neurological Issues: Developmental delays, microcephaly, and other neurological impairments.

diseases.name: Congenital Scoliosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Congenital scoliosis is a spinal deformity that occurs due to malformations of the spine present at birth. This condition can lead to significant physical challenges and complications if not diagnosed and managed appropriately. Understanding congenital scoliosis is crucial for early detection and intervention, which can greatly improve the quality of life for affected individuals. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding congenital scoliosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of congenital scoliosis can vary based on the severity of the curvature and the specific vertebral anomalies present. Common symptoms include:
Visible Curvature: An abnormal curve in the spine that may be noticeable when the child is standing or bending.
Uneven Shoulders: One shoulder may appear higher than the other.
Uneven Hips: The hips may be at different heights, leading to an uneven gait.
Back Pain: While not always present in children, some may experience discomfort or pain as they grow.
Limited Mobility: In severe cases, the curvature can restrict movement and flexibility.

diseases.name: Congenital Syphilis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Congenital syphilis is a serious and preventable condition that occurs when a mother with syphilis passes the infection to her baby during pregnancy. This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause severe health issues in newborns but also due to its implications for public health. The rise in congenital syphilis cases in recent years highlights the need for increased awareness, prevention, and treatment strategies. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of congenital syphilis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Symptoms of congenital syphilis can vary widely and may not appear until weeks or months after birth. Common symptoms include:
Rash: A rash may develop on the baby's skin, often resembling a copper-colored or reddish-brown appearance.
Fever: Newborns may experience unexplained fevers.
Swollen Liver or Spleen: Enlargement of these organs can occur.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes may be present.
Bone Abnormalities: Infants may have bone deformities or abnormalities.
Neurological Issues: Some infants may experience developmental delays or neurological problems.

diseases.name: Congestive Heart Failure: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Most of the symptoms and signs of heart failure are due to congestion and fluid collection in the lungs, legs, abdomen etc and the inability of the heart to pump efficiently to meet the demands of the organs and tissues in the body. There is a mismatch between demand and supply. There could be breathlessness, which could be an exaggerated uncomfortable awareness of breathing. The description of this sensation is various: –
Air does not go all the way down
Shortness of breath
Heavy breathing
Tightness in chest
Choking
Air hunger

This may come on during exertion in early stages of the disease but may occur at rest when the disease is advanced. There could be breathlessness occurring in lying posture that is relieved on sitting up. Patients state that they have to sleep on three or more pillows to feel comfortable at night. And then there could be what we call in technical parlance as Paroxymal Nocturnal Dyspnoea (PND) which usually starts 2-4 hours after onset of sleep. Patients develop cough and sweating with breathlessness, which is relieved by getting out of bed. Fatigue and impaired effort capacity are other prominent symptoms of heart failure. Patients may also report abdominal fullness, leg swinging, nausea and loss of appetite.

diseases.name: Conjoined Twins - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Conjoined twins, a rare phenomenon in human development, capture the curiosity and compassion of many. These unique individuals share a physical connection, which can range from minor to significant, and their existence raises important medical, ethical, and emotional questions. Understanding conjoined twins is crucial not only for medical professionals but also for families and communities that may encounter them. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of conjoined twins, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of conjoined twins can vary widely depending on the extent and location of their physical connection. Common symptoms may include:
Physical Connection: Visible joining of body parts, which may include shared organs or limbs.
Developmental Delays: Some conjoined twins may experience delays in physical or cognitive development.
Health Complications: Depending on shared organs, conjoined twins may face challenges such as heart defects, respiratory issues, or digestive problems.

diseases.name: Conjunctival Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Conjunctival cysts, also known as conjunctival inclusion cysts, are benign growths that can occur on the surface of the eye. While they are generally harmless, understanding their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for maintaining eye health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of conjunctival cysts, their significance, and how they can be effectively managed.
symptoms: Common symptoms of conjunctival cysts include:
Visible Bump: A small, clear, or yellowish bump on the conjunctiva.
Irritation: Mild discomfort or irritation in the affected eye.
Tearing: Increased tear production may occur in some cases.
Redness: The surrounding area may appear slightly red or inflamed.

diseases.name: Conjunctivitis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Conjunctivitis symptoms are:
Redness
Itchiness
Gritty feeling
Watery eyes
Blurred vision
Burning sensation in the eyes
Increased sensitivity to light
Discharge forming a crust during the night that may prevent the eyes from opening in the morning

diseases.name: Conns Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Conns Syndrome, also known as primary hyperaldosteronism, is a rare endocrine disorder characterized by the overproduction of the hormone aldosterone from the adrenal glands. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe health complications, including hypertension (high blood pressure) and electrolyte imbalances, if left untreated. Understanding Conns Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve a patient's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Conns Syndrome can vary widely among individuals, but common signs include:
Hypertension: Often the most prominent symptom, high blood pressure may be resistant to standard treatments.
Hypokalemia: Low potassium levels can lead to muscle weakness, fatigue, and irregular heart rhythms.
Increased Thirst and Urination: Excessive aldosterone can cause the body to retain sodium and lose potassium, leading to increased thirst and urination.
Headaches: Persistent headaches may occur due to elevated blood pressure.
Muscle Cramps: Low potassium levels can result in muscle cramps and spasms.

diseases.name: Constrictive Pericarditis: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: When a patient suffers from constrictive pericarditis, the walls of the pericardium – the fluid-filled pouch that surrounds the heart become too stiff or thick. This condition restricts the heart from beating correctly and may lead to severe long-term complications. However, the treatment options depend on the severity and cause of the condition and the patient’s overall health.

diseases.name: Contact Dermatitis: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatments
diseases.description: Contact dermatitis is a form of eczema that occurs when your skin comes in contact with certain metals used in jewelry, some fragrances, plants, cosmetics, and soaps. It usually starts off as a rash and causes a reaction on the surface of the skin. Contact dermatitis is not a life-threatening condition and the reaction usually goes away a few weeks later when the substance that’s causing it is no more in contact with the skin. However, it can relapse on using the substance/jewelry again. The rash is generally noticed near sensitive areas like around the eyes, nose or mouth. Self-care tips like soothing the irritated area with cold wet compresses, and applying anti-itch creams can help treat the condition at home.
symptoms: Contact dermatitis is a condition where the symptoms usually depend on how sensitive your skin is to substances. There are various substances that can cause an allergic reaction as they take away the surface shielding oils from your skin. Some of the symptoms you may notice are:
Blisters that may crust or ooze fluid
Tenderness at the site of contact, accompanied by swelling and burning.
Severe itching
A red rash
Cracked and scaly skin.
Usually, the symptoms subside on their own with some self-care. However, you should call the doctor if the symptoms get worse such as: The rash becomes painful, severe and widespread.
The rash is very uncomfortable that you cannot sleep at night and cannot work during the daytime.
The rash doesn’t heal within three weeks.
When the rash is so much worse than you have to hide it in public.
The rash appears on your face or genitals.
Immediate medical attention is needed in the following conditions:
You feel the rash has damaged the mucous lining of the mouth and has spread to the digestive tract.
When your skin becomes infected and you have pus oozing out from the blisters.
Your eyes are red and swollen and the nose is inflamed.
Your lungs feel painful by inhaling an allergen.

diseases.name: Conversion Disorder in Adults
diseases.description: ‘Functional Neurological Symptoms’ disorder or conversion disorder is a rare mental condition in which an subconscious emotional conflict is expressed by an alteration or loss of physical functioning. Any physical or psychological examination cannot explain these symptoms or signs. It is primarily a nerve disorder in the body where the brain cannot send or receive signals properly, thereby leaving the patient feeling unable to use their senses.
symptoms: Conversion disorder occurs suddenly and resembles problems associated with the nervous system. Some of the symptoms of conversion disorder are:
Blindness
Loss of speech or smell
Unable to control movements
Paralysis
Lack of balance
Urine retention
Deafness
Seizures
Loss of touch and pain
Hallucinations
Chronic pain
Tremors and spasms
Sleep associated problems
Memory related problems
Migraines and severe headaches

diseases.name: COPD – All you Want to Know
diseases.description: Are you or your loved ones keep coughing and feel short of breath? Do you or any of your loved ones feel a little more tired than usual after a day of walking? These could be symptoms of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), a progressive loss of lung function that affects millions across the world. The most common symptom is shortness of breath. It may be very subtle. A person might just think, “I am getting a little puffy while walking/climbing steps, or I’m getting fat, old.” People, generally, tend to put it aside and not worry about it. However, ignoring those early signs means that many people only see their doctor when the disease has progressed, and more chronic and bothersome COPD symptoms set in. Occasionally, COPD comes on very suddenly; usually because an individual has been ignoring symptoms.
symptoms: Common COPD symptoms include:
Cough, a major symptom
Coughing-up sputum. Sputum is the thicker mucus that is made in our lungs
Shortness of breath
Tightness in the chest
Wheezing
Body pains. A small percentage of COPD patients report general aches and pains.
Difficulty in sleeping
Heart failure
Swollen legs or feet
Weight loss
Loss of muscle strength
A bluish tint to the lips or fingernails (if patients are not getting enough oxygen)

diseases.name: Cor Pulmonale - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cor Pulmonale is a serious medical condition that affects the heart and lungs, leading to significant health complications if left untreated. It occurs when the right side of the heart fails due to increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries, often as a result of chronic lung diseases. Understanding Cor Pulmonale is crucial for early detection and management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life and overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of Cor Pulmonale can vary depending on the severity of the condition but often include:
Shortness of Breath: This is the most common symptom, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Individuals may feel unusually tired or weak.
Swelling: Edema, or swelling in the legs, ankles, and abdomen, can occur due to fluid retention.
Chest Pain: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the chest.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, particularly around the lips and fingertips, may indicate low oxygen levels.

diseases.name: Corneal Abrasion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corneal abrasion is a common yet often overlooked eye injury that can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not properly managed.
