The cornea, the clear front surface of the eye, plays a crucial role in vision by refracting light and protecting the inner structures of the eye. When this delicate layer is scratched or damaged, it can result in pain, sensitivity to light, and blurred vision. Understanding corneal abrasion is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ensuring timely intervention and optimal recovery.
symptoms: Individuals with corneal abrasions may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Pain: A sharp, stabbing pain in the eye is often the most prominent symptom.
Redness: The affected eye may appear red and inflamed.
Tearing: Increased tear production is common as the eye attempts to flush out irritants.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, can occur due to irritation of the cornea.
Blurred Vision: Vision may become blurry or distorted, depending on the severity of the abrasion.

diseases.name: Corneal Ectasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corneal ectasia is a progressive eye condition that affects the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. This condition is characterized by the abnormal thinning and bulging of the cornea, leading to distorted vision and other complications. Understanding corneal ectasia is crucial, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and may lead to severe visual impairment if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of corneal ectasia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of corneal ectasia can vary in severity and may include:
Blurred or Distorted Vision: As the cornea changes shape, vision may become increasingly blurred or distorted.
Increased Sensitivity to Light: Individuals may experience discomfort in bright light or glare.
Frequent Changes in Prescription Glasses: Those with corneal ectasia may find that their vision changes frequently, requiring regular updates to their eyewear prescription.
Halos Around Lights: Some individuals report seeing halos or starbursts around lights, especially at night.

diseases.name: Corneal Edema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corneal edema is a condition characterized by the swelling of the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. This swelling can lead to blurred vision, discomfort, and, in severe cases, vision loss. Understanding corneal edema is crucial for maintaining eye health, as it can be a sign of underlying issues that may require medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of corneal edema, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of corneal edema can vary in severity and may include:
Blurred Vision: The most common symptom, often worsening in bright light.
Eye Discomfort: A feeling of pressure or heaviness in the eye.
Halos Around Lights: Distorted vision, especially at night.
Redness: Inflammation of the eye may cause redness.

diseases.name: Corneal Hydrops - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corneal Hydrops is a serious eye condition that can significantly impact vision and quality of life. It occurs when fluid accumulates in the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye, leading to swelling and distortion. Understanding Corneal Hydrops is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can lead to complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Corneal Hydrops, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Corneal Hydrops can vary but often include:
Blurred Vision: The swelling of the cornea can lead to distorted or blurred vision.
Eye Pain: Patients may experience discomfort or pain in the affected eye.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to bright lights is common.
Redness: The eye may appear red or inflamed.
Tearing: Excessive tearing can occur as the eye attempts to cope with irritation.

diseases.name: Corneal Ulcer - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corneal ulcers are serious eye conditions that can lead to significant vision impairment or even blindness if not treated promptly. The cornea, the clear front surface of the eye, plays a crucial role in focusing light and protecting the inner structures of the eye. When this delicate layer becomes damaged or infected, it can result in a corneal ulcer, which is essentially an open sore on the cornea. Understanding corneal ulcers, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is vital for maintaining eye health and preventing complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of a corneal ulcer can vary in severity but often include:
Eye Pain: A sharp, intense pain in the affected eye is common.
Redness: The eye may appear red and inflamed.
Tearing: Increased tear production or discharge may occur.
Blurred Vision: Vision may become cloudy or distorted.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, is a frequent symptom.
Swelling: The eyelids may become swollen.

diseases.name: Cornelia De Lange Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cornelia De Lange Syndrome (CdLS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects multiple systems in the body, leading to a range of physical, cognitive, and developmental challenges. First identified in the 1930s, this syndrome is significant not only for its clinical implications but also for the insights it provides into genetic disorders and their management. Understanding CdLS is crucial for early diagnosis, effective treatment, and improved quality of life for affected individuals and their families.
symptoms: Cornelia De Lange Syndrome presents a wide range of symptoms, which can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Distinctive Facial Features: These may include arched eyebrows, long eyelashes, a short nose, and thin upper lips.
Growth Delays: Children with CdLS often experience growth retardation, leading to shorter stature compared to peers.
Developmental Delays: Cognitive and motor development may be delayed, with some individuals experiencing intellectual disabilities.
Limb Abnormalities: Some individuals may have limb malformations, such as missing fingers or toes, or limbs that are shorter than average.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Feeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux, and constipation are common in affected individuals.
Hearing Loss: Many individuals with CdLS experience hearing impairments, which can affect communication and social interaction.

diseases.name: Corns - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Corns are hard and thick patches of the skin that stem from constant friction and pressure in a localized area. It is not a dangerous condition, but they may cause constant irritation. Read on to find out all about this particular skin condition and ways to get rid of them:

diseases.name: Corns And Calluses - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Corns and calluses are common foot conditions that many people experience at some point in their lives. While they may seem like minor nuisances, they can lead to discomfort and pain, affecting daily activities and overall quality of life. Understanding what corns and calluses are, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for effective management and prevention. This comprehensive guide aims to provide you with all the information you need about corns and calluses, ensuring you can take proactive steps toward foot health.
symptoms: The symptoms of corns and calluses can vary depending on their location and severity. Common symptoms include:
Thickened Skin: A noticeable thickening of the skin in the affected area.
Pain or Discomfort: Pain may occur when pressure is applied, especially in corns.
Inflammation: Surrounding skin may appear red or swollen.
Hard Center: Corns often have a hard, central core that can be painful.

diseases.name: Coronary Artery Calcification - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a condition characterized by the buildup of calcium deposits in the coronary arteries, which supply blood to the heart muscle. This process is a significant indicator of coronary artery disease (CAD) and can lead to serious cardiovascular events, including heart attacks. Understanding CAC is crucial for early detection and management of heart disease, as it often develops silently without noticeable symptoms until it reaches an advanced stage. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of coronary artery calcification, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Coronary artery calcification often develops without noticeable symptoms, making it a silent threat. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience symptoms related to reduced blood flow to the heart, including:
Chest Pain (Angina): A feeling of pressure, squeezing, or fullness in the chest, often triggered by physical activity or stress.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during exertion or at rest.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy, especially during physical activity.
Heart Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.

diseases.name: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)
diseases.description: Coronary artery disease occurs when the arteries that supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart become narrowed by plaque buildup, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle.
symptoms: Chest pain or pressure (angina)
Shortness of breath
Fatigue with exertion
Pain in neck, jaw, shoulder, or back
Symptoms may be absent until a heart attack

diseases.name: Coronary Artery Disease in Women
diseases.description: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is a major killer heart disease in both men and women. CAD is a disease in which cholesterol deposits on the inner wall of the heart blood vessels. These blood vessels carry oxygen to the heart. When a plaque builds up, the oxygen does not reach the heart in adequate amounts causing chest pain and a Heart Attack. CAD can also cause Heart Failure, Arrhythmia (electrical abnormality) and sudden death (SCD). Women tend to have CAD 10 years later than men but CAD remains as the number 1 killer. Coronary Artery Diseases in young females is common as women are more prone to small vessel disease where in the tiny vessels of the heart are diseased or damaged without major cholesterol deposits. It is thought that fall in oestrogen levels during menopause along with conventional risk factors cause microvascular disease in women. Although the death rate from heart disease has dropped significantly in last few decades, not much reduction has been seen in women. Coronary microvascular disease and broken heart syndrome are more seen in women than men. This is can be attributed to the lack of awareness on the facts about Heart Diseases in Women. Women tend to ignore their symptoms because of family commitments like husband’s office work, children’s exam etc. Many a time, initial symptoms are ignored and they seek advice only when the problem is more severe.
symptoms: Understanding the symptoms of heart attack in women plays an important role in saving the Patient’s life.
Chest pain: discomfort, heaviness, uneasiness, burning
Atypical symptoms: stomach pain with vomiting, jaw & tooth pain
Sweating and arm pain
Increases on walking
Discomfort which repeats
Strange feeling in the chest
Sweating
Shortness of breath
Fast Heart Beat
Light headedness
Many a times, the symptoms of heart disease in Women are atypical, hence they try to ignore them

diseases.name: Corpus Luteum Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A corpus luteum cyst is a common ovarian condition that arises during the menstrual cycle. While often benign and self-resolving, understanding its significance is crucial for women’s health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of corpus luteum cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook. By the end of this article, readers will have a clearer understanding of this condition and when to seek medical attention.
symptoms: Most corpus luteum cysts are asymptomatic and do not cause any noticeable symptoms. However, some women may experience:
Pelvic Pain: This can range from mild discomfort to sharp pain, particularly during ovulation or menstruation.
Irregular Menstrual Cycles: Changes in the menstrual cycle, such as delayed periods or heavier bleeding, may occur.
Bloating: Some women report a feeling of fullness or bloating in the abdomen.
Breast Tenderness: Hormonal changes associated with the cyst may lead to breast sensitivity.

diseases.name: Costochondritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Costochondritis is a condition that affects the cartilage connecting the ribs to the breastbone (sternum). While it may sound alarming, it is often benign and can be managed effectively. Understanding costochondritis is crucial for anyone experiencing chest pain, as it can mimic more serious conditions like heart disease. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of costochondritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of costochondritis is chest pain, which can vary in intensity and may be sharp, aching, or pressure-like. The pain is often localized to the area where the ribs meet the sternum and may worsen with certain movements, deep breathing, or physical activity.
Localized Chest Pain: Pain is usually felt on the left side of the chest but can occur on either side.
Tenderness: The area around the sternum may be tender to the touch.
Pain with Movement: Activities such as lifting, twisting, or deep breathing can exacerbate the pain.

diseases.name: Cough Variant Asthma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cough Variant Asthma (CVA) is a lesser-known form of asthma characterized primarily by a persistent cough rather than the typical wheezing or shortness of breath associated with the condition. This variant can often be overlooked or misdiagnosed, leading to inadequate treatment and management. Understanding CVA is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early recognition and appropriate management can significantly improve quality of life and prevent complications.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Cough Variant Asthma is a persistent cough, which may be accompanied by other symptoms, including:
Dry Cough: Often worse at night or early morning.
Chest Tightness: A feeling of constriction in the chest.
Shortness of Breath: May occur during physical activity or at rest.
Wheezing: Less common but can occur in some cases.

diseases.name: Could the Pain in Your Legs Be Sciatica? Here's How to Find Out
diseases.description: Sciatica is a common condition that affects the sciatic nerves, that branches from the lower back through the hips to the buttocks and down each leg. This complication typically affects only one side of the body.
symptoms: Sciatica usually affects one side of the lower body. Although you may feel pain anywhere along the nerve path, it is likely to extend from the lower back to the back of your thigh and calf muscles.
Some of the common indications of sciatica include –
Pain at the lower back and/or hips
Pain in the rear side of the leg that worsens while sitting
Tingling or burning sensation on the leg
Numbness or weakness of the leg causing difficulty in moving
A sharp pain the leg that makes it difficult to stand up
Continuous pain at the back of the leg
For some people, the pain can be severe and excruciating; it might be irritating but infrequent for others. Seek medical attention if you observe any of the above symptoms gradually getting worse.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.
When to consult a doctor?
Mild sciatic pain usually gets cured over time. Even if your condition does not demand immediate attention, it is better to seek medical advice to prevent it from worsening.
You should consult a healthcare practitioner if you experience any of the following –
Lasting excruciating pain in the leg for more than a couple of hours.
Muscle weakness or numbness in the leg.
Severe or sudden pain from trauma or sudden accident.
Loss of bladder and bowel control.

diseases.name: COVID-19
diseases.description: COVID-19 is a respiratory infection caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. It spreads mainly through respiratory particles in the air and can range from mild illness to severe disease.
symptoms: Fever or chills
Sore throat
Cough
Shortness of breath
Fatigue or body aches
Loss or change of taste or smell

diseases.name: Cowden Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cowden Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that significantly impacts an individual's health and well-being. It is characterized by the development of multiple non-cancerous tumors, known as hamartomas, and an increased risk of certain types of cancer. Understanding Cowden Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can greatly improve the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Cowden Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Cowden Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Hamartomas: Non-cancerous growths that can occur in various tissues, including the skin, mucous membranes, and internal organs.
Skin Changes: These may include trichilemmomas (benign tumors of hair follicles), papillomatous papules, and other skin lesions.
Breast Cancer: Women with Cowden Syndrome have a significantly increased risk of developing breast cancer, often at a younger age.
Thyroid Cancer: There is also an elevated risk of thyroid cancer, particularly follicular thyroid carcinoma.
Endometrial Cancer: Women are at a higher risk for endometrial cancer, which affects the lining of the uterus.
Gastrointestinal Polyps: Individuals may develop polyps in the gastrointestinal tract, which can lead to complications if not monitored.

diseases.name: Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease (CJD) is a rare but severe neurodegenerative disorder that affects the brain, leading to rapid cognitive decline and physical deterioration. It is classified as a prion disease, which means it is caused by misfolded proteins that induce abnormal folding of normal proteins in the brain. CJD is significant not only because of its devastating effects on individuals and families but also due to its implications for public health and safety, particularly concerning transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs). Understanding CJD is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease can vary but generally progress rapidly. Common symptoms include:
Cognitive Decline: Memory loss, confusion, and difficulty concentrating.
Personality Changes: Mood swings, depression, and anxiety.
Motor Symptoms: Impaired coordination, muscle stiffness, and involuntary movements.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or hallucinations.
Speech Difficulties: Slurred speech or difficulty finding words.

diseases.name: Cri Du Chat Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Cri Du Chat Syndrome (CdCS) is a rare genetic disorder that arises from a deletion of a portion of chromosome 5. The name "Cri Du Chat" is French for "cry of the cat," which refers to the distinctive high-pitched cry of affected infants that resembles a cat's meow. This syndrome is significant not only because of its unique symptoms but also due to its impact on the lives of those affected and their families. Understanding Cri Du Chat Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for individuals with this condition.
symptoms: Individuals with Cri Du Chat Syndrome may exhibit a variety of symptoms, which can include:
Distinctive Cry: A high-pitched, cat-like cry in infancy.
Developmental Delays: Delays in reaching developmental milestones such as sitting, walking, and talking.
Intellectual Disabilities: Varying degrees of cognitive impairment.
Physical Features: Characteristic facial features, including a round face, wide-set eyes, and a small jaw.
Hypotonia: Low muscle tone, which can affect motor skills.
Behavioral Issues: Increased likelihood of behavioral problems, including hyperactivity and anxiety.

diseases.name: Crigler Najjar Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Crigler Najjar Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects the body's ability to process bilirubin, a substance produced during the breakdown of red blood cells. This condition can lead to severe jaundice and other complications if not properly managed. Understanding Crigler Najjar Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Crigler Najjar Syndrome.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Crigler Najjar Syndrome is jaundice, which is characterized by yellowing of the skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels. Other symptoms may include:
Dark urine: Due to the presence of excess bilirubin.
Pale stools: Resulting from a lack of bilirubin in the intestines.
Fatigue: Caused by the body's inability to process bilirubin effectively.
Poor feeding: Common in infants with severe jaundice.
Irritability: Infants may be more fussy or irritable than usual.

diseases.name: Critical Congenital Heart diseases – The Risk Factors
diseases.description: Congenital Heart Diseases(CHD) are the most prevalent and serious of all recognized structural birth defects. Their estimated prevalence is 0.9%, which means that one in every 110 newborns is born with the disease. They are considered multi-factorial (meaning involvement of many factors) in origin and as a result, it is difficult to pinpoint a single cause for the defect. As the embryonic heart develops between 14 – 60 days of pregnancy, any issues arising during this phase in the form of infection or drugs in a genetically susceptible individual can result in a serious CHD. Many babies with CHDs die in just one year of their lives, and those who survive often need many surgeries, lengthy hospital stays and lifelong treatment for associated disabilities.

diseases.name: Critical Limb Ischemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Critical Limb Ischemia (CLI) is a severe form of peripheral artery disease (PAD) characterized by inadequate blood flow to the limbs, particularly the legs and feet. This condition is significant because it can lead to debilitating pain, non-healing wounds, and even limb loss if not diagnosed and treated promptly. CLI is often a marker of systemic atherosclerosis, indicating that other parts of the body may also be affected. Understanding CLI is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve quality of life and reduce the risk of severe complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of Critical Limb Ischemia can vary but typically include:
Rest Pain: Severe pain in the legs or feet while at rest, often worse at night.
Non-Healing Wounds: Ulcers or sores on the toes, feet, or legs that do not heal.
Gangrene: Tissue death due to lack of blood flow, which can lead to amputation.
Coldness in the Lower Leg or Foot: Affected limbs may feel colder than the rest of the body.
Weak or Absent Pulse: Reduced blood flow can lead to weak or absent pulses in the legs or feet.
