diseases.name: Dermatitis Herpetiformis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dermatitis Herpetiformis (DH) is a chronic skin condition characterized by itchy, blistering rashes that typically appear on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. It is closely associated with celiac disease, an autoimmune disorder triggered by the ingestion of gluten. Understanding DH is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and management can significantly improve the quality of life for patients. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Dermatitis Herpetiformis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark of Dermatitis Herpetiformis is the appearance of itchy, blistering skin lesions. Common symptoms include:
Itching and Burning: Intense itching often precedes the appearance of blisters.
Blisters: Small, fluid-filled blisters that can break open and crust over.
Redness and Inflammation: Affected areas may appear red and swollen.
Location: Lesions typically occur on the elbows, knees, buttocks, and scalp.

diseases.name: Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare type of skin cancer that originates in the dermis, the middle layer of the skin. This tumor is characterized by its slow growth and tendency to invade surrounding tissues, making it significant in dermatological oncology. Understanding DFSP is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, as it can lead to complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of DFSP, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Firm, Raised Nodule: The most common presentation is a firm, painless nodule on the skin, often found on the trunk, arms, or legs.
Color Changes: The nodule may be skin-colored, brown, or purple.
Growth Over Time: DFSP typically grows slowly over months to years.
Ulceration: In some cases, the tumor may ulcerate, leading to bleeding or discharge.

diseases.name: Dermatographia – Causes, Symptoms, Treatment, Diagnosis and Prevention
diseases.description: Dermatographia, also known as skin writing, is a skin disorder where light scratching of the skin creates red bruises. When people with dermatographia scratch their skin lightly, the scratches turn into a raised wound that looks like Cholinergic Urticaria (hives) . These marks usually disappear within 30 minutes. This illness affects about 5% of the population, with older children and adults most affected.
symptoms: Dermatographia symptoms appear mostly when the skin is scratched. These signs and symptoms might develop suddenly and without notice. The following are some of the signs and symptoms of dermatographia:
Redness
Raised marks on the skin
Bruises that resemble hives
Itchiness
Inflammation or swelling
Extreme temperatures and dry weather might worsen the symptoms, which can persist for about 30 minutes to a day or more.
Consult a doctor if the signs and symptoms are very severe.

diseases.name: Dermatomyositis
diseases.description: Dermatomyositis is an uncommon inflammatory disease characterized by muscle weakness and a distinctive skin rash. It belongs to the group of inflammatory myopathies. The disease can affect adults and children. In adults, dermatomyositis may be associated with a higher risk of cancer. In children, it causes skin changes and muscle weakness.
symptoms: Skin rash (heliotrope rash on eyelids, Gottron's papules on knuckles)
Progressive muscle weakness
Difficulty swallowing
Hardening skin deposits under skin (calcinosis) in children
Fatigue
Weight loss
Fever

diseases.name: Dermoid Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dermoid cysts are benign growths that can occur in various parts of the body, often containing hair, skin, and sometimes even teeth. While they are generally harmless, understanding their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is crucial for anyone who may be affected by them. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of dermoid cysts, their significance, and what individuals should know about managing them.
symptoms: Dermoid cysts may not always present symptoms, especially if they are small. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Swelling or lump: A noticeable lump or swelling in the affected area, often painless.
Pain or discomfort: If the cyst becomes inflamed or infected, it may cause pain.
Skin changes: In cases where the cyst is located on the skin, changes in color or texture may be observed.

diseases.name: Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor (DSRCT) is a very rare and aggressive cancer that usually develops inside the abdomen or pelvis. It belongs to a group of cancers called soft tissue sarcomas, which start in the body’s supporting tissues like fat, muscles, and blood vessels.
symptoms: In the early stages, desmoplastic small round cell tumor may not cause noticeable problems. As tumors grow, symptoms often appear due to pressure on organs in the abdomen.
Abdominal pain or discomfort
A firm lump or swelling in the belly
Unexplained weight loss
Loss of appetite
Feeling full quickly
Bowel obstruction (constipation, bloating, or vomiting)
Difficulty breathing (if tumors spread to the chest)
Fatigue and weakness
Fluid build-up in the abdomen (ascites)
Because these symptoms can be mistaken for more common conditions, desmoplastic small round cell tumor is often diagnosed late.

diseases.name: Deviated nasal septum
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: In most cases, visible signs of a deviated septum may not even occur. In fact, you may not even realise that you may have a deviated septum at most times. However, the most common signs and symptoms include:
Noisy breathing during sleep
Nose bleeds
Facial pain
Obstruction of one or both nostrils
The need to sleep on a particular side
Awareness of the nasal cycle
Recurring sinus infections
If you have any/some/all of the above symptoms, seek medical attention promptly.

diseases.name: Dextrocardia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dextrocardia is a rare congenital condition where the heart is positioned on the right side of the chest instead of the left. This anatomical anomaly can have significant implications for an individual's health, particularly concerning the heart's function and its relationship with other organs. Understanding dextrocardia is crucial for early diagnosis and management, as it can sometimes be associated with other congenital heart defects or syndromes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of dextrocardia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Dextrocardia may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in mild cases. However, some common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area may occur, particularly if associated with other heart defects.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded during physical activity can be a sign of underlying heart issues.
Fatigue: Unexplained tiredness or lack of energy may indicate heart problems.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a racing heart can occur in some individuals.

diseases.name: Dextrocardia Situs Inversus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dextrocardia Situs Inversus is a rare congenital condition where the heart and other internal organs are positioned in the opposite direction to their normal anatomical placement. While it may sound alarming, most individuals with dextrocardia situs inversus can live normal lives without major complications. However, it can have significant implications for diagnosis, medical treatment, and emergency care. In this article, we’ll explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more to provide a complete understanding of this condition.
symptoms: In many cases, individuals with dextrocardia situs inversus may not experience any symptoms, and the condition is often discovered incidentally during a routine medical exam or imaging studies, such as a chest X-ray or ultrasound. However, certain symptoms may arise, particularly if the condition is part of a syndrome or if the person develops complications.

Chest Pain or Discomfort: Some individuals may experience chest pain or discomfort, but this is typically related to other underlying conditions (e.g., heart disease) and not directly due to the heart's position.

Breathing Difficulties: If dextrocardia situs inversus is associated with a condition like Kartagener syndrome, individuals may experience chronic respiratory issues such as coughing, wheezing, or difficulty breathing due to the presence of ciliary defects that affect the lungs and sinuses.

Heart Murmurs or Abnormal Heart Sounds: Although the heart's location is altered, it may function normally. However, in rare cases, the abnormal heart position may be associated with congenital heart defects that lead to murmurs or irregular heartbeats.

Situs Inversus-Related Symptoms: When other organs are mirror-imaged, some individuals may experience digestive discomfort, such as acid reflux or difficulties with digestion, though these symptoms are not directly caused by dextrocardia.

diseases.name: Diabetes Care in the Elderly: A Pragmatic Approach
diseases.description: Dr Ravi Sankar Erukulapati MBBS, MRCP ( UK ), CCT – GIM, Diabetes & Endocrinology (UK) Senior Endocrinologist Apollo Hospitals, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad

diseases.name: Diabetes Insipidus
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The most common symptoms of Diabetes Insipidus in adults are:
Extreme undying thirst
Excretion of large amounts of urine
Nocturia – waking up frequently at night to urinate
Bed-wetting
In infants and small children, the symptoms of Diabetes Insipidus may include:
Diarrhoea
Fever
Vomiting
Inconsolable crying
Trouble sleeping
Weight loss
Delayed growth
If you or your child have any/some/all of the above symptoms, seek medical attention promptly.

diseases.name: Diabetes Mellitus
diseases.description: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic condition where blood glucose levels are too high because the body does not make enough insulin or cannot use it properly. Type 2 diabetes is the most common form.
symptoms: Excessive thirst
Frequent urination
Fatigue
Blurred vision
Unintentional weight loss

diseases.name: Diabetic Coma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic coma is a serious medical condition that can occur in individuals with diabetes, characterized by a state of unconsciousness due to extremely high or low blood sugar levels. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe complications, including brain damage or even death, if not treated promptly. Understanding diabetic coma is crucial for individuals with diabetes, their families, and caregivers, as it can help in recognizing the signs and symptoms early, ensuring timely medical intervention.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of diabetic coma is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Hyperglycemic Coma: Excessive thirst and dry mouth Frequent urination Nausea and vomiting Abdominal pain Weakness or fatigue Confusion or difficulty concentrating Fruity-smelling breath (in DKA)
Excessive thirst and dry mouth
Frequent urination
Nausea and vomiting
Abdominal pain
Weakness or fatigue
Confusion or difficulty concentrating
Fruity-smelling breath (in DKA)
Hypoglycemic Coma: Sweating and clammy skin Tremors or shaking Rapid heartbeat Dizziness or lightheadedness Hunger Confusion or irritability Seizures or loss of consciousness
Sweating and clammy skin
Tremors or shaking
Rapid heartbeat
Dizziness or lightheadedness
Hunger
Confusion or irritability
Seizures or loss of consciousness

diseases.name: Diabetic Dermopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic Dermopathy is a common skin condition that affects individuals with diabetes, particularly those with poorly controlled blood sugar levels. This condition manifests as light brown, scaly patches on the skin, primarily on the lower legs. While it is not harmful in itself, it serves as a visible indicator of underlying diabetes-related complications. Understanding Diabetic Dermopathy is crucial for individuals with diabetes, as it highlights the importance of managing blood sugar levels and maintaining overall skin health.
symptoms: Brownish Patches: The most noticeable symptom is the appearance of small, round, brownish patches on the skin, primarily on the shins.
Scaly Texture: The affected areas may have a scaly or rough texture.
Painless: These patches are typically painless and do not cause itching or discomfort.

diseases.name: Diabetic Feet - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic feet refer to a range of foot problems that can occur in individuals with diabetes. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe complications, including infections, ulcers, and even amputations if not properly managed. With diabetes affecting millions of people worldwide, understanding diabetic feet is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of diabetic feet, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: Individuals with diabetic feet may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Numbness or Tingling: A common sign of neuropathy, which can lead to a lack of awareness of foot injuries.
Pain or Discomfort: Some may experience sharp or burning pain in their feet.
Changes in Skin Color: The skin may appear red, blue, or pale, indicating poor circulation.
Swelling: Inflammation can occur due to infection or injury.
Blisters or Ulcers: Open sores can develop, often without the individual realizing it.

diseases.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening condition that can occur in individuals with diabetes, particularly those with Type 1 diabetes. It arises when the body starts breaking down fat at an alarming rate, leading to the production of ketones, which can cause the blood to become acidic. Understanding DKA is crucial for anyone living with diabetes, as early recognition and treatment can save lives. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of DKA can develop quickly, often within 24 hours. Common symptoms include:
Excessive Thirst: Increased thirst due to dehydration.
Frequent Urination: The body attempts to eliminate excess glucose through urine.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal distress is common.
Abdominal Pain: Often described as severe and cramp-like.
Weakness or Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness and lack of energy.
Shortness of Breath: Rapid breathing as the body tries to compensate for acidosis.
Fruity-Scented Breath: A distinctive odor due to the presence of ketones.
Confusion or Difficulty Concentrating: Changes in mental status can occur.

diseases.name: Diabetic Nephropathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic nephropathy is a serious complication of diabetes that affects the kidneys, leading to progressive kidney damage and, ultimately, kidney failure if left untreated. As diabetes continues to rise globally, understanding diabetic nephropathy's significance is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of diabetic nephropathy, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: In the early stages, diabetic nephropathy may not present noticeable symptoms. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Proteinuria: The presence of excess protein in the urine, often detected through routine urine tests.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or feet due to fluid retention.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may arise as kidney function declines.
Changes in Urination: Increased frequency of urination, especially at night ( nocturia ), or decreased urine output.

diseases.name: Diabetic Retinopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diabetic retinopathy is a serious eye condition that affects individuals with diabetes, leading to potential vision loss and blindness. As diabetes continues to rise globally, understanding diabetic retinopathy's significance is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of diabetic retinopathy, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Diabetic retinopathy may not present noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Blurred or distorted vision
Difficulty seeing at night
Floaters or spots in the field of vision
Sudden vision loss
Colors appearing faded or washed out

diseases.name: Dialysis- A treatment for advanced Renal Diseases
diseases.description: You have two kidneys, each of which is about the size of your fist. These bean-shaped organs are located near the middle of your back, below the rib cage. Your kidneys filter out all the extra waste and water out of the blood, converting it into the urine. Inside these kidneys are million tiny structures known as nephrons which do the job. Having a kidney or renal disease implies that your kidneys are damaged and cannot carry out the filtering function as it should. Most of these diseases are due to the impact on nephrons which makes the kidneys unable to remove waste from your body. Chronic kidney diseases affect nephrons slowly over several years. So, you need to know more about what causes such advanced kidney diseases and the primary treatment for the same.
symptoms: The following are the warning signs for Renal Disease:
Itching
Muscle cramps
Nausea and vomiting
Not feeling hungry
Swelling in your feet and ankles
Too much or not enough urine
Trouble breathing
Trouble sleeping
In acute kidney failure (kidneys stop working suddenly), you may notice one or more of the following symptoms:
Belly (abdominal) pain
Back pain
Diarrhoea
Fever
Nosebleeds
Rash
Vomiting

diseases.name: Diamond Blackfan Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diamond Blackfan Anemia (DBA) is a rare blood disorder characterized by a failure of the bone marrow to produce enough red blood cells. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the affected individuals but also due to its implications for their families and healthcare systems. Understanding DBA is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Diamond Blackfan Anemia can vary widely among individuals but commonly include:
Fatigue: Due to a lack of red blood cells, individuals often feel tired and weak.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin and mucous membranes.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or even at rest in severe cases.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Especially when standing up quickly.
Increased Heart Rate: The heart may work harder to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Growth Delays: In children, DBA can lead to delayed growth and development.

diseases.name: Diaper Rash: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Diaper rash is a common form of inflamed skin (dermatitis) which appears as a patchwork of bright red skin on the bottom of your baby.
symptoms: Diaper rash is very easily identifiable by checking the bottom of the child from time to time. The symptoms are as follows:
The skin in and around the buttocks, other private parts, and thighs becomes reddish with uneven patches and eruptions.
The areas where the rash emerges get itchy and irritated, resulting in the child’s discomfort and crankiness.
The child starts crying during a diaper change or when the area with the diaper rash is touched.

diseases.name: Diaphoresis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diaphoresis, commonly known as excessive sweating, is a condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. While sweating is a natural and essential bodily function that helps regulate body temperature, diaphoresis occurs when sweating is excessive and not necessarily related to heat or exercise. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of diaphoresis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more, to help readers understand this condition better.
symptoms: Diaphoresis can manifest in various ways, and recognizing the symptoms is essential for timely intervention.
Excessive Sweating: Noticeable sweating that occurs even in cool environments or without physical exertion.
Skin Changes: Skin may appear clammy or wet, and in some cases, rashes or infections can develop due to moisture.
Body Odor: Increased sweating can lead to body odor, which may cause social discomfort.

diseases.name: Diarrhoeal Disease
diseases.description: Diarrhoeal disease is usually caused by infection of the intestinal tract and is commonly spread through contaminated food or drinking water or poor hygiene.
symptoms: Frequent loose or watery stools
Abdominal cramps
Nausea or vomiting
Fever in some cases
Signs of dehydration
Blood in stool in severe cases

diseases.name: Diastasis Recti - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diastasis Recti is a condition that affects many individuals, particularly women during and after pregnancy. It involves the separation of the rectus abdominis muscles, which can lead to various physical and aesthetic concerns. Understanding Diastasis Recti is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers and fitness professionals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Diastasis Recti, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Visible Bulge: A noticeable bulge in the midline of the abdomen, especially when straining or during physical activity.
Weakness in the Core: Difficulty engaging the abdominal muscles, leading to instability and poor posture.
Back Pain: Increased strain on the back muscles due to weakened core support.
Bloating: Some individuals may experience bloating or discomfort in the abdominal area.
Urinary Incontinence: Weakened abdominal muscles can contribute to pelvic floor dysfunction.

diseases.name: Diastema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diastema is a dental condition characterized by a gap or space between two teeth, most commonly seen between the upper front teeth. While it may seem like a cosmetic issue, diastema can have significant implications for oral health, self-esteem, and overall well-being. Understanding diastema is essential for recognizing its causes, symptoms, and treatment options, as well as for taking proactive steps to maintain dental health.
symptoms: The primary symptom of diastema is the visible gap between teeth. However, individuals may also experience:
Difficulty Chewing: Depending on the size of the gap, some individuals may find it challenging to chew food properly.
Speech Issues: Gaps can affect speech, particularly the pronunciation of certain sounds.
Tooth Sensitivity: Exposed tooth roots due to gum recession can lead to sensitivity to hot or cold foods.

diseases.name: Diastolic Heart Failure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diastolic heart failure, also known as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), is a significant and increasingly recognized condition that affects millions of people worldwide. Unlike systolic heart failure, where the heart's ability to contract is impaired, diastolic heart failure occurs when the heart muscle becomes stiff and cannot relax properly. This leads to inadequate filling of the heart's chambers, resulting in insufficient blood flow to meet the body's needs. Understanding diastolic heart failure is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of diastolic heart failure, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Diastolic heart failure presents with various symptoms, which may include:
Shortness of Breath: Often experienced during physical activity or while lying flat.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Swelling: Fluid retention in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a racing heart.
Coughing or Wheezing: Especially when lying down, due to fluid buildup in the lungs.

diseases.name: Diastolic Murmur - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A diastolic murmur is an abnormal sound heard during the heart's diastolic phase, which is when the heart relaxes and fills with blood. This sound can be an important indicator of underlying heart conditions and may require further investigation. Understanding diastolic murmurs is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as they can signify various cardiovascular issues that may need attention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis related to diastolic murmurs.
symptoms: Diastolic murmurs themselves may not cause symptoms, but the underlying conditions that lead to them can. Common symptoms associated with these conditions may include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or when lying down.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.

diseases.name: Diet and Nutrition for Kidney Patients
diseases.description: Your kidneys are small in size but perform many crucial functions of your body, including blood filtration, regulating blood pressure, maintaining electrolyte balance, and producing urine. However, certain health conditions, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, and obesity, along with your lifestyle and diet, tend to cause damage to your kidneys, thus, reducing their functional abilities.

diseases.name: Diet for Jaundice: Foods to Eat and Avoid
diseases.description: Jaundice is a disease that is caused by the buildup of bilirubin in the blood. This bilirubin is released during the red blood cell breakdown and is in yellow color. Jaundice causes the skin, eyes, gums to turn yellow. Jaundice is caused by a problem in any of the three stages in bilirubin production.

diseases.name: Different Kinds of Breast Tumors – Know How to Identify Them
diseases.description: A tumor is a lump of abnormal tissue. In a healthy being, body cells grow, divide and replace each other as per the normal process of life. As the new cells begin to form, the old ones start to die. However, if there are too many new cells, an accumulation of the cells could form a tumor. A tumor could be located anywhere in the body and one in the breasts is known as breast tumor. Not all kinds of tumors are cancerous. So, let us take a look at the different types of tumors found in breasts and how to differentiate between them.
symptoms: The symptoms of benign and malignant tumors are often similar. Depending on the type of tumor, the symptoms are experienced. The common symptoms for the different kinds of tumors are:
Fibrocystic breasts: Breast discomfort and tenderness. Small lumps. Swelling increases right before menstruation. Can be extremely painful to some.
Fibroadenoma: Well-rounded, smooth, rubbery, solid lumps. They are painless and may disappear on their own. When touched, they move freely.
Breast cysts: They are generally round, soft grape like, with distinct edges, tiny or big, and may be painful only if it is large or grows during the menstrual cycle.

Breast cancer: During the early stages, the symptoms are not quite noticeable. However, with time, you can feel a thickening or firm lump, size or shape of the breast may change, dimpling in the breast skin, nipple may turn inwards and even turn red, swollen and scaly. Also, nipple discharge, either bloody or clear is common.

diseases.name: Different Types of Scleroderma and How to Cope
diseases.description: A scleroderma is a disease that hardens and tightens the skin and connective tissues. It is not a contagious (or infectious) disease. Women are at higher risk of getting scleroderma than men. Individuals between the ages of 35 and 50 are more prone to get scleroderma.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of scleroderma differ according to the affected part of the body:
1. Skin:
● Patches on the skin which are stiff and tight.
● Ovals or straight lines shaped patches.
● Patches cover larger areas of the torso and limbs.
● The shiny appearance of the skin.
● The affected area may have restrictions in movement.
● Lack of blood flow to parts of your body such as your fingers, toes, or nose, usually because of cold-causing Raynaud’s disease.
● The colour of your skin might turn red, white, or blue.
2. Digestive system:
● Heartburn or dysphagia, if the esophagus is affected.
● Cramps, bloating, diarrhea , or constipation, if the intestines are affected.
● Difficulty in absorbing nutrients due to improper function of intestinal muscles.
3. Heart, lungs, or kidneys:
The function of the vital organs like the lungs, heart, and kidneys can be affected by Scleroderma. The conditions can become critical if proper treatment is not carried out.

diseases.name: Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that is characterized by the rapid growth of large B cells in the lymphatic system. As one of the most common forms of lymphoma, DLBCL accounts for approximately 30% of all non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases. Understanding DLBCL is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers, as it can significantly impact quality of life and requires timely intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of DLBCL can vary widely, but common signs include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Painless swelling in the neck, armpit, or groin.
Fever: Unexplained fevers that may come and go.
Night Sweats: Profuse sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss over a short period.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Abdominal Pain or Swelling: If the lymphoma affects the abdomen, it may cause discomfort or swelling.

diseases.name: DiGeorge Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: DiGeorge Syndrome, also known as 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, is a genetic disorder that can affect various systems in the body. It is characterized by a range of health issues, including heart defects, immune system problems, and developmental delays. Understanding DiGeorge Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for families and healthcare providers, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of DiGeorge Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: DiGeorge Syndrome presents a wide range of symptoms, which can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Heart Defects: Congenital heart issues are prevalent, including tetralogy of Fallot and ventricular septal defects.
Immune System Problems: Individuals may have a weakened immune system, leading to increased susceptibility to infections.
Facial Features: Distinctive facial characteristics may include a long face, low-set ears, and a small jaw.
Developmental Delays: Many children with DiGeorge Syndrome experience delays in speech and motor skills.
Hypoparathyroidism: This condition can lead to low calcium levels, resulting in muscle spasms and seizures.
Psychiatric Disorders: Some individuals may develop mental health issues, including anxiety and depression.

diseases.name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a serious heart condition that affects the heart muscle, leading to a decrease in its ability to pump blood effectively. This condition is significant because it can lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, and other serious complications if not diagnosed and managed properly. Understanding DCM is crucial for early detection and treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of DCM can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Shortness of Breath: This may occur during exertion or even at rest as the condition progresses.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy is common.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen due to fluid retention.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a feeling of the heart racing.
Chest Pain: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the chest.

diseases.name: Dilated Pore Of Winer - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dilated Pore of Winer (DPOW) is a benign skin condition characterized by a large, dilated pore that resembles a cyst or a comedone. This condition is often mistaken for other skin lesions, making it essential for both patients and healthcare providers to recognize its unique features. Understanding DPOW is significant not only for accurate diagnosis but also for effective management and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Dilated Pore of Winer, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of DPOW is the appearance of a single, enlarged pore, which may be:
Flesh-colored or slightly pigmented: The lesion can vary in color.
Firm to the touch: It may feel like a small bump on the skin.
Filled with keratin: The pore may contain a keratin plug, which can sometimes be expressed.

diseases.name: Diphtheria
diseases.description: Diphtheria is a serious bacterial infection that can affect the throat or skin and produce a toxin that causes severe illness.
symptoms: Sore throat
Fever
Swollen neck glands
Gray coating in throat or nose
Weakness

diseases.name: Disc Prolapse : Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: A disc Prolapse or a Herniated disc is a problem in the rubbery cushions or discs that sit between the individual bones, known as vertebrae, which stack to make the spine. The spinal disc is quite soft and has a jelly-like center nucleus where it is encased in the rubbery exterior or annulus. In a ruptured disc or a herniated disc this nucleus is pushed out through a tear in the annulus. This herniated disc is something which can occur at any part of the spine. When there is a herniated disc, it can easily irritate a nearby nerve and depending on this, there can be pain, numbness or weakness in the arm or leg or area supplied by that nerve . It generally happens in the legs. You don’t necessarily need surgery to relieve the problem unless it is very severe.
symptoms: When you have a lot of pain in the lower back or in the neck, it can be due to disc prolapse. The signs appear as the prolapse presses the nerve. They also affect only one side of the body either left or on the right side.

You may have immense pain in your arm or leg and if it is the leg, the pain shoots from the lower back and if it is in the arm, the pain shoots from the neck. You will feel the pain when you sneeze or cough or move.
You may have a little bit of numbness. If you ever feel a tingling sensation or numbness, then it means that part is heavily affected and the nerves are suppressed due to the prolapse.

There is a prolonged weakness and if this is so, you need to visit the doctor immediately. Muscles are often weakened by the nerves and this may cause you to fall frequently or simply have the inability to lift heavy items.
You need to see the doctor when the neck or the back pain travels down your arm or leg and also if you have numbness or severe weakness.

diseases.name: Discoid Lupus Erythematosus (DLE)
diseases.description: Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes scarring skin lesions. It is the most common form of cutaneous (skin) lupus. Lesions are typically round, scaly, and red-to-violet in color and can leave permanent scars. Although primarily a skin condition, a small percentage of DLE patients may develop systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
symptoms: Round, coin-shaped, scaly plaques on the face, scalp, ears, and neck
Skin discoloration (hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation) after lesions heal
Scarring hair loss (scarring alopecia) on the scalp
Thickened skin
Photosensitivity

diseases.name: Dislocated Jaw - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A dislocated jaw, also known as temporomandibular joint (TMJ) dislocation, is a condition where the lower jaw (mandible) becomes displaced from its normal position in the joint that connects it to the skull. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and functional impairment, affecting a person's ability to speak, eat, and perform daily activities. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options for a dislocated jaw is crucial for effective management and recovery.
symptoms: Jaw Pain: A dislocated jaw often causes significant pain in the jaw area, which may radiate to the ears or neck.
Inability to Close the Mouth: Individuals may find it difficult or impossible to close their mouths completely.
Swelling: The area around the jaw may become swollen and tender to the touch.
Jaw Deformity: The jaw may appear misaligned or protruded to one side.
Difficulty Speaking or Eating: Dislocation can hinder normal speech and eating functions.

diseases.name: Disorders Associated With Low Dietary Fibre Intake
diseases.description: A balanced diet containing all types of nutrients is essential for every person, irrespective of his/her age and physical condition. Dietary fibre is a critical component of our daily diet, helping keep our digestive system healthy. Unlike other nutrients, it does not break down and get absorbed by our body cells. Thus, it passes down the digestive tract to the colon and rectum, increasing the bulk of excretory products moving out of our body.

diseases.name: Dissociative Amnesia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dissociative Amnesia is a complex psychological condition that affects an individual's ability to recall important personal information, often related to traumatic or stressful events. This condition is significant not only because it can severely impact a person's daily life and relationships but also because it highlights the intricate connection between memory, trauma, and mental health. Understanding Dissociative Amnesia is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can lead to effective treatment and recovery.
symptoms: Memory Loss: Inability to recall personal information, particularly related to traumatic events.
Disorientation: Confusion about time, place, or identity.
Emotional Numbness: Difficulty experiencing emotions or connecting with others.
Depersonalization: Feeling detached from oneself or one's surroundings.
Derealization: A sense that the world around is unreal or distorted.

diseases.name: Dissociative Identity Disorder - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Risks and Treatment
diseases.description: Dissociative identity disorder (DID) is a severe mental disease that causes individuals to have two or more personalities or identities. These identities take over a person’s behaviour at different times. Dissociative identity disorder leads to memory gaps and other problems. This blog is a comprehensive guide to understanding dissociative identity disorder, causes, symptoms, prevention, and treatment.
symptoms: People with dissociative identity disorder have two or more recognizable identities – called alters. The normal personality is the ‘core’ identity. Some people with this disorder have 100 alters. These alternative personalities tend to be very different from one another. The identities may have different genders, interests, ethnicities, and methods of interacting with their environment.
The other common signs and symptoms of this disorder include:
Anxiety
Delusions
Disorientation
Depression
Memory loss
Drug or alcohol abuse
Suicidal thoughts or self-harm

diseases.name: Distributive Shock - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Distributive shock is a serious medical condition that occurs when the body's blood vessels lose their ability to constrict properly, leading to inadequate blood flow to vital organs. This condition is significant because it can result in severe complications, including organ failure and death, if not recognized and treated promptly. Understanding distributive shock is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early intervention can save lives.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of distributive shock is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Low Blood Pressure: A significant drop in blood pressure is a hallmark of distributive shock.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may beat faster in an attempt to compensate for low blood pressure.
Warm, Flushed Skin: Unlike other types of shock, the skin may feel warm and appear flushed due to vasodilation.
Confusion or Altered Mental Status: Reduced blood flow to the brain can lead to confusion, disorientation, or loss of consciousness.
Weakness or Fatigue: Individuals may feel unusually weak or fatigued due to inadequate blood flow to muscles and organs.

diseases.name: Diverticulitis
diseases.description: Diverticulitis is caused as a result of diverticula – small, bulging pouches that form in the lining of your digestive system. They are found most often in the colon . When these pouches become inflamed or infected they cause a condition named diverticulitis. Diverticulitis can cause severe abdominal pain, fever, nausea and can also hamper your bowel movements to a great extent.
symptoms: Most common signs and symptoms of diverticulitis include:
Fever
Nausea and vomiting
Pain is usually felt in the lower left side of the abdomen, but may occur on the right side
Nausea
Vomiting
Constipation or, less commonly, diarrhoea
Abdominal tenderness
If you have any/some/all of the above symptoms, do seek prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Diverticulosis

symptoms: Majority of people do not exhibit symptoms of Diverticulosis. Patients might have had diverticulosis for years together by the time the symptoms exhibit. And over time, some patients get an infection in the pouches (Diverticulitis).

diseases.name: Don't Underestimate the Risk: The Truth About Sudden Cardiac Arrest in Young People
diseases.description: Imagine a seemingly healthy young person suddenly collapsing, unconscious, and fighting for their life. This frightening scenario is the reality of Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA), an unexpected and life-threatening event that occurs when the heart abruptly stops beating. In these critical moments, survival hinges on the swift actions of bystanders and emergency responders, employing crucial life-saving measures like CPR and automated defibrillators.

diseases.name: Don’t Let Type2 Diabetes Control You
diseases.description: Diabetes is a metabolic disease characterized by high blood sugar (glucose) levels that are a result of impaired insulin secretion in the body, or inability of the body to use the secreted insulin effectively. As you are aware, the blood glucose levels are controlled by insulin which is a hormone produced by the pancreas. When the blood glucose elevates (for example, after eating food), insulin is released from the pancreas which helps in the uptake of glucose into body cells. In patients with diabetes , the impaired production of or lack of response to insulin causes hyperglycemia. Inadequately managing type 2 diabetes can lead to complications later on. You need to manage your blood sugars and regularly monitor them to be sure they are within the target range. Taking care of yourself is ‘empowering’ yourself. Here are few easy ways to take an active role in diabetes care and enjoy a healthier future

diseases.name: Double Aortic Arch - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Double Aortic Arch (DAA) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly characterized by the presence of two aortic arches that encircle the trachea and esophagus. This condition can lead to significant clinical implications, including respiratory and swallowing difficulties. Understanding DAA is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can impact the quality of life and overall health of affected individuals.
symptoms: Individuals with Double Aortic Arch may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Stridor: A high-pitched wheezing sound during breathing, often due to airway compression.
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, which can occur if the esophagus is compressed.
Respiratory Distress: Increased effort in breathing, especially during physical activity.
Coughing: Persistent cough that may worsen with exertion.
Recurrent Respiratory Infections: Increased susceptibility to infections due to airway obstruction.

diseases.name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Double Outlet Right Ventricle (DORV) is a complex congenital heart defect that significantly impacts the heart's structure and function. This condition is characterized by both the aorta and the pulmonary artery arising from the right ventricle, rather than the normal arrangement where the aorta originates from the left ventricle. Understanding DORV is crucial, as it can lead to serious health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of DORV, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of DORV can vary widely depending on the severity of the defect and the presence of associated heart conditions. Common symptoms include:
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, lips, and nails due to low oxygen levels in the blood.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate, especially during feeding or exertion.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty feeding or poor weight gain in infants.
Fatigue: Excessive tiredness or lethargy, particularly during physical activity.
Heart Murmurs: Abnormal heart sounds detected during a physical examination.

diseases.name: Double Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Double uterus, medically known as uterus didelphys, is a rare congenital condition where a woman has two separate uterine cavities, each with its own cervix. This condition arises during fetal development when the Müllerian ducts, which form the female reproductive system, fail to fuse properly. While many women with a double uterus may lead normal lives, understanding this condition is crucial for those affected, as it can have implications for reproductive health and pregnancy. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of double uterus, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Many women with a double uterus may not experience any symptoms. However, some may encounter:
Menstrual Irregularities: This can include heavy bleeding or prolonged periods.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort may arise due to the presence of two uterine cavities.
Infertility: Some women may face challenges in conceiving.
Pregnancy Complications: Women with a double uterus may experience complications such as preterm labor or miscarriage.

diseases.name: Down Syndrome
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Each person with down syndrome is distinct with respect to the degree of development issues ranging from mild to severe health problems. Children with the condition have a distinctive appearance and some of the most common features are
Compressed facial appearance
Undersized head
Dwarfed neck
Obtruding tongue
Unusually formed ears
Low muscle tone (Hypotonia)
Overall stunted growth
Excessive flexibility
Tiny white spots on the colored part (iris) of the eye

diseases.name: Dracunculiasis (Guinea worm disease)
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms don’t show up to a year after infection. Typically before the worm bursts through the skin in the legs and feet or other parts of the body, the host may feel ill and manifest the following:
Mild Fever
Swelling
Slow and Disabling pain
Nausea and Vomiting
Diarrhoea
Secondary bacterial infection and Allergic Rashes
Dizziness
Joint infection and locking of joints

diseases.name: Dravet Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dravet Syndrome is a severe form of epilepsy that typically begins in infancy. It is characterized by prolonged seizures, developmental delays, and a range of other neurological issues. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the affected individuals and their families but also due to the challenges it presents in terms of diagnosis and management. Understanding Dravet Syndrome is crucial for early intervention, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Dravet Syndrome is characterized by a range of symptoms that can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Seizures: The hallmark of Dravet Syndrome, these can be prolonged and may include generalized tonic-clonic seizures, myoclonic seizures, and focal seizures.
Developmental Delays: Many children with Dravet Syndrome experience delays in reaching developmental milestones, including speech and motor skills.
Behavioral Issues: Children may exhibit behavioral problems, including hyperactivity, aggression, and social withdrawal.
Temperature Sensitivity: Many individuals with Dravet Syndrome are sensitive to changes in temperature, which can trigger seizures.

diseases.name: Drug allergy
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: If you are allergic to a certain drug, you may start feeling the effects within an hour of its intake. Most common signs and symptoms of a drug allergy include:
Hives
Skin rash
Itching
Swelling
Shortness of breath
Fever
Wheezing
Itchy, watery eyes
Runny nose
Anaphylaxis: As mentioned earlier, anaphylaxis is a life-threatening condition that can occur if you have an allergic reaction to a drug. Its signs and symptoms include:
Nausea or abdominal cramps
Tightening of the airways and throat, causing trouble breathing
Vomiting
Diarrhoea
Dizziness or feeling lightheaded
Drop in blood pressure
Loss of consciousness
Seizure
Weak, rapid pulse

diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: As mentioned earlier, there are two types of withdrawal symptoms.
Restlessness
Anxiety
Irritability
Poor concentration
Insomnia
Social isolation
Headaches
Depression
Palpitations
Difficulty breathing
Muscle tension
Sweating
Racing heart
Tightness in the chest
Tremors
Nausea
Vomiting
Diarrhoea
Some symptoms can be extremely dangerous and life-threatening including seizures, heart attacks , hallucination and delirium tremens.

diseases.name: Dry Socket - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dry socket , medically known as alveolar osteitis, is a painful condition that can occur after a tooth extraction, particularly the removal of wisdom teeth. It is significant because it can lead to severe discomfort and complications if not properly managed. Understanding dry socket is essential for anyone undergoing dental procedures, as awareness can help in prevention and prompt treatment.
symptoms: Severe Pain: The most prominent symptom is intense pain that can radiate to the ear, eye, or neck.
Bad Breath: An unpleasant odor may emanate from the mouth due to exposed bone and potential infection.
Visible Bone: In some cases, the dentist may observe exposed bone in the socket during an examination.
Delayed Healing: The extraction site may take longer to heal than expected.

diseases.name: Duane Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Duane Syndrome is a rare congenital eye movement disorder that affects the ability of the eyes to move properly. It is characterized by limited eye movement, particularly in the horizontal plane, and can lead to various visual and cosmetic concerns. Understanding Duane Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Duane Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of Duane Syndrome can vary widely among individuals, but common signs include:
Limited Eye Movement: The most characteristic symptom is the inability to move the affected eye outward (abduction) or inward (adduction) properly.
Strabismus: Misalignment of the eyes, which may be more pronounced when the person is tired or stressed.
Head Turn: Many individuals with Duane Syndrome adopt a head turn or tilt to compensate for the limited eye movement.
Double Vision: Some individuals may experience diplopia (double vision) due to misalignment.
Amblyopia: Reduced vision in one eye may occur if the brain favors one eye over the other.

diseases.name: Dubin Johnson Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dubin Johnson Syndrome (DJS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the liver's ability to process and excrete bilirubin, a substance produced during the breakdown of red blood cells. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on liver function but also due to its implications for overall health and well-being. Understanding DJS is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can help mitigate potential complications and improve quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Dubin Johnson Syndrome can vary in severity and may include:
Jaundice: A yellowing of the skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels.
Dark Urine: Urine may appear darker than usual, indicating increased bilirubin excretion.
Fatigue: Individuals may experience general tiredness or lack of energy.
Abdominal Discomfort: Some may report mild abdominal pain or discomfort, particularly in the liver area.

diseases.name: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a severe form of muscular dystrophy that primarily affects boys, leading to progressive muscle degeneration and weakness. This genetic disorder is caused by a mutation in the dystrophin gene, which is essential for maintaining muscle cell integrity. Understanding DMD is crucial not only for those affected but also for families, caregivers, and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can significantly impact the quality of life and disease progression.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy include:
Muscle Weakness: Initial weakness often affects the hips, pelvis, and legs, leading to difficulty in walking and climbing stairs.
Delayed Motor Skills: Children may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones such as walking.
Frequent Falls: Increased susceptibility to falls due to muscle weakness.
Waddling Gait: A characteristic gait pattern due to muscle weakness.
Calf Hypertrophy: Enlargement of calf muscles, which may appear strong but are actually weakened.
Difficulty with Motor Activities: Challenges with running, jumping, and other physical activities.

diseases.name: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a very early form of breast cancer. It begins in the milk ducts of the breast but does not spread outside them. Because it has not invaded nearby breast tissue, DCIS is often called "non-invasive breast cancer" or "stage 0 breast cancer".
symptoms: Most women with ductal carcinoma in situ do not notice any symptoms. In fact, it is usually found during a screening mammogram before it causes problems.
Rarely, it may present as:
A lump in the breast.
Discharge from the nipple (sometimes bloody).
Changes in breast appearance, such as a small area of thickening.
These signs are not always cancer, but they should always be checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Dumping Syndrome: Treatment, Symptoms and Causes
diseases.description: Do you feel full after having a stomach-related surgery? The dumping syndrome may cause that sensation. Dumping syndrome is a set of effects that can develop post-surgery to remove all or a part of the stomach or, to bypass your stomach after surgery in order to help you lose weight or after esophageal surgery.
symptoms: The symptoms of dumping syndrome usually present after having meals post-surgery. There can be early and late symptoms. Some of the common signs of the early phase of the condition include:
Bloated feeling
Vomiting
Abdominal cramps
Nausea
Rapid heart rate
Flushing
Dizziness
Diarrhea
Some common symptoms of late-phase dumping syndrome include:
Weakness
Sweating
Some individuals have both early and late symptoms. And, dumping syndrome can develop years after the surgery.
When to see a doctor for dumping syndrome?

Whether you have had a surgery or not, visit your doctor if you have any of the above signs and symptoms for a prolonged period. Also, you need to see a doctor if dietary changes do not help alleviate the symptoms or if you are losing large amounts of weight.

diseases.name: Duodenal Atresia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Duodenal atresia is a congenital condition that affects the digestive system, specifically the duodenum, which is the first part of the small intestine. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding duodenal atresia is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: Newborns with duodenal atresia typically present with several characteristic symptoms, including:
Vomiting: Often bilious (greenish-yellow), indicating that bile is present.
Abdominal Distension: The abdomen may appear swollen or bloated due to trapped gas and fluid.
Inability to Feed: Infants may refuse to feed or show signs of distress during feeding.
Failure to Pass Meconium: Newborns may not pass their first stool within the first 24 hours of life.

diseases.name: Duodenitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Duodenitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. This condition is significant because it can lead to various gastrointestinal issues, affecting digestion and overall health. Understanding duodenitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as untreated cases can lead to complications that may require more intensive medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of duodenitis can vary in severity and may include:
Abdominal Pain : Often described as a burning sensation in the upper abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting : These symptoms may occur, especially after eating.
Bloating : A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Loss of Appetite : Due to discomfort or pain associated with eating.
Weight Loss : Unintentional weight loss may occur if symptoms persist.

diseases.name: Duplex Kidney - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Duplex kidney, also known as renal duplication, is a congenital condition characterized by the presence of two ureters (the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder) for one kidney. This condition can have significant implications for kidney function and overall health. Understanding duplex kidney is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to complications if left untreated. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of duplex kidney.
symptoms: Many individuals with duplex kidney may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some common symptoms can include:
Frequent Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Due to abnormal urine flow.
Back Pain: Resulting from kidney dysfunction or infection.
Abdominal Pain: May occur if there are complications such as obstruction.
Blood in Urine: A sign of potential complications or infections.
Difficulty Urinating: May indicate obstruction or other urinary tract issues.

diseases.name: Dupuytren's Contracture
diseases.description: Dupuytren's contracture is a hand deformity that usually develops over years, in which the tissue beneath the skin of the palm — the fascia — thickens and tightens over time, eventually causing one or more fingers to curl inward. It most commonly affects the ring finger and little finger and can make it difficult to use the hand fully.
symptoms: Firm lumps or nodules in the palm
Cords of tissue forming under skin of palm
Fingers bending toward palm and unable to fully straighten
Difficulty picking up or grasping objects

diseases.name: Dust Mite Allergies: Causes, Symptoms, Treatmened
diseases.description: Dust allergy (also called dust mite allergy) is an allergic reaction to tiny dust mites that are present in the house. These mites eat flakes of dead skin that people regularly shed and are typically present on beddings, mattresses, carpets, and furniture. The tiny bugs are known to thrive in all climates and most altitudes. They are the most common triggers for allergy and asthma.
symptoms: The symptoms of dust mite allergies include the following:
Sneezing
Wheezing
Coughing
Red, itchy, or watery eyes
Runny or stuffy nose
Itchiness in skin, nose, mouth, or throat
Postnasal mucus drip
Sinus pressure that may cause facial pain
Trouble in sleeping
Swollen and discolored skin below the eyes
People with asthma along with dust mite allergies may experience aggravated symptoms, including:
Increased chest pain or tightness
Difficulty breathing
Wheezing, coughing, or shortness of breath
Severe asthma attack
Difficulty talking

diseases.name: Dysarthria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysarthria is a speech disorder that affects the muscles used for speaking, leading to slurred or slow speech that can be difficult to understand. This condition can significantly impact an individual's ability to communicate effectively, which can affect their social interactions, self-esteem, and overall quality of life. Understanding dysarthria is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain their communication skills and improve their quality of life.
symptoms: Dysarthria can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Slurred Speech: Words may sound mumbled or unclear.
Slow Speech: Speech may be noticeably slower than normal.
Soft or Weak Voice: The volume of speech may be reduced, making it difficult to hear.
Changes in Pitch: The voice may sound monotone or have an unusual pitch.
Difficulty Controlling Speech: Individuals may struggle to control their speech rate or rhythm.

diseases.name: Dysbiosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysbiosis is a term that has gained significant attention in recent years, particularly in the fields of gastroenterology and immunology. It refers to an imbalance in the microbial communities that inhabit our bodies, particularly in the gut. These microbial communities, known as the microbiome, play a crucial role in our overall health, influencing everything from digestion to immune function. Understanding dysbiosis is essential because it can lead to a variety of health issues, including gastrointestinal disorders, autoimmune diseases, and even mental health conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of dysbiosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Dysbiosis can present a wide range of symptoms, which may vary depending on the individual and the severity of the imbalance. Common symptoms include:
Digestive Issues: Bloating, gas, diarrhea, constipation, and abdominal pain are frequent complaints.
Fatigue: Many individuals with dysbiosis report feeling unusually tired or fatigued.
Skin Problems: Conditions like eczema or acne may be exacerbated by dysbiosis.
Mood Changes: Dysbiosis has been linked to anxiety and depression, leading to mood swings or irritability.
Autoimmune Symptoms: Individuals with autoimmune conditions may experience worsening symptoms.

diseases.name: Dyscalculia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dyscalculia is a specific learning disability that affects an individual's ability to understand and work with numbers. Often referred to as "math dyslexia," it can significantly impact a person's academic performance and daily life. While many people may struggle with math at some point, dyscalculia is a persistent condition that requires understanding and support. Recognizing dyscalculia is crucial, as early intervention can lead to better outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of dyscalculia can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Difficulty understanding number concepts and relationships.
Trouble with basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division).
Inability to memorize math facts or formulas.
Difficulty telling time or understanding measurements.
Struggles with spatial awareness and visualizing numbers.
Anxiety or frustration when faced with math-related tasks.

diseases.name: Dysentery (Loose Motions): Types, Causes, Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysentery is a common gastrointestinal illness that causes inflammation of the intestines, typically the colon. It leads to severe diarrhea, often accompanied by blood or mucus in the stools. The condition is especially prevalent during the monsoon season , as it spreads through contaminated water and food. That’s why it's important to be extra cautious about what you eat and drink during this time.
symptoms: Dysentery symptoms can appear suddenly and may last for five days or longer. Some people experience mild discomfort, while others may suffer from severe diarrhea or vomiting , leading to dehydration .
Common symptoms include:
Abdominal pain
Abdominal bloating .
Nausea, with or without vomiting
Fever and chills
Fatigue and weakness
Pain while passing stools
Watery diarrhea, sometimes with blood, mucus, or pus
Intermittent constipation or Flatulence
In more severe cases, dehydration may occur, leading to symptoms like:
Excessive thirst
Dry mouth or dry skin
Decreased urine output
Muscle cramps
Rapid weight loss

If you experience any of these symptoms, especially blood in your stool or signs of dehydration, seek medical attention immediately. Early treatment can help prevent complications and ensure faster recovery.

diseases.name: Dysgeusia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysgeusia is a medical condition characterized by a distorted sense of taste. It can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, affecting their ability to enjoy food and, in some cases, leading to nutritional deficiencies. Understanding dysgeusia is essential not only for those experiencing it but also for healthcare providers who can help manage this often-overlooked condition. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding dysgeusia.
symptoms: The primary symptom of dysgeusia is a persistent alteration in taste. Other associated symptoms may include:
Metallic Taste: A common complaint where food tastes metallic or bitter.
Loss of Taste: Some individuals may experience a reduced ability to taste altogether (hypogeusia).
Increased Sensitivity: Foods may taste overly salty or sweet, leading to discomfort while eating.

diseases.name: Dysgraphia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysgraphia is a specific learning disability that affects an individual's ability to write coherently and legibly. It is a condition that can significantly impact a person's academic performance and self-esteem, making it essential for parents, educators, and healthcare professionals to understand its implications. Dysgraphia is not merely a problem with handwriting; it encompasses a range of difficulties related to the physical act of writing, spelling, and organizing thoughts on paper. Recognizing and addressing dysgraphia early can lead to better outcomes for those affected, allowing them to develop effective coping strategies and achieve their full potential.
symptoms: Dysgraphia can present a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Illegible Handwriting: Letters may be poorly formed, inconsistent in size, or difficult to read.
Inconsistent Spacing: Words may be spaced too closely together or too far apart, making written work hard to follow.
Difficulty with Spelling: Individuals may struggle to spell words correctly, often omitting letters or using incorrect letter sequences.
Poor Organization: Written work may lack structure, with ideas presented in a disorganized manner.
Physical Discomfort: Writing may cause discomfort or fatigue, leading to a reluctance to engage in writing tasks.
Slow Writing Speed: Individuals may take longer to complete writing assignments compared to their peers.

diseases.name: Dyshidrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dyshidrosis, also known as dyshidrotic eczema or pompholyx, is a skin condition characterized by the development of small, itchy blisters on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. This condition can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected, causing discomfort and emotional distress. Understanding dyshidrosis is crucial for effective management and treatment, as well as for preventing potential complications. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding dyshidrosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of dyshidrosis can vary in severity and may include:
Itchy Blisters: Small, fluid-filled blisters that can be very itchy.
Redness and Inflammation: The skin around the blisters may appear red and inflamed.
Cracking and Peeling: After the blisters burst, the skin may crack and peel, leading to discomfort.
Thickened Skin: Chronic cases may result in thickened, scaly skin.

diseases.name: Dyshidrotic Eczema - Symptoms, Causes, Prevention, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Dyshidrotic Eczema, also known as Dyshidrosis, is a skin condition that causes blisters on the palms of the hands or soles of the feet. There is no cure for dyshidrotic eczema yet, but it is manageable . In mild cases of dyshidrotic eczema, the blisters usually go away on their own.
symptoms: The blisters linked to dyshidrosis occur most commonly on the sides of your fingers and the palms. Sometimes the soles of your feet can also be affected. The blisters are generally small — about the width of a standard pencil lead — and grouped in clusters.

In more-serious cases, the small blisters may merge to become larger blisters. The skin affected by dyshidrosis can become very itchy and painful. Once the blisters get dry and flake off (which occurs in about 3 weeks), the underlying skin might be red and tender.
Dyshidrosis tends to recur fairly regularly for months or years.
In most cases, dyshidrotic eczema goes away in about two to three weeks. Even after the blisters disappear, the skin underneath can be tender and red for a few days.

Dyshidrotic Eczema can be mild or severe. If you develop severe dyshidrotic eczema on your feet, you may face difficulty walking. Severe cases of blisters on hands may make it difficult for you to carry out daily chores.
If you scratch the blisters, it may get infected and cause pain. The common signs of infection include:
Pus in the blisters
Swelling
Severe pain
Crusting

diseases.name: Dyslexia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Our brain controls the learning process and the development of skills. Brain functioning is a complex process that coordinates learning, reading, speech, language, and many more. Dyslexia does not imply mental retardation, brain damage, or decreased intelligence. It runs within families and can be transferred to the next generation.
symptoms: Symptoms of dyslexia in a child are hard to diagnose unless they are at school-going age. You might get contacted by the school teachers about their learning difficulties, as they are the first ones who will notice it. Mentioned below are a few common symptoms of dyslexia in a child:
Less talkative
Difficulty in reading
Problems identifying words correctly or mixing up words
Confusion to words that sounds similar
Difficulties in remembering/ recalling names, numbers, colors, or memorizing
Difficulties in rhyming songs or solving simple puzzles
Not able to spell things correctly
Avoiding tasks such as reading, singing, etc
Writing difficulties
Depression

diseases.name: Dyslipidemia (High Cholesterol)
diseases.description: Dyslipidemia means unhealthy levels of blood fats (cholesterol and triglycerides), which increases the risk of heart disease and stroke.
symptoms: Usually no symptoms

diseases.name: Dysmenorrhea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Dysmenorrhea, commonly known as painful menstruation, is a condition that affects a significant number of individuals who menstruate. It is characterized by severe pain during menstruation, which can interfere with daily activities and overall quality of life. Understanding dysmenorrhea is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers and society at large, as it highlights the importance of menstrual health and well-being.
symptoms: The primary symptom of dysmenorrhea is pelvic pain, which can vary in intensity. Other common symptoms include:
Cramping: Sharp or dull pain in the lower abdomen, often radiating to the lower back and thighs.
Nausea: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal discomfort, including nausea or vomiting.
Headaches: Hormonal changes can trigger headaches or migraines during menstruation.
Fatigue: Many individuals report feeling unusually tired or fatigued during their menstrual cycle.
Mood Changes: Hormonal fluctuations can lead to mood swings, irritability, or anxiety.

diseases.name: Dyspareunia or Painful Intercourse - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Painful intercourse or dyspareunia is the name given to the recurring pain in the genital region of a human being during intercourse. It is a treatable pain that occurs in women more than in men. The pain is unbearably severe and intense. It can happen anytime, before, after, or during sexual intercourse.
symptoms: Pelvic inflammatory disease
Uterine fibroids
Irritable bowel syndrome
Radiation and chemotherapy
Infections like yeast or urinary tract infections
Injury or trauma from childbirth, an accident, an episiotomy , a hysterectomy , or pelvic surgery
Pain at the time of sexual penetration
Vaginal dryness from menopause , childbirth, breastfeeding, medications, or too little arousal before intercourse
Pain with every penetration, including putting in a tampon
Skin disorders that cause ulcers, cracks, itching, or burning
Deep pain during thrusting
Vaginitis or inflammation of the vagina
Endometriosis
Cystitis
Burning pain or aching pain in the genitals
Throbbing pain, lasting hours after intercourse.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Dystonia: Types, Symptoms, Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Multiple disorders may affect the normal movement of the human body. These disorders may happen due to a malfunctioning nervous system or genetic reasons. Let us delve deep into one of the significant movement disorders, dystonia, to understand it better and catch the signs early. This blog is a comprehensive guide on dystonia, its symptoms and treatment options.
symptoms: Symptoms of dystonia may be either very subtle or extremely severe. Different body parts may be affected by dystonia, and the condition’s symptoms frequently change over time. Some early signs are cramping of the foot, involuntary neck spasm, uncontrollable blinking of the eyes or difficulty speaking.

The symptoms may appear or get worse due to stress or exhaustion. Because the muscles constantly contract, people with dystonia frequently complain of pain and tiredness. Usually, it is during early adulthood that dystonia starts manifesting, and it starts in the upper body. Over time, the symptoms gradually develop. Early-onset adult dystonia is segmental or focal, affecting one specific body part or the nearby parts.
When dystonia symptoms manifest in children, it usually shows up first in the foot or hand, but they soon progress to the rest of the body after that.

diseases.name: Dystrophic Nails - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
