diseases.description: Dystrophic nails are a common yet often overlooked condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Characterized by abnormal nail growth and appearance, dystrophic nails can be a sign of underlying health issues or simply a cosmetic concern. Understanding dystrophic nails is essential for early detection and effective management, as they can indicate more serious health problems. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of dystrophic nails, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Dystrophic nails can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Discoloration: Nails may appear yellow, brown, or white.
Thickening: Nails can become thicker than normal, making them difficult to trim.
Brittleness: Dystrophic nails may be prone to breaking or splitting.
Ridges or Pitting: The surface of the nails may develop ridges or small depressions.
Separation: In severe cases, the nail may separate from the nail bed (onycholysis).

diseases.name: E.coli (Escherichia coli) - Symptoms, Causes Its Transmission and Treatment
diseases.description: Escherichia coli (E.coli) , present in the intestine, may sometimes cause infection. It damages the intestinal lining and causes symptoms such as diarrhea . Pathogenic strains of E. coli are found in both humans and animals. A high percentage of E. coli is found in meat, water, milk and milk products , contaminated water , and seafood .
symptoms: Generally, you may have symptoms within 3 to 4 days after exposure. However, symptoms may also occur 1 to 7 days after the exposure. Following are the symptoms a patient with an E. coli infection experiences:
Pain and tenderness in the stomach
Stomach cramps
Severe, persistent diarrhea
Bloody diarrhea
Constant fatigue

diseases.name: Eagle Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eagle Syndrome is a rare medical condition that arises from an elongated styloid process or calcification of the stylohyoid ligament, leading to various symptoms that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Named after Dr. Watt Eagle, who first described it in 1937, this syndrome is often underdiagnosed due to its nonspecific symptoms, which can mimic other conditions. Understanding Eagle Syndrome is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to chronic pain and discomfort if left untreated.
symptoms: Eagle Syndrome can present a variety of symptoms, which may vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Throat Pain: Often described as a sharp or dull ache, which may worsen with swallowing or turning the head.
Jaw Pain: Discomfort in the jaw, particularly when chewing or opening the mouth wide.
Neck Pain: Pain that may radiate from the throat to the neck and shoulders.
Ear Pain: A sensation of fullness or pain in the ear, which may be mistaken for an ear infection.
Headaches: Frequent headaches, particularly in the temples or back of the head.
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, which can be exacerbated by the elongated styloid process.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears, which may occur due to nerve compression.

diseases.name: Ear Infections - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Acute otitis media is a term that refers to ear infections that occur in the space behind the eardrum. Viruses or bacteria cause ear infections, and the common pathogens are bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. The infection often results from a blockage of your Eustachian tubes, which causes fluid to accumulation in your middle ear. Eustachian tubes are tiny tubes that run from each of your middle ears directly to the back of your throat.
symptoms: The onset of signs and symptoms is usually quick and observable. Those are:
A sharp piercing pain followed by warm drainage from the ear canal
Nausea
Muffled hearing
Ear drainage
A sharp sudden pain
A dull continuous pain
Irritability
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Ear Tumors - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ear tumors are abnormal growths that can develop in various parts of the ear, including the outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear. While some ear tumors are benign (non-cancerous), others can be malignant (cancerous) and pose significant health risks. Understanding ear tumors is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, as they can affect hearing, balance, and overall quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ear tumors, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of ear tumors can vary depending on the type and location of the tumor. Common symptoms include:
Hearing Loss: This is often the first noticeable symptom, as tumors can obstruct sound transmission.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears may occur due to pressure on the auditory nerve.
Ear Pain: Discomfort or pain in the ear can result from tumor growth or associated infections.
Balance Issues: Tumors affecting the inner ear may disrupt balance, leading to dizziness or vertigo.
Fluid Discharge: In some cases, tumors can cause fluid to drain from the ear.

diseases.name: Early Warning Signs Of Ovarian Cancer
diseases.description: Ovaries are the female reproductive glands situated in the lower part of abdomen in both sides of the womb. They produce the ova and are the source of very important hormones (Estrogen and progesterone) in the body. Ovarian cancer is not a single entity. It represents several tumors originating from different parts of Ovary. The most common cancer of ovary (almost 90%), i.e. the epithelial ovarian cancer arises from the covering of the organ. Most of these patients present at advanced stage and after menopause. Most of the patients of epithelial ovarian cancers experience no signs or symptoms of disease at early stage. Abdominal discomfort, bloating and early satiety are the most common symptoms experienced by them at advanced stage. Some patients experience lower abdominal lump and abdominal pain. Ovarian malignancy patients also develop fluid collection within the abdominal cavity resulting in abdominal distension. Occasionally these tumors are diagnosed during routine health check up . Epithelial ovarian cancers can be hereditary (approximately 5-10%) and runs in family due to genetic mutations. Women with family members affected by ovarian cancer, cancer of both breasts or breast cancer at an early age, both ovarian and breast cancer or male breast cancer can be suspected to have such hereditary disease and are at high risk of developing ovarian cancer. In contrast to the epithelial cancers, other tumors like germ cell cancers may cause severe abdominal pain at an early stage and can present with lower abdominal or pelvic lump. Patients experiencing any of the above-mentioned signs and symptoms requires immediate medical attention. Patients with family history of breast and ovarian malignancy can consult physician for necessary tests to detect early malignancy. Diagnosis and treatment at an early stage is associated with better outcome.

diseases.name: Eating Disorders - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eating disorders are complex mental health conditions that can have severe physical and emotional consequences. They are characterized by abnormal eating habits that negatively impact an individual's health, relationships, and daily functioning. The significance of understanding eating disorders lies in their prevalence and the serious health risks they pose. According to the National Eating Disorders Association (NEDA), approximately 30 million Americans will experience an eating disorder in their lifetime. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of eating disorders, including their definitions, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of eating disorders can vary widely depending on the specific type. However, some common symptoms include:
Anorexia Nervosa: Extreme weight loss, fear of gaining weight, distorted body image, and restrictive eating patterns.
Bulimia Nervosa: Binge eating followed by purging (vomiting, excessive exercise, or laxative use), feelings of shame or guilt, and fluctuations in weight.
Binge Eating Disorder: Recurrent episodes of binge eating without compensatory behaviors, feelings of loss of control, and distress regarding eating habits.

diseases.name: Ebola
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms mostly begin unexpectedly within ten days of the virus infection which can include:
Rise in temperature
Severe headache
Joint and muscle pain
Shivers and weakness
Over time, these signs become very severe and may cause:
Vomiting
Diarrhea and blood in the stool
Redness of the eyes
Rashes
Chest pain and cough
Stomach ache
Weight loss
Internal bleeding and bleeding from the eyes

diseases.name: Eclampsia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eclampsia is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition that can occur during pregnancy, characterized by the onset of seizures. It is often preceded by a condition known as preeclampsia, which involves high blood pressure and signs of damage to other organ systems. Eclampsia is significant not only because of its immediate risks to the mother and baby but also due to its potential long-term effects on maternal health. Understanding eclampsia is crucial for expectant mothers, healthcare providers, and families to ensure timely intervention and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of eclampsia can vary, but common signs include:
Seizures: The hallmark symptom of eclampsia, which may present as generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
Severe Headaches: Persistent and severe headaches that do not respond to typical pain relief.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision, seeing spots, or temporary loss of vision.
Abdominal Pain: Severe pain in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Persistent nausea or vomiting that may accompany other symptoms.

diseases.name: Ectopia Cordis: Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Complications
diseases.description: Ectopia Cordis (EC) is a rare genetic defect in which some or all of a baby’s heart is not covered by the breastbone. Instead, the heart lies beneath a layer of skin and appears to be outside the chest. Babies with Ectopia Cordis have a lower chance of survival. However, there are cases where doctors have successfully performed surgeries.
symptoms: Its main feature is the heart being outside the body. Babies with this condition often also suffer other ‘midline defects’(problems along the line going up and down in the centre of the body, from the head to the groin). They include the following:
Cranial cleft (a division in the shape of the baby’s face)
Cleft lip/palate (a split in the upper mouth of the baby)
Scoliosis (abnormal lateral curvature of the spine)
Lungs that are not entirely developed
An abnormal hole in the diaphragm

diseases.name: Ectopia Lentis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ectopia lentis is a medical condition characterized by the displacement of the eye's lens from its normal position. This condition can significantly impact vision and may lead to various complications if not properly managed. Understanding ectopia lentis is crucial for early diagnosis and treatment, which can help preserve vision and improve quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding ectopia lentis.
symptoms: The symptoms of ectopia lentis can vary depending on the degree of lens displacement and whether one or both eyes are affected. Common symptoms include:
Blurry Vision: Displacement of the lens can lead to refractive errors, causing blurred or distorted vision.
Double Vision: Misalignment of the lens may result in diplopia, or double vision.
Light Sensitivity: Individuals may experience increased sensitivity to light, known as photophobia.
Difficulty with Depth Perception: Lens displacement can affect the ability to judge distances accurately.

diseases.name: Ectopic Heartbeat - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ectopic heartbeat, often referred to as ectopic beats or premature contractions, is a common cardiac phenomenon that can cause concern for many individuals. While it is usually benign, understanding its significance is crucial for maintaining heart health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ectopic heartbeat, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Ectopic heartbeats may not always present noticeable symptoms. However, when they do occur, individuals may experience:
Palpitations: A feeling of fluttering or pounding in the chest.
Skipped Beats: A sensation that the heart has missed a beat.
Anxiety: Feelings of unease or panic, often triggered by the awareness of irregular heartbeats.
Dizziness: Lightheadedness or faintness, particularly if the ectopic beats are frequent.

diseases.name: Ectopic Pregnancy - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: When the fertilized egg attaches itself outside the uterus, it is called an ectopic pregnancy. The uterus of a woman, also called the womb, is the fetus’s home before the baby is born. Pregnancy begins when the fertilized egg implants itself in the uterus. For a normal pregnancy, the fertilized egg must attach to the uterine wall.
symptoms: The early symptoms and signs of an ectopic pregnancy may be confused with the signs of a normal pregnancy. Nausea , breast tenderness, and missed periods are the early symptoms of both.

One of the first and early signs of an ectopic pregnancy is pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding . However, these coincide with the normal early symptoms of any pregnancy, and therefore, your doctor will use a step-by-step method to diagnose if your pregnancy is ectopic. The following are the early signs of ectopic pregnancy:
● Pelvic pain as well as light vaginal bleeding
● Urge to have a bowel movement
● Referred pain on the shoulder
Certain symptoms depend on where the blood collects and which nerves are irritated.

If the fertilized egg keeps growing in the fallopian tube, it can lead the tube to rupture. There is a possibility of heavy bleeding inside the abdomen. Symptoms of this life-threatening event include extreme lightheadedness, fainting as well as shock.
If you suffer from any of these symptoms, seek medical help immediately.

diseases.name: Ectopic Ureter - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ectopic ureter is a medical condition that occurs when one or both ureters, the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder, do not connect to the bladder in the usual anatomical position. Instead, they may drain into other structures, such as the vagina, urethra, or even the rectum. This condition is significant because it can lead to various complications, including urinary tract infections, kidney damage, and incontinence. Understanding ectopic ureters is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, especially in pediatric populations where it is more commonly diagnosed.
symptoms: The symptoms of ectopic ureters can vary depending on the location of the ureter's opening and whether one or both ureters are affected. Common symptoms include:
Urinary Incontinence: In children, this may manifest as wetting accidents, especially if the ureter drains into the vagina or urethra.
Frequent Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Due to abnormal urine flow, children may experience recurrent UTIs.
Abdominal Pain: Some children may complain of pain in the lower abdomen or flank.
Poor Growth: In severe cases, kidney function may be compromised, leading to growth issues.

diseases.name: Ectropion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ectropion is a medical condition that affects the eyelids, specifically causing them to turn outward away from the eyeball. This condition can lead to various complications, including dryness, irritation, and exposure of the eye, which can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding ectropion is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can arise from various causes and may affect individuals of all ages.
symptoms: The symptoms of ectropion can vary in severity but commonly include:
Redness and Irritation: The exposed conjunctiva may become inflamed, leading to redness and discomfort.
Dryness: The eye may feel dry due to inadequate tear coverage.
Tearing: Paradoxically, some individuals may experience excessive tearing as the eye attempts to compensate for dryness.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to light (photophobia) may occur due to exposure of the eye.
Crusting or Discharge: Mucous discharge may develop as a result of irritation.

diseases.name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
diseases.description: Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes the skin to become itchy, red, dry, and cracked. It is common in children but can occur at any age. Eczema tends to flare periodically, often in association with environmental triggers. It is frequently found alongside other allergic conditions such as asthma and hay fever.
symptoms: Dry skin
Itching (pruritus), especially at night
Red to brownish-gray patches
Small, raised bumps that may weep fluid when scratched
Thickened, cracked, or scaly skin
Raw, swollen skin from scratching

diseases.name: Eczema On Face - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eczema on the face, also known as facial eczema, is a common skin condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. It manifests as red, inflamed patches on the skin, often accompanied by itching and discomfort. The face is a particularly sensitive area, and the visible nature of this condition can lead to emotional distress and social anxiety. Understanding eczema on the face is crucial for effective management and prevention, allowing individuals to maintain healthy skin and improve their overall well-being.
symptoms: Eczema on the face can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Red, inflamed patches: These can appear on the cheeks, forehead, and around the eyes.
Itching: Intense itching is a hallmark symptom, often leading to scratching and further irritation.
Dry, scaly skin: The affected areas may become dry and flaky, leading to discomfort.
Crusting or oozing: In severe cases, the skin may develop crusts or ooze fluid, indicating a potential infection.

diseases.name: Edema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Edema is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of excess fluid in the body's tissues, leading to swelling. While it may seem like a minor inconvenience, edema can be a sign of underlying health issues and can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding edema is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can arise from various causes, ranging from benign to serious medical conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of edema, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The primary symptom of edema is swelling in the affected areas, which may be accompanied by:
Puffiness: Noticeable swelling in the feet, ankles, legs, hands, or face.
Skin Changes: The skin may appear stretched, shiny, or discolored.
Pain or Discomfort: Swollen areas may feel heavy, tight, or painful.
Limited Mobility: Swelling can restrict movement, particularly in the joints.

diseases.name: Edwards Syndrome - A Rare Genetic Disorder
diseases.description: Edward’s syndrome, named after the doctor who first described it, is a condition which causes extreme developmental delays owing to the presence of an extra chromosome 18 in the DNA. Also known as Trisomy 18, this condition is basically a chromosomal abnormality and quite rare. However, it is an extremely serious genetic condition that leads to a wide range of medical problems. It is the second most common trisomy condition after Trisomy 21 or Down Syndrome. Sadly enough, most babies who are born with Edward’s syndrome die within the first week of life. Very few of the affected babies live beyond that. So, it is very important to learn more about this rare but extremely fatal genetic condition.
symptoms: Babies with Edward’s Syndrome are born with a wide range of physical problems. They have multiple health problems and the physical symptoms include:
Clenched fists, underdeveloped thumbs and long, overlapping fingers which are difficult to straighten.
Cleft palate i.e. an oral malformation and a split in the roof of the mouth.
Feeding troubles
Low-set ears
Defects of the kidneys, stomach, intestines and lungs
Small, abnormally-shaped head (microcephaly)
Less birth weight
Small, abnormal shape of the jaw (micrognathia)
Smooth feet with rounded soles
Extreme developmental delays
Deformed feet also known as rocker-bottom feet as they are shaped like the bottom of a rocking chair
Slowed-down growth
Weak cry
Heart defects
Exomphalos i.e. the intestines are carried in a sac outside the tummy
Breathing problems
Abnormalities in the bone structure i.e. a curved spine
Regular infections of the lungs and the urinary system
Hernias in the stomach wall
Learning disabilities

diseases.name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS)
diseases.description: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) is a group of inherited disorders that affect the connective tissues — primarily the skin, joints, and blood vessel walls. People who have EDS usually have overly flexible joints and stretchy, fragile skin. EDS is caused by defects in collagen production, and there are 13 subtypes with varying severity.
symptoms: Overly flexible joints (hypermobility)
Stretchy skin
Fragile skin that bruises easily
Skin that heals poorly leaving wide scars
Joint pain and dislocations
Fatigue
Chronic musculoskeletal pain

diseases.name: Electrolytes: Definition, Imbalance Symptoms, Causes and Prevention
diseases.description: Electrolytes are chemical substances that possess natural negative or positive electrical charges when dissolved in water. They help the body to regulate chemical reactions, maintain the balance between fluids inside and outside the cells, and more. Electrolytes are also essential to diagnose various diseases and medical conditions in your body.

diseases.name: Embolic Stroke
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: An embolic stroke, just like any other stroke has the same symptoms. These include:
Dizziness
Loss of balance
Trouble walking
Loss of vision in one or both eyes
Sudden numbness in an arm, a leg or face
Difficulty speaking or understanding words
If you have any/some/all of the above symptoms, seek medical attention immediately.

diseases.name: Embolism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Embolism is a critical medical condition that can have severe consequences if not promptly diagnosed and treated. It occurs when a substance, known as an embolus, travels through the bloodstream and lodges in a blood vessel, obstructing blood flow. This blockage can lead to serious complications, including tissue damage and organ failure. Understanding embolism is essential for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of embolism can vary depending on the location of the blockage. Common symptoms include:
Pulmonary Embolism: Shortness of breath, chest pain, rapid heart rate, and coughing up blood.
Cerebral Embolism: Sudden headache, confusion, difficulty speaking, weakness on one side of the body, and loss of coordination.
Peripheral Embolism: Pain, numbness, or coldness in the affected limb, along with changes in skin color.

diseases.name: Embryonal Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Embryonal tumors are a group of fast-growing cancers that arise from very early (embryonic) cells that remain in a child's body after birth. Because these tumors come from cells that were meant to develop into mature tissues, they often appear in infants, young children, and occasionally adolescents. While the term "embryonal" can sound alarming, many of these tumors are highly treatable today with coordinated care, modern chemotherapy, precision surgery, and child-friendly radiation techniques. This article explains what embryonal tumors are, the main subtypes, symptoms, diagnosis, staging, treatment options, prognosis, and prevention tips.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the tumor's location and size. Because children may struggle to describe symptoms, caregivers should watch for persistent or unusual signs.
Common early signs by location:

diseases.name: Emphysema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Emphysema is a chronic lung disease that significantly impacts the quality of life for millions of people worldwide. It is a form of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) characterized by the destruction of the air sacs in the lungs, leading to breathing difficulties. Understanding emphysema is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of emphysema, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Shortness of Breath: Initially occurs during physical activity but may progress to rest during rest.
Chronic Cough: A persistent cough that may produce mucus.
Wheezing: A whistling sound when breathing, especially during exhalation.
Chest Tightness: A feeling of pressure or constriction in the chest.
Fatigue: Increased tiredness due to the effort of breathing.

diseases.name: Empty Sella Syndrome: Types, Symptoms, Causes and Treatments
diseases.description: Empty Sella Syndrome (ESS) is a neurological disorder in which the pituitary gland either gets flattened or shrinks due to the enlargement of the sella turcica. It is a bony structure that surrounds and protects the pituitary gland and is present at the base of the brain. The disorder gets its name because, during imaging tests of the sella turcica, the shell may appear to be empty. Empty Sella Syndrome causes symptoms such as hormonal imbalances, frequent headaches, and vision problems.
symptoms: Often Empty Sella Symptoms do not show any signs or symptoms. Depending on age, symptoms may differ from person to person, and doctors believe only 1% of patients show symptoms. If a patient notices symptoms, they may be as follows:
Impotence in men
Reduced sexual desire
Irregular or no menstrual periods in women
Chronic headaches
High blood pressure
Fatigue
Infertility
Hormonal imbalance
Erectile dysfunction
Galactorrhea – irregular nipple discharge
Some of the lesser-known symptoms include the following:
A feeling of pressure within the skull
A spinal fluid that leaks from the nose
Swelling of eyes
Blurry vision

The function of the pituitary gland in the empty sella syndrome is generally not affected. While it’s often not well seen on imaging, it is perfectly functional otherwise. The pituitary is a small gland situated close to the base of your skull that stores numerious critical hormones and releases these harmones into the bloodstream as required by the body. These hormones regulate various different functions of the body. Although a rarely, some decreased or abnormal pituitary function can happen (hypopituitarism) in the setting of empty sella. A detailed finding in some people with empty sella, like children, has been the isolated growth hormone deficiency.

diseases.name: Empyema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Empyema is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of pus in the pleural space, the area between the lungs and the chest wall. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe respiratory issues and may require immediate medical intervention. Understanding empyema is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of empyema can vary depending on the severity of the condition and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: Often sharp and worsens with deep breathing or coughing.
Cough: A persistent cough that may produce sputum.
Fever and Chills: Indicating an infection.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling breathless, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: General tiredness and weakness.

diseases.name: Enamel Hypoplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Enamel hypoplasia is a dental condition characterized by the underdevelopment of tooth enamel, the hard outer layer that protects teeth from decay and damage. This condition can lead to various dental issues, including increased susceptibility to cavities, sensitivity, and aesthetic concerns. Understanding enamel hypoplasia is crucial for both prevention and management, as it can significantly impact oral health and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of enamel hypoplasia can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Discoloration: Teeth may appear yellow, brown, or white, depending on the degree of enamel loss.
Pitting or Grooves: The surface of the teeth may have visible pits or grooves, making them more susceptible to decay.
Sensitivity: Individuals may experience increased sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods and beverages.
Cavities: Due to weakened enamel, individuals with enamel hypoplasia are at a higher risk of developing cavities.

diseases.name: Encephalitis - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Risks, Complications, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Encephalitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the brain tissue, most often caused by viral infections. While it can start with mild flu-like symptoms, some cases can progress rapidly to more severe issues such as confusion, seizures, difficulty in movement, and changes in personality or consciousness. If left untreated, severe encephalitis can become life-threatening.
symptoms: Encephalitis symptoms can range from mild to severe, and often begin with signs that resemble the flu. The condition can worsen rapidly, especially in children, the elderly, or individuals with weakened immune systems.
Headache
Fever
Fatigue or general weakness
Muscle and joint aches
Seizures
Confusion, delirium, or hallucinations
Agitation or personality changes
Paralysis in parts of the face or body
Muscle weakness or stiffness
Trouble speaking or understanding speech
Hearing difficulties
Double vision or blurred vision
Altered sense of smell (e.g., foul or burnt odor)
Loss of consciousness or coma
Bulging fontanelle (soft spot on the baby’s head)
Persistent or high-pitched crying
Nausea and vomiting
Body stiffness or inflexibility
Irritability or unusual fussiness

diseases.name: Encephalocele - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Encephalocele is a rare but significant neurological condition that affects the brain and skull. It occurs when a portion of the brain protrudes through an opening in the skull, often covered by a thin layer of tissue. This condition can lead to various neurological issues and developmental challenges, making early diagnosis and treatment crucial. Understanding encephalocele is essential for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals to provide the best possible care and support for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of encephalocele can vary widely depending on the size and location of the defect. Common symptoms may include:
Visible Bulge: A noticeable bulge or sac on the head, often covered by skin or a thin membrane.
Neurological Issues: Developmental delays, seizures, or cognitive impairments may occur due to the involvement of brain tissue.
Motor Skill Challenges: Difficulty with coordination and motor skills may be present, depending on the affected brain areas.
Vision and Hearing Problems: Some individuals may experience vision or hearing impairments.

diseases.name: Encephalopathy: Types, Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention
diseases.description: Encephalopathy is a condition usually confused with encephalitis due to the way both sound. But they are different. Encephalitis is a condition where there is brain inflammation. On the other hand, encephalopathy is a mental state resulting from various brain-related issues. But encephalopathy can result from encephalitis . It is vital to be aware of this difference. This blog is a comprehensive guide on encephalopathy, its types, causes and treatment options available.
symptoms: Some common symptoms are:
Confusion
Memory loss
Changes in behaviour
Having trouble focusing or thinking clearly
Some individuals may also have problems like:
difficulty speaking
difficulty swallowing
sleepiness
seizures
muscle weakness or uncontrollable twitches
uncontrollable eye movements
tremors

diseases.name: Enchondroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Enchondroma is a type of benign bone tumor that arises from cartilage. While it is generally non-cancerous, its presence can lead to various complications, including pain and fractures. Understanding enchondromas is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as they can sometimes mimic more serious conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of enchondromas, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Enchondromas often do not present noticeable symptoms, especially in their early stages. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Localized Pain: Pain may be felt in the area of the tumor, particularly during physical activity.
Swelling: There may be noticeable swelling or a lump over the affected bone.
Fractures: Enchondromas can weaken the bone structure, leading to fractures with minimal trauma.

diseases.name: Encopresis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Encopresis is a condition that affects many children and can have significant emotional and social implications. It is characterized by the involuntary passage of stool in inappropriate places, often leading to embarrassment and distress for both the child and their family. Understanding encopresis is crucial for parents, caregivers, and educators, as early recognition and intervention can lead to better outcomes. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of encopresis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Involuntary Stool Passage: The primary symptom is the involuntary release of stool in inappropriate places.
Constipation: Many children with encopresis experience chronic constipation, leading to hard, painful stools.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the abdomen may occur due to stool buildup.
Soiling: Children may have episodes of soiling, which can be intermittent or frequent.
Avoidance Behavior: Children may avoid using the toilet due to fear of pain or embarrassment.

diseases.name: End Stage Renal Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) is a critical health condition characterized by the irreversible loss of kidney function, requiring either dialysis or a kidney transplant for survival. The kidneys play a vital role in filtering waste products from the blood, regulating electrolytes, and maintaining fluid balance. When they fail, the body can accumulate harmful substances, leading to severe health complications. Understanding ESRD is essential not only for those affected but also for their families and caregivers, as it significantly impacts quality of life and requires comprehensive management.
symptoms: As kidney function declines, various symptoms may manifest, including:
Fatigue: A common symptom due to the accumulation of toxins in the body.
Swelling: Fluid retention can cause swelling in the legs, ankles, and around the eyes.
Changes in Urination: This may include decreased urine output or changes in urine color.
Nausea and Vomiting: Accumulation of waste products can lead to gastrointestinal symptoms.
Shortness of Breath: Fluid buildup in the lungs can cause difficulty breathing.
Itching: Accumulation of waste products can lead to skin irritation and itching.
Metallic Taste: A common complaint among those with kidney failure.

diseases.name: Endocardial Cushion Defect - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Endocardial Cushion Defect (ECD) is a congenital heart defect that affects the structure of the heart, specifically the walls that separate the heart's chambers. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated early. Understanding ECD is crucial for parents, caregivers, and individuals who may be affected by this condition, as it can impact overall health and quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Endocardial Cushion Defect can vary widely depending on the severity of the defect. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or when lying down.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy, particularly in infants and children.
Poor Growth: In infants, failure to thrive or gain weight appropriately.
Heart Murmurs: Abnormal sounds during a heartbeat, often detected during a physical examination.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, lips, or nails, indicating low oxygen levels in the blood.

diseases.name: Endocarditis
diseases.description: Endocarditis is termed as inflammation of the inner lining of the heart valves and heart chamber called endocardium. This condition usually occurs when fungi, bacteria or other germs from others parts of your body, such as the mouth, are spread through blood circulation and then attach themselves to the damaged regions in the heart. It can cause life-threatening complications by damaging your heart valves if it is not treated immediately. This condition can be treated by means of antibiotic medications and in some cases, surgery may be required. Since there are numerous ways to develop this condition, your medical practitioner might not be able to identify the exact reason that caused endocarditis . However, individuals at higher risk of endocarditis generally have artificial heart valves, damaged heart valves, mitral valve repair or other heart ailments.
symptoms: Endocarditis may come up suddenly or slowly, based on the type of germs that are causing the infection, and depending on whether if you have any cardiac ailments. Endocarditis symptoms can differ from one person to another.
Fatigue
A changed or new heart murmur, which is the heart sound made by blood passing through the heart
Swelling in the legs, abdomen or feet
Night sweats
Bacterial endocarditis
Aching muscles and joints
Abnormal heartbeat
Shortness of breath
Flu-like symptoms like chills and fever
Chest pain when you breathe
Unexplained weight loss.
Softness in your spleen, which is an abdominal organ present on the left side of your body just under your rib cage that is key to immunity.
Blood in urine, which you will be able to see or your doctor may find out when he/she analyses urine using a microscope.
Jane way lesions, which are red spots on the palms of your hands or on soles of your feet.
Osler’s nodes, which are red, tender spots under the skin of your toes or fingers.
Petechial, which are red spots or tiny purple on the whites of your eyes, on the skin or inside your mouth?

diseases.name: Endolphthalmitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Endophthalmitis is a serious eye condition that can lead to vision loss and even blindness if not treated promptly. It is characterized by inflammation of the interior of the eye, typically caused by infection. Understanding endophthalmitis is crucial for anyone who has undergone eye surgery, has a history of eye infections, or is at risk due to other health conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of endophthalmitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of endophthalmitis can vary but often include:
Eye Pain: A sudden onset of severe eye pain is a common symptom.
Redness: The eye may appear red and inflamed.
Vision Changes: Blurred vision, decreased vision, or complete vision loss can occur.
Floaters: Patients may notice an increase in floaters or spots in their vision.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, may be present.

diseases.name: Endometrial Cancer
diseases.description: Endometrial cancer originates in the uterus. The uterus is the concave, pear-shaped pelvic organ in women where fetal growth happens.
symptoms: Signs of endometrial cancer may consist of:
Vaginal bleeding past menopause
Unusual bleeding between periods
An unusual, dilute or blood-tinged discharge from vagina
Pain in the pelvic area
Pain during sex

diseases.name: Endometrial Polyp
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Signs of endometrial polyps consist of:
Irregular period bleeding
Bleeding between the menstrual periods
Extreme heavy menstrual periods
Vaginal bleeding post menopause
Infertility

diseases.name: Endometriosis Diet: Foods to Eat and Avoid
diseases.description: Endometriosis occurs when tissue that lines the woman’s uterus grows outside of the uterus. Read the blog to know about endometriosis diet.
symptoms: The main symptom of endometriosis is pelvic pain , often accompanied by periods . Although many women may experience cramping during their periods, but those with endometriosis describe menstrual pain as being far worse than usual. Pain also may increase over time.
Common signs and symptoms of it include:
Painful periods or dysmenorrhea- Pelvic pain and cramping may start before and extend several days into a period. You might also get lower back and abdominal pain.
Pain with intercourse – Pain during or post sex is common with endometriosis.
Pain with bowel movements or urination -you’re most likely to observe these symptoms during a menstrual period.
Excessive bleeding – you may experience occasional heavy menstrual periods or bleeding between periods, which is also called intermenstrual bleeding.
Infertility – sometimes, endometriosis is first diagnosed in those seeking treatment for infertility .
Other symptoms that you might experience are fatigue , diarrhea , constipation , bloating or nausea , especially during menstrual periods

The severity of your pain might not be a reliable indicator of the extent of your condition. You might have mild endometriosis with acute pain, or you might have advanced endometriosis with little or no pain at all.

Sometimes, endometriosis is mistaken for other illnesses that may cause pelvic pain like ovarian cysts or pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) . It could be confused with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) , a condition that causes bouts of constipation, diarrhoea and abdominal cramping. IBS might accompany endometriosis, which may complicate the diagnosis.

diseases.name: Endometriosis: Causes, Symptoms, Types, Treatment & Risk Factors
diseases.description: Endometriosis is a painful disorder in which the endometrium, a tissue similar to the one that normally lines the inside of the uterus, grows outside the uterus. Endometriosis normally involves the ovaries, Fallopian tubes and the tissue lining the pelvis.
symptoms: Women with endometriosis suffer from pelvic pain as the primary symptom. This is often associated with menstrual periods. However, many women experience cramping during their periods, those with endometriosis suffer from far worse pain than usual. Pain may also increase over time. The common signs and symptoms include:

Painful periods (dysmenorrhea): The pelvic pain and cramping may start before or extend after several days into a menstrual period. There is a possibility that you may also have lower back and abdominal pain.
Pain during sex: This is common for women with endometriosis. It causes pain during or after sex.
Pain with bowel movements or urination: This symptom is mostly likely to occur during a menstrual period.
Excessive bleeding: You may experience occasional heavy menstrual periods or bleeding between periods (intermenstrual bleeding).
Infertility : Sometimes, it is first diagnosed in those seeking treatment for infertility.

You may also experience fatigue, diarrhea , constipation , bloating or nausea , especially during menstrual periods.The severity of the pain may not be an indicator of the extent of the condition. Sometimes, you might have mild endometriosis with severe pain or you could have severe endometriosis with little or no pain.

This condition is sometimes mistaken for other conditions that cause pelvic pain such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), ovarian cysts , and could be confused with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – a condition that causes bouts of diarrhea, constipation, and abdominal cramping. If you are suffering from endometriosis, you can also have IBS which complicates the diagnosis.

diseases.name: Endometritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Endometritis is a medical condition that affects the inner lining of the uterus, known as the endometrium. This inflammation can lead to a range of symptoms and complications, making it a significant health concern for women. Understanding endometritis is crucial not only for those who may experience it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of endometritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of endometritis can vary depending on whether the condition is acute or chronic. Common symptoms include:
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen.
Abnormal Vaginal Discharge: This may be foul-smelling or discolored.
Fever: A low-grade fever may accompany the condition.
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Some women may experience heavier than normal periods.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness or malaise.

diseases.name: Endothelial Dysfunction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Endothelial dysfunction is a critical condition that affects the inner lining of blood vessels, known as the endothelium. This dysfunction can lead to a range of cardiovascular diseases and other health issues, making it a significant concern in modern medicine. Understanding endothelial dysfunction is essential for recognizing its implications on overall health and well-being. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of endothelial dysfunction, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: Endothelial dysfunction may not present with obvious symptoms initially, but as it progresses, individuals may experience:
Chest Pain: Often a sign of reduced blood flow to the heart.
Shortness of Breath: Can occur during physical activity due to impaired blood circulation.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue may arise from reduced oxygen delivery to tissues.
Swelling: Edema in the legs or feet can indicate vascular issues.

diseases.name: Enlarged Heart- Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: An enlarged heart (cardiomegaly) is a symptom of another underlying disorder rather than a disease in itself. It can be caused by certain factors, such as pregnancy, or by a medical condition, such as heart muscle weakening, coronary artery disease, heart valve abnormalities, or irregular heart rhythms.
symptoms: For some people, an enlarged heart causes no signs or symptoms. The initial symptoms indicating the presence of cardiomegaly are listed below:
Breathing difficulties
Abnormal heart rhythm ( arrhythmia )
Fluid retention ( edema )

diseases.name: Enophthalmos - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Enophthalmos is a medical condition characterized by the posterior displacement of the eyeball within the orbit, leading to a sunken appearance of the eye. This condition can have significant implications for an individual's vision, appearance, and overall health. Understanding enophthalmos is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can be a symptom of underlying health issues that require attention.
symptoms: The primary symptom of enophthalmos is the noticeable sunken appearance of one or both eyes. Other associated symptoms may include:
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or double vision may occur, depending on the underlying cause.
Eye Discomfort: Patients may experience discomfort or a sensation of pressure in the eye.
Changes in Eye Movement: Limited eye movement may be observed in some cases.

diseases.name: Enterocolitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Enterocolitis is a medical condition that affects the intestines, specifically the small intestine and the colon (large intestine). It is characterized by inflammation of these areas, which can lead to a range of gastrointestinal symptoms and complications. Understanding enterocolitis is crucial, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life and may lead to severe health issues if not properly managed. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of enterocolitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of enterocolitis can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Diarrhea: Frequent, watery stools are a hallmark symptom.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or sharp pain in the abdomen may occur.
Fever: A low-grade fever may accompany the inflammation.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur, especially in cases of infectious enterocolitis.
Bloating and Gas: Increased gas production and a feeling of fullness may be present.

diseases.name: Entropion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Entropion is a medical condition that affects the eyelids, specifically causing them to turn inward. This inward folding can lead to significant discomfort and complications, as the eyelashes and skin rub against the surface of the eye. Understanding entropion is crucial not only for those who may be affected but also for caregivers and healthcare providers. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of entropion, providing a thorough overview of this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of entropion can vary in severity but typically include:
Irritation: A constant feeling of discomfort or irritation in the eye.
Redness: The eye may appear red and inflamed due to the constant rubbing of the eyelashes against the cornea.
Tearing: Increased tear production as the eye attempts to wash away irritants.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, may occur.
Vision Changes: In severe cases, vision may be affected due to corneal damage.

diseases.name: Eosinophilia: Definition, Causes, Symptoms, Treatment & Prevention
diseases.description: Eosinophils are white blood cells that destroy allergens or foreign substances such as parasites and aid the immune system in starting an allergic reaction. When there is a rise in eosinophils, it is called eosinophilia. Some medical conditions and medicines cause high eosinophil levels.
symptoms: The reason behind the elevated eosinophil count will determine the symptoms associated with eosinophilia. If the eosinophils count is mildly high, you may not experience any symptoms. However, the common symptoms include –
Itching
Asthma
Rash
Diarrhea in case of parasite infection
Runny nose for those with allergic problems

diseases.name: Eosinophilic Fasciitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eosinophilic Fasciitis (EF) is a rare autoimmune condition characterized by inflammation and thickening of the skin and underlying tissues, particularly the fascia, which is the connective tissue surrounding muscles, nerves, and blood vessels. This condition is significant not only due to its physical manifestations but also because it can lead to considerable discomfort and disability if left untreated. Understanding EF is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Eosinophilic Fasciitis presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: Often localized to the arms and legs, swelling may be accompanied by a feeling of tightness.
Skin Changes: The skin may appear thickened, hardened, or have a "peau d'orange" (orange peel) texture.
Pain and Discomfort: Patients may experience pain in the affected areas, which can limit mobility.
Fatigue: General fatigue and malaise are common, as the body is in a state of inflammation.

diseases.name: Eosinophilic Gastritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eosinophilic Gastritis (EG) is a rare but significant gastrointestinal disorder characterized by the infiltration of eosinophils, a type of white blood cell, into the stomach lining. This condition can lead to inflammation, discomfort, and various gastrointestinal symptoms. Understanding eosinophilic gastritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. In this comprehensive article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding eosinophilic gastritis.
symptoms: Eosinophilic gastritis can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or sharp pain in the stomach area is a frequent complaint.
Nausea and Vomiting: Many individuals experience persistent nausea, which may lead to vomiting.
Diarrhea: Some patients may have diarrhea, which can be chronic in nature.
Loss of Appetite: Due to discomfort and nausea, individuals may find it challenging to eat.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can occur due to reduced food intake and malabsorption.

diseases.name: Epidermoid Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epidermoid cysts are common skin growths that can occur anywhere on the body. While they are generally harmless, understanding their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for anyone who may encounter them. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of epidermoid cysts, their significance, and how to manage them effectively.
symptoms: Epidermoid cysts are usually painless and may not cause any symptoms. However, they can present with the following characteristics:
A small, round lump beneath the skin
A visible opening or punctum on the skin surface
A soft, movable texture
Possible redness or swelling if the cyst becomes inflamed

diseases.name: Epidermolysis Bullosa - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) is a rare genetic skin disorder characterized by extreme fragility of the skin and mucous membranes. This condition leads to blister formation in response to minor friction or trauma, making everyday activities challenging for those affected. Understanding EB is crucial not only for patients and their families but also for healthcare providers, as it can significantly impact the quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Epidermolysis Bullosa, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Epidermolysis Bullosa can vary widely depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Blisters : The hallmark of EB, blisters can form on the skin and mucous membranes, often in response to minor trauma.
Skin Fragility : The skin is extremely sensitive and can tear easily.
Scarring : Repeated blistering can lead to scarring and changes in skin texture.
Nail Abnormalities : Some individuals may experience nail loss or deformities.
Oral and Esophageal Issues : Blisters can also form in the mouth and esophagus, leading to difficulty eating and swallowing.

diseases.name: Epididymitis Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Epididymitis is the inflammation of the epididymis – a tube which is located at the back of testicle that carries and stores sperm. Epididymitis can affect males at any age and is usually caused by a bacterial infection.
symptoms: The following symptoms indicate a condition of acute epididymitis :
Swollen, red or warm scrotum
Painful testicle . This is usually on one side, such as a painful left testicle , and usually occurs gradually
Discharge from the penis
Painful urination or bowel movements or a frequent or urgent or need to urinate
Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen or pelvic area
Semen showing traces of blood
Mild recurring fever
Cold or shivering
Enlargement of lymph nodes in the groin region In some rare cases, you might need surgery to drain any abscesses that have formed.

diseases.name: Epidural Hematoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epidural hematoma (EDH) is a serious medical condition characterized by the accumulation of blood between the outer membrane of the brain (the dura mater) and the skull. This condition is often the result of a traumatic head injury and can lead to significant neurological impairment or even death if not promptly diagnosed and treated. Understanding epidural hematoma is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, as timely intervention can greatly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of an epidural hematoma can vary depending on the size of the hematoma and the speed at which it develops. Common symptoms include:
Headache: Often severe and sudden in onset.
Nausea and Vomiting: May occur as pressure increases in the skull.
Confusion or Altered Consciousness: Patients may experience confusion, drowsiness, or loss of consciousness.
Pupil Changes: One pupil may become larger than the other (anisocoria).
Weakness or Numbness: This may occur on one side of the body.

diseases.name: Epiglottitis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms of epiglottitis may be different in children and adults. However, the most common and obvious symptoms are:
Severe sore throat
Drooling
Fever
Restless behaviour
Discomfort lying down
Difficulty in swallowing
High-pitched sound while inhaling

diseases.name: Epilepsy - Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: Epilepsy is a neurological (central nervous system) disorder. In this, the cluster of nerve cells present in the brain gives abnormal signals, and the normal pattern of neuronal activity is affected. The brain activity becomes abnormal, causing periods of unusual behavior or seizures, muscle spasms, and sometimes, loss of awareness and sensations. A spectrum of brain disorders can cause epilepsies and seizures . They may be life-threatening sometimes. If you have a single seizure, it does not mean that you have epilepsy . Epilepsy requires at least two unprovoked seizures. During an episode, some people may manifest twitching of arms and legs while some may have a blank stare. It affects both females and males of all races and ages. Most people with seizures lead a normal, healthy life. In the epileptic patients, the two life-threatening conditions are status epilepticus and even sudden death (unexplained). In status epilepticus, the patients may have a prolonged seizure or they main not regain consciousness for a prolonged period after a seizure. Epilepsy can be caused by an abnormality in the brain development or from a severe illness that may cause brain damage. Some disorders that may cause brain damage leading to epilepsy could be Alzheimer ‘s disease, head injury, pre-natal injuries and poisoning. Other causes that may trigger seizures are hormonal changes (during menstrual cycle or pregnancy), lack of good sleep, stress and alcohol consumption. Seizures are divided into two major categories. They are focal and generalized seizures. In a majority of the people who have epilepsy, dietary changes, medical management or occasionally surgical intervention is required. Some patients may need life-long treatment.
symptoms: Involuntary movements (jerking) of the arms and legs (uncontrollable)
Loss of awareness of surroundings or consciousness
A blank staring spell
Temporary loss of memory or confusion
Other psychic symptoms such as fear, déjà vu (feeling that the current situation has already happened sometime in the past) or anxiety .

diseases.name: Epilepsy In Children - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, which are sudden bursts of electrical activity in the brain. In children, epilepsy can significantly impact their development, education, and overall quality of life. Understanding epilepsy in children is crucial for parents, caregivers, and educators, as it allows for better management and support for affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of epilepsy in children, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of epilepsy can vary widely depending on the type of seizure. Common symptoms include:
Convulsions: Uncontrollable shaking or jerking movements.
Loss of Consciousness: A child may appear unresponsive or confused during a seizure.
Staring Spells: Brief episodes of staring into space, often mistaken for daydreaming.
Unusual Sensations: Some children may experience strange feelings, such as tingling or visual disturbances.

diseases.name: Epiploic Appendagitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epiploic appendagitis is a relatively uncommon condition that can cause significant abdominal pain and discomfort. While it may not be as widely recognized as other gastrointestinal disorders, understanding its implications is crucial for timely diagnosis and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of epiploic appendagitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. By the end, readers will have a clearer understanding of this condition and its management.
symptoms: The symptoms of epiploic appendagitis can vary, but the most common include:
Localized Abdominal Pain: Typically, the pain is sharp and located in the lower abdomen, often on the left side.
Tenderness: The affected area may be tender to the touch.
Nausea: Some individuals may experience nausea, although vomiting is less common.
Fever: A mild fever may occur in some cases.

diseases.name: Episcleritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Episcleritis is a relatively common, yet often overlooked, eye condition that affects the episclera, the thin layer of tissue that lies between the sclera (the white part of the eye) and the conjunctiva (the clear membrane covering the front of the eye). While it is generally considered a benign condition, understanding its significance is crucial for timely diagnosis and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of episcleritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more, to help individuals recognize and address this condition effectively.
symptoms: The symptoms of episcleritis can vary in severity and may include:
Redness: A prominent sign of episcleritis is localized redness in the eye, often described as a "bloodshot" appearance.
Discomfort: Patients may experience mild discomfort or a sensation of grittiness in the affected eye.
Tearing: Increased tear production may occur, leading to watery eyes.
Sensitivity to Light: Some individuals may experience photophobia, or sensitivity to light.

diseases.name: Epispadias - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epispadias is a rare congenital condition that affects the urinary system, specifically the urethra. It is characterized by an abnormal opening of the urethra on the upper side of the penis in males or the clitoris in females. This condition can lead to various complications, including urinary incontinence and difficulties with sexual function. Understanding epispadias is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of epispadias can vary based on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Abnormal Urethral Opening: The most noticeable symptom is the abnormal location of the urethral opening.
Urinary Incontinence: Individuals may experience difficulty controlling urination, leading to involuntary leakage.
Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Increased susceptibility to UTIs due to abnormal urinary tract anatomy.
Sexual Dysfunction: In males, epispadias can affect sexual function and fertility.

diseases.name: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is a rare vascular tumor that arises from endothelial cells, which line blood vessels. This tumor is characterized by its unique histological features and can occur in various organs, including the liver, lungs, and soft tissues. Understanding EHE is crucial not only for medical professionals but also for patients and their families, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly impact outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prognosis.
symptoms: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma can present with a variety of symptoms, depending on the location and extent of the tumor. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Patients may experience localized pain in the area where the tumor is located.
Swelling: Tumors can cause swelling or a palpable mass in soft tissues or organs.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue and weakness may occur, particularly in advanced cases.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can be a symptom of EHE.
Respiratory Issues: If the tumor affects the lungs, patients may experience cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain.

diseases.name: Epstein Barr Virus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) is a member of the herpesvirus family and is one of the most common viruses affecting humans worldwide. It is best known for causing infectious mononucleosis, often referred to as "mono," but its implications extend far beyond this single condition. EBV is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its association with various other diseases, including certain cancers and autoimmune disorders. Understanding EBV is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, managing its effects, and preventing its complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of EBV infection can vary widely, ranging from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Fever: A mild to moderate fever is often present.
Sore Throat: A severe sore throat, often resembling strep throat.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Particularly in the neck and armpits.
Headache: Generalized headaches can occur.
Muscle Aches: Generalized body aches and discomfort.
Rash: Some individuals may develop a rash, particularly if treated with certain antibiotics.

diseases.name: Epstein Pearls - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Epstein Pearls are small, harmless cysts that can appear in the mouths of newborns. While they are often a source of concern for new parents, understanding what Epstein Pearls are and their significance can help alleviate anxiety. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of Epstein Pearls, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Epstein Pearls are typically asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause any pain or discomfort. The most common symptoms include:
Small, white or yellowish cysts on the gums or palate.
The presence of multiple cysts, often in clusters.

diseases.name: Erbs Palsy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erb's Palsy, also known as Erb-Duchenne Palsy, is a condition that affects the arm's movement and function due to injury to the brachial plexus, a network of nerves that control the muscles of the shoulder, arm, and hand. This condition is significant not only because it can lead to long-term disability but also because it often arises during childbirth, making awareness and understanding crucial for parents and healthcare providers alike. In this article, we will explore Erb's Palsy in detail, covering its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Erb's Palsy can vary in severity but typically include:
Weakness in the Arm: The affected arm may appear limp or weak, making it difficult for the child to lift or move it.
Limited Range of Motion: The child may have difficulty moving their arm, particularly in raising it or rotating it outward.
Loss of Muscle Control: The child may struggle with fine motor skills, such as grasping objects.
Asymmetrical Posture: The affected arm may hang lower than the other arm, leading to an asymmetrical appearance.

diseases.name: Erdheim Chester Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erdheim Chester Disease (ECD) is a rare and complex condition that falls under the category of non-Langerhans cell histiocytoses. It is characterized by the abnormal proliferation of histiocytes, a type of immune cell, which can lead to a variety of symptoms and complications. Understanding ECD is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the disease but also for healthcare providers and researchers working to improve treatment options and patient outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Erdheim Chester Disease, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Erdheim Chester Disease can present with a wide range of symptoms, which may vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Bone Pain: Often the first symptom, bone pain can be severe and may affect multiple bones.
Skin Lesions: Patients may develop yellowish-brown patches or nodules on the skin.
Cardiac Symptoms: ECD can lead to heart complications, including pericardial effusion (fluid around the heart) and heart failure.
Respiratory Issues: Patients may experience shortness of breath or cough due to lung involvement.
Neurological Symptoms: Headaches, dizziness, or other neurological issues may arise if the central nervous system is affected.
Fatigue and Weight Loss: General malaise, fatigue, and unintended weight loss are common.

diseases.name: Erectile Dysfunction
diseases.description: Erectile dysfunction, more commonly known as impotence, can be defined as an inability to get and keep an erection firm enough for sex. If an erectile dysfunction takes place once in a while, there is no cause for concern. However, if erectile dysfunction is recurring issue, it can not only cause stress but have an adverse effect on the marital relationship as well as the man’s self-esteem.
symptoms: Most common signs and symptoms for erectile dysfunction include:
The inability to get an erection
The inability to keep an erection
Reduced sexual desire
There may also be other sexual problems such as:
Delayed or premature ejaculation
Condition related to erectile dysfunction such as heart disease or diabetes
Hence, seeking medical help is always advised.

diseases.name: Erythema Multiforme - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythema Multiforme (EM) is a skin condition characterized by the sudden appearance of red patches or spots on the skin, often resembling targets or "bull's-eyes." While it can be alarming to see these symptoms, understanding EM is crucial for effective management and treatment. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Erythema Multiforme, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more, to help patients and caregivers navigate this condition.
symptoms: Erythema Multiforme presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Skin Lesions: The hallmark of EM is the appearance of red, raised patches or spots on the skin, often with a target-like appearance.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many individuals report discomfort associated with the lesions.
Mucosal Involvement: In cases of Erythema Multiforme Major, lesions may also appear on mucosal surfaces, such as the mouth, eyes, and genital area.
Fever and Malaise: Some patients may experience systemic symptoms like fever, fatigue, and general malaise.

diseases.name: Erythema Nodosum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythema Nodosum (EN) is a skin condition characterized by the appearance of painful, red nodules, typically located on the lower legs. While it may seem like a minor issue, EN can be a significant indicator of underlying health problems. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective management and treatment. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Erythema Nodosum.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Erythema Nodosum is the appearance of painful, red nodules on the skin, particularly on the lower legs. These nodules can vary in size and may be accompanied by other symptoms, including:
Fever: A mild fever may accompany the skin lesions.
Joint Pain: Some individuals may experience arthralgia or joint pain.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness or malaise can occur.
Swelling: The affected areas may become swollen and tender.

diseases.name: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum (ETN) is a common skin condition that affects newborns, particularly during the first few days of life. While it may appear alarming to new parents, ETN is generally harmless and resolves on its own without treatment. Understanding this condition is crucial for parents and caregivers, as it helps to alleviate concerns and ensures that appropriate care is provided. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum.
symptoms: The symptoms of Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum typically include:
Red Patches: The rash often appears as red, blotchy areas on the skin.
Fluid-Filled Blisters: Small, raised bumps or blisters may develop, often filled with a clear or yellowish fluid.
Location: The rash is most commonly found on the face, trunk, and extremities, but it can appear anywhere on the body.
No Itching or Discomfort: Unlike other skin conditions, ETN usually does not cause itching or discomfort for the infant.

diseases.name: Erythroblastosis Fetalis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythroblastosis Fetalis (EF) is a serious medical condition that affects fetuses and newborns, primarily due to blood type incompatibility between the mother and the baby. This condition can lead to severe anemia, jaundice, and even heart failure in the fetus or newborn. Understanding erythroblastosis fetalis is crucial for expectant parents and healthcare providers, as early detection and management can significantly improve outcomes for affected infants.
symptoms: Erythroblastosis fetalis can present with various symptoms, including:
Anemia: The fetus may show signs of severe anemia, which can lead to fatigue and weakness.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to high bilirubin levels is common in affected newborns.
Swelling: Edema or swelling in the fetus can occur, particularly in the abdomen and extremities.
Heart Failure: In severe cases, the fetus may develop heart failure due to the strain of anemia.

diseases.name: Erythrocytosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythrocytosis is a medical condition characterized by an increased number of red blood cells (RBCs) in the bloodstream. This elevation in red blood cell count can lead to various health complications, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options. Erythrocytosis can be a primary condition or secondary to other underlying health issues, and recognizing its significance is crucial for effective management and prevention of potential complications.
symptoms: Erythrocytosis may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Headaches: Increased blood viscosity can lead to headaches.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Reduced blood flow to the brain can cause these sensations.
Fatigue: An increased workload on the heart and circulatory system can lead to fatigue.
Blurred Vision: Changes in blood flow can affect vision.
Red or Purple Skin: A ruddy complexion may be observed due to increased red blood cell count.

diseases.name: Erythrodermic Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythrodermic psoriasis is a severe and rare form of psoriasis that can cover the entire body with a red, peeling rash that can itch or burn intensely.
