This condition is significant not only because of its physical symptoms but also due to its potential complications, which can be life-threatening. Understanding erythrodermic psoriasis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can drastically affect a person's quality of life.
symptoms: Erythrodermic psoriasis presents with a variety of symptoms, including:
Red, inflamed skin: The skin appears bright red and can cover large areas of the body.
Severe itching or burning: Patients often experience intense discomfort.
Peeling skin: The skin may shed in large sheets, leading to further irritation.
Swelling: Inflammation can cause swelling in affected areas.
Nail changes: Some individuals may notice changes in their nails, such as pitting or separation from the nail bed.

diseases.name: Erythroplakia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Erythroplakia is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it represents a significant health concern, particularly in the realm of oral health. This condition is characterized by the presence of red patches in the oral cavity that cannot be attributed to any other identifiable cause. While erythroplakia itself is not a diagnosis of cancer, it is considered a precancerous condition, which means that it has the potential to develop into oral cancer if left untreated. Understanding erythroplakia is crucial for early detection and intervention, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Erythroplakia is often asymptomatic, which means that many individuals may not experience any noticeable symptoms. However, some may report:
Red patches in the mouth that may be smooth or velvety.
Changes in the texture of the oral mucosa.
Difficulty swallowing or chewing if the lesions are extensive.

diseases.name: Esophageal Atresia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esophageal atresia (EA) is a congenital condition that affects the esophagus, the tube that connects the throat to the stomach. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding esophageal atresia is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of esophageal atresia typically present shortly after birth and may include:
Difficulty Feeding: Infants may struggle to swallow and may choke or gag during feeding.
Coughing or Choking: Babies may cough or choke when attempting to feed, which can lead to aspiration.
Excessive Salivation: Increased drooling or saliva production is common due to the inability to swallow.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially around the lips and face, may occur during feeding or crying, indicating a lack of oxygen.
Respiratory Distress: Difficulty breathing or rapid breathing may be observed, particularly if aspiration occurs.

diseases.name: Esophageal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Esophageal cancer is a type of cancer that begins in the esophagus — the long, hollow tube that carries food and liquids from your throat to your stomach. Although it is less common than cancers of the breast, lung, or colon, esophageal cancer is considered serious because it often goes undetected until it reaches advanced stages. According to the American Cancer Society, about 22,000 new cases are diagnosed in the United States each year, and it is more common in men than in women.
symptoms: Early esophageal cancer often causes no symptoms. As the tumor grows, it can narrow the esophagus and interfere with swallowing.
Painful swallowing
Hoarseness or chronic cough
Vomiting blood or passing black stools (signs of bleeding)
Feeling of food stuck in the throat or chest
Fatigue and weakness due to poor nutrition
Anyone experiencing persistent swallowing problems or unexplained weight loss should seek medical attention promptly.

diseases.name: Esophageal Diverticulum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esophageal diverticulum is a medical condition characterized by the formation of pouches or sacs in the esophagus, the muscular tube that connects the throat to the stomach. These pouches can develop at various points along the esophagus and may lead to a range of symptoms, including difficulty swallowing, regurgitation, and chest pain. Understanding esophageal diverticulum is crucial, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life and may lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of esophageal diverticulum, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of esophageal diverticulum can vary widely depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, which may lead to choking or a sensation of food getting stuck.
Regurgitation: The backflow of food or liquid into the throat or mouth, often accompanied by a foul taste or odor.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may mimic heart-related issues.
Coughing or Aspiration: Coughing during or after eating, which may indicate aspiration of food into the lungs.
Halitosis: Bad breath due to food stagnation in the diverticulum.

diseases.name: Esophageal Rupture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esophageal rupture is a serious medical condition that occurs when there is a tear in the esophagus, the tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach. This rupture can lead to severe complications, including infection, sepsis, and even death if not treated promptly. Understanding esophageal rupture is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of esophageal rupture, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of esophageal rupture can vary depending on the severity of the tear and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Severe Chest Pain: Often described as sharp or stabbing, this pain may worsen with swallowing or movement.
Difficulty Swallowing: Patients may experience dysphagia, or difficulty swallowing, due to the rupture.
Fever and Chills: These symptoms may indicate an infection resulting from the rupture.
Nausea and Vomiting: Patients may feel nauseated and may vomit, sometimes with blood.
Shortness of Breath: If the rupture leads to complications such as pneumothorax (air in the chest cavity), patients may experience difficulty breathing.

diseases.name: Esophageal Strictures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esophageal strictures are a significant medical condition that can affect an individual's ability to swallow and digest food properly. This narrowing of the esophagus can lead to various complications, impacting quality of life and overall health. Understanding esophageal strictures, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is crucial for anyone who may be affected by this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of esophageal strictures, making the information accessible and easy to understand for a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of esophageal strictures can vary in severity and may include:
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing is the most common symptom, which may start with solid foods and progress to liquids.
Pain: Patients may experience pain or discomfort in the chest or throat while swallowing.
Regurgitation: Some individuals may experience regurgitation of food or liquids, which can lead to aspiration and further complications.
Weight Loss: Due to difficulty eating, individuals may unintentionally lose weight.
Coughing or Choking: Some may experience coughing or choking episodes while eating or drinking.

diseases.name: Esophageal varices
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The usual symptoms don’t kick in till there are signs of bleeding which include:
Bleeding, in the form of vomiting blood
Tarry black or blood in the stools
Shock, in extreme cases
If a person already has liver disease, chances of varices are high if the patient displays the following which are indicative of cirrhosis.
Jaundice of the skin and the eyes
Spider nevi or formation of clusters of tiny blood vessels under the skin resembling a spider
Palmar erythema or reddening of the skin on the palm of hands
Dupuytren’s contracture which is a hand deformity
Shrunken testicles
Swollen spleen
Ascites or fluid build-up in the abdomen

diseases.name: Esophagitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esophagitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the esophagus, the tube that connects the throat to the stomach. This inflammation can lead to a variety of symptoms, including pain and difficulty swallowing, and can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding esophagitis is crucial, as it can arise from various causes and may lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of esophagitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of esophagitis can vary depending on the underlying cause but commonly include:
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, which may feel like food is stuck in the throat or chest.
Odynophagia: Painful swallowing, often described as a sharp or burning sensation.
Heartburn: A burning sensation in the chest, often related to acid reflux.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest that may mimic heart-related issues.
Nausea and Vomiting: Some individuals may experience nausea or vomiting, particularly if food intake is affected.

diseases.name: Esotropia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Esotropia is a common type of strabismus, or misalignment of the eyes, where one or both eyes turn inward. This condition can significantly impact an individual's vision and quality of life, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options. Early detection and intervention can lead to better outcomes, making awareness of esotropia crucial for parents, caregivers, and individuals alike.
symptoms: Inward Turning of the Eye: The most noticeable symptom is the inward turning of one or both eyes.
Double Vision: Individuals may experience diplopia, where they see two images of a single object.
Difficulty with Depth Perception: Misalignment can affect the ability to judge distances accurately.
Squinting or Closing One Eye: To compensate for misalignment, individuals may squint or close one eye, especially in bright light.
Head Tilting: Some may tilt their heads to align their vision better.

diseases.name: Essential Tremor: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Essential tremor is a neurological condition that causes uncontrollable, unintentional, and rhythmic shaking of body parts. The tremors usually occur in the hands, legs, arms, head, tongue, and chin. Although the disorder is not life-threatening, it can be challenging to perform simple, daily tasks, such as tying shoelaces, writing, or drinking a cup of water.
symptoms: Patients suffering from essential tremors may experience minor, quick, rapid movements at different intervals, frequencies, and circumstances. The disorder may or may not affect both sides of the body equally.

Sometimes, patients experience tremors when performing a task like extending their hand. These are called action tremors. The other type of tremor is called tremors at rest. It happens when the person is resting. The tremors can range from minor to severe. The following are some of the common symptoms of essential tremors:
The first sign of essential tremor is noticed in the hands
Tremors can make the head and neck involuntarily move in different directions, such as up-and-down or side-to-side motion.
Certain parts of the face may appear to twitch , such as the eyelids
Sometimes, the tremors in the tongue or voice box can give a shaky voice when the person speaks
Problems in the gait and balance due to tremors in the legs and feet
Tremors that worsen as the person ages
Performing everyday tasks becomes difficult
The following are certain factors that briefly worsen the tremors:
Emotional stress
Fatigue
Hunger
Change in temperature
Caffeinated or alcoholic beverages
Cigarettes

diseases.name: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction (ETD) is a common yet often overlooked condition that affects many individuals at some point in their lives. The Eustachian tube is a small passage that connects the middle ear to the back of the throat, playing a crucial role in equalizing ear pressure and draining fluid from the middle ear. When this tube does not function properly, it can lead to discomfort, hearing issues, and even infections. Understanding ETD is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ultimately improving quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in intensity. Common symptoms include:
Ear Pain: Discomfort or pain in the ear, often described as a feeling of pressure.
Fullness in the Ear: A sensation of fullness or blockage in the ear, similar to the feeling experienced during altitude changes.
Hearing Loss: Temporary hearing impairment due to fluid buildup or pressure changes.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears, which can accompany ETD.
Dizziness: A feeling of unsteadiness or vertigo, particularly if pressure changes affect balance.

diseases.name: Evali - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: EVALI, or e-cigarette or vaping product use-associated lung injury, is a serious health condition that emerged in the United States in 2019. It has garnered significant attention due to its association with the rising popularity of vaping, particularly among young adults and adolescents. Understanding EVALI is crucial as it highlights the potential dangers of vaping and the importance of awareness regarding the health risks associated with e-cigarette use. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of EVALI, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: EVALI presents with a variety of symptoms that can range from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Cough: A persistent cough that may worsen over time.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling out of breath, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Fever: Elevated body temperature, often accompanied by chills.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Evans Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Evans Syndrome is a rare and complex autoimmune disorder characterized by the simultaneous occurrence of autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) and immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP). This condition can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and requires careful management. Understanding Evans Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can help mitigate its complications and improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Evans Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Fatigue: Due to anemia, individuals may experience extreme tiredness and weakness.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin may occur as a result of low red blood cell counts.
Easy Bruising and Bleeding: Low platelet counts can lead to easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from cuts, and spontaneous bleeding.
Petechiae: Small red or purple spots on the skin caused by bleeding under the skin.
Shortness of Breath: This may occur during physical activity due to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Often related to anemia, these symptoms can occur, especially when standing up quickly.

diseases.name: Everything about Piles (Hemorrhoids): Symptoms, Causes, Treatments and Prevention.
diseases.description: Piles, also called hemorrhoids, are swollen veins in the rectum or anus that can cause discomfort, pain, and bleeding. They are a common condition that affects individuals across all age groups and genders. This comprehensive guide explores the symptoms, causes, treatments, and preventive measures for piles to address your concerns and help you manage this condition effectively.
symptoms: Piles, also called hemorrhoids, can cause a range of symptoms that vary based on their type (internal or external) and severity. Recognizing these symptoms early can help in seeking timely treatment. Below are the common piles symptoms:
Pain or discomfort during bowel movements : Often felt with external piles or thrombosed hemorrhoids.
Bleeding during or after defecation : One of the key symptoms is bright red blood observed on toilet paper, blood in the stool , or in the toilet bowl.
Itching or irritation around the anus : Caused by inflammation or mucus discharge.
Swelling or a lump near the anus : Typically associated with external piles, these lumps may be tender or painful.
Mucus discharge : This can occur after bowel movements, leading to further irritation.

In females, piles are common during pregnancy due to increased pressure on the rectal veins, hormonal changes, and constipation. Common symptoms include swelling, itching, and bleeding, which may worsen with straining during bowel movements.

Men are prone to piles due to lifestyle factors like prolonged sitting, heavy lifting, or a low-fiber diet. Common complaints include a painful lump near the anus, discomfort during defecation, and rectal bleeding .
If you experience any of these hemorrhoid symptoms, consult a healthcare professional. Early diagnosis and treatment can alleviate discomfort and prevent complications.

diseases.name: Everything You Need to Know About Anal Abscess
diseases.description: An anal abscess is a painful condition wherein a collection of pus forms near the anus. Many anal abscesses result from infection in the small anal glands. Perianal abscess, which often looks like painful boil-like swelling near the anus, is the most common type of abscess. Another type includes anorectal abscess, a collection of pus under the skin in the anus and rectum area.
symptoms: There may be constant pain and a throbbing sensation . These are the most noticeable symptoms, Swelling in the anal area and pain during bowel movements are usually seen . Some other common symptoms are:
Bleeding or rectal discharge
Constipation
Swelling
Fatigue

A red, bloated, and sensitive nodule or bump at the rim of the anus may be felt . The illness might cause a fever and chills. One may also experience rectal bleeding or discharge . Those experiencing inflammatory bowel diseases may have anal abscesses deeper in the rectum. This may result in pain and discomfort in the abdominal area. Other than discomfort or pain, which may lead a child to become irritable, there aren’t many symptoms in toddlers. A bulge or nodule around the anal area may also be visible or felt.
Also Read About: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Everything You Need To Know About Cervical Spondylitis
diseases.description: Cervical spondylitis and lumbar spondylosis are the two very common forms of spondylitis. Cervical spondylitis occurs when the cartilage, bones, ligaments, and bones in your neck begin to wear and tear with age or without age. In the olden days, cervical spondylitis and spondylosis were associated with old age. But with the present generation and the current lifestyle, spondylitis and spondylosis are not restricted to any age group.
symptoms: The symptoms of cervical spondylitis are mentioned below:

Neck Pain: Cervical spondylosis leads to neck pain that can travel to your arms or shoulders. There is a tingling pain in the beginning which can worsen if left untreated. Cervical pain can increase standing, sneezing, sitting, coughing, or tilting the neck backward. This is the most common symptom of cervical spondylitis .
Muscle Weakness: Cervical spondylosis can lead to muscle weakness. The muscles become so weak and stiff that it becomes difficult to lift the arms or grasp something properly.
Headaches. A stiff neck can lead to headaches. The headaches will mostly occur at the back of your head.

Numbness: There are tingling and numbness mainly in the arm and shoulders. In many cases, tingling can travel down to the legs. Tingling can be accompanied by numbness if the disease is left untreated.
Loss of Balance: Since the bones begin to lose strength, you might suffer from loss of balance and difficulty in walking.
Loss of Bladder Control: In rare cases, cervical spondylosis can lead to loss of bladder and bowel control. If you face such a problem, you need to seek immediate medical attention.

diseases.name: Everything You Need to Know about Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
diseases.description: COPD stands for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease , a condition affecting the oxygen exchange in the lungs by narrowing of the air passages within the lungs, making it difficult for oxygen and carbon dioxide to be exchanged.
symptoms: COPD is a chronic condition. You will not develop symptoms immediately. It might begin with symptoms like shortness of breath during any physical or strenuous activities; and mild coughing, which may eventually worsen to a stage where you start avoiding physical activities and require medical oxygen support. The symptoms include:
Breathlessness or shortness of breath
Chronic, productive coughing(coughing producing sputum)
Tightness in chest
Weight loss
Frequent attacks of cold, flu, and respiratory infections in the past
Edema (swelling) in the lower extremities

diseases.name: Everything You Need to Know About Fifth Disease
diseases.description: Fifth disease, also known as Erythema Infectiosum, is a contagious viral infection that affects children of school age. The fifth disease is a rash that occurs on the cheeks and causes a bright red rash. Because of the rash, it’s been dubbed “slapped cheek disease”. A virus known as parvovirus B19 causes this disease. This virus is very contagious, and infected individuals can pass it on to others by coughing or sneezing.
symptoms: About 20% of patients exhibit no symptoms. They are still contagious and can spread the disease to others. Symptoms are common at the start of the disease, and the virus is most contagious at this time. The following are some of the most common symptoms of the fifth disease:
Fatigue
Headaches
Low fever (temperatures of 99°F to 101°F (37°C to 38.5°C))
Running nose
Sore throat

After a few days, a raised, slap-like rash on the face or body may appear. The patient is no longer contagious after the rash appears. The rash may be itchy. In five to ten days, it should be gone. In certain situations, a second rash may appear after the “slapped cheek” rash has faded. This time, the rash may be found on:
Arms
Legs
The trunk (chest and back)
Buttocks
Joint discomfort and swelling affect approximately 10% of children with fifth disease.

Although the fifth disease is more common in youngsters, it can also affect adults. Adults frequently experience flu-like symptoms without a rash. In addition to those symptoms, about 80% of individuals experience joint discomfort in their wrists, hands, and knees.

diseases.name: Everything You Need to Know About Omicron Sub-Variant BA. 2.75
diseases.description: The Omicron variant of coronavirus, which has driven most of the global surges since the beginning of 2022, is mutating continuously. While its sub-variants BA.4 and BA.5 were found prevalent in Europe and America, a new sub-lineage of Omicron, BA.2.75 , has been detected in India. As per the World Health Organization (WHO) , this new sub-lineage has also been detected in many other countries as well.
symptoms: No distinct symptoms have been reported so far. It is said that the infection caused by Omicron variant BA.2.75 is mild or asymptomatic. However, it is too early to say anything about this sub-variants clinical symptoms.

Many health experts have said that the number of severe COVID cases has reduced these days compared to earlier. However, experts advise looking out for COVID-19-induced sore throat that causes scratchiness, dryness, and pain. The symptoms are usually mild and may last no more than 4-5 days.

Older adults and those with comorbidities should be extra careful and consult a doctor immediately. Sometimes, sore throat is followed by other symptoms such as loss of taste or smell, congestion, chills, fatigue, body aches, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting .
However, the symptoms are milder, particularly in vaccinated or previously infected people.

diseases.name: Everything you need to know about Patent Ductus Arteriosus
diseases.description: Patent Ductus Arteriosus or PDA is a heart condition. PDA is a persistent opening between two major blood vessels leading from your heart. The opening (known as the ductus Arteriosus), is a normal part of an infant’s circulatory system before birth that generally closes shortly after the birth. However, if it remains open, it is called a Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA).
symptoms: The symptoms of PDA vary and depend on two factors. These include –
● The size of the opening
● If the baby is born full-term or is premature.
If the PDA is small in the baby, there could be no signs or symptoms, even until adulthood. However, babies with large PDA may experience symptoms soon after their birth. It includes the following –
● Poor growth
● Inadequate feeding
● Breathlessness or fast breathing
● Rapid pulse rate
● Sweating while eating or crying
● Getting tired easily

diseases.name: Everything You Need to Know about Pulmonary Fibrosis
diseases.description: Pulmonary fibrosis is a lung disease that occurs because of lung tissue damage or scarring. As the affected area is the lung, the patient can become short of breath. The body suffers from an oxygen deficit, which can lead to cardiac and respiratory complications. Although the ill-effects caused to the lung are irreversible, medicines and therapies can manage the condition and ease the symptoms.
symptoms: Typically, the symptoms are very mild and even unnoticeable at the beginning. Most commonly, people face difficulty in breathing as the initial symptom. Some other symptoms include:
Long dry cough
Weakness and muscle ache
Weight loss
Severe shortness of breath
Chest stiffness
Curving of nails (nail clubbing)

diseases.name: Everything You Want to Know About Ringworm
diseases.description: Ringworm, also known as dermatophytosis, is a fungal infection. It occurs on the skin, or on the scalp, and is transmitted by skin-to-skin contact. It is a very common infection and can spread very easily.
symptoms: As ringworm can appear on any part of your body, the symptoms can vary, depending on which part is affected. Common symptoms include:
Itchiness
Ring-shaped rashes
Redness
Scaly and cracked skin
Hair loss

diseases.name: Everything you Wanted to know about Thrombosed Hemorrhoids
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus. Close to three out of four adults will have hemorrhoids from time to time. Hemorrhoids have a number of causes, but often the cause is unknown. However, swollen hemorrhoids can be painful, irritating, and cause rectal bleeding , making bowel movements uncomfortable. There are two kinds of hemorrhoids – External and Thrombosed hemorrhoids.
symptoms: Thrombosed hemorrhoids that appear as a small lump outside the anus. Acutely thrombosed external hemorrhoids appear as a dark bluish lump at the edge of the anal canal and is painful. The blood clot inside the lump causes a dark bluish colour. External hemorrhoid that is not thrombosed are more rubbery lumps that are usually not bluish.
Pain during bowel movements, sitting, walking and other strenuous activities
Bleeding during bowel movements
Itching around the anus
Lumps or swelling around the anus

diseases.name: Ewing’s Sarcoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Ewing's sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that typically develops in the bones or soft tissues of children and young adults. Because its symptoms—such as bone pain or swelling—can be mistaken for more common childhood ailments, understanding this condition is especially important. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about Ewing's sarcoma—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, available treatment options, and what to expect throughout the journey. Our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this challenge with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of Ewing's sarcoma can be vague and are often mistaken for other, more common conditions like sports injuries or "growing pains." However, if you notice these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
Common Early Signs:

Persistent Pain: The most common symptom is a persistent pain in the affected bone or soft tissue. The pain may come and go at first, but it can become constant and may get worse at night or with activity.
A Lump or Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling may appear in the affected area, which may feel warm and soft to the touch.
Unexplained Fever: A persistent, unexplained fever that comes and goes.
Unexplained Broken Bone (Fracture): In rare cases, a bone can become so weakened by the cancer that it breaks after a minor fall or injury.
Advanced Symptoms:
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
Breathing Problems: If the cancer has spread to the lungs, it can cause a persistent cough or shortness of breath.
If your child has a persistent bone pain or a lump that doesn't go away, it is crucial to consult a doctor right away for an accurate diagnosis.

diseases.name: Exertion Headaches - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Exertion headaches are a type of headache that occurs during or after physical activity. They can be a significant concern for individuals who engage in strenuous exercise or heavy lifting, as they can disrupt daily activities and impact overall quality of life. Understanding exertion headaches is crucial for effective management and prevention, especially for those who lead active lifestyles. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of exertion headaches, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of exertion headaches can vary but typically include:
Throbbing or Pulsating Pain: This is often felt on both sides of the head and can range from mild to severe.
Nausea: Some individuals may experience feelings of nausea accompanying the headache.
Sensitivity to Light and Sound: Bright lights and loud noises may exacerbate the discomfort.
Dizziness: A sense of lightheadedness or imbalance can occur during an exertion headache.

diseases.name: Exostosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Exostosis is a medical term that refers to the formation of a benign bone growth on the surface of a bone. This condition can occur in various parts of the body and is significant because, while often asymptomatic, it can lead to discomfort, pain, or complications if left untreated. Understanding exostosis is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their quality of life.
symptoms: Exostosis may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in its early stages. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Localized Pain: Discomfort or pain at the site of the bone growth, particularly during movement or pressure.
Swelling: Visible swelling or a lump over the affected bone.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the joint near the exostosis due to pain or mechanical obstruction.
Nerve Compression: In some cases, exostosis can press on nearby nerves, leading to tingling, numbness, or weakness in the affected area.

diseases.name: Exotropia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Exotropia is a type of strabismus, commonly known as "crossed eyes," where one or both eyes turn outward. This condition can significantly impact an individual's vision and quality of life. Understanding exotropia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to complications such as amblyopia (lazy eye) and binocular vision problems. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding exotropia.
symptoms: Outward Eye Deviation: The most noticeable symptom is the outward turning of one or both eyes.
Double Vision: Individuals may experience diplopia, where they see two images of a single object.
Difficulty with Depth Perception: This can affect activities such as driving or playing sports.
Eye Strain: Prolonged visual tasks may lead to discomfort or fatigue.
Squinting or Closing One Eye: To compensate for misalignment, individuals may squint or close one eye.

diseases.name: External Hemorrhoids - Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids (also known as piles) are bulging veins that resemble varicose veins in the anus and lower rectum. Internal hemorrhoids form inside the rectum, while external hemorrhoids form beneath the skin around the anus. Three out of every four individuals will experience hemorrhoids at some point in their lives.
symptoms: External hemorrhoids are itchy and uncomfortable.
People frequently feel them when they touch the area around the anus. External hemorrhoids are frequently a shade or two darker than the surrounding skin color.
A patient with hemorrhoids may experience a variety of symptoms. The degree of the hemorrhoids will influence the symptoms. The following are some of the symptoms the patient may be experiencing:
Pain and Itching in the anus area or rectal area
Bumps on or around the anus
Blood in stool
Blood detected on toilet paper or in the toilet.
Bloated bumps around the anus

diseases.name: Extramammary Pagets Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Extramammary Paget's Disease (EMPD) is a rare skin condition that primarily affects the genital and perianal regions. It is characterized by the presence of malignant cells in the epidermis, which can lead to significant discomfort and complications if left untreated. Understanding EMPD is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and the general public, as early detection and intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of EMPD can vary but typically include:
Red, Scaly Patches: The most common symptom is the appearance of red, scaly patches on the skin in the genital or perianal area.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many patients report itching, burning, or discomfort in the affected areas.
Discharge: Some individuals may experience a discharge from the lesions.
Thickened Skin: The skin may become thickened or crusted over time.

diseases.name: Extramedullary Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Extramedullary tumors are growths that arise outside the bone marrow, often in soft tissues such as the spine, meninges (brain coverings), lymph nodes, or muscles. The word “extramedullary” simply means “outside the marrow.” These tumors can occur in many areas such as the spine, brain coverings (meninges), soft tissues, or lymph nodes. Some are noncancerous (benign), while others are cancerous (malignant).
symptoms: Symptoms vary depending on the tumor’s size and location. Early signs may be mild but should not be ignored.
Common early symptoms include:
A lump or swelling that does not go away.
Pain or discomfort in the affected area.
Tingling, numbness, or weakness if nerves are compressed.
Advanced symptoms may include:
Difficulty moving or walking if the spinal cord is affected.
Vision or hearing changes (for tumors near the brain or nerves).
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or night sweats.

diseases.name: Eye Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Eye cancer is rare, but when it's found early and treated promptly, many people do well. This article provides comprehensive information on eye cancer ---what it is, how doctors diagnose it, the latest treatments, and expected recovery.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on where the cancer starts and how advanced it is. Early eye cancers can be subtle or have no symptoms at all, which is why regular eye exams are important.
Noticeable vision loss or blind spots
Eye pain or redness that doesn't go away
Bulging of one eye (proptosis)
A visible mass on the eye surface or eyelid
Change in pupil shape or a new squint
Persistent tearing or irritation
Headaches when the tumor affects surrounding structures
Any sudden change in vision, a persistent eye lesion, or a white pupil reflex in a child should be checked promptly by an eye specialist.

diseases.name: Eye Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eye infections are a common yet often misunderstood health issue that can affect individuals of all ages. These infections can range from mild irritations to severe conditions that may threaten vision. Understanding eye infections is crucial not only for effective treatment but also for prevention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of eye infections, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and preventive measures.
symptoms: The symptoms of eye infections can vary depending on the type and severity of the infection. Common symptoms include:
Redness: The eye may appear red or bloodshot due to inflammation.
Itching or Burning: Many individuals experience discomfort, itching, or a burning sensation.
Discharge: There may be a watery or purulent discharge from the eye.
Swelling: The eyelids or surrounding tissues may become swollen.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, is common in many eye infections.
Blurred Vision: In some cases, vision may become blurred or impaired.

diseases.name: Eye Stroke - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eye stroke, also known as retinal artery occlusion, is a serious condition that can lead to sudden vision loss. It occurs when the blood supply to the retina is interrupted, depriving the retinal cells of essential nutrients and oxygen. This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause irreversible vision loss but also due to its association with systemic health issues, such as cardiovascular disease. Understanding eye stroke is crucial for early detection and intervention, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of eye stroke can vary depending on the severity and location of the blockage. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Vision Loss: This may occur in one eye and can range from partial to complete loss of vision.
Visual Disturbances: Patients may experience blurred vision, dark spots, or a curtain-like shadow over their field of vision.
Pain: While eye stroke is often painless, some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the affected eye.

diseases.name: Eyelid Dermatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Eyelid dermatitis is a common skin condition that affects the delicate skin surrounding the eyes. It can cause discomfort, irritation, and cosmetic concerns, making it significant for those who experience it. Understanding eyelid dermatitis is crucial not only for effective management but also for preventing potential complications. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of eyelid dermatitis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: Eyelid dermatitis can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Redness: The skin on the eyelids may appear red and inflamed.
Itching: A common symptom, itching can range from mild to severe.
Swelling: The eyelids may become swollen, leading to discomfort and difficulty opening the eyes.
Flaking or Peeling: The skin may become dry and flaky, which can be unsightly and irritating.
Crusting: In some cases, crusting may occur, especially if there is an associated infection.

diseases.name: Fabry Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fabry Disease is a rare genetic disorder that affects various systems in the body, leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact quality of life. Understanding Fabry Disease is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Fabry Disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more, to help individuals better understand this complex condition.
symptoms: Fabry Disease presents a wide range of symptoms that can vary significantly between individuals. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Episodes of severe pain, known as acroparesthesia, often occur in the hands and feet.
Skin Changes: Angiokeratomas, small red or purple spots on the skin, are a hallmark of the disease.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea are common.
Kidney Problems: Progressive kidney disease can occur, leading to kidney failure if untreated.
Heart Issues: Individuals may develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which can lead to heart failure.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals experience hearing impairment.
Eye Problems: Corneal opacities and other eye issues may arise.

diseases.name: Failure To Thrive - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Failure to thrive (FTT) is a term used to describe a significant decline in a person's physical health, particularly in children and the elderly. It is characterized by inadequate growth or weight gain, leading to a range of health complications. Understanding FTT is crucial, as it can indicate underlying medical issues that require immediate attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of failure to thrive, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of failure to thrive can vary depending on the age of the individual and the underlying causes. Common symptoms include:
In Children: Poor weight gain or weight loss Delayed developmental milestones Irritability or lethargy Decreased appetite Frequent infections
Poor weight gain or weight loss
Delayed developmental milestones
Irritability or lethargy
Decreased appetite
Frequent infections
In Adults: Unintentional weight loss Decreased appetite Fatigue or weakness Decline in physical function Social withdrawal
Unintentional weight loss
Fatigue or weakness
Decline in physical function
Social withdrawal

diseases.name: Fanconi Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fanconi Syndrome is a rare but significant disorder that affects the kidneys' ability to reabsorb essential nutrients and minerals. This condition can lead to a variety of health issues, including bone disease, growth retardation in children, and electrolyte imbalances. Understanding Fanconi Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Fanconi Syndrome can vary widely depending on the underlying cause and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Increased Urination: Frequent urination due to the loss of glucose and other substances in the urine.
Dehydration: Resulting from excessive urination, leading to thirst and dry mouth.
Growth Retardation: Particularly in children, due to nutrient loss.
Bone Pain or Weakness: Caused by phosphate loss, leading to weakened bones.
Fatigue: General tiredness due to metabolic imbalances.
Muscle Weakness: Resulting from electrolyte imbalances.

diseases.name: Farsightedness - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Farsightedness, also known as hyperopia, is a common vision condition that affects millions of people worldwide. It occurs when light entering the eye is focused behind the retina, making it difficult to see nearby objects clearly. While many individuals may experience mild farsightedness without significant issues, others may find it impacts their daily activities, such as reading or using a computer. Understanding farsightedness is crucial for early detection and effective management, ensuring a better quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Individuals with farsightedness may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty focusing on nearby objects, leading to a sense of blurriness.
Eye Strain: Discomfort or fatigue in the eyes, especially after prolonged reading or close work.
Headaches: Frequent headaches, particularly after visual tasks, can be a sign of eye strain related to hyperopia.
Difficulty with Near Tasks: Challenges in activities such as reading, sewing, or using a smartphone.

diseases.name: FAST FACTS ON JUVENILE IDIOPATHIC ARTHRITIS (JIA) OR CHILDHOOD ARTHRITIS
diseases.description: Arthritis developing in children below 16 years of age is called Juvenile Idiopathic arthritis (JIA). The word arthritis means joint inflammation; “arth” means joint and “itis” mean inflammation. The etiology of childhood arthritis is unknown but a dysfunctional immune system starts attacking healthy joints and tissues causing symptoms. Occasionaly an infection can trigger for onset of arthritis . Untreated arthritis in children can lead to joint contractures, damage the cartilage and bones and cause altered bone growth leading to growth retardation.

diseases.name: Fat embolism
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Typically, fat embolism arises suddenly 12-36 hours after an injury. Symptoms and signs rest on the specific location of the blocked arteries. Signs and symptoms of fat embolus include central nervous system dysfunction that may progress to coma or death, irregularities in the heartbeat, respiratory distress, and fever. Anemia and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) are common. Normally, small haemorrhages are seen on the neck, shoulders, armpits, and conjunctiva. The mortality (death) rate is 10%-20%. Senior citizens and those with existing medical conditions or poor health have worse outcomes.

diseases.name: Fat Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fat necrosis is a medical condition that involves the death of fat cells in the body. While it may sound alarming, understanding fat necrosis is crucial for recognizing its implications, potential causes, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of fat necrosis, making it accessible to a general audience while ensuring medical accuracy.
symptoms: Fat necrosis can present with various symptoms, including:
Firm Lumps: The most common symptom is the presence of firm, palpable lumps in the affected area.
Pain or Discomfort: Some individuals may experience pain or tenderness in the area of necrosis.
Skin Changes: The skin overlying the necrotic tissue may appear discolored or have a different texture.

diseases.name: Fatal Familial Insomnia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fatal Familial Insomnia (FFI) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the brain's ability to regulate sleep. This condition is not just a simple sleep disorder; it is a severe and progressive illness that can lead to death. FFI is significant not only because of its devastating effects on individuals and families but also due to its unique genetic basis and the insights it provides into the mechanisms of sleep and neurodegeneration. Understanding FFI is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support for affected families.
symptoms: The symptoms of Fatal Familial Insomnia can be divided into early and late stages:
Early Symptoms: Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep. Increased anxiety and panic attacks. Hallucinations and confusion. Memory problems and cognitive decline.
Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Increased anxiety and panic attacks.
Hallucinations and confusion.
Memory problems and cognitive decline.

Late Symptoms: Severe insomnia leading to total sleep deprivation. Autonomic dysfunction: Changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and temperature regulation. Loss of motor control and coordination. Progressive dementia and personality changes. Coma and eventual death.
Severe insomnia leading to total sleep deprivation.
Autonomic dysfunction: Changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and temperature regulation.
Loss of motor control and coordination.
Progressive dementia and personality changes.
Coma and eventual death.

diseases.name: Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD)
diseases.description: Fatty liver disease occurs when excess fat builds up in the liver, often linked to obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome.
symptoms: Often no symptoms
Fatigue
Discomfort in the upper right abdomen

diseases.name: Fatty Liver Disease : Syptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Fatty liver disease is the buildup of excess fat in the liver. Excessive consumption of alcohol may lead to the fatty liver, which can lead to a severe form of liver damage if the individual continues to drink excess alcohol.
symptoms: Most individuals with fatty liver do not have any symptoms, although some may experience dull pain on the right side of the stomach, due to enlargement of the liver. Other symptoms are general fatigue, nausea , and loss of appetite. Once cirrhosis develops, and liver failure sets in, there may be yellowness of the eyes ( jaundice ), accumulation of fluid (edema), vomiting of blood, mental confusion and jaundice.

diseases.name: Febrile Seizure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Febrile seizures are a common neurological event in young children, often occurring in response to fever. While they can be alarming for parents and caregivers, understanding febrile seizures is crucial for managing them effectively. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of febrile seizures, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of a febrile seizure can vary, but they typically include:
Convulsions: Uncontrolled shaking or jerking movements of the body.
Loss of Consciousness: The child may appear unresponsive during the seizure.
Stiffening of the Body: The child may exhibit rigidity or arching of the back.
Postictal State: After the seizure, the child may be drowsy, confused, or irritable.

diseases.name: Febrile Seizures in Children
diseases.description: Febrile seizures are convulsions or seizures that usually occur among children within the age of 6 months to 5 years. These convulsions are often triggered by ear infections, flu, fever, or any minor childhood illness. In some cases, a child may experience these seizures without a spike in temperature and get fever after a few hours. The condition may occur in children with normal neurological as well as physical development and are often harmless. The risk of febrile seizures occurs between 12 and 18 months of age.

diseases.name: Fecal Impaction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fecal impaction is a common yet often overlooked condition that can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not addressed promptly. It occurs when a large mass of stool becomes stuck in the colon or rectum, making it difficult or impossible to pass. This condition is significant not only because of the physical discomfort it causes but also due to its potential to lead to more serious health issues if left untreated. Understanding fecal impaction, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is essential for maintaining digestive health.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of fecal impaction is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or cramping in the abdomen is often the first sign of fecal impaction.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen can occur.
Constipation: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements are a hallmark of fecal impaction.
Nausea and Vomiting: In severe cases, individuals may experience nausea or vomiting due to the buildup of stool.
Rectal Pain: Pain during bowel movements or a feeling of pressure in the rectum can indicate fecal impaction.

diseases.name: Feeling a burning sensation in stomach? It might be IBD
diseases.description: Do you experience a burning sensation in your stomach or have stomach infections? It could be a symptom of IBD (Inflammatory bowel disease). IBD is a group of health conditions leading to chronic inflammation of your alimentary canal (digestive tract).
symptoms: Symptoms of IBD vary depending on the severity of inflammation and where it occurs. Some of the common signs and symptoms are:
Diarrhea
Fever and fatigue
Abdominal pain
Blood in stool
Reduced appetite
Weight loss

diseases.name: Felon Finger - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Felon finger, a term that may sound unfamiliar to many, refers to a painful and potentially serious infection of the fingertip. This condition is significant not only because of the discomfort it causes but also due to the risk of complications if left untreated. Understanding felon finger is crucial for early recognition and effective management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their hand health and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of felon finger can vary in severity but typically include:
Severe Pain: The fingertip may be extremely painful, especially when touched or moved.
Swelling: The affected area often becomes swollen and may feel warm to the touch.
Redness: The skin around the fingertip may appear red and inflamed.
Pus Formation: In advanced cases, pus may accumulate, leading to the formation of an abscess.
Limited Mobility: Movement of the affected finger may be restricted due to pain and swelling.

diseases.name: Felty Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Felty Syndrome is a rare but significant autoimmune disorder that primarily affects individuals with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). It is characterized by a triad of symptoms: rheumatoid arthritis, splenomegaly (enlarged spleen), and neutropenia (low levels of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell). Understanding Felty Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Felty Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Felty Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Rheumatoid Arthritis Symptoms: Joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, particularly in the hands and feet.
Splenomegaly: An enlarged spleen, which may cause discomfort or a feeling of fullness in the abdomen.
Neutropenia: Low levels of neutrophils, leading to increased susceptibility to infections.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Fever: Low-grade fevers may occur due to underlying inflammation or infections.

diseases.name: Fetal Alcohol Syndrome: Types, Symptoms, Causes, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: When a pregnant woman drinks alcohol, the unborn child is also exposed to alcohol exposure. It can cause a congenital disability in the child called fetal alcohol syndrome. The condition is irreversible and can cause several health issues, such as brain damage or growth problems. Although, the condition varies from child to child, it is important to note that any amount of alcohol exposure can result in this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms and severity of the condition may vary from child to child. However, some children experience severity much higher than others. The signs and symptoms of the condition may include a combination of physical, intellectual, or cognitive deficits.
The physical deficits include:
Distinct facial features include small eyes, a thin upper lip, a short and upturned nose, and smooth skin between the upper lips and the nose.
Joints, limbs, and fingers deformities
Sluggish physical growth before and after birth
Hearing or vision issues
Small head and brain size
Heart problems and issues with kidneys and bones
The symptoms of the brain and central nervous system issues are:
Poor coordination and imbalance
Intellectual and learning disability
Developmental delays
Weak memory
Attention and processing information deficit
Issues with reasoning and problem-solving
Problem linking the consequences of choices
Lack judgment skills
Restlessness or hyperactivity
Severe mood swings
The following are the symptoms of social and behavioural issues:
Trouble interacting with others
Poor social skills
Issues in school
Unable to adapt to change or switch between one task to another
Behavioural issues and impulse control
Difficulty planning and staying on one task

diseases.name: Fetal Distress - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fetal distress is a critical condition that can arise during pregnancy and labor, indicating that a fetus is not receiving adequate oxygen or is experiencing other forms of stress. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications for both the mother and the baby if not identified and managed promptly. Understanding fetal distress is essential for expectant parents and healthcare providers alike, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of fetal distress is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Abnormal Fetal Heart Rate: A heart rate below 110 beats per minute or above 160 beats per minute can indicate distress.
Decreased Fetal Movement: A noticeable reduction in the baby's movements may signal a problem.
Meconium-Stained Amniotic Fluid: The presence of meconium in the amniotic fluid can indicate fetal distress.

diseases.name: Fetal Hydantoin Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fetal Hydantoin Syndrome (FHS) is a condition that arises when a fetus is exposed to the anticonvulsant medication phenytoin (Dilantin) during pregnancy. This syndrome is significant because it can lead to a range of developmental and physical abnormalities in the child, impacting their quality of life and requiring ongoing medical care. Understanding FHS is crucial for expectant mothers who may be on anticonvulsant therapy, as well as healthcare providers who manage their care.
symptoms: Fetal Hydantoin Syndrome presents with a variety of symptoms that can affect physical appearance, cognitive function, and overall health. Common symptoms include:
Facial Features: Distinctive facial characteristics such as a broad forehead, flat nasal bridge, and thin upper lip.
Growth Deficiencies: Children may be born with low birth weight and may experience growth delays.
Cognitive Impairments: Learning disabilities and developmental delays are common, affecting the child’s ability to thrive in educational settings.
Skeletal Abnormalities: Some children may have limb deformities or other skeletal issues.
Cardiac Defects: Congenital heart defects may also be present.

diseases.name: Fetal Macrosomia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fetal macrosomia is a term that refers to a condition where a fetus is significantly larger than average for its gestational age. This condition is not just a matter of size; it carries significant implications for both the mother and the baby. Understanding fetal macrosomia is crucial for expectant parents and healthcare providers alike, as it can lead to various complications during pregnancy, labor, and delivery. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and the long-term outlook for fetal macrosomia.
symptoms: Fetal macrosomia may not present obvious symptoms during pregnancy, but there are some signs that healthcare providers may monitor:
Increased Fundal Height: The measurement of the uterus may be larger than expected for the gestational age.
Ultrasound Findings: An ultrasound may indicate a larger-than-average fetus.
Maternal Discomfort: The mother may experience increased discomfort due to the size of the fetus.

diseases.name: Fibrinoid Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fibrinoid necrosis is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it plays a crucial role in understanding certain pathological processes in the body. This condition is characterized by the deposition of fibrin-like protein in the walls of blood vessels and surrounding tissues, often associated with various diseases, particularly autoimmune disorders. Understanding fibrinoid necrosis is essential for recognizing its implications in health and disease, as well as for guiding appropriate treatment strategies.
symptoms: Fibrinoid necrosis itself may not present with specific symptoms, as it is often a histological finding rather than a standalone condition. However, the underlying diseases associated with fibrinoid necrosis can lead to various symptoms, including:
Joint Pain and Swelling: Common in autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis.
Skin Rashes: Such as the butterfly rash seen in systemic lupus erythematosus.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness and lack of energy.
Fever: Often associated with inflammation and infection.
Organ Dysfunction: Depending on the affected organs, symptoms may vary widely.

diseases.name: Fibroadenomas
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The way to identify fibroadenomas on your own is by knowing what they feel like. Fibroadenomas are:
Firm or rubbery
Round with distinct borders
Painless
Easily moved

If the tumour is big enough, you can just by running your hand over it, identify it. However, for small tumours that cannot be detected easily, an ultrasound is required. Usually, fibroadenomas are not painful. However, they can be uncomfortable or very sensitive to touch. Often women find that their fibroadenoma gets tender in the days before their period. Pushing or prodding at the lump can also make it tender. If you do feel like you may have a fibroadenoma, do seek medical attention.

diseases.name: Fibrocystic Breasts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fibrocystic breasts are a common condition that affects many women, often causing discomfort and anxiety. While the term may sound alarming, it is important to understand that fibrocystic breast changes are typically benign (non-cancerous) and part of the normal spectrum of breast tissue. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of fibrocystic breasts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. By understanding this condition, women can better manage their breast health and make informed decisions about their care.
symptoms: Women with fibrocystic breasts may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Lumpiness: The breast tissue may feel lumpy or nodular, particularly in the upper outer quadrant of the breast.
Tenderness: Many women report breast tenderness or pain, especially before menstruation.
Swelling: Breasts may become swollen or engorged during certain times of the menstrual cycle.
Nipple Discharge: Some women may notice a clear or milky discharge from the nipple.

diseases.name: Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a rare and debilitating genetic disorder characterized by the abnormal formation of bone in muscles, tendons, and other connective tissues. This condition is significant not only due to its rarity but also because it leads to progressive loss of mobility and severe physical limitations. Understanding FOP is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support for affected individuals and their families.
symptoms: The symptoms of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva can vary widely among individuals but generally include:
Progressive Loss of Mobility: As bone forms in soft tissues, movement becomes increasingly restricted.
Swelling and Pain: Episodes of swelling and discomfort may occur, often triggered by minor injuries or infections.
Formation of Bone: The most distinctive symptom is the gradual formation of bone in areas where it should not occur, such as muscles and tendons.
Deformities: Over time, the abnormal bone growth can lead to skeletal deformities.

diseases.name: Fibroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fibromas are benign tumors that can develop in various tissues throughout the body. While they are generally non-cancerous and often asymptomatic, their presence can lead to discomfort or complications depending on their size and location. Understanding fibromas is essential for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their health and well-being.
symptoms: Many individuals with fibromas may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Pain or Discomfort: Depending on the location of the fibroma, individuals may experience localized pain or discomfort.
Swelling or Lumps: Fibromas can present as noticeable lumps or swelling in the affected area.
Changes in Organ Function: In cases where fibromas develop in organs, they may interfere with normal function, leading to symptoms such as difficulty breathing or changes in menstrual cycles.

diseases.name: Fibromyalgia
diseases.description: Fibromyalgia is a disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain accompanied by fatigue, sleep, memory, and mood issues. Researchers believe that fibromyalgia amplifies painful sensations by affecting the way the brain and spinal cord process painful and nonpainful signals.
symptoms: Widespread pain described as a constant dull ache lasting at least three months
Fatigue
Cognitive difficulties (fibro fog)
Sleep problems
Headaches
Irritable bowel syndrome
Tingling or numbness in hands and feet
Sensitivity to temperature, light, or sound

diseases.name: Fight Sleepwalking (Somnambulism) and Have a Good Night's Sleep
diseases.description: Somnambulism, also commonly known as sleepwalking, is a sleep behavior disorder. In most cases, people with this disorder walk around while they are asleep. Sometimes, it also involves physical behavior other than walking. Somnambulism is more common among kids than adults. People suffering through the sleepwalking disorder cannot recall the occurrence because they tend to remain in deep sleep during the entire episode of sleepwalking. They might open their eyes while sleepwalking but they can’t see the same way they do when awake. Often times it can be difficult to wake them up. There is a higher chance of a sleepwalking episode in case the person is sleep deprived. Other than sleep deprivation, sleepwalking can be triggered by certain medications, fever related illness and alcohol. Sometimes, sleepwalking is an inherited trait and tends to run in families. According to sleepfoundation.org, the prevalence of sleepwalking in the general population is estimated to be between 1% and 15%.
symptoms: Sleepwalking symptoms mostly occurs after 1-2 hours of being asleep. It can last for a few minutes and sometimes longer. The frequency is often not consistent. It can involve walking around in a smaller area to leaving the house and covering a longer distance. People with sleepwalking disorder may experience the following symptoms while asleep:
Sitting up in bed, walking, rubbing eyes
Sleep talking
Glazed, glassy-eyed expression
Unable to respond to others
Unable to wake up while sleepwalking
Disorientation for a short time after waking up
Unable to hold any memory of the episode after waking up in the morning
Unable to properly function during the day
Sleep terrors in addition to sleepwalking
In some cases, people also show the following behaviours while asleep:
Routine activities, like talking or eating
Driving a car
Unusual behavior, like urinating in a closet
Jumping out a window
Getting violent

diseases.name: First Bite Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: First Bite Syndrome (FBS) is a rare but significant condition that affects individuals during the initial bites of a meal. Characterized by intense pain in the jaw and neck, this syndrome can lead to significant discomfort and anxiety around eating. Understanding FBS is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can impact nutritional intake and overall quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of First Bite Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of First Bite Syndrome can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Sharp Pain: A sudden, intense pain in the jaw, neck, or ear during the first bite of food.
Radiating Discomfort: Pain may radiate to other areas, such as the temple or throat.
Muscle Spasms: Some individuals may experience muscle spasms in the jaw or neck.
Anxiety Around Eating: Fear of pain can lead to avoidance of meals, resulting in weight loss or nutritional deficiencies.

diseases.name: Fissured Tongue - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fissured tongue, also known as lingua plicata, is a benign condition characterized by deep grooves or fissures on the surface of the tongue. While it may appear alarming, fissured tongue is generally harmless and often goes unnoticed by those who have it. However, understanding this condition is significant as it can sometimes be associated with other health issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of fissured tongue, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Fissured tongue is primarily characterized by the following symptoms:
Grooves or Fissures: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of deep grooves or fissures on the surface of the tongue.
Color Changes: The tongue may appear redder or have a different texture in the affected areas.
Discomfort or Sensitivity: Some individuals may experience mild discomfort, especially when consuming spicy or acidic foods.
Trapped Food Particles: Food particles may become lodged in the fissures, leading to irritation or bad breath.

diseases.name: Fitz Hugh Curtis Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fitz Hugh Curtis Syndrome (FHCS) is a rare but significant medical condition that primarily affects women. It is characterized by inflammation of the liver capsule, often associated with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Understanding this syndrome is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Fitz Hugh Curtis Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Fitz Hugh Curtis Syndrome can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Right Upper Quadrant Pain: This is the hallmark symptom, often described as sharp or stabbing pain that may radiate to the shoulder.
Fever: A low-grade fever may accompany the pain, indicating an underlying infection.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to the inflammation and irritation of the liver capsule.
Abdominal Tenderness: Physical examination may reveal tenderness in the right upper abdomen.
Menstrual Irregularities: Women may experience changes in their menstrual cycle due to the underlying reproductive health issues.

diseases.name: Flail Chest - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Flail chest is a serious medical condition that occurs when a segment of the rib cage becomes detached from the rest of the chest wall, leading to significant respiratory complications. This condition is often the result of severe trauma, such as a car accident or a fall, and can pose life-threatening risks if not promptly diagnosed and treated. Understanding flail chest is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, which can ultimately save lives.
symptoms: The symptoms of flail chest can vary in severity but typically include:
Severe Pain: Intense pain at the site of the injury, which may worsen with movement or breathing.
Difficulty Breathing: Patients may experience shortness of breath or rapid breathing due to compromised lung function.
Abnormal Chest Movement: The flail segment may move inward during inhalation and outward during exhalation, a phenomenon known as paradoxical movement.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, particularly around the lips and fingertips, indicating low oxygen levels.
Coughing Up Blood: Hemoptysis may occur if there is associated lung injury.

diseases.name: Flat Feet (Pes Planus)
diseases.description: Flat feet (pes planus) is a condition in which the arch of the foot is lower than normal or entirely absent, causing the entire sole of the foot to make contact with the ground. Flat feet can be present from birth or may develop over time. Most people with flat feet experience no pain; however, some develop foot, ankle, knee, or back pain.
symptoms: Foot pain, especially in the arch or heel
The inside bottom of the foot touching the ground
Tired or achy feet after standing
Swelling on the inside of the ankle
Difficulty standing on tiptoe
Knee, hip, or back pain due to altered alignment

diseases.name: Fluorosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fluorosis is a condition that affects the teeth and bones, primarily caused by excessive exposure to fluoride during the early years of life. While fluoride is known for its benefits in preventing tooth decay, overexposure can lead to a range of dental and skeletal issues. Understanding fluorosis is crucial for parents, healthcare providers, and individuals living in areas with high fluoride levels in water or other sources. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of fluorosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Fluorosis primarily affects the teeth, and its symptoms can vary in severity:
Mild Fluorosis: White spots or streaks on the teeth, which may be barely noticeable.
Moderate Fluorosis: More pronounced white spots, with some brown discoloration and surface irregularities.
Severe Fluorosis: Pitting, severe discoloration, and structural damage to the teeth, leading to increased susceptibility to cavities.

diseases.name: Focal Dystonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Focal dystonia is a neurological movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions that cause abnormal postures or movements in specific parts of the body. This condition can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, affecting their ability to perform daily activities, work, and engage in social interactions. Understanding focal dystonia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can lead to improved outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Focal dystonia presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary depending on the affected body part. Common symptoms include:
Involuntary Muscle Contractions: These can lead to abnormal postures or movements in the affected area.
Tremors: Some individuals may experience shaking or tremors in the affected muscles.
Pain or Discomfort: Muscle contractions can cause pain or discomfort, particularly if they lead to abnormal postures.
Difficulty with Fine Motor Skills: For those with hand dystonia, tasks such as writing or playing an instrument may become challenging.

diseases.name: Focal Seizure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Focal seizures, also known as partial seizures, are a type of seizure that originates in a specific area of the brain. Unlike generalized seizures, which affect both hemispheres of the brain simultaneously, focal seizures begin in one localized region. Understanding focal seizures is crucial not only for those who experience them but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of focal seizures, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of focal seizures can vary widely based on the area of the brain affected. Common symptoms include:
Motor Symptoms: Involuntary movements, such as twitching or jerking of a limb.
Sensory Symptoms: Unusual sensations, such as tingling, numbness, or visual disturbances.
Autonomic Symptoms: Changes in heart rate, sweating, or gastrointestinal symptoms.
Psychic Symptoms: Altered emotions, déjà vu, or hallucinations.

diseases.name: Folate Deficiency - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Folate deficiency is a significant health concern that can lead to a variety of serious medical conditions. Folate, also known as vitamin B9, is a water-soluble vitamin that plays a crucial role in DNA synthesis, repair, and methylation, as well as in the production of red blood cells. It is particularly important during periods of rapid growth, such as during pregnancy and infancy.
