Understanding folate deficiency is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and potential complications, as well as for implementing effective prevention and treatment strategies.
symptoms: Folate deficiency can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Weakness: Reduced physical strength and endurance.
Pale Skin: A noticeable paleness due to decreased red blood cell production.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity.
Heart Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a racing heart.
Cognitive Impairment: Difficulty concentrating or memory problems.
Mood Changes: Increased irritability or feelings of depression.

diseases.name: Folate Deficiency Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Folate Deficiency Anemia is a condition that arises when the body lacks sufficient folate, a vital B vitamin (B9) necessary for the production of red blood cells. This deficiency can lead to a decrease in the number of healthy red blood cells, which are essential for transporting oxygen throughout the body. Understanding folate deficiency anemia is crucial, as it can significantly impact overall health and well-being. This article will explore the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for this condition, providing a comprehensive overview for those seeking to understand this important health issue.
symptoms: Folate Deficiency Anemia can present with a variety of symptoms, which may develop gradually. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Weakness: Reduced physical strength and endurance.
Pale Skin: A noticeable paleness due to reduced red blood cell count.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, especially when standing up.
Heart Palpitations: An irregular or rapid heartbeat.
Cognitive Issues: Difficulty concentrating or memory problems.

diseases.name: Folic acid deficiency - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Folic acid deficiency is a significant health concern that can lead to various medical complications if left unaddressed. Folic acid, also known as vitamin B9, is essential for the production of DNA and the proper functioning of cells. It plays a crucial role in the formation of red blood cells and is particularly important during periods of rapid growth, such as during pregnancy and infancy. Understanding folic acid deficiency, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options is vital for maintaining overall health.
symptoms: Common symptoms of folic acid deficiency include:
Fatigue and weakness
Pale skin
Shortness of breath
Dizziness or lightheadedness
Heart palpitations
Irritability and mood changes
Glossitis (inflammation of the tongue)
Diarrhea

diseases.name: Follicular Lymphoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) that originates in the lymphatic system, specifically from B-cells, which are a type of white blood cell crucial for the immune response. This condition is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its unique characteristics, which can lead to a range of clinical outcomes. Understanding follicular lymphoma is essential for early detection, effective management, and improving patient quality of life.
symptoms: Follicular lymphoma often presents with vague symptoms, which can make early diagnosis challenging. Common symptoms include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Painless swelling in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Night Sweats: Excessive sweating during the night.
Fever: Low-grade fevers that come and go.
Itching: Generalized itching without a rash.

diseases.name: Folliculitis Decalvans - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Folliculitis decalvans is a chronic inflammatory condition that primarily affects the hair follicles on the scalp, leading to hair loss and scarring. This condition is significant not only because of its physical manifestations but also due to its psychological impact on those affected. Understanding folliculitis decalvans is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for individuals suffering from this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of folliculitis decalvans can vary but typically include:
Red, inflamed bumps: These may appear on the scalp and can be painful or itchy.
Pustules: Small, pus-filled blisters may develop around the hair follicles.
Hair loss: Affected areas may experience thinning or complete loss of hair.
Scarring: Over time, the inflammation can lead to scarring, which may be permanent.

diseases.name: Food Allergies - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Food allergies are a growing concern in today's society, affecting millions of individuals worldwide. They can lead to severe and sometimes life-threatening reactions, making it crucial for both patients and caregivers to understand the nature of these allergies. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of food allergies, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook. By understanding food allergies, individuals can better manage their health and make informed decisions.
symptoms: Food allergy symptoms can vary widely among individuals and may include:
Skin Reactions: Hives, eczema, or swelling of the lips, face, or throat.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal cramps.
Respiratory Issues: Nasal congestion, sneezing, coughing, wheezing, or difficulty breathing.
Anaphylaxis: A severe, life-threatening reaction that can cause difficulty breathing, a rapid drop in blood pressure, and loss of consciousness.

diseases.name: Food Poisoning (Gastroenteritis)
diseases.description: Food poisoning (acute gastroenteritis) is illness caused by eating or drinking contaminated food or water. It often leads to diarrhea and vomiting.
symptoms: Diarrhea
Stomach cramps
Nausea
Vomiting
Fever

diseases.name: Food Poisoning - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Food poisoning, also called foodborne illness, is illness caused by eating contaminated food . Infectious organisms — including bacteria, viruses and parasites — or their toxins are the most common causes of food poisoning. Infectious organisms or their toxins can contaminate food at any point of processing or production.
symptoms: Depending on the cause of the illness, the symptoms may differ. The following are some of the most common signs and symptoms of food poisoning:
Stomach cramps
Diarrhoea
Nausea
Vomiting
A decrease in appetite
A low-grade fever
Weakness
Headache
A bout of diarrhoea that lasts more than three days
A temperature of more than 102°F (38.9°C)
Having trouble seeing or speaking
Dry mouth, little to no pee, and trouble keeping fluids down are all indicators of severe dehydration .
Bloody urine

diseases.name: Foot Drop - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Foot drop, also known as drop foot, is a condition characterized by difficulty in lifting the front part of the foot. This can lead to dragging the foot while walking, which may increase the risk of falls and injuries. Understanding foot drop is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for caregivers and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of foot drop, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Foot drop presents with several symptoms, which can vary in severity:
Difficulty Lifting the Foot: The most prominent symptom is the inability to lift the front part of the foot, leading to a dragging motion while walking.
Steppage Gait: Individuals may adopt a steppage gait, where they lift their knee higher than normal to avoid dragging the foot.
Numbness or Tingling: Some may experience numbness or tingling in the foot or lower leg.
Weakness in the Ankle and Foot Muscles: There may be noticeable weakness in the muscles that control foot movement.

diseases.name: Foot Pain and Numbness Could Be Signs of Diabetic Neuropathy
diseases.description: The human nervous system consists of two parts – the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system. The peripheral nervous system transmits messages between the central nervous system (the brain and spinal cord) and the rest of your body. These nerves regulate a large variety of functions throughout the body, such as perception of stimuli (sensory nerves), involuntary organ activity (autonomic nerves) and voluntary muscle movement (motor nerves). Neuropathy, often referred as Peripheral Neuropathy , is a condition that occurs when peripheral nerves become disrupted or damaged.

diseases.name: Foot Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Foot tendonitis is a common yet often overlooked condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. It refers to the inflammation of the tendons in the foot, which are the fibrous tissues connecting muscles to bones. Tendonitis can lead to pain, swelling, and reduced mobility, making everyday activities challenging. Understanding foot tendonitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their normal routines without discomfort.
symptoms: Pain: A sharp or aching pain in the affected area, often worsening with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation around the tendon, leading to visible swelling.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion, particularly in the morning or after periods of inactivity.
Tenderness: Sensitivity to touch in the affected area.
Crepitus: A grating sensation or sound when moving the tendon.

diseases.name: Foraminal Stenosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Foraminal stenosis is a medical condition that affects the spinal column, specifically the foramina—small openings through which spinal nerves exit the vertebral column. This narrowing can lead to significant discomfort and neurological issues, making it a condition of considerable importance. Understanding foraminal stenosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can impact an individual's quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding foraminal stenosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of foraminal stenosis can vary depending on the location and severity of the narrowing. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Localized pain in the neck or lower back, which may radiate to the arms or legs.
Numbness or Tingling: A sensation of pins and needles in the extremities, often associated with nerve compression.
Weakness: Muscle weakness in the arms or legs, making it difficult to perform daily activities.
Loss of Coordination: Difficulty with balance and coordination, particularly in the lower extremities.

diseases.name: Fordyce Spots - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fordyce spots are small, painless, pale bumps that can appear on the lips, inside the cheeks, and on the genitalia. While they are a common occurrence and generally harmless, many people may find them concerning or confusing. Understanding what Fordyce spots are, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options can help demystify this condition and alleviate any worries. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Fordyce spots, ensuring that readers have access to accurate and easy-to-understand information.
symptoms: Fordyce spots are typically asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause pain or discomfort. The most common characteristics include:
Small, painless bumps
Yellowish or white color
Size ranging from 1 to 3 millimeters
Occurrence on the lips, inner cheeks, or genital area

diseases.name: Fournier's Gangrene - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Fournier’s gangrene is a fast progressing, tissue-destroying infection on the genitals and nearby region. It is a medical emergency that can be fatal without immediate treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of an advanced infection of the Fournier’s gangrene are:
Greying or blackening of the skin
Foul odor from the infection site
Rapid heartbeat
High fever
Swelling in the affected area
Though Fournier’s gangrene is rare, it is required to treat the infection immediately to avoid fatality, multiple organ failure and amputation.

diseases.name: Fractures (Bone Fractures)
diseases.description: A bone fracture is a break in the continuity of a bone. Fractures can range from a thin crack to a complete break, and may be caused by high-force impact, stress, or weakening of the bone by conditions such as osteoporosis or cancer. They can occur in any bone in the body and are one of the most common musculoskeletal injuries.
symptoms: Sudden onset pain at the time of injury
Swelling and bruising
Deformity of the affected limb
Tenderness
Inability to use the affected area
Numbness or tingling (if nerves affected)

diseases.name: Fragile X Syndrome : Periodontitis - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Fragile X syndrome is an inherited condition that causes intellectual disability.
symptoms: There are certain signs and symptoms that are typical in those afflicted with Fragile X syndrome: 1. Physical characteristics – These include a long face, large ears, high arched palate, highly flexible joints (especially fingers), low muscle tone and enlarged testes at puberty (macro-orchidism). 2. Medical conditions – Serious health conditions that occur as a consequence of Fragile X syndrome are hernia , , visual defects , seizures , recurrent ear infections and a heart murmur (abnormal sound heard by a physician using a stethoscope) due to weak connective tissues in multiple organ systems in the body . In adult life some men develop hand tremors and difficulty in walking due to lack of balance. Some women may develop premature ovarian failure or POF in which their ovaries stop functioning before 40 years of age. This means getting pregnant may be a challenge unless the problem is treated. Early menopause leads to its share of problems like dry skin and osteoporosis due to lack of oestrogen secreted by the ovaries. 3. Speech and language – This may range from one end of the spectrum to another but men are more severely affected than women. Women are able to read and write without difficulty and can also follow instructions. Men however have trouble with pronunciation, reading and understanding simple instructions and giving meaningful responses in a discussion. They also have difficulty in altering pitch, tone and loudness; some may stutter and others may repeatedly ask the same question. In the case of children, they may talk much later than their peers and some may not ever be able to talk. 4. Intelligence – Most people suffering from FXS have IQs ranging from mild to moderate. They have an inability to think, reason and learn due to limited intellectual capacity. They may have anxiety , attention disorders and learning problems whereas they are generally good at remembering pictures and visual patterns. Females have almost normal cognitive development , thus showing that both sexes have different strengths and weaknesses making a thorough evaluation an absolute necessity. Problem areas include organising information, solving problems and thinking about abstract ideas. Children with FXS are categorized as special children and can often do well academically with special coaching. Adults can usually hold down simple jobs. 5. Sensory – Our five senses are that of sight, smell, taste, touch and hearing. People with FXS have sensory overload to even minor sounds for example, a dog barking is enough to upset them. They do not like to change their locations. They are very sensitive to textures of clothes they are wearing. They shy away from even a light touch.

diseases.name: Fregoli Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Fregoli Syndrome is a rare and intriguing psychological condition that can significantly impact an individual's perception of reality. Named after the Italian actor Leopoldo Fregoli, who was known for his ability to impersonate various characters, this syndrome is characterized by a person's belief that different people are, in fact, a single person who is changing their appearance or disguising themselves. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Fregoli Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Fregoli Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Belief in Disguise: The primary symptom is the firm belief that different people are the same individual in disguise.
Paranoia: Individuals may feel that they are being followed or watched by the person they believe is disguising themselves.
Confusion: There may be significant confusion regarding the identities of people in their environment.
Anxiety and Distress: The delusional beliefs can lead to heightened anxiety and emotional distress.

diseases.name: Freys Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Frey's Syndrome, also known as gustatory sweating, is a rare but significant condition that affects the autonomic nervous system, leading to unusual sweating patterns. This syndrome is particularly notable because it can occur after certain surgical procedures or injuries, especially those involving the parotid gland. Understanding Frey's Syndrome is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can impact quality of life and may require specific management strategies.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of Frey's Syndrome is gustatory sweating, which can manifest as:
Sweating on the Cheeks: Increased perspiration on one or both sides of the face, particularly during meals.
Flushing: Redness of the skin in the affected area.
Warm Sensation: A feeling of warmth in the facial region when eating.
Tearing: Some individuals may also experience increased tearing or salivation.

diseases.name: Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia (FFA) is a form of hair loss that primarily affects the frontal hairline and is characterized by a progressive recession of the hairline, often accompanied by other symptoms. This condition has gained attention in recent years due to its increasing prevalence, particularly among postmenopausal women. Understanding FFA is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can significantly impact the quality of life for individuals experiencing this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia can vary from person to person, but common signs include:
Receding Hairline: The most noticeable symptom is the gradual recession of the frontal hairline, which may extend to the temples.
Scalp Itching or Burning: Some individuals report discomfort, including itching or a burning sensation in the affected areas.
Loss of Eyebrows and Body Hair: In some cases, FFA can lead to the loss of eyebrows and other body hair.
Scarring: The affected areas may show signs of scarring, which can be observed during a physical examination.

diseases.name: Frostbite
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Signs of frostbite include:
Cold skin and a itchiness
Numbness
Red, white, bluish-white or grayish-yellow skin
Stiff or waxy looking skin
Ungainliness because of joint and muscle inflexibility
Blisters after rewarming, in extreme cases
Because of skin numbness, one may not realize it is a frostbite until somebody else spots it. The stages of frostbite are:

Frostnip: Frostnip doesn’t damage the skin permanently but causes the skin to turn pale or red and extremely cold. Constant contact leads to prickling and numbness in the area affected. As the skin warms, a feeling of pain and tingling occurs.

Superficial Frostbite: The skin may begin to feel warm. If frostbite is treated with rewarming at this phase, the surface of your skin may appear spotty, blue or purple. And you may observe stinging, burning and inflammation. A fluid filled blister may emerge 24- 36 hours after rewarming the skin

Deep Frostbite: As the frostbite progresses, it becomes extremely severe affecting all the layers of the skin, including the underlying tissues. Joints or muscles don’t function at this stage and large blisters appear 24-48 hours after rewarming the skin. The affected area turns black and solid as the tissues die.

diseases.name: Frozen Shoulder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatement
diseases.description: Frozen shoulder or ‘adhesive capsulitis’ is a very common ailment characterized by a stiff painful shoulder joint. If you have a frozen shoulder , your arm and shoulder movement is significantly limited. You would typically find the shoulder pain getting worse and then finally see improvement. This condition is also referred to as ‘periarthritis” or simply as a “painful stiff shoulder”.
symptoms: Since it takes a relatively long period for a frozen shoulder to develop, peak, and begin healing, the ailment can be divided into three phases – the freezing stage, the frozen stage, and the thawing stage. Each of these phases has its own distinct symptoms and last for a few months each.

Freezing Stage : Your shoulder would begin to stiffen progressively. Moving your shoulder will cause a sharp pain. The shoulder pain is typically worse at night and may cause difficulty in sleeping. This phase usually spans around 2 to 9 months.
Frozen Stage: Your shoulder would stiffen further until it is virtually immobilized. The shoulder pain would start dying down. This intermediate phase usually lasts around 4 to 12 months.
Thawing Stage : The pain improves considerably. The mobility of the arm is restored gradually during this phase. This recovery phase could last anywhere between 5 to 24 months.

diseases.name: Fructose Intolerance - Types, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment and Management
diseases.description: Have you ever experienced bloating, abdominal pain, or diarrhoea? It might be due to fructose intolerance. Like glucose, fructose is also a type of sugar. It also occurs naturally in some healthy food such as honey, fruits, and vegetables.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the type. Essential fructosuria does not develop any symptoms nor requires treatment. But the other two types can show the following signs:
Primary symptoms of fructose malabsorption include:
Bloating
Diarrhea
Gas
Nausea
Usually, the symptoms of hereditary fructose intolerance develop during infancy. Some common symptoms are:
Physical development delays
Jaundice
Hyperventilation
Dislike of sweets
Vomiting
Liver or kidney failure

diseases.name: Functional Dyspepsia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder that affects millions of people worldwide. Characterized by persistent or recurrent pain and discomfort in the upper abdomen, FD can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Despite its prevalence, many people remain unaware of what functional dyspepsia is, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of functional dyspepsia, helping readers understand this condition and its implications.
symptoms: Functional dyspepsia presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Upper Abdominal Pain: A burning or aching sensation in the stomach area.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Nausea: A sensation of queasiness or the urge to vomit.
Early Satiety: Feeling full after eating only a small amount of food.
Indigestion: Discomfort or difficulty in digesting food.

diseases.name: Fungal Skin Infection: Causes, Types, Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Fungal skin infections are common conditions caused by microscopic organisms known as fungi. These infections affect the skin, nails, and hair and thrive in warm, moist environments—making India’s humid climate a perfect breeding ground.
symptoms: Symptoms vary depending on the type and location of the infection, but common signs include:
Itchy, red, or scaly patches
Rashes that spread or worsen
Cracking, peeling, or discolored skin
Thickened or brittle nails
Burning or stinging sensation
Hair loss (in scalp infections)
Bad odor (especially in foot infections)
White patches in the mouth (in candidiasis)
In more severe cases, blisters or pus-filled sores may develop, especially if there is scratching or secondary bacterial infection.

diseases.name: Galactorrhea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Galactorrhea is a condition characterized by the unexpected production of breast milk in individuals who are not breastfeeding or pregnant. While it may seem like a benign issue, galactorrhea can be a symptom of underlying health problems that require medical attention. Understanding this condition is crucial for those affected, as it can impact emotional well-being and physical health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of galactorrhea, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of galactorrhea is the unexpected discharge of milk from the breasts. This discharge can vary in color, consistency, and amount. Other symptoms may include:
Breast tenderness or pain
Changes in menstrual cycle (irregular periods)
Headaches
Vision changes (if caused by a pituitary tumor)

diseases.name: Galactosemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Galactosemia is a rare genetic disorder that affects how the body processes galactose, a sugar found in milk and dairy products. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious health complications if not diagnosed and managed properly. Early detection and dietary management are crucial for individuals with galactosemia to prevent long-term health issues. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions about galactosemia.
symptoms: Symptoms of galactosemia can vary depending on the age of onset and the severity of the enzyme deficiency. Common symptoms include:
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to liver dysfunction.
Vomiting: Frequent vomiting, especially after feeding.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty in feeding or poor weight gain in infants.
Lethargy: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Irritability: Increased fussiness or irritability in infants.
Cataracts: Clouding of the lens of the eye, which can develop in some cases.
Developmental Delays: Delays in reaching developmental milestones.

diseases.name: Gall Bladder Stones
diseases.description: Diseases and Conditions

diseases.name: Gallbladder Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Gallbladder cancer is a rare but serious form of cancer that begins in the gallbladder, a small, pear-shaped organ located beneath the liver. The gallbladder’s job is to store bile, a digestive fluid made by the liver that helps break down fats.
symptoms: Early gallbladder cancer may not cause symptoms. When symptoms do appear, they often mimic other digestive conditions, making diagnosis difficult.
Yellowing of skin and eyes (jaundice)
Unexplained weight loss
Loss of appetite
Lumps in the abdomen
Dark urine and pale stools
Persistent itching
If you experience these symptoms, especially in combination with gallstones or chronic gallbladder issues, consult a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Gallbladder Polyps - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gallbladder polyps are growths that form on the inner lining of the gallbladder, a small organ located beneath the liver that plays a crucial role in digestion. While many gallbladder polyps are benign and asymptomatic, understanding their significance is essential for early detection and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of gallbladder polyps, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Most gallbladder polyps are asymptomatic and are often discovered incidentally during imaging studies for other conditions. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper right abdomen, especially after eating fatty meals.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur, particularly during episodes of gallbladder inflammation.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or bloating after meals.
Indigestion: Difficulty digesting fatty foods.

diseases.name: Gallstones
diseases.description: Gallstones are toughened deposits of digestive juices that can form in the gallbladder. Gallstones vary in size from as minute as a granule of sand to as huge as a golf ball. Some individuals develop just one gallstone, while others may develop several gallstones all at the same point in time.
symptoms: Gallstones may cause no symptoms. If a gallstone is found in a duct and leads to blockage, symptoms may include:
Sudden and swiftly growing pain in the upper right section of the abdomen
Sudden and rapidly increasing pain in the center of the abdomen
Back pain between the shoulder blades
Right shoulder ache
Gallstone pain may last more than a few minutes to many hours

diseases.name: Ganglioglioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ganglioglioma is a rare type of brain tumor that arises from a combination of nerve cells (neurons) and glial cells, which support and protect the neurons. This tumor is most commonly found in the brain, particularly in the temporal lobe, but can also occur in the spinal cord. Understanding ganglioglioma is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ganglioglioma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of ganglioglioma can vary widely depending on the tumor's size and location. Common symptoms include:
Seizures: The most frequent symptom, often presenting as focal seizures that may evolve into generalized seizures.
Headaches: Persistent or worsening headaches that may not respond to typical pain relief methods.
Cognitive Changes: Memory problems, difficulty concentrating, or changes in behavior.
Motor Weakness: Weakness or numbness in specific areas of the body, depending on the tumor's location.
Vision or Hearing Changes: Blurred vision, double vision, or hearing difficulties.

diseases.name: Ganglion Cysts
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The lumps that are formed as a result of ganglion cysts are characterised by the following:
Location: The places at which ganglion cysts are likely to develop are along the tendons or joints of the wrists or hands. They can also form in the ankles and feet and near other joints as well.
Pain: Ganglion cysts usually are painless. But if a cyst presses on a nerve, even if the cyst is too small to form a noticeable lump it can cause pain, tingling, numbness or muscle weakness.
Shape and size: The size of a cyst can fluctuate, often getting larger when the joint is used for repetitive motions.

diseases.name: Gangrene - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Risks and Prevention
diseases.description: Gangrene is a serious condition in which the blood supply from the circulatory system to certain parts of the tissue stops and the tissue eventually decays and dies. This often happens in the extremities (the parts farthest from the heart) like hands and legs (especially in the toes and fingers) . In very few cases, this can happen to internal organs like the gallbladder which is called internal gangrene. The part affected by it usually appears greenish-black in color.
symptoms: The symptoms of gangrene depend on the causes. Some of the common symptoms for all types of gangrene are:
Discoloration of skin – skin turns pale and cold
No feeling felt on the affected area – numbness
Infrequent pain felt on the affected area
Redness and swelling are seen on the skin around the affected area
When the gangrene is infected, the symptoms may include:
Chills
Persistent fever with high temperature
Dizziness
breathing issues
Rise in heartbeat
Bleeding and pus formation in the sores and blisters – often a discharge is seen
Discomfort or severe pain in the gangrenous area
Crackling feeling on the affected area – this happens in the case of gas gangrene
Discoloration of skin around the affected area (the color change may be from red to brown and to purple to black
Low blood pressure , mental confusion – when the gangrene is internal
Sudden shock

diseases.name: Gardner Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gardner Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that significantly impacts the lives of those affected. It is characterized by the presence of multiple benign tumors, particularly in the skin and gastrointestinal tract, as well as an increased risk of colorectal cancer. Understanding Gardner Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Gardner Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Colorectal Polyps: The hallmark of Gardner Syndrome is the development of numerous adenomatous polyps in the colon and rectum, which can lead to colorectal cancer if left untreated.
Skin Tumors: Patients may develop epidermoid cysts, fibromas, and lipomas on the skin.
Dental Abnormalities: Individuals may have extra teeth (supernumerary teeth) or impacted teeth.
Desmoid Tumors: These are benign but aggressive tumors that can occur in the abdominal wall or other soft tissues.
Ocular Lesions: Some patients may develop congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE), which can be detected during an eye examination.

diseases.name: Gas Gangrene - Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Gas gangrene is a deadly form of tissue death. It usually develops in case of deep, penetrating wounds.
symptoms: Symptoms in gas gangrene begin quickly:
Painful swelling. Skin turns pale to brownish red
Blisters develop and are filled with brown red fluid
Heaviness in affected extremity.
Increased heart rate
Fever
Sweating
Vesicle formation which combine into large blisters
Yellow colour of the skin

diseases.name: Gastric Cancer - Causes, Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Introduction
symptoms: The symptoms may appear different in every individual. In the initial stages, gastric cancer may cause the following symptoms:
Nausea
Heartburn
Indigestion
Feeling bloated after having a meal
Loss of appetite
As gastric cancer starts spreading, you may experience severe symptoms such as
Dark stools
Vomiting
Stomach pain
Swelling in the stomach
Unexplained weight loss
Yellowing of eyes or skin
Trouble swallowing
Having indigestion or heartburn may not always indicate gastric cancer. But if you experience these symptoms frequently, consult a doctor.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: Gastric Varices - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gastric varices are dilated veins located in the stomach that can develop as a result of increased pressure in the portal vein, a condition known as portal hypertension. These varices are significant because they can lead to serious complications, including life-threatening bleeding. Understanding gastric varices is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Gastric varices may not present symptoms until they become severe or rupture. Common symptoms include:
Vomiting Blood: This can appear as bright red blood or dark, coffee-ground-like material.
Black or Tarry Stools: This indicates digested blood and is a sign of internal bleeding.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen may occur.
Swelling in the Abdomen: This can be due to fluid accumulation (ascites).
Dizziness or Fainting: These symptoms may occur due to significant blood loss.

diseases.name: Gastritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment and Diet
diseases.description: Gastritis has become a common phenomenon among young as well as adults in India due to fact that our food contains high amounts of spices. Current lifestyle of working at odd hours, eating at odd hours like, midnight biryani lead to adverse effects on digestive system. Let’s know more about Gastritis, what are its main causes, symptoms and treatment options.
symptoms: Symptoms of gastritis vary from person to person. Severe gastritis may be present without any symptoms. Conversely, severe gastric symptoms may be present despite only minor changes in the stomach lining. However, some of the most common symptoms include
Pain or discomfort in the upper abdomen (the most common symptom)
Belching, which either doesn’t relieve pain or only relieves it briefly
Nausea and vomiting . Severity of vomiting depends on the extent of stomach inflammation.
Burning or gnawing feeling in the stomach between meals or at night
Chest pain or severe stomach pain
Bloody bowel movements or dark, very foul smelling stools

diseases.name: Gastroenteritis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Although it’s commonly called stomach flu, gastroenteritis isn’t the same as influenza. Real flu ( influenza ) affects only the respiratory system – the nose, throat and lungs. Gastroenteritis, on the other hand, attacks the intestines, causing signs and symptoms, such as:
Watery, usually non-bloody diarrhea – bloody diarrhea usually indicates more severe infection
Abdominal cramps and pain
Nausea, vomiting or both
Occasional muscle aches or headache
Low-grade fever

Depending on the cause, viral gastroenteritis symptoms may appear within one to three days after the patient is infected and can range from mild to severe. Symptoms usually last just a day or two, but occasionally they may persist as long as 10 days.

diseases.name: Gastroesophageal Junction Cancers - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: The gastroesophageal junction is where your food pipe (esophagus) meets your stomach. Cancer that starts here is called gastroesophageal junction cancer. It is less common than breast, lung, or colon cancer, but cases are rising worldwide. Because the junction connects two important organs, cancers here can behave like both esophageal and stomach cancers, making them more complex to treat.
symptoms: Early gastroesophageal junction cancer may not cause noticeable symptoms. As the disease progresses, symptoms become clearer.

diseases.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD): Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment and Diet
diseases.description: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease, commonly known as GERD, is a chronic digestive disorder where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus (the tube connecting the mouth and stomach). This backflow, known as acid reflux, irritates the lining of the esophagus and causes symptoms such as heartburn, chest discomfort, regurgitation, and a sour or bitter taste in the mouth.
symptoms: GERD presents with a variety of symptoms that may range from mild to severe. Recognizing these symptoms early is key to timely diagnosis and management.
Most common symptoms include:
Heartburn: A burning sensation in the chest, usually after meals or at night.
Regurgitation: Sour or bitter-tasting acid backing up into the throat or mouth.
Chest pain: Especially behind the breastbone, often mistaken for a heart attack.
Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia): A feeling of food getting stuck in the throat.
Sensation of a lump in the throat
Other associated symptoms:
Chronic cough
Hoarseness or sore throat
Bad breath
Nausea
Bloating
Asthma-like symptoms (wheezing, especially at night)
These symptoms may worsen when lying down or after heavy meals.

diseases.name: Gastrointestinal Bleeding - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GI bleeding) is a significant medical condition that can range from mild to life-threatening. It refers to any form of bleeding that occurs in the gastrointestinal tract, which includes the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine (colon), rectum, and anus. The significance of GI bleeding lies in its potential to indicate serious underlying health issues, such as ulcers, cancers, or vascular malformations. Understanding the causes, symptoms, and treatment options for gastrointestinal bleeding is crucial for timely intervention and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding can vary depending on the location and severity of the bleeding. Common symptoms include:
Hematemesis: Vomiting blood, which may appear bright red or have a "coffee ground" appearance.
Melena: Black, tarry stools indicating upper GI bleeding.
Hematochezia: Bright red blood in the stool, often associated with lower GI bleeding.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or sharp pain in the abdomen.
Weakness or Fatigue: Due to blood loss, individuals may feel weak or fatigued.
Dizziness or Fainting: Severe blood loss can lead to low blood pressure and fainting.

diseases.name: Gastrointestinal Fistula - Everything you Need to Know
diseases.description: Gastrointestinal fistula (GIF) is an abnormal opening in your stomach or intestines which causes gastric fluid to leak through the lining of your stomach or intestines. This could lead to infections when such fluids seep into your skin or other organs. This most commonly takes place after intra-abdominal surgery or in people with chronic digestive problems. The leaks from one part of the gastrointestinal tract to another are known as entero-enteral fistulas and the ones which connect the GI tract to the skin are known as entero-cutaneous fistulas. A fistula is an abnormal connection between two hollow spaces such as blood vessels, intestines, or other hollow organs. Fistulas are usually caused by injury or surgery, but they can also result from an infection or inflammation.
symptoms: When a person has GIF, digested food material cannot freely move through the body. Your symptoms will depend on whether you have an internal or external fistula. It also depends on whether the patient has developed a complicated condition known as sepsis. In this condition, the person’s body attacks itself, as a response to severe bacterial infection. The symptoms of external fistulas include:
Skin discharge
Abdominal pain
Fever
Increased white blood cell count
Painful bowel obstruction
Diarrhea
Blood stream infection
Dehydration
Rectal bleeding
Poor absorption of nutrients and weight loss
Worsening of the underlying disease

diseases.name: Gastroparesis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gastroparesis is a chronic condition that affects the normal movement of the muscles in the stomach, leading to delayed gastric emptying. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, as it interferes with the digestion process and can lead to various complications. Understanding gastroparesis is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can help alleviate symptoms and improve overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of gastroparesis can vary in severity and may include:
Nausea: A common symptom that can occur after eating.
Vomiting: This may include undigested food, especially if the stomach is unable to empty properly.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the stomach area can be frequent.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Loss of Appetite: Many individuals with gastroparesis may not feel hungry or may avoid eating due to discomfort.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can occur due to reduced food intake and malnutrition.

diseases.name: Gastropathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gastropathy is a term that encompasses a variety of conditions affecting the stomach's lining, leading to inflammation, irritation, and dysfunction. Understanding gastropathy is crucial as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and overall health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of gastropathy, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of gastropathy can vary widely depending on the underlying cause and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Often described as a burning sensation or discomfort in the upper abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Individuals may experience persistent nausea, which can lead to vomiting.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat can occur, often due to discomfort or pain.
Bloating and Gas: Many individuals report feelings of fullness or bloating after meals.
Indigestion: This may manifest as heartburn or a feeling of heaviness in the stomach.

diseases.name: Gastroschisis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gastroschisis is a congenital condition that affects newborns, characterized by a defect in the abdominal wall. This condition is significant not only because of its physical implications but also due to the emotional and psychological impact it can have on families. Understanding gastroschisis is crucial for expectant parents, healthcare providers, and the general public, as it raises awareness about congenital anomalies and the importance of prenatal care.
symptoms: The most apparent symptom of gastroschisis is the visible protrusion of the intestines and other organs from the abdominal cavity at birth. Other symptoms may include:
Abdominal Distension: The abdomen may appear swollen or distended.
Feeding Difficulties: Infants may struggle to feed due to the condition.
Vomiting: This may occur if the intestines are obstructed.
Signs of Infection: Redness, swelling, or discharge around the exposed organs may indicate infection.

diseases.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is a prevalent mental health condition characterized by excessive, uncontrollable worry about various aspects of life. This disorder can significantly impact daily functioning, relationships, and overall quality of life. Understanding GAD is crucial, as it affects millions of individuals worldwide, yet it often goes unrecognized and untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of GAD, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more, to empower individuals with knowledge and encourage those affected to seek help.
symptoms: Individuals with GAD may experience a range of symptoms, which can vary in intensity. Common symptoms include:
Excessive Worry: Persistent worry about various aspects of life, often disproportionate to the actual situation.
Restlessness: A feeling of being on edge or unable to relax.
Fatigue: Chronic tiredness, even after adequate rest.
Difficulty Concentrating: Trouble focusing or mind going blank.
Irritability: Increased irritability or frustration.
Muscle Tension: Physical tension in the muscles, leading to discomfort or pain.
Sleep Disturbances: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or experiencing restless sleep.

diseases.name: Genital Herpes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Genital herpes is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). It is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its potential impact on physical and emotional health. Understanding genital herpes is crucial for prevention, management, and reducing stigma associated with the condition. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of genital herpes, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of genital herpes can vary widely among individuals. Some may experience severe symptoms, while others may have mild or no symptoms at all. Common symptoms include:
Painful blisters or sores: These typically appear on the genitals, buttocks, or thighs and can be painful and itchy.
Flu-like symptoms: Some individuals may experience fever, body aches, and swollen lymph nodes during the initial outbreak.
Itching or burning: Many people report itching or a burning sensation in the genital area before sores appear.
Discharge: Some may notice an unusual discharge from the genital area.

diseases.name: Genital Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Genital psoriasis is a specific form of psoriasis that affects the genital area, including the vulva, penis, and surrounding skin. This condition can be particularly distressing due to its sensitive location and the discomfort it can cause. Understanding genital psoriasis is crucial not only for those who suffer from it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of genital psoriasis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of genital psoriasis can vary but typically include:
Red, inflamed patches: These may appear on the vulva, penis, or surrounding areas.
Scaling: The affected skin may have silvery-white scales, which can be itchy or painful.
Cracking and bleeding: In severe cases, the skin may crack, leading to bleeding and increased discomfort.
Discomfort during sexual activity: The condition can cause pain or discomfort during intercourse.

diseases.name: Genital Ulcers - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Genital ulcers are painful sores that develop in the genital area, which includes the external reproductive organs, the perineum, and the inner thighs. These ulcers can be a source of significant discomfort and distress, impacting an individual's quality of life. Understanding genital ulcers is crucial not only for those who experience them but also for healthcare providers who aim to offer effective treatment and support. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of genital ulcers, providing a thorough overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of genital ulcers can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Painful Sores: Ulcers may be painful, making it uncomfortable to sit or engage in sexual activity.
Itching or Burning: Many individuals experience itching or a burning sensation in the affected area.
Swelling: The surrounding tissue may become swollen and inflamed.
Discharge: Some ulcers may produce a discharge, which can be clear, cloudy, or bloody.

diseases.name: Genital Warts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Genital warts are a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by certain strains of the human papillomavirus (HPV). They can affect both men and women, leading to physical discomfort and emotional distress. Understanding genital warts is crucial not only for those affected but also for the general public, as awareness can help reduce stigma and promote preventive measures. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of genital warts, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Genital warts may not always cause noticeable symptoms, but when they do, they can include:
Small, flesh-colored or gray growths in the genital area
Itching or discomfort in the affected area
Bleeding during intercourse
Changes in the appearance of warts over time

diseases.name: Geographic Tongue - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Geographic tongue, also known as benign migratory glossitis, is a common condition that affects the surface of the tongue, leading to a distinctive appearance and various symptoms. While it is generally harmless, its presence can cause discomfort and concern for those affected. Understanding geographic tongue is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, allowing individuals to manage the condition effectively.
symptoms: Geographic tongue is characterized by several distinct symptoms:
Irregular Patches: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of smooth, red patches on the tongue, often surrounded by a white or yellow border.
Sensitivity: Many individuals report increased sensitivity in the affected areas, particularly when consuming spicy, acidic, or hot foods.
Burning Sensation: Some people may experience a burning or tingling sensation on the tongue, which can be uncomfortable.
Changes Over Time: The patches can change in size and location, often appearing to "migrate" across the tongue.

diseases.name: Geriatric Oncology at Apollo Cancer Centre
diseases.description: As life expectancy increases, a growing number of people diagnosed with cancer are older adults. While cancer treatment has advanced rapidly, older patients often face unique challenges that go beyond the tumour alone. Geriatric Oncology bridges this gap - integrating the science of ageing with modern cancer care to deliver treatment that is safe, individualised, and meaningful.

diseases.name: Gestational Hypertension - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gestational hypertension is a condition that affects pregnant women, characterized by high blood pressure that develops after the 20th week of pregnancy. It is significant because it can lead to serious complications for both the mother and the baby if not properly managed. Understanding gestational hypertension is crucial for expectant mothers, healthcare providers, and families, as it can impact pregnancy outcomes and overall health.
symptoms: Gestational hypertension may not always present noticeable symptoms, but some common signs include:
Elevated blood pressure: Regular monitoring may reveal high readings.
Swelling: Sudden swelling in the hands, feet, or face.
Headaches: Persistent or severe headaches that do not respond to usual pain relief.
Vision changes: Blurred vision or seeing spots.
Nausea or vomiting: Especially if it is sudden and severe.

diseases.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease (GTD) is a rare condition that starts in pregnancy when the cells that normally form the placenta (the organ that nourishes a baby) grow in an abnormal way. Some forms are harmless and easily treated, while others can behave like cancer and need chemotherapy. The good news: with modern treatment, almost all women are cured and can go on to have healthy pregnancies. This comprehensive article explains what GTD is, how it's diagnosed, modern treatment options, recovery and follow‑up, and support for international patients at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms vary by type and stage. Some are similar to normal pregnancy symptoms, which is why evaluation is important.
Common early signs:
Vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy (often irregular or heavier than expected)
Larger-than-expected uterine size for gestational age (complete mole)
Severe nausea/vomiting (hyperemesis gravidarum)
Very high pregnancy hormone (hCG) levels for gestational age
Absence of fetal heartbeat when expected (complete mole)
Sometimes, women may pass small, grape-like clumps of tissue from the vagina. This does not happen in every case but is a classic sign doctors look for.
Possible later or advanced symptoms:
Pelvic pain or pressure
Anemia from bleeding, lightheadedness
Shortness of breath or cough if GTN has spread to other organs like the lungs
Headaches or neurologic symptoms if spread to other organs like the brain (rare)
For PSTT/ETT, bleeding can be subtle and occur months to years after any pregnancy
Any abnormal bleeding during or after pregnancy warrants prompt evaluation.

diseases.name: GI Cancer Treatment in Hyderabad
diseases.description: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancer is a collective term for cancers that affect the digestive system, including the oesophagus, stomach, liver, pancreas, gallbladder, small intestine, colon, and rectum. GI cancers rank among the most frequently diagnosed cancers worldwide and are a leading cause of cancer-related deaths each year. ( ref. )
symptoms: GI cancer symptoms vary depending on the location and stage of the cancer. Many early-stage GI cancers cause no symptoms at all, which is why screening is so important. When symptoms do appear, they may include:
Persistent abdominal pain or discomfort: Ongoing pain, cramping, or bloating that does not resolve with usual treatments
Unexplained weight loss: Losing weight without changes in diet or exercise, often accompanied by fatigue or weakness
Changes in bowel habits: Persistent constipation, diarrhoea, narrowing of stool, or a feeling of incomplete evacuation lasting more than a few weeks
Blood in stool or rectal bleeding: Bright red blood or dark, tarry stools may indicate colorectal or stomach cancer
Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia): Food feeling stuck in the throat or chest, or pain while swallowing common in oesophageal cancer
Persistent indigestion or heartburn: Chronic acid reflux or discomfort that does not respond to medication
Loss of appetite, nausea, or vomiting: Especially if accompanied by unintended weight loss or vomiting blood
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, and pale stools often associated with liver, gallbladder, or pancreatic cancers
Early satiety: Feeling full after eating only a small amount of food, which may indicate stomach cancer

These symptoms are often mistaken for common digestive issues and dismissed. However, if any of these signs persist for more than two weeks, worsen over time, or occur alongside other warning signs, consult a gastroenterologist or oncologist without delay. Early evaluation can make a critical difference in outcomes.

diseases.name: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)
diseases.description: Giant cell arteritis is an inflammation of the blood vessels, especially the arteries that supply the head. It most often causes headaches, jaw pain, and vision problems. Immediate treatment is needed to prevent blindness. Giant cell arteritis often occurs with polymyalgia rheumatica. It primarily affects people over 50.
symptoms: Persistent, severe headache usually in the temple area
Scalp tenderness
Jaw pain when chewing (jaw claudication)
Vision problems (double vision or vision loss)
Fever
Fatigue
Unintended weight loss
Shoulder and hip pain (if also PMR)

diseases.name: Giant Cell Tumors - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Giant Cell Tumors (GCTs) are a type of bone tumor that primarily affects young adults, often occurring around the knee joint. These tumors are characterized by the presence of multinucleated giant cells and can lead to significant morbidity if not diagnosed and treated appropriately. Understanding GCTs is crucial for early detection and effective management, as they can cause pain, swelling, and even joint dysfunction. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Giant Cell Tumors, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Pain: The most common symptom, often worsening with activity.
Swelling: Localized swelling around the affected bone.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the joint near the tumor.
Weakness: Muscle weakness in the affected area due to pain or disuse.

diseases.name: Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis (GPC) is a condition that affects the conjunctiva, the thin membrane covering the white part of the eye and the inner surface of the eyelids. This condition is characterized by the formation of large bumps, or papillae, on the inner eyelids, leading to discomfort and visual disturbances. GPC is particularly significant because it can impact individuals who wear contact lenses, potentially leading to complications that may affect vision. Understanding GPC is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that those affected can maintain their eye health and quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis can vary in severity and may include:
Itching: A persistent itch in the eyes is one of the hallmark symptoms.
Redness: The conjunctiva may appear red and inflamed.
Discharge: A watery or mucous discharge may be present, especially upon waking.
Swelling: The eyelids may become swollen due to inflammation.
Foreign Body Sensation: Many individuals report feeling as though there is something in their eye.

diseases.name: Giardiasis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms can vary a lot amongst those infected by Giardiasis. While some people do not display any symptoms, they may end up releasing cysts through stool and thereby pass the disease to others. Other people may develop chronic or diarrheal sickness within one to two weeks of contracting the infection. Small children are particularly susceptible to this infection. Some common symptoms are:
Diarrhoea with large amount of watery stool initially, gradually turning greasy and foul smelling
Weight and appetite loss
Failure to absorb fat, digest milk and vitamins (A & B)
Abdominal cramps, vomiting
Headaches & Nausea
Constipation & Gas
Small children are particularly susceptible to this infection as severe cases of Giardiasis infection can lead to slower physical and brain development and can lead to malnutrition.

diseases.name: Gigantism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gigantism is a rare but significant medical condition characterized by excessive growth and height due to an overproduction of growth hormone. This condition typically arises during childhood or adolescence, before the growth plates in the bones close. Understanding gigantism is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers and the general public, as early diagnosis and intervention can lead to better outcomes. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of gigantism, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of gigantism can vary but often include:
Excessive Height: Individuals may grow significantly taller than their peers.
Large Hands and Feet: Proportional enlargement of extremities is common.
Facial Changes: Features may become coarser, with a prominent jaw and enlarged nose.
Joint Pain: Increased growth can lead to discomfort in joints.
Delayed Puberty: Hormonal imbalances may affect sexual development.

diseases.name: Gigantomastia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gigantomastia, a rare medical condition characterized by excessive breast tissue growth, can significantly impact a person's physical and emotional well-being. While it is not commonly discussed, understanding gigantomastia is crucial for those affected and their healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of gigantomastia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of gigantomastia can vary in severity and may include:
Excessive Breast Size: Noticeable enlargement of one or both breasts.
Physical Discomfort: Pain or discomfort in the back, neck, or shoulders due to the weight of enlarged breasts.
Skin Changes: Stretch marks, skin irritation, or rashes under the breasts.
Emotional Distress: Anxiety, depression, or social withdrawal due to body image issues.

diseases.name: Gilberts Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gilbert's Syndrome is a common, benign liver condition that affects the way bilirubin is processed in the body. While it is often overlooked and considered a minor health issue, understanding Gilbert's Syndrome is significant for those diagnosed with it, as well as for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Gilbert's Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Gilbert's Syndrome is jaundice, which may present as:
Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes
Dark urine
Pale stools
Other symptoms may include:
Fatigue
Abdominal discomfort
Nausea

diseases.name: Gingivitis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: As mentioned earlier, in many cases, there might not be symptoms obvious enough to make one aware that he/she has gingivitis. However, the common signs and symptoms of gingivitis include
Swollen gums
Receding gums
Soft and puffy gums
Bad breath
Tender gums on occasion
Bleeding gums, especially when you brush
Change in the colour of the gums from pink to red
If one has any/some/all of the above symptoms, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Gingivostomatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gingivostomatitis is a medical condition that affects the oral cavity, characterized by inflammation of the gums (gingiva) and the mucous membranes of the mouth (stomatitis). This condition can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding gingivostomatitis is crucial for early detection and effective management, especially since it can affect individuals of all ages, particularly children. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of gingivostomatitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of gingivostomatitis can vary in severity but typically include:
Swollen and red gums: Inflammation is often the first noticeable sign.
Painful sores or ulcers: These can develop on the gums, tongue, and inner cheeks, making eating and drinking painful.
Bad breath: Foul-smelling breath may occur due to the presence of sores and bacteria.
Difficulty swallowing: Pain and discomfort can lead to challenges in swallowing food and liquids.
Fever: In cases of viral infection, a mild fever may accompany the oral symptoms.
Irritability: Particularly in children, discomfort can lead to increased fussiness and irritability.

diseases.name: GIST - Is it a Cancer?
diseases.description: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GISTs) are tumours of the variety known as soft tissue sarcomas, arising from the cells of the autonomous nervous system in walls of the gastrointestinal tract (GI tract. Most GISTs do not show any symptoms for a long time and are usually small in size. In rare cases, the tumors grow rapidly and may require surgery. It is common in people in the age group of 50-70 to develop GISTs.
symptoms: Symptoms and signs of GISTs may show up completely differently in every individual. The symptoms will occur depending on the size and location of the GIST in your stomach. Here are some of the possible symptoms: ● Nausea ● Vomiting ● Weight loss ● Difficulty swallowing ● Anemia ● Loss of appetite ● Abdominal pain ● Blood in stool The anemia is usually caused by the tumor that slowly starts to bleed in your abdomen. Sometimes, you may also feel the growth in your stomach.

diseases.name: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia (GT) is a rare inherited bleeding disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot properly. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the quality of life for those affected but also due to the challenges it presents in diagnosis and management. Understanding Glanzmann Thrombasthenia is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and effective treatment.
symptoms: Individuals with Glanzmann Thrombasthenia may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Easy Bruising: Frequent bruising with minimal or no trauma.
Prolonged Bleeding: Extended bleeding from cuts or injuries.
Nosebleeds: Frequent or spontaneous nosebleeds.
Gum Bleeding: Bleeding gums, especially during dental hygiene.
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Women may experience menorrhagia (heavy menstrual periods).
Joint Bleeding: Bleeding into joints, leading to pain and swelling.

diseases.name: Glaucoma: Symptoms, Causes, Types, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Medically reviewed by the Apollo Ophthalmology Team.
symptoms: One of the most challenging aspects of glaucoma is that it often develops without noticeable symptoms in its early stages. Many people do not experience warning signs until the disease has already caused significant damage to vision. As glaucoma progresses, symptoms may begin to appear, and these can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition.
Understanding the signs of glaucoma can help in recognizing the disease earlier and seeking timely care.
As glaucoma advances, individuals may experience one or more of the following glaucoma signs and symptoms:
Gradual loss of side (peripheral) vision
Patchy blind spots in side or central vision, often affecting both eyes
Difficulty seeing in low-light conditions
Blurred or hazy vision
Seeing halos around lights
Frequent headaches
Eye pain or redness
Sudden vision changes in severe cases
Open-angle glaucoma is the most common form of the disease and usually progresses slowly. Symptoms often go unnoticed until later stages, when vision loss becomes more apparent.
Typical glaucoma symptoms associated with open-angle glaucoma include:
Gradual loss of peripheral vision
Tunnel vision in advanced stages
Patchy blind spots in side or central vision
Acute angle-closure glaucoma is a medical emergency and causes sudden, severe symptoms that require immediate attention.
These signs of glaucoma may include:
Severe headache
Intense eye pain
Redness of the eye
Blurred vision
Nausea and vomiting

The most common forms of glaucoma are progressive and painless. But in the emergency situation called sudden angle closure glaucoma, severe eye pain, headache, nausea, vomiting, blurred vision, and the sensation of seeing halos around lights are felt.

diseases.name: Glioblastoma: Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Glioblastoma is a rare and aggressive cancer of the brain or spinal cord. It is an aggressive form of cancer with no cure available. However, with various treatments, you can slow the progression and manage the symptoms better. Glioblastoma can occur at any age, but it is often noticed among older adults.
symptoms: As glioblastoma is aggressive and fast-growing, it puts immense pressure on your brain resulting in:
Intense and constant headaches
Seizures
Vomiting
Issues in cognitive ability
Mood and personality changes
Vision problems, such as double or blurred vision
Speech problems
Loss of appetite
Lack of coordination and muscle weakness
Sensory changes, such as increased numbness or tingling

diseases.name: Glioma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Gliomas are tumors that start in the brain or spinal cord in cells called glial cells. They can range from slow-growing (low-grade, sometimes non-cancerous) to fast-growing and aggressive (high-grade, cancerous). Gliomas account for about 25% of all brain tumors and nearly 80% of malignant brain tumors in adults.
symptoms: The symptoms of glioma depend on the size, type, and location of the tumor. They may appear slowly or suddenly.
Early symptoms may include:
Persistent headaches (especially in the morning)
Seizures
Nausea and vomiting
Fatigue or weakness
Advanced symptoms may include:
Difficulty speaking or understanding speech
Changes in vision or hearing
Memory problems
Trouble with balance or coordination
Personality or behavioral changes
If you experience persistent headaches or neurological symptoms, it is important to consult a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Glomerular Diseases - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glomerular diseases are a group of disorders that affect the glomeruli, the tiny filtering units in the kidneys. These diseases can lead to significant health issues, including kidney failure, if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding glomerular diseases is crucial, as they can impact overall health and quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of glomerular diseases, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of glomerular diseases can vary widely depending on the specific condition and its severity. Common symptoms include:
Swelling (Edema): Often seen in the face, hands, feet, and abdomen due to fluid retention.
Foamy Urine: Indicates the presence of excess protein in the urine.
Blood in Urine (Hematuria): May appear as pink, red, or cola-colored urine.
High Blood Pressure: Often a result of kidney dysfunction.
Fatigue: General tiredness due to the body’s inability to filter waste effectively.

diseases.name: Glossitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glossitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the tongue, which can lead to changes in its color, texture, and size. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, affecting their ability to eat, speak, and maintain oral hygiene. Understanding glossitis is crucial not only for those who experience its symptoms but also for healthcare providers who may encounter it in their practice. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of glossitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of glossitis can vary widely but often include:
Swelling: The tongue may appear enlarged and swollen.
Color Changes: The tongue may become redder than usual or develop a pale appearance.
Texture Changes: The surface of the tongue may become smooth or develop bumps.
Pain or Discomfort: Individuals may experience pain, tenderness, or a burning sensation on the tongue.
Difficulty Eating or Speaking: Swelling and discomfort can make it challenging to eat or speak comfortably.

diseases.name: Glucagonoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glucagonoma is a rare type of neuroendocrine tumor that arises from the alpha cells of the pancreas, which are responsible for producing glucagon, a hormone that plays a crucial role in glucose metabolism. This condition is significant not only due to its rarity but also because it can lead to serious health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding glucagonoma is essential for both patients and healthcare providers, as early detection and management can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of glucagonoma can vary widely among individuals, but some of the most common include:
Hyperglycemia: Elevated blood sugar levels can lead to symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss is often observed due to the body's inability to utilize glucose effectively.
Skin Changes: A characteristic rash known as necrolytic migratory erythema may develop, presenting as red, blistering lesions that can be itchy and painful.
Diarrhea: Some patients may experience chronic diarrhea, which can contribute to weight loss and dehydration.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the abdominal area may occur, often related to the tumor's size or location.

diseases.name: Glue Ear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glue ear, medically known as otitis media with effusion (OME), is a common condition that affects the middle ear, particularly in children. It occurs when fluid accumulates behind the eardrum without any signs of acute infection. While glue ear is often temporary and resolves on its own, it can lead to significant hearing loss and developmental delays if not addressed. Understanding glue ear is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and management.
symptoms: Hearing Loss: The most significant symptom, often described as muffled or distant sounds.
Ear Fullness or Pressure: A sensation of fullness in the ear.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing sounds in the ear.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance due to impaired hearing.
Delayed Speech Development: In children, glue ear can lead to delays in speech and language skills.

diseases.name: Glycosuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Glycosuria is a medical condition characterized by the presence of glucose in the urine. While it may seem like a minor issue, glycosuria can be a significant indicator of underlying health problems, particularly diabetes mellitus. Understanding glycosuria is essential for early detection and management of potential complications. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of glycosuria, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: Glycosuria itself may not present noticeable symptoms. However, it can be associated with symptoms of underlying conditions, particularly diabetes. Common symptoms include:
Increased Thirst: Excess glucose in the blood can lead to dehydration, causing increased thirst.
Frequent Urination: The kidneys excrete more urine to eliminate excess glucose, leading to increased urination.
