Fatigue: High blood sugar levels can cause fatigue and weakness.
Blurred Vision: Fluctuating blood sugar levels can affect vision.

diseases.name: Gm1 Gangliosidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gm1 Gangliosidosis is a rare genetic disorder that affects the nervous system and is classified as a type of lysosomal storage disease. This condition is significant not only because of its profound impact on affected individuals and their families but also due to the challenges it presents in terms of diagnosis, management, and treatment. Understanding Gm1 Gangliosidosis is crucial for early detection and intervention, which can significantly influence the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Gm1 Gangliosidosis can vary significantly depending on the age of onset and the severity of the enzyme deficiency. Common symptoms include:
Infantile Form: Developmental delays Loss of motor skills Muscle weakness Seizures Vision and hearing loss Enlarged liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly) Cherry-red spot in the eye
Developmental delays
Loss of motor skills
Muscle weakness
Seizures
Vision and hearing loss
Enlarged liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly)
Cherry-red spot in the eye
Late-Infantile Form: Similar to the infantile form but may present with more pronounced neurological decline.
Similar to the infantile form but may present with more pronounced neurological decline.
Adult-Onset Form: Cognitive decline Movement disorders Psychiatric symptoms
Cognitive decline
Movement disorders
Psychiatric symptoms

diseases.name: Goiter (Enlarged Thyroid): Types, Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Goiter is a condition of the thyroid gland, a butterfly-shaped gland present below Adam’s apple. In goiter, the thyroid gland enlarges for numerous reasons and is usually painless. However, in certain rare cases, it can lead to difficulty in swallowing and breathing.
symptoms: The position or size of a goiter can obstruct the voice box and airway. Symptoms may include:
Cough ,
Difficulty breathing with exertion
Difficulty swallowing
Snoring
Hoarseness
Swelling of neck vein
Swollen neck base
Feeling dizzy when the arms are stretched over the head
In certain cases, the goiter may develop without causing any symptoms.
A goiter that causes an under active or overactive thyroid gland would lead to symptoms of hyper or hypothyroidism. These include:

diseases.name: Goitre
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Not all goitres cause signs and symptoms, but when they do, it may have the following signs and symptoms:
Swelling at the base of your neck
Coughing
A tight feeling in your throat
Hoarseness
Difficulty breathing
Difficulty swallowing

diseases.name: Golfer's Elbow (Medial Epicondylitis)
diseases.description: Golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis) is a painful condition caused by overuse of the forearm muscles and tendons that control wrist and finger movements. It causes pain and inflammation at the medial epicondyle — the bony bump on the inside of the elbow. Despite the name, it affects more than just golfers.
symptoms: Pain and tenderness on the inner side of the elbow
Stiffness of the elbow
Weakness in the hands and wrists
Numbness or tingling radiating to the ring and little fingers
Pain worsens with specific movements (swinging, squeezing, turning)

diseases.name: Gonorrhea : Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, Risk Factors and Complication
diseases.description: Gonorrhea, otherwise known as “the clap” or “the drip,” is a common sexually transmitted bacterial infection. The areas affected are largely the genital tract but it can also affect other areas of the body such as the rectum ,eye and joints.
symptoms: Usually, people who have gonorrhea do not know it as symptoms rarely show up. When they do, they typically occur in the genital areas. Some of the signs and symptoms of gonorrhea are:
Painful urination
Frequent, persistent, and urgent urination
Inflammation and redness on the penis
Pain or inflammation in the testicles
Pus-like discharge from the rectum and penis
Abdominal or pelvic pain
Increase in vaginal discharge
Bleeding in between the periods
A sharp pain in the abdomen
Vaginal bleeding and pain after vaginal intercourse
Eye pain
Photosensitivity
Pus-like discharge from the eyes
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
Septic arthritis (a bacterial infection in the joints that causes pain, redness, and inflammation)

diseases.name: Gorlin Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gorlin Syndrome, also known as Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (NBCCS), is a rare genetic disorder that significantly impacts the lives of those affected. This condition is characterized by the development of multiple basal cell carcinomas, jaw cysts, and various other abnormalities. Understanding Gorlin Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for healthcare providers and families, as early detection and management can lead to better outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Gorlin Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Gorlin Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Basal Cell Carcinomas: Multiple skin tumors that appear as small, pearly bumps or lesions, often on sun-exposed areas.
Jaw Cysts: Odontogenic keratocysts that can lead to jaw pain, swelling, and dental issues.
Skeletal Abnormalities: Such as scoliosis, spina bifida, or other bone malformations.
Facial Features: Distinctive facial features may include a broad forehead, hypertelorism (widely spaced eyes), and a prominent jaw.
Neurodevelopmental Issues: Some individuals may experience learning disabilities or developmental delays.

diseases.name: Gout
diseases.description: Gout is a common and complex form of arthritis that can affect anyone. It's characterized by sudden, severe attacks of pain, swelling, redness, and tenderness in one or more joints, most often in the big toe. Gout occurs when urate crystals accumulate in your joint, causing the inflammation and intense pain of a gout attack.
symptoms: Intense joint pain (most severe in the first 4–12 hours)
Lingering discomfort
Inflammation and redness
Limited range of motion
Kidney stones (chronic gout)

diseases.name: Granuloma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Granulomas are small clusters of immune cells that form in response to inflammation. They are a significant part of the body’s defense mechanism, often appearing as a reaction to infections, foreign substances, or autoimmune conditions. Understanding granulomas is crucial for recognizing their implications in various diseases and conditions. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding granulomas.
symptoms: Granulomas may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when they do, they can vary depending on their location and underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Lumps or Nodules: Granulomas can appear as small, firm lumps under the skin or in organs.
Respiratory Symptoms: If granulomas form in the lungs, symptoms may include cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain.
Skin Changes: Granulomas can cause skin lesions, which may be red, raised, or ulcerated.
Fever and Fatigue: General symptoms of inflammation, such as fever and fatigue, may also occur.

diseases.name: Granuloma Inguinale - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Granuloma inguinale, also known as donovanosis, is a rare but significant sexually transmitted infection characterized by the development of painless ulcers in the genital and perianal regions. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of granuloma inguinale, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Granuloma inguinale typically presents with the following symptoms:

Painless Ulcers: The hallmark of granuloma inguinale is the presence of painless, beefy-red ulcers that may bleed easily. These ulcers can vary in size and may appear on the genitalia, perianal area, or other parts of the body.
Foul Odor: The ulcers may produce a foul-smelling discharge, which can be distressing for the affected individual.
Swelling: In some cases, the surrounding tissue may become swollen and inflamed.
Secondary Infections: The open ulcers can become infected with other bacteria, leading to additional symptoms such as pain, redness, and increased discharge.

diseases.name: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Wegener's)
diseases.description: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), formerly called Wegener's granulomatosis, is a rare disorder that causes inflammation of the blood vessels in the nose, sinuses, throat, lungs, and kidneys. It belongs to the group of vasculitis disorders. Untreated, GPA can be life-threatening due to organ damage.
symptoms: Runny nose, nosebleeds, sinus pain
Ear pain, hearing loss
Coughing (sometimes with blood)
Shortness of breath
Blood in urine (kidney involvement)
Joint pain
Eye inflammation
Skin rashes
Fever and fatigue

diseases.name: Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis (GPA), formerly known as Wegener's granulomatosis, is a rare but serious autoimmune condition that primarily affects the blood vessels and can lead to significant organ damage. This condition is characterized by inflammation of the blood vessels (vasculitis) and the formation of granulomas—small clusters of immune cells that form in response to inflammation. Understanding GPA is crucial, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve outcomes and quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis can vary widely depending on the organs affected. Common symptoms include:
Respiratory Symptoms: Chronic sinusitis, nasal congestion, cough, and shortness of breath.
Kidney Symptoms: Blood in urine, proteinuria (excess protein in urine), and kidney dysfunction.
Skin Symptoms: Rashes, ulcers, or nodules on the skin.
Joint Symptoms: Pain and swelling in the joints.
General Symptoms: Fatigue, fever, weight loss, and night sweats.

diseases.name: Granulomatous Cheilitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Granulomatous Cheilitis (GC) is a rare inflammatory condition that primarily affects the lips, leading to swelling, discomfort, and changes in appearance. While it may seem like a minor issue, its significance lies in its potential to impact a person's quality of life, self-esteem, and overall health. Understanding Granulomatous Cheilitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can sometimes be associated with systemic diseases or other underlying conditions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Granulomatous Cheilitis can vary in severity and may include:
Swelling of the Lips: The most noticeable symptom, often leading to a puffy appearance.
Cracking and Fissures: The lips may develop painful cracks, which can become infected.
Ulceration: In some cases, ulcers may form on the lip surface.
Discoloration: The affected area may appear red or discolored.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Some individuals report discomfort or a burning feeling in the lips.

diseases.name: Granulosa Cell Tumor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Granulosa Cell Tumor (GCT) is a rare type of tumor that originates from the granulosa cells of the ovary. These tumors are classified as sex-cord stromal tumors and are known for their unique characteristics and behavior. Understanding GCT is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Granulosa Cell Tumor, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Granulosa Cell Tumors can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the tumor's size and hormone production. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Persistent or severe abdominal pain may occur as the tumor grows.
Abnormal Menstrual Bleeding: Irregular periods or postmenopausal bleeding can be a sign of hormone production by the tumor.
Bloating or Swelling: A noticeable increase in abdominal size may occur due to the tumor's presence.
Changes in Breast Tissue: Hormonal changes may lead to breast tenderness or enlargement.
Weight Gain: Unexplained weight gain can occur due to hormonal imbalances.

diseases.name: Graves’ Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Graves’ disease, also known as toxic diffuse goiter or Flajani-Basedow-Graves disease, is an autoimmune disorder that causes your immune system to mistakenly attack the thyroid gland. This leads to an overproduction of thyroid hormones, a condition known as hyperthyroidism .
symptoms: Graves’ disease can affect multiple systems in the body due to excess production of thyroid hormones. Symptoms may develop gradually or appear suddenly, and their severity can vary from person to person.
Irritability and anxiety
Unintentional weight loss despite normal eating habits
Heat sensitivity, increased sweating, and warm, moist skin
Fatigue and muscle weakness
Fine tremors in hands or fingers
Irregular or rapid heartbeat (palpitations)
Goiter (enlargement of the thyroid gland)
Frequent bowel movements
Sleep disturbances
Menstrual irregularities
Reduced libido or erectile dysfunction
Some individuals may also develop specific complications such as:
Graves’ ophthalmopathy – bulging eyes, eye discomfort, light sensitivity
Graves’ dermopathy – red, thickened skin, typically on the shins or tops of the feet
These manifestations are explained in detail in the next section.

In Graves’ ophthalmopathy, the TRAb antibody also affects the tissues and muscles around the eyes, leading to inflammation and the buildup of carbohydrates, which can cause bulging eyes, pain, and vision problems.
In Graves’ dermopathy, the same mechanism may cause skin thickening and reddening, especially on the shins and tops of the feet.

diseases.name: Gray Baby Syndrome : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: All pregnant women want their babies to be healthy. Therefore, they need to receive prenatal care from doctors. They should also take other measures to ensure a healthy pregnancy, including regular exercise, maintaining a healthy diet, and quitting alcohol, drugs, and tobacco.
symptoms: When toxic levels of chloramphenicol collect in the baby’s bloodstream, they can develop the gray baby syndrome. Babies usually display symptoms within two to nine days after the doctor begins the chloramphenicol treatment. The symptoms may differ. However, one may observe the following:
Vomiting
Limp body
Greyish skin colour
Low blood pressure
Hypothermia (low body temperature)
Blue lips and skin
Abdominal swelling
Green stools
Difficulty breathing
Irregular heartbeat

diseases.name: Groin Strain - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A groin strain is a common injury that affects many individuals, particularly athletes and those engaged in physical activities. It occurs when the muscles in the groin area are stretched or torn, leading to pain and discomfort. Understanding groin strains is essential not only for athletes but also for anyone who engages in physical activities, as it can significantly impact mobility and quality of life. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of groin strains, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of a groin strain can vary depending on the severity of the injury. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Sudden pain in the groin area, which may radiate to the inner thigh.
Swelling: Swelling or bruising may occur in the affected area.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness in the groin and inner thigh.
Weakness: Difficulty in moving the leg or performing activities that require leg movement.

diseases.name: Group A Streptococcal Infections - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Group A Streptococcal infections, often referred to as strep infections, are caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pyogenes . This organism is responsible for a range of illnesses, from mild throat infections to severe diseases such as rheumatic fever and necrotizing fasciitis. Understanding these infections is crucial, as they can lead to significant health complications if not properly managed. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of Group A Streptococcal infections, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Group A Streptococcal infections can vary depending on the type of infection. Common symptoms include:
Strep throat: Sore throat, difficulty swallowing, red and swollen tonsils, fever, headache, and swollen lymph nodes.
Scarlet fever: A red rash that feels like sandpaper, fever, and a sore throat.
Impetigo: Red sores that can ooze and form a yellow-brown crust.
Cellulitis: Redness, swelling, warmth, and pain in the affected area.

diseases.name: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) is a rare but serious autoimmune disorder in which the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nerves. It often begins with weakness and tingling sensations in the legs or arms, which can quickly spread and progress to muscle weakness, and, in severe cases, full-body paralysis .
symptoms: Guillain-Barré Syndrome typically begins with mild symptoms but can progress rapidly, sometimes leading to life-threatening complications. Most people experience their worst symptoms within two to four weeks after onset, followed by gradual recovery. Symptoms may vary depending on the type and severity of the condition.
Common signs and symptoms include:
Tingling or “pins and needles” sensations in the fingers, toes, ankles, or wrists
Muscle weakness that often begins in the lower limbs and spreads upwards
Paralysis in one or multiple parts of the body, in severe cases
Unsteady gait or difficulty walking, climbing stairs, or maintaining balance
Difficulty with facial and eye movements, making it hard to speak, chew, or swallow
Blurred or impaired vision due to eye muscle involvement
Severe pain, which may feel achy, cramp-like, or sharp, often worsening at night
Loss of bladder or bowel control
Rapid or irregular heartbeat (tachycardia)
Fluctuations in blood pressure, either high or low
Difficulty breathing or a sensation of suffocation, which may require emergency intervention

In about 10% of individuals, the symptoms may begin in the arms or face rather than the legs. Early recognition and prompt medical care are crucial to managing the condition and preventing complications.

diseases.name: Guttate Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Guttate psoriasis is a specific type of psoriasis that manifests as small, drop-shaped lesions on the skin. This condition is significant not only because of its distinctive appearance but also due to its potential impact on a person's quality of life. Understanding guttate psoriasis is crucial for effective management and treatment, as it can often be mistaken for other skin conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of guttate psoriasis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The primary symptoms of guttate psoriasis include:
Drop-shaped Lesions: Small, red spots that can be covered with a fine scale.
Itching and Burning: The lesions may be itchy or cause a burning sensation.
Dry Skin: Affected areas may appear dry and flaky.
Nail Changes: Some individuals may experience pitting or discoloration of the nails.

diseases.name: Gynecomastia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Gynecomastia is a condition characterized by the enlargement of breast tissue in males. While it is often a source of embarrassment and psychological distress for those affected, understanding gynecomastia is crucial for effective management and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of gynecomastia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. By shedding light on this condition, we hope to empower individuals with the knowledge they need to seek appropriate care.
symptoms: The primary symptom of gynecomastia is the enlargement of breast tissue, which may be accompanied by:
Tenderness or sensitivity in the breast area
A firm, rubbery mass beneath the nipple
Swelling or puffiness of the nipple
Discharge from the nipple (in some cases)

diseases.name: H. Pylori - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Helicobacter pylori, commonly known as H. pylori, is a type of bacteria that plays a significant role in gastrointestinal health. It is a spiral-shaped organism that resides in the stomach lining and is known to cause various digestive disorders, including gastritis, peptic ulcers, and even stomach cancer. Understanding H. pylori is crucial not only for those experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms but also for anyone interested in maintaining optimal digestive health. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook associated with H. pylori.
symptoms: Many individuals infected with H. pylori may remain asymptomatic. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Abdominal Pain: Often described as a burning sensation in the stomach.
Nausea and Vomiting: May occur, especially after eating.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Loss of Appetite: Reduced desire to eat, which can lead to weight loss.
Frequent Burping: Increased belching can be a sign of digestive distress.

diseases.name: H3N2 Influenza A: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, Prevention and How it Spreads
diseases.description: The weather in India changes quickly, one month it’s warm and humid, and the next it turns cooler. Around this time, people across cities start developing fever, cough, sore throat, and a sense of extreme tiredness that feels like more than just a common cold. Clinics become crowded, children miss school, and adults feel drained for days. During these waves, doctors often diagnose H3N2, a subtype of the influenza A virus.
symptoms: Most patients experience a sudden onset of symptoms; one moment they're fine, and the next they feel extremely unwell.

Families often search phrases like h3n2 influenza virus symptoms, h3n2 virus symptoms, symptoms of h3n2 virus, or influenza A h3n2 symptoms online. Others mistakenly type h2n3 symptoms, thinking it’s the same thing. H2N3 is not a human influenza subtype; the correct human subtype is H3N2.
The symptoms of H3N2 typically include:
High fever (often 101–103°F)
Intense body aches
Chills
Headache
Sore throat
Persistent dry cough
Runny or blocked nose
Fatigue and weakness
Loss of appetite
These symptoms are more intense than a typical cold.
Vomiting or loose stools (more common in children)
Chest discomfort
Red, watery eyes
Dizziness due to dehydration

This is the toughest phase. Fever may persist for 2–4 days. The cough becomes harsher. Fatigue is very strong, and even simple tasks feel exhausting. Many people prefer to rest all day because standing or walking feels tiring.
Throat pain worsens, and appetite remains low.
Most cases of H3N2 improve with home care and simple medications. The goal is to ease discomfort, reduce fever, maintain hydration, and prevent complications.

Families often search “h3n2 symptoms and treatment” or “h3n2 virus treatment” because the illness feels overwhelming in the first few days. The good news is that with proper care, recovery typically follows the timeline described in Part 1.
Pregnant women with H3N2 may experience the same fever, body aches, and cough as others, but they are more likely to:
Become breathless
Develop dehydration
Feel extremely weak
Require medical monitoring
Early treatment is crucial.
H3N2 virus symptoms include sudden high fever, intense body aches, sore throat, dry cough, headache, and fatigue. Some may have vomiting or diarrhea, especially children.

The influenza A H3N2 symptoms are similar to other influenza infections, fever, chills, tiredness, cough, and nasal congestion. Symptoms usually appear suddenly and are more intense than a common cold.
Treatment focuses on reducing fever, soothing cough, and preventing dehydration. Most people recover in 7–10 days with home care.
No, h2n3 symptoms refers to a non-human strain. The correct human influenza subtype is H3N2.
Seek care if you have breathlessness, chest pain, persistent high fever, confusion, dehydration, or worsening symptoms.

diseases.name: Haemophilia
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Signs and symptoms of haemophilia change with levels of clotting factors. If clotting-factor level is mildly reduced, one may bleed only after surgery or trauma. If the deficiency is severe, one may experience spontaneous bleeding.
Signs and symptoms of spontaneous bleeding include:
Unexplained and excessive bleeding from cuts or injuries, or after surgery or dental work
Many large or deep bruises
Unusual bleeding after vaccinations
Pain, swelling or tightness in the joints
Blood in urine or stool
Nosebleeds without a known cause
In infants, unexplained irritability
Emergency signs and symptoms of haemophilia include:
Sudden pain, swelling and warmth in large joints, such as knees, elbows, hips and shoulders, and in your arm and leg muscles
Bleeding from an injury, especially if one have a severe form of haemophilia
Painful, prolonged headache
Repeated vomiting
Extreme fatigue
Neck pain
Double vision

diseases.name: Haglunds Deformity - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Haglund's deformity is a condition that affects the heel of the foot, characterized by a bony enlargement on the back of the heel bone (calcaneus). This deformity can lead to discomfort and pain, particularly when wearing shoes. Understanding Haglund's deformity is essential for those who experience heel pain, as it can significantly impact mobility and quality of life. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Haglund's deformity.
symptoms: The symptoms of Haglund's deformity can vary in intensity and may include:
Pain: A sharp or aching pain at the back of the heel, especially when walking or wearing shoes.
Swelling: Inflammation around the heel, which may be accompanied by redness and warmth.
Bursitis: Inflammation of the bursa, leading to additional pain and discomfort.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty in flexing the ankle or moving the foot due to pain.

diseases.name: Hair Disorders
diseases.description: Hair disorders encompass a variety of conditions affecting hair growth, structure, and scalp health. These include androgenetic alopecia (male/female pattern baldness), telogen effluvium, trichotillomania, and tinea capitis among others. Hair loss affects millions of people and can have significant psychological impact.
symptoms: Gradual thinning on top of head
Circular or patchy bald spots
Sudden loosening of hair
Full-body hair loss
Patches of scaling that spread over the scalp

diseases.name: Hairy Cell Leukemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hairy Cell Leukemia (HCL) is a rare type of blood cancer that affects the bone marrow and blood. It is classified as a chronic lymphoproliferative disorder, meaning it involves the overproduction of a specific type of white blood cell known as B lymphocytes. The significance of HCL lies in its unique characteristics, treatment options, and the impact it has on patients' lives. Understanding this condition is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can lead to favorable outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Hairy Cell Leukemia can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Frequent Infections: Increased susceptibility to infections due to low white blood cell counts.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: This can occur due to low platelet counts.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Enlargement of lymph nodes, particularly in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Abdominal Discomfort: This may be caused by an enlarged spleen or liver.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can occur in some patients.

diseases.name: Hallux Rigidus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hallux Rigidus is a condition that affects the big toe, leading to stiffness and pain in the joint. This condition is significant not only because it can limit mobility and affect daily activities but also because it can lead to further complications if left untreated. Understanding Hallux Rigidus is essential for those experiencing foot pain, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Hallux Rigidus can vary in severity but typically include:
Pain: Discomfort in the big toe, especially during movement or weight-bearing activities.
Stiffness: Reduced ability to bend the toe, leading to difficulty in walking or running.
Swelling: Inflammation around the joint may occur, causing visible swelling.
Bony Growths: Formation of bone spurs (osteophytes) around the joint, which can be felt or seen.
Difficulty Wearing Shoes: Pain or discomfort when wearing certain types of footwear.

diseases.name: Hamartoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hamartoma is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it plays a significant role in the field of medicine. These benign tumors are composed of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that are normally found in the area where the hamartoma develops. While hamartomas are generally non-cancerous and often asymptomatic, understanding their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is crucial for effective management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hamartomas, making the information accessible to a general audience.
symptoms: Many hamartomas are asymptomatic and may be discovered incidentally during imaging studies for unrelated issues. However, when symptoms do occur, they can vary depending on the location and size of the hamartoma. Common symptoms may include:
Lung Hamartomas: Cough, chest pain, or difficulty breathing.
Skin Hamartomas: Changes in skin appearance, such as growths or discoloration.
Kidney Hamartomas: Flank pain or hematuria (blood in urine).
Liver Hamartomas: Abdominal pain or discomfort.

diseases.name: Hammer Toe: Causes, Symptoms, and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Hammer toe is a foot deformity caused by an imbalance in the muscles, tendons, and ligaments that keep the toe straight. This condition is caused by multiple factors, such as the type of shoes you wear, your foot shape, and any history of injury or trauma to your foot.
symptoms: The abnormal bend of joints in one or more toes is the primary sign of a hammertoe. It may be difficult or uncomfortable to move the affected toe. The continuous pressing of the toe on the inside of your shoes, as a result, can also lead to the formation of foot corns and calluses.
Mild signs and symptoms include:
A downward bent toe
Calluses or corns
Walking difficulties
Inability to wiggle your toes or stretch your foot
Toes that resemble claws

diseases.name: Hamstring Injury - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hamstring injuries are among the most common musculoskeletal injuries, particularly in athletes and active individuals. These injuries can significantly impact mobility and quality of life, making it essential to understand their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hamstring injuries, helping readers recognize the signs, seek appropriate care, and implement preventive measures.
symptoms: The symptoms of a hamstring injury can vary depending on the severity of the injury. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Pain: A sharp pain in the back of the thigh during physical activity.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling may develop within hours, and bruising can appear as the injury progresses.
Muscle Spasms: Involuntary contractions of the hamstring muscles may occur.
Weakness: Difficulty in straightening the leg or walking may be experienced.
Stiffness: The affected area may feel tight or stiff, especially after periods of inactivity.

diseases.name: Hamstring Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hamstring tendonitis is a common condition that affects many individuals, particularly those who engage in physical activities that involve running, jumping, or sudden changes in direction. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and may hinder one’s ability to participate in sports or even perform daily activities. Understanding hamstring tendonitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their normal routines as quickly as possible.
symptoms: Pain: A dull ache or sharp pain in the back of the thigh, especially during physical activities.
Swelling: Inflammation around the tendon area may lead to visible swelling.
Stiffness: Reduced flexibility and stiffness in the hamstring muscles.
Tenderness: Sensitivity to touch in the affected area.
Weakness: Difficulty in performing activities that require leg strength, such as running or jumping.

diseases.name: Hand Foot Mouth Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hand Foot Mouth Disease (HFMD) is a common viral infection that primarily affects children but can also occur in adults. It is characterized by sores in the mouth and a rash on the hands and feet. Understanding HFMD is crucial as it can lead to discomfort and complications if not managed properly. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of HFMD, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Hand Foot Mouth Disease include:
Fever
Sore throat
Painful mouth sores (ulcers)
Rash on the hands and feet, which may appear as red spots or blisters
Loss of appetite
Irritability in children

diseases.name: Hand Foot Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hand Foot Syndrome (HFS) , also known as Hand-Foot-Mouth Disease (HFMD) in some contexts, is a condition that primarily affects the skin on the hands, feet, and sometimes the mouth. It is characterized by painful sores and rashes, which can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding HFS is crucial not only for those who may be affected but also for caregivers and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Hand Foot Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Hand Foot Syndrome can vary in severity and may include:
Painful Sores: Blisters or sores on the palms of the hands, soles of the feet, and inside the mouth.
Rash: Red, raised spots that may develop into blisters.
Fever: A mild to moderate fever may accompany the rash and sores.
Sore Throat: Discomfort or pain in the throat, often due to mouth sores.
Loss of Appetite: Painful sores in the mouth can lead to difficulty eating and drinking.

diseases.name: Hantavirus: Precautions for Prevention
diseases.description: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome, is an infectious disease caused by a virus carried by several types of rodents, particularly the deer mouse. You become infected primarily by breathing air infected with Hantaviruses that are shed in rodent urine and droppings.
symptoms: Hantavirus infection advances in two stages. In the first stage, the signs and symptoms resemble that of the flu. It may be difficult to distinguish the infection from pneumonia , influenza, and other viral infections. The initial symptoms include:
● Headache
● Fever
● Chills
● Diarrhea
● Vomiting
● Abdominal pain
In the second stage, the symptoms get severe; these include:
● Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
● Low blood pressure
● Secretions produced through cough like postnasal drainage
● Presence of fluid in the lungs
● Reduced heart efficiency
If you notice any of these symptoms, immediately visit a doctor.

diseases.name: Harlequin Ichthyosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Harlequin Ichthyosis is a severe genetic skin disorder that significantly impacts the lives of those affected. Characterized by thick, diamond-shaped scales covering the body, this condition presents unique challenges for patients and their families. Understanding Harlequin Ichthyosis is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for healthcare providers, caregivers, and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Harlequin Ichthyosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Harlequin Ichthyosis are severe and can include:
Thick, Scaly Skin: The most distinctive feature, with large, diamond-shaped scales covering the body.
Deep Fissures: Cracks in the skin that can lead to infections and discomfort.
Erythema: Redness and inflammation of the skin.
Limited Movement: The tightness of the skin can restrict movement, particularly in joints.
Dehydration: Due to the inability of the skin to retain moisture, individuals may experience dehydration.
Temperature Regulation Issues: Difficulty in regulating body temperature due to the compromised skin barrier.

diseases.name: Harlequin Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Harlequin Syndrome is a rare neurological condition characterized by a distinctive pattern of sweating and flushing on one side of the body, while the other side remains unaffected. This phenomenon can be both puzzling and alarming for those who experience it, as well as for healthcare providers. Understanding Harlequin Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for medical professionals who may encounter it in their practice. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Harlequin Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of Harlequin Syndrome is the asymmetrical sweating and flushing of the skin. Common symptoms include:
Unilateral Sweating: Excessive sweating on one side of the face or body.
Flushing: Redness and warmth on the affected side, often accompanied by a feeling of heat.
Temperature Regulation Issues: Difficulty in regulating body temperature, particularly in response to heat or exercise.
Facial Asymmetry: Noticeable differences in appearance between the two sides of the face.

diseases.name: Hashimoto's disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: Hashimoto affects the functioning of the thyroid gland. The thyroid gland is present at the base of your neck, and its function is to maintain the body’s metabolism. It secretes thyroid hormones into the bloodstream that helps to regulate various body functions.
symptoms: As mentioned above, Hashimoto’s disease takes several years to form. Thus, the symptoms can be minimal at the initial stage. The first sign may be a goiter (that is an enlarged thyroid gland).
Other than goiter being a major symptom, there are other common symptoms such as:
Sudden weight gain
Extreme fatigue
Swollen, pale, or puffed face
Excessive pain in joints and muscles
Chronic or severe constipation
Cold hands , feet, and other parts of the body
Issues of infertility or trouble in getting pregnant
Hair loss or fragile hair
Heavy or irregular menstrual cycle
Depression and anxiety
Reduced heart rate

diseases.name: Hay Fever - Causes, Symptoms and Risk Factors
diseases.description: Hay Fever is known as allergic rhinitis. It is caused due to inhaling airborne outdoor or indoor allergens like dust mites, grass, tree, pollen, spores, animal fur or the skin, urine, and saliva of pet animals. These allergens cause cold-like symptoms like sneezing, itchy eyes, runny nose, congestion, and sinus pressure.
symptoms: The warning signs of Hay Fever are:-
● Runny , itchy, and a stuffy nose.
● Watery, itchy, red eyes
● Sneezing when in contact with allergens
● Itching of the throat
● The skin color beneath the eyes will be blue and swollen.
● Postnasal drip, cough, and fatigue

diseases.name: Head Injury & Treatment
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE

diseases.name: Headache - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment
diseases.description: Headache is one of the most common medical conditions that affect everyone at some point in their lives. The main symptom of a headache is a pain in the head or face that can be throbbing, constant, sharp, or dull. Doctors treat headache pain with medicines, stress management, and biofeedback.
symptoms: The symptoms of headaches differ depending on the type of headache.
Primary headaches
a. Tension Headaches The common signs and symptoms are
Pain is associated with band-like tightness or pressure and may encircle the head. The pressure is felt at the temples and all over the forehead. Bilateral pain (pain on both sides) is seen.
Nausea and vomiting are not seen in this type. The headache is not aggravated by sound and light.
The quality of life is not affected much, and the patient can follow a daily routine.
b. Cluster Headaches

The pain comes in groups (as clusters) separated by pain-free periods. The pain can last from months to years, and one may not experience headaches for a few months to years. These headaches often wake the patient in the middle of the night.

Each episode of the pain may last from 30-90 seconds. It is excruciating pain and usually occurs behind or around the eyes. The nose on the affected side may become runny or congested, and the eyes may become watery, swollen, or inflamed.
It may be hereditary. Sleep pattern changes, medications such as nitroglycerin, alcohol consumption, cigarette smoking and some foods such as smoked meats and chocolate may trigger these headaches.
According to a study conducted, brain scans performed on patients during cluster headaches, researchers observed abnormal activity in the hypothalamus.
Regularly counselling is required for patients with such headaches as they might develop suicidal tendencies (due to excruciating and throbbing pain).
c. Migraines The symptoms of migraines include the following:
Moderate to severe pain and in some cases pounding or throbbing pain
Pain that lasts between four hours to three days
Nausea or vomiting
Sensitivity to light, noise, or odours
Stomach upset or abdominal pain
Secondary headaches
a. Sinus headaches The symptoms of sinus headaches include the following:
Fever
Bad taste in the mouth
Facial swelling
Deep, constant pain in the cheekbones and forehead
A feeling of fullness in ears
Pain that gets worse with sudden head movement or straining
b. Medication overuse headaches The symptoms of medication overuse headaches include the following:
Nausea
Restlessness
Difficulty concentrating
Memory problems
Increase in frequency of headaches
Pain that’s worse in the morning
c. Thunderclap headaches The symptoms of thunderclap headaches include:
Numbness
Weakness
Speech problems
Seizures
Change in vision
Confusion
Change in sensation

diseases.name: Heart and Chest Pain - Causes & Symptoms
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The chest pain of cardiac ischemia and an impending heart attack is described variously as pressing, squeezing, strangling, constrictive, bursting, or burning. “Band across chest”, “Weight in center of chest” is another description. The pain normally spreads from the centre of the chest to the shoulders, the arms (especially the inner aspect of the left arm) neck, jaws and teeth. Emotions / effort / heavy meals / stress may precipitate it. The pain is normally relieved by rest. Such pain lasting for longer than 20 minutes may imply significant ischemia leading to a heart attack . A Nitroglycerine tablet kept under the tongue relieves the pain. Not all cardiac pains have descriptions as above. There are some symptoms called ‘Anginal equivalents’ such as shortness of breath, discomfort localized to left arm, lower jaw, teeth (with people seeking a Dental opinion!) neck belching, indigestion, sweating or dizziness.

diseases.name: Heart Attack In Children
diseases.description: Heart attack is a raging topic in India as we Indians are genetically prone to coronary artery disease. The public perception is to label any issue of the heart as a “heart attack”. Heart disease that afflicts children is quite different from that of adults and most of these conditions can be permanently rectified.

diseases.name: Heart Defects In Children And Its Management
diseases.description: द्वारा – डॉ. सुनिल कुमार स्वेन एमबीबीएस, एमएस, एमसीएच (ह्रदय शस्त्रक्रिया, एम्स), एफआयएसीएस सल्लागार बाल ह्रदय शल्यचिकित्सक (कन्सल्टंट पेडिअॅट्रिक कार्डिअॅक सर्जन)

diseases.name: Heart Failure
diseases.description: Heart failure is a progressive disorder in which damage to the heart results in the weakening of the patient’s cardiovascular efficiency. It is generally a chronic, long-term condition though it can sometimes develop suddenly. While the most common cause of heart failure is coronary artery disease, this condition can also occur when an infection weakens the heart muscle or due to certain diseases like diabetes or thyroid problems, due to uncontrolled hypertension, renal failure, persistent fast heart rhythms, and also due to certain drugs used in cancer treatment.
symptoms: Most of the signs and symptoms of heart failure are because of fluid collection and congestion in the legs, lungs, abdomen etc., and the inability of the heart to pump efficiently to meet the demands of the tissues and the organs in the body.
Some of the symptoms of heart failure are breathlessness, which could be an exaggerated, uncomfortable awareness of breathing. The breath does not go all the way down the lungs.
Other symptoms include:
Shortness of breath
Heavy breathing
Tightness in chest
Choking

Breathlessness may arise during exertion in the early stage of the disease, but may also occur at rest when the disease is advanced. There could be breathlessness occurring in a lying posture but relieved on sitting up. Patients usually say that they need three or more pillows to sleep comfortably at night.

This leads to Paroxymal Noctumal Dyspnoea (PND), which usually starts 2-4 hours after onset of sleep. Patients sweat a lot and develop a cough with breathlessness, which is generally relieved by getting out of bed.
Other prominent symptoms include fatigue and impaired effort capacity. Patients may also report abdominal fullness swelling of legs, nausea and loss of appetite.

diseases.name: Heart Inflammation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heart inflammation, medically known as myocarditis, is a condition that involves the inflammation of the heart muscle (myocardium). This inflammation can disrupt the heart's ability to pump blood effectively, leading to a range of health issues. Understanding heart inflammation is crucial, as it can have significant implications for overall cardiovascular health. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of heart inflammation.
symptoms: The symptoms of heart inflammation can vary widely, but common signs include:
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may feel like pressure or tightness.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy, even with minimal exertion.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or when lying down.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or feet due to fluid retention.

diseases.name: Heart Murmur - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heart murmurs are sounds made by turbulent blood flow within the heart. While they can be harmless, they may also indicate underlying heart conditions that require medical attention. Understanding heart murmurs is crucial for early detection and management of potential heart issues. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions about heart murmurs.
symptoms: Many individuals with heart murmurs may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or at rest.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.

diseases.name: Heart Palpitations In Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heart palpitations during pregnancy can be a concerning experience for many expectant mothers. These sensations, often described as a racing, fluttering, or pounding heartbeat, can be alarming, especially when they occur unexpectedly. Understanding heart palpitations in pregnancy is crucial, as they can be a normal physiological response to the changes occurring in a woman's body or, in some cases, a sign of an underlying issue that requires medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of heart palpitations in pregnancy, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Heart palpitations can manifest in various ways, including:
A racing or pounding heartbeat
Fluttering sensations in the chest
Irregular heartbeats
A feeling of skipped beats

diseases.name: Heart Transplant Rejection
diseases.description: The human heart beats around 100,000 times in a day and pumps about 5,000 gallons of blood through our body every day. Heart transplant surgery is reserved for those patients who did not respond to any other treatment or surgery. Heart transplant rejection occurs due to our defense mechanism which deals with the transplanted heart just like it opposes any virus or bacteria. The rejection can be handled with immunosuppressive medication, which one has to take lifelong. The dosage will be altered by the doctor as and when required. One should be aware of the signs of organ rejection in a heart transplant , to enable early management.

diseases.name: Heartburn
diseases.description: Heartburn is that burning sensation in our throat or chest that occurs when stomach acid rises up from our stomach into the mouth. Heartburn is a common symptom of Gastro-Esophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) also called Acid Reflux.

diseases.name: Heartburn or Gastroesophageal Reflux (GER) - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, Diet and Prevention
diseases.description: Heartburn or Gastroesophageal Reflux (GER) is a digestive problem that is also acidity or indigestion. It occurs if the acid formed in your stomach comes back up to the esophagus, causing a burning sensation in your chest or in the upper area of the stomach. On the other hand, GERD Gastroesophageal reflux disease is a more serious condition that can lead to several health complications if any medical care isn’t taken promptly. Heartburn is a burning pain that occurs in your chest, which can be felt behind your breastbone. The pain becomes more acute subsequent to eating, at night, or when resting or bending over. Periodic acid reflux or heartburn is normal and there is no reason to unnecessarily worrying. Many people can deal with the distress of heartburn with changes in lifestyle and over-the-counter drugs. Heartburn that is frequent and often causes trouble in your daily routine can be the symptoms of the aggravated condition and it requires medical attention.
symptoms: Frequent heartburn and chest pain
Trouble in swallowing food
Digestive disorders
Breathing difficulties similar to Asthma
Coughing
A sore throat
Regurgitation of foods

diseases.name: Heat Exhaustion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heat exhaustion is a serious condition that occurs when the body overheats, often due to prolonged exposure to high temperatures, particularly when combined with high humidity and strenuous physical activity. It is a significant health concern, especially during the hot summer months or in environments where heat is prevalent. Understanding heat exhaustion is crucial for prevention and effective management, as it can lead to more severe heat-related illnesses, such as heat stroke, if not addressed promptly.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of heat exhaustion is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Heavy Sweating: Profuse sweating is often the first sign of heat exhaustion.
Weakness and Fatigue: A feeling of extreme tiredness and weakness is common.
Dizziness and Fainting: Individuals may feel lightheaded or faint.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms can occur as the body reacts to overheating.
Headache: A throbbing headache may develop due to dehydration.
Muscle Cramps: Painful muscle cramps, particularly in the legs and abdomen, can occur.

diseases.name: Heat Stroke
diseases.description: Heat stroke is the most severe heat-related illness and occurs when the body can no longer control its temperature.
symptoms: Very high body temperature
Confusion or altered mental state
Hot, dry skin or heavy sweating
Seizures
Loss of consciousness

diseases.name: Heel Spurs - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heel spurs are a common foot condition that can cause significant discomfort and impact daily activities. They are often associated with plantar fasciitis, a condition characterized by inflammation of the tissue that runs along the bottom of the foot. Understanding heel spurs is essential for anyone experiencing heel pain, as early diagnosis and treatment can lead to better outcomes. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of heel spurs, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The primary symptom of heel spurs is pain in the heel, which may be sharp or aching. This pain is often most pronounced in the morning or after prolonged periods of rest. Other common symptoms include:
Swelling: Inflammation around the heel may lead to visible swelling.
Tenderness: The heel may be sensitive to touch.
Stiffness: Individuals may experience stiffness in the foot, particularly after sitting for long periods.

diseases.name: Hellp Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: HELLP Syndrome is a serious medical condition that can occur during pregnancy, particularly in the third trimester. It is a variant of preeclampsia, a pregnancy complication characterized by high blood pressure and signs of damage to other organ systems. HELLP stands for Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, and Low Platelet count, which are the three main features of this syndrome. Understanding HELLP Syndrome is crucial for expectant mothers and healthcare providers, as early detection and management can significantly improve outcomes for both the mother and the baby.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of HELLP Syndrome is vital for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Severe and persistent headaches that do not respond to typical pain relief.
Nausea and Vomiting: Frequent nausea, often accompanied by vomiting.
Abdominal Pain: Pain in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen, which may indicate liver involvement.
Fatigue: Extreme tiredness or weakness that is unusual for the individual.
Swelling: Sudden swelling of the face, hands, or feet.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or seeing spots.

diseases.name: Hemicrania Continua - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemicrania Continua (HC) is a rare and often misunderstood headache disorder characterized by persistent, unilateral (one-sided) pain that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Unlike other headache types, HC is unique in its continuous nature and responsiveness to specific treatments. Understanding this condition is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can lead to improved outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Hemicrania Continua, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of Hemicrania Continua is a continuous, unilateral headache that can vary in intensity. Other common symptoms include:
Autonomic Symptoms: These may include nasal congestion, runny nose, drooping eyelid, and redness of the eye on the affected side.
Nausea and Vomiting: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal symptoms during headache episodes.
Sensitivity to Light and Sound: Increased sensitivity to environmental stimuli is common during headache attacks.

diseases.name: Hemifacial Spasm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemifacial spasm (HFS) is a neurological condition characterized by involuntary muscle contractions on one side of the face. These spasms can be both distressing and disruptive, affecting a person's quality of life. Understanding hemifacial spasm is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hemifacial spasm, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of hemifacial spasm is involuntary muscle contractions on one side of the face. These spasms can vary in intensity and frequency and may include:
Twitching around the eye: Often the first noticeable symptom, this may progress to more extensive facial spasms.
Facial grimacing: Involuntary movements may cause the mouth to pull to one side.
Difficulty with facial expressions: Spasms can interfere with the ability to smile, frown, or perform other facial movements.

diseases.name: Hemiplegic Migraine - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemiplegic migraine is a rare and complex type of migraine that can cause temporary paralysis on one side of the body, mimicking the symptoms of a stroke. This condition is significant not only because of its debilitating symptoms but also due to the potential for misdiagnosis and the need for appropriate management. Understanding hemiplegic migraine is crucial for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and effective treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemiplegic migraine can vary widely but typically include:
Severe Headache: Often unilateral and throbbing, similar to other migraine types.
Aura: Visual disturbances such as flashing lights, zigzag patterns, or temporary loss of vision.
Neurological Symptoms: These may include weakness or paralysis on one side of the body, difficulty speaking, and sensory changes (numbness or tingling).
Nausea and Vomiting: Common in many migraine types, including hemiplegic migraine.

diseases.name: Hemochromatosis (Iron Overload) - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Hemochromatosis is a condition in which iron absorption and accumulation in the body increases. It is a rare disorder with less than a million cases recorded each year in India.
symptoms: Symptoms are usually not noticeable until quite late in life. In men, the symptoms can present at around 40 years of age. Comparatively, women exhibit symptoms 10 (or more) years later; this is primarily because of the menstrual cycle that naturally keeps iron levels in check.
The common symptoms include:
Getting tired easily
Reduced energy levels
Weakness
Joint pain
Abdominal pain
Darkening of skin
Abnormal heart rate
Erectile dysfunction
Diabetes
Menstrual irregularities in some cases

diseases.name: Hemolysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemolysis is a medical condition characterized by the destruction of red blood cells (RBCs), leading to the release of hemoglobin into the bloodstream. This process can significantly impact the body’s ability to transport oxygen, resulting in various health complications. Understanding hemolysis is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, as well as for preventing potential complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hemolysis, making it accessible to a general audience while maintaining medical accuracy.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemolysis can vary depending on the severity and underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Due to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin and mucous membranes.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, resulting from the accumulation of bilirubin, a byproduct of hemoglobin breakdown.
Dark Urine: Caused by the presence of hemoglobin or bilirubin.
Shortness of Breath: Especially during physical activity, due to anemia.
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart compensates for low oxygen levels by beating faster.

diseases.name: Hemolytic Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemolytic anemia is a condition characterized by the premature destruction of red blood cells, leading to a deficiency in the number of these vital cells in the bloodstream. This condition is significant because red blood cells are essential for transporting oxygen throughout the body. When their numbers dwindle, it can lead to a range of health issues, including fatigue, weakness, and more severe complications if left untreated. Understanding hemolytic anemia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their health and quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemolytic anemia can vary depending on the severity of the condition and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Pallor: Pale skin and mucous membranes due to reduced red blood cell count.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Rapid Heartbeat: An increased heart rate as the body tries to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to the buildup of bilirubin from the breakdown of red blood cells.
Dark Urine: Urine may appear darker due to the presence of hemoglobin or bilirubin.

diseases.name: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS) is a serious medical condition characterized by the combination of hemolytic anemia, acute kidney failure, and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count). It primarily affects children but can occur in adults as well. Understanding HUS is crucial due to its potential to lead to severe complications, including long-term kidney damage and even death if not promptly treated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of HUS, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of HUS can vary but typically include:
Fatigue and weakness: Due to anemia.
Pallor: A pale appearance resulting from low red blood cell counts.
Bruising and bleeding: Caused by low platelet counts.
Abdominal pain: Often associated with gastrointestinal symptoms.
Diarrhea: May be bloody, especially in cases linked to STEC infection.
Decreased urine output: A sign of kidney dysfunction.
Swelling: Particularly in the legs and ankles, due to fluid retention.

diseases.name: Hemoperitoneum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemoperitoneum is a medical condition characterized by the presence of blood in the peritoneal cavity, the space within the abdomen that houses various organs, including the liver, stomach, and intestines. This condition can arise from various causes, ranging from trauma to underlying medical issues, and can lead to serious complications if not promptly addressed. Understanding hemoperitoneum is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ultimately aiding in better health outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemoperitoneum can vary depending on the amount of blood present and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Often severe and may be localized or diffuse.
Abdominal Distension: Swelling of the abdomen due to fluid accumulation.
Nausea and Vomiting: May occur as a response to pain or irritation in the abdomen.
Dizziness or Fainting: Resulting from blood loss and decreased blood volume.
Rapid Heart Rate: A compensatory mechanism due to low blood pressure.

diseases.name: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition characterized by an overactive immune response. This hyper-inflammatory syndrome can lead to significant organ damage and, if left untreated, can result in death. Understanding HLH is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of HLH, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of HLH can vary widely but often include:
Fever: Persistent high fever is a hallmark symptom.
Enlarged Liver and Spleen: Hepatosplenomegaly is common.
Cytopenias: Low blood cell counts, including anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia.
Rash: A rash may develop, often resembling other conditions.
Neurological Symptoms: Confusion, seizures, or other neurological deficits can occur.

diseases.name: Hemophilia A - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemophilia A is a rare but significant genetic disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot. This condition can lead to excessive bleeding, which can be life-threatening if not managed properly. Understanding Hemophilia A is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families, caregivers, and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Hemophilia A, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Individuals with Hemophilia A may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Excessive Bleeding: Prolonged bleeding after injuries, surgeries, or dental work.
Spontaneous Bleeding: Unexplained bleeding episodes, particularly into joints and muscles.
Bruising: Easy bruising, often with large, painful bruises.
Joint Pain and Swelling: Bleeding into joints can cause pain, swelling, and limited mobility.
Nosebleeds: Frequent or prolonged nosebleeds without an obvious cause.
Blood in Urine or Stool: Hematuria (blood in urine) or melena (black, tarry stools) can occur.

diseases.name: Hemophilia B - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemophilia B is a rare but significant genetic disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot. This condition can lead to excessive bleeding, which can be life-threatening if not managed properly. Understanding Hemophilia B is crucial for those affected, their families, and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve quality of life and outcomes. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Hemophilia B.
symptoms: Individuals with Hemophilia B may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Prolonged Bleeding: Excessive bleeding from cuts, injuries, or dental work.
Spontaneous Bruising: Unexplained bruises that appear without any known cause.
Joint Pain and Swelling: Bleeding into joints can cause pain, swelling, and limited mobility.
Blood in Urine or Stool: Hematuria (blood in urine) or melena (black, tarry stools) can indicate internal bleeding.
Nosebleeds: Frequent or prolonged nosebleeds can be a symptom of Hemophilia B.

diseases.name: Hemophilia C - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemophilia C is a rare bleeding disorder that affects the blood's ability to clot properly. Unlike the more commonly known Hemophilia A and B, which are primarily associated with deficiencies in specific clotting factors, Hemophilia C is linked to a deficiency in factor XI. This condition can lead to prolonged bleeding after injuries, surgeries, or even spontaneously without any apparent cause. Understanding Hemophilia C is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Hemophilia C can vary widely among individuals but may include:
Prolonged Bleeding: Excessive bleeding after cuts, injuries, or surgeries.
Spontaneous Bleeding: Unexplained bleeding episodes, particularly in the joints or muscles.
Easy Bruising: Increased tendency to bruise easily.
Nosebleeds: Frequent or prolonged nosebleeds.
Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: Women may experience heavier than normal menstrual periods.

diseases.name: Hemophilic Arthropathy
diseases.description: Hemophilic arthropathy is progressive joint damage resulting from repeated bleeding into the joints (hemarthrosis) in people with hemophilia. Repeated blood accumulation in joint cavities leads to chronic synovitis, cartilage degradation, and joint destruction. The knees, ankles, and elbows are most commonly affected.
symptoms: Swollen, warm, painful joints after bleeding episode
Decreased range of motion
Progressive joint deformity
Muscle wasting around affected joints
Chronic joint pain and stiffness

diseases.name: Hemopneumothorax - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemopneumothorax is a medical condition characterized by the presence of both blood (hemorrhage) and air (pneumothorax) in the pleural cavity, the space between the lungs and the chest wall. This condition can arise from various causes, including trauma, disease, or medical procedures, and it poses significant health risks if not promptly diagnosed and treated. Understanding hemopneumothorax is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemopneumothorax can vary depending on the severity of the condition but often include:
Chest Pain: Sharp or stabbing pain in the chest, which may worsen with deep breathing or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of breathlessness, especially during physical activity.
Coughing: A persistent cough, which may produce blood-tinged sputum.
Rapid Heart Rate: Increased heart rate as the body attempts to compensate for reduced oxygen levels.
Pale or Bluish Skin: A sign of inadequate oxygenation, known as cyanosis.

diseases.name: Hemorrhagic Cystitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the bladder that leads to bleeding. This condition can be distressing and may significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding hemorrhagic cystitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hemorrhagic cystitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemorrhagic cystitis can vary in severity but often include:
Hematuria: The presence of blood in the urine, which may appear pink, red, or brown.
Dysuria: Painful urination or a burning sensation during urination.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little urine output.
Lower Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen or pelvic area.
Urinary Urgency: A sudden, strong need to urinate.

diseases.name: Hemorrhagic Stroke - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemorrhagic stroke is a critical medical condition that occurs when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures, leading to bleeding in or around the brain. This type of stroke is less common than ischemic stroke, which is caused by a blockage in a blood vessel, but it is often more severe and can lead to significant complications or even death. Understanding hemorrhagic stroke is essential for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and knowing when to seek medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of hemorrhagic stroke, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of hemorrhagic stroke is crucial for prompt medical intervention. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Severe Headache: Often described as the worst headache of one’s life.
Nausea and Vomiting: Accompanied by dizziness or loss of balance.
Altered Consciousness: Confusion, difficulty speaking, or loss of consciousness.
Weakness or Numbness: Particularly on one side of the body, affecting the face, arm, or leg.
Seizures: Sudden onset of seizures can occur in some cases.

diseases.name: Hemothorax - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hemothorax is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of blood in the pleural cavity, the space between the lungs and the chest wall. This condition can arise from various causes, including trauma, disease, or complications from medical procedures. Understanding hemothorax is crucial, as it can lead to serious health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding hemothorax.
symptoms: The symptoms of hemothorax can vary depending on the amount of blood in the pleural space and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: Often sharp and worsens with deep breathing or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of breathlessness.
Rapid Heart Rate: Increased heart rate as the body responds to blood loss.
Coughing Up Blood: Hemoptysis may occur if the bleeding is significant.
Pale or Clammy Skin: Signs of shock due to blood loss.

diseases.name: Henoch Schonlein Purpura - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Henoch-Schönlein Purpura (HSP) is a small-vessel vasculitis that primarily affects children but can also occur in adults. It is characterized by a distinctive rash, abdominal pain, joint pain, and kidney involvement. Understanding HSP is crucial, as early diagnosis and management can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of HSP, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Rash: A purplish rash, often resembling bruises, typically appears on the buttocks, legs, and sometimes the arms.
Joint Pain: Swelling and pain in the joints, particularly the knees and ankles, are common.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping and pain in the abdomen may occur, sometimes accompanied by gastrointestinal bleeding.
Kidney Involvement: Symptoms may include blood in the urine (hematuria) and protein in the urine (proteinuria), indicating kidney inflammation.

diseases.name: Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) is a serious condition that can arise in patients receiving heparin, a commonly used anticoagulant (blood thinner). This condition is characterized by a decrease in platelet count and an increased risk of thrombosis (blood clots), which can lead to severe complications. Understanding HIT is crucial for both healthcare providers and patients, as timely recognition and management can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia can vary, but common signs include:
Low Platelet Count: A significant drop in platelet levels, often detected through routine blood tests.
Thrombosis: Unexplained blood clots, which may occur in veins (deep vein thrombosis) or arteries (pulmonary embolism).
Skin Reactions: Red or purple spots on the skin, particularly at the injection site of heparin.
Other Symptoms: Patients may experience headaches, dizziness, or shortness of breath if clots affect blood flow.

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.description: Hepatitis A is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis A virus, usually spread through contaminated food or water or close contact with an infected person.
symptoms: Fever
Loss of appetite
Nausea or vomiting
Abdominal discomfort
Dark urine
Jaundice (yellowing of eyes or skin)

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.description: Hepatitis B is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus, spread through blood or body fluids. It can become chronic and lead to serious liver disease.
symptoms: Fever
Fatigue
Loss of appetite
Nausea or vomiting
Abdominal pain
Jaundice and dark urine

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.description: Hepatitis C is the most common contagious, blood-borne viral liver disease. And, most individuals with hepatitis C do not realize that they actually have it.
