This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of KSS, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Kearns Sayre Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Progressive External Ophthalmoplegia: Weakness of the eye muscles leading to difficulty in moving the eyes.
Pigmentary Retinopathy: A degenerative condition affecting the retina, which can lead to vision loss.
Cardiac Conduction Defects: Abnormalities in the heart's electrical system, which can lead to arrhythmias.
Muscle Weakness: Generalized weakness, particularly in the skeletal muscles.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals may experience sensorineural hearing loss.
Endocrine Disorders: Issues such as diabetes or thyroid dysfunction may occur.

diseases.name: Keep your Liver healthy to avoid Esophageal Varices
diseases.description: Esophageal varices are abnormal, enlarged veins present in the lower part of the esophageal tube which connects the throat to the stomach. This medical condition mostly occurs in people who are affected with serious liver diseases. They usually develop when there is a blockage in the normal blood flow to the liver. This blockage is caused due to a clot or scar tissue in the liver. Varices can turn out to be quite life-threatening if they rupture and bleed. So, you need to know more about these swollen veins on the esophagus lining and its complications.
symptoms: Esophageal varices do not usually cause any signs or symptoms, until they start bleeding. When this happens, you may experience:
Vomiting too much of blood i.e. hematemesis
Black, tarry and bloody stools
Light-headedness or unconsciousness
Stomach pain
Extremely low blood pressure
Shock
Pale, clammy skin
Irregular breathing

diseases.name: Keloid On Ear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keloids are a type of raised scar that can develop on various parts of the body, including the ear. They occur when the body produces excess collagen during the healing process, leading to an overgrowth of scar tissue. Keloids on the ear can be particularly significant due to their visibility and potential impact on a person's self-esteem. Understanding keloids, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for anyone affected by this condition.
symptoms: Keloids on the ear can present with various symptoms, including:
Raised, Firm Texture: Keloids are typically raised above the surrounding skin and feel firm to the touch.
Color Changes: They may appear pink, red, or darker than the surrounding skin.
Itching or Pain: Some individuals may experience itching or discomfort in the affected area.
Growth Over Time: Keloids can continue to grow, sometimes becoming larger than the original injury.

diseases.name: Keloid Scar - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keloid scars are a unique type of skin abnormality that can significantly impact an individual's appearance and self-esteem. Unlike regular scars, keloids extend beyond the original site of injury, forming raised, thickened areas of skin. They can occur anywhere on the body but are most commonly found on the chest, shoulders, and earlobes. Understanding keloid scars is essential not only for those who have them but also for healthcare providers and individuals interested in skin health. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding keloid scars.
symptoms: Keloid scars can present with various symptoms, including:
Raised, thickened skin: Keloids are typically elevated above the surrounding skin.
Color changes: They may appear pink, red, or darker than the surrounding skin.
Itching or discomfort: Some individuals experience itching or tenderness in the affected area.
Size variation: Keloids can grow larger than the original injury, sometimes reaching several centimeters in diameter.

diseases.name: Keloids and Hypertrophic Scars
diseases.description: Keloids are raised overgrowths of scar tissue that occur at the site of a skin injury. Unlike hypertrophic scars, keloids grow beyond the original wound boundaries and do not regress over time. They result from an overproduction of collagen during wound healing. Keloids can cause discomfort and cosmetic concerns.
symptoms: Thick, raised scar
Scar extends beyond original wound
Itching, pain, or tenderness
Firm, rubbery texture
Dark or pink discoloration

diseases.name: Keratitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keratitis is a medical condition that affects the cornea, the clear, dome-shaped surface that covers the front of the eye. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and, if left untreated, may result in serious complications, including vision loss. Understanding keratitis is crucial for maintaining eye health and ensuring timely treatment. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of keratitis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of keratitis can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Eye Pain: A sharp or dull pain in the affected eye is common.
Redness: The eye may appear red and inflamed.
Blurred Vision: Vision may become hazy or distorted.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, is a frequent symptom.
Tearing or Discharge: Increased tear production or discharge from the eye may occur.
Foreign Body Sensation: Many individuals report feeling as though there is something in their eye.

diseases.name: Keratoconjunctivitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keratoconjunctivitis is a term that encompasses inflammation of both the cornea and the conjunctiva, two critical components of the eye. This condition can significantly impact vision and overall eye health, making it essential for individuals to understand its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. With the increasing prevalence of eye-related issues in our modern world, awareness of keratoconjunctivitis is vital for early detection and effective management.
symptoms: Keratoconjunctivitis presents a range of symptoms, which may vary depending on the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Redness: The eye may appear red or bloodshot due to inflammation.
Itching and Burning: Patients often experience discomfort, which can be exacerbated by environmental factors.
Tearing: Increased tear production is common, especially in allergic cases.
Discharge: Bacterial infections may lead to a thick, yellow discharge, while viral infections may produce a watery discharge.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, can occur due to inflammation.

diseases.name: Keratoconus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keratoconus is a progressive eye condition that affects the shape and structure of the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. This condition is significant not only because it can lead to visual impairment but also due to its impact on the quality of life for those affected. As keratoconus progresses, the cornea thins and bulges into a cone-like shape, distorting vision and making it difficult to see clearly. Understanding keratoconus is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can help preserve vision and improve the overall quality of life for individuals diagnosed with this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of keratoconus can vary in severity and may include:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty seeing clearly, especially at night.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent.
Increased Sensitivity to Light: Bright lights may cause discomfort.
Frequent Changes in Prescription: A need for frequent updates to glasses or contact lens prescriptions.
Halos Around Lights: Especially noticeable at night.

diseases.name: Keratosis Pilaris - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Keratosis pilaris, often referred to as "chicken skin," is a common skin condition that affects many individuals worldwide. While it is generally harmless, its appearance can be bothersome for those who experience it. Understanding keratosis pilaris is essential not only for those who have it but also for healthcare providers and the general public. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of keratosis pilaris, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The primary symptoms of keratosis pilaris include:
Rough Bumps: Small, raised, and rough patches on the skin, often resembling goosebumps.
Red or Brownish Color: The bumps may appear red, brown, or skin-colored, depending on the individual's skin tone.
Dry Skin: The affected areas may feel dry and rough to the touch.
Itching or Irritation: Some individuals may experience mild itching or irritation, although this is not always the case.

diseases.name: Kerion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kerion is a significant dermatological condition that primarily affects the scalp, presenting as a painful, inflammatory mass. It is often associated with fungal infections, particularly those caused by dermatophytes, which are fungi that thrive on keratin-rich tissues. Understanding kerion is crucial not only for effective treatment but also for preventing potential complications that can arise if left untreated. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of kerion, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Kerion presents with a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Swollen Lesion: A painful, raised area on the scalp that may be red and inflamed.
Pus Formation: The lesion may ooze pus, indicating an inflammatory response to the fungal infection.
Hair Loss: The affected area may experience hair loss, which can be temporary or permanent.
Itching and Discomfort: Patients often report itching and discomfort in the affected area.
Fever: In some cases, systemic symptoms like fever may occur, especially if the infection is severe.

diseases.name: Kernicterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kernicterus is a serious neurological condition that arises from untreated jaundice in newborns. It is characterized by the accumulation of bilirubin in the brain, leading to irreversible damage. Understanding kernicterus is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers, as early detection and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding kernicterus.
symptoms: Kernicterus can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, often the first sign of elevated bilirubin levels.
Lethargy: Unusual sleepiness or lack of energy in the infant.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty breastfeeding or bottle-feeding.
High-Pitched Cry: An abnormal, high-pitched cry that may indicate neurological distress.
Muscle Tone Changes: Floppiness or rigidity in the limbs.
Seizures: In severe cases, infants may experience seizures due to brain damage.

diseases.name: Kidney Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kidney cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form in the kidneys, and they are quite common, especially as people age. While many individuals with kidney cysts experience no symptoms and require no treatment, understanding their significance is crucial. Kidney cysts can sometimes indicate underlying health issues or lead to complications if not monitored properly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of kidney cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Most kidney cysts are asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause noticeable symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Flank Pain: Discomfort or pain in the side or back, often on the side of the affected kidney.
Abdominal Pain: Generalized pain in the abdomen, which may be related to the size or location of the cyst.
Blood in Urine: Hematuria, or blood in the urine, can occur if a cyst ruptures or irritates the kidney.
Frequent Urination: Increased urgency or frequency of urination may be experienced.
High Blood Pressure: Kidney cysts can sometimes lead to hypertension.

diseases.name: Kidney disease - Stages, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The kidneys are a pair of bean-shaped organs responsible for eliminating waste from our body. Kidneys also ensure fluid and mineral balance, are involved in red blood cell production, vitamin D metabolism etc. Kidney disease can be acute (sudden) or chronic (gradually, over a period of time). Acute kidney failure happens suddenly or within a few hours or days. Acute kidney failure is not permanent but it needs immediate medical attention. Chronic kidney disease happens gradually over a period of time and in progressive stages. Even if one kidney is damaged, the other kidney carry out all the functions. In some cases, the kidney disease is diagnosed only when it reaches the advanced stage, which can later lead to kidney failure, if left untreated.
symptoms: Increased urination
Blood in urine
Fatigue
Uncontrollable high blood pressure
Loss in appetite
Nausea and Vomiting
Anaemia
Oedema
Sleeping problem
Persistent itching
Muscle cramps
Shortness of breath

Kidney disease is a progressive disease, hence gets worse as time passes. Right at the onset of symptoms, we suggest you to visit the Nephrologist. The Nephrologist will initially ask you few questions related to your family history, blood pressure, diabetes etc.

diseases.name: Kidney Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A kidney infection, medically known as pyelonephritis, is a type of urinary tract infection (UTI) that begins in the bladder or urethra and can spread to one or both kidneys. It is a serious medical condition that can lead to permanent kidney damage if left untreated. Kidney infections are more common in women but can affect anyone, regardless of age or gender. Prompt diagnosis and treatment are critical to prevent complications and protect kidney function.
symptoms: The symptoms of a kidney infection can range from mild to severe, depending on the extent of the infection. Early detection is crucial to prevent the infection from spreading and causing complications.
Pain or Tenderness in the Lower Back or Sides: This is one of the most common symptoms of kidney infection, and the pain can be sharp or dull, often on one side or both.
This is one of the most common symptoms of kidney infection, and the pain can be sharp or dull, often on one side or both.
Fever and Chills: A high fever accompanied by chills is a classic sign of infection. The body’s immune system is trying to fight off the bacteria.
A high fever accompanied by chills is a classic sign of infection. The body’s immune system is trying to fight off the bacteria.
Painful Urination: A burning sensation during urination or a constant urge to urinate is common with kidney infections.
A burning sensation during urination or a constant urge to urinate is common with kidney infections.
Cloudy, Bloody, or Foul-Smelling Urine: The presence of blood or an unusual odor in the urine may indicate a kidney infection or other urinary tract problems.
The presence of blood or an unusual odor in the urine may indicate a kidney infection or other urinary tract problems.
Fatigue and Weakness: The body’s response to infection can lead to overwhelming fatigue and feelings of weakness.
The body’s response to infection can lead to overwhelming fatigue and feelings of weakness.
Nausea and Vomiting: As the infection worsens, nausea and vomiting may occur, often accompanied by dehydration.
As the infection worsens, nausea and vomiting may occur, often accompanied by dehydration.
Confusion (in Older Adults): Older adults may experience confusion or disorientation, particularly if the infection becomes severe.
Older adults may experience confusion or disorientation, particularly if the infection becomes severe.

diseases.name: Kidney Stones - Symptoms, Causes, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Diseases and Conditions
symptoms: Kidney stones often go unnoticed until they start moving inside the kidney or pass into the ureter (the tube that connects the kidney to the bladder). Once this happens, they can block urine flow and trigger painful symptoms.
Severe, sharp pain in the back, side, lower abdomen, or groin. The pain may come in waves and vary in intensity.
Pain that radiates to the abdomen, groin, or under the ribs.
Burning sensation or pain while urinating.
Frequent urge to urinate or passing only small amounts of urine.
Blood in urine (hematuria): urine may appear pink, red, or brown.
Cloudy or foul-smelling urine.
Nausea and vomiting due to intense pain.
Fever and chills (if an infection is also present).
Excessive sweating may accompany painful episodes.
A non-invasive procedure that uses sound shock waves to break stones into small fragments that can pass in urine.
Usually performed under light anesthesia.
May cause temporary side effects like blood in urine, bruising, or discomfort as fragments pass.
A thin scope (ureteroscope) is passed through the urethra and bladder into the ureter.
The stone is either removed or broken into smaller pieces using special instruments or laser energy.
A temporary stent may be placed in the ureter to help healing.
Recommended for large or complex stones .
A small incision is made in the back to access the kidney, and the stone is broken and removed using special instruments.
Performed under general anesthesia, with a short hospital stay.
Rarely needed, only if other methods fail or are not feasible.
Involves direct removal of the stone through a surgical incision.

diseases.name: Kienbocks Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kienbock's Disease is a rare but significant condition that affects the wrist, specifically the lunate bone, which is one of the eight small bones in the wrist. This disease is characterized by the avascular necrosis (death of bone tissue due to a lack of blood supply) of the lunate, leading to pain, dysfunction, and potential long-term complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding Kienbock's Disease is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life.
symptoms: Kienbock's Disease presents with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in intensity depending on the stage of the disease. Common symptoms include:
Wrist Pain: Often the first symptom, which may worsen with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation around the wrist joint.
Reduced Range of Motion: Difficulty in moving the wrist or fingers.
Tenderness: Pain when pressing on the wrist, particularly over the lunate area.
Weakness: A feeling of instability or weakness in the wrist.

diseases.name: Klebsiella Pneumoniae infection - Symptoms, Risks, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Klebsiella Pneumoniae are common bacteria that are usually harmless when they are present in the intestines, But can be dangerous if they enter into the other parts of the body, especially if people are already ill. They can convert into “superbugs” that are almost impossible to fight with common antibiotics. They can cause pneumonia , infect the wounds or blood and lead to other serious problems.
symptoms: The symptoms are dependent on the location of the infection. For instance, if bacteria cause pneumonia, the patient can suffer from:
Fever
Cough
Chest pain
Shortness of breath
Mucus , which can be thick and bloody
Klebsiella pneumonia can also affect other parts of the body. For instance, the surgical wound may be infected. Other infections include that of :
Blood (bacteremia or septicemia)
Brain (meningitis)
Heart ( endocarditis )
Skin ( cellulitis )
Urinary tract (UTIs)

diseases.name: Kleine Levin Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kleine Levin Syndrome (KLS) is a rare neurological disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of excessive sleepiness, altered behavior, and hyperphagia (excessive eating). Often referred to as "Sleeping Beauty Syndrome," KLS primarily affects adolescents and young adults, leading to significant disruptions in daily life and functioning. Understanding KLS is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for their families and healthcare providers, as early recognition and management can greatly improve quality of life.
symptoms: Kleine Levin Syndrome is characterized by a range of symptoms that can vary in severity and duration. The most common symptoms include:
Excessive Sleepiness: Individuals may sleep for 18 to 20 hours a day during episodes, waking only for brief periods.
Altered Behavior: Confusion, irritability, and mood swings are common, with some individuals exhibiting hypersexuality or inappropriate behavior.
Hyperphagia: An overwhelming urge to eat, often leading to binge eating during episodes.
Cognitive Impairment: Difficulty concentrating, memory problems, and disorientation may occur during episodes.
Hallucinations: Some individuals may experience visual or auditory hallucinations during sleep episodes.

diseases.name: Kleptomania - Symptoms, Causes, Risks, Diagnosis, and Treatment
diseases.description: Kleptomania is characterized by an uncontrollable, recurring urge to steal. It shares similarities with mood and addictive disorders. This is a disorder that occurs very rarely but can be extremely distressing.
symptoms: The signs of kleptomania are as follows:
Inability to control your strong desire to steal things
An uncontrollable urge to steal an item you do not need or that you can easily afford
Feelings of increased anxiety , stress, and/or arousal before the theft
Feelings of relief, gratification, and/or pleasure during the theft
Feelings of intense guilt, fear of arrest, self-loathing, remorse, and/or shame after the theft
Repetition of these urges in the same pattern
Presence of other disorders such as anxiety, eating, and substance abuse
The occurrence of kleptomania episodes that are spontaneous and without collaboration or planning

diseases.name: Klinefelter Syndrome or XXY Syndrome - Symptoms and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Chromosomes are responsible for carrying our genetic information and are present within every cell in our body. The ‘sex chromosomes’, either ‘X’ or ‘Y’, are a pair of chromosomes that denotes a baby’s genetic sex. A female fetus carries two X chromosomes (XX), while a male carries one X chromosome and one Y chromosome (XY). Occasionally, a male child is born with an extra X chromosome known as Klinefelter Syndrome or XXY syndrome.
symptoms: While most males with XXY syndrome are diagnosed in adulthood, multiple symptoms are indicating the condition across various stages of maturity. Current diagnosis is made on the extent of these symptoms:
Based on age, the symptoms of XXY syndrome vary as illustrated below:
Stunted motor development
Hernia
Testicles that have not descended into the scrotal sac
Slower to learn to talk and unusually quiet
Weak musculature
Delayed onset of puberty or puberty is incomplete
Taller than expected based on the average height of the family
Relatively broader hips, short torso, longer limbs
Small penis and testicles
Relatively leaner musculature and scanty body or facial hair
Gynecomastia (abnormally large breast tissue in a male)
Weak bones
Socially inept due to low confidence, shyness, lower energy levels and difficulty connecting with peers
Learning disorders such as Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder , under-developed problem-solving skills
Behavioural issues including stunted maturity and impulsive nature
Low sperm count leading to infertility
Low libido
Lower testosterone levels
Erectile dysfunction
Larger breast tissues than typical males
More belly fat
Leaner musculature
Scanty beard or body hair
Degenerating bones

diseases.name: Kluver Bucy Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kluver-Bucy Syndrome (KBS) is a rare neurological disorder that arises from damage to specific areas of the brain, particularly the temporal lobes. This condition is significant not only because of its unique symptoms but also due to its implications for understanding the brain's role in behavior and emotion. KBS can profoundly affect an individual's personality, emotional responses, and social interactions, making it a critical area of study in neurology and psychiatry.
symptoms: Kluver-Bucy Syndrome presents a range of symptoms that can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Hyperphagia: An uncontrollable urge to eat excessively, often leading to weight gain.
Hypersexuality: Increased sexual behavior or inappropriate sexual advances.
Agnosia: Difficulty recognizing familiar objects or people.
Emotional Changes: A lack of fear or anxiety, leading to risky behaviors.
Memory Issues: Problems with short-term memory and learning new information.
Changes in Social Behavior: Difficulty in social interactions, often appearing overly friendly or inappropriate.

diseases.name: Knee Arthritis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: knee Arthritis is one of the most common causes of knee pain. Along with pain, one can notice swelling and stiffness in the knee joint. Different types of arthritis can affect your knee, and each type is treated differently depending on the symptoms and location in the knee joint affected.
symptoms: Every individual may experience a different set of knee arthritis symptoms. The common signs and symptoms include:
Swelling in the knee
Stiffness
Knee tenderness
Pain while moving the leg
An obvious deformity in the knee joint
Limited range of motion
Crepitus, a popping or clicking sound in the knee joint during movement
Weakness in the knee joint
Unstable knee

diseases.name: Knee Cartilage Injury
diseases.description: Cartilage is the white, flexible but firm connective tissue, which covers the ends of the bones. Cartilage provides a smooth cushion, letting the bones of the joint to move effortlessly without painful contact. Although cartilage is tough, it can be damaged either suddenly due to an injury or degenerate from general wear and tear or due to any infection or inflammatory disease.

diseases.name: Knee Problems
diseases.description: The knee is the largest joint in the body. Knee problems are very common, and they occur in people of all ages. Knee problems can interfere with many things, from participation in sports to simply getting up from a chair and walking. Many types of minor knee problems can be treated with self-care and do not require medical treatment.
symptoms: Pain
Swelling and stiffness
Redness and warmth to the touch
Weakness or instability
Popping or crunching noises
Inability to fully straighten the knee

diseases.name: Know Why Respiratory Tract Infection is Common in Winter
diseases.description: As the temperatures slowly dip, you start getting out your blankets, sweaters, socks, and warmers from your closet. Winters are usually synonymous with staying under a warm blanket, drinking a hot cup of coffee or tea, and wearing your warmest clothes. But it also sees many of us getting infected with colds, flu , and other respiratory tract infections.

diseases.name: Know Your Hepatitis Risk
diseases.description: Hepatitis is not a disease that affects only those involved in risky behaviour. Any individual can be at risk if he/she, for example:

diseases.name: Knuckle Pads - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Knuckle pads, also known as dorsal hand nodules or knuckle pads of the fingers, are benign growths that can develop on the knuckles. While they are not typically harmful, their presence can be a source of discomfort or cosmetic concern for many individuals. Understanding knuckle pads is essential for recognizing their significance, potential causes, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of knuckle pads, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Knuckle pads are characterized by the following symptoms:
Firm, Raised Lesions: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of firm, raised nodules on the knuckles.
Painlessness: In most cases, knuckle pads are painless and do not cause discomfort.
Color Variation: The color of knuckle pads can range from skin-colored to slightly darker than the surrounding skin.

diseases.name: Koebner Phenomenon - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The Koebner Phenomenon is a fascinating and significant dermatological response that can occur in individuals with certain skin conditions. Named after the German dermatologist Heinrich Koebner, this phenomenon refers to the development of skin lesions in response to trauma or injury. Understanding the Koebner Phenomenon is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can influence the management of various skin disorders, particularly psoriasis and other autoimmune conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the Koebner Phenomenon, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of the Koebner Phenomenon can vary depending on the underlying skin condition. However, common symptoms include:
New Lesions: The appearance of new skin lesions at the site of trauma, which may resemble existing lesions.
Itching or Burning: The affected area may be itchy or cause a burning sensation.
Redness and Inflammation: The skin around the new lesions may appear red and inflamed.
Scaling or Crusting: In cases related to psoriasis, the new lesions may be scaly or crusted.

diseases.name: Kwashiorkor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition that primarily affects children, particularly in developing countries where food scarcity is prevalent. It is characterized by a deficiency in protein intake despite an adequate caloric intake. The significance of Kwashiorkor lies in its potential to cause severe health complications, including growth retardation, immune dysfunction, and even death if not treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Kwashiorkor, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Kwashiorkor presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Edema: Swelling in the legs, feet, and abdomen due to fluid retention.
Irritability: Affected children may become unusually irritable or lethargic.
Skin Changes: Skin may become dry, flaky, or discolored, and may develop lesions or sores.
Hair Changes: Hair may become thin, brittle, or lose its color, often referred to as "flag sign" hair.
Growth Retardation: Children may fail to grow or gain weight as expected.
Weakness: Generalized weakness and fatigue are common due to muscle wasting.

diseases.name: Kyphosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Kyphosis is a spinal condition characterized by an excessive curvature of the thoracic spine, leading to a hunchback appearance. While some degree of spinal curvature is normal, kyphosis can lead to significant physical and emotional challenges. Understanding kyphosis is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can impact mobility, posture, and overall quality of life.
symptoms: Common symptoms of kyphosis include:
Visible Curvature: An abnormal hunchback appearance.
Back Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper back, which may worsen with activity.
Stiffness: Reduced flexibility in the spine.
Fatigue: Increased tiredness due to muscle strain from maintaining posture.
Breathing Difficulties: In severe cases, the curvature can compress the lungs, leading to respiratory issues.

diseases.name: Labial Adhesions - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Labial adhesions, also known as labial fusion, is a condition that affects the labia minora, the inner folds of skin surrounding the vaginal opening. This condition is particularly significant in pediatric populations, as it can lead to discomfort, urinary issues, and potential complications if left untreated. Understanding labial adhesions is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and appropriate management.
symptoms: Labial adhesions can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Pain or Discomfort: This may occur during urination or sexual activity.
Difficulty Urinating: Adhesions can obstruct the urinary opening, leading to straining or incomplete voiding.
Vaginal Discharge: Increased discharge may occur due to irritation or infection.
Itching or Burning: These sensations can result from inflammation or irritation of the affected area.

diseases.name: Labyrinthitis: Symptoms, Causes, Tests and Treatment
diseases.description: Among the many conditions that may affect human ears, labyrinthitis is a significant condition . It is an inflammation of the inner portion of the ear called the labyrinth. Labyrinthitis can, in rare instances, result in long-term balance problems and permanent hearing loss if left untreated. Therefore, recognising the symptoms early and treating it is essential. This blog is a comprehensive guide on labyrinthitis, its symptoms, causes, and treatment options available.
symptoms: Labyrinthitis symptoms appear abruptly and may remain fairly severe for several days. After that, they usually start to fade. But a sudden shifting or movement of the head may bring it back. Typically, this ailment doesn’t cause any pain.

Some symptoms of labyrinthitis are vertigo, balance issues, and dizziness. nausea & vomiting , tinnitus , which causes ringing or buzzing in the ear, hearing loss in the high-frequency range in one ear, and Nystagmus (involuntary eye movements} are some other symptoms. Permanent hearing loss is a problem that occurs in extremely rare circumstances.

diseases.name: Lactic Acidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lactic acidosis is a serious medical condition characterized by an accumulation of lactic acid in the body, leading to a decrease in blood pH. This condition can arise from various underlying issues and can have significant implications for health. Understanding lactic acidosis is crucial, as it can be a sign of severe underlying health problems and may require immediate medical attention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding lactic acidosis.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of lactic acidosis is essential for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate as the body attempts to compensate for acidosis.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal distress can occur as the body reacts to metabolic changes.
Weakness and Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness and lack of energy.
Confusion or Disorientation: Changes in mental status due to decreased oxygen delivery to the brain.
Muscle Pain or Cramps: Discomfort in muscles as lactic acid builds up.

diseases.name: Lactose Intolerance - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lactose intolerance is a common digestive condition that affects millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the body is unable to properly digest lactose, a sugar found in milk and dairy products. This condition can lead to uncomfortable symptoms and can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Understanding lactose intolerance is essential for those affected, as well as for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of lactose intolerance, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Lactose intolerance can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which typically occur within a few hours after consuming lactose-containing foods or beverages. Common symptoms include:
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Diarrhea: Loose, watery stools that may occur frequently.
Gas: Increased flatulence or belching.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the stomach area.
Nausea: A feeling of sickness that may be accompanied by vomiting.

diseases.name: Lagophthalmos - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lagophthalmos is a medical condition characterized by the inability to fully close the eyelids. This condition can lead to various complications, including dry eyes, corneal damage, and even vision loss if left untreated. Understanding lagophthalmos is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can significantly impact quality of life and ocular health. In this comprehensive article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding lagophthalmos.
symptoms: Lagophthalmos can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity depending on the underlying cause.
Inability to Close Eyes: The most obvious symptom is the inability to fully close the eyelids, which may be noticeable during sleep or when blinking.
Dry Eyes: Patients often experience dryness, irritation, and a gritty sensation in the eyes due to exposure.
Redness and Inflammation: The exposed conjunctiva may become red and inflamed, leading to discomfort.
Tearing: Paradoxically, some individuals may experience excessive tearing as the eyes attempt to compensate for dryness.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to light (photophobia) may occur due to corneal exposure.

diseases.name: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Langerhans cell histiocytosis, or histiocytosis X, is an uncommon condition primarily occurring in children. It stands out by an unusual proliferation of a type of immune cell called histiocytes. The condition mainly develops in toddlers and young children. In rare cases, adults can develop it too.
symptoms: The signs of Langerhans cell histiocytosis are noticed in various body parts. But it is prominent in the skin and bones. It also affects multiple internal organs, including the liver, lungs, brain, spleen, and lymph nodes.
Your child may experience mild to severe symptoms. But some children develop a severe form of the disorder that affects several body parts.
The following are the signs and symptoms of Langerhans cell histiocytosis:
Skin: Children born with the disorder develop red, scaly scalps, often confused with cradle cap – a common skin condition. You may notice red, scaly bumps in the skin folds of your child.
Liver: Severe cases of the disorder only affect the liver. Therefore, your child may appear jaundiced, and your child’s blood clots slower.

Lymph nodes: These glands are behind the ears, neck, and other body places. With the disorder, your child may experience inflammation of the lymph nodes. Sometimes, they may also develop breathing issues and cough.
Bone: Your child may develop bone lesions, extreme pain, and a limp in the legs.
Teeth and gums: Swelling in the gums. Your child may also lose teeth too.
Eyes: It affects vision or may cause your child’s eyes to bulge
Central nervous system: You may notice that your child complains of constant and chronic headaches , dizziness, vomiting , excessive thirst, and frequent urination
Ear: Frequent and regular infection and discharge from your child’s ear

Pituitary gland: It is present at the base of the brain that produces hormones. Hormones are responsible for several bodily functions. When the pituitary gland gets affected, the child may experience delayed puberty, infertility , excessive urination, and thyroid issues.
Other general signs include the following:
Fever
Tiredness
Fatigue
Irritability
Not gaining weight
Anemia
Seizures
Other underlying health conditions may also cause the symptoms mentioned above. Therefore, seeking proper medical attention and receiving the appropriate diagnosis is crucial.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Large Granular Lymphocytic Leukemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Large Granular Lymphocytic Leukemia (LGL) is a rare form of blood cancer that primarily affects the lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell crucial for the immune system. This condition is characterized by the proliferation of large granular lymphocytes, which can lead to various health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding LGL is essential not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers, as it can significantly impact quality of life and overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of LGL can vary widely among individuals, but common signs include:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Fever: Unexplained fevers that may come and go.
Night Sweats: Excessive sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss without changes in diet or exercise.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Enlarged lymph nodes, particularly in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Recurrent Infections: Increased susceptibility to infections due to a weakened immune system.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: Unexplained bruises or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts.

diseases.name: Laryngeal Papillomatosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Laryngeal papillomatosis is a rare but significant condition characterized by the growth of benign tumors, known as papillomas, in the larynx (voice box). These growths can lead to various complications, including voice changes and breathing difficulties. Understanding laryngeal papillomatosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of laryngeal papillomatosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of laryngeal papillomatosis can vary depending on the size and location of the papillomas. Common symptoms include:
Hoarseness: A change in voice quality is often the first noticeable symptom.
Breathing Difficulties: Larger papillomas can obstruct the airway, leading to stridor (a high-pitched wheezing sound).
Coughing: A persistent cough may occur, especially if the papillomas irritate the larynx.
Throat Pain: Discomfort or pain in the throat can accompany other symptoms.
Difficulty Swallowing: In some cases, papillomas can interfere with swallowing.

diseases.name: Laryngomalacia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Laryngomalacia is a condition that primarily affects infants and young children, characterized by the softening of the tissues of the larynx (voice box). This condition is significant because it is the most common cause of stridor (a high-pitched wheezing sound) in infants, often leading to concerns for parents and caregivers. While laryngomalacia is usually benign and self-limiting, understanding its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options is crucial for effective management and reassurance for families.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of laryngomalacia is stridor, which is a high-pitched sound that occurs during inhalation. Other symptoms may include:
Noisy Breathing: This may be more pronounced when the infant is active or upset.
Feeding Difficulties: Some infants may have trouble feeding due to breathing difficulties.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially during feeding or crying, may indicate severe airway obstruction.
Poor Weight Gain: Infants may struggle to gain weight due to feeding difficulties.

diseases.name: Laryngospasm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Laryngospasm is a sudden and involuntary contraction of the muscles in the larynx (voice box), which can temporarily obstruct the airway. This condition can be alarming, as it often leads to difficulty breathing, a sensation of choking, and can even result in panic. Understanding laryngospasm is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for caregivers and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of laryngospasm, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of laryngospasm can vary in intensity and duration but typically include:
Sudden Difficulty Breathing: A feeling of tightness in the throat and an inability to breathe normally.
Stridor: A high-pitched wheezing sound during breathing, particularly when inhaling.
Choking Sensation: A feeling of obstruction in the throat, which can lead to panic.
Coughing or Gagging: Reflexive actions that may occur as the body attempts to clear the airway.
Voice Changes: Hoarseness or loss of voice may occur during or after an episode.

diseases.name: Lassa Fever - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lassa Fever is a viral hemorrhagic illness that poses significant health risks, particularly in West Africa. Named after the town of Lassa in Nigeria where it was first identified in 1969, this disease is caused by the Lassa virus, which is primarily transmitted to humans through contact with infected rodents or their excreta. The significance of Lassa Fever lies not only in its potential for severe illness and death but also in its impact on public health systems in endemic regions. Understanding Lassa Fever is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of Lassa Fever can vary widely, ranging from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Fever: A sudden onset of fever is often the first sign of infection.
Weakness: Generalized weakness and fatigue are common.
Headache: Many patients report severe headaches.
Muscle Pain: Myalgia or muscle aches can occur.
Sore Throat: A sore throat may develop as the illness progresses.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms, including nausea and vomiting, are frequent.
Diarrhea: Some patients may experience diarrhea.

diseases.name: Latex Allergy: Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Latex allergy is a reaction to certain proteins found in natural rubber latex, which is a product made from the sap of Brazilian rubber trees. If a person has a latex allergy, the immune system in their body releases histamine to latex – mistaken as a harmful substance entering the body.
symptoms: Allergic reactions to latex often result in the form of a rash at the point of contact, known as contact dermatitis. The signs may include:
itchy hands
skin rash that may be warm to the touch
hives
eczema (denoted as weeping or cracking skin)
Although such reactions are usually temporary, they may begin to show up within minutes of exposure. In some instances, the reaction may also take several hours to develop.
Latex proteins may sometimes become airborne. When this happens, a hypersensitive person may unknowingly inhale them in and develop more severe reactions. These reactions may include:
swollen and red skin, lips, or tongue
runny or stuffy nose
shortness of breath (with or without wheezing)
abdominal pain
diarrhea
vomiting
rapid heartbeat
dizziness

Anaphylaxis, as a reaction to latex is quite rare, and if it happens, it may be life-threatening. Anaphylactic shock may also cause severe breathing difficulties, decreased blood pressure , or even death if it is untreated.

diseases.name: Lattice Degeneration - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lattice degeneration is a condition that affects the retina, the light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye. It is characterized by the thinning and weakening of the retinal tissue, which can lead to serious complications, including retinal detachment. Understanding lattice degeneration is crucial for early detection and management, as it can significantly impact vision if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of lattice degeneration, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Lattice degeneration often does not present noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Flashes of Light: Sudden flashes of light in the peripheral vision.
Floaters: Small specks or cobweb-like shapes that float across the field of vision.
Blurred Vision: Difficulty focusing or seeing clearly, particularly in low light.
Dark Shadows: The appearance of dark areas or shadows in the peripheral vision.

diseases.name: Leaky Heart Valve - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A leaky heart valve, medically known as valvular regurgitation, is a condition where one or more of the heart's valves do not close properly, allowing blood to flow backward instead of forward through the heart. This can lead to various complications, including heart failure, arrhythmias, and other serious cardiovascular issues. Understanding the significance of a leaky heart valve is crucial, as early detection and management can significantly improve outcomes and quality of life for affected individuals.
symptoms: Individuals with a leaky heart valve may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity or when lying down.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.
Swelling: Fluid retention in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may be mistaken for angina.

diseases.name: Lebers Congenital Amaurosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lebers Congenital Amaurosis (LCA) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects vision, leading to severe visual impairment or blindness from birth or early infancy. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the quality of life for affected individuals but also due to its implications for families and healthcare systems. Understanding LCA is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support for those affected and their families.
symptoms: The symptoms of Lebers Congenital Amaurosis can vary but typically include:
Severe Visual Impairment: Most infants with LCA have very limited vision or are completely blind.
Photophobia: Increased sensitivity to light is common.
Nystagmus: Involuntary eye movements may be observed.
Poor Eye Tracking: Difficulty in following moving objects.
Strabismus: Misalignment of the eyes may occur.

diseases.name: Left Anterior Fascicular Block - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Left Anterior Fascicular Block (LAFB) is a condition that affects the electrical conduction system of the heart. It is characterized by a delay or blockage in the electrical impulses that travel through the left anterior fascicle of the left bundle branch. This condition can be significant as it may indicate underlying heart disease and can affect the heart's ability to function properly. Understanding LAFB is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can help prevent complications and improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: LAFB may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when it does, they can include:
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: This may occur due to reduced blood flow.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area, which may indicate underlying heart issues.

diseases.name: Left Atrial Enlargement - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Left Atrial Enlargement (LAE) is a condition characterized by the abnormal enlargement of the left atrium, one of the four chambers of the heart. This enlargement can be a significant indicator of underlying heart disease and can lead to various complications if not addressed. Understanding LAE is crucial for early detection and management, as it can be associated with serious cardiovascular issues, including atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Left Atrial Enlargement, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Left Atrial Enlargement may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, individuals may experience:
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or at rest.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area, which may be related to underlying heart issues.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, especially during exertion.

diseases.name: Left Bundle Branch Block - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Left Bundle Branch Block (LBBB) is a condition that affects the heart's electrical conduction system, specifically the left bundle branch of the heart. This condition can have significant implications for heart health, as it may indicate underlying heart disease or other cardiovascular issues. Understanding LBBB is crucial for early detection and management, which can lead to better health outcomes.
symptoms: LBBB may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when it does, they can include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, particularly when standing up quickly.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may indicate underlying heart issues.

diseases.name: Left Posterior Fascicular Block - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Left Posterior Fascicular Block (LPFB) is a condition that affects the electrical conduction system of the heart. It is characterized by a delay or blockage in the electrical impulses that travel through the left posterior fascicle of the left bundle branch. Understanding LPFB is crucial because it can be an indicator of underlying heart conditions and may influence treatment decisions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of LPFB, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: LPFB may not always present with noticeable symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during exertion.

diseases.name: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy (LVH) is a condition characterized by the thickening of the heart's left ventricle, the chamber responsible for pumping oxygenated blood to the body. This thickening can lead to various complications, including heart failure, arrhythmias, and increased risk of cardiovascular events. Understanding LVH is crucial, as it often serves as a marker for underlying health issues, particularly hypertension and heart disease. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of LVH, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Many individuals with LVH may not experience noticeable symptoms initially. However, as the condition progresses, the following symptoms may arise:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity or at rest.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, especially during exertion.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats or a sensation of the heart racing.
Dizziness or Fainting: Lightheadedness or loss of consciousness, particularly during physical activity.

diseases.name: Legionnaire's Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Legionnaire's Disease is a severe form of pneumonia caused by the bacterium Legionella pneumophila . This disease is significant not only because of its potential severity but also due to its association with outbreaks linked to contaminated water sources, such as cooling towers, hot tubs, and large plumbing systems. Understanding Legionnaire's Disease is crucial for both public health and individual well-being, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Legionnaire's Disease can present with a variety of symptoms, which may appear 2 to 10 days after exposure to the bacteria. Common symptoms include:
Fever: Often high, accompanied by chills.
Cough: May be dry or produce mucus.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or rapid breathing.
Muscle Aches: Generalized body aches and fatigue.
Headache: Often severe and persistent.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

diseases.name: Leigh's Disease: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: There are many medical conditions that occur rarely and have a poor prognosis. Leigh’s disease is one such disorder.
symptoms: Leigh’s disease is characterised by symptoms which progress as time passes. Some earliest signs of this disorder are loss of appetite, irritability, poor suckling ability, and loss of head or motor control. The children may cry continuously and may experience seizures . They may also experience weakness, lactic acidosis, or a lack of muscle tone. However, the symptoms differ for each person. Some of the other symptoms are as follows:
Abnormal motor skills: As the central nervous system is affected, patients with Leigh’s disease suffer from uncoordinated and involuntary movements.
Low muscle tone: Patients also experience muscular hypotonia , otherwise known as low muscle tone. It shows signs during infancy.

Loss of developmental skills: Leigh’s disease affects the brain cells. Therefore, patients either do not reach the required milestones or there is a degeneration of already acquired developmental skills.
Failure to thrive: When the physical growth of the children is below the expected level is known as failure to thrive.
Difficulty in feeding: Patients suffer from eating-related issues such as sucking, chewing, or swallowing food.
Uncontrollable movements: In Leigh’s disease, a child may experience involuntary muscle contractions that lead to involuntary movements of the neck, trunk, or face.
Congestive heart failure : The failure of the heart to pump at a regular rate is often related to a defect in myocardial contraction.
Respiratory failure: When the lung cannot adequately exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide within the normal range, it is called respiratory failure.
If you notice any of the above-mentioned symptoms of the disease, seek medical help immediately.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Leiomyosarcoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Leiomyosarcoma is a rare and aggressive form of cancer that arises from smooth muscle tissue, which is found in various organs throughout the body, including the uterus, stomach, and blood vessels. This type of sarcoma is significant not only due to its rarity but also because of its potential to metastasize, or spread, to other parts of the body. Understanding leiomyosarcoma is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of leiomyosarcoma can vary depending on the tumor's location and size. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Often the first symptom, especially if the tumor is located in the abdomen.
Lump or Mass: A noticeable lump may develop, particularly in the case of tumors in the limbs or abdomen.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Patients may experience significant weight loss without trying.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur if the tumor affects the digestive tract.
Changes in Bowel Habits: This may include constipation or diarrhea, depending on the tumor's location.

diseases.name: Leishmaniasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Leishmaniasis is a complex and often misunderstood disease caused by parasites of the genus Leishmania. It is transmitted through the bite of infected sandflies and can lead to a range of health issues, from mild skin lesions to severe systemic disease. The significance of leishmaniasis lies not only in its impact on individual health but also in its public health implications, particularly in endemic regions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of leishmaniasis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of leishmaniasis vary depending on the type of infection:

Cutaneous Leishmaniasis: This form typically presents as skin sores or ulcers that may be painless or painful. The lesions can appear weeks to months after the sandfly bite and may heal spontaneously but can leave scars.

Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis: This type affects the mucous membranes, leading to symptoms such as nasal congestion, nosebleeds, and lesions in the mouth and throat. It can cause significant disfigurement if left untreated.

Visceral Leishmaniasis: Also known as kala-azar, this severe form affects internal organs, particularly the liver and spleen. Symptoms include fever, weight loss, anemia, and swelling of the spleen and liver. This form can be life-threatening if not treated promptly.

diseases.name: Leprosy - Symptoms, Types, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The bacterium, Mycobacterium leprae, causes a chronic, progressive bacterial infection known as leprosy. In this condition, the nerves of the limbs, the skin, the lining of the nose, and the upper respiratory tract are the most affected areas. Also known as Hansen’s disease, skin sores, nerve degeneration, and muscle weakness are the common symptoms of leprosy. It can also lead to severe deformity and significant disability if not treated correctly.
symptoms: Leprosy mainly affects the skin and peripheral nerves located outside of the brain and spinal cord. The eyes and the delicate tissue lining that lies in the inner area of the nose may also be affected. Other symptoms include:
Disfiguring skin lesions
Lumps or bumps that lasts for several weeks or months
Skin lesions that are pale in color
Weakness in the muscles
Skin lesions cause a loss of touch, warmth, or feeling of pain. Even after several weeks, the lesions do not completely heal and are paler than the typical skin tone or are irritated and inflamed.

diseases.name: Leptospirosis
diseases.description: Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease spread through contact with water or soil contaminated with urine from infected animals, often after heavy rains or floods.
symptoms: Fever and chills
Headache
Muscle aches
Red eyes
Nausea or vomiting

diseases.name: Lesch Nyhan Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lesch Nyhan Syndrome (LNS) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects males and is characterized by a combination of neurological and behavioral symptoms. This condition is significant not only due to its unique clinical presentation but also because it highlights the intricate relationship between genetics and behavior. Understanding LNS is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for affected individuals and their families.
symptoms: Lesch Nyhan Syndrome presents a range of symptoms that can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Neurological Symptoms: These may include developmental delays, intellectual disability, and motor dysfunction. Affected individuals may exhibit spasticity, dystonia, and involuntary movements.

Behavioral Symptoms: One of the hallmark features of LNS is self-injurious behavior, such as biting or scratching oneself. This behavior often emerges in early childhood and can be distressing for caregivers.
Gout and Uric Acid Accumulation: High levels of uric acid can lead to gout, characterized by painful swelling in the joints, particularly in the feet and hands.
Kidney Stones: The accumulation of uric acid can also result in kidney stones, leading to additional complications.

diseases.name: Lesser-Known Causes of Tooth Cavities: Prevention is Better Than Cure
diseases.description: Damage caused to the tooth, leading to a decayed tooth is what causes cavities. Tooth cavities and decay are one of the most common health problems people face across the world. They are common amongst children and adults, but in some cases, even infants can develop cavities.
symptoms: Depending on the severity and the location of the cavity, the symptoms and signs vary. In the initial stages, you may not notice any symptoms. But, as cavities get larger, you may start to notice some symptoms such as:
● Painful teeth.
● Tiny holes or openings in the teeth
● Coloured staining on the teeth
● Sensitive teeth.
● Sharp pain from consuming something cold or hot
● Spontaneous pain without any cause
If you notice any of these symptoms, immediately visit your nearest hospital for a dental checkup.

diseases.description: Diseases and Conditions

diseases.name: Leukoplakia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Leukoplakia is a condition characterized by the formation of white patches on the mucous membranes of the mouth, tongue, or other areas. While these patches may seem harmless, they can be a sign of underlying health issues and, in some cases, may lead to more serious conditions, including cancer. Understanding leukoplakia is crucial for early detection and management, making it an important topic for both patients and healthcare providers.
symptoms: Leukoplakia often presents as white or gray patches in the mouth that may vary in size and shape. These patches are typically painless and may not cause any discomfort. However, some individuals may experience:
A burning sensation in the mouth
Difficulty swallowing
Changes in taste
Red patches (erythroplakia) alongside white patches, which may indicate a higher risk of cancer

diseases.name: Lewy body dementia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Lewy Body Dementia (LBD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects an individual's memory, movement, and overall cognitive functions. It is the second most common type of progressive dementia, following Alzheimer's disease. Characterized by the presence of abnormal protein deposits in the brain known as Lewy bodies, this condition shares many symptoms with both Alzheimer's and Parkinson’s disease, making it difficult to diagnose. LBD not only impairs memory and cognitive function but also affects motor control, often leading to tremors, stiffness, and other movement-related issues.
symptoms: Memory Loss : Difficulty with short-term memory is a hallmark symptom of LBD. Affected individuals may struggle to remember recent events, conversations, or appointments.
Difficulty with short-term memory is a hallmark symptom of LBD. Affected individuals may struggle to remember recent events, conversations, or appointments.

Confusion and Disorientation : As LBD progresses, individuals may become confused about time, place, or identity. They may struggle to recognize familiar faces or become easily disoriented in known environments.
As LBD progresses, individuals may become confused about time, place, or identity. They may struggle to recognize familiar faces or become easily disoriented in known environments.
Difficulty with Attention and Concentration : LBD can cause individuals to have trouble focusing on tasks or maintaining attention, which can impair their ability to complete everyday activities.
LBD can cause individuals to have trouble focusing on tasks or maintaining attention, which can impair their ability to complete everyday activities.

Visuospatial Impairment : Difficulty interpreting visual information, such as judging distances or recognizing objects, is common in LBD. This can lead to problems with activities like driving or reading.
Difficulty interpreting visual information, such as judging distances or recognizing objects, is common in LBD. This can lead to problems with activities like driving or reading.

Fluctuating Cognition : Cognitive abilities in LBD patients often fluctuate. A person may appear alert and engaged at one moment, only to become confused or drowsy shortly after. This variability can make it difficult to diagnose and manage the condition.

Cognitive abilities in LBD patients often fluctuate. A person may appear alert and engaged at one moment, only to become confused or drowsy shortly after. This variability can make it difficult to diagnose and manage the condition.

Parkinsonism : Parkinsonism, including tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia (slowness of movement), is common in individuals with LBD. These symptoms are similar to those seen in Parkinson’s disease and often worsen as the disease progresses.

Parkinsonism, including tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia (slowness of movement), is common in individuals with LBD. These symptoms are similar to those seen in Parkinson’s disease and often worsen as the disease progresses.
Muscle Stiffness : Stiffness and rigidity in the muscles, particularly in the arms and legs, can make movement difficult and can contribute to falls and mobility issues.

Balance Problems : Impaired balance and coordination are common in LBD, increasing the risk of falls and injuries.

Shuffling Gait : Individuals with LBD may develop a slow, shuffling gait with reduced arm swing, similar to the gait seen in Parkinson’s disease.

Hallucinations : Visual hallucinations (seeing things that are not present) are common in LBD. A person may believe they see animals, people, or objects that aren’t really there.

Delusions : Delusions, or false beliefs, may also occur. These can include paranoia or the belief that someone is trying to harm them.

Depression and Anxiety : Individuals with LBD often experience mood changes, including depression and anxiety. This can be exacerbated by cognitive and motor difficulties.

Sleep Disturbances : People with LBD often have trouble sleeping and may experience REM sleep behavior disorder, in which they act out their dreams, potentially leading to injury.
