diseases.name: Myocardial Ischemia - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Myocardial ischemia is a condition that is characterized by inadequate blood flow in the coronary arteries (of the heart) owing to a partial or complete blockage of the arteries . The disease causes the heart muscles to lose their ability to pump blood and causes severe abnormal heart rhythms.
symptoms: Patients may have myocardial ischemia and still not present any signs and symptoms. However, it typically causes pressure with pain in the chest and pain on the left side of the body. Some common symptoms of myocardial ischemia include:
Rapid heartbeats
Pain in neck and shoulder
Pressure on chest
Chest discomfort
Heartburn
Feeling like indigestion/ choking
Sweating
Tiredness
Shortness of breath
Nausea and vomiting

diseases.name: Myocarditis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Inflammation in the muscular layer of the heart or the myocardium is termed as myocarditis. It affects heart muscles, making them inflamed, which restricts the ability to pump blood effectively.
symptoms: Early-stage myocarditis does not display any signs and symptoms. It can occur at any age. The symptoms of this condition may vary depending on the causes. The common symptoms are:
Chest pain
Rapid or abnormal heart rhythms
Shortness of breath, even at rest or during activity
Fluid retention in the legs, ankles and feet
Fatigue
Other symptoms of a viral infection like body aches, a headache , fever, diarrhea , a sore throat , or joint pain
Sometimes, symptoms may be similar to a heart attack . If you are having unexplained chest pain and shortness of breath, seek emergency medical help.

diseases.name: Myoclonic Seizure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myoclonic seizures are a type of seizure characterized by sudden, brief muscle jerks. These involuntary movements can occur in one or multiple muscle groups and may happen in isolation or as part of a more complex seizure disorder. Understanding myoclonic seizures is crucial not only for those who experience them but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of myoclonic seizures, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark of myoclonic seizures is the sudden muscle jerks, which can vary in intensity and duration. Other symptoms may include:
Twitching or jerking movements: These can affect one or multiple muscle groups.
Clumsiness: Individuals may experience difficulty with coordination.
Awareness: Most people remain aware during the seizure, although they may not remember the event afterward.

diseases.name: Myoclonus - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Myoclonus is when we experience a sudden and involuntary muscle spasm. Be it hiccups, shakes, or sleep starts – they all are a form of myoclonus. Read on to know everything you should be aware of about myoclonus.
symptoms: People who experience myoclonus define the symptoms as sudden jerks, spasms, and shock like shakes.
The nature of such jerks is:
Sudden
Unpredictable
Involuntary
Shock-like
Brief
In one part of the body or all over the body
Variable in intensity
Variable in frequency
Interference in regular movements like eating, sleeping, and walking

diseases.name: Myofascial Pain Syndrome: Causes, Symptoms and Treatments
diseases.description: Almost all of us have experienced muscle pain at some point. Mostly, muscle pain goes away on its own after a few days or weeks. Yet, in some cases, the pain persists and gets worse. Myofascial pain syndrome is a chronic pain syndrome where pressure on sensitive points in your muscles (trigger points) causes pain and sometimes even in unrelated parts of your body.
symptoms: A person suffering from myofascial pain syndrome may suffer from the following symptoms:
Muscle aches
Deep pain in muscles
Worsening pain when affected muscle is strained or stretched
Tender and painful knots in the muscle
Difficulty in sleeping with the pain
Weak, inflexible, and stiff muscles
Muscle pain that worsens and does not improve with time
Limited range of motion of muscles
Mood swings
Fatigue
Sleep and behavioral disturbances

diseases.name: Myopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myopathy is a term that encompasses a range of disorders affecting the muscles, leading to weakness and dysfunction. These conditions can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, making it essential to understand their causes, symptoms, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of myopathy, its implications, and the latest medical insights to help patients and their families navigate this complex condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of myopathy can vary widely depending on the specific type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Weakness: This is the hallmark symptom of myopathy, often affecting the proximal muscles (those closer to the center of the body) first.
Muscle Pain or Cramps: Some individuals may experience discomfort or cramping in the affected muscles.
Fatigue: Increased tiredness during physical activity is common.
Difficulty with Movement: Challenges with tasks such as climbing stairs, lifting objects, or even walking may arise.
Muscle Wasting: Over time, affected muscles may shrink in size due to disuse or damage.

diseases.name: Myositis (Inflammatory Muscle Disease)
diseases.description: Myositis refers to any condition causing inflammation in muscles. The most common forms are polymyositis, dermatomyositis, and inclusion-body myositis. These conditions are autoimmune diseases in which the body's own immune system attacks healthy muscle tissue, resulting in inflammation, swelling, pain, and eventual weakness.
symptoms: Muscle weakness (typically proximal muscles)
Falling or tripping
Difficulty swallowing
Skin rash (in dermatomyositis)
Fatigue
Weight loss
Fever

diseases.name: Myositis Ossificans - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myositis ossificans is a rare but significant medical condition characterized by the abnormal formation of bone tissue within muscles. This condition can lead to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility, significantly impacting a person's quality of life. Understanding myositis ossificans is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can arise from various causes and affect individuals differently. In this comprehensive article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding myositis ossificans.
symptoms: The symptoms of myositis ossificans can vary depending on the severity and location of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Localized pain in the affected muscle, which may worsen with movement.
Swelling: Swelling or tenderness in the muscle area.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness in the affected muscle.
Warmth: The area may feel warm to the touch due to inflammation.

diseases.name: Myositis: Types, Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Myositis is a disorder that signals the immune system to attack the muscle, causing inflammation of the muscles. There are different types of myositis, and depending on the type, the patient may find it challenging to move or use the affected muscles. It may also lead to infection, injury, medication, or autoimmune disease. The condition is incurable, but several treatment options can reduce the symptoms.
symptoms: Different types of myositis have their distinctive symptoms. However, the common symptoms are as follows:
Weakness in the muscle
Pain in the muscle and joint
Tiredness
Inflammation
Breathing and swallowing difficulties
Arrhythmia
Patients with polymyositis may experience difficulty performing regular movements, such as the following:
Standing up after sitting
Climbing stairs
Lifting
Reaching over the head
Other symptoms also include the following:
Weakness and pain in the muscle
Troubled swallowing and breathing
Frequent falling
Difficulty standing from a seated position
Constant dry cough
Fatigue
Sudden onset of fever
Skin thickening on the hands
The symptoms of inclusion body myositis are as follows:
Difficulty using hands and fingers to perform precise and mundane tasks, such as buttoning a shirt or tying a shoelace.
Gripping small objects
Troubled walking or standing
Swallowing
Frequently tripping, falling, and loss of balance
Difficulty in getting up from a seated position
Pain in the muscle and swallowing issues
Decreased deep tendon reflexes
The following are the symptoms of dermatomyositis:
Dry, scaly, or rough skin with rashes
Presence of lumps over the knuckles, elbows, and knees that are often raised and scaly and easily break out. These bumps are called Gottron’s papules or Gottron’s sign.
Difficult getting up from a seated position
Weakness in the muscle present in the neck, hip, back, and shoulders
Troubled swallowing
Hoarse voice
Pain in the muscle and inflammation of the joint
Solidified lumps of calcium under the skin
Abnormalities in the nail bed
Weight loss
Gastrointestinal ulcers
The symptoms of juvenile myositis are as follows:
The appearance of reddish-purple rash on the eyelids and joints. Sometimes these rashes appear similar to a heliotrope flower.
Moodiness or irritability
Stomach pains
Difficulties in motor functions, including trouble climbing stairs, standing from a seated position and getting dressed
Trouble reaching over, for example, shampooing or combing hair
Difficulty in lifting the head and swallowing
Weakness in the muscle and joint pain
Gottron’s papules
Swelling or redness of the skin around the fingernails
Solidification of calcium under the skin
Patients with toxic myositis present similar symptoms to other forms of myositis.

diseases.name: Myotonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myotonia is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by the delayed relaxation of muscles after voluntary contraction. This condition can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, affecting their ability to perform daily activities. Understanding myotonia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can help mitigate its effects and improve the overall well-being of those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of myotonia can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Muscle Stiffness: Prolonged muscle contraction leading to difficulty in relaxing muscles, especially after periods of inactivity.
Weakness: A general feeling of muscle weakness, particularly in the hands and legs.
Fatigue: Increased tiredness after physical activity.
Pain: Muscle pain or discomfort may accompany stiffness.
Difficulty with Fine Motor Skills: Challenges in tasks requiring precise movements, such as buttoning a shirt or writing.

diseases.name: Myotonia Congenita - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myotonia Congenita is a rare genetic disorder that affects muscle function, leading to prolonged muscle stiffness and difficulty in relaxation after contraction. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on daily activities but also due to its underlying genetic causes and the potential for misdiagnosis. Understanding Myotonia Congenita is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers to ensure timely diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of Myotonia Congenita can vary in severity and may include:
Muscle Stiffness: Prolonged stiffness after muscle contraction, particularly after periods of rest.
Delayed Relaxation: Difficulty in relaxing muscles after use, which can lead to cramping.
Weakness: Some individuals may experience muscle weakness, particularly after exertion.
Fatigue: Increased fatigue during physical activity due to muscle stiffness.
Pain: Muscle pain or discomfort may occur, especially after exercise.

diseases.name: Myxoid Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myxoid cysts, also known as mucous cysts, are benign (non-cancerous) growths that typically appear on the fingers or toes, particularly near the nail bed. While they are not harmful, they can cause discomfort and may affect the appearance of the affected area. Understanding myxoid cysts is essential for early diagnosis and effective management. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding myxoid cysts.
symptoms: Appearance: Myxoid cysts typically present as smooth, dome-shaped nodules that can range in color from skin-toned to bluish.
Location: They are most commonly found on the fingers, particularly near the nail bed, but can also occur on the toes.
Size: Cysts can vary in size, from a few millimeters to over a centimeter in diameter.
Texture: The cyst may feel soft or firm, and it may fluctuate in size.

diseases.name: Myxoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Myxoma is a rare type of tumor that primarily occurs in the heart, although it can also develop in other parts of the body. This benign tumor is significant due to its potential to cause serious health complications, particularly when it obstructs blood flow or leads to other cardiovascular issues. Understanding myxoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Myxomas can present with a variety of symptoms, depending on their size and location. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: This may occur due to obstruction of blood flow in the heart.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest can arise from pressure on the heart or surrounding structures.
Palpitations: Irregular heartbeats may be experienced as the tumor interferes with normal heart function.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness can result from reduced cardiac output.
Swelling: Edema in the legs or abdomen may occur if the tumor affects blood circulation.

diseases.name: Nabothian Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nabothian cysts are small, benign growths that can develop on the cervix, the lower part of the uterus that connects to the vagina. While they are generally harmless and often go unnoticed, understanding their significance is essential for women’s health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Nabothian cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Most Nabothian cysts are asymptomatic and do not cause any noticeable symptoms. However, some women may experience:
Vaginal Discharge: Increased mucus discharge may occur, especially if the cysts are larger.
Pelvic Discomfort: Rarely, larger cysts may cause mild discomfort or pressure in the pelvic area.

diseases.name: Nail Disorders
diseases.description: Nail disorders include a wide range of conditions affecting the fingernails and toenails, including infections (onychomycosis), inflammation (paronychia), structural changes (pitting, thickening), and nail changes associated with systemic diseases such as psoriasis or lupus. Some nail changes can be indicators of systemic health conditions.
symptoms: Nail discoloration (yellow, white, brown)
Thick or brittle nails
Nail pitting
Separation of nail from nail bed (onycholysis)
Ridges
Nail fold inflammation (paronychia)
Clubbing (associated with lung disease)

diseases.name: Nail Fungus
diseases.description: Nail fungus, also known onychomycosis, is a common fungal disorder which starts as a white or yellow spot right under the tip of your toenail or fingernail
symptoms: Some of the major symptoms of this disease are,
White or yellow spots under your finger or toenails
Discoloration of nails
Thickened nails
Distorted shape of your nails
Your nails may have debris under them, causing them to have a dark color
Slightly foul smell coming from your nails

diseases.name: Nail Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nail psoriasis is a chronic skin condition that affects the nails, leading to various changes in their appearance and structure. While psoriasis is commonly associated with skin lesions, its impact on the nails can be equally distressing for those affected. Understanding nail psoriasis is crucial not only for effective management but also for improving the quality of life for individuals living with this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nail psoriasis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Nail psoriasis can manifest in various ways, and symptoms may differ from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Pitting: Small depressions or indentations on the surface of the nails.
Discoloration: Nails may appear yellow, brown, or have a reddish hue.
Thickening: The nails may become thicker than normal, making them more prone to breakage.
Separation: The nail may lift away from the nail bed, a condition known as onycholysis.
Crumbling: The nails may become brittle and crumble easily.

diseases.name: Narcissistic Personality Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD) is a complex mental health condition characterized by an inflated sense of self-importance, a deep need for excessive attention and admiration, and a lack of empathy for others. This disorder can significantly impact an individual's relationships, work life, and overall well-being. Understanding NPD is crucial not only for those who may be affected by it but also for their loved ones and mental health professionals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Narcissistic Personality Disorder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Individuals with NPD may exhibit a range of symptoms, including:
Grandiosity: An exaggerated sense of self-importance and superiority.
Need for Admiration: A constant craving for attention and validation from others.
Lack of Empathy: Difficulty recognizing or caring about the feelings and needs of others.
Exploitation of Others: Using others to achieve personal goals without regard for their well-being.
Envy: Feeling envious of others or believing that others are envious of them.
Arrogant Behavior: Displaying haughty or disdainful attitudes towards others.
Preoccupation with Success: Obsessively thinking about fantasies of unlimited success, power, or beauty.

diseases.name: Narcolepsy - Causes, Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: People suffering from narcolepsy often find it hard to stay awake during most parts of the day. The exact cause of this sleep disorder is not known yet. However, research indicates some abnormal signaling in the brain and some genetic factors behind this disease.
symptoms: A neurochemical named hypocretin regulates the pattern of our falling asleep and waking up. People with narcolepsy have a deficient level of hypocretin, which may be the reason behind this disorder. Sometimes, genetic issues can also be considered a reason behind this disease. Some of the significant symptoms of this disease are,
Falling asleep anywhere, anytime, without any warning
Slurred speech or complete weakness of most of the body muscles for a few minutes
Sleep paralysis for a few minutes
REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep that makes the individual start dreaming within 15 minutes of falling asleep, even during daytime
Hallucinations

diseases.name: Nasal Cancer - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nasal cancer, also known as nasopharyngeal cancer, is a rare form of cancer that develops in the nasal passages or the paranasal sinuses. It can affect anyone, but it is more commonly diagnosed in older adults and people with certain risk factors. Though it is a relatively uncommon condition, nasal cancer can be challenging to detect early due to its subtle symptoms, which often mimic those of other conditions like sinus infections or allergies.
symptoms: The symptoms of nasal cancer can vary based on the location of the tumor and the stage of the disease. Early symptoms may be subtle and similar to those of other, less serious conditions, which can delay diagnosis. However, as the disease progresses, the symptoms typically become more noticeable and persistent.

Nasal Obstruction: One of the most common early signs of nasal cancer is persistent nasal congestion or blockage, particularly on one side of the nose. This symptom is often mistaken for a sinus infection or allergy-related congestion.

One of the most common early signs of nasal cancer is persistent nasal congestion or blockage, particularly on one side of the nose. This symptom is often mistaken for a sinus infection or allergy-related congestion.

Frequent Nosebleeds: Recurrent nosebleeds, especially those that occur without an apparent cause, may be a sign of nasal cancer. Tumors in the nasal cavity can damage blood vessels, leading to bleeding.
Recurrent nosebleeds, especially those that occur without an apparent cause, may be a sign of nasal cancer. Tumors in the nasal cavity can damage blood vessels, leading to bleeding.

Loss of Sense of Smell: People with nasal cancer may experience a diminished or complete loss of their sense of smell (anosmia). This can occur due to the tumor obstructing the olfactory nerve or other related structures.
People with nasal cancer may experience a diminished or complete loss of their sense of smell (anosmia). This can occur due to the tumor obstructing the olfactory nerve or other related structures.

Facial Pain or Pressure: Tumors in the nasal cavity or sinuses can cause pain or a feeling of pressure in the face, particularly around the nose, cheeks, or forehead. This may worsen with time and become more severe.
Tumors in the nasal cavity or sinuses can cause pain or a feeling of pressure in the face, particularly around the nose, cheeks, or forehead. This may worsen with time and become more severe.

Headaches: Persistent headaches, especially those localized to the forehead or around the eyes, can be indicative of nasal cancer. These headaches are often caused by pressure from the tumor on surrounding tissues.

Swelling or Lump in the Neck: Swelling or the appearance of a lump in the neck can be a sign that the cancer has spread to the lymph nodes. This is a more advanced symptom and may occur if the tumor has metastasized.

Vision Problems: In rare cases, nasal cancer may affect the eyes, causing double vision, blurred vision, or bulging eyes (proptosis), particularly if the tumor spreads to the surrounding structures.

diseases.name: Nasal Cavity and Paranasal Sinus Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Nasal cavity and paranasal sinus cancer refers to cancers that start inside the nose (nasal cavity) or in the air-filled spaces around the nose (paranasal sinuses: maxillary, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid). These areas sit close to critical structures such as the eyes, optic nerves, skull base, and brain, so precise, multidisciplinary care is essential. Although these cancers are uncommon, many are curable—especially when detected early and treated by a coordinated team using modern imaging, surgery, advanced radiation, and tailored systemic therapy. This comprehensive article explains what nasal cavity and paranasal sinus cancer is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, current treatments (endoscopic and open surgery, reconstruction, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and proton therapy in select cases), prognosis, prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Early symptoms resemble sinusitis or allergies; persistence and one‑sided (unilateral) symptoms are key clues.
Facial pain or pressure (often one‑sided), numbness of cheek, upper teeth, or palate
Loose teeth or non‑healing dental socket in the upper jaw
Swelling around the cheek, nose, or forehead
Double vision, eye bulging, tearing, or vision changes
Headaches, especially in the frontal or deep head region
A mass inside the nose or visible on exam
Neck lump (enlarged lymph node), though nodal spread is less common than in other head and neck sites
Any unilateral, persistent "sinus" symptom lasting longer than 4--6 weeks despite standard therapy deserves specialist evaluation.

diseases.name: Nasal Polyps - Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Nasal Polyps can be detected on your nasal passage lines or sinuses ; they are painless, soft, and noncancerous growths seen in these nose areas. They appear like teardrops or grapes in your rose and can form due to chronic inflammation. They are often related to asthma, allergies, recurring infection, immune disorders, or drug sensitivity.
symptoms: Running nose or blocked nose is a common symptom of polyps. Dust, chemicals, and fumes create more irritation to the nasal passage and lead to more infection. If there is a persistent irritation in the nasal cavity for more than 12 weeks or acute sinusitis, then nasal polyps occur. If polyps are small and soft, they will not create many problems. However, if the polyps are multiple or large-sized, they will block the nasal passage.
Headache – mild to severe pain in the face.
Persistent stuffy nose
Consistent congested nose.
Running nose
Losing a sense of taste and smell.
Snoring at night.
Sinus headache
Postnasal drip
Sense of pressure in the forehead and the face
Feeling of pressure in the face and forehead.
Nose bleeding – frequent at night.
Pain in the upper jaw – mild to severe.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: Nasal Septum Deviation – Symptoms, Causes & Treatment
diseases.description: Nasal septum deviation is a condition in which the nasal septum is displaced towards one side. Most people have a mild form of septal deformity and in most cases, it does not result in symptoms. But for people with moderate and severe cases of deviated septum, their breathing will be negatively impacted and this can lead to other serious conditions like sleep apnea and nose bleeds.
symptoms: The most obvious symptoms for a deviated septum are nasal congestion and difficulty in breathing through the nose. Due to this obstruction in the nasal airways, breathing through the nose may produce a sound (similar to a low whistle) when inhaling and exhaling.
Other symptoms associated with a deviated septum include:
Obstruction in the nasal cavity – Such obstructions can distort the shape of the nose. The blockage causes one of the nostrils to shrink in size, resulting in a bottleneck effect when breathing.
Nosebleed – A deviated septum can cause dryness on the surface of the nasal septum, which increases the chances of nosebleeds.
Facial pain – Facial pain can manifest itself on either side of the face.
Snoring/Loud breathing during sleep – The swelling of the intranasal tissues can be one of the many reasons why people tend to snore when sleeping.
Sinusitis – Obstructions in the nasal cavity can lead to blockage, causing inflammation of the tissue lining of the sinuses .
Preference for sleeping on a particular side – In order to optimize breathing through the nose, patients may prefer to sleep on one side, to favor the nostril that is not hampered.

diseases.name: Nasal Vestibulitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nasal vestibulitis is a condition that affects the nasal vestibule, the area just inside the nostrils. This condition is characterized by inflammation and irritation, which can lead to discomfort and various symptoms. Understanding nasal vestibulitis is essential, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nasal vestibulitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of nasal vestibulitis can vary in severity and may include:
Redness and Swelling: The affected area may appear inflamed and swollen.
Pain or Discomfort: Individuals may experience tenderness or pain in the nostrils.
Crusting: Dry, crusty lesions may form in the nasal vestibule.
Bleeding: In severe cases, the inflammation can lead to minor bleeding.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many individuals report an itchy or burning feeling in the nostrils.

diseases.name: Nasopharyngeal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) is a head and neck cancer that starts in the nasopharynx—the upper part of the throat behind the nose and near the base of the skull. Unlike many other head and neck cancers, NPC has a strong association with the Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) and is more common in certain regions (parts of Southeast Asia, North Africa, and the Middle East). Because the nasopharynx sits close to critical structures such as the Eustachian tubes, skull base, cranial nerves, and the brain, modern imaging and precise radiation therapy are central to safe and effective care. This article on NPC explains what it is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, evidence‑based treatments (radiation, chemotherapy, targeted and immune therapies, proton therapy in select cases), recovery, prevention strategies at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Early NPC often presents with subtle, one‑sided symptoms. Any symptom persisting beyond 2--3 weeks deserves evaluation by an ENT/head and neck specialist.
Headache or facial pain/pressure
Double vision, drooping eyelid, facial numbness or pain (cranial nerve involvement)
Persistent sore throat or a sensation of something behind the nose
Difficulty opening the mouth (trismus)
Unintended weight loss or fatigue
Because NPC sits near the skull base and cranial nerves, neurologic symptoms call for urgent specialist assessment.

diseases.name: Natural and Home Remedies for Migraine Headache
diseases.description: According to the Migraine Research Foundation, migraine is the third most predominant illness affecting people around the globe. Talking to a doctor can help a person understand and manage migraine better. Read to find out 15 natural and home remedies to manage the symptoms of migraine headaches.
symptoms: The predominant symptom of migraine is a headache. Often, people describe the pain as pounding or throbbing. It can begin as a dull pain that further develops into pulsing pain that is mild, moderate, or severe.

If left untreated, the headache may become moderate to severe. Pain may shift from one side of the head to the other, or may affect the front or back of the head. It may also affect the whole head. Some people also feel pain around their eyes or temple.
Other symptoms of migraine headaches include:
Sensitivity to light, noise, and smell
Vomiting and nausea, upset stomach, and abdominal pain
Loss of appetite
Feeling very warm or cold
Pale skin colour
Feeling tired
Dizziness and blurred vision
Tender scalp
Diarrhoea
Fever
Most migraine headaches last about four hours, although severe ones may last much longer.
Each phase of migraine attack may come with different symptoms:

Aura symptoms: Numbness and tingling Visual disturbances similar to a kaleidoscope, view blurry spots or see sparkles or lines Temporary loss of sight Weakness on one side of the body Speech changes Headache that may be accompanied by : Neck pain, stiffness Depression, giddiness and anxiety Sensitivity to light, smell, and sound Nasal congestion Insomnia Nausea and vomiting

diseases.name: Nearsightedness - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nearsightedness, also known as myopia, is a common refractive error that affects millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the eye is unable to focus light correctly, leading to blurred vision for distant objects while close objects remain clear. This condition can significantly impact daily activities, academic performance, and overall quality of life. Understanding nearsightedness is crucial for early detection, effective management, and prevention of potential complications.
symptoms: Blurry Vision: Difficulty seeing distant objects clearly, such as road signs or a blackboard in school.
Eye Strain: Discomfort or fatigue in the eyes, especially after prolonged near work.
Headaches: Frequent headaches can occur due to eye strain from squinting to see distant objects.
Squinting: A tendency to squint to improve focus on distant objects.

diseases.name: Neck Pain
diseases.description: Neck pain is a very common complaint that can result from various causes, including poor posture, muscle strain, worn joints, nerve compression, injuries, and diseases. Most neck pain improves gradually with home treatment. If neck pain persists, doctors might recommend other treatments.
symptoms: Pain that's often worsened by holding your head in one place for long periods
Muscle tightness and spasms
Decreased ability to move your head
Headache

diseases.name: Neck Sprain - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The seven bones of spinal column in the neck, called cervical vertebrae, are connected to each other by ligaments and muscles — the strong bands of tissue which act like a thick rubber bands. When a tear or a sprain (stretch) occur in one or more of these soft tissues due to a sudden movement like a hard fall or a a motor vehicle collision, it can cause the neck to bend to an extreme position. A neck sprain can occur without any visible injury as well.
symptoms: The symptoms of a neck sprain include:
Pain in the back of the neck that worsens with movement.
Headache at the back of the head.
Muscle tightness or spasm .
Stiffness in the neck or a reduced range of motion.
Difficulty sleeping and concentrating.
Increased irritability and fatigue .
Tingling or weakness in the arms.

diseases.name: Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Necrosis is a medical term that refers to the death of cells or tissues in the body. This condition can occur in any part of the body and can have significant implications for overall health. Understanding necrosis is crucial because it can lead to severe complications if not addressed promptly. In this article, we will explore the definition of necrosis, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of necrosis can vary depending on the location and extent of tissue death. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Affected areas may be painful, especially if there is inflammation.
Swelling: Swelling can occur due to inflammation and fluid accumulation.
Discoloration: The skin over necrotic tissue may appear discolored, often turning black or dark brown.
Foul Odor: In cases of necrotizing infections, a foul odor may emanate from the affected area.
Loss of Function: If necrosis occurs in a limb or organ, it may lead to loss of function in that area.

diseases.name: Necrotizing Enterocolitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC) is a severe gastrointestinal condition primarily affecting premature infants. It is characterized by inflammation and necrosis (tissue death) of the intestines, which can lead to serious complications and even death if not promptly treated. Understanding NEC is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of NEC, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of NEC can vary but often include:
Abdominal Distension: A swollen or bloated abdomen is a common sign.
Feeding Intolerance: Infants may refuse to feed or show signs of discomfort during feeding.
Vomiting: This may include bile-stained vomit, which can indicate a blockage.
Lethargy: Affected infants may appear unusually tired or inactive.
Temperature Instability: Fluctuations in body temperature can occur.
Blood in Stool: This can be a concerning sign and should be reported to a healthcare provider immediately.

diseases.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Necrotizing fasciitis is a severe and rapidly progressing soft tissue infection that can lead to significant morbidity and mortality if not recognized and treated promptly. Often referred to as "flesh-eating disease," this condition is characterized by the death of tissue and can affect any part of the body, although it most commonly occurs in the extremities and abdominal wall. Understanding necrotizing fasciitis is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early recognition and intervention can be life-saving.
symptoms: The symptoms of necrotizing fasciitis can develop rapidly and may include:
Severe pain: Often out of proportion to the physical findings.
Swelling and redness: The affected area may appear swollen and red.
Fever and chills: Systemic symptoms such as fever may accompany local symptoms.
Skin changes: The skin may develop blisters, discoloration, or necrosis (blackened tissue).
Fatigue: General malaise and fatigue are common.

diseases.name: Necrotizing Pancreatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Necrotizing pancreatitis is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition characterized by the death of pancreatic tissue due to inflammation. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications, including organ failure and death, if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding necrotizing pancreatitis is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of necrotizing pancreatitis can vary but often include:
Severe Abdominal Pain: This is usually the most prominent symptom, often described as a sudden onset of intense pain in the upper abdomen that may radiate to the back.
Nausea and Vomiting: Patients may experience persistent nausea and vomiting, which can exacerbate dehydration.
Fever: A low-grade fever may occur as the body responds to inflammation.
Rapid Heart Rate: Increased heart rate can be a sign of stress on the body due to pain or infection.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes may occur if bile ducts are obstructed.

diseases.name: Nemaline Myopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nemaline Myopathy (NM) is a rare genetic muscle disorder characterized by muscle weakness and the presence of rod-like structures called nemaline bodies in muscle fibers. This condition significantly impacts the quality of life for those affected, leading to varying degrees of disability. Understanding NM is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can help improve outcomes for patients and their families.
symptoms: The symptoms of Nemaline Myopathy can vary widely among individuals, but common signs include:
Muscle Weakness : This is the hallmark symptom, often affecting the proximal muscles (those closer to the center of the body) more than distal muscles.
Delayed Motor Milestones : Infants may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones such as sitting, crawling, or walking.
Hypotonia : Low muscle tone is often observed in infants, leading to a floppy appearance.
Respiratory Issues : Some individuals may experience breathing difficulties due to weak respiratory muscles.
Swallowing Difficulties : Dysphagia, or difficulty swallowing, can occur, leading to nutritional challenges.

diseases.name: Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome (NAS) is a serious condition that affects newborns who have been exposed to certain substances during pregnancy. As the prevalence of substance use during pregnancy rises, understanding NAS becomes increasingly significant for healthcare providers, parents, and society at large. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of NAS, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Infants with NAS may exhibit a range of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Irritability: Excessive crying and difficulty being soothed.
Tremors: Shaking or jitteriness, particularly in the hands and feet.
Sleep Disturbances: Difficulty sleeping or frequent waking.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty latching or feeding, leading to weight loss.
Vomiting and Diarrhea: Gastrointestinal disturbances that can lead to dehydration.
Hyperactive Reflexes: Exaggerated responses to stimuli.
Seizures: In severe cases, infants may experience seizures.

diseases.name: Neonatal Herpes Simplex - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neonatal Herpes Simplex is a serious viral infection that affects newborns, primarily caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). This condition is significant due to its potential to cause severe complications, including neurological damage and even death. Understanding neonatal herpes simplex is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure early detection and appropriate management.
symptoms: Symptoms of neonatal herpes simplex can vary widely, but common signs include:
Skin Lesions: Blisters or sores on the skin, often appearing within the first few weeks of life.
Fever: Elevated body temperature may indicate an infection.
Irritability: Infants may be unusually fussy or difficult to soothe.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty feeding or refusal to eat can be a sign of illness.
Lethargy: Excessive sleepiness or lack of responsiveness may indicate a serious condition.

diseases.name: Neonatal Lupus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neonatal lupus is a rare autoimmune condition that affects newborns, primarily those born to mothers with certain autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This condition is significant not only because of its potential health implications for the infant but also due to its connection with maternal health. Understanding neonatal lupus is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can significantly improve outcomes for affected infants.
symptoms: Neonatal lupus can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Rash: A characteristic rash may appear on the face, resembling a butterfly rash, or on other parts of the body. This rash typically resolves within a few months.
Heart Block: One of the more serious manifestations, congenital heart block can occur, leading to irregular heart rhythms.
Blood Disorders: Infants may experience low blood cell counts, including anemia and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count).
Liver Issues: Some infants may show signs of liver dysfunction, such as jaundice.

diseases.name: Neonatal Sepsis
diseases.description: Neonatal sepsis is a serious infection in newborns that can rapidly become life-threatening without early recognition and treatment.
symptoms: Poor feeding
Fever or low temperature
Fast breathing
Lethargy
Irritability

diseases.name: Neonatal Tetanus
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Neonatal tetanus starts showing symptoms in newborns about 8 days post birth. Common symptoms to watch out for are.
Rigidity of muscles with spasms
Irritability (continuous crying)
Grimacing of face & restlessness
Poor feeding / suckling ability
Neonatal tetanus generally has a poor prognosis (outlook). If any of the above signs are noted, immediate medical attention is a must.

diseases.name: Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus (NDI) is a rare but significant condition that affects the body's ability to concentrate urine, leading to excessive thirst and urination. Unlike the more commonly known Diabetes Mellitus, which involves issues with insulin and blood sugar levels, NDI is primarily related to the kidneys' response to a hormone called vasopressin (also known as antidiuretic hormone or ADH). Understanding NDI is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as untreated cases can lead to severe dehydration and other complications.
symptoms: The hallmark symptoms of Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus include:
Excessive Thirst (Polydipsia): Individuals may feel an unquenchable thirst, leading to increased fluid intake.
Frequent Urination (Polyuria): Patients often produce large volumes of dilute urine, which can be several liters per day.
Dehydration: Symptoms may include dry mouth, fatigue, dizziness, and confusion, particularly if fluid intake does not keep pace with urine output.

diseases.name: Nerve Compression Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nerve Compression Syndrome (NCS) is a medical condition that occurs when a nerve is compressed or pinched, leading to a variety of symptoms that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This syndrome is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its potential to cause chronic pain, weakness, and functional impairment if left untreated. Understanding NCS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain their daily activities and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of Nerve Compression Syndrome can vary depending on the location and severity of the nerve compression. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Often described as sharp, burning, or aching, pain may radiate from the site of compression.
Numbness: A loss of sensation in the affected area is common, which may be temporary or persistent.
Tingling: Many individuals report a "pins and needles" sensation, particularly in the hands or feet.
Weakness: Muscle weakness may occur in the affected area, making it difficult to perform everyday tasks.

diseases.name: Nerve Entrapment Syndromes
diseases.description: Nerve entrapment syndrome occurs when a nerve is compressed or pinched by surrounding structures, leading to pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness. Common types include carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve), cubital tunnel syndrome (ulnar nerve), and tarsal tunnel syndrome. The compression can result from repetitive motion, injury, or anatomical variations.
symptoms: Numbness and tingling in the distribution of the affected nerve
Pain (can be burning, shooting, or aching)
Weakness in muscles supplied by the nerve
Atrophy in chronic cases
Symptoms often worse at night or with specific positions

diseases.name: Nerve Sheath Tumors - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nerve sheath tumors are a group of tumors that arise from the protective coverings of nerves, known as the nerve sheath. These tumors can occur anywhere in the body where nerves are present, but they are most commonly found in the peripheral nervous system. Understanding nerve sheath tumors is crucial, as they can vary significantly in terms of their behavior, treatment options, and potential complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nerve sheath tumors, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of nerve sheath tumors can vary depending on the tumor's location, size, and whether it is benign or malignant. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Localized pain in the area where the tumor is located.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations of numbness or tingling in the affected area.
Weakness: Muscle weakness in the area supplied by the affected nerve.
Lumps or Masses: Visible lumps or masses under the skin, particularly in the case of neurofibromas.
Changes in Sensation: Altered sensation in the skin or muscles supplied by the affected nerve.

diseases.name: Neuroblastoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Neuroblastoma is a rare type of cancer that most often affects young children, developing from immature nerve cells found in the adrenal glands, spine, or other areas of the body. Because its symptoms—such as abdominal pain, lumps, or changes in behavior—can be similar to common childhood illnesses, understanding the condition is especially important. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about neuroblastoma—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what to expect throughout the journey. Our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of neuroblastoma can be vague and are often mistaken for other common childhood illnesses. However, if you notice these symptoms, especially if they are persistent or getting worse, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation. The symptoms depend on the tumor's location, size, and how far it has spread.
As the cancer progresses and spreads, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Fever : A persistent, unexplained fever.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
Diarrhea or High Blood Pressure: In some cases, neuroblastoma cells can produce hormones called catecholamines that can cause these symptoms.
Neurological Symptoms: If the tumor presses on the spinal cord, it can cause weakness, numbness, or paralysis in the legs or arms.
If you have a gut feeling that something is wrong with your child, do not hesitate to seek medical attention.

diseases.name: Neurodegenerative Diseases - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neurodegenerative diseases are a group of disorders characterized by the progressive degeneration of the structure and function of the nervous system. These diseases can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, leading to cognitive decline, motor dysfunction, and emotional disturbances. As the global population ages, the prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases is expected to rise, making it crucial for individuals, families, and healthcare providers to understand these conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of neurodegenerative diseases, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of neurodegenerative diseases can vary widely depending on the specific condition and the individual. However, some common symptoms include:
Cognitive Decline: Memory loss, difficulty concentrating, and impaired judgment are often early signs of neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's.
Motor Dysfunction: Tremors, stiffness, and difficulty with coordination are hallmark symptoms of Parkinson's disease.
Emotional Changes: Depression, anxiety, and mood swings can occur in various neurodegenerative conditions.
Speech and Swallowing Difficulties: As the diseases progress, individuals may experience challenges with communication and eating.

diseases.name: Neurodermatitis – Symptoms and Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Neurodermatitis is a non-life-threatening skin disorder characterized by itching and scratching on a patch of skin. Lichen simplex chronicus is another name for it. The itch can appear everywhere on the body, although it is most prevalent in the arms, shoulders, elbows, thighs, ankles, wrists, hands, back of the neck, and scalp.
symptoms: Neurodermatitis symptoms and signs include:
A rash or patches of irritated skin
The affected parts have a leathery or scaly feel.
A raised, rough patch, or patches that are reddish or deeper in color than the rest of your skin

The illness affects parts of the body such as the head, neck, wrists, forearms, ankles, vulva, scrotum, and anus. Itching can be acute and come and go, or it can be constant. Scratching is often done out of habit or during sleeping.

diseases.name: Neuroendocrine Tumors - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are a group of uncommon cancers that start in specialized cells called neuroendocrine cells. These cells act like a mix between nerve cells and hormone-producing (endocrine) cells. They are found throughout the body — especially in the lungs, pancreas, and digestive tract. Because of their dual role, tumors that develop in these cells can sometimes make excess hormones, leading to unusual symptoms.
symptoms: Neuroendocrine tumor symptoms vary widely depending on tumor type, size, and whether it produces hormones.
Flushing (sudden redness and warmth of the skin)
Diarrhea
Low blood sugar (insulinomas)
Stomach ulcers (gastrinomas)
Wheezing, palpitations, flushing, and watery diarrhea (carcinoid syndrome)
Fatigue
Severe abdominal pain
Yellowing of the skin (jaundice) if the liver is affected
Bone pain if cancer has spread

diseases.name: Neurofibroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neurofibroma is a type of tumor that develops on the nerves, primarily composed of Schwann cells, which are responsible for the myelin sheath that insulates nerve fibers. While neurofibromas are generally benign (non-cancerous), their presence can lead to various complications, depending on their size and location. Understanding neurofibromas is crucial for early detection and management, especially since they can be associated with genetic conditions like Neurofibromatosis. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of neurofibromas, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Neurofibromas can present with a variety of symptoms, depending on their location and size. Common symptoms include:
Skin Changes: Soft, fleshy lumps on the skin that may be painless.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the area where the tumor is located, especially if it compresses nearby nerves.
Nerve Dysfunction: Symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in the affected area.
Cosmetic Concerns: Visible tumors can lead to self-esteem issues and psychological distress.

diseases.name: Neurofibromatosis - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms of NF1
Café-au-lait spots (light brown skin patches, usually appearing in early childhood).
Freckling in unusual areas such as the armpit or groin.
Neurofibromas (soft lumps under the skin).
Lisch nodules (tiny spots on the iris of the eye).
Bone deformities, scoliosis, or bowed legs.
Learning difficulties in some children.
May cause optic gliomas (tumors on the optic nerve affecting vision).
Symptoms of NF2
Hearing loss, often in both ears.
Ringing in the ears (tinnitus).
Poor balance or dizziness.
Vision problems such as cataracts at an early age.
Weakness or numbness in arms or legs.
Symptoms of Schwannomatosis
Chronic pain, sometimes severe.
Numbness or tingling in different parts of the body.
Muscle weakness.

diseases.name: Neurogenic Shock - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neurogenic shock is a critical medical condition that arises from the disruption of the autonomic nervous system, leading to a sudden drop in blood pressure and inadequate blood flow to vital organs. This condition is significant because it can result in severe complications, including organ failure and death, if not promptly recognized and treated. Understanding neurogenic shock is essential for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early intervention can save lives.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of neurogenic shock is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Hypotension: Significantly low blood pressure, which can lead to dizziness or fainting.
Bradycardia: A slower than normal heart rate, which may accompany low blood pressure.
Warm, dry skin: Due to vasodilation, the skin may feel warm and dry, particularly in the lower extremities.
Weakness or paralysis: Depending on the level of spinal cord injury, individuals may experience varying degrees of weakness or paralysis.
Altered mental status: Confusion or decreased alertness may occur due to inadequate blood flow to the brain.

diseases.name: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) is a rare but potentially life-threatening reaction to antipsychotic medications, also known as neuroleptics. This syndrome is characterized by severe muscle rigidity, fever, autonomic instability, and altered mental status. Understanding NMS is crucial for both healthcare providers and patients, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of NMS, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome can vary in severity and may develop rapidly. Common symptoms include:
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature, often exceeding 38°C (100.4°F).
Muscle Rigidity: Severe stiffness in the muscles, which can lead to discomfort and pain.
Altered Mental Status: Confusion, agitation, or decreased responsiveness.
Autonomic Dysfunction: Changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and sweating.

diseases.name: Neuromuscular Disorders - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neuromuscular disorders encompass a diverse group of conditions that affect the nerves controlling voluntary muscles. These disorders can lead to muscle weakness, atrophy, and a range of other symptoms that significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding neuromuscular disorders is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers, healthcare providers, and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of neuromuscular disorders, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of neuromuscular disorders can vary widely depending on the specific condition but often include:
Muscle Weakness: Difficulty in performing everyday tasks, such as lifting objects or climbing stairs.
Muscle Cramps and Spasms: Involuntary contractions that can be painful and disruptive.
Fatigue: An overwhelming sense of tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Numbness or Tingling: Abnormal sensations in the limbs, often due to nerve damage.
Difficulty Breathing or Swallowing: In severe cases, neuromuscular disorders can affect respiratory and swallowing muscles.

diseases.name: Neuromyelitis Optica (NMO) Disease: Symptoms, Causes, and Treatment
diseases.description: Neuromyelitis Optica is an autoimmune disease and a rare condition that damages the nerves in the spinal cord and the optic nerves. Sometimes, the brain also gets affected. Loss of vision in one or both eyes, painful spasms, and the onset of paralysis in the legs and arms are some of the symptoms of Neuromyelitis Optica Disease.
symptoms: Neuromyelitis Optica disease causes episodic attacks, which means they come and go. These attacks can be severe and last anywhere between a few days and months.
Sometimes, these attacks may cause permanent nerve damage. Each patient experiences symptoms differently, from mild to severe.
The symptoms are classified into optic neuritis , myelitis, and brain function disruption.

diseases.name: Neuropathic Pain : Causes, Treatment, and Medication
diseases.description: A shooting or burning pain that is often chronic, unrelenting, and sometimes severe may indicate neuropathic pain. It is often the result of nerve damage or miscommunication between nerves. Neuropathic pain is typically caused due to trauma or the body sending unprompted pain signs to the brain.Damage to the nerve can affect the site of the injury and the areas around it. The pain progressively worsens. The symptoms may be mild to severe.
symptoms: Each patient experiences the symptoms differently. Some patients experience mild pain, whereas others experience severe pain. The following are some of the common symptoms of neuropathic pain:

Sudden onset of pain caused without any stimulation. This pain can be shooting, burning, stabbing, or electric shock-like pain. Sometimes, patients experience a sense of tingling, numbness, or a feeling of pins and needles.

Pain that occurs with non-painful stimuli. These stimuli include gentle touch on the skin, pressure, and many others. Such pain is known as allodynia. However, evoked pain may also mean increased pain for painful stimuli, such as pinpricks and heat. These are known as hyperalgesia.
Dysesthesia means an unpleasant and abnormal sensation due to spontaneous or evoked pain stimuli
Emotional issues due to troubled sleep and pain
Mottled or red skin
Severe itchiness
Changes in pain that are linked to the weather
Depression
Anxiety

diseases.name: Neuropraxia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neuropraxia is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it represents a significant aspect of nerve injuries that can affect individuals of all ages. Understanding neuropraxia is crucial, as it can lead to temporary loss of function in the affected nerves, impacting daily activities and overall quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of neuropraxia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of neuropraxia can vary depending on the location and severity of the nerve injury. Common symptoms include:
Weakness: Affected muscles may feel weak or unable to perform normal movements.
Numbness or Tingling: Patients often report a sensation of pins and needles in the area supplied by the injured nerve.
Loss of Coordination: Difficulty in coordinating movements may occur, particularly if the injury affects motor nerves.
Pain: Some individuals may experience sharp or aching pain in the affected area.

diseases.name: Neurosis: Symptoms, Causes, Types and Treatment
diseases.description: Neurosis, also known as psychoneurosis or psychoneuroses in the plural, is a mental illness that causes suffering and functional impairment to the patient. Anxiety , depression , or other feelings of misery or suffering that are out of proportion to the circumstances of a person’s life are a few common symptoms of neuroses. They may affect a person’s ability to operate in nearly any aspect of his life, including relationships and external activities.
symptoms: If one is unsure whether they have neurosis, consider whether they have ever had any of the following symptoms or traits:
Anxiety and trepidation for no fathomable reason
Worry and guilt in excess
A proclivity towards negative emotions and reactions
Anger and irritability
Self-consciousness and low self-esteem
Very poor reaction to stress.
Everyday circumstances are interpreted as dangerous.
Depression
Instability of emotions

diseases.name: Neutropenia
diseases.description: Neutropenia is a medical condition that occurs when you have lower than normal neutrophils (a type of white blood cells) in your bloodstream. It can make you susceptible to infections. In severe cases of neutropenia, the normal bacteria present in your mouth and digestive tract can also cause infections .
symptoms: Neutropenia does not cause any visible symptoms as such. In most cases, people are diagnosed with neutropenia only when they have a blood test for a completely different reason. More commonly, neutropenia is seen in people who undergo chemotherapy for cancer treatment.

In some cases, infections can occur as a complication of neutropenia. More often, these infections occur in the mucous membranes, such as the skin or the inside of the mouth. The infection can occur in the form of:
Rashes.
Ulcers .
Wounds that take a long time to heal.
An abscess (also known as a collection of pus).

diseases.name: Neutrophilia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Neutrophilia is a medical condition characterized by an elevated level of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell that plays a crucial role in the body’s immune response. Neutrophils are the first line of defense against infections, particularly bacterial infections. Understanding neutrophilia is significant because it can be an indicator of underlying health issues, ranging from infections to more serious conditions like leukemia. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of neutrophilia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Neutrophilia itself may not cause specific symptoms, but it often indicates an underlying condition. Common symptoms associated with the conditions that cause neutrophilia include:
Fever: A common response to infection.
Fatigue: General tiredness due to the body fighting an infection.
Swelling or Redness: Inflammation at the site of infection.
Pain: Discomfort in areas affected by infection or inflammation.

diseases.name: New Delta Plus Variant (Covid) : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The Delta Plus variant, first reported in a Public Health England bulletin on June 11 2021, is the mutated form of Delta variant, which was earlier discovered in India.
symptoms: According to India’s virologists, Delta Plus variant carries symptoms of the Delta variant and the beta variant. Some of these symptoms include:
Cough
Diarrhoea
Fever
Headache
Skin rash
Discolouration of fingers and toes
Chest pain
Shortness of breath.
Other symptoms listed by specialists and attributed to the Delta Plus variant include:
Stomach ache
Nausea
Appetite loss

diseases.name: Newborn Jaundice - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The skin and eyes of a newborn may seem yellow due to newborn jaundice, which is a common and usually innocuous disease. It usually happens in babies born before 38 weeks of pregnancy and some breastfed babies. Generally, infant jaundice occurs because the liver of a baby is not mature enough to get rid of bilirubin in the bloodstream.
symptoms: A yellow tone to the baby’s skin and yellow in the whites of their eyes are clear signs of jaundice. It usually begins on the face. The yellow tint spreads to the chest and stomach as bilirubin levels in the blood rise, then to the legs and arms. Consult the doctor straight away if the baby:
Isn’t feeding properly
Isn’t wetting the diaper
Is difficult to wake up
Is wailing incessantly or in a high-pitched cry.
Has arched spine and he or she is limp or stiff.
Has unusual movements of eyes
Drowsiness
Stool of mild greenish-yellow tint for breastfed newborns and a greenish-mustard color for bottle-fed babies.
Dark pee – a newborn’s urine should be colorless
Yellow abdomen or limbs
Irritability
Failure to gain weight
Poor feeding

diseases.name: Nicotine Dependence - Causes Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Nicotine is a highly addictive substance found in tobacco. Many people, especially those who smoke cigarettes, find it hard to quit using them. The craving for nicotine is called nicotine dependence. The more you smoke, the higher the craving.
symptoms: Inability to quit smoking
Unable to stop consuming tobacco
Withdrawal symptoms when you do not use nicotine
Continuous urge to smoke
Becoming antisocial and avoiding gatherings

diseases.name: Niemann-Pick - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Niemann-Pick disease is a progressive genetic metabolic disorder that affects the body’s ability to metabolize fat within cells. It can occur at any age, but it is common in children. Although research is underway for finding suitable treatment, no complete remedy has yet been found.
symptoms: The symptoms of type A form of Niemann-Pick disease are present within the first few months of birth and include:
Swollen abdomen
Swollen lymph nodes
A red spot in the eye
Feeding difficulties and reduced appetite
Loss of reflexes, motor skills
Repeated respiratory problems

The signs and symptoms of the type B form of Niemann-Pick disease usually start to appear in late childhood or at the adolescence age. This form of Niemann-Pick disease does not include motor difficulty which is found commonly in type A disease. The symptoms of type B could include:
Respiratory infections
Mental retardation
Delayed growth
Eye abnormalities
Poor coordination
Low level of blood platelets
High level of lipids in the blood
Enlarged liver and spleen

Type B form of Niemann-Pick disease differs significantly from type A form of Niemann-Pick disease which is a more serious, early-onset form of Niemann-Pick disease, in which symptoms appear in early infancy, development do not progress beyond 12 months level, and survival beyond age three is very rare.
Dystonia (excessive muscle contractions resulting in abnormal postures of limbs, face)
Clumsiness and difficulty walking
Slurring of speech
Difficulty swallowing
Seizures and tremors
Dementia
Impaired eye movements
Jaundice
Recurrent respiratory infections

diseases.name: Nightmare Disorder - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Nightmare disorder is one where recurrent and distressing nightmares occur. A nightmare is a disturbing dream linked to negative feelings like anxiety or fear that wakes you up.
symptoms: It occurs when people experience vivid and terrifying dreams frequently. Generally, patients wake up in the middle of their sleep. Some symptoms are:
Fear having more nightmares
Fatigue , sleepiness, unknown fear and low energy during the day
Nightmares occurring many times at night
Concentration problems and memory loss
Changes in behavior
Fear of the dark
Daytime activities suffering due to the disorder
Anybody can suffer from a nightmare disorder. A patient feels insecure and fearful throughout the day and at night.

diseases.name: Nodular Fasciitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nodular fasciitis is a benign soft tissue tumor that often presents as a rapidly growing lump in the skin or subcutaneous tissue. While it is not cancerous, its rapid growth can cause concern for both patients and healthcare providers, often leading to misdiagnosis. Understanding nodular fasciitis is crucial for timely diagnosis and appropriate management, as it can mimic more serious conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nodular fasciitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The primary symptom of nodular fasciitis is the presence of a firm, painless nodule that can grow rapidly over a few weeks. Other symptoms may include:
Swelling: The area around the nodule may appear swollen.
Redness: The skin over the nodule may become red or discolored.
Warmth: The nodule may feel warm to the touch.
Mobility: The nodule is usually mobile and not fixed to underlying structures.

diseases.name: Nodular Melanoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nodular melanoma is a serious form of skin cancer that arises from melanocytes, the cells responsible for producing the pigment melanin. This type of melanoma is particularly aggressive and can grow rapidly, making early detection and treatment crucial. Understanding nodular melanoma is essential not only for those at risk but also for the general public, as awareness can lead to earlier diagnosis and better outcomes.
symptoms: Nodular melanoma can present with various symptoms, including:
A New Growth: A raised, dome-shaped lesion that may be black, brown, or colorless.
Changes in Existing Moles: If a mole changes in size, shape, or color, it may indicate melanoma.
Itching or Pain: The affected area may be itchy or painful.
Bleeding or Oozing: The lesion may bleed or ooze, which is a warning sign.

diseases.name: Non Ossifying Fibroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Non Ossifying Fibroma (NOF) is a benign bone lesion commonly found in children and adolescents. While it is often asymptomatic and may resolve on its own, understanding its significance is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Non Ossifying Fibroma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Most cases of Non Ossifying Fibroma are asymptomatic and do not present any noticeable symptoms. However, in some instances, individuals may experience:
Localized Pain: Mild pain or discomfort in the affected area, especially during physical activity.
Swelling: Swelling around the lesion site may occur, although it is usually minimal.
Limited Range of Motion: In rare cases, the lesion may affect joint movement if located near a joint.

diseases.name: Non Surgical Treatment for Obesity| Weight Loss without Surgery
diseases.description: Diseases and Conditions

diseases.name: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) - Stages, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: NAFLD is often silent – which is why it is important to perform the necessary tests regularly to track the conditions of the liver. Patients do not experience any specific complaints in the early period, and even with advancing fibrosis, the disease may not cause any problems. In the later stages, patients may feel non- specific symptoms such as vague right sided abdomen pain, fatigue, tiredness, and some mild weakness. It is only after developing cirrhosis and liver failure, that patients may experience obvious problems such as swelling of feet or abdomen, blood vomiting, impaired memory and periods of confusion, easy bruising or excessive bleeding after minor injuries, loss of muscle mass, increasing jaundice , frequent infections and eventually coma. Liver cancer too can develop silently, and many times diagnosed only on routine scans such as ultrasound.

diseases.name: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL) is a type of blood cancer that develops in the lymphatic system, an essential part of the body’s immune defense. Because there are many different subtypes of NHL, the condition can vary widely in how it presents and how it is treated, which often leads to questions for patients and families. This guide provides clear and reliable information about Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma—its symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and what to expect during the journey. With a better understanding of the condition, you can feel more informed and supported as you move forward.
symptoms: The symptoms of NHL can be vague and are often mistaken for other, less serious conditions. However, if you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
The symptoms can also depend on where the lymphoma is located.
Abdominal Pain or Swelling: If the lymphoma is in the abdomen, it can cause pain, a feeling of fullness, or swelling.
Chest Pain, Cough, or Shortness of Breath: If the lymphoma is in the chest, it may press on the lungs or airways.
Itchy Skin: A persistent itch all over the body.
If you have a swollen lymph node that doesn't go away, especially if accompanied by B symptoms, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.

diseases.name: Nonallergic Rhinitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: In nonallergic rhinitis, patients experience congestion, sneezing, and runny nose. People with nonallergic rhinitis suffer from chronic sneezing or a drippy, congested nose with no apparent cause.
symptoms: Symptoms are as follows –
Runny nose
Decreased sense of smell
Excessive mucus from the nose
Sneezing
Coughing

diseases.name: Nongonococcal Urethritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nongonococcal urethritis (NGU) is a common condition that affects the urethra, the tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body. Unlike gonococcal urethritis, which is caused by the Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacteria, NGU is not caused by this specific pathogen. Understanding NGU is crucial because it can lead to significant discomfort and complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nongonococcal urethritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of NGU can vary but often include:
Painful Urination: A burning sensation during urination is a hallmark symptom.
Urethral Discharge: A discharge from the urethra, which may be clear, cloudy, or yellowish.
Itching or Irritation: Discomfort or itching around the urethral opening.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little urine produced.

diseases.name: Noonan Syndrome - Causes Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Noonan syndrome is a genetic disorder that prevents the normal development of various body parts. It is a genetic condition
symptoms: The symptoms of Noonan syndrome vary greatly,
Change in facial features is one of the most visible symptoms. These include:
Backwards rotated and low set ears
Wide eyes with drooping eyelids with pale blue or green iris
Large head with a prominent forehead
Low hairline
Crooked teeth
Droopy face
Nose with wide base and bulbous tip
Hearing problem
Rapid eyeball movement
Cataract
Sparse hair
Mouth with a groove between the nose and the mouth and wide peaks in the upper lip.
Highly arched palate and small lower jaw
Many people who are diagnosed with Noonan syndrome also face growth issues, such as,
Eating difficulty
Abnormal weight
Hormone deficiency
Short stature
Delayed puberty
Some of the other conditions seen in people suffering from Noonan syndrome are,
Thickening of heart muscles
Irregular heartbeat
Hole in the heart
Spine deformity
Undescended testicles (cryptorchidism)
Wide-set nipples
Lymphatic conditions
Excessive bleeding when hurt
An oddly shaped chest often with raised sternum (pectus carinatum) or sunken sternum (pectus excavatum)
Short neck, often with prominent neck muscles (trapezius) or extra folds of skin (webbed neck)
