Increased risk of learning disabilities as well as mild intellectual disability
Cataracts
A variety of emotional, mental and behavioral issues that are generally mild
Problems with the eye muscles like strabismus (cross-eye)
Curly, coarse hair or sparse hair
Nystagmus (Rapid movement of eyeballs)
Lymphedema (excess fluid on the back of hands or top of the feet)
Refractive problems like myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), or astigmatism
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals.

diseases.name: Normocytic Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Normocytic anemia is a type of anemia characterized by red blood cells that are of normal size but are present in insufficient quantities. This condition is significant because it can indicate underlying health issues that may require medical attention. Anemia, in general, affects millions of people worldwide and can lead to fatigue, weakness, and other serious health complications if left untreated. Understanding normocytic anemia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of normocytic anemia can vary depending on the severity of the condition and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Weakness: Reduced physical strength and endurance.
Pale Skin: A noticeable paleness, especially in the face and palms.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, especially when standing up quickly.
Rapid Heartbeat: An increased heart rate, particularly during exertion.

diseases.name: Norovirus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that causes gastroenteritis, an inflammation of the stomach and intestines. Often referred to as the "stomach flu," norovirus is responsible for a significant number of foodborne illnesses and outbreaks worldwide. Its significance lies not only in its ability to spread rapidly but also in the discomfort and health risks it poses, particularly to vulnerable populations such as the elderly and young children. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of norovirus, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of norovirus typically manifest within 12 to 48 hours after exposure and can include:
Nausea: A feeling of queasiness that may lead to vomiting.
Vomiting: Sudden and severe vomiting is a hallmark symptom of norovirus.
Diarrhea: Watery diarrhea that can be frequent and urgent.
Stomach Cramps: Abdominal pain and cramping are common.
Fever: A mild fever may accompany other symptoms.
Headache and Muscle Aches: General malaise and discomfort.

diseases.name: Norovirus Infection - Causes Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Norovirus infection is a virus that causes acute gastroenteritis. It is the second most common reason behind diarrhea and vomiting. Norovirus is widespread in winter. Thus, it is also known as “winter vomiting bug” or “winter vomiting disease”.
symptoms: Some of the symptoms that show your body is infected by norovirus are.
Vomiting
Diarrhea
Low grade Fever
Chills
Fatigue
Headache
Muscle aches
Stomach ache

The symptoms are visible in a day or two after getting in contact with the infected person. Some people may not show any signs and symptoms, but they are still contagious. Norovirus is shed in the faces of infected animals and humans.

diseases.name: Notalgia Paresthetica - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Notalgia Paresthetica (NP) is a neurological condition characterized by localized itching and discomfort, primarily affecting the upper back. While it may seem like a minor annoyance, NP can significantly impact the quality of life for those who experience it. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective management and treatment. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Notalgia Paresthetica.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of Notalgia Paresthetica is localized itching, which may be accompanied by:
Tingling or burning sensations
Sensitivity to touch
Skin changes, such as discoloration or thickening in the affected area

diseases.name: Nummular Eczema: Causes, Symptoms, and Diagnosis?
diseases.description: Nummular eczema is a condition in which a coin-shaped lesion develops on the skin. It is a chronic condition also called nummular dermatitis or discoid eczema. The spots are itchy and well-defined. They may ooze clear fluid or grow dry and crusty. It develops after a skin injury such as a burn, abrasion, or an insect bite . The disorder might cause a single patch of coin-shaped lesions or many patches of coin-shaped lesions. The patches may last for months.
symptoms: There are several symptoms experienced by people with nummular eczema. They are:
Coin-shaped, discolored lesions – The color of the lesions may be red, pink or sometimes brown.
Burning and itching sensation
Inflamed or scaly skin
Lesions on the leg and hands
The appearance of eczema depends on the skin tone of the individual. If a black-skinned person has eczema, then the patches are grey, purple or dark brown.

diseases.name: Nursemaid Elbow - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nursemaid elbow, also known as radial head subluxation, is a common injury that primarily affects young children, particularly those aged 1 to 4 years. This condition occurs when the radius, one of the bones in the forearm, slips out of its normal position at the elbow joint. While it may sound alarming, nursemaid elbow is generally not serious and can be easily treated. Understanding this condition is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure prompt recognition and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of nursemaid elbow can vary, but common signs include:
Pain: The child may experience sudden pain in the elbow or forearm, often after being pulled or lifted by the arm.
Inability to use the arm: The child may refuse to use the affected arm, keeping it close to their body.
Swelling or tenderness: There may be mild swelling or tenderness around the elbow joint.
Visible deformity: In some cases, the elbow may appear slightly deformed or out of place.

diseases.name: Nut Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nut carcinoma, while not a widely recognized term in the medical community, refers to a rare form of cancer that can arise in various tissues, often linked to specific environmental and genetic factors. Understanding nut carcinoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can significantly impact the quality of life and overall health of affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of nut carcinoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Symptoms of nut carcinoma can vary depending on the specific type and location of the cancer. Common symptoms may include:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Significant weight loss without trying can be a warning sign.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the abdominal area.
Changes in Appetite: A sudden increase or decrease in appetite.
Nausea or Vomiting: Frequent feelings of nausea or episodes of vomiting.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, indicating liver involvement.

diseases.name: Nutcracker Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Nutcracker Syndrome is a rare but significant vascular condition that affects the renal vein, leading to a range of symptoms and complications. This syndrome occurs when the left renal vein is compressed, typically between the abdominal aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Understanding Nutcracker Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to serious health issues if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Nutcracker Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Flank Pain: Often described as a dull ache or sharp pain on the left side of the abdomen or back.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which may be visible or detected through laboratory tests.
Varicocele: Enlargement of veins in the scrotum, particularly in males.
Nausea and Vomiting: May occur due to pain or associated gastrointestinal issues.
Fatigue: Chronic fatigue may result from ongoing pain or blood loss.

diseases.name: Obesity
diseases.description: Obesity is a chronic condition of excess body fat that increases the risk of many health problems, including diabetes, heart disease, and joint disorders.
symptoms: Excess body weight or fat
Breathlessness with activity
Fatigue
Joint or back pain
Sleep problems such as snoring

diseases.name: Oblique Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: An oblique fracture is a type of bone fracture characterized by a diagonal break across the bone. This type of fracture is significant because it can occur in various bones throughout the body and may result from different types of trauma. Understanding oblique fractures is crucial for both prevention and effective treatment, as they can lead to complications if not managed properly. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding oblique fractures.
symptoms: The symptoms of an oblique fracture can vary depending on the location and severity of the fracture. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Sudden and severe pain at the site of the fracture.
Swelling: Swelling and bruising around the affected area.
Deformity: Visible deformity or abnormal positioning of the limb.
Inability to Use the Affected Limb: Difficulty or inability to move the affected limb or joint.
Tenderness: Increased sensitivity to touch around the fracture site.

diseases.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Risks, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, or OCD, can be defined as an illness that causes the urge to do something repeatedly or have unwanted sensations or thoughts. There are many types of OCD, but most cases fall in the main four general categories – checking, contamination, symmetry, and intrusive thoughts.
symptoms: In most cases of OCD, people develop both obsessions and compulsions. However, there are some people who either develop only obsessions or only compulsions.
The symptoms of obsessions include:
Intense stress when things are not in a particular order
Fear of being contaminated by touching objects or surfaces other people have touched
Unpleasant sexual images in the head
Doubts about turning off the stove or locking the door
Images of driving the car into a group of people
Avoidance of situations that may trigger obsessions such as shaking hands
Thoughts about behaving inappropriately in public
The symptoms of compulsions include:
Checking doors or windows multiple times to ensure they are locked properly
Washing hands until the skin becomes raw
Counting in a certain pattern
Checking repeatedly if the stove is turned off
Arranging objects in a certain pattern
Silently repeating a word, phrase, or prayer
If you or someone you know has these symptoms, immediately seek medical assistance. Getting an early diagnosis and treatment may help the OCD from worsening or affecting the daily activities.

diseases.name: Obstructive Shock - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Obstructive shock is a critical medical condition that arises when blood flow is impeded due to a physical obstruction in the circulatory system. This obstruction can lead to inadequate blood supply to vital organs, resulting in severe complications if not promptly addressed. Understanding obstructive shock is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, ultimately improving patient outcomes. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of obstructive shock, making it accessible to a general audience while maintaining medical accuracy.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of obstructive shock is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Rapid Heart Rate: The heart may beat faster in an attempt to compensate for reduced blood flow.
Low Blood Pressure: A significant drop in blood pressure can occur, leading to dizziness or fainting.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may arise due to inadequate oxygenation.
Cold, Clammy Skin: The skin may feel cool and sweaty as blood flow is redirected to vital organs.
Confusion or Altered Mental Status: Reduced blood flow to the brain can lead to confusion or disorientation.

diseases.name: OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA – ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW
diseases.description: Obstructive Sleep apnea is a condition that causes individuals to stop breathing for short periods during their sleep. This period is called apnea. Each episode of apnea usually lasts between 10 and 30 seconds. In severe cases, apnea can happen many hundreds of times each night, disrupting the person’s ability to get a good night’s sleep. This makes the person less alert during the day, which can lead to accidents. Individuals with untreated sleep apnea are more prone to motor vehicle accidents. People with untreated sleep apnea also are more likely to develop high blood pressure .
symptoms: Obstructive sleep apnea symptoms include:
Excessive sleepiness during the waking time
Loud snoring (bed partner may be the first to notice the problem)
Morning headache and dry mouth
Obesity is also a common symptom, although not all individuals with sleep apnea are overweight.

diseases.name: Occipital Neuralgia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Occipital Neuralgia is a condition that can cause debilitating pain in the back of the head and neck. Often mistaken for other types of headaches, this condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding Occipital Neuralgia is crucial for effective management and treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Occipital Neuralgia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Occipital Neuralgia can vary from person to person but typically include:
Sharp, shooting pain: This pain often starts at the base of the skull and can radiate to the scalp, forehead, and behind the eyes.
Sensitivity to light: Many individuals experience discomfort in bright light.
Neck stiffness: Tightness in the neck muscles can accompany the pain.
Tingling or numbness: Some may feel a tingling sensation in the scalp or neck.

diseases.name: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome (OIS) is a rare but significant condition that affects the blood supply to the eye, leading to various visual impairments. It is characterized by a reduction in blood flow to the ocular structures, primarily due to carotid artery disease. Understanding OIS is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications, including vision loss. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Ocular Ischemic Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Ocular Ischemic Syndrome can vary but often include:
Vision Loss: This can range from mild blurriness to complete loss of vision in one eye.
Visual Disturbances: Patients may experience transient visual obscurations or flashes of light.
Eye Pain: Some individuals report discomfort or pain in the affected eye.
Redness of the Eye: This may occur due to increased blood flow or inflammation.
Floaters: The presence of floaters or spots in the visual field can be a symptom.

diseases.name: Ocular Migraine - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ocular migraine, also known as retinal migraine, is a type of migraine that primarily affects vision. It is characterized by temporary visual disturbances that can be alarming and disruptive. While ocular migraines are generally not considered dangerous, they can significantly impact daily life and may be indicative of underlying health issues. Understanding ocular migraine is crucial for effective management and prevention, as well as for distinguishing it from more serious conditions.
symptoms: The symptoms of ocular migraine can vary from person to person but typically include:
Visual Disturbances: Flashes of light, zigzag patterns, or blind spots in one eye.
Temporary Vision Loss: A brief loss of vision in one eye, which usually resolves within 30 minutes.
Headache: Some individuals may experience a headache following the visual symptoms, although this is not always the case.

diseases.name: Ocular Rosacea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ocular rosacea is a chronic inflammatory condition that affects the eyes and eyelids, often associated with facial rosacea. While many people are familiar with the skin manifestations of rosacea, ocular rosacea can lead to significant discomfort and complications if left untreated. Understanding this condition is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals maintain their quality of life and eye health.
symptoms: Ocular rosacea can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Redness: Persistent redness of the eyes and eyelids.
Irritation: A burning or stinging sensation in the eyes.
Dryness: A feeling of dryness or grittiness, often described as having sand in the eyes.
Swelling: Inflammation and swelling of the eyelids.
Crusting: Crusty debris on the eyelids, especially upon waking.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to bright lights or glare.

diseases.name: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy (OPMD) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the muscles responsible for eye movement and swallowing. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on daily living but also due to its genetic basis, which can have implications for family members. Understanding OPMD is crucial for early diagnosis and management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy can vary in severity and may progress over time. Common symptoms include:
Ptosis: Drooping of the eyelids, which can affect vision.
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, which can lead to choking or aspiration pneumonia.
Weakness in facial muscles: This can affect facial expressions and lead to difficulties in chewing.
Muscle weakness: Generalized weakness may occur, particularly in the neck and limbs.

diseases.name: Ogilvie Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ogilvie Syndrome, also known as acute colonic pseudo-obstruction, is a rare but significant gastrointestinal condition characterized by the abnormal dilation of the colon without any mechanical obstruction. This syndrome can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding Ogilvie Syndrome is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Ogilvie Syndrome can vary in severity and may include:
Abdominal Distension: A noticeable swelling of the abdomen due to gas and fluid accumulation.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or sharp pain in the abdomen, which may be intermittent.
Nausea and Vomiting: Feelings of nausea and episodes of vomiting, particularly if the condition worsens.
Constipation: Difficulty passing stool or a significant decrease in bowel movements.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat, often due to discomfort.

diseases.name: Oligoarthritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oligoarthritis is a form of arthritis characterized by inflammation in a limited number of joints, typically affecting four or fewer joints during the initial six months of the disease. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on mobility and quality of life but also due to its potential to evolve into more severe forms of arthritis if left untreated. Understanding oligoarthritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of oligoarthritis can vary depending on the individual and the joints affected. Common symptoms include:
Joint Pain: Affected joints may feel painful, especially during movement.
Swelling: Inflammation can cause visible swelling around the joints.
Stiffness: Morning stiffness or stiffness after periods of inactivity is common.
Reduced Range of Motion: Affected joints may have limited movement due to pain and swelling.
Fatigue: Chronic inflammation can lead to feelings of tiredness and fatigue.

diseases.name: Oligodendroglioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oligodendroglioma is a type of brain tumor that arises from oligodendrocytes, the cells responsible for producing the myelin sheath that insulates nerve fibers in the central nervous system. This tumor is classified as a glioma, which is a broad category of tumors that originate from glial cells. Oligodendrogliomas are significant due to their unique biological behavior, treatment responses, and the challenges they pose in terms of diagnosis and management. Understanding oligodendroglioma is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers alike, as it can lead to better outcomes through early detection and appropriate treatment.
symptoms: Oligodendrogliomas can present with a variety of symptoms, depending on their size and location in the brain. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Persistent or worsening headaches that may be different from previous headaches.
Seizures: New-onset seizures, particularly in adults, can be a significant warning sign.
Cognitive Changes: Memory problems, difficulty concentrating, or changes in personality.
Motor Symptoms: Weakness or numbness in limbs, difficulty with coordination or balance.
Visual or Auditory Disturbances: Changes in vision or hearing can occur if the tumor affects areas of the brain responsible for these senses.

diseases.name: Oligohydramnios - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oligohydramnios is a medical condition characterized by an insufficient amount of amniotic fluid surrounding a developing fetus during pregnancy. Amniotic fluid plays a crucial role in fetal development, providing cushioning, facilitating movement, and aiding in the development of the lungs and digestive system. Understanding oligohydramnios is essential for expectant parents and healthcare providers, as it can significantly impact pregnancy outcomes. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding oligohydramnios.
symptoms: Oligohydramnios may not always present noticeable symptoms, but some common signs include:
Decreased fetal movement: A noticeable reduction in the baby's movements may indicate low amniotic fluid levels.
Abdominal discomfort: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the abdomen.
Unusual fetal heart rate patterns: Healthcare providers may detect abnormal heart rate patterns during routine check-ups.

diseases.name: Oligomenorrhea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oligomenorrhea is a medical term that refers to infrequent menstrual periods, specifically when a woman experiences cycles that occur more than 35 days apart but less than six months. This condition can be a significant indicator of underlying health issues and can affect a woman's reproductive health, emotional well-being, and overall quality of life. Understanding oligomenorrhea is crucial for women who may be experiencing irregularities in their menstrual cycles, as it can lead to complications if left untreated.
symptoms: The primary symptom of oligomenorrhea is infrequent menstruation. However, women may also experience other symptoms, including:
Irregular bleeding patterns
Changes in menstrual flow (lighter or heavier)
Symptoms of hormonal imbalance, such as acne, weight gain, or hair loss
Mood swings or emotional disturbances

diseases.name: Oliguria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oliguria is a medical term that refers to a significant decrease in urine output. It is defined as the production of less than 400 milliliters of urine per day in adults, which is considerably lower than the normal range of 800 to 2,000 milliliters. Oliguria can be a critical indicator of underlying health issues, particularly related to kidney function. Understanding oliguria is essential, as it can signal serious medical conditions that require prompt attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of oliguria, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of oliguria can vary depending on the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Decreased Urine Output: The most obvious sign is a noticeable reduction in urine production.
Swelling: Fluid retention may lead to swelling in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness can occur due to fluid imbalance.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may arise from the buildup of waste products in the body.

diseases.name: Omicron Coronavirus : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Omicron is a new mutant of the coronavirus (COVID-19) that was identified by South African scientists in November 2021. This new variant is said to be behind the recent spike in COVID-19 infections in the region and now seen across the world.
symptoms: The Omicron (B.1.1.529) variant infection symptoms are similar to that of the Delta variant infection . Those infected with the Omicron variant may develop one or more of the following symptoms:
Throat pain or Scratchy throat
Extreme tiredness
Fever
Dry Cough
Skin rashes
Loss of smell or taste
Breathlessness
Drop in oxygen saturation levels
But, there are cases where people infected with this infection are asymptomatic as well.

diseases.name: Omphalitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Omphalitis is a medical condition characterized by the inflammation of the umbilical stump, which is the remnant of the umbilical cord after birth. This condition is particularly significant in newborns, as it can lead to serious complications if not promptly diagnosed and treated. Understanding omphalitis is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure the health and safety of infants during the vulnerable neonatal period.
symptoms: The symptoms of omphalitis can vary but typically include:
Redness and Swelling: The area around the umbilical stump may appear red and swollen.
Discharge: There may be a discharge from the umbilical stump, which can be yellow, green, or foul-smelling.
Fever: A low-grade fever may be present, indicating an underlying infection.
Irritability: The infant may be more irritable or fussy than usual.

diseases.name: Omphalocele - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Omphalocele is a congenital condition that affects newborns, characterized by the protrusion of abdominal organs through a defect in the abdominal wall. This condition is significant not only because of its physical implications but also due to the potential complications that can arise if not properly managed. Understanding omphalocele is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment, ultimately improving outcomes for affected infants.
symptoms: The primary symptom of omphalocele is the visible protrusion of abdominal organs through the abdominal wall at the umbilical cord site. This may be apparent at birth or detected during prenatal ultrasounds. Other symptoms may include:
Difficulty Breathing: If the organs are pressing against the diaphragm.
Feeding Difficulties: Due to gastrointestinal complications.
Signs of Infection: Such as fever or unusual irritability.

diseases.name: Onycholysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Onycholysis is a condition characterized by the separation of the nail from the nail bed. While it may seem like a cosmetic issue, onycholysis can indicate underlying health problems and may lead to complications if left untreated. Understanding onycholysis is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals maintain not only the appearance of their nails but also their overall health.
symptoms: The primary symptom of onycholysis is the visible separation of the nail from the nail bed. Other symptoms may include:
Discoloration: The affected nail may appear white, yellow, or greenish.
Thickening of the Nail: The nail may become thicker or develop irregularities.
Pain or Discomfort: Some individuals may experience pain, especially if the nail is injured.

diseases.name: Oppositional Defiant Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD) is a behavioral condition that primarily affects children and adolescents, characterized by a pattern of angry, irritable mood, argumentative behavior, and defiance toward authority figures. Understanding ODD is crucial, as it can significantly impact a child's social, academic, and family life. Early recognition and intervention can lead to better outcomes, making it essential for parents, educators, and healthcare providers to be informed about this disorder.
symptoms: Children with ODD may exhibit a range of symptoms, including:
Angry/Irritable Mood: Frequent temper tantrums, easily annoyed, and often angry.
Argumentative Behavior: Regularly arguing with adults, refusing to comply with requests, and actively defying rules.
Vindictiveness: Spiteful or vindictive behavior, often seeking revenge for perceived wrongs.
Blaming Others: Frequently blaming others for their mistakes or misbehavior.
Low Frustration Tolerance: Difficulty managing frustration, leading to outbursts or aggressive behavior.

diseases.name: Optic Atrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Optic atrophy is a condition that affects the optic nerve, the crucial pathway that transmits visual information from the eye to the brain. This condition can lead to significant vision loss and is often a sign of underlying health issues. Understanding optic atrophy is essential for early diagnosis and management, which can help preserve vision and improve quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding optic atrophy.
symptoms: The symptoms of optic atrophy can vary depending on the extent of nerve damage. Common symptoms include:
Vision Loss: This can range from mild blurriness to significant loss of vision.
Color Vision Deficiency: Difficulty distinguishing colors may occur.
Peripheral Vision Loss: A narrowing of the visual field can happen, making it hard to see objects outside of direct vision.
Visual Disturbances: Patients may experience visual distortions or flickering lights.

diseases.name: Optic Disc Drusen - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Optic disc drusen (ODD) is a condition characterized by the accumulation of small, calcified deposits in the optic nerve head, which can lead to various visual disturbances. While often asymptomatic, optic disc drusen can be significant as they may mimic or mask other serious eye conditions, such as glaucoma or papilledema. Understanding optic disc drusen is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that individuals maintain optimal eye health.
symptoms: Many individuals with optic disc drusen are asymptomatic, meaning they do not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some may report:
Visual Disturbances: Fluctuations in vision, particularly in peripheral vision.
Visual Field Loss: Some patients may experience localized areas of vision loss.
Photopsia: The perception of flashes of light, particularly in low-light conditions.

diseases.name: Optic Neuritis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The optic nerve is very important for the normal vision of human eyes. Any inflammation or irritation in this nerve leads to a serious optical problem called optic neuritis . This condition might occur in one or both eyes due to diverse reasons.
symptoms: Temporary vision loss in the affected eye
Dull pain in the eye that increases due to movements of the eyeball
Sudden flashes of light seen by the affected eye
Colors appear much less bright
Inability to see things sidewise
Blurry vision at times
Seeing a dark hole at the centre while looking straight

diseases.name: Oral Allergy Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oral Allergy Syndrome (OAS) is a condition that affects many individuals, particularly those with existing pollen allergies. It occurs when certain fruits, vegetables, and nuts trigger allergic reactions in the mouth and throat due to cross-reactivity with pollen proteins. Understanding OAS is crucial for those who experience allergic reactions, as it can significantly impact their quality of life and dietary choices. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Oral Allergy Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Oral Allergy Syndrome can vary in severity and may include:
Itching or tingling in the mouth, throat, or lips
Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat
Redness or irritation in the oral cavity
Gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea or abdominal discomfort (less common)

diseases.name: Oral Herpes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oral herpes, commonly known as cold sores, is a viral infection caused primarily by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). This condition is significant not only due to its prevalence but also because it can lead to discomfort, social stigma, and complications in certain populations. Understanding oral herpes is crucial for effective management and prevention, as it affects millions of people worldwide.
symptoms: The symptoms of oral herpes can vary from person to person but typically include:
Blisters: Painful, fluid-filled blisters around the lips, mouth, or gums.
Sores: Crusty sores that develop after the blisters break.
Itching or Tingling: A tingling or itching sensation may occur before blisters appear.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the affected area, especially when eating or drinking.

diseases.name: Oral Lichen Planus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oral Lichen Planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory condition that affects the mucous membranes inside the mouth. It is characterized by white patches, red swollen tissues, and sometimes painful sores. While OLP is not contagious, it can significantly impact a person's quality of life due to discomfort and potential complications. Understanding OLP is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, making it an important topic for both patients and healthcare providers.
symptoms: Oral Lichen Planus can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
White Patches: These are often seen on the inner cheeks, gums, and tongue. They may appear as lace-like patterns (Wickham's striae).
Red Areas: Inflammation can lead to red, swollen patches in the mouth.
Ulcers: Painful sores may develop, which can make eating and speaking uncomfortable.
Burning Sensation: Many patients report a burning or tingling sensation in the mouth, especially when consuming certain foods.
Dry Mouth: Some individuals may experience xerostomia (dry mouth), which can lead to further complications.

diseases.name: Oral Mucocele - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Oral mucocele is a common condition that affects the mucous membranes of the mouth, often presenting as a painless swelling. While it is generally benign, understanding its significance is crucial for effective management and prevention of complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of oral mucocele, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Oral mucoceles typically present as painless, soft, and dome-shaped swellings in the mouth. They can vary in size, ranging from a few millimeters to several centimeters. The color of the mucocele may range from normal mucosal color to bluish or translucent, depending on the amount of fluid inside.

diseases.name: Oral Thrush - Causes Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Oral thrush is a condition of the mouth caused by a yeast or fungal infection. It is also known as oral candidiasis or oropharyngeal candidiasis. Oral thrush occurs when the fungus called Candida albicans accumulates inside your mouth. Candida is normally found inside the human mouth, but it needs treatment when it grows excessively to cause troubling symptoms.
symptoms: Oral thrush in its early stages does not show any symptoms. But if the infection grows and starts spreading, it can show the following symptoms:
Creamy white or yellow patches on the lining of your mouth, inner cheeks, gums, lips, and even tonsils
Your patches or bumps might bleed on slight scraping while brushing or cleaning your mouth
Burning sensation in your mouth
Loss of taste
A feeling that food is stuck in the throat
A cottony feeling inside your mouth
Redness and pain under dentures, called denture stomatitis
Median rhomboid glossitis, a large red painless mark in the tongue’s center
Pain while swallowing food
Cracked and red corners of the mouth

In severe cases, the infection may spread downward into your esophagus (Candida esophagitis). If it spreads to esophagus, you may experience difficulty swallowing and pain or feel as if food is getting stuck in your throat.
Infants with candida infection may experience trouble feeding or be irritable and fussy. They can pass infection to their mothers during breast-feeding.

diseases.name: Orbital Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Orbital fractures are a significant concern in the field of medicine, particularly in trauma care and ophthalmology. These fractures occur in the bony structure surrounding the eye, known as the orbit, and can lead to a range of complications affecting vision, eye movement, and overall facial aesthetics. Understanding orbital fractures is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective treatment, which can significantly impact a patient's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of orbital fractures can vary depending on the severity and type of fracture. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Localized pain around the eye, which may worsen with eye movement.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling of the eyelids and surrounding areas, often accompanied by bruising.
Vision Changes: Blurred or double vision, which may indicate involvement of the eye muscles or optic nerve.
Difficulty Moving the Eye: Limited eye movement due to muscle entrapment.
Numbness: Numbness in the cheek or upper lip if the infraorbital nerve is affected.

diseases.name: Orchitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Orchitis is an inflammation caused in one or both testicles. It can be the result of a bacterial infection. The mumps virus can also cause orchitis.
symptoms: The symptoms are:
Swelling in one or both testicles
Pain ranging from mild to severe
Fever
Nausea and vomiting
A general feeling of un-wellness (malaise)
Tenderness or infection in the scrotum
Pain while ejaculating
Pain while urinating
Blood in your semen
Abnormal discharge
Swollen lymph nodes in the groin

diseases.name: Organ Failure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Organ failure is a critical medical condition that occurs when one or more organs in the body cease to function properly. This failure can lead to severe health complications and, if left untreated, can be life-threatening. Understanding organ failure is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, which can significantly impact patient outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of organ failure, its implications, and how to manage and prevent it effectively.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of organ failure is vital for timely intervention. Common symptoms may vary depending on the affected organ but often include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded with minimal exertion.
Swelling: Edema, particularly in the legs, ankles, or abdomen.
Confusion: Changes in mental status or cognitive function.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal distress can indicate organ issues.
Chest Pain: Particularly in cases of heart failure.

diseases.name: Oropharyngeal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Oropharyngeal cancer is a head and neck cancer that starts in the middle part of the throat (the oropharynx), which includes the tonsils, base of the tongue (back one-third), soft palate, and the side and back walls of the throat. It’s increasingly recognized because many cases are related to human papillomavirus (HPV). The encouraging news is that early diagnosis and coordinated care can lead to excellent outcomes for many people. This article explains symptoms, diagnosis, staging, treatments (surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and proton therapy), recovery, and prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Early symptoms can be subtle and easy to miss. Any symptom persisting beyond 2–3 weeks should be checked by an ENT (ear, nose, and throat) specialist.
Ear pain, especially on one side (referred pain)
Unintentional weight loss, fatigue
Persistent bad breath, coughing up blood-streaked saliva
A visible or palpable mass in the tonsil or base of tongue
Noisy breathing or shortness of breath
Prompt evaluation can expand treatment choices and improve long-term function.

diseases.name: Orthostatic Hypotension or Postural Hypotension - Causes and Symptoms
diseases.description: Orthostatic hypotension is a kind of low blood pressure that develops when you suddenly stand up or lie down. Orthostatic hypotension or postural hypotension is generally mild and lasts for a few minutes. It makes you dizzy, and you may even faint.
symptoms: Orthostatic hypotension mostly occurs in the mornings. The reason is that blood pressure is at its lowest in the mornings. The main sign or symptom is dizziness, when you suddenly stand up from a lying or sitting position. Fainting is also a sign of orthostatic hypotension.
Blurred vision
Headaches
Nausea
Feeling hot or sweaty
Chest, shoulder or neck pain
Difficulty in concentrating
Heart palpitations
Shortness of breath

diseases.name: Orthostatic Proteinuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Orthostatic proteinuria is a condition that often goes unnoticed but can have significant implications for those affected. It is characterized by the presence of excess protein in the urine when a person is in an upright position, which typically resolves when lying down. Understanding orthostatic proteinuria is crucial for early diagnosis and management, as it can be a marker for underlying health issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of orthostatic proteinuria, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Orthostatic proteinuria is often asymptomatic, meaning many individuals may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some may report:
Foamy Urine: A common sign of proteinuria, where urine appears bubbly or frothy.
Frequent Urination: Increased urination may occur, particularly after standing for extended periods.
Mild Edema: Swelling in the legs or feet may be observed in some cases.

diseases.name: Osgood-Schlatter Disease - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Osgood-Schlatter disease is responsible for knee pain in adolescents, especially those who play sport. Osgood-Schlatter disease is common in children who play the sport that involves running, jumping and swift changes of direction like basketball, soccer, ballet and figure skating.
symptoms: Knee pain in the lower part of the knee
Swollen and tender joints
Knee lock
Hindrance in performing daily essential activities, causing instability
Pain generally gets worse during certain activities like kneeling, jumping and running, and eases with rest.
Development of painful lump at the knee joint – the primary sign of Osgood-Schlatter disease
Recurring flares

diseases.name: Ossifying Fibroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ossifying fibroma is a benign tumor that primarily affects the jawbones, particularly the mandible (lower jaw) and maxilla (upper jaw). This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause discomfort and aesthetic concerns but also due to its implications for dental health and overall well-being. Understanding ossifying fibroma is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals affected can maintain their quality of life.
symptoms: Ossifying fibromas may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in the early stages. However, as the tumor grows, individuals may experience:
Swelling: A noticeable swelling or lump in the jaw area.
Pain or Discomfort: Some patients report pain or discomfort in the affected area, particularly when chewing or speaking.
Facial Asymmetry: As the tumor expands, it may cause changes in facial appearance.
Dental Issues: Displacement of teeth or difficulty in dental alignment may occur.

diseases.name: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica (OFC) is a rare bone disorder characterized by the replacement of normal bone tissue with fibrous tissue and cyst-like spaces. This condition is primarily associated with hyperparathyroidism, a condition where the parathyroid glands produce excessive parathyroid hormone (PTH). The significance of Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica lies in its potential to cause severe bone pain, deformities, and fractures, significantly impacting a person's quality of life. Understanding OFC is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can prevent complications and improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: Bone Pain: Persistent pain in the bones, particularly in the long bones and spine.
Fractures: Increased susceptibility to fractures due to weakened bone structure.
Deformities: Changes in bone shape, particularly in the skull and long bones.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue and weakness due to chronic pain and metabolic disturbances.
Nerve Compression: Symptoms such as tingling or numbness if nerves are compressed by expanding cysts.

diseases.name: Osteitis Pubis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Osteitis Pubis is a condition that affects the pubic symphysis, the joint located at the front of the pelvis. This joint connects the left and right pubic bones and plays a crucial role in maintaining pelvic stability. Osteitis Pubis is characterized by inflammation of this joint, leading to pain and discomfort, particularly in athletes and individuals engaged in activities that involve repetitive stress on the pelvis. Understanding Osteitis Pubis is essential, as it can significantly impact mobility and quality of life if not properly managed.
symptoms: The symptoms of Osteitis Pubis can vary in intensity and may include:
Groin Pain: A common symptom, often worsening with physical activity.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort in the lower abdomen or pelvic region.
Pain During Movement: Increased pain when walking, running, or performing activities that involve hip movement.
Tenderness: Sensitivity in the pubic area when touched.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the hips or pelvis.

diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
diseases.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common form of arthritis, affecting millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the protective cartilage that cushions the ends of bones in joints gradually wears down. Although osteoarthritis can damage any joint, the disorder most commonly affects joints in the hands, knees, hips, and spine.
symptoms: Pain during or after movement
Joint stiffness most notable upon waking or after inactivity
Tenderness when pressing the joint
Loss of flexibility
Grating sensation
Bone spurs
Swelling

diseases.name: Osteogenesis Imperfecta (Brittle Bone Disease)
diseases.description: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), also known as brittle bone disease, is a group of genetic disorders that primarily affect the bones. People with OI have bones that break easily, often from minor trauma or even with no apparent cause. Severity ranges from mild to severe. It is caused by mutations in genes responsible for producing type I collagen.
symptoms: Frequent bone fractures
Blue or grey sclera (whites of eyes)
Hearing loss in adolescence or adulthood
Loose joints and low muscle tone
Short stature
Scoliosis
Triangular face shape
Dental problems (dentinogenesis imperfecta)

diseases.name: Osteomalacia (Rickets in Adults)
diseases.description: Osteomalacia is a condition in which the bones become soft and weak due to a defect in the bone-building process. In children, this condition is called rickets. It most commonly results from vitamin D deficiency, which impairs the absorption of calcium and phosphate needed for bone mineralization. Unlike osteoporosis (loss of already mineralized bone), osteomalacia is a failure to mineralize new bone.
symptoms: Bone pain and tenderness (dull, aching)
Muscle weakness, especially in the hip girdle
Difficulty walking (waddling gait)
Increased susceptibility to fractures
Muscle cramps (if hypocalcemia present)
Bone deformity in severe cases

diseases.name: Osteomyelitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Osteomyelitis is a serious bone infection that can result in pain, swelling, and in severe cases, the destruction of bone tissue. The infection typically occurs when bacteria, fungi, or other pathogens invade the bone, causing inflammation and damage. While osteomyelitis can affect people of all ages, it is more common in individuals with weakened immune systems, chronic conditions like diabetes, or a history of trauma or surgery.
symptoms: The symptoms of osteomyelitis can vary depending on the severity of the infection and whether it is acute or chronic. Common symptoms include pain, swelling, fever, and difficulty moving the affected area.

Pain: Pain is the most common symptom of osteomyelitis. The pain may be localized in the affected area, particularly around the joint or bone. It can range from mild to severe and may worsen with movement or pressure.

Pain is the most common symptom of osteomyelitis. The pain may be localized in the affected area, particularly around the joint or bone. It can range from mild to severe and may worsen with movement or pressure.
Swelling and Redness: The affected area may become swollen, warm to the touch, and red due to inflammation. Swelling is often a sign of infection.
The affected area may become swollen, warm to the touch, and red due to inflammation. Swelling is often a sign of infection.
Fever and Chills: A fever is a common sign of infection. Individuals with osteomyelitis may also experience chills as the body tries to fight the infection.

Fatigue: People with osteomyelitis often feel tired or weak due to the body’s immune response to the infection.
People with osteomyelitis often feel tired or weak due to the body’s immune response to the infection.

Loss of Function: The infection can impair the movement of the affected area. If the infection involves the spine, it can cause difficulty walking. If it affects a joint, it may cause stiffness and pain when moving the joint.

The infection can impair the movement of the affected area. If the infection involves the spine, it can cause difficulty walking. If it affects a joint, it may cause stiffness and pain when moving the joint.
Drainage: In severe cases, an abscess may form, and pus may drain from an open wound or surgical site. This is more common in chronic osteomyelitis.
In severe cases, an abscess may form, and pus may drain from an open wound or surgical site. This is more common in chronic osteomyelitis.

diseases.name: Osteopenia (Bone Loss)
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: While bone loss occurs gradually and in many cases may not show any signs at all, Osteopenia eventually leading to Osteoporosis, may have the following early signs of development:
1. Hunching or stooped posture
2. Frequent backaches
3. Loss of bone in the jaw
4. Weakness from a previous injury or fracture

diseases.name: Osteopoikilosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Osteopoikilosis is a rare bone disorder characterized by the presence of small, round areas of increased bone density, known as osteopoikilotic lesions. While it is often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally during imaging studies for other conditions, understanding osteopoikilosis is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of osteopoikilosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Most individuals with osteopoikilosis are asymptomatic, meaning they do not experience any noticeable symptoms. However, some may report mild discomfort or pain in areas where the lesions are present, particularly if they are located near joints.

diseases.name: Osteoporosis
diseases.description: Osteoporosis is a bone disease that occurs when the body loses too much bone, makes too little bone, or both. As a result, bones become weak and may break from a fall or, in serious cases, from minor bumps or even from sneezing. Osteoporosis means 'porous bone.' It is the most common reason for a broken bone among older adults.
symptoms: No symptoms in early stages
Back pain (due to fractured or collapsed vertebra)
Loss of height over time
Stooped posture
Bone fracture more easily than expected

diseases.name: Osteoradionecrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a serious condition that can arise following radiation therapy, particularly in the treatment of head and neck cancers. It involves the death of bone tissue due to radiation damage, leading to significant complications and challenges in management. Understanding ORN is crucial for patients undergoing radiation therapy, as well as for healthcare providers, to ensure early detection and appropriate intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of osteoradionecrosis can vary but often include:
Pain: Persistent pain in the jaw or mouth area.
Swelling: Swelling in the affected area, which may be accompanied by redness.
Exposed Bone: Visible areas of bone that are exposed in the mouth or jaw.
Infection: Signs of infection, such as fever, pus, or foul odor from the mouth.
Difficulty Eating: Pain or discomfort while chewing or swallowing.

diseases.name: Osteosarcoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Osteosarcoma is a rare type of bone cancer that most commonly affects the long bones, such as those in the arms or legs. It often develops during periods of rapid bone growth, which makes understanding the condition especially important. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about osteosarcoma—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, available treatment options, and what you can expect throughout your journey. Our aim is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of osteosarcoma can be vague and are often mistaken for other, more common conditions like sports injuries or "growing pains." However, if you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
Common Early Signs:

Persistent Bone Pain or Tenderness: The most common symptom is a persistent pain in the affected bone. The pain may come and go at first, but it can become constant and may get worse at night or with activity.
A Lump or Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling may appear in the affected area, which may or may not be painful.
Problems with Movement: If the cancer is near a joint, it may cause a limp or make it difficult to move the joint.
Unexplained Broken Bone (Fracture): In rare cases, a bone can become so weakened by the cancer that it breaks after a minor fall or injury.
Advanced Symptoms:
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Fever: A persistent, unexplained fever.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
Breathing Problems: If the cancer has spread to the lungs, it can cause a persistent cough or shortness of breath.
If you or a loved one has a persistent bone pain that doesn't go away, especially if it is worse at night, it is crucial to consult a doctor right away for an accurate diagnosis.

diseases.name: Otitis Media - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Otitis media is one of the most common ear infections, particularly in children. It refers to inflammation or infection of the middle ear, which is the air-filled space behind the eardrum that contains tiny vibrating bones. Otitis media can affect anyone, but it is most commonly seen in young children due to their developing immune systems and anatomy. It can occur suddenly (acute) or last for long periods (chronic).
symptoms: Otitis media presents with a variety of symptoms, ranging from mild discomfort to severe pain and hearing loss. Recognizing the signs early is essential for effective treatment.
Ear Pain : The most common symptom of otitis media is ear pain, which may be mild to severe. The pain can be persistent or intermittent and may worsen when lying down or touching the ear.
The most common symptom of otitis media is ear pain, which may be mild to severe. The pain can be persistent or intermittent and may worsen when lying down or touching the ear.
Hearing Loss : Fluid buildup in the middle ear can cause temporary hearing loss, which may be noticeable as a sensation of muffled sounds. In chronic cases, hearing loss can persist.
Fluid buildup in the middle ear can cause temporary hearing loss, which may be noticeable as a sensation of muffled sounds. In chronic cases, hearing loss can persist.
Fluid Drainage : Drainage from the ear is a common symptom of otitis media, especially if the eardrum ruptures or if there is an active infection. The fluid may be clear or contain pus.
Drainage from the ear is a common symptom of otitis media, especially if the eardrum ruptures or if there is an active infection. The fluid may be clear or contain pus.
Fever : A fever may accompany otitis media, especially if there is a bacterial infection. The fever is typically low-grade but can rise in more severe cases.
A fever may accompany otitis media, especially if there is a bacterial infection. The fever is typically low-grade but can rise in more severe cases.

Irritability and Fussiness : In young children, irritability, crying, and difficulty sleeping may be signs of ear pain associated with otitis media. Infants and toddlers may tug at their ears in response to the discomfort.

Loss of Appetite : Ear pain can make swallowing uncomfortable, leading to a decreased appetite, especially in children.
Ear pain can make swallowing uncomfortable, leading to a decreased appetite, especially in children.
Balance Problems : The middle ear plays a key role in balance, so an infection may cause dizziness or problems with coordination.
The middle ear plays a key role in balance, so an infection may cause dizziness or problems with coordination.

diseases.name: Otorrhea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Otorrhea, commonly referred to as ear discharge, is a medical condition characterized by the abnormal flow of fluid from the ear. This condition can be a symptom of various underlying issues, ranging from infections to more serious health concerns. Understanding otorrhea is crucial, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life and may indicate the presence of an underlying health issue that requires medical attention. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding otorrhea.
symptoms: The symptoms of otorrhea can vary based on the underlying cause but may include:
Fluid Discharge: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of fluid coming from the ear, which may be clear, cloudy, or purulent (pus-like).
Ear Pain: Discomfort or pain in the ear is common, especially if an infection is present.
Itching: The ear canal may feel itchy or irritated.
Hearing Loss: Fluid buildup can lead to temporary hearing impairment.
Fever: In cases of infection, a fever may accompany other symptoms.

diseases.name: Otosclerosis
diseases.description: Otosclerosis is a rare condition that commonly leads to progressive hearing loss , especially among young to middle-aged adults. It occurs when one of the small bones in the middle ear, called the stapes, becomes abnormally fixed in place due to irregular bone growth. This prevents it from vibrating properly in response to sound, which is essential for transmitting sound waves from the middle ear to the inner ear.
symptoms: Otosclerosis often develops gradually, and many individuals may not notice the symptoms in the early stages. However, certain signs can be recognized either by the person affected or by family members.
The most common symptoms include:
Gradual hearing loss, typically starting in one ear and later affecting the other
Difficulty hearing low-pitched sounds, such as whispers
Paradoxical hearing improvement in noisy environments, due to the way otosclerosis affects lower frequencies
Tinnitus – a ringing, buzzing, roaring, or hissing sound in the ears or head
Dizziness
Balance problems, including occasional vertigo
If you or someone you know is experiencing these symptoms, especially progressive hearing loss, it is advisable to consult an ENT specialist or audiologist for further evaluation and diagnosis.

diseases.name: Ototoxicity - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ototoxicity is a term that refers to the harmful effects of certain substances on the inner ear, leading to hearing loss, balance issues, and other auditory problems. This condition is significant because it can arise from various sources, including medications, environmental toxins, and even certain diseases. Understanding ototoxicity is crucial for early detection and management, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of ototoxicity can vary depending on the severity and cause of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Hearing Loss: This can range from mild to profound and may affect one or both ears.
Tinnitus: A persistent ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in the ears.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance or feeling unsteady.
Ear Fullness: A sensation of pressure or fullness in the ear.

diseases.name: Outwit Poison Ivy: Is It Communicable?
diseases.description: A Poison ivy rash is an allergic reaction of the skin. The rash is not communicable. The allergy is caused by direct contact with an oily resin called urushiol. The oil is in the roots, stems and leaves of poison ivy, poison oak and poison sumac.
symptoms: If you are in doubt, check for the following signs and symptoms in the area of contact—redness, itching, swelling. Blisters and hives might develop in serious cases.
You may experience difficulty in breathing if you have breathed the smoke from burning poison ivy.

diseases.name: Ovarian Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Ovarian cancer is a group of cancers that begin in or near the ovaries. Because the ovaries sit deep in the pelvis and early symptoms can be subtle, the disease is sometimes diagnosed after it has spread within the abdomen. Even so, outcomes continue to improve with modern surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, targeted maintenance therapies, and coordinated multidisciplinary care. This article explains what ovarian cancer is, how it's diagnosed and staged, today's treatment options, recovery and follow-up, prevention and risk reduction, international patient support, and answers to common questions.
symptoms: Ovarian cancer symptoms may seem like ordinary stomach or bladder problems. Watch out for:
Increasing abdominal girth from fluid (ascites)
Unintentional weight loss or loss of muscle
Shortness of breath (large ascites or pleural effusion)
Pelvic mass found on examination or imaging
👉 If these symptoms keep coming back for more than 2–3 weeks, see a gynecologist.

diseases.name: Ovarian Cyst: Causes and Symptoms
diseases.description: An ovarian cyst is a solid or a fluid-filled pocket in or on the surface of your ovary. Women have two ovaries, each of an almond shape and size on each side of the uterus. Eggs develop in these ovaries and are released during your monthly cycles.

diseases.name: Ovarian Dermoid Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ovarian dermoid cysts, also known as mature cystic teratomas, are a type of benign tumor that can develop in the ovaries. These cysts are significant not only because of their potential to cause discomfort and complications but also due to their unique composition, which can include hair, skin, and even teeth. Understanding ovarian dermoid cysts is crucial for women’s health, as early detection and appropriate management can lead to better outcomes.
symptoms: Ovarian dermoid cysts can be asymptomatic, meaning many women may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Pelvic Pain: This can range from mild discomfort to severe pain, especially if the cyst ruptures.
Abdominal Swelling: A noticeable increase in abdominal size may occur due to the cyst's growth.
Changes in Menstrual Cycle: Irregularities in menstrual periods can be a sign of ovarian issues.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may arise if the cyst causes pressure on surrounding organs.
Urinary Symptoms: Increased frequency or urgency of urination can occur if the cyst presses on the bladder.

diseases.name: Ovarian Endometrioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ovarian endometrioma, often referred to as "chocolate cysts," is a type of cyst that forms on the ovaries as a result of endometriosis. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on reproductive health but also due to its association with chronic pelvic pain and infertility. Understanding ovarian endometrioma is crucial for women who may be affected by this condition, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can lead to better health outcomes.
symptoms: Pelvic Pain: This is the most common symptom, often worsening during menstruation.
Painful Intercourse: Discomfort during or after sexual activity is frequently reported.
Menstrual Irregularities: Heavy or irregular periods may occur.
Infertility: Many women with ovarian endometriomas experience difficulty conceiving.
Bloating and Nausea: Some women report gastrointestinal symptoms, including bloating and nausea.

diseases.name: Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) refers to an amplified response of female hormones. It occurs when injectable hormone medications are given to stimulate the ovaries. Mild cases of OHSS improve on their own, while severe cases require hospitalization.
symptoms: Symptoms of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome can be mild, moderate or severe. Most women experience them within one to two weeks after injecting gonadotropins.
Mild to moderate symptoms of OHSS
Moderate abdominal pain
Bloating and feeling full
Nausea and vomiting
Pain in the pelvis due to tender ovaries
In most women, a mild ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome resolves on its own.
Rapid weight gain — more than 2.2 pounds (1 kilogram) in 24 hours
Severe abdominal pain
Severe, persistent nausea and vomiting
Blood clots
Decreased urination
Shortness of breath
Tight or enlarged abdomen
A severe form of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome requires urgent hospitalization and medical attention.

diseases.name: Ovarian Torsion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ovarian torsion is a serious medical condition that occurs when an ovary twists around the ligaments that hold it in place, cutting off its blood supply. This condition can lead to severe pain and, if not treated promptly, can result in the loss of the affected ovary. Understanding ovarian torsion is crucial for women of all ages, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding ovarian torsion.
symptoms: The symptoms of ovarian torsion can vary but typically include:
Severe Pelvic Pain: Sudden onset of sharp, severe pain on one side of the lower abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Accompanying symptoms may include nausea and vomiting due to the intensity of the pain.
Abdominal Tenderness: The affected area may be tender to the touch.
Changes in Menstrual Cycle: Some women may experience changes in their menstrual cycle, including delayed periods.

diseases.name: Overactive Bladder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a common yet often misunderstood condition that affects millions of people worldwide. Characterized by a sudden and uncontrollable urge to urinate, OAB can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. It is not merely a nuisance; it can lead to social embarrassment, anxiety, and even depression. Understanding OAB is crucial for those affected, as well as for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of overactive bladder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of overactive bladder is essential for timely diagnosis and treatment.
Urgency: A sudden, compelling need to urinate that is difficult to control.
Frequency: Needing to urinate more than eight times in a 24-hour period.
Nocturia: Waking up multiple times during the night to urinate.
Urge Incontinence: Involuntary leakage of urine following a strong urge to urinate.

diseases.name: Overflow Incontinence - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Overflow incontinence is a condition that affects many individuals, often leading to significant discomfort and embarrassment. It occurs when the bladder is unable to empty completely, resulting in involuntary leakage of urine. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of overflow incontinence, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies. Understanding this condition is crucial for those affected, as well as their families and caregivers, to ensure timely intervention and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of overflow incontinence can vary but typically include:
Frequent Urination: An increased need to urinate, often with little urine produced.
Dribbling: Continuous leakage of urine, especially after urination.
Weak Urine Stream: Difficulty initiating urination or a weak stream.
Feeling of Incomplete Emptying: A sensation that the bladder is not fully emptied after urination.

diseases.name: Overpronation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Overpronation is a common biomechanical issue that affects many individuals, particularly those who engage in physical activities such as running or walking. It occurs when the foot rolls inward excessively during the gait cycle, which can lead to various complications if left unaddressed. Understanding overpronation is crucial not only for athletes but also for anyone who wants to maintain optimal foot health and prevent potential injuries. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of overpronation.
symptoms: Individuals with overpronation may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Foot Pain: Discomfort in the arch, heel, or ball of the foot is common.
Knee Pain: Overpronation can lead to misalignment of the knees, resulting in pain or discomfort.
Shin Splints: This condition, characterized by pain along the shin bone, is often associated with overpronation.
Plantar Fasciitis: Inflammation of the plantar fascia can occur due to excessive foot rolling.
Hip and Lower Back Pain: The misalignment caused by overpronation can extend to the hips and lower back, leading to discomfort.

diseases.name: Overriding Aorta - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The heart is a remarkable organ, responsible for pumping blood throughout the body and ensuring that all tissues receive the oxygen and nutrients they need. However, congenital heart defects can disrupt this vital function, one of which is the condition known as an overriding aorta. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of overriding aorta, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook. By understanding this condition, patients and their families can better navigate the complexities of diagnosis and treatment.
symptoms: Symptoms of an overriding aorta can vary depending on the severity of the defect and whether it is associated with other heart conditions. Common symptoms may include:
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, lips, and nails due to low oxygen levels in the blood.
Difficulty Breathing: Shortness of breath or rapid breathing, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lethargy, particularly in infants and children.
Poor Weight Gain: Infants may struggle to gain weight or grow at a normal rate.
Heart Murmurs: Abnormal sounds during a heartbeat, often detected during a physical examination.

diseases.name: Paget Disease of Bone - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Paget’s disease is a bone illness that disrupts your body’s natural recycling mechanism, which involves new bone tissue progressively replacing old bone tissue. Bones can become brittle and deformed over time. The most often affected areas are the pelvis, skull, spine, and legs. The risk of Paget’s disease of the bones increases as you become older and if you have a family member suffering from the condition.
symptoms: Pelvis: It can cause hip pain, when the condition affects the pelvis
Skull: An overgrowth of bone in your skull can lead to headaches or hearing loss
Spine: It can lead to nerve root compression and cause numbness, tingling and pain in a leg or an arm

Leg: As the bones get weakened, they cab bend which may result in causing bowlegs . Misshapen and enlarged bones in the legs can put extra stress on your nearby joints, which may lead to osteoarthritis in your hip or knee
Hip pain
Weakness
Constipation
The fracturing of the bone easily
Loss of appetite
Abdominal pain
Fatigue
Twisting or weakening of bones

diseases.name: Paget's Disease of Bone
diseases.description: Paget's disease of bone is a chronic disease that causes bones to grow larger and weaker than normal. In Paget's disease, the process of old bone being replaced by new bone is disrupted. The new bone that forms is softer and weaker. Paget's disease most commonly occurs in the pelvis, skull, spine, and legs.
symptoms: Bone pain
Enlarged head size
Bowing of legs
Hearing loss (if skull affected)
Hip pain
Damage to cartilage of joints adjacent to affected bone
Nerve problems if spine affected

diseases.name: Paget’s Disease of the Breast - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Paget’s disease of the breast is a rare type of breast cancer that affects the skin of the nipple and the darker area around it (areola). Unlike other breast cancers that form a lump deeper in the breast tissue, this cancer often starts in the milk ducts and spreads to the surface of the nipple and areola.
symptoms: Paget’s disease often mimics skin conditions, which can make it tricky to identify.
Redness, flaking, or scaly skin on the nipple or areola
Itching, tingling, or burning around the nipple
Flattened or inverted nipple
Discharge from the nipple (sometimes bloody or yellowish)
A lump in the breast (in about half of patients)
Thickened skin on the nipple or areola
If you notice these changes in one breast, especially if they don’t improve with creams or ointments, it’s important to see a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Pain At Pressure Points? You May Have A Stress Fracture
diseases.description: Stress fractures are minute cracks in your bones often developed owing to repetitive force (stress) such as constant running or jumping. Stress fractures can be caused by repetitive force, often from overuse — like running long distances or repeatedly jumping up and down.
