They can also develop from normal use of a bone that is weakened by a condition called osteoporosis (weak or porous bone).
symptoms: Stress fractures don’t show any major signs. The most common symptoms include:
Pain in body parts surrounding the affected bone
Swelling around the fracture site
Bruising
Tenderness at the fracture site
Pain that diminishes or stays after rest

diseases.name: Pancoast Tumor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pancoast tumors are a rare type of lung cancer that arise in the apex, or top, of the lung. Named after Dr. H. Richard Pancoast, who first described them in the early 20th century, these tumors are significant due to their unique location and the complex symptoms they can cause. Unlike more common lung cancers, Pancoast tumors often invade nearby structures, leading to a distinct set of challenges in diagnosis and treatment. Understanding Pancoast tumors is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly impact patient outcomes.
symptoms: Pancoast tumors can present with a variety of symptoms, many of which may be mistaken for other conditions. Common symptoms include:
Shoulder Pain: Often the first symptom, this pain can radiate down the arm and may be mistaken for a musculoskeletal issue.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area, particularly on the side of the tumor.
Cough: A persistent cough that may produce blood or phlegm.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of breathlessness.
Horner's Syndrome: A rare condition characterized by drooping eyelids, constricted pupils, and loss of sweating on one side of the face, indicating nerve involvement.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can occur as the body fights the cancer.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.

diseases.name: Pancreas Divisum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pancreas divisum is a congenital anomaly of the pancreas that affects its drainage system. This condition occurs when the pancreatic duct, which is responsible for transporting digestive enzymes from the pancreas to the small intestine, does not fuse properly during fetal development. As a result, the pancreas has two separate drainage systems instead of one. While many individuals with pancreas divisum may remain asymptomatic, the condition can lead to complications such as pancreatitis, making it significant in the field of gastroenterology. Understanding pancreas divisum is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, especially for those who experience symptoms.
symptoms: Many individuals with pancreas divisum are asymptomatic. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Abdominal Pain: Often located in the upper abdomen, this pain can be intermittent or persistent and may worsen after eating.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur, especially during episodes of abdominal pain.
Digestive Issues: Individuals may experience diarrhea or steatorrhea (fatty stools) due to malabsorption of nutrients.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to chronic digestive issues.

diseases.name: Pancreatic Cancer and Its Symptoms Introduction
diseases.description: Cases of pancreatic cancer in India are on the rise. The prevalence rate of pancreatic cancer globally is 1 in 1,00,000 people per year. The prevalence rate in men in India is 0.5 to 2.4, while in women, it is 0.2 to 1.8 per 1,00,000. The risk factor for pancreatic cancer is smoking and sedentary lifestyle.
symptoms: Patients experience the symptoms of pancreatic cancer in the advanced stage. The presence of a few symptoms does not confirm the presence of pancreatic cancer. The symptoms may be due to other underlying medical conditions. Some of the symptoms of pancreatic cancer are:

Abdominal Pain Or Back Pain : Pancreatic cancer may cause pain in the belly or the back. An increase in the size of the pancreas due to cancer may press the surrounding organs resulting in pain. Further, the pancreas also compresses the nearby nerves, which also causes pain.

Jaundice : The head of the pancreas is present near the bile duct. Jaundice may be the early-stage symptom of pancreatic cancer if it starts in the head of the pancreas. If cancer initiates in the tail or body of the pancreas, jaundice may occur at an advanced stage. The pancreatic enlargement compresses the bile duct resulting in its blockage. This results in the accumulation of bile and high bilirubin levels in the body.

Enlargement of Liver Or Gallbladder: Pancreatic cancer may cause enlargement of the gallbladder or liver. When cancer blocks the bile duct, the bile accumulates in the gallbladder, causing gallbladder enlargement. Liver enlargement may also occur when pancreatic cancer spreads to the liver.

Diabetes : Pancreas has insulin-secreting cells. When the cancer damages these cells, the patient may experience symptoms of diabetes . The symptoms of diabetes include frequent urination, excessive thirst and hunger, and persistent fatigue.
Nausea and Vomiting : Cancer in the pancreas may also cause problems in the stomach. The patient may experience nausea and vomiting. The patient may feel stomach pain that becomes severe with eating.

Blood Clots: In some cases of pancreatic cancer, the presence of blood clots is the first sign of pancreatic cancer. The blood clot usually occurs in the legs. This condition is known as deep vein thrombosis . Sometimes the blood clot may travel to the lungs and cause respiratory complications.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Like in various other cancers, patients with pancreatic cancer may experience unexplained weight loss.
Loss of Appetite: Pancreatic cancer results in burning more calories than normal and causes muscle protein to break down. It also suppresses the appetite of the patients.
Weakness Or fatigue: The patient with pancreatic cancer experiences extreme fatigue and tiredness
When to See a Doctor
Pancreatic cancer might not show symptoms during the early stage. Book an appointment with your doctor:
If you have jaundice or any other symptoms that concern you
If you have persistent fatigue, nausea, and vomiting
If you have an increased risk of pancreatic cancer
If you have a family history of pancreatic cancer
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: Pancreatic Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pancreatic cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form in the pancreas, an organ located behind the stomach that plays a crucial role in digestion and blood sugar regulation. While many pancreatic cysts are benign and asymptomatic, their presence can sometimes indicate underlying health issues or lead to complications. Understanding pancreatic cysts is essential for early detection and effective management, as they can impact overall health and well-being.
symptoms: Pancreatic cysts often do not present symptoms, especially when they are small. However, larger cysts or those that cause complications may lead to the following symptoms:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen, which may radiate to the back.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur if the cyst compresses surrounding structures.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur due to changes in appetite or digestive issues.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes can happen if a cyst obstructs the bile duct.

diseases.name: Pancreatic Pseudocysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pancreatic pseudocysts are fluid-filled sacs that form in the pancreas, often as a result of pancreatitis, which is inflammation of the pancreas. These pseudocysts can vary in size and may cause significant discomfort and complications if left untreated. Understanding pancreatic pseudocysts is crucial for early detection and management, as they can lead to serious health issues. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pancreatic pseudocysts, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Abdominal Pain: This is the most common symptom, often felt in the upper abdomen and may radiate to the back.
Nausea and Vomiting: Patients may experience persistent nausea and occasional vomiting.
Bloating and Fullness: A feeling of fullness or bloating may occur due to the presence of the pseudocyst.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can happen due to pain and dietary changes.
Fever: In some cases, fever may indicate an infection associated with the pseudocyst.

diseases.name: Pancytopenia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pancytopenia is a medical condition characterized by a reduction in the number of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets in the bloodstream. This triad of blood cell deficiencies can lead to a variety of health issues, making it a significant concern in the field of medicine. Understanding pancytopenia is crucial, as it can be a symptom of underlying diseases, ranging from benign to life-threatening conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pancytopenia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Pancytopenia can manifest through various symptoms, which may vary depending on the severity of the condition:
Fatigue: A common symptom due to anemia, leading to decreased oxygen delivery to tissues.
Weakness: Generalized weakness can occur as a result of low red blood cell counts.
Frequent Infections: A decrease in white blood cells can lead to increased susceptibility to infections.
Easy Bruising or Bleeding: Low platelet counts can result in easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from cuts, or spontaneous bleeding.
Pale Skin: Anemia can cause paleness due to reduced red blood cell levels.

diseases.name: Pandas Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pandas Syndrome, or Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal infections, is a condition that has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its complex interplay between infections and neuropsychiatric symptoms. This syndrome primarily affects children and is characterized by sudden onset of obsessive-compulsive behaviors, tics, and other neuropsychiatric symptoms following a streptococcal infection. Understanding Pandas Syndrome is crucial for parents, educators, and healthcare providers, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes for affected children.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pandas Syndrome can vary widely among affected children but typically include:
Obsessive-Compulsive Behaviors: Sudden onset of intrusive thoughts and compulsive actions.
Tics: Motor or vocal tics that may appear suddenly and can be severe.
Emotional Disturbances: Increased irritability, anxiety, mood swings, and emotional lability.
Behavioral Changes: Regression in behavior, such as loss of previously acquired skills or increased separation anxiety.
Physical Symptoms: Sleep disturbances, bedwetting, and changes in appetite.

diseases.name: Panhypopituitarism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Panhypopituitarism is a rare but significant endocrine disorder characterized by the inadequate production of hormones by the pituitary gland. This condition can lead to a cascade of health issues, affecting various bodily functions and overall well-being. Understanding panhypopituitarism is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can have profound implications for an individual's health.
symptoms: Panhypopituitarism presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary depending on the specific hormones that are deficient. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy.
Weight Changes: Unexplained weight loss or gain due to metabolic imbalances.
Cold Intolerance: Increased sensitivity to cold temperatures.
Decreased Libido: Reduced sexual desire and function.
Menstrual Irregularities: In women, changes in menstrual cycles or amenorrhea (absence of menstruation).
Growth Issues: In children, stunted growth or delayed puberty.
Low Blood Pressure: Hypotension can occur due to adrenal insufficiency.
Hypoglycemia: Low blood sugar levels leading to dizziness or fainting.

diseases.name: Panic Attack - Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: A panic attack causes sudden fear, overwhelming feelings, and strong reactions to normal, ordinary, and non-threatening situations. In a panic attack situation, an individual can sweat a lot and can have difficulty breathing and feel as if they are about to have a heart attack .

diseases.name: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (Cancer): Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Your heart rate, blood pressure, metabolism, and growth are influenced by various hormones released by your thyroid gland. When your thyroid gland fails to function efficiently for several reasons, it causes havoc in your body. One of the reasons for the inefficient functioning of your thyroid gland can be papillary thyroid carcinoma.
symptoms: Papillary thyroid carcinoma causes solid or fluid-filled nodules on your thyroid. Usually, this is accidentally detected when your doctor is diagnosing or testing for another health condition. Papillary thyroid carcinoma is asymptomatic, meaning it doesn’t show any symptoms at an early stage. However, as cancer progresses, you may experience the following symptoms:
Visible lumps that can be felt as well
Difficulty in and painful swallowing
Food or pills getting stuck in the throat
Sore throat or constant hoarseness that doesn’t decrease
Inflammation of the lymph nodes
Difficulty breathing, mainly when you are lying down
In rare cases, you may experience neck, jaw, and ear pain

diseases.name: Paraganglioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paraganglioma is a rare type of tumor that arises from paraganglia, which are clusters of neuroendocrine cells found throughout the body. These tumors can develop in various locations, including the head, neck, abdomen, and pelvis. Paragangliomas are significant not only because of their rarity but also due to their potential to produce hormones that can lead to serious health complications. Understanding paraganglioma is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of paraganglioma can vary widely depending on the tumor's location and whether it produces hormones. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Often due to elevated blood pressure from catecholamine secretion.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Sweating: Excessive sweating can occur, especially in sympathetic paragangliomas.
High Blood Pressure: Persistent hypertension is a common symptom.
Facial Pain or Swelling: Particularly in head and neck paragangliomas.
Difficulty Swallowing: If the tumor is located near the throat.

diseases.name: Paralysis – Causes, Symptoms and Types & Treatment
diseases.description: The human nervous system is an intricate, highly complex, yet fascinating part of the body, through which the brain controls and communicates to different parts of body. But it’s also the most susceptible to lasting damage if it encounters physical trauma or injury. Paralysis is when you can’t move certain parts of your body after something goes wrong with their connection to your brain.
symptoms: The primary symptom is the loss of muscle function in any or all parts of the body. Early symptoms involve numbness or a tingling sensation in a patient’s toes and fingers.

Patients suffering from paralysis due to a birth defect, spinal cord injury or stroke would lose control over their muscles almost instantly. But patients who experience paralysis due to an underlying medical condition, would lose muscle function slowly over a period of time.
Paralysis can also be classified based on which part of the body is affected.
Monoplegia affects just one limb.
Diplegia affects the same area on both sides, like both arms, both legs, or both sides of your face.
Hemiplegia affects just one side of your body and is usually caused by a stroke , which damages one side of your brain.
Quadriplegia (or tetraplegia) is when all four limbs are paralyzed, sometimes along with certain organs.
Paraplegia is paralysis from the waist down.
Locked-in syndrome is the rarest and most severe form of paralysis, where a person loses control of all their muscles except the ones that control them eye movements.

diseases.name: Paralytic Ileus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paralytic ileus is a condition that affects the normal movement of the intestines, leading to a temporary cessation of bowel activity. This condition is significant because it can result in severe abdominal pain, bloating, and complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding paralytic ileus is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early recognition and management can prevent serious health issues.
symptoms: The symptoms of paralytic ileus can vary in severity but often include:
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the abdomen.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur as the body attempts to expel contents that cannot pass through the intestines.
Constipation: Inability to pass stool or gas.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat due to discomfort.

diseases.name: Paraneoplastic Syndromes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paraneoplastic syndromes are a group of disorders that arise in patients with cancer, resulting from the immune system's response to the tumor or from substances produced by the tumor itself. These syndromes can manifest in various ways, affecting multiple organ systems and leading to a wide range of symptoms. Understanding paraneoplastic syndromes is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as they can significantly impact the quality of life and may even precede the diagnosis of cancer. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of paraneoplastic syndromes, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Paraneoplastic syndromes can present with a wide array of symptoms, depending on the organ systems affected. Common symptoms include:

Neurological Symptoms: These may include weakness, numbness, coordination problems, and cognitive changes. Conditions like Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome and paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration are examples of neurological paraneoplastic syndromes.

Endocrine Symptoms: Hormonal imbalances can lead to symptoms such as weight gain, changes in appetite, and abnormal blood sugar levels. For instance, ectopic hormone production by tumors can cause Cushing's syndrome.
Dermatological Symptoms: Skin changes, such as rashes or hyperpigmentation, can occur in some paraneoplastic syndromes.
Hematological Symptoms: Anemia, thrombocytopenia, or other blood-related issues may arise due to the cancer or its treatment.

diseases.name: Paranoid Personality Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paranoid Personality Disorder (PPD) is a mental health condition characterized by pervasive distrust and suspicion of others. Individuals with PPD often believe that others are out to harm them, deceive them, or exploit them, even in the absence of evidence. This disorder can significantly impact personal relationships, work life, and overall quality of life. Understanding PPD is crucial not only for those affected but also for their families, friends, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Paranoid Personality Disorder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Individuals with Paranoid Personality Disorder may exhibit a range of symptoms, including:
Distrust and Suspicion: A pervasive belief that others are untrustworthy or have ulterior motives.
Interpreting Neutral Events as Threatening: Misinterpreting benign comments or actions as personal attacks.
Reluctance to Confide in Others: A fear that information shared will be used against them.
Holding Grudges: An inability to forgive perceived slights or insults.
Perceiving Attacks on Character: A tendency to react with anger or hostility to perceived criticism.
Social Isolation: Avoiding social interactions due to fear of betrayal or harm.
Hypervigilance: Being excessively alert to potential threats or dangers.

diseases.name: Paranoid Schizophrenia: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Risk Factors
diseases.description: Paranoid schizophrenia is considered the most common form of schizophrenia. A patient having paranoid schizophrenia often experiences delusions, and hallucinations. If a patient has schizophrenia, they find it difficult to distinguish between fantasy and reality, thus affecting the way they perceive and interact with the world. In 2013, the American Psychiatric Association recognized paranoia as one of the chief symptoms of schizophrenia , but not a separate diagnostic condition. Consequently, the name of this condition was changed to simply, ‘schizophrenia’.
symptoms: The symptoms of paranoid schizophrenia include the following:
● Delusions such as delusions of control, grandeur, jealousy, and persecution.
● Hallucinations- hearing, feeling, seeing, smelling, or tasting things that are not present
● Disorganized thinking and behavior
● Withdrawing from family, friends, and other activities
● Lack of motivation and self-care
● Suicidal thoughts and behaviour

diseases.name: Paraovarian Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paraovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs that develop near the ovaries, often without causing any symptoms. While they are generally benign and may not require treatment, understanding their significance is crucial for women’s health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of paraovarian cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Most paraovarian cysts are asymptomatic and do not cause any noticeable symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen, which may be sharp or dull.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Menstrual Irregularities: Changes in menstrual cycle patterns, although this is less common.
Pressure Symptoms: Increased urinary frequency or difficulty emptying the bladder due to pressure from the cyst.

diseases.name: Paraplegia
diseases.description: Paraplegia is a spinal cord injury that paralyses the lower limbs. It is a result of severe damage to the spinal cord and the nervous system. Paraplegia mainly affects the trunk, legs, and the pelvic region, resulting in loss of movement.
symptoms: Loss of ability to feel and move
No control over bowel and bladder activities
Intense pain or tingling sensation in the trunk, legs, and the pelvic region
Problems in breathing and coughing
Sexual function and fertility can be affected
There are no apparent symptoms that could be seen. Moreover, there may be delayed symptoms like numbness and paralyses.

diseases.name: Paraquat Poisoning - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paraquat poisoning is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition resulting from exposure to paraquat, a highly toxic herbicide widely used in agriculture. Its significance lies not only in the health risks it poses to individuals who come into contact with it but also in the broader implications for public health and safety. Understanding paraquat poisoning is crucial for farmers, agricultural workers, and the general public, as it can lead to severe health complications and even death if not addressed promptly.
symptoms: The symptoms of paraquat poisoning can vary depending on the route of exposure and the amount ingested. Common symptoms include:
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.
Respiratory Symptoms: Coughing, shortness of breath, and chest pain.
Neurological Symptoms: Confusion, seizures, and tremors.
Skin Reactions: Burns or irritation at the site of contact.

diseases.name: Parathyroid Adenoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Parathyroid adenoma is a benign tumor of the parathyroid glands, which are small glands located in the neck that play a crucial role in regulating calcium levels in the body. These glands produce parathyroid hormone (PTH), which helps maintain the balance of calcium and phosphorus in the bloodstream and bones. The significance of parathyroid adenoma lies in its potential to disrupt this balance, leading to various health issues, including hypercalcemia (high calcium levels), osteoporosis, and kidney stones. Understanding parathyroid adenoma is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring better health outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of parathyroid adenoma primarily stem from elevated calcium levels in the blood. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy.
Weakness: Muscle weakness and decreased physical endurance.
Bone Pain: Discomfort or pain in the bones, often due to osteoporosis.
Kidney Stones: Increased calcium levels can lead to the formation of kidney stones, causing severe pain.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal disturbances may occur.
Increased Thirst and Urination: Excessive thirst and frequent urination are common due to the body's attempt to eliminate excess calcium.

diseases.name: Parathyroid Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Parathyroid cancer is a very rare type of cancer that begins in the parathyroid glands, which are four small glands located in your neck near the thyroid gland. These glands help control the body's calcium levels by producing a hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH).
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of parathyroid cancer are mainly related to high calcium levels (hypercalcemia) in the blood. Common symptoms include:
Persistent bone pain or fractures.
Kidney stones or frequent urination.
Severe fatigue, weakness, or muscle aches.
Nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite.
Constipation and abdominal pain.
Depression, confusion, or memory problems.
A noticeable lump in the neck (less common).

In advanced cases, the tumor may invade nearby tissues, causing hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, or breathing problems. Some patients may be asymptomatic at diagnosis or present only with a neck lump

diseases.name: Parkinson’s Disease
diseases.description: Parkinson’s disease is a neurodegenerative disease that manifests as a movement disorder. The main features of Parkinson’s disease are a progressive loss of muscle control leading to trembling of the head and limbs at rest, slowness, stiffness, and impaired balance. As symptoms worsen, it becomes difficult to talk, walk and complete simple tasks. The progression of the disease and the degree of injury differ from person to person. Many persons with Parkinson ‘s disease may live long, productive life, while others become disabled more quickly. Complications of Parkinson’s are pneumonia or injuries due to falls leading to premature death of the person. The life expectancy of people with and without Parkinson’s disease is about the same as the general population. Persons who develop Parkinson’s disease are usually above 60 years of age. Since overall life expectancy is rising, the number of individuals with Parkinson’s disease will increase in the future. Though the adult-onset disease is more common, early-onset Parkinson’s disease (onset between 21-40 years) and juvenile-onset Parkinson’s disease (onset before age 21) can also occur. Historically, Parkinson’s disease was reported 5000 BC ago in the ancient Indian civilization. It was known as Kampavata and was treated with plant seeds which have therapeutic levels of levodopa. Parkinson’s disease is named after James Parkinson, a British doctor, who first described the disorder as “shaking palsy.”
symptoms: The primary symptoms usually start on one side of the body and are related to voluntary and involuntary motor function. Mild symptoms are present in the beginning and will improve over time. By the time that primary symptoms appear, individuals with Parkinson’s disease will have lost 60% to 80% or more of the dopamine-producing cells in the brain. Most of the important motor symptoms include the following:

Tremors : Trembling in hands, arms, fingers, legs, feet, jaw, or head. The person usually has resting tremors but not while involved in a task. Tremors usually worsen when the person is tired, excited or stressed.

Rigidity : The limbs and trunk become stiff, which increase during movement. Rigidity usually causes muscle pain and aches. Cramped handwriting (micrographia) occurs due to loss of fine hand movements and lead to difficult in eating.
Bradykinesia : The voluntary movements become slow. After sometime, it becomes difficult to initiate movements. An expressionless mask-like facies also occurs.
Postural Instability : Due to lost or impaired reflexes it becomes difficult to change posture or maintain balance. Instability in the Posture may lead to falls.

Parkinsonian Gait : Persons with more progressive Parkinson’s disease usually have a characteristic shuffling walk with an arched position and a diminished or absent arm swing. It becomes difficult to start walking and to make turns. Individuals may freeze in mid-stride and appear to fall forward while walking.

The foremost symptoms of Parkinson’s disease are a progressive loss of muscle control. Damage to the brain leads to secondary symptoms. These vary in severity, and not every individual will experience all of them. The symptoms usually start on one side of the body; Some of the secondary symptoms include
Insecurity, Anxiety, and stroke
Memory loss , Confusion, and dementia (more common in elderly individuals)
Depression
Constipation
Excessive salivation and difficulty swallowing
Sense of smell is reduced
Sweating increases
Erectile dysfunction in males
Skin problems
Quieter speech, slowed and monotone voice
Urinary frequency or urgency

diseases.name: Parosmia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Parosmia is a condition that affects the sense of smell, leading to distorted perceptions of odors. For individuals experiencing parosmia, familiar scents may become unpleasant or even repulsive. This condition can significantly impact quality of life, affecting appetite, nutrition, and emotional well-being. Understanding parosmia is crucial, especially in the context of recent global health events, where it has gained attention as a symptom associated with viral infections, particularly COVID-19. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of parosmia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of parosmia is the distortion of smell. Individuals may experience:
Altered Smell Perception: Familiar scents may smell different, often unpleasant.
Nausea: The unpleasant odors can lead to feelings of nausea or even vomiting.
Loss of Appetite: Distorted smells can affect food enjoyment, leading to decreased appetite and potential weight loss.
Emotional Distress: The psychological impact of parosmia can lead to anxiety or depression.

diseases.name: Paroxysmal Hemicrania - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Paroxysmal Hemicrania (PH) is a rare and debilitating headache disorder characterized by recurrent, unilateral (one-sided) headaches that occur in clusters. These headaches can be extremely painful and are often accompanied by autonomic symptoms such as tearing and nasal congestion. Understanding Paroxysmal Hemicrania is crucial not only for those who suffer from it but also for healthcare providers who may encounter patients with this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Paroxysmal Hemicrania, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark of Paroxysmal Hemicrania is the occurrence of severe, unilateral headaches. Other common symptoms include:
Intensity: The pain is often described as sharp, stabbing, or throbbing.
Duration: Attacks typically last from 2 to 30 minutes.
Frequency: Patients may experience multiple attacks per day, sometimes exceeding 20 episodes.
Autonomic Symptoms: These may include tearing, nasal congestion, or eyelid drooping on the affected side.

diseases.name: Parsonage Turner Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Parsonage Turner Syndrome (PTS), also known as neuralgic amyotrophy, is a rare neurological disorder characterized by sudden onset shoulder pain and weakness in the arm. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to physical limitations and emotional distress. Understanding PTS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can help mitigate its effects and improve recovery outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Parsonage Turner Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Sudden Shoulder Pain: Often described as severe and debilitating, this pain can occur without any apparent cause.
Weakness in the Arm: Following the initial pain, weakness may develop in the shoulder and arm muscles, making it difficult to perform everyday tasks.
Muscle Atrophy: Over time, affected muscles may begin to shrink due to disuse and nerve damage.
Sensory Changes: Some individuals may experience tingling, numbness, or a burning sensation in the arm.

diseases.name: Partial Molar Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Partial molar pregnancy is a rare but significant condition that can occur during early pregnancy. It is a type of gestational trophoblastic disease, which involves abnormal growth of the tissue that normally develops into the placenta. Understanding partial molar pregnancy is crucial for expectant mothers and healthcare providers alike, as it can have implications for maternal health and future pregnancies. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of partial molar pregnancy, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of a partial molar pregnancy can vary, but common signs include:
Vaginal Bleeding: This may occur early in the pregnancy and can be light or heavy.
Enlarged Uterus: The uterus may grow larger than expected for the gestational age.
Severe Nausea and Vomiting: Some women experience hyperemesis gravidarum, which is severe morning sickness.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic area may be present.

diseases.name: Patella Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A patella fracture, commonly known as a kneecap fracture, is a significant injury that can impact mobility and quality of life. The patella is a small, flat bone located at the front of the knee joint, playing a crucial role in knee function and stability. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for patella fractures is essential for anyone who may be at risk or affected by this injury.
symptoms: Pain: Severe pain at the front of the knee, especially when moving or bearing weight.
Swelling: Swelling around the knee joint is common and may develop quickly after the injury.
Bruising: Discoloration around the knee may occur due to bleeding under the skin.
Inability to Move the Knee: Difficulty or inability to straighten the leg or bear weight on the affected knee.
Deformity: In some cases, the kneecap may appear out of place or misaligned.

diseases.name: Patellar Tendinitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Patellar tendinitis, often referred to as "jumper's knee," is a common condition that affects the patellar tendon, which connects the kneecap (patella) to the shinbone (tibia). This condition is particularly significant for athletes and active individuals, as it can severely impact performance and quality of life. Understanding patellar tendinitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their activities with minimal disruption.
symptoms: Common symptoms of patellar tendinitis include:
Pain: Typically located at the front of the knee, just below the kneecap. Pain may worsen with activity, especially jumping or running.
Swelling: The area around the patellar tendon may become swollen and tender to the touch.
Stiffness: Individuals may experience stiffness in the knee, particularly after periods of inactivity.
Weakness: A feeling of weakness in the knee, making it difficult to perform certain movements.

diseases.name: Patellar Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Patellar tendonitis, often referred to as "jumper's knee," is a common condition that affects the patellar tendon, which connects the kneecap (patella) to the shinbone (tibia). This condition is particularly significant for athletes and active individuals, as it can severely impact performance and quality of life. Understanding patellar tendonitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their activities with minimal disruption.
symptoms: Pain: The most prominent symptom is pain located just below the kneecap, which may worsen with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation of the tendon can lead to noticeable swelling around the knee.
Stiffness: Affected individuals may experience stiffness, particularly after periods of inactivity.
Tenderness: The area around the patellar tendon may be tender to the touch.
Weakness: There may be a noticeable weakness in the knee, affecting overall mobility.

diseases.name: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
diseases.description: Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) is a broad term used to describe pain in the front of the knee and around the kneecap (patella). It is sometimes called 'runner's knee' or 'jumper's knee.' The pain often occurs when using stairs, kneeling, squatting, or sitting with bent knees for a long time. It is one of the most common causes of knee pain.
symptoms: Dull, aching pain in the front of the knee or around the kneecap
Pain during activities that repeatedly bend the knee
Pain after prolonged sitting
Clicking or popping sounds in the knee when climbing stairs

diseases.name: PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease) : Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Diet and Treatment
diseases.description: Polycystic Ovarian Disease (PCOD) is one of the most common hormonal disorders affecting women in their reproductive years, typically between the ages of 12 and 45. It is characterized by hormonal imbalances that disrupt normal ovulation and menstrual cycles. In PCOD, the ovaries tend to produce an excess number of immature eggs, which fail to release and eventually form small fluid-filled sacs or cysts.
symptoms: Polycystic Ovarian Disease (PCOD) presents with a range of symptoms primarily related to hormonal imbalance and ovarian dysfunction. While the severity and combination of symptoms can vary among individuals, the following are the most commonly observed in PCOD:

Irregular Menstrual Cycles - Women with PCOD often experience irregular, delayed, or missed periods due to the failure of ovulation. This is a result of multiple immature follicles that do not develop or release properly each month.
Acne and Oily Skin - Hormonal fluctuations, particularly elevated androgen levels, can cause increased sebum production, leading to acne breakouts and oily skin.

Excessive Facial and Body Hair (Hirsutism) - Higher levels of androgens may result in unwanted hair growth on the face, chest, abdomen, or back—a condition known as hirsutism . This is one of the more visible symptoms of PCOD.
Hair Thinning or Hair Loss - Alongside excess body hair, PCOD may also cause thinning of hair on the scalp, especially near the crown, resembling male-pattern baldness.

5. Weight Gain or Difficulty Losing Weight - Women with PCOD often struggle with unexplained weight gain or find it difficult to lose weight despite efforts. This is often related to hormonal imbalance rather than metabolic disorders.
6. Abdominal Bloating or Pelvic Discomfort - Some women may experience mild lower abdominal bloating, pelvic pain, or a feeling of heaviness due to enlarged ovaries filled with immature follicles.
7. Difficulty Conceiving
PCOD is a common cause of infertility. The irregular release of eggs affects ovulation and reduces the chances of conception, especially without medical assistance.

Your doctor will begin by discussing your menstrual history , any patterns of weight gain, skin changes (like acne or hair growth), fertility concerns, and any family history of PCOD or diabetes . This helps assess whether your symptoms align with common PCOD patterns.

diseases.name: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) - Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, and Lifestyle Tips
diseases.description: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is characterized by irregular menstrual cycles, excessive androgen levels, and the presence of multiple cysts in the ovaries. Despite its prevalence, PCOS is often misunderstood, leaving many women searching for answers about its symptoms, causes, treatments, and implications for fertility. This comprehensive guide aims to be your one-stop resource for everything related to PCOS, including PCOS symptoms, causes, treatment options, PCOS diet charts, and its impact on pregnancy.
symptoms: PCOS symptoms can vary widely from person to person. While some women experience severe symptoms, others may have mild or no noticeable signs. Common symptoms include:
Irregular periods: Having fewer than eight periods a year, prolonged menstrual cycles, or abnormally heavy bleeding. PCOS periods can also be unpredictable.

Excessive hair growth (hirsutism): Unwanted hair on the face, chest, back, or other areas typically associated with male-pattern hair growth. Bilateral PCOS symptoms may include hair growth on both sides of the body.
Acne and oily skin: Persistent acne , especially on the face, chest, and upper back, due to increased androgen levels.
Hair thinning or male-pattern baldness: Hair loss on the scalp in a male-pattern distribution.
Weight gain: Difficulty losing weight or unexplained weight gain, often linked to insulin resistance.
Polycystic ovaries: Enlarged ovaries containing multiple small follicles (cysts) visible on an ultrasound.
Infertility: Difficulty conceiving due to irregular ovulation or lack of ovulation.
Mood swings and depression: Hormonal imbalances can lead to emotional distress, including anxiety and depression.
It varies for each person. Some notice changes within 3–6 months, while others may take a year or more. Consistency is key.

diseases.name: Pectus Carinatum - Symptoms, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: Pectus Carinatum is a rare and genetic deformity of the chest wall. It makes the breast-bone (sternum) bulge out and results in the appearance of a pigeon, hence the name pigeon chest.
symptoms: The appearance of symptoms of pectus carinatum can be late, and you may notice the bulging out of the chest bone only as the child reaches puberty. The following symptoms may be present during early childhood or infancy:
Rapid breathing
Asthma
Pain or tenderness in the cartilage having abnormal growth
Irregular depression in the chest
Chest pain
Broad chest with a thin appearance
Recurrent respiratory infections
Irregular curvature of the spine
Shortness of breath after strenuous physical activities

diseases.name: Pectus Excavatum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pectus excavatum, often referred to as "sunken chest" or "funnel chest," is a congenital deformity characterized by a depression in the sternum and rib cage. This condition can vary in severity and may have significant implications for an individual's physical health, self-esteem, and overall quality of life. Understanding pectus excavatum is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can lead to improved outcomes for those affected.
symptoms: Pectus excavatum can present with a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Visible Deformity: A noticeable indentation in the chest wall, which can vary in depth and width.
Respiratory Issues: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical exertion, due to reduced lung capacity.
Cardiovascular Symptoms: Palpitations or irregular heartbeats may occur in severe cases.
Chest Pain: Some individuals report discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Psychosocial Effects: Low self-esteem, anxiety, or depression due to the physical appearance of the chest.

diseases.name: Pediatric Cancer
diseases.description: In India, out of every one million population, 150 children are diagnosed with cancer every year. Cancers affecting children are of a unique kind. Leukemia, cancer of bone marrow and blood, is the most common cancer that accounts for approximately 30 percent of all cancers in children. Common symptoms include fatigue, bone, and joint pain, weakness, bleeding or bruising, pale skin, weight loss, fever amongst others.

diseases.name: Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea
diseases.description: Obstruction of the upper airway because of some reason can cause pediatric obstructive sleep apnea that results in the stoppage of breathing when the child is asleep. It results in a fall in oxygen levels, causing sleep interruption. This can severely affect the growth, behaviour, and learning capability of the child.
symptoms: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea causes an obstruction in breathing while the child is asleep. As this leads to a fall in oxygen levels, the child often wakes up at night and has disturbed sleep. This disturbance is momentary, and the child may not remember this happening. Following are symptoms of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea:
Restless sleep
Choking during sleep or mouth breathing
Bed-wetting or sweating
Unusual sleeping positions
Intermittent snoring with gasps and snorts
Heavy breathing during sleep
Nightmares
Sleepwalking
Behavioral issues
Children with sleep apnea experience difficulty waking up and are either hyperactive or tired during the daytime. They usually also find it difficult to perform well at school.

diseases.name: Pediculosis Capitis: Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Pediculosis capitis, more commonly known as head lice and nits (Lice eggs), is a condition which involves infestation of the human scalp by tiny insects known as lice. Head lice mostly affect children. This condition spreads via use of personal items, like hair brushes, hats, scarves etc. These insects, which are ectoparasites, feed on human blood right from the human scalp. A head lice infestation does not involve any bacterial or viral infection. This is an issue which causes much distress to parents, caregivers and teachers. So, let us take a look at how to stay at a safe distance from these blood-sucking parasites.
symptoms: You may not be exactly aware of a lice infestation as soon as it occurs as the nits or lice eggs are very small, hard to see and often confused with dandruff. They take about a week to hatch. The signs and symptoms commonly observed are:

Itching: Itching on the neck, ears and scalp is one of the most common symptoms. This is an allergic reaction which happens due to louse saliva. However, the itching may not be felt for until after two to six weeks post infestation.
Lice on scalp: Lice may be difficult to spot as they are small and move quickly. However, they may be visible moving down the hair or down the hairline and also felt against the skin at times.
Nits on hair shafts: Nits stick on to your hair shafts and can be difficult to spot because of their small size. They can be found easily around the ears and hairline.
Tickly feeling: Lice could cause a tickling feeling when they move on your scalp or in the hair.
Head sores: Often, scratching the scalp due to lice infestation leads to sores on your head.

diseases.name: Pelizaeus Merzbacher Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pelizaeus Merzbacher Disease (PMD) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the central nervous system. It is classified as a leukodystrophy, which means it involves the abnormal development or destruction of the myelin sheath—the protective covering that surrounds nerve fibers. This disease is significant not only because of its profound impact on affected individuals and their families but also due to its implications for understanding myelin-related disorders. In this article, we will explore the various aspects of PMD, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Pelizaeus Merzbacher Disease presents a range of symptoms that can vary significantly among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Motor Impairments: Delayed motor skills, spasticity, and difficulty with coordination and balance.
Cognitive Impairments: Intellectual disability, learning difficulties, and challenges with communication.
Vision Problems: Nystagmus (involuntary eye movement) and other visual disturbances.
Seizures: Some individuals may experience seizures as a result of abnormal brain activity.
Behavioral Issues: Hyperactivity, anxiety, and other behavioral challenges may occur.

diseases.name: Pellagra - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pellagra is a nutritional deficiency disease primarily caused by a lack of niacin (vitamin B3) in the diet. It is significant not only because of its health implications but also due to its historical context, particularly in regions where corn is a staple food. Understanding pellagra is crucial for public health, especially in areas where dietary deficiencies are prevalent. This article will explore the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of pellagra.
symptoms: Pellagra is characterized by the classic triad of symptoms:
Dermatitis: Skin lesions typically appear on sun-exposed areas, such as the face, neck, and hands. The skin may become red, scaly, and itchy.
Diarrhea: Gastrointestinal symptoms can include diarrhea, which may be severe and lead to dehydration.
Dementia: Neurological symptoms can range from confusion and memory loss to severe cognitive impairment.

diseases.name: Pellucid Marginal Degeneration - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pellucid Marginal Degeneration (PMD) is a progressive eye condition that primarily affects the cornea, leading to significant visual impairment. This condition is characterized by a thinning of the cornea, particularly at the lower part, which can result in irregular astigmatism and other visual disturbances. Understanding PMD is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Pellucid Marginal Degeneration, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Pellucid Marginal Degeneration can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Blurred Vision: One of the most prevalent symptoms, often due to irregular astigmatism caused by corneal thinning.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent, affecting daily activities such as reading or driving.
Increased Sensitivity to Light: Patients may experience discomfort in bright light conditions.
Frequent Changes in Prescription: Individuals may notice that their glasses or contact lens prescriptions change frequently.
Night Vision Problems: Difficulty seeing at night or in low-light conditions is common.

diseases.name: Pelvic Congestion Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pelvic Congestion Syndrome (PCS) is a condition that affects many women, often leading to chronic pelvic pain and discomfort. Despite its prevalence, it remains underdiagnosed and misunderstood. Understanding PCS is crucial not only for those who suffer from it but also for healthcare providers who may encounter patients with unexplained pelvic pain. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Pelvic Congestion Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pelvic Congestion Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Chronic Pelvic Pain: A dull, aching pain that may worsen after prolonged standing or sitting.
Pain During Intercourse: Discomfort or pain during sexual activity.
Menstrual Irregularities: Changes in menstrual cycles, including increased pain during menstruation.
Varicose Veins: Visible varicose veins in the vulvar or pelvic area.
Lower Back Pain: Discomfort in the lower back that may accompany pelvic pain.
Swelling: Swelling in the legs or pelvic area, particularly after long periods of standing.

diseases.name: Pelvic Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pelvic fractures are significant injuries that can have serious implications for an individual's health and mobility. The pelvis, a complex structure of bones at the base of the spine, supports the weight of the upper body and protects vital organs in the lower abdomen. When a fracture occurs in this area, it can lead to complications that affect not only physical function but also overall quality of life. Understanding pelvic fractures, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is crucial for anyone looking to maintain their health and well-being.
symptoms: Pelvic fractures can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Pain: Severe pain in the pelvic area, lower back, or hips.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling and bruising around the pelvic region.
Difficulty Walking: Inability to bear weight or walk without assistance.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations in the legs or groin area due to nerve involvement.

diseases.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) - Symptoms, Diagnosis, Risks, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is a bacterial infection of the female reproductive organs. PID is often transmitted sexually, but not always. While chlamydia or gonorrhea infections are the most common, PID can also be caused by many types of bacteria. Usually, these bacteria are contracted during unprotected sex. These bacteria spread from your vagina to your fallopian tubes, uterus, and ovaries when the normal barrier created by the cervix gets disturbed. This can occur during menstruation and after childbirth, abortion, or miscarriage.
symptoms: Some women do not always show signs of PID until there are difficulties during pregnancy. The symptoms of the pelvic inflammatory disease include the following –
The pain intensity ranges from moderate to severe, primarily in the lower abdominal area and pelvis.
Vaginal discharge – It can be an abnormal and heavy discharge with a bad smell.
Uterine bleeding – It is abnormal and between periods or after sexual intercourse.
Intercourse accompanied by frequent pain.
You might have difficulty urinating due to pain and increased frequency.
You may have a fever with chills.

diseases.name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse- Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Pelvic organ prolapse, also known as POP, is a medical condition that occurs when the tissues and muscles supporting the pelvic organs become weak, and as a result, leads to a prolapse of the pelvic organs from their usual position. Examples of pelvic organs include bladder, uterus , vagina, cervix, urethra and rectum .
symptoms: The common symptom that women with pelvic organ prolapse experience are discomfort during physical activity or sexual intercourse.
The other usual symptoms are:
Bulging structure seen or felt in the vagina
Ache or discomfort in the pelvis
Problems with bowel movement or urine leakage
Unusual discomfort during periods (while inserting tampons or placing napkins)
Pain or pressure in the pelvis during coughing, walking, standing, or sitting.
The basic treatment for pelvic organ prolapse is to strengthen the pelvic floor muscles in order for it to support and keep the pelvic organs firm and intact.
Below are some of the measures that can be followed to help with the symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse.

Prevent constipation – constipation is one of the causes of pelvic organ prolapse. While straining, there are high chances of having a prolapse. Hence, it is good to avoid constipation . Fiber-rich foods help with relieving the condition. Some of the practices that may help with clearing constipation are: Drinking plenty of fluids Consuming lots of fruits and vegetables Eating high fiber foods like whole grains, beans, carrots, etc., Avoid oily and junk foods that can contribute to constipation Do not strain much while passing stools .
Drinking plenty of fluids
Consuming lots of fruits and vegetables
Eating high fiber foods like whole grains, beans, carrots, etc.,
Avoid oily and junk foods that can contribute to constipation
Do not strain much while passing stools .

Following exercises – doing exercises that focus on the pelvic floor muscles, helps to improve and strengthen the muscles and ligaments that hold the pelvic organs in place. Doctors advise women follow Kegel exercises. It is found to give good results when followed consistently. As a beginner you can try holding back and tightening the muscles for 5 seconds and releasing for 5 seconds, and repeating the process 5 times helps. Gradually the duration can be increased to 10 seconds and repeated 10 times at a stretch after getting used to this motion.

Avoid putting pressure in the pelvic area . This can be done by avoiding lifting heavy weights, straining, walking or standing for a long period of time, sitting by crossing the legs tightly together, etc.,

Quit smoking – smoking causes innumerous damages to the health. The habit may weaken the tissues around the pelvic region making the symptoms worse. Smoking will also lead to chronic coughing and ultimately puts pressure on the pelvic muscles. Hence, it is normally advised to quit smoking when a woman has this ailment.

Losing excess weight – being obese may again put pressure on the lower part of the body, which in turn affects the pelvic floor muscles, leading to prolapse. Hence, maintaining weight is essential to prevent the occurrence of pelvic organ prolapse.

diseases.name: Pemphigus Foliaceus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pemphigus Foliaceus is a rare autoimmune skin disorder characterized by the formation of blisters and sores on the skin. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on the quality of life of those affected but also due to its potential complications if left untreated. Understanding Pemphigus Foliaceus is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can lead to better outcomes for patients.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pemphigus Foliaceus can vary from person to person but typically include:
Blisters: The most characteristic symptom, blisters usually appear on the scalp, face, chest, and back. They may be painful and can rupture easily, leading to open sores.
Erosions: When blisters break, they can leave behind painful erosions that may become infected.
Crusting: The affected areas may develop crusts as they heal.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many patients report itching or a burning sensation in the affected areas.

diseases.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pemphigus Vulgaris (PV) is a rare but serious autoimmune disorder characterized by the formation of painful blisters on the skin and mucous membranes. This condition is significant not only due to its physical manifestations but also because of its potential complications if left untreated. Understanding PV is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pemphigus Vulgaris can vary in severity and may include:
Blisters: Painful, fluid-filled blisters that can develop on the skin and mucous membranes, including the mouth, throat, and genitals.
Erosions: When blisters rupture, they leave behind painful erosions that can be slow to heal.
Itching and Burning: Affected areas may be itchy or burn, contributing to discomfort.
Difficulty Swallowing: If blisters form in the throat, they can make swallowing painful and difficult.

diseases.name: Pendred Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pendred Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects hearing and thyroid function. It is significant not only because of its impact on individuals and families but also due to its implications for genetic counseling and management. Understanding Pendred Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Hearing Loss: The most prominent symptom, which can be bilateral (affecting both ears) or unilateral (affecting one ear). The severity can vary widely.
Goiter: An enlargement of the thyroid gland, which may be visible or palpable in the neck.
Balance Issues: Some individuals may experience difficulties with balance due to inner ear dysfunction.
Thyroid Dysfunction: Symptoms related to hypothyroidism may occur, including fatigue, weight gain, and sensitivity to cold.

diseases.name: Penicillin Allergy - Causes, symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: penicillin allergy : Penicillin was discovered in 1928 as an antibiotic produced by blue molds, P. chrysogenum and P. rubens . Today, penicillin is produced synthetically as a broad-spectrum antibiotic against infections caused that are caused by gram-positive bacteria like streptococci and staphylococcus. It is used as Penicillin G for intravenous use and Penicillin V for oral consumption.
symptoms: Some of the common symptoms are:
Allergic reactions such as rashes, redness, itching and hives
Coughing, wheezing and difficulty breathing
Fever
Watery eyes , runny nose
Swelling on the face/neck
Anaphylaxis is a rare, life-threatening allergic reaction which can cause widespread dysfunction of the body systems. The signs and symptoms of anaphylaxis include:
Diarrhea or vomiting
Abdominal cramps and nausea
Tightening of airways and throat, causing troubled breathing
Seizures
Weak, rapid pulse
Dizziness or lightheadedness
Loss of consciousness
Drop in blood pressure
Less-common penicillin allergy reactions happen days or weeks after the exposure to this drug and may persist for some time after stopping it. Such conditions include:
Serum sickness: that may cause swelling, rash, nausea, joint pain and fever
Drug-induced anemia
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS): This may cause rash, general swelling, high white blood cell counts, recurrence of dormant hepatitis infection and swollen lymph nodes
Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis that involves severe blistering as well as peeling of the skin
Inflammation in the kidneys (nephritis) that may result in general swelling, fever, blood in the urine, confusion, including other signs and symptoms
If you experience any of these symptoms, emergency care immediately.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: Penile Cancer: Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Men, pay attention to genital hygiene!
symptoms: Penile cancer begins from the tip of the penis (glans penis) and spreads to the other parts of penis. You should consult a doctor, if following symptoms are present: · Skin discoloration and skin thickening · Wart like genital lesions on the penis · Reddish rash on the penis · Persistent foul discharge under the foreskin · Pain and bleeding from the penis (in advanced cases) · A sore penis

diseases.name: Penile Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Penile fracture is a rare but serious medical condition that occurs when there is a rupture of the tunica albuginea, the fibrous sheath surrounding the erectile tissue of the penis. This injury typically results from trauma during sexual intercourse or vigorous physical activity. Understanding penile fracture is crucial not only for those who may be at risk but also for healthcare providers who need to recognize and treat this condition promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of penile fracture, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of a penile fracture can vary in severity but typically include:
Sudden Pain: A sharp, intense pain in the penis immediately following the injury.
Swelling and Bruising: Rapid swelling and discoloration of the penis, often extending to the surrounding areas.
Deformity: A noticeable bend or curvature in the penis, which may indicate a significant injury.
Difficulty Urinating: In some cases, men may experience difficulty urinating due to swelling or injury to the urethra.

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
diseases.description: Peptic ulcers are sores on the lining of the stomach or duodenum, commonly caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use.
symptoms: Burning stomach pain
Bloating
Nausea or vomiting
Feeling full quickly

diseases.name: Peptic Ulcers, and What Action Can Be Taken To Prevent Them from Worsening
diseases.description: A peptic ulcer (commonly known as a stomach ulcer) is an open sore that develops on the stomach’s inner lining and the upper portion of the small intestine. The ulcers damaging the small intestines are known as duodenal ulcers.
symptoms: You will feel discomfort or a burning sensation in your stomach during the night or in between meals. The pain may reduce when you eat food or take an antacid, but will return.
Other symptoms include:
● Lack of appetite
● Weight loss.
● Vomiting blood
● Black or bloody stool
● Bloating.
● Heartburn .
● Trouble breathing.
● Nausea .
A mild ulcer may not cause any symptoms. But, if the symptoms start getting worse, it is best to consult a doctor.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: Periapical Abscess - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A periapical abscess is a localized collection of pus that forms at the apex (tip) of a tooth's root due to infection. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe pain, swelling, and even systemic complications if left untreated. Understanding periapical abscesses is crucial for maintaining oral health and preventing more serious dental issues. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of periapical abscesses.
symptoms: The symptoms of a periapical abscess can vary in severity but often include:
Severe toothache: This is usually the first symptom and can be persistent or throbbing.
Swelling: There may be swelling in the gums, face, or jaw.
Sensitivity: The affected tooth may be sensitive to hot or cold temperatures.
Foul taste: A bad taste in the mouth may occur due to pus drainage.
Fever: In some cases, a low-grade fever may accompany the infection.

diseases.name: Pericardial Effusion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pericardial effusion is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of excess fluid in the pericardial cavity, the space surrounding the heart. This condition can have significant implications for heart function and overall health. Understanding pericardial effusion is crucial, as it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding pericardial effusion.
symptoms: The symptoms of pericardial effusion can vary depending on the amount of fluid present and the rate of accumulation. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: This may be sharp or dull and can worsen with deep breathing or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially when lying down, is a common symptom.
Cough: A persistent cough may occur due to pressure on the lungs.
Palpitations: Patients may feel an irregular heartbeat or a sensation of the heart racing.
Fatigue: General tiredness and weakness can result from the heart's reduced ability to pump blood effectively.

diseases.name: Pericarditis – Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Pericarditis is an inflammation of pericardium. This is a disease that can develop suddenly and can last for several months. The pericardium is a thin and two-layered sac filled with fluid, covering the outer area of your heart. This provides lubrication—acting as a shield for the heart to protect it.
symptoms: Chronic chest pain : It is one of the common symptoms of acute pericarditis where the person might suffer severe, stabbing, sharp, and sudden chest pain . Often this pain is observed at the left side or middle side of the chest.
Severe pain behind the breastbone : It comes as a quick pain at the left side of your chest, making you feel extremely uncomfortable. The pain gets worse while coughing or lying down.

Pain in the left shoulder and neck : The same kind of pain occurs during heart attacks, so most of the time, it can be confusing. But the difference is that in pericarditis, the pain is sudden and sharp, which goes through your left shoulder to neck and then reaches the back.
Excessive pain while coughing or sleeping : The chest pain gets worse and sharp, which can create problems of excessive pain to an individual while coughing or lying down.
Swelling in the abdomen or legs : People suffering from chronic pericarditis can have swelling in the abdomen & legs
Cough or shortness of breath : Person might feel shortness of breath.
Fatigue or weakness : Chronic pericarditis can cause scarring of the pericardium, which makes it difficult for the heart to perform its main function, making the person extremely tired and weak.
Low-grade fever
Heart palpitations (increase in a heartbeat)
Pericardial effusion : It is the symptom when the fluid builds-up in the pericardium, making it difficult for your heart to function

diseases.name: Perichondritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Perichondritis is a medical condition that affects the cartilage, primarily in the ear, but can also occur in other areas of the body. This inflammation can lead to significant discomfort and, if left untreated, may result in serious complications. Understanding perichondritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their quality of life. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of perichondritis, providing a thorough overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of perichondritis can vary depending on the severity of the inflammation and the area affected. Common symptoms include:
Pain and Tenderness: The affected area, especially the ear, may be painful to touch.
Swelling: Inflammation can lead to noticeable swelling around the cartilage.
Redness: The skin over the affected area may appear red and inflamed.
Warmth: The area may feel warm to the touch due to increased blood flow.
Discharge: In cases of infection, there may be pus or other discharge from the affected area.

diseases.name: Pericoronitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pericoronitis is a dental condition that affects the soft tissues surrounding a partially erupted tooth, most commonly the wisdom teeth. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding pericoronitis is crucial for maintaining oral health, especially for young adults and those with emerging wisdom teeth. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more related to pericoronitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of pericoronitis can vary in severity but often include:
Pain: Localized pain around the affected tooth, which may radiate to the jaw, ear, or throat.
Swelling: Inflammation of the gum tissue surrounding the tooth.
Difficulty Opening the Mouth: Limited jaw movement due to pain and swelling.
Bad Breath: Foul odor from the mouth due to infection.
Fever: In some cases, a mild fever may accompany the infection.

diseases.name: Perilymphatic Fistula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Perilymphatic fistula (PLF) is a medical condition that involves an abnormal connection between the inner ear and the surrounding structures, particularly the perilymphatic space. This condition can lead to significant auditory and vestibular symptoms, impacting a person's quality of life. Understanding PLF is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as untreated cases can lead to complications such as hearing loss and balance disorders. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of perilymphatic fistula, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of PLF can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Hearing Loss: Sudden or progressive hearing loss in one ear is a common symptom.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ear may accompany hearing loss.
Vertigo: A sensation of spinning or dizziness can occur, often triggered by changes in head position.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance or coordination may be experienced.
Ear Fullness: A feeling of pressure or fullness in the affected ear.

diseases.name: Perimenopause - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Perimenopause is a significant phase in a woman’s life that marks the transition to menopause, the time when menstrual periods cease permanently. This period can last for several years and brings various physical and emotional changes. Understanding perimenopause and its implications is crucial, as it prepares women for the upcoming changes in their bodies and helps them manage the symptoms that often accompany it. Early education about perimenopause can help women navigate this transition more smoothly, improving their overall health and quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of perimenopause can vary widely from woman to woman and may fluctuate in severity over time. While some women may experience only mild changes, others may encounter more disruptive symptoms that require medical intervention.

Irregular Periods: One of the first signs of perimenopause is changes in menstrual cycles. Periods may become shorter, longer, lighter, or heavier. Some women may experience skipped periods, while others may have more frequent cycles.

One of the first signs of perimenopause is changes in menstrual cycles. Periods may become shorter, longer, lighter, or heavier. Some women may experience skipped periods, while others may have more frequent cycles.

Hot Flashes: Hot flashes are sudden feelings of heat that spread over the body, often accompanied by sweating and redness. They can last for a few seconds to several minutes and typically occur during the day or night (night sweats).

Hot flashes are sudden feelings of heat that spread over the body, often accompanied by sweating and redness. They can last for a few seconds to several minutes and typically occur during the day or night (night sweats).

Mood Swings: Hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause can lead to mood swings, irritability, anxiety, and even depression. Women may experience heightened emotional sensitivity or feel overwhelmed by day-to-day stressors.

Hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause can lead to mood swings, irritability, anxiety, and even depression. Women may experience heightened emotional sensitivity or feel overwhelmed by day-to-day stressors.

Sleep Disturbances: Perimenopausal women often report difficulty falling or staying asleep. Night sweats, hot flashes, and increased anxiety can disrupt sleep patterns, leading to fatigue and decreased overall well-being.

Perimenopausal women often report difficulty falling or staying asleep. Night sweats, hot flashes, and increased anxiety can disrupt sleep patterns, leading to fatigue and decreased overall well-being.

Vaginal Dryness and Discomfort: Reduced estrogen levels can cause vaginal dryness, leading to discomfort during sex or while performing everyday activities. This can affect sexual health and confidence.
Reduced estrogen levels can cause vaginal dryness, leading to discomfort during sex or while performing everyday activities. This can affect sexual health and confidence.
Weight Gain: Many women experience changes in their body composition during perimenopause, particularly around the abdomen. Decreased metabolism and hormonal shifts may contribute to weight gain.
Many women experience changes in their body composition during perimenopause, particularly around the abdomen. Decreased metabolism and hormonal shifts may contribute to weight gain.

Decreased Libido: A reduction in sexual desire can occur as a result of hormonal changes, vaginal dryness, and fatigue. Emotional changes, such as mood swings or anxiety, can also contribute to decreased libido.
A reduction in sexual desire can occur as a result of hormonal changes, vaginal dryness, and fatigue. Emotional changes, such as mood swings or anxiety, can also contribute to decreased libido.

Memory and Concentration Issues: Perimenopausal women may notice difficulties with memory, concentration, and "brain fog." Hormonal changes can affect cognitive function, although these symptoms are usually temporary.
Perimenopausal women may notice difficulties with memory, concentration, and "brain fog." Hormonal changes can affect cognitive function, although these symptoms are usually temporary.
