diseases.name: Perineal Hernia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Perineal hernia is a medical condition that occurs when tissue protrudes through a weak spot in the perineum, the area between the anus and the genitals. This condition can lead to discomfort and various complications if left untreated. Understanding perineal hernia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of perineal hernia.
symptoms: Bulge in the Perineal Area: A noticeable lump or bulge may be felt or seen in the perineal region.
Pain or Discomfort: Patients may experience pain, especially when sitting, standing, or during physical activity.
Difficulty with Bowel Movements: Some individuals may have trouble passing stool or experience constipation.
Urinary Issues: There may be difficulty urinating or a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying.

diseases.name: Perineal Tear (Vaginal Tear): Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: A vaginal tear or a perineal tear is an injury to the tissue around the vagina and rectum that can occur during childbirth. A woman may experience any of the four grades of tear. During delivery, an episiotomy is a procedure that may be used to widen the vaginal opening in a controlled way.

diseases.name: Periodic Fever Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Periodic Fever Syndrome (PFS) is a group of rare, inherited disorders characterized by recurrent episodes of fever and inflammation. These episodes can vary in duration and intensity, often accompanied by other symptoms such as joint pain, abdominal pain, and skin rashes. Understanding PFS is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, as misdiagnosis can lead to unnecessary treatments and complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Periodic Fever Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Periodic Fever Syndrome can vary widely depending on the specific type of syndrome. However, common symptoms include:
Recurrent Fever: Episodes can last from a few hours to several days, often recurring every few weeks or months.
Joint Pain: Many individuals experience arthritis-like symptoms during fever episodes.
Abdominal Pain: Severe abdominal pain can occur, often mimicking appendicitis.
Skin Rashes: Some syndromes are associated with specific skin manifestations, such as erysipelas-like erythema.
Fatigue: Persistent fatigue is common, especially after fever episodes.

diseases.name: Periodontal Abscess - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Periodontal abscess is a localized infection that occurs in the tissues surrounding the teeth, specifically within the periodontal pockets. This condition is significant not only because it can cause severe pain and discomfort but also due to its potential to lead to more serious dental and systemic health issues if left untreated. Understanding periodontal abscesses is crucial for maintaining oral health and preventing complications that can arise from untreated infections.
symptoms: Common symptoms of a periodontal abscess include:
Pain: A sharp, throbbing pain in the affected area, which may radiate to other parts of the mouth or face.
Swelling: Noticeable swelling of the gums or face, often accompanied by redness.
Pus: The presence of pus that may ooze from the gum line, indicating an active infection.
Bad Breath: Persistent foul odor from the mouth due to the infection.
Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to hot or cold temperatures, especially when chewing.
Tooth Mobility: In advanced cases, the affected tooth may become loose.

diseases.name: Periodontitis - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Periodontitis means inflammation surrounding the gum area. This is a common yet serious gum disease that progressively deteriorates the soft tissues around the teeth; this loosens the tooth structure and ultimately results in tooth loss.
symptoms: Healthy teeth have firm, pale pink gums. Early stages of periodontitis have no or minuscule symptoms, but as the disease progresses, the following symptoms occur :
Recurring swelling of gums
Gingivitis
Bleeding after brushing teeth
Permanent bad breath, a condition called halitosis
Reddish and bleeding gums
Pus accumulation in between teeth and gums
Pain while chewing
Loosened teeth
Receding gums giving the tooth an abnormally longer look
Spaces in between teeth
Tooth x-ray showing pocket development in between teeth and gums
Gingivitis is mostly painless; hence, patients tend to ignore these painless bleeding symptoms; on the contrary, these are the primary symptoms of growing periodontitis.

diseases.name: Perioral Dermatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Perioral dermatitis is a common skin condition that primarily affects the area around the mouth, but it can also extend to the nose and eyes. This condition is characterized by a rash that can be both uncomfortable and unsightly, leading to significant distress for those affected. Understanding perioral dermatitis is crucial not only for effective management but also for preventing its recurrence. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of perioral dermatitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of perioral dermatitis can vary from person to person but typically include:
Red, inflamed bumps around the mouth
Pustules or papules that may resemble acne
Itching or burning sensations
Dry, flaky skin in the affected area
A rash that may spread to the nose or eyes

diseases.name: Periorbital Cellulitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Periorbital cellulitis is a serious condition that affects the tissues surrounding the eyes. It is characterized by inflammation and infection, which can lead to significant complications if not treated promptly. Understanding periorbital cellulitis is crucial for early detection and effective management, especially since it can mimic other conditions and may escalate quickly. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of periorbital cellulitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of periorbital cellulitis can vary in severity but typically include:
Redness and Swelling: The area around the eye may appear red and swollen.
Pain and Tenderness: Patients often experience discomfort or pain in the affected area.
Warmth: The skin around the eye may feel warm to the touch.
Fever: Many individuals will develop a fever as the body fights the infection.
Vision Changes: In some cases, there may be blurred vision or difficulty moving the eye.

diseases.name: Peripheral Artery Disease
diseases.description: Peripheral artery disease which is also called as a peripheral arterial disease is a common circulatory problem where the blood flow to the limbs is reduced due to narrowed arteries. When one develops peripheral artery disease (PAD) the lower extremities of the body such as legs don’t receive enough blood flow. This leads to leg pain while walking. It also could be a sign of widespread accumulation of fatty deposits in the arteries. In this condition, even the blood flow to the heart and brain is reduced. However, peripheral artery disease can be successfully treated if one quits tobacco, regularly exercises, and also maintains a healthy diet. Peripheral artery disease or PAD is a variant of peripheral vascular disease (PVD) which is generally known to occur only in the arteries. Building up of fatty material which is a gradual process inside the vessels where the arteries harden is what causes the condition. And over a long time period, the arteries gets blocked, narrowed and also weakened. It usually occurs in people who are above the age of 60 and affects around 12% to 20% of people in this age group. It is also found to be common among people who suffer from diabetes and it is the men who are more affected than women. The condition is also found in people who are heavy smokers. PVD is also found to be the leading cause of disability among people who are above the age of 60 and also those who have diabetes. Around 50% of the people with the peripheral vascular disease don’t experience any symptoms. However, those who have symptoms end up ignoring their condition and do not consult a doctor, assuming it to be normal and a part of the aging process. One should be aware that surgery is one of the most effective treatments available for the peripheral vascular disease, and treating PVD medically and also with few lifestyle modifications can prevent it from getting worse and further protect the person affected by it against complications.
symptoms: Most of the individuals, about 60% of them who suffer from peripheral artery disease have shown some symptoms of it. The most common of all is the symptom caused by the leg muscles which do not get enough blood. If one has PAD, the most common symptom is the pain in the leg that comes and goes and is especially found in both calves and hips. The pain is severe while walking or climbing stairs, but this usually stops when at rest. A dull and cramping pain is often the complaint but it can at times feel like tightness, heaviness or fatigue in the legs. Other symptoms include:
Weakness or Numbness in the Legs
Atrial septal defect
Coldness in the lower leg or foot
Sores on feet, toes or legs that take a long time to heal or won’t heal
Change in the color of legs
Loss of hair or slower hair growth on legs and feet
Pain the buttocks
Aching or burning pain in the feet or toes while taking rest

diseases.name: Peritonitis - Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Peritonitis is a condition that leads to the inflammation of the peritoneum, the inner lining of the abdominal wall. This inner lining of the abdominal wall is known to cover the organs of the abdomen. Peritonitis is caused either due to fungal or bacterial infection. Peritonitis requires immediate medical attention. If left untreated, it can give rise to acute infection that spreads throughout the body. Apart from bacterial or fungal infection leading to peritonitis, it can also be caused by peritoneal dialysis therapy.
symptoms: The common symptoms of peritonitis include:
Pain in the abdomen
A feeling of fullness or bloating
Appetite loss
Fatigue along with confusion
Diarrhea and low output of urine
Difficulty in the passage of stool
In the case of patients receiving peritoneal dialysis therapy, the symptoms also include:
Dialysis fluid is of an unusual color with white flecks
Dialysis fluid contains clumps of fibrin
Dialysis fluid has an unusual odor

diseases.name: Pernicious Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pernicious anemia is a serious condition that affects the body’s ability to produce healthy red blood cells due to a deficiency of vitamin B12. This deficiency is often caused by an autoimmune response that impairs the absorption of this essential nutrient. Understanding pernicious anemia is crucial, as it can lead to severe health complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of pernicious anemia, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Pernicious anemia can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may develop gradually. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness and weakness.
Pale or Jaundiced Skin: A yellowish tint to the skin and eyes due to the breakdown of red blood cells.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Especially when standing up quickly.
Numbness or Tingling: Often in the hands and feet, indicating potential nerve damage.
Cognitive Changes: Memory loss, confusion, or difficulty concentrating.
Glossitis: Inflammation of the tongue, which may appear swollen and smooth.

diseases.name: Peroneal Nerve Injury - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Peroneal nerve injury is a condition that affects the peroneal nerve, a crucial nerve in the lower leg responsible for controlling movement and sensation in the foot and toes. This injury can lead to significant mobility issues and discomfort, impacting daily activities and quality of life. Understanding peroneal nerve injury is essential for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can help prevent long-term complications.
symptoms: Foot Drop: Difficulty lifting the front part of the foot, leading to dragging while walking.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations of numbness or tingling in the top of the foot or the outer part of the lower leg.
Weakness: Weakness in the muscles that control foot movement, making it hard to walk or stand.
Pain: Sharp or aching pain in the knee or lower leg, which may worsen with activity.

diseases.name: Peroneal Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Peroneal tendonitis is a condition that affects the peroneal tendons, which are located on the outside of the ankle and foot. These tendons play a crucial role in stabilizing the ankle and facilitating movement. Understanding peroneal tendonitis is significant not only for athletes and active individuals but also for anyone who engages in regular physical activity. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding peroneal tendonitis.
symptoms: Pain: The most common symptom is pain along the outside of the ankle, which may worsen with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation can lead to noticeable swelling around the ankle.
Stiffness: Individuals may experience stiffness in the ankle, particularly in the morning or after prolonged periods of inactivity.
Tenderness: The area around the peroneal tendons may be tender to the touch.
Weakness: There may be a feeling of weakness in the ankle, making it difficult to perform certain movements.

diseases.name: Persistent Depressive Disorder Dysthymia - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Persistent depressive disorder dysthymia, previously known as dysthymia, is chronic depression that can vary from mild to severe. People with this disorder are known to have a gloomy personality, affecting work, relationships, and other activities. The symptoms can last from months to years, and the most common way of treating them is through talk therapy or psychotherapy .
symptoms: The symptoms of persistent depressive disorder dysthymia are not constantly present. They are known to come and go over a period, and their intensity is also variable. Another phenomenon known as double depression may also occur during or before persistent disorder dysthymia, which leads to major depressive episodes. A few common symptoms of persistent depressive disorder dysthymia are:
Loss of interest in pleasurable and daily activities
Decrease in productivity
Feelings of guilt, sadness, and helplessness
Loss of hope
Difficulty sleeping
Prolonged lack of energy
Difficulty concentrating
Irritability, along with social withdrawal

diseases.name: Persistent Post-concussive Symptoms (Post-concussion Syndrome)
diseases.description: Many injuries cause permanent damage to the body. Out of the serious injuries to the human body, concussion is one such brain injury that affects the brain function severely. It may be caused by a sudden jolt on the head.
symptoms: Concussion is a slight traumatic brain injury that generally occurs after a blow to your head. It can also happen with violent shaking and movement of the body or head. Risk of developing persistent post-concussive symptoms does not appear to be linked with the severity of the initial injury.

Persistent post-concussive symptoms, also termed post-concussion syndrome, occur in 15-20% of the persons who suffer from a concussion. This is a medical condition in which the concussion symptoms last beyond the expected recovery time after the concussion injury. The symptoms like dizziness, memory issues, headaches issues, etc., can last from more than a few weeks to a couple of months. Thus, it needs immediate medical intervention to treat post-concussion syndrome to improve the person’s quality of life.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

It is recommended to see a qualified medical professional in case you are suffering from post-concussion syndrome. The condition often worsens without medical help and hence to prevent further damage due to concussion, you should immediately seek medical consultation. Your doctor can help you improve the symptoms and your lifestyle after a concussion.
Call 1860-500-1066 t o book an appointment
You can prevent post-concussion syndrome by protecting your head. The simple steps to ensure the protection of your head from injuries and hence post-concussion syndrome include:

Use of helmets : You should never miss on wearing a helmet while driving two-wheelers. Also, while playing sports like roller-skating, ice-skating, snowboarding, bicycling, skiing, in-line skating, etc., you must ask your kids and friends to wear helmets.
Preventing falls : You must take steps at your place to prevent falls, such as removing rugs, ensuring proper lighting, including rails at stairs, etc.

Wearing seat belts : While traveling in the car and other means of transport, it is highly advised to wear seat belts and encourage your kids to do the same. Seat belts are significantly helpful in preventing head injuries.
Staying away from the conditions that promote post-concussion symptoms like headaches, dizziness, anxiety, etc.
Avoiding stressful activities and take enough rest
Avoiding driving while you are treating post-concussion syndrome conditions
Staying in a dark and quiet room while facing a headache
You can place a cold and moist cloth or cold pack to relieve headaches
Post-concussion syndrome can be treated in accordance with the severity of the symptoms. Some of the treatments for post-concussion syndrome include the following:

Cognitive issues related to memory and thinking do not have any direct treatment. Certain forms of cognitive therapy may be helpful, including focused rehabilitation that provides training in the specific areas that you need to strengthen. Some people may need occupational or speech therapy or stress management strategies .

Educating the patients help them handle things better. Many times, patients are treated using medication like antidepressants or anti-anxiety drugs. Sometimes doctors may recommend psychotherapy that involves an experienced psychiatrist or psychologist ns.
Antidepressants, anti-epileptic agents, antihypertensive agents, etc., are used to treat concussion headaches.

diseases.name: Persistent Pupillary Membrane - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Persistent Pupillary Membrane (PPM) is a condition that affects the eye, specifically the iris, and is often overlooked in discussions about ocular health. While it is generally benign and may not cause significant issues for many individuals, understanding PPM is crucial for early detection and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Persistent Pupillary Membrane, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Many individuals with PPM may not experience noticeable symptoms, especially if the membrane is thin and does not obstruct vision. However, some common symptoms may include:
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or difficulty focusing, particularly if the membrane is substantial.
Light Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to bright lights or glare.
Abnormal Eye Movements: In some cases, individuals may experience strabismus (crossed eyes) due to visual disturbances.

diseases.name: Perthes disease: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Perthes disease is a hip disorder that commonly affects children, and this condition develops when the blood flow to the ball part of the femoral head of the hip joint is disrupted or blocked.
symptoms: A limp or a change in the way your child walks or runs is frequently the first sign of Perthes disease. This initial symptom may go unnoticed by your child, and it’s usually visible or noticeable when observing them play.
Other signs and symptoms include:
Recurring pain in the hip, groin, thigh, and knees
Inflammation and irritation in the hip area, which can lead to muscle spasms
Pain while exercising
Hip joint stiffness or reduced mobility
The presence of pain even if there is no visible injury
Some children who suffer from this condition may not display any signs of being in pain. Perthes disease may be undetected until an X-ray is taken as a result of a fall or other incident.

diseases.name: Pertussis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pertussis, commonly known as whooping cough, is a highly contagious respiratory disease caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis . It is characterized by severe coughing fits that can lead to difficulty breathing, vomiting, and exhaustion. Pertussis is significant not only due to its potential severity, especially in infants and young children, but also because it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. Understanding pertussis is crucial for prevention and effective management, particularly in vulnerable populations.
symptoms: Common symptoms of pertussis include:
Severe coughing fits that may end in a "whoop" sound
Vomiting after coughing
Exhaustion after coughing fits
Runny nose
Mild fever

diseases.name: Pervasive Developmental Disorders - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pervasive Developmental Disorders (PDD) represent a group of conditions characterized by delays in the development of socialization and communication skills. These disorders can significantly impact an individual's ability to function in everyday life, making early diagnosis and intervention crucial. Understanding PDD is essential not only for affected individuals and their families but also for educators, healthcare providers, and society as a whole. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Pervasive Developmental Disorders, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pervasive Developmental Disorders can vary widely among individuals but generally include:
Social Challenges: Difficulty in understanding social cues, forming relationships, and engaging in reciprocal conversations.
Communication Difficulties: Delayed speech development, challenges in using language effectively, or atypical speech patterns.
Repetitive Behaviors: Engaging in repetitive movements or routines, such as hand-flapping, rocking, or insistence on sameness.
Sensory Sensitivities: Over- or under-reacting to sensory stimuli, such as sounds, lights, textures, or tastes.
Impaired Imagination: Difficulty in engaging in pretend play or understanding abstract concepts.

diseases.name: Petit Mal Seizure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Petit Mal Seizures, also known as absence seizures, are a type of seizure that primarily affects children and can sometimes continue into adulthood. These seizures are characterized by brief lapses in consciousness, often mistaken for daydreaming. Understanding Petit Mal Seizures is crucial, as they can significantly impact a person's daily life, academic performance, and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Petit Mal Seizures, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The hallmark of a Petit Mal Seizure is a brief lapse in consciousness. Other common symptoms include:
Staring: The individual may appear to be staring blankly.
Unresponsiveness: They may not respond to questions or stimuli during the episode.
Subtle Movements: Some may exhibit minor movements, such as eye blinking or lip smacking.
Postictal Confusion: After the seizure, the individual may be unaware that a seizure occurred and may not remember the event.

diseases.name: Pfeiffer Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pfeiffer Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that falls under the category of craniosynostosis syndromes. It is characterized by the premature fusion of certain skull bones, leading to a distinctive head shape and facial features. This condition not only affects physical appearance but can also have significant implications for neurological development and overall health. Understanding Pfeiffer Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can greatly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Pfeiffer Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Craniosynostosis: Premature fusion of skull bones leading to an abnormal head shape.
Facial Features: Wide-set eyes (hypertelorism), a beaked nose, and a prominent forehead.
Skeletal Abnormalities: Short fingers and toes, broad thumbs, and fusion of certain bones in the hands and feet.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals may experience hearing difficulties due to structural changes in the ear.
Developmental Delays: There may be delays in speech and motor skills, although many children develop normally with appropriate interventions.

diseases.name: Phace Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Phace Syndrome is a rare and complex disorder that primarily affects the vascular system and can lead to a variety of developmental issues. It is characterized by a specific set of physical anomalies, particularly those involving the face and neck, and can have significant implications for affected individuals. Understanding Phace Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can greatly improve the quality of life for those impacted.
symptoms: Phace Syndrome presents a range of symptoms that can vary significantly among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Hemangiomas: These are often the most visible signs, appearing as red or purple marks on the skin, typically on the face or neck.
Neurological Issues: Posterior fossa malformations can lead to developmental delays, seizures, or other neurological symptoms.
Cardiac Defects: Some individuals may have congenital heart defects that require monitoring and management.
Eye Abnormalities: These can include strabismus (crossed eyes), cataracts, or other vision problems.

diseases.name: Pharyngeal Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Pharyngeal cancer is a group of head and neck cancers that start in the throat (pharynx), the muscular tube that carries air to the larynx and food to the esophagus. While it is not as common as many other cancers, pharyngeal cancer can affect speaking, swallowing, and breathing—key functions for daily life. The reassuring news: when it’s detected early and treated by a coordinated, experienced team, many people do well and maintain a strong quality of life. This comprehensive article explains symptoms, causes, risk factors, diagnosis, staging, treatment options, and prognosis at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms vary by location and stage. Early signs can be subtle; any symptom lasting longer than 2–3 weeks deserves an ENT (ear, nose, and throat) evaluation.
Common symptoms by region:

Nasopharynx Nasal blockage or stuffiness, frequent nosebleeds Ringing in the ear or hearing loss (often one-sided), a feeling of fullness in the ear Headaches, facial pain or numbness A neck lump (enlarged lymph node)
Nasal blockage or stuffiness, frequent nosebleeds
Ringing in the ear or hearing loss (often one-sided), a feeling of fullness in the ear
Headaches, facial pain or numbness
A neck lump (enlarged lymph node)

Oropharynx Persistent sore throat or one-sided throat pain Difficulty or pain with swallowing; the feeling that food sticks A neck lump that doesn’t go away Changes in voice or muffled voice; ear pain on one side
Persistent sore throat or one-sided throat pain
Difficulty or pain with swallowing; the feeling that food sticks
A neck lump that doesn’t go away
Changes in voice or muffled voice; ear pain on one side

Hypopharynx Progressive swallowing difficulty; choking or coughing during meals Voice changes, persistent sore throat, or referred pain to the ear Unintentional weight loss and fatigue A painless neck lump
Progressive swallowing difficulty; choking or coughing during meals
Voice changes, persistent sore throat, or referred pain to the ear
Unintentional weight loss and fatigue
A painless neck lump
Other possible symptoms:
Bad breath, blood-streaked saliva, or persistent cough
Noisy breathing or shortness of breath in advanced cases
Prompt evaluation improves treatment choices and preserves function.

diseases.name: Phenylketonuria (PKU) - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Phenylketonuria, also known as PKU, refers to a rare inherited disorder that results in the build-up of amino acid, known as phenylalanine, in the body. A defect in the gene that helps produce the enzyme required to break down phenylalanine causes this disorder. Many countries screen for Phenylketonuria (PKU) soon after a child is born, as early diagnosis helps prevent major health problems.
symptoms: Initially, newborn babies with Phenylketonuria (PKU) do not have any symptoms. However, if this condition remains untreated, they can develop signs within a few months. They include:
A musty odor in the skin, urine, or breath
Eczema (skin rashes)
An abnormally small head
Intellectual disability
Neurological problems , such as seizures
Hyperactivity
Delayed development
Psychiatric disorders
Behavioral, emotional, and social problems
Also Read About: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder

diseases.name: Philophobia (Fear of Falling in Love): Causes & Treatment
diseases.description: Falling in love or the ability to maintain a relationship comes naturally to most individuals. However, there are a few people or instances that make a person experience a fear of falling in love. This in turn, adversely affects the ability to maintain relationships. There can be various reasons why Philophobia develops. The reasons for this phobia could be many, such as a divorce, abandonment or rejection during childhood, a traumatic breakup, the experience of cheating in relationships, and others.
symptoms: People with philophobia show various physical and emotional symptoms like:
Inability to initiate and maintain intimate relationships
A constant fear of losing the current partner or ending relationships abruptly
Never-ending feelings of insecurity and inferiority in a relationship
Shortness of breath
Nausea and vomiting
Diarrhea
Dry mouth
Excessive sweating
Some practices can help manage the symptoms and effects of philophobia.
One can evaluate their past relationships and try to identify if any particular incident is causing fear of repeating the experience in a new relationship.
A person should train their thoughts towards positivity which enables a person to experience love and happiness.
They can evaluate and question their expectations and preconceived notions about relationships to help in maintaining a healthy relationship.

A person should face their emotions instead of running away from them or finding a refuge in drugs and alcohol. Repeatedly releasing negative emotional feelings allows a person to understand that this too shall pass.

diseases.name: Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens (PCD) is a rare but serious condition characterized by severe venous thrombosis, leading to significant swelling and discoloration of the affected limb. This condition is not only a medical emergency but also a critical indicator of underlying health issues, often requiring immediate intervention. Understanding PCD is essential for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens can be severe and may include:
Swelling: Marked swelling of the affected limb, often more pronounced than in typical DVT.
Discoloration: A bluish or purplish hue to the skin, indicating compromised blood flow.
Pain: Severe pain in the affected limb, which may be out of proportion to the physical findings.
Warmth: The affected area may feel warm to the touch due to inflammation.
Tissue Necrosis: In advanced cases, there may be signs of tissue death due to lack of blood supply.

diseases.name: Photokeratitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Photokeratitis, often referred to as "sunburn of the eye," is a painful condition that affects the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. This condition is significant not only because of the discomfort it causes but also due to its potential to lead to more serious eye problems if left untreated. Understanding photokeratitis is crucial for anyone who spends time outdoors, especially in sunny or reflective environments. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of photokeratitis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of photokeratitis can appear within hours of UV exposure and may include:
Redness: The eyes may appear bloodshot due to inflammation.
Pain: A burning or gritty sensation in the eyes is common.
Sensitivity to Light: Bright lights may cause discomfort or pain.
Tearing: Increased tear production can occur as the eyes attempt to flush out irritants.
Blurred Vision: Vision may become temporarily impaired due to corneal swelling.

diseases.name: Phthisis Bulbi - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Phthisis bulbi is a term that may not be familiar to many, yet it represents a significant condition affecting the eye. This term refers to a pathological state of the eye characterized by shrinkage and atrophy, often resulting from severe ocular disease or trauma. Understanding phthisis bulbi is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can lead to significant visual impairment and impact quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of phthisis bulbi, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of phthisis bulbi can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Vision Loss: A significant reduction in visual acuity or complete blindness in the affected eye.
Eye Discomfort: Patients may experience pain, discomfort, or a sensation of pressure in the eye.
Changes in Eye Appearance: The affected eye may appear smaller, with a sunken appearance and changes in the surrounding tissues.
Redness and Inflammation: There may be visible signs of inflammation or redness in the eye.

diseases.name: Phyllodes Tumor (Breast): Symptoms, Causes, Treatments and Diagnosis
diseases.description: Numerous newspapers, magazines, and online articles greatly emphasize breast care and self-diagnosis for breast cancer. But these articles do not shed light on lesser-known breast conditions. One of them is a phyllodes tumor.
symptoms: Like most breast tumors, you can also feel the phyllodes tumor, or your doctor may notice the lump during a regular check-up. The tumor is not painful. The lumps are hard, smooth, and well-defined, typically growing 3 centimeters or more in width in a few weeks or months. In some cases, it can stretch your skin, causing ulcers in the breast. It is also seen that the tumor generally appears more in the left breast than in the right.
If you have cancerous tumors, the symptoms appear as follows:
Extreme fatigue
Issues breathing
Pain in the bone – indicating that cancer has metastasized to the bone and lungs.

diseases.name: Pica - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pica is a complex eating disorder characterized by the persistent consumption of non-nutritive, non-food substances. This condition can have significant health implications, affecting individuals across various age groups and backgrounds. Understanding pica is crucial not only for those who may be affected but also for caregivers, healthcare providers, and educators. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pica, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The primary symptom of pica is the persistent consumption of non-food items. Commonly ingested substances include:
Dirt or clay (geophagia)
Chalk
Paper
Hair (trichophagia)
Paint chips
Metal objects
Soap

diseases.name: Pilocytic Astrocytoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pilocytic astrocytoma (PA) is a type of brain tumor that primarily affects children and young adults. It is classified as a low-grade glioma, which means it tends to grow slowly and is generally less aggressive than other types of brain tumors. Understanding pilocytic astrocytoma is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pilocytic astrocytoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of pilocytic astrocytoma can vary depending on the tumor's location and size. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Persistent or worsening headaches, especially in the morning or after waking up.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to increased intracranial pressure.
Balance and Coordination Issues: Difficulty walking or maintaining balance, particularly if the tumor is located in the cerebellum.
Vision Problems: Blurred or double vision, especially if the tumor affects the optic nerve.
Seizures: New-onset seizures can occur, particularly in older children and adults.
Cognitive Changes: Memory problems, difficulty concentrating, or changes in behavior.

diseases.name: Pilon Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pilon fractures are complex injuries that occur at the distal end of the tibia, where the bone meets the ankle joint. These fractures are significant not only because of their impact on mobility but also due to their potential complications and the challenges they present in treatment. Understanding pilon fractures is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely and appropriate management can significantly affect recovery outcomes.
symptoms: Severe Pain: Intense pain at the site of the fracture, often worsening with movement.
Swelling and Bruising: Significant swelling and bruising around the ankle and foot.
Deformity: Visible deformity or misalignment of the ankle joint.
Inability to Bear Weight: Difficulty or inability to put weight on the affected leg.

diseases.name: Pilonidal Cysts - Symptoms, Diagnosis, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: pilonidal cysts is a fluid-filled sac of tissue located at the base of the spine, near the crease of your buttocks. It presents as a small pit or dimple in the skin area overlying the tailbone or the coccyx. Pilonidal cyst can be very painful, especially while sitting.
symptoms: Some symptoms of pilonidal cysts are:
The presence of pain in the area above the tailbone, which aggravates further while sitting
The presence of small dimples or large swelling in the area between your buttocks indicates pilonidal cysts. The affected area is usually red and tender to the touch.
A foul-smelling odour or pus draining from the affected area might be observed.
Developing a fever is possible.

diseases.name: Pineoblastoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pineoblastoma is a rare and aggressive type of brain tumor that primarily affects the pineal gland, a small organ located deep within the brain. This tumor is classified as a primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) and is most commonly found in children and young adults. Understanding pineoblastoma is crucial not only for those directly affected but also for healthcare providers and families, as early detection and treatment can significantly impact outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pineoblastoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Pineoblastoma can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary depending on the tumor's size and location. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Persistent or worsening headaches, often due to increased intracranial pressure.
Vision Problems: Blurred vision, double vision, or difficulty focusing, which may occur if the tumor affects the optic pathways.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can result from increased pressure in the brain.
Balance and Coordination Issues: Difficulty walking or maintaining balance may occur if the tumor affects areas of the brain responsible for motor control.
Changes in Behavior or Personality: Cognitive changes, irritability, or mood swings may be observed, particularly in children.

diseases.name: Pinguecula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pinguecula is a common eye condition that affects many individuals, particularly those who are frequently exposed to sunlight, wind, and dust. While it is generally benign and does not usually lead to serious complications, understanding its significance is crucial for maintaining eye health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pinguecula, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Pinguecula may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when they do occur, they can include:
Yellowish Growth: A small, raised, yellowish bump on the conjunctiva.
Irritation: Mild irritation or discomfort in the eye, especially in windy or dry conditions.
Redness: The eye may appear slightly red or inflamed.
Tearing: Increased tear production may occur as a response to irritation.

diseases.name: Pinworm Infection - Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: A pinworm infection is an infection of the large intestine caused by a small white parasite. The medical term for the parasite is Enterobius vermicularis , but it is commonly referred to as pinworm. These pinworms are tiny, narrow worms white in color and less than half an inch in length. Pinworms, like other parasitic infections, survive by feeding off the host. Hence, they depend on their host for nutrition.
symptoms: The symptoms of pinworm infection include:
The strong urge to frequently itch the anal area at night.
Restlessness and lack of sleep due to constant itching and discomfort.
Presence of pain, rashes, or other skin irritations around the anal area.
Presence of pinworms around the anal region.
Presence of pinworms in stool samples.
Vaginal itching and discharge may also be seen if the pinworm has reached these areas.
Nausea, vomiting , and stomach pain may also be seen, but these are very rare.

diseases.name: Piriformis Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Piriformis Syndrome is a condition that affects the piriformis muscle, a small muscle located deep in the buttock, near the top of the hip joint. This muscle plays a crucial role in the movement of the hip and the stabilization of the pelvis. When the piriformis muscle becomes tight or spasms, it can compress the nearby sciatic nerve, leading to pain, discomfort, and a range of other symptoms. Understanding Piriformis Syndrome is significant not only for those who experience its symptoms but also for healthcare providers who aim to offer effective treatment options. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Piriformis Syndrome.
symptoms: The symptoms of Piriformis Syndrome can vary in intensity and may include:
Buttock Pain: A deep, aching pain in the buttock that may worsen with prolonged sitting or standing.
Sciatica: Pain that radiates down the back of the leg, often described as a sharp or burning sensation.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations in the buttock or down the leg, particularly in the back of the thigh and calf.
Difficulty Sitting: Discomfort when sitting for extended periods, often requiring frequent position changes.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the hip or leg, particularly when trying to cross the legs or rotate the hip.

diseases.name: Pitted Keratolysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pitted keratolysis is a skin condition that primarily affects the feet, characterized by the presence of small, crater-like depressions on the skin's surface. While it may not be as widely recognized as other dermatological conditions, understanding pitted keratolysis is essential for effective management and prevention. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of pitted keratolysis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of pitted keratolysis can vary in severity but typically include:
Pitted Lesions: Small, round depressions on the skin, often surrounded by a reddish or inflamed area.
Odor: A foul smell may emanate from the affected area due to bacterial activity.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Some individuals may experience discomfort or irritation in the affected areas.
Peeling Skin: The skin may appear flaky or scaly around the pits.

diseases.name: Pituitary Apoplexy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare but serious medical condition that occurs when there is sudden bleeding or impaired blood supply to the pituitary gland, a small but crucial gland located at the base of the brain. This condition can lead to a range of symptoms, some of which may be life-threatening if not addressed promptly. Understanding pituitary apoplexy is essential for recognizing its signs, seeking timely medical intervention, and managing potential complications effectively.
symptoms: The symptoms of pituitary apoplexy can vary widely but often include:
Severe Headache: Often described as a sudden, intense headache, sometimes referred to as a "thunderclap headache."
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision, double vision, or loss of peripheral vision due to pressure on the optic nerves.
Nausea and Vomiting: Resulting from increased intracranial pressure.
Altered Mental Status: Confusion, lethargy, or loss of consciousness in severe cases.
Hormonal Imbalances: Symptoms related to hormonal deficiencies, such as fatigue, weight changes, or changes in libido.

diseases.name: Pituitary Tumor - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: A pituitary tumor is an abnormal growth in the pituitary gland, a small pea-sized organ located at the base of the brain. Despite its size, the pituitary gland is often called the “master gland” because it regulates hormones that control growth, metabolism, reproduction, and many other vital functions.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on whether the tumor is hormone-producing (functioning) or not, and how large it is.
Common Early Symptoms
Persistent headaches
Vision changes, especially loss of peripheral vision
Unexplained fatigue
Hormonal imbalance symptoms (irregular periods, low libido, weight changes)
Advanced Symptoms
Nausea and vomiting
Severe vision loss or double vision
Symptoms of hormone excess:
Cushing’s disease (round face, weight gain, purple stretch marks)
Acromegaly (enlarged hands, feet, facial features)
Symptoms of hormone deficiency:
Fatigue, low blood pressure, infertility
Because these symptoms overlap with many other conditions, pituitary tumors are often diagnosed only after careful evaluation.

diseases.name: Pityriasis Rosea: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Most of us have gone through one or more episodes of rashes or allergies. The spectrum of skin allergies or skin diseases is huge some of which are severe in nature while some are comparatively mild. One such skin condition is Pityriasis Rosea which is a relatively mild skin disease and is not directly contagious in nature. It can affect people belonging to any age group and is equally widespread in men and women. Mostly, its victims are kids, teens, and people belonging to an age group of 10-35 years including expectant mothers.
symptoms: Systemic symptoms: Most of the people having pityriasis rosea display no other symptoms, but the rash sometimes follows a few days after an upper respiratory viral infection like cold , cough, sore throat or similar infection.

The herald patch: Herald patch is a single plaque (oval pink or red plaque about 2 to 5 cm in diameter), which appears about 1 to 20 days before a general rash of pityriasis rosea. The herald patch has a scale trailing, like a collaret, just inside the edge of the lesion.

Secondary rash: After the appearance of the herald patch, a few days later, more plaques (thickened lesions) or scaly patches (flat lesions) appear on the back and chest. Some plaques may also appear on the neck, upper arms and thighs, but are not common on the scalp or face. compared to the herald patch, these secondary lesions of the pityriasis rosea tend to be smaller. They are also oval in shape with a dry surface. Like the herald patch, they may have an inner collaret of scaling. Some plaques may be annular (ring-shaped).

Pityriasis rosea plaques usually follow the relaxed skin tension lines/cleavage lines (langer lines) on both sides of your upper trunk. The rash looks like a fir tree and does not involve the scalp, face, soles or palms. While pityriasis rosea may be very itchy, in most cases, it does not itch at all.

Atypical pityriasis rosea: Pityriasis rosea is atypical when diagnosis becomes difficult. Atypical pityriasis rosea is diagnosed when the rash has features like multiple herald patches, absence of herald patch, atypical morphology, severe itch, etc

diseases.name: Pityrosporum Folliculitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pityrosporum Folliculitis, also known as Malassezia Folliculitis, is a skin condition that affects hair follicles, leading to inflammation and discomfort. This condition is significant not only because of its physical manifestations but also due to its potential to cause psychological distress and impact the quality of life. Understanding Pityrosporum Folliculitis is essential for effective management and treatment, allowing individuals to seek appropriate care and improve their skin health.
symptoms: Pityrosporum Folliculitis presents with several characteristic symptoms, including:
Itchy Red Bumps: Small, itchy, red bumps that resemble acne.
Pustules: Some lesions may develop pus, resembling pustular acne.
Inflammation: The affected areas may appear swollen and inflamed.
Distribution: Commonly occurs on the chest, back, shoulders, and face.

diseases.name: Placenta Accreta - Symptoms, Causes, Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Placenta accreta is a severe condition in pregnancy. It occurs when the placenta starts growing too deeply into the wall of the uterus. What usually happens is that the placenta detaches from the uterine wall after the baby’s delivery. However, a part or all of the placenta stays attached to the wall in placenta accrete. It can result in severe blood loss after delivery. Placenta accreta is a high-risk pregnancy complication .
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of placenta accreta are usually not noticeable during pregnancy . Most often, doctors detect it when they perform a routine ultrasound . However, in some cases, it causes vaginal bleeding when a woman is in her third trimester, i.e., weeks 27 to 40.

Thus, it is essential to see a doctor if a pregnant woman experiences vaginal bleeding during her third trimester. Apart from that, if a pregnant woman experiences heavy or severe bleeding accompanied by abdominal pain, she must seek emergency care.

diseases.name: Placenta Praevia
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The major symptom is bright red vaginal bleeding which ranges from light to heavy with or without contractions in the second half of pregnancy. Bleeding stops on its own without treatment and sometimes, comes back after days or weeks.

diseases.name: Placental Abruption - Causes, Risk Factors, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The placenta is an organ developed during pregnancy that contains vital nutrients for the fetus and is attached to the uterine lining. The condition where the placenta separates from the uterus lining is known as placental abruption. It is a life-threatening condition to both mother and baby if left untreated. Hence, a proper diagnosis, treatment, and management plan are required to avoid any medical complications during pregnancy.
symptoms: This class of placental abruption has no harmful effect on the baby or mother. Also, there is no sign of pain or vaginal bleeding and can be detected on placental examination after the delivery.
There is a sudden onset of symptoms seen in placental abruption. Some of the symptoms are mentioned below.
Vaginal bleeding though in certain cases it may not be evident
Intense abdominal and back pain
Uterus tenderness
Uterine contractions, coming often one right after another

diseases.name: Placental Insufficiency : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The placenta is an organ that develops in the womb when women are pregnant. Sometimes, it does not grow as it must or can get injured. The result can be a health condition known as placental insufficiency. The condition is also commonly known as placental dysfunction or uteroplacental vascular insufficiency. It is a severe complication of pregnancy that is uncommon.
symptoms: Placental insufficiency is challenging to identify, particularly in first-time pregnancies . There are generally few or no symptoms that are related to placental insufficiency. However, some clues can result in the early diagnosis of this condition. Women can observe the size of their uterus to be smaller than in previous pregnancies, and the fetus can also be less active than anticipated. Vaginal bleeding or preterm labour contractions can also occur with placental insufficiency.

diseases.name: Plague: Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Plague, a severe bacterial infection that spreads via fleas, has caused many deaths in the past. It was first reported in medieval times and caused millions of deaths across the globe. Now ,less than 5000 worldwide cases are found every year in the rural parts of Africa, Asia, and the United States. If left untreated, plague leads to serious health complications and even death.

diseases.name: Plantar Fasciitis
diseases.description: Plantar fasciitis is one of the most common causes of heel pain. It involves inflammation of a thick band of tissue that runs across the bottom of each foot and connects the heel bone to the toes (plantar fascia). It commonly causes stabbing pain that usually occurs with the first steps in the morning.
symptoms: Stabbing pain near the heel
Pain that is usually worse in the morning
Pain after prolonged standing or when getting up from sitting
Pain after — but not during — exercise

diseases.name: Plantar Fibroma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Plantar fibroma is a benign growth that occurs in the plantar fascia, the thick band of tissue that runs along the bottom of the foot. While these fibromas are non-cancerous, they can lead to discomfort and pain, affecting mobility and quality of life. Understanding plantar fibroma is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain an active lifestyle without the burden of foot pain.
symptoms: Pain: The most common symptom is localized pain in the arch of the foot, which may worsen with activity.
Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling may be present in the arch area.
Tenderness: The fibroma may be tender to the touch, especially when pressure is applied.
Stiffness: Some individuals may experience stiffness in the foot, particularly after periods of rest.

diseases.name: Plantar Warts Symptoms, Prevent And Treatment
diseases.description: Plantar warts are common among men and women. The majority of plantar warts are not a serious health concern and usually disappear on their own without needing treatment. These warts are usually found at the bottom of your feet. A plantar wart is the symptom of an infection with the human papillomavirus ( HPV ), specifically types 1, 2, 4, 60, and 63. The human papillomavirus enters your body via cracks in your skin.
symptoms: Here are some of the most common signs of plantar warts:
Round fleshy, hard bump with depression in the center present at the bottom of your feetusually at the toe bases or heels
Formation of callus (thickened rough skin) over a spot where the wart may have grown inward
Black dots of pinpoint size called wart seeds that are small clotted blood vessels
Pain or tenderness in feet while walking or standing

diseases.name: Plaque Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Plaque psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that primarily affects the skin, leading to the formation of raised, red patches covered with silvery-white scales. This condition is not just a cosmetic issue; it can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to physical discomfort and emotional distress. Understanding plaque psoriasis is crucial for effective management and treatment, as well as for reducing stigma associated with this common skin disorder.
symptoms: The symptoms of plaque psoriasis can vary in severity and may include:
Red Patches: Raised, inflamed areas of skin that may be itchy or painful.
Silvery Scales: Thick, silvery-white scales that cover the red patches.
Dry Skin: Skin that may crack and bleed.
Itching or Burning: Discomfort that can range from mild to severe.
Nail Changes: Pitting, discoloration, or separation of the nail from the nail bed.

diseases.name: Plasmacytoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Plasmacytoma is a type of tumor that arises from plasma cells, which are a kind of white blood cell responsible for producing antibodies. While it is often associated with multiple myeloma, a more widespread form of blood cancer, plasmacytoma can occur independently. Understanding plasmacytoma is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of plasmacytoma, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of plasmacytoma can vary depending on the location of the tumor. Common symptoms include:
Bone Pain: This is often the most prominent symptom, especially in solitary bone plasmacytoma. The pain may be localized to the area of the tumor.
Swelling: In cases of extramedullary plasmacytoma, swelling may occur in the affected soft tissue.
Fatigue: General fatigue and weakness can occur due to the body’s response to the tumor.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss may be a sign of an underlying malignancy.
Nerve Symptoms: If the tumor compresses nearby nerves, symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness may occur.

diseases.name: Pleomorphic Adenoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pleomorphic adenoma, often referred to as a "benign tumor," is the most common type of salivary gland tumor, primarily affecting the parotid gland. This tumor is significant not only because of its prevalence but also due to its potential for complications if left untreated. Understanding pleomorphic adenoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can lead to better health outcomes.
symptoms: Pleomorphic adenomas often present as painless, slow-growing masses in the salivary glands. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling in the jaw or neck area.
Discomfort: Mild discomfort or pressure in the affected area.
Changes in Saliva Production: Altered saliva flow or dry mouth.

diseases.name: Pleural Effusion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pleural effusion is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of excess fluid in the pleural space, the thin cavity between the layers of tissue that line the lungs and the chest wall. This condition can significantly impact respiratory function and overall health, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options. Recognizing pleural effusion early can lead to better management and improved outcomes for affected individuals.
symptoms: Common symptoms of pleural effusion include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially when lying down.
Chest Pain: Sharp or stabbing pain that may worsen with deep breaths or coughing.
Cough: A persistent cough that may be dry or produce sputum.
Fever: In cases of infection, fever may accompany other symptoms.

diseases.name: Pleurisy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pleurisy , also known as pleuritis, is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the pleura, the double-layered membrane surrounding the lungs. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and can be indicative of underlying health issues. Understanding pleurisy is crucial not only for those experiencing symptoms but also for anyone interested in maintaining lung health. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of pleurisy, providing a thorough overview for readers.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of pleurisy is sharp, stabbing chest pain that worsens with deep breaths, coughing, or sneezing. Other symptoms may include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may occur, especially if fluid accumulates in the pleural space.
Cough: A dry cough may accompany pleurisy.
Fever: If an infection is present, fever may be a symptom.
Chills: Accompanying fever, chills may also occur.

diseases.name: Pleurodynia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pleurodynia, often referred to as "devil's grip," is a medical condition characterized by sudden, severe chest pain that can mimic the symptoms of a heart attack. This condition is significant not only because of the discomfort it causes but also due to its potential to lead to misdiagnosis and unnecessary anxiety among patients. Understanding pleurodynia is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals can return to their daily lives with minimal disruption.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of pleurodynia is sharp, localized chest pain that can vary in intensity. Other common symptoms include:
Pain on Deep Breathing: The pain often worsens with deep breaths, coughing, or sneezing.
Muscle Spasms: Some individuals may experience muscle spasms in the chest wall.
Shortness of Breath: Due to pain, individuals may avoid deep breathing, leading to a feeling of breathlessness.
Fever and Malaise: If caused by a viral infection, symptoms may include fever, fatigue, and general malaise.

diseases.name: Plica Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Plica Syndrome is a condition that affects the knee joint, often leading to pain and discomfort. It is significant because it can mimic other knee disorders, making accurate diagnosis and treatment essential for effective management. Understanding Plica Syndrome is crucial for individuals experiencing knee pain, as it can impact mobility and quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Plica Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Plica Syndrome can vary but often include:
Knee Pain: Typically located on the inner side of the knee, pain may worsen with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation around the knee joint can lead to noticeable swelling.
Clicking or Popping Sensation: Patients may experience a sensation of catching or popping when moving the knee.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness, especially after prolonged periods of inactivity.

diseases.name: Pneumococcal Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pneumococcal disease is a significant public health concern that affects millions of people worldwide. It is caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae , which can lead to various serious infections, including pneumonia, meningitis, and bloodstream infections. Understanding pneumococcal disease is crucial for prevention and effective management, especially for vulnerable populations such as young children, the elderly, and individuals with certain underlying health conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pneumococcal disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of pneumococcal disease can vary depending on the type of infection. Common symptoms include:
Pneumonia: Cough, fever, chills, shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue.
Meningitis: Severe headache, fever, neck stiffness, sensitivity to light, and confusion.
Bacteremia: Fever, chills, rapid heartbeat, and low blood pressure.

diseases.name: Pneumomediastinum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pneumomediastinum is a medical condition characterized by the presence of air in the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavity that houses vital structures such as the heart, trachea, esophagus, and major blood vessels. While it may sound alarming, pneumomediastinum can occur in various contexts, ranging from benign to life-threatening situations. Understanding this condition is crucial for timely diagnosis and management, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated.
symptoms: The symptoms of pneumomediastinum can vary depending on the underlying cause and the amount of air present in the mediastinum. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: Often sharp or stabbing, this pain may worsen with deep breathing or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing can occur due to pressure on the lungs.
Coughing: A persistent cough may develop, sometimes accompanied by a feeling of tightness in the chest.
Neck Pain: Pain or discomfort in the neck may arise due to the proximity of the mediastinum to the cervical structures.
Voice Changes: Hoarseness or changes in voice may occur if the air compresses the laryngeal structures.

diseases.name: Pneumonia
diseases.description: Pneumonia is an infection of one or both lungs that can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.
symptoms: Fever and chills
Cough with phlegm
Shortness of breath
Chest pain when breathing or coughing

diseases.name: Pneumonitis - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Pneumonitis is a common health condition that causes inflammation of the lungs. Unlike pneumonia, it is a non-infectious condition. Pneumonia too is a type of pneumonitis because the infection causes inflammation. However, the term Pneumonitis, usually refers to non-infectious causes of lung inflammation.
symptoms: Here are some of the common signs that you may have pneumonitis:
Breathing problems
Shortness of breath
Persistent cough
Constant fatigue
Loss of appetite
Unexpected weight loss
Fever
Dry cough
Chills
Headaches
Clubbing of fingers

diseases.name: Pneumothorax - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pneumothorax is a medical condition that occurs when air enters the pleural space, the area between the lungs and the chest wall. This can lead to a partial or complete collapse of the lung, which can be life-threatening if not treated promptly. Understanding pneumothorax is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, as well as for knowing when to seek medical attention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pneumothorax, making it accessible to a general audience while ensuring medical accuracy.
symptoms: The symptoms of pneumothorax can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Chest Pain: Often sharp and localized, this pain may worsen with deep breaths or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing can occur, especially if the lung is significantly collapsed.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate may be observed as the body attempts to compensate for reduced lung capacity.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, particularly around the lips and fingertips, may indicate a lack of oxygen.

diseases.name: Poikiloderma Of Civatte - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Poikiloderma of Civatte is a skin condition that manifests as a combination of pigmentation changes, atrophy, and telangiectasia, primarily affecting sun-exposed areas of the skin, particularly the neck and face. This condition is significant not only for its aesthetic implications but also as a marker of sun damage and potential skin health issues. Understanding Poikiloderma of Civatte is essential for early recognition, effective management, and prevention of further skin complications.
symptoms: Skin Discoloration: The most noticeable symptom is the mottled pigmentation, which can appear as brownish or reddish patches on the skin.
Atrophy: The skin may become thinner and more fragile, leading to increased susceptibility to injury.
Telangiectasia: Small, visible blood vessels may appear on the affected areas, contributing to the overall appearance of the skin.

diseases.name: Polio (Poliomyelitis)
diseases.description: Polio is a viral disease that mainly affects children and can cause paralysis. Most infections are asymptomatic.
symptoms: Fever and sore throat
Tiredness and headache
Nausea or stomach pain
Meningitis in some cases
Paralysis in severe cases

diseases.name: Polio - Symptoms, Causes, Vaccine and Treatment
diseases.description: Polio is a life-threatening disease that is a real menace to humanity. Also, this disease is highly contagious. Individuals most likely to contract this disease are children below the age of 5 years. Fortunately, the development of the polio vaccine has dealt a severe blow to this dangerous ailment.
symptoms: One can divide the symptoms of polio into two types: non-paralytic and paralytic polio and following paralytic polio, the post polio symptoms.

Some who get infected with the polio virus contract a type of polio that does not cause paralysis (abortive polio). Usually, this causes the same mild, flu-like signs and symptoms typical of other viral diseases.
Fatigue
Fever
Headache
Sore throat
Vomiting
Neck pain or stiffness
Back pain or stiffness
Muscle weakness or tenderness
Stiffness or pain in the arms or legs
Initial signs of paralytic polio like headache and fever , often mimic those of nonparalytic polio. However, within a week other signs and symptoms appear, including:
Loss of reflexes
Severe muscle aches or weakness
Loose and floppy limbs (flaccid paralysis)

diseases.name: Pollen Allergy : Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment & Prevention
diseases.description: Flowers, trees, grass, and weeds produce a fine powder called pollen. It is crucial for plant growth as it fertilizes other plants of the same species. However, pollens can cause unpleasant symptoms for people with pollen allergies.
symptoms: The most common symptom of pollen allergy are as follows:
Nasal congestion
Runny nose
Sinus pressure, which can cause facial pain
Sore throat
Cough
Itchy, watery eyes
Swollen, bluish skin beneath the eyes
Reduced sense of taste or smell
Increased asthmatic reactions
However, some symptoms are typical of specific pollen allergies.
1. Tree pollen allergy – The symptoms of tree pollen allergy include:
Runny nose and increased mucus production
Stuffy nose (nasal congestion)
Itchy nose, eyes, ears, and mouth
Swollen eyes
2. Grass pollen allergy – the most common symptoms of grass pollen allergy include:
Itchy eyes and throat
Blocked sinuses
Post-nasal drip
3. Weed pollen allergy – Weed pollen allergy causes symptoms including:
Eye and throat irritation

diseases.name: Polyarthritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Polyarthritis is a term that refers to inflammation in multiple joints, typically affecting five or more joints simultaneously. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility. Understanding polyarthritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can be a symptom of various underlying health issues, including autoimmune diseases and infections. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of polyarthritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of polyarthritis can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Joint Pain: Persistent pain in multiple joints is a hallmark symptom.
Swelling: Inflammation can lead to noticeable swelling around the affected joints.
Stiffness: Many individuals experience stiffness, particularly in the morning or after periods of inactivity.
Fatigue: Chronic inflammation can lead to feelings of fatigue and malaise.
Fever: In some cases, especially with infectious causes, a low-grade fever may accompany joint symptoms.

diseases.name: Polychromasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Polychromasia is a term that refers to the presence of red blood cells (RBCs) in the bloodstream that exhibit a variety of colors when stained and viewed under a microscope. This condition is significant because it can indicate underlying health issues, particularly those related to the production and maturation of red blood cells. Understanding polychromasia is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can serve as a marker for various hematological disorders and other systemic conditions.
symptoms: Polychromasia itself may not present specific symptoms, but it is often associated with underlying conditions that can cause various symptoms, including:
Fatigue: A common symptom of anemia, which may accompany polychromasia.
Paleness: A noticeable paleness of the skin and mucous membranes.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Often due to reduced oxygen delivery to tissues.
Rapid Heartbeat: The heart may work harder to compensate for low red blood cell counts.

diseases.name: Polycythemia Vera: Causes, Symptoms and Treatments
diseases.description: Polycythemia vera is a rare blood cancer which causes the bone marrow to produce too many red blood cells. The increase in red blood cells thickens the blood and slows down the blood flow, causing severe health issues, including blood clots .
symptoms: Some people do not experience any signs or symptoms. However, over time some may experience vague symptoms, such as:
Headaches
Dizziness
Fatigue
Ringing in the ears
Blurred or doubled vision
Increased blood pressure
However, as the disease progresses, the symptoms also become a little more severe, including:
Itchiness, particularly after a warm bath or shower
Numbness, tingling, burning, or weakness in the hands, feet, arms, or legs
A sense of fullness soon after eating a meal and bloating or pain in the left upper abdomen due to an enlarged spleen
Unusual and unexpected bleeding, including nosebleeds or bleeding gums
Painful swelling in one joint, mainly in the big toe
Breathing problems when lying down
Excessive sweating, particularly at night
Unexplained weight loss
Gout
Easy bruising
Concentration issues
Flushed face

diseases.name: Polyhydramnios - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Polyhydramnios is a medical condition characterized by an excessive accumulation of amniotic fluid in the amniotic sac surrounding a developing fetus. This condition can have significant implications for both the mother and the baby, affecting pregnancy outcomes and necessitating careful monitoring and management. Understanding polyhydramnios is crucial for expectant parents and healthcare providers alike, as it can influence prenatal care and delivery plans.
symptoms: Polyhydramnios may present with various symptoms, including:
Rapidly growing abdomen: An unusually large belly for the stage of pregnancy.
Shortness of breath: Increased pressure on the diaphragm can lead to difficulty breathing.
Swelling: Edema in the legs and feet may occur due to fluid retention.
Abdominal discomfort: This can include pain or cramping.

diseases.name: Polymorphous Light Eruption - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Polymorphous Light Eruption (PLE) is a skin condition that affects many individuals, particularly during the warmer months when sun exposure increases. It is characterized by an abnormal skin reaction to sunlight, leading to a variety of symptoms that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding PLE is crucial for those who experience it, as early recognition and management can help alleviate symptoms and prevent complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of PLE, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of PLE can vary widely among individuals but typically include:
Itchy or Burning Rash: The rash often appears within hours of sun exposure and can be intensely itchy or burning.
Red Bumps or Blisters: The rash may present as small red bumps, blisters, or patches on sun-exposed areas of the skin, such as the face, neck, and arms.
