Scaling or Crusting: In some cases, the rash may develop scaling or crusting as it heals.

diseases.name: Polymyalgia Rheumatica
diseases.description: Polymyalgia rheumatica is an inflammatory disorder that causes muscle pain and stiffness, especially in the shoulders, neck, upper arms, thighs, and hips. Signs and symptoms of polymyalgia rheumatica usually occur quickly — within two weeks. It primarily affects people older than 50.
symptoms: Aches or pain in the shoulders
Aches or pain in the neck, upper arms, buttocks, hips, or thighs
Stiffness in affected areas, particularly in the morning or after being inactive
Limited range of motion
Pain or stiffness in the wrists, elbows, or knees
Fatigue
Weight loss
Fever

diseases.name: Polymyositis
diseases.description: Polymyositis is a rare autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness and inflammation, primarily affecting the muscles closest to the trunk of the body. It can affect your ability to swallow and breathe, and can be associated with other autoimmune conditions. It occurs mostly in adults and is more common in women.
symptoms: Muscle weakness, especially in the hips, thighs, shoulders, upper arms, and neck
Difficulty swallowing
Difficulty breathing
Mild joint pain and swelling
Fatigue
Weight loss
Raynaud's phenomenon

diseases.name: Polymyositis and Dermatomyositis Overview
diseases.description: Polymyositis and dermatomyositis are two closely related inflammatory muscle diseases (myopathies) in which muscle fiber inflammation leads to progressive muscle weakness. While polymyositis lacks skin involvement, dermatomyositis is distinguished by its characteristic skin rash. Both are autoimmune conditions that can also affect the lungs, heart, and joints.
symptoms: Progressive proximal muscle weakness
Difficulty rising from a chair, climbing stairs, lifting arms overhead
Skin rash (in dermatomyositis)
Difficulty swallowing
Shortness of breath
Joint pain
Fatigue

diseases.name: Pompe Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pompe Disease, also known as Glycogen Storage Disease Type II, is a rare but significant genetic disorder that affects the body’s ability to break down glycogen, a form of stored sugar. This condition can lead to severe muscle weakness and respiratory issues, impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding Pompe Disease is crucial not only for patients and their families but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Pompe Disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Pompe Disease can vary widely depending on the age of onset and the severity of the enzyme deficiency. Common symptoms include:
Infantile-Onset Symptoms: Muscle weakness (hypotonia) Difficulty in feeding and swallowing Enlarged heart (cardiomyopathy) Respiratory distress Delayed motor skills
Muscle weakness (hypotonia)
Difficulty in feeding and swallowing
Enlarged heart (cardiomyopathy)
Respiratory distress
Delayed motor skills

Late-Onset Symptoms: Progressive muscle weakness, particularly in the proximal muscles (those closest to the center of the body) Respiratory issues, including sleep apnea Difficulty climbing stairs or lifting objects Frequent falls or trouble walking Fatigue
Progressive muscle weakness, particularly in the proximal muscles (those closest to the center of the body)
Respiratory issues, including sleep apnea
Difficulty climbing stairs or lifting objects
Frequent falls or trouble walking
Fatigue

diseases.name: Popliteal Artery Aneurysm - Treatment and Symptoms
diseases.description: The popliteal artery that supplies blood to the knee joint, thigh, and calf, may develop a popliteal artery aneurysm, which causes bulging and weakening in the vessel wall. When a popliteal aneurysm ruptures, it can result in life-threatening, uncontrollable bleeding. A blood clot caused by the aneurysm might necessitate the amputation of the limb.
symptoms: Many popliteal aneurysms go undetected. Symptoms that are common include,
Pain at the back of the knee
Lower leg edema (swelling due to fluid retention)
Injuries to the feet
Unhealed ulcers on the soles of the feet
Popliteal aneurysms are frequently bigger than 2.5cm, posing a significant risk of clotting and subsequent consequences. They should be evaluated for use as a preventative measure.
When a popliteal aneurysm causes a blood deficit in the leg, it presents an emergency. It should be treated as a high-risk wound regardless of its size to avoid amputation of the lower leg.

Popliteal artery aneurysms have traditionally been treated surgically using open bypass methods. However, endovascular methods/keyhole surgery can be utilized to stent-graft (fabric lined metal mesh) through the popliteal artery aneurysm. Your health, age, and the intricacy of the intervention required will all influence your treatment.

diseases.name: Porencephaly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Porencephaly is a rare neurological condition characterized by the presence of cysts or cavities within the brain's cerebral hemispheres. These cavities can disrupt normal brain function and development, leading to a range of neurological symptoms. Understanding porencephaly is crucial for early diagnosis and management, as it can significantly impact the quality of life for affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of porencephaly, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of porencephaly can vary widely depending on the size and location of the cysts. Common symptoms include:
Seizures: Many individuals with porencephaly experience seizures due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
Developmental Delays: Children may exhibit delays in reaching developmental milestones, such as walking or talking.
Motor Impairments: Weakness or paralysis on one side of the body (hemiparesis) is common, as the cysts can affect motor control areas of the brain.
Cognitive Impairments: Some individuals may experience difficulties with learning, memory, and problem-solving.
Behavioral Issues: Changes in behavior, including increased irritability or difficulty with social interactions, may occur.

diseases.name: Porphyria: Types, Symptoms, and Treatment
diseases.description: Porphyria refers to a rare group of genetic (inherited) ailments that occur due to porphyrin (natural chemicals) buildup in the body. Porphyrins play a crucial role in the functioning of hemoglobin in your body. Hemoglobin is a red blood cell protein that attaches iron, links to porphyrin, and supplies oxygen all over your body. When the level of porphyrins goes higher, it can lead to many problems, including porphyria.
symptoms: Few individuals might develop symptoms of both the types of porphyria.
Chest pain
Reddish-brown colored urine
Fast heartbeat that causes high blood pressure
Pain in the back and limb
Abdominal pain
Constipation and nausea
Urinary retention meaning the bladder does not clear out urine completely
Mental health instability
A perception of something seen, heard, touched, smelled, or tasted that did not happen in reality or hallucination
An uncontrolled disturbance which arises in the brain and results in involuntary movement of body parts
Extreme sensitivity to sunlight
Itching and swelling of the affected part
Formation of a blister on the skin when exposed to light
Skin darkening
The outer layer or epidermis of skin comes off, leaving a denuded surface

diseases.name: Portal Hypertension - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Portal hypertension is a serious medical condition that arises when there is increased blood pressure in the portal venous system, which is responsible for directing blood from the digestive organs to the liver. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe complications, including liver failure, variceal bleeding, and ascites, which can be life-threatening. Understanding portal hypertension is crucial for early detection, effective management, and improving patient outcomes.
symptoms: Portal hypertension may not present noticeable symptoms in its early stages. However, as the condition progresses, several symptoms may arise:
Ascites: Accumulation of fluid in the abdominal cavity, leading to swelling and discomfort.
Variceal Bleeding: Enlarged veins (varices) in the esophagus or stomach can rupture, causing severe bleeding.
Splenomegaly: Enlargement of the spleen, which can lead to a decrease in blood cell counts.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to liver dysfunction.
Fatigue: General tiredness and weakness.

diseases.name: Portal Vein Thrombosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Portal Vein Thrombosis (PVT) is a medical condition characterized by the formation of a blood clot in the portal vein, which is responsible for transporting blood from the digestive organs to the liver. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications, including liver dysfunction, portal hypertension, and even liver failure if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding PVT is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of PVT can vary widely, and some individuals may be asymptomatic. However, common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Often localized in the upper abdomen, this pain may be sharp or dull.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to increased pressure in the portal vein.
Swelling of the Abdomen: This can result from fluid accumulation (ascites) due to portal hypertension.
Changes in Bowel Habits: Diarrhea or constipation may occur.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes can indicate liver dysfunction.

diseases.name: Post Concussion Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Post Concussion Syndrome (PCS) is a complex disorder that can occur after a concussion, which is a type of traumatic brain injury (TBI). It is characterized by a range of physical, cognitive, and emotional symptoms that persist for weeks, months, or even longer after the initial injury. Understanding PCS is crucial, as it can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, daily functioning, and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Post Concussion Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Post Concussion Syndrome can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Headaches: Often described as tension-type or migraine-like headaches.
Cognitive Difficulties: Problems with memory, concentration, and attention.
Dizziness and Balance Issues: Feelings of lightheadedness or unsteadiness.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Sleep Disturbances: Insomnia or excessive sleepiness.
Emotional Changes: Increased irritability, anxiety, or depression.
Sensitivity to Light and Noise: Heightened sensitivity to environmental stimuli.

diseases.name: Post Thrombotic Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Post Thrombotic Syndrome (PTS) is a chronic condition that can develop after a deep vein thrombosis (DVT), which is a blood clot that forms in a deep vein, usually in the legs. PTS can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to pain, swelling, and other complications. Understanding PTS is crucial for those who have experienced DVT, as early recognition and management can help mitigate its effects. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of Post Thrombotic Syndrome.
symptoms: The symptoms of PTS can vary in severity and may include:
Swelling: Persistent swelling in the affected leg, often worsening throughout the day.
Pain: Aching or cramping pain in the leg, which may be aggravated by standing or walking.
Skin Changes: Changes in skin color, texture, or temperature, including discoloration or thickening of the skin.
Varicose Veins: The appearance of enlarged veins near the surface of the skin.
Ulcers: In severe cases, open sores or ulcers may develop on the skin.

diseases.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder or PTSD is a condition concerning one’s mental health that usually develops after a traumatic event leading to harmful and anxious feelings. Sometimes, people who have PTSD can relive the events repeatedly, while others stay away from any reminders of it. If the condition persists for months and years, it can obstruct life, work, and even relationships. However, medication and counselling can help improve the condition over time.
symptoms: People can experience PTSD within a month or, in certain cases, years after the traumatic event. Some common symptoms of PTSD are:
Undesirable or bitter memories of a trauma
Nightmares
Evocative memories or flashbacks that make people feel like they are reliving the event
A feeling of anxiety , fear, suspicion, or worry
Strong reactions when people are reminded of the trauma (or sometimes for no apparent reason at all)
Intrusive thoughts about war, death, or killing
A feeling of being emotionally disconnected or isolated
Losing interest in things once enjoyed
A feeling of being agitated, tensed, or easily startled
Eruption of anger or irritation
Difficulty in concentrating
Difficulty falling or staying asleep
The symptoms of PTSD are identical to those of other mental health conditions. Therefore, it is advised to get professional help from a therapist or doctor for diagnosis and PTSD treatments.

diseases.name: Posterior Capsular Opacification - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Posterior Capsular Opacification (PCO) is a common complication that can occur after cataract surgery, leading to vision impairment. It is often referred to as "secondary cataract" and can significantly affect the quality of life for those who experience it. Understanding PCO is crucial for patients who have undergone cataract surgery, as it can help them recognize symptoms early and seek appropriate treatment. This article will provide a comprehensive overview of PCO, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Blurred Vision: The most common symptom, often described as a "hazy" or "cloudy" vision.
Difficulty with Night Vision: Patients may find it challenging to see in low-light conditions.
Glare and Halos: Increased sensitivity to light and seeing halos around lights, especially at night.
Double Vision: Some individuals may experience double vision in one eye.

diseases.name: Posterior Cortical Atrophy - Symptoms, Causes And Risk Factors
diseases.description: Posterior cortical atrophy (PCA), also called Benson’s syndrome, is a degenerative brain and nervous system syndrome. If left untreated, PCA can affect your vision permanently. It can also cause your memory and thinking abilities (cognitive skills) to decline.
symptoms: The most common symptom of posterior cortical atrophy is vision problems. These visual problems may include,
Objects may appear to you in unusual colors or distorted shapes
You may experience trouble recognizing objects
The depth and surface of objects may look different to you; for instance, a tiny puddle of water may look like a large hole to you
You may experience trouble seeing more than one object at the same time
Other symptoms include
Difficulty reading books, for instance, missing out on lines, jumbling of letters, trouble reading certain fonts
Troubled sense of direction
Difficulty with bright lights or shiny surfaces

Some patients also experience hallucinations, while other symptoms may include difficulty in spelling or performing mathematical calculations. In addirion, many people with posterior cortical atrophy experience anxiety and memory can be affected in later stage
When to see a doctor?

If you start experiencing the aforementioned symptoms or any issues concerning your vision, you must consult with a specialist. An early diagnosis and proper treatment can relieve some of your symptoms.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

In the case of posterior cortical atrophy, it is not clear what affects the posterior part of the brain, However, doctors believe that people’s risk of developing posterior cortical atrophy is similar to other forms of dementia.
The common risk factors that can increase your chances of developing posterior cortical atrophy include the following:
Age
Lifestyle habits
Environmental factors
Family history of posterior cortical atrophy or other types of neurological disorders
Overall health
What are the treatment options for posterior cortical atrophy?
Depending on the cause and severity of posterior cortical atrophy, your doctor may recommend a treatment plan.

If Alzheimer’s disease is the cause of your posterior cortical atrophy, the doctor may recommend a medication known as cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications work by making your brain cells communicate with one another. Although the medication may improve your symptoms temporarily, it may not stop your posterior cortical atrophy from worsening.
Some people may notice a visible difference with these medications, while others may see no effects.

Suppose you have posterior cortical atrophy and dementia with Lewy bodies. In that case, you may benefit from treatment options that help with your movement problems. For this, the doctor may recommend a drug known as levodopa. It is used to treat Parkinson’s disease and in some cases dementia with Lewy bodies.

If your symptoms involve anxiety or depression , your doctor may recommend drug or non-drug treatments. Cognitive-behavioral therapy is one of the standard treatment options for depression and anxiety in posterior cortical atrophy. The therapy will allow you to talk about your worries and concerns with your therapist.
Furthermore, the doctor may even recommend antidepressant drugs, with or without cognitive behavioral therapy.
Conclusion

Posterior cortical atrophy is a rare neurological disorder. Since the symptoms of posterior cortical atrophy may look similar to other neurological diseases, it is critical to consult with a doctor for an accurate diagnosis.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
1. What is the life expectancy of someone suffering from posterior cortical atrophy?

Since posterior cortical atrophy is a progressive disorder, its prognosis is poor. Doctors believe the life expectancy of posterior cortical atrophy after the diagnosis is similar to that of Alzheimer’s disease, 8 to 12 years.
2. How does posterior cortical atrophy progress?
The symptoms of posterior cortical atrophy usually progress over a brief period. However, you may also experience a decline in your cognitive abilities, along with visual impairment.
3. Can posterior cortical atrophy be reversed?

There is no specific treatment for posterior cortical atrophy yet. However, your doctor may recommend medications that will help ease some of your symptoms but not reverse the effects of posterior cortical atrophy.
4. How common is posterior cortical atrophy?

Posterior cortical atrophy is a rare form of dementia. There are no exact numbers of how many people around the world have been affected by it. However, people who have Alzheimer’s disease may develop posterior cortical atrophy symptoms too.

diseases.name: Posterior Urethral Valves - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Posterior Urethral Valves (PUV) are a significant congenital condition affecting the urinary tract in males. This condition occurs when abnormal folds of tissue form in the urethra, leading to obstruction of urine flow. Understanding PUV is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Posterior Urethral Valves, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of PUV can vary depending on the severity of the obstruction. Common symptoms include:
Urinary Retention: Difficulty in urinating or a weak urine stream.
Frequent Urination: Increased frequency of urination, often with small amounts of urine.
Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Recurrent UTIs due to stagnant urine.
Abdominal Distension: Swelling of the abdomen due to bladder overdistension.
Poor Weight Gain: Infants may struggle to gain weight due to feeding difficulties.

diseases.name: Posterior Vaginal Prolapse (Rectocele) - Types, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Posterior Vaginal Prolapse (Rectocele) is a pelvic organ prolapse that occurs when the thin tissue wall separating your rectum from the vagina becomes weak.
symptoms: Signs and symptoms of posterior vaginal prolapse (rectocele) may vary from person to person. The common symptoms commonly include:
A slight bulge of tissue protruding through the vaginal opening
Feeling a sensation of fullness or rectal pressure
Difficulty during bowel movements
Feeling that your bowels have not been completely emptied
A sense of looseness in the vaginal tissues during sexual intercourse

diseases.name: Posterior Vitreous Detachment - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Posterior Vitreous Detachment (PVD) is a common eye condition that occurs when the vitreous gel, which fills the eye, separates from the retina at the back of the eye. While PVD is often a natural part of the aging process, it can lead to complications that may affect vision. Understanding PVD is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, potential complications, and the importance of timely medical intervention.
symptoms: Floaters: Small specks or cobweb-like shapes that drift across the field of vision.
Flashes of Light: Sudden bursts of light, often described as lightning streaks, can occur.
Blurred Vision: Some individuals may experience a decrease in visual clarity.
Shadow or Curtain Effect: A shadow or curtain may appear in the peripheral vision.

diseases.name: Postherpetic Neuralgia - Symptoms, Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Postherpetic neuralgia is a painful skin condition that develops as a complication of shingles . Typically, people aged above 60 are at an increased risk of developing postherpetic neuralgia. While there is no cure for the condition, treatment can help ease the symptoms.
symptoms: The symptoms are only limited to the area on your body where the shingles outbreak first occurred.
The common signs and symptoms of postherpetic neuralgia include:
A burning sensation to the skin, even with a light touch
Chronic pain that continues for one to two months even after the shingles rash goes away
Itching or numbness in the affected region

diseases.name: Posthitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Posthitis is a medical condition that affects the foreskin of the penis, leading to inflammation and discomfort. While it may not be a widely discussed topic, understanding posthitis is crucial for maintaining male genital health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of posthitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies. By shedding light on this condition, we hope to empower individuals with the knowledge they need to recognize and address posthitis effectively.
symptoms: The symptoms of posthitis can vary in severity but often include:
Redness and Swelling: The foreskin may appear inflamed and swollen.
Pain or Discomfort: Individuals may experience pain, especially during urination or sexual activity.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Irritation can lead to persistent itching or a burning feeling.
Discharge: There may be a discharge from the penis, which can be clear, cloudy, or purulent.
Foul Odor: Accumulation of smegma or infection can lead to an unpleasant smell.

diseases.name: Postictal State - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postictal state is a term that refers to the period following a seizure, during which an individual may experience a range of physical and cognitive symptoms. This state is significant because it can provide insights into the nature of the seizure and the overall health of the individual. Understanding postictal state is crucial for caregivers, medical professionals, and individuals with epilepsy or seizure disorders, as it can impact treatment decisions and quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms experienced during the postictal state can vary significantly but often include:
Confusion: Individuals may feel disoriented or have difficulty concentrating.
Fatigue: A sense of extreme tiredness is common, as the body recovers from the seizure.
Headache: Many people report headaches following a seizure.
Muscle Soreness: Muscle aches and stiffness can occur due to the physical exertion during the seizure.
Mood Changes: Some individuals may experience irritability, anxiety, or depression.

diseases.name: Postmenopause - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postmenopause is a significant phase in a woman's life that marks the end of her reproductive years. It occurs after menopause, which is defined as the cessation of menstrual periods for 12 consecutive months. This transition is not just a biological milestone; it carries profound implications for a woman's health, emotional well-being, and quality of life. Understanding postmenopause is crucial for women to navigate this stage effectively, manage symptoms, and maintain overall health.
symptoms: Postmenopause can bring about a range of symptoms, which may vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Hot Flashes: Sudden feelings of warmth, often accompanied by sweating and flushing.
Night Sweats: Hot flashes that occur during sleep, leading to disrupted rest.
Vaginal Dryness: Decreased estrogen levels can lead to thinning and drying of vaginal tissues, causing discomfort during intercourse.
Mood Changes: Many women experience mood swings, anxiety, or depression during this phase.
Sleep Disturbances: Insomnia or difficulty staying asleep can be common.
Weight Gain: Hormonal changes can lead to weight gain, particularly around the abdomen.
Memory Issues: Some women report difficulties with concentration and memory, often referred to as "brain fog."

diseases.name: Postpartum Depression - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postpartum Depression (PPD) is a significant mental health condition that affects many new mothers after childbirth. It is more than just the "baby blues," which many women experience in the days following delivery. PPD can have profound effects on a mother's emotional well-being, her ability to bond with her baby, and her overall quality of life. Understanding PPD is crucial for new mothers, their families, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and support.
symptoms: The symptoms of PPD can vary widely but often include:
Persistent sadness or low mood
Anxiety or excessive worry
Irritability or anger
Difficulty concentrating or making decisions
Changes in sleep patterns (insomnia or excessive sleeping)
Changes in appetite (overeating or loss of appetite)
Feelings of guilt or worthlessness
Loss of interest in activities once enjoyed
Withdrawal from family and friends

diseases.name: Postpartum Hemorrhage - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) is a serious condition that can occur after childbirth, characterized by excessive bleeding. It is one of the leading causes of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide. Understanding PPH is crucial for new mothers, healthcare providers, and families, as timely recognition and management can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of postpartum hemorrhage, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of postpartum hemorrhage can vary but may include:
Excessive bleeding: Soaking through one or more pads in an hour.
Severe abdominal pain: Pain that is more intense than typical postpartum discomfort.
Dizziness or fainting: Signs of significant blood loss.
Rapid heartbeat: A compensatory response to blood loss.
Pale or clammy skin: Indicating shock or severe blood loss.

diseases.name: Postpartum Preeclampsia - Symptoms, Causes , Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Postpartum Preeclampsia is a rare and serious condition that occurs in mothers who have given birth recently. It generally develops around 48 hours after childbirth . This condition needs immediate clinical attention and treatment to avoid complications.
symptoms: It is possible that you may not notice the symptoms of preeclampsia during pregnancy . However, if you do develop this condition, be careful to watch out for the following symptoms:
Constant headache
Swelling in the legs , face, or hands
Sudden weight gain
Temporary loss of vision
Blurry vision or increased sensitivity to light
Upper abdominal pain
Decreased urination
Protein in urine

diseases.name: Postpartum Psychosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postpartum psychosis is a severe mental health condition that can occur in women after childbirth. It is a rare but serious disorder that can have profound effects on both the mother and her newborn. Understanding postpartum psychosis is crucial for new mothers, their families, and healthcare providers, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of postpartum psychosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Postpartum psychosis can present with a variety of symptoms, which may include:
Hallucinations: Seeing or hearing things that are not present.
Delusions: Strongly held false beliefs, such as believing that one has special powers or that the baby is in danger.
Severe Mood Swings: Rapid changes in mood, from extreme elation to deep despair.
Disorganized Thinking: Difficulty concentrating or making coherent decisions.
Paranoia: Intense feelings of suspicion or fear regarding others' intentions.

diseases.name: Postprandial Hypotension - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Postprandial hypotension is a condition characterized by a significant drop in blood pressure after eating. This phenomenon can lead to various symptoms, including dizziness, lightheadedness, and even fainting. Understanding postprandial hypotension is crucial, as it can significantly impact the quality of life, particularly in older adults and those with certain medical conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of postprandial hypotension, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of postprandial hypotension can vary in severity and may include:
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A common symptom that occurs due to reduced blood flow to the brain.
Fainting or Near-Fainting: In severe cases, individuals may experience syncope (loss of consciousness).
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness after meals.
Nausea: Some individuals may feel nauseous, particularly after large meals.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.

diseases.name: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: POTS or Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome is a blood circulation condition in which your heart rate changes whenever you change positions. However, ideally, your heart rate should remain the same whether you are sitting up, lying down, or standing. This change in heart rate is known as Orthostatic Intolerance (OI).
symptoms: POTS symptoms are more pronounced after a meal when the blood is redirected to your digestive tract. You might also experience the symptoms when stressed, standing in line, or in the shower.
Pain in the stomach
Dizziness or fainting
Blurry vision
Brain fog
Feeling hot or cold
Shaking or tremors
Excessive sweating
Nausea
Vomiting
Bloating
Diarrhea or constipation
Extreme fatigue
Higher or lower blood pressure
Changed heart rate
Chest pain
Anxiety
Headaches, body aches, or neck pain
Insomnia
Unusual color of the hands and feet

diseases.name: Potter Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Potter Syndrome, also known as Potter's sequence, is a rare congenital condition that arises from a lack of amniotic fluid during pregnancy, leading to a series of developmental abnormalities in the fetus. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on fetal development but also due to the profound implications it has for families and healthcare providers. Understanding Potter Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support for affected individuals and their families.
symptoms: The symptoms of Potter Syndrome can vary widely depending on the severity of the condition and the specific deformities present. Common symptoms include:
Facial Deformities: This may include a flattened nose, low-set ears, and a recessed chin.
Limb Deformities: Abnormalities such as clubfoot or limb reduction may occur.
Pulmonary Hypoplasia: Underdeveloped lungs can lead to respiratory difficulties at birth.
Abdominal Wall Defects: Conditions such as omphalocele or gastroschisis may be present.

diseases.name: Potts Puffy Tumor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Potts Puffy Tumor is a rare but significant medical condition that primarily affects the forehead region. It is characterized by a localized swelling of the soft tissues over the frontal bone, often associated with underlying osteomyelitis (infection of the bone). This condition is named after Sir Percival Pott, an 18th-century surgeon who first described it. Understanding Potts Puffy Tumor is crucial, as it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Potts Puffy Tumor, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of Potts Puffy Tumor can vary but typically include:
Swelling: A noticeable swelling on the forehead, often warm to the touch.
Pain: Localized pain or tenderness in the forehead area.
Fever: Elevated body temperature indicating an infection.
Headache: Persistent headaches that may worsen with time.
Nasal Congestion: Difficulty breathing through the nose due to sinus blockage.
Discharge: Possible nasal discharge, which may be purulent (pus-like).

diseases.name: Pouchitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pouchitis is a condition that affects individuals who have undergone surgery to create a pouch from the end of the small intestine, typically following the removal of the colon due to conditions like ulcerative colitis or familial adenomatous polyposis. This pouch, known as an ileal pouch, serves as a reservoir for waste. While this surgical intervention can significantly improve quality of life, pouchitis can develop as a complication, leading to inflammation and discomfort. Understanding pouchitis is crucial for those who have undergone this surgery, as well as for healthcare providers and caregivers.
symptoms: Pouchitis can present with a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Diarrhea: Frequent, watery stools are a hallmark of pouchitis.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the abdomen is common.
Rectal Bleeding: Blood in the stool or from the rectum may occur.
Urgency: A sudden, strong need to have a bowel movement.
Fever: Low-grade fever may accompany inflammation.
Fatigue: Chronic inflammation can lead to feelings of tiredness or weakness.

diseases.name: Power Nap : Napping Benefits, Length, and How To Do It
diseases.description: It’s known that babies and toddlers need naps. But studies have proven that short naps are beneficial for everyone. Due to its great benefits, these short naps are called power naps, and many corporates have started incorporating nap times into their work schedule and installing nap pods in offices. This blog is a comprehensive guide on the benefits of power naps and other important information about power naps.

diseases.name: Pre Menstrual Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Risk Factors
diseases.description: Pre menstrual syndrome (PMS) is a condition in women that starts five to eleven days before menstruation and lasts until after menstruation. It is a combination of physical, emotional, psychological and mood disturbances that usually end with the onset of menstrual flow. The mood-related symptoms that commonly occur are depression, oversensitivity, crying, irritability, and mood swings. The physical symptoms are fatigue, bloating, breast tenderness (mastalgia), acne , and appetite changes associated with the craving for food. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) or late luteal phase dysphoric disorder, is a more severe form of PMS, known to occur in some women and leads to significant loss of function. Unusually severe symptoms like irritability, anger, anxiety or tension are particularly prominent. About 90% of women at some point in their lifetime have premenstrual symptoms. It is estimated that 20% to 30% of women have clinically significant PMS, i.e., moderate to severe in intensity affecting the woman’s functioning. A more severe form of PMS occurs in the 4th decade of life and 3% to 8% of women are known to have this condition. Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals
symptoms: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) vary every month and from person to person. There are many different symptoms of PMS. The PMS symptoms may be similar or vary every month in intensity. Slightly different symptoms occur every few months. For every woman, the symptoms are different. The symptoms of PMS may happen in the menstrual cycle each month at the same time. It can happen two weeks before menstruation begins. Symptoms start to improve as the period is about to start and disappear once the period begins. Some of the symptoms of PMS, such as depression , weight gain, fatigue are similar to symptoms of thyroid disorders. This can help to rule out a thyroid disorder as a cause of the symptoms.
Feeling of bloating
Discomfort and pain in the abdomen
Backache
Headaches
Breast pain
Joint and muscle pain
Trouble in sleeping ( insomnia )
Nausea
Weight gain (up to 1kg)
Long-term or (chronic) illnesses like migraines or asthma usually get worse
Mood swings
Feeling upset or emotional
Social withdrawal
Feeling irritable or angry
Crying
Anxiety
Difficulty concentrating
Confusion and forgetfulness
Clumsiness
Restlessness
Tiredness
Decreased self-esteem
Loss of interest in sex
Appetite changes or food cravings

Many women with PMS have severe symptoms. Some symptoms are severe enough to prevent them living their usual lives. This type of PMS the result is more intense and is known as premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). The symptoms of PMDD are similar to those of PMS, but are more blown up and has more physical symptoms than psychological symptoms
Feelings of hopelessness
Persistent sadness or depression
Extreme anger and anxiety
Decreased interest in usual activities
Sleeping much more or less than usual
Very low self-esteem
Extreme tension and irritability

Woman with PMDD may usually have suicidal thoughts . Depression is a common symptom of PMDD. PMDD is very difficult to deal with as it has a negative effect on the daily relationships and life. Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Precocious Puberty - Causes, Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: When a child’s body begins to undergo sexual and physical development sooner than usual (puberty), it is known as precocious puberty. If puberty begins in girls before the age of 8 and before the age of 9 in boys it is considered precocious puberty. Although the cause is unknown, certain rare conditions that lead to hormone disorders, infections, brain abnormalities , or injuries may cause precocious puberty. Medications are given as the mainstay treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms for precocious puberty in boys are as follows:
Acne
Enlargement of the testicles or penis
Armpit or pubic hair
Increased facial hair, generally on the upper lip
Muscle growth
Deepening of voice
Growth spurt
Spontaneous erections
Increased sperm production
Growth and development of breasts
Underarm and pubic hair
Early onset of menstruation
Ovulation
Rapid height growth

diseases.name: Precordial Catch Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Precordial Catch Syndrome (PCS) is a benign condition that primarily affects children and adolescents, characterized by sharp, localized chest pain. While it can be alarming for both the patient and their caregivers, PCS is generally harmless and does not indicate any underlying heart disease or serious medical condition. Understanding PCS is crucial for parents, educators, and healthcare providers to alleviate concerns and provide appropriate care. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Precordial Catch Syndrome.
symptoms: Sharp Chest Pain: The hallmark symptom of PCS is a sudden, sharp pain in the chest, often on the left side.
Localized Discomfort: The pain is usually localized and can be pinpointed by the patient.
Duration: The pain typically lasts from a few seconds to several minutes and may resolve spontaneously.
Exacerbation with Movement: Symptoms may worsen with deep breathing, coughing, or certain movements.

diseases.name: Prediabetes - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: When you have a higher than normal blood sugar level, but not to the level that indicates diabetes , you are said to have prediabetes. If you do not take any corrective action, you have a higher chance of developing type 2 diabetes. It may show symptoms. Blood sugar level testing can help determine if you have it. If you are at risk of developing diabetes , you need to make lifestyle changes like exercising, eating healthy, and losing weight to reverse prediabetes and avoid type 2 diabetes.
symptoms: It usually has no signs or symptoms. You may, however, experience the following.
Acanthosis nigricans, which is darkened skin usually seen in your armpit, neck, elbows, knuckles, and knees
Small skin growths or skin tags
Changes in the eye can cause diabetic retinopathy (damage to the blood vessels of the eyes)
Symptoms such as increased thirst, increased urination, excess hunger, blurred vision, and fatigue can indicate that you have moved onto type 2 diabetes.

diseases.name: Pregnancy After Miscarriage: Causes and Chances of Conceiving Again
diseases.description: Pregnancy brings happiness to women. However, it can also be filled with worry if they have previously suffered from a miscarriage. It is usual for them to feel a range of emotions after a pregnancy loss. However, there is no need to be unduly anxious as most women who experience a miscarriage will have a healthy baby.

diseases.name: Pregnancy Constipation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pregnancy is a beautiful journey filled with excitement and anticipation, but it can also bring about various physical challenges. One of the most common yet often overlooked issues is pregnancy constipation. This condition can significantly impact a woman's quality of life during pregnancy, leading to discomfort and distress. Understanding pregnancy constipation, its causes, symptoms, and management options is crucial for expectant mothers to navigate this phase with ease.
symptoms: Pregnancy constipation can manifest through various symptoms, including:
Infrequent bowel movements (fewer than three times a week)
Hard, dry stools
Straining during bowel movements
Abdominal discomfort or bloating
A feeling of incomplete evacuation

diseases.name: Pregnancy Gingivitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pregnancy is a beautiful journey filled with anticipation and joy, but it also comes with its own set of challenges, including changes in a woman's oral health. One common condition that can arise during this time is Pregnancy Gingivitis . This condition is not just a minor inconvenience; it can have significant implications for both the mother and the developing fetus. Understanding what Pregnancy Gingivitis is, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options is crucial for maintaining optimal oral health during pregnancy.
symptoms: Pregnancy Gingivitis can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Swollen Gums: Gums may appear puffy and inflamed.
Red or Bleeding Gums: Gums may bleed during brushing or flossing.
Bad Breath: Persistent halitosis can occur due to bacterial buildup.
Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity in the gums may be experienced.
Changes in Gum Color: Gums may appear darker red instead of the usual pink.

diseases.name: Pregnancy Hemorrhoids: Causes, Risks & Treatment
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids, also known as piles , are swollen blood vessels in and around the anus and lower rectum. This is commonly seen in pregnant women in their third trimester when the enlarged uterus puts pressure on the veins, which is called pregnancy hemorrhoids.
symptoms: Piles during pregnancy have the following symptoms:
Bleeding during bowel movement
Itching, discomfort and swelling in anus
A lump like growth hanging out of the anus
Discomfort during passing stools
Discharge of mucus after the bowel movement
Burning sensation after the bowel movement

diseases.name: Pregnancy Stretch Marks: During and After Pregnancy, and What to Expect
diseases.description: A pregnant woman experiences numerous hormonal and physical changes, including stretch marks. The cause of stretch marks is the stretching of the skin. Their severity is affected by several factors, including your genetics and the degree of stress on the skin. It can develop during or after pregnancy and typically appear on the stomach, thighs, and breasts. However, it can continue even after delivering the baby and can be made less visible with various treatments.
symptoms: The following are the symptoms of stretch marks:
Indented streaks or lines on different parts of the body, particularly the abdomen, breasts, hips, and buttocks
Bright streaks that are in pink, red, black, blue or purple in colours and that may fade to a lighter shade after pregnancy
The lines cover large areas of the body

diseases.name: Premature Birth: When Does it Become a Necessity?
diseases.description: A pregnancy lasts for approximately 280 days or 40 weeks. A birth three weeks prior, i.e., before the 37th week of the estimated pregnancy, is termed as premature birth. Due to a lack of proper development, premature babies are often at a high risk of medical complications. These complications vary depending on the pre-maturity of birth.

diseases.name: Premature Ejaculation – Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Also called rapid ejaculation, premature climax, or early ejaculation, premature ejaculation is a term used to describe the premature or untimely release (ejaculate) that occurs sooner than either the man or his partner would like. It usually occurs prior to or immediately after penetration when having intercourse.
symptoms: The inability to hold ejaculation for more than one minute after penetration is the main symptom. This problem may also occur during masturbation evidenced by rapid climax and ejaculation. Based on the symptoms, it is of the following types:
Lifelong (primary) – in which premature ejaculation occurs right from your very first sexual encounter
Acquired (secondary) – in which you may have had previous normal sexual experiences and have lately developed the problem
Natural variable premature ejaculation – in which you may alternate between periods of normal ejaculation and rapid ejaculation.

diseases.name: Premature Rupture Of Membranes - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Premature Rupture of Membranes (PROM) is a significant obstetric condition that occurs when the amniotic sac, which surrounds and protects the fetus during pregnancy, ruptures before labor begins. This event can lead to various complications for both the mother and the baby, making it crucial for expectant parents to understand its implications. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding PROM.
symptoms: The primary symptom of PROM is the sudden release of amniotic fluid from the vagina. This may be experienced as a gush or a slow leak. Other symptoms may include:
Fluid Leakage : Continuous leaking of clear or pale yellow fluid.
Increased Pressure : A feeling of pressure in the pelvis.
Contractions : Some women may experience contractions after the membranes rupture.

diseases.name: Premature Ventricular Contractions - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs) are a common type of heart arrhythmia characterized by early heartbeats originating from the ventricles. While PVCs are often benign and may not require treatment, their significance lies in their potential to indicate underlying heart conditions or provoke more serious arrhythmias. Understanding PVCs is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can lead to better management and improved outcomes.
symptoms: Many people with PVCs may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Palpitations: A feeling of skipped or extra heartbeats.
Fluttering Sensation: A sensation of the heart racing or fluttering in the chest.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Some individuals may feel faint or dizzy, especially if PVCs are frequent.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness may accompany frequent PVCs.

diseases.name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder Pmdd - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) is a severe form of premenstrual syndrome (PMS) that affects a significant number of women during their reproductive years. While PMS is characterized by mild to moderate emotional and physical symptoms, PMDD can lead to debilitating emotional distress and physical discomfort. Understanding PMDD is crucial not only for those who suffer from it but also for healthcare providers and loved ones who can offer support. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of PMDD, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: PMDD symptoms can vary widely among individuals but generally include:
Emotional Symptoms: Severe mood swings, irritability, anxiety, depression, and feelings of hopelessness.
Physical Symptoms: Fatigue, muscle or joint pain, headaches, bloating, and breast tenderness.
Cognitive Symptoms: Difficulty concentrating, memory problems, and a sense of being overwhelmed.

diseases.name: Prepatellar Bursitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prepatellar bursitis, commonly known as "housemaid's knee," is a condition characterized by inflammation of the bursa located in front of the kneecap (patella). This small, fluid-filled sac plays a crucial role in reducing friction between the knee joint and surrounding tissues, allowing for smooth movement. While prepatellar bursitis can affect anyone, it is particularly significant for individuals whose occupations or activities involve frequent kneeling or pressure on the knees. Understanding this condition is essential for effective management and prevention.
symptoms: Common symptoms of prepatellar bursitis include:
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the front of the knee.
Pain: Tenderness and pain, especially when kneeling or bending the knee.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty in fully extending or flexing the knee.
Warmth and Redness: The skin over the bursa may appear warm and red, particularly in cases of infection.

diseases.name: Presbyopia - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Presbyopia is an eye condition. In presbyopia, your eyes gradually lose their ability to focus on objects which are nearby. It usually occurs due to the aging process. You may notice presbyopia after your 40s till around 65 years. For example, your inability to read without holding the item at arm’s length will make you aware of your presbyopia. An eye exam can confirm your presbyopia. Glasses, contact lenses, or surgery are among the treatment alternatives for presbyopia.
symptoms: The main symptoms of presbyopia are after the age of 40, which are as follows.
Difficulty in reading small print
Facing fatigue when doing work that requires close distance from your eyes
Blurred vision when reading from an average distance
Holding material further away from you to read better
Requiring brighter light when reading from a close distance
Difficulty in focusing and seeing objects which are at a near distance from you
Squinting

diseases.name: Prescription Drug Abuse - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Prescription drug abuse is a condition that compels you to consume medication without being prescribed to do so. You can become addicted to the drugs if continued long enough. Swallowing medicines without any reason or snorting the powdered drug, or injecting it into your body are all types of prescription drug abuse.
symptoms: Abuse of prescription drugs can get identified by various symptoms. The doctor can diagnose the problem by noting a few complications caused by the overuse of specific drugs.
A decrease in the dosage of Opioid until it is no longer essential
Buprenorphine, buprenorphine with naloxone
You will get asked to consume a low dose of anti- anxiety pills or sedatives to overcome the withdrawal symptoms until your body is ready to sleep naturally.
The doctor will advise you to stop taking stimulants . Problems of insomnia , fatigue and depression will get treated separately.

diseases.name: Presyncope - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Presyncope is a medical term that refers to a state of near-fainting or lightheadedness that occurs before a person actually loses consciousness. It is a significant condition that can serve as a warning sign for various underlying health issues. Understanding presyncope is crucial, as it can help individuals recognize symptoms early and seek appropriate medical attention, potentially preventing more serious complications.
symptoms: Individuals experiencing presyncope may report a variety of symptoms, including:
Lightheadedness: A feeling of dizziness or unsteadiness.
Weakness: A sudden loss of strength or energy.
Nausea: An upset stomach or feeling of queasiness.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or seeing spots.
Sweating: Increased perspiration, often accompanied by a feeling of warmth.

diseases.name: Preterm Labor - Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Preterm labor occurs when uterine contractions result in the opening of the cervix after week 20 and before week 37 of pregnancy resulting in early labor.
symptoms: The symptoms of preterm labor may include the following:
A sensation of alternate contraction and relaxation of the abdomen
A continuous dull ache in your lower back
Low pressure in your pelvis or lower part of the abdomen
Cramps similar to menstrual cramps
Spotting of blood or mild bleeding through the vagina
A sudden rush of fluid from the vagina
The type of vaginal discharge changes from thin, watery, to thick, mucous-filled one; it may be stained with blood

diseases.name: Pretibial Myxedema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pretibial myxedema is a skin condition that often serves as a visible marker of underlying thyroid dysfunction, particularly in individuals with hyperthyroidism or Graves' disease. This condition is characterized by the thickening and swelling of the skin, primarily on the shins, and can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding pretibial myxedema is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers who may encounter this condition in their practice.
symptoms: The symptoms of pretibial myxedema can vary in severity and may include:
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the pretibial area, often described as a "puffy" appearance.
Thickened Skin: The skin may feel thick and rubbery to the touch.
Waxy Appearance: The skin may have a shiny, waxy look.
Itching or Discomfort: Some individuals may experience itching or discomfort in the affected area.

diseases.name: Preventive Health Check-ups – A smart step for your good health
diseases.description: Many of us live a hectic life today be it tiring social engagements or pressing deadlines. However, in all this hustle-bustle we are more likely to neglect our health often. As good health helps us enjoy life and live well, there is a great need for preventive care. The cause of most of the fatalities or deaths are due to chronic disease and half of these can be prevented by knowing early symptoms and risks with proper screening and regular check-ups. A regular check-up will not only assess your overall wellbeing but can also detect any disease or health risks before they strike. In fact, preventive health check-ups can actually be lifesaving, as they update us on how fit and healthy we are. Preventive health check-up packages and wellness checks are generally tailored to prevent diseases and conditions that may be caused due to many factors including the individual’s genetic predisposition, environmental factors, lifestyle choices, and disease agents.

diseases.name: Priapism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Priapism is a medical condition characterized by a prolonged and often painful erection that lasts for more than four hours without sexual arousal. This condition is not only uncomfortable but can also lead to serious complications if left untreated. Understanding priapism is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely intervention can prevent long-term damage to the penis and associated psychological distress. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of priapism.
symptoms: The primary symptom of priapism is a prolonged erection that lasts for more than four hours. This erection is often painful and not associated with sexual desire or stimulation. Other symptoms may include:
Swelling or tenderness in the penis
Pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis
Difficulty urinating

diseases.name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis -Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Primary biliary cholangitis is a disease that occurs when bile ducts in the liver get damaged. It is also known as primary biliary cirrhosis . When the bile ducts get damaged, the bile starts building up in the liver. Over time, the accumulation of bile leads to liver damage. As a result, permanent scarring and cirrhosis can happen. New treatments are being introduced that work to enhance the outlook for people with primary biliary cholangitis.
symptoms: It develops slowly and sometimes people may not have symptoms for years even after being diagnosed. The early symptoms include fatigue, dry mouth and eyes, and itchy skin. However, as it progresses, the succeeding symptoms may include:
Pain in the upper right abdomen
Enlargement of the spleen
Darkening of the skin
Loss of appetite
Dry eyes and mouth
Nausea
Weight loss
Small white or yellow bumps under skin or eyes
Jaundice
Swollen legs and ankles
Fractures due to weakened bones and osteoporosis
Joint, bone, or muscle pain
Swollen abdomen
Brittle and weak bones (osteoporosis) that can lead to fractures
High cholesterol
Diarrhea , which might include greasy stools
Underactive thyroid

diseases.name: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the cilia, the tiny hair-like structures that line the respiratory tract and other organs. These cilia play a crucial role in moving mucus and other substances out of the lungs and maintaining the health of the respiratory system. When cilia do not function properly, it can lead to a range of health issues, including chronic respiratory infections, fertility problems, and other complications. Understanding PCD is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Chronic Cough: A persistent cough that may produce mucus.
Frequent Respiratory Infections: Increased susceptibility to colds, bronchitis, and pneumonia.
Sinusitis: Chronic inflammation of the sinuses, leading to nasal congestion and facial pain.
Ear Infections: Recurrent ear infections due to fluid buildup in the middle ear.
Infertility: In males, PCD can lead to reduced sperm motility, while females may experience issues with egg transport.
Bronchiectasis: A condition where the airways become damaged and widened, leading to further respiratory complications.

diseases.name: Primary Lateral Sclerosis (PLS) - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Primary lateral sclerosis or PLS is a disease where the nerve cells in the brain that control movement, which is also called upper motor neurons, slowly break down and fail over time.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of primary lateral sclerosis are:
Weakness and stiffness and spasms in the legs
Slowing movement
Tripping or problem in balancing because of the weakness in the leg muscles
Weakness as well as stiffness in the arms, tongue, hands and also in the jaw sometimes
Slowed speech, hoarseness and drooling
Difficulty in swallowing breathing and bladder issues at a later stage in this disease
Signs and symptoms of primary lateral sclerosis generally take years to progress and usually begin in the legs.
Less frequently, primary lateral sclerosis starts in the hands and the tongue and after some time, it reaches the spinal cord and then the legs.

diseases.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a condition that damages the bile ducts. In this disease, inflammation causes scars within the bile ducts. The scars make the bile ducts hard and narrow and slowly lead to serious liver damage. Most of the PSC patients also have inflammatory bowel disease , such as ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease . The bile ducts carry bile, which is a digestive liquid that helps in the digestion of fats and fatty acids. In the majority of people, the disease progression is slow but serious cases can lead to liver failure .
symptoms: Many people continue to feel generally well for several years. It is difficult predict how quickly or slowly the disease will progress for any individual.
Itching on the body
Yellow eyes and skin due to onset of jaundice
Abdominal pain
Fatigue
Enlargement of liver and spleen
Fever
Loss of weight
Fever with chills
Night sweats

diseases.name: Prinzmetal Angina - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prinzmetal Angina, also known as variant angina, is a type of chest pain that occurs due to spasms in the coronary arteries, which supply blood to the heart muscle. Unlike typical angina, which is often triggered by physical exertion or stress, Prinzmetal Angina can occur at rest, often during the night or early morning. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Prinzmetal Angina, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Prinzmetal Angina is chest pain, which may be described as a squeezing, pressure-like sensation. Other common symptoms include:
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate to the shoulders, arms, neck, jaw, or back.
Shortness of Breath: Some individuals may experience difficulty breathing during episodes.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats may accompany the pain.
Nausea: Some patients report feelings of nausea or lightheadedness during episodes.

diseases.name: Prion Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prion diseases are a group of rare, progressive neurodegenerative disorders that affect both humans and animals. They are caused by misfolded proteins known as prions, which lead to brain damage and a range of severe neurological symptoms. The significance of prion diseases lies not only in their devastating effects on health but also in their unique mechanism of transmission and resistance to conventional sterilization methods. Understanding prion diseases is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Prion diseases manifest through a variety of neurological symptoms, which may include:
Cognitive decline: Memory loss, confusion, and difficulty concentrating.
Behavioral changes: Personality shifts, anxiety, and depression.
Motor dysfunction: Tremors, muscle stiffness, and coordination problems.
Visual disturbances: Blurred vision or hallucinations.
Severe insomnia: Difficulty sleeping or changes in sleep patterns.

diseases.name: Proctalgia Fugax - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Proctalgia Fugax is a medical condition characterized by sudden, severe pain in the rectal area. While it may sound alarming, it is often benign and self-limiting. Understanding this condition is crucial for those who experience it, as it can significantly impact quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Proctalgia Fugax, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of Proctalgia Fugax is sudden, severe pain in the rectal area. Other associated symptoms may include:
Cramping Sensation: Some individuals report a cramping feeling in the lower abdomen.
Discomfort: A sense of discomfort or pressure in the rectal region may accompany the pain.
Frequency of Episodes: Episodes can occur sporadically, sometimes multiple times a day or week.

diseases.name: Proctitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The rectum is the tube connected to the end of your colon. Stool passes through the rectum and is excreted. Proctitis is a condition that causes inflammation of the inner lining of the rectum. Several factors cause the disease, including sexually transmitted infection.
symptoms: The symptoms associated with proctitis are:
Rectal bleeding and pain
Continuous feeling or need for a bowel movement
Passing of mucus through the rectum
Diarrhea
Pain associated with bowel movements
Pain commonly on the left side of the abdominal region

diseases.name: Progeria: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatments
diseases.description: Progeria is a condition that affects young children. It causes the child to experience aging from the tender age of two. Known as Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome in medical parlance, it is a rare genetic disorder. Such children generally have a low life expectancy. Nonetheless, modern research has made progress, with proper treatment becoming more promising.
symptoms: Intelligence and physical development is not hampered in the child after birth. But your child may develop the following symptoms and change in appearance as they age:
Reduced growth with height and weight not being up to the normal standards
A thin face with a thin lower lip, beak-like nose, and a small lower jaw
Head bigger in size in comparison to other facial features
Prominent eyes with the eyelids being incapable of closing fully
Hair loss all over the body including from head, eyelashes, and eyebrows
Thin skin marked with spots and wrinkles
Prominent veins
Shrill high-pitched voice
Severe cardiovascular (heart & blood vessels) diseases that progress with time
Tightening of the skin in the trunk and limbs
Abnormality or delayed teething
Loss of hearing
Reduced fat in the skin with loss of muscle bulk
Abnormality in skeletal structure resulting in brittle bones
Increased chances of hip dislocation
Stiffness of joints
Resistance to insulin

diseases.name: Prognathism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prognathism is a dental and skeletal condition characterized by the protrusion of the jaw, particularly the lower jaw (mandible) or the upper jaw (maxilla). This condition can significantly impact an individual's oral health, facial aesthetics, and overall quality of life. Understanding prognathism is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to complications such as difficulty in chewing, speech issues, and even psychological effects due to altered appearance. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of prognathism, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Individuals with prognathism may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Facial Asymmetry: Noticeable differences in the alignment of facial features.
Difficulty Chewing: Problems with biting and chewing food due to misaligned teeth.
Speech Issues: Difficulty pronouncing certain sounds, leading to speech impediments.
Jaw Pain: Discomfort or pain in the jaw, especially during movement.
Frequent Headaches: Tension headaches resulting from jaw strain.
Dental Problems: Increased risk of cavities, gum disease, and tooth wear due to misalignment.

diseases.name: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) : Causes, Symptoms, Treatment
diseases.description: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a rare brain infection due to a virus. It is known to destroy our brain’s white matter, myelin. Myelin is a fatty substance that covers and protects our brain’s nerve cells that send signals to different body parts. As the virus progresses, causing a gradual decrease of myelin, we may be at a higher risk of developing neurological disorders. The progress of the disease can slow down when we receive timely treatment from the doctor.
symptoms: So long as the virus is inactive, we may not be aware of its presence within us. However, if we are immunocompromised, the chances of the virus being active are higher. And when it happens, the symptoms are based on the affected part of the brain. The initial symptoms are similar to those of other health conditions. However, the following are the signs of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy:
Lack of coordination
Weakness in the legs and arms that progressively worsen
Speaking and walking issues
Loss of memory
Changes in personality
Facial drooping
A decline in mental ability
As the disease continues to damage the white cells of our brain, the symptoms start to become severe. We may experience:
Dementia
Loss of speech and vision
Coma
Headaches and seizures , in rare cases
PML is fatal. But timely treatment and our response to it significantly affect our prognosis.

diseases.name: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Progressive supranuclear palsy is an unusual type of brain disorder that affects mobility, balance, vision, speech, and swallowing. You may experience difficulty in moving your eyes and have trouble swallowing food. This is caused by the degeneration of particular brain cells, making it extremely difficult for you to continue normal functions. There is no treatment available at present. The condition is life-threatening but doctors manage it by treating the symptoms.
symptoms: The symptoms of progressive Supranuclear palsy may include some or all of the following:
Loss of balance and mobility issues
Difficulty in focusing the eyes
Stiffness felt during walking with the movements becoming awkward
Falling frequently
Slurring
Difficulty in swallowing
Light sensitivity
Disinterest in enjoyable activities
Behavioral changes
Memory loss
Losing reasoning and analytical skills
Anxiety and depression
Fixed expression due to rigidity of facial muscles

diseases.name: Prolactinoma - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Prolactinoma is a nonmalignant tumor of the pituitary gland. This growth affects a hormone produced by the pituitary gland called prolactin. This, in turn, affects two sex hormones. It decreases the level of estrogen in women and testosterone in men.
symptoms: The following are the symptoms of prolactinoma:
Acne
Excessive hair growth on the body and face
Erectile Dysfunction
Vaginal dryness
Irregular periods
Milk like discharge when not pregnant
Infertility
Decreased interest in sexual intercourse
Pain during sexual intercourse
Decreased body and facial hair in men
Enlarged breasts in men (uncommonly)
In both sexes, prolactinoma can cause:
Reduction in the production of other hormone by the pituitary gland as a result of tumor pressure
Loss of interest in sexual activity
Low bone density
Visual disturbances
Headaches

diseases.name: Prolapsed Bladder - Causes, Symptoms, and Treatments
diseases.description: prolapsed Bladder is when the ligaments that hold your bladder up and the muscle that connects your vagina to your bladder stretch or weaken, enabling the bladder to drop into your vagina. It is also known as cystocele , herniated, dropped, or fallen bladder.
symptoms: The presence of tissue in the vaginal area, which many women describe as feeling like a ball, is frequently the initial symptom of a prolapsed bladder.
Other signs and symptoms of a prolapsed bladder include:
Pelvic dissatisfaction or discomfort
Protruding tissue from the vaginal canal (The tissue may be tender and may bleed)
Urination problems
Feeling as if your bladder isn’t empty after you’ve urinated (incomplete voiding)
Incontinence due to stress (urine leakage during sneezing, coughing, or exertion)
Frequent bladder infections
Intercourse that is painful ( dyspareunia )
Pelvic or lower back pain , fullness, heaviness, or discomfort. When the person stands, lifts, coughs, or as the day develops, the sensation may worsen
Tampons or applicators are difficult to implant
The bladder pushes its way into or out of the vaginal opening
Heaviness or pressure in the vaginal area

diseases.name: Prolapsed Hemorrhoids - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Hemorrhoids can become prolapsed and protrude out of the anus or rectum if they go untreated for a long time or are put under increased physical strain. Prolapsed hemorrhoids are usually not painful, but they can cause discomfort, bleeding, and itching, making sitting, using the bathroom, and going about everyday life difficult.
symptoms: The following are the most prevalent symptoms of prolapsed hemorrhoids:
There may be a lump on the anus. It can be noticed when wiping after a bowel movement. This is the enlarged vein, which might be painful when touched, painful all of the time, or painless.
The skin around the anus may be quite irritated in a prolapsed hemorrhoid.

There is blood in the toilet, on the toilet paper, or even on the underwear. Typically, the blood is brilliant red and highly fluid. Blood from the stomach or intestinal bleeding is usually dark, black, or tarry in appearance.

Large prolapsed hemorrhoids can cause general discomfort as well as a sense of incomplete bowel evacuation, or the impression that the patient still needs to evacuate stool after a bowel movement. When the hemorrhoid is touched by a bowel movement or anything else, it may become tender. It may also be irritated by the pressure of sitting.
Hemorrhoids are uncomfortable, but they are not life-threatening, and they usually go away without treatment.

However, if the patient has any bleeding or black bowel motions, they should visit a doctor. Bleeding can be caused by a variety of things other than hemorrhoids, so it is important to get it checked out.

diseases.name: Prostate Cancer - Types, Stages, Causes, Symptoms, Screening, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Prostate cancer is a significant health concern for men worldwide, with increasing incidence in both developing and developed countries. While it most commonly affects men over the age of 50, cases are now being reported in younger age groups as well, especially those between 35 and 55 years. Early detection plays a critical role in improving treatment outcomes and preserving quality of life.
symptoms: Prostate cancer often develops silently in its early stages and may not produce noticeable symptoms for years. This is why routine screening is crucial , especially for men over 50 or those at higher risk. When symptoms do occur, they are often related to urinary or reproductive function, due to the prostate’s location around the urethra.
In the early stages, prostate cancer symptoms may be subtle or mistaken for benign conditions such as Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) or prostatitis . Common signs include:
Frequent urination, especially at night
Difficulty starting or stopping urination
Weak or interrupted urinary stream
Burning or painful sensation while urinating
Painful ejaculation
Erectile dysfunction
Blood in the urine ( hematuria ) or blood in semen ( hematospermia )
Feeling of incomplete bladder emptying
Urine leakage while coughing, sneezing, or laughing
These symptoms are not exclusive to prostate cancer and may also occur with non-cancerous prostate conditions, but they warrant evaluation by a healthcare provider.
As prostate cancer progresses, it can spread to nearby tissues, lymph nodes, and bones. Symptoms of advanced prostate cancer may include:
Persistent pain or stiffness in the pelvic region , lower back , hips , ribs , or upper thighs
Swelling in the legs or pelvic area due to lymphatic obstruction
Unexplained weight loss and fatigue
Numbness, weakness, or even paralysis in the lower limbs (if cancer spreads to the spine)
Loss of bladder or bowel control in extreme cases
