Not necessarily. Several conditions, such as BPH and prostatitis , can mimic the symptoms of prostate cancer. These are non-cancerous and more common in younger men. However, any persistent urinary, sexual, or pelvic symptoms should be evaluated by a urologist to rule out cancer and ensure early intervention if needed.

diseases.name: Prostatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Risk Factors and Treatment
diseases.description: Prostatitis is a condition where the prostate gland and its surrounding area are inflamed.
symptoms: The symptoms are as follows:
Pain while urinating
Increased pain after ejaculation
Frequent urination
Weak urine stream
Fever
Chills
Burning sensation when urinating
Pain in the pelvic region
Nausea or vomiting
Trouble urinating
Pain or discomfort in the region between the scrotum and the anus, the penis, the lower back, or the lower abdomen.

diseases.name: Protein S Deficiency - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Protein S deficiency is a rare but significant blood disorder that plays a crucial role in the body’s ability to regulate blood clotting. This condition can lead to an increased risk of developing abnormal blood clots, known as thrombosis, which can have serious health implications. Understanding Protein S deficiency is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can help prevent life-threatening complications such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of Protein S deficiency.
symptoms: Individuals with Protein S deficiency may not exhibit symptoms until they experience a thrombotic event. Common symptoms associated with thrombosis include:
Swelling: Swelling in the legs or arms, often accompanied by pain or tenderness.
Redness: Affected areas may appear red or discolored.
Warmth: The skin over the affected area may feel warm to the touch.
Shortness of Breath: If a clot travels to the lungs (pulmonary embolism), it can cause sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood.

diseases.name: Protein-Energy Malnutrition
diseases.description: Protein-energy malnutrition occurs when the body does not get enough calories and protein to meet its needs.
symptoms: Weight loss
Muscle wasting
Weakness or fatigue
Poor growth in children

diseases.name: Proteinuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Proteinuria is a medical condition characterized by the presence of excess protein in the urine. While the kidneys typically filter waste products from the blood, they also retain essential proteins. When this filtration process is disrupted, proteins can leak into the urine, leading to proteinuria. This condition can be a sign of underlying health issues, making it significant for both diagnosis and treatment. Understanding proteinuria is crucial for early detection and management of potential kidney problems and other systemic diseases.
symptoms: Proteinuria itself may not cause noticeable symptoms, but it can be associated with other signs, including:
Foamy Urine: Excessive protein can create a frothy appearance in urine.
Swelling: Edema, or swelling, particularly in the legs, ankles, and around the eyes, can occur due to fluid retention.
Fatigue: General tiredness may result from kidney dysfunction.
High Blood Pressure: Kidney issues can lead to elevated blood pressure.

diseases.name: Proteus Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Proteus Syndrome is a rare and complex genetic disorder characterized by an overgrowth of various tissues in the body. This condition can lead to a wide range of physical abnormalities, including skin lesions, skeletal deformities, and vascular malformations. The significance of Proteus Syndrome lies not only in its physical manifestations but also in the challenges it poses for diagnosis, management, and the overall quality of life for affected individuals. Understanding this condition is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers alike.
symptoms: Proteus Syndrome presents a wide array of symptoms that can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Skin Abnormalities: These may include thickened skin, nevi (moles), and lipomas (benign fatty tumors).
Skeletal Deformities: Individuals may experience asymmetrical growth of bones, scoliosis, or other skeletal abnormalities.
Vascular Malformations: These can manifest as varicose veins or other vascular anomalies.
Neurological Issues: Some individuals may experience developmental delays or neurological complications.
Tumors: There is an increased risk of benign and malignant tumors in individuals with Proteus Syndrome.

diseases.name: Prurigo Nodularis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prurigo Nodularis is a chronic skin condition characterized by the presence of itchy nodules on the skin. These nodules can be quite uncomfortable and may lead to significant distress for those affected. Understanding Prurigo Nodularis is crucial not only for those who suffer from it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Prurigo Nodularis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark of Prurigo Nodularis is the presence of itchy nodules on the skin. These nodules can be:
Firm and raised: Typically, they are round or oval-shaped and can vary in size.
Red or brown: The color may change over time, often becoming darker as the condition progresses.
Scaly or crusted: Scratching can lead to the formation of scabs or crusts on the nodules.

diseases.name: Prurigo Of Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Prurigo of pregnancy is a skin condition that affects some women during pregnancy, characterized by intense itching and the formation of small, raised bumps on the skin. While it is not harmful to the mother or the baby, it can significantly impact the quality of life for expectant mothers. Understanding prurigo of pregnancy is essential for managing symptoms effectively and ensuring a comfortable pregnancy experience.
symptoms: The primary symptom of prurigo of pregnancy is intense itching, which can be distressing for expectant mothers. Other common symptoms include:
Raised Bumps: Small, red, itchy bumps that may resemble hives or insect bites.
Dry Skin: The affected areas may become dry and flaky.
Discomfort: The itching can lead to discomfort and difficulty sleeping.

diseases.name: Pseudoaneurysm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A pseudoaneurysm, often referred to as a false aneurysm, is a vascular condition that can pose significant health risks if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Unlike a true aneurysm, which involves all three layers of the arterial wall, a pseudoaneurysm occurs when there is a breach in the arterial wall, leading to blood leakage that forms a hematoma outside the vessel. This condition can arise from various causes, including trauma, infection, or medical procedures, and its significance lies in the potential for serious complications, including rupture and hemorrhage. Understanding pseudoaneurysms is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can ultimately save lives.
symptoms: The symptoms of a pseudoaneurysm can vary widely depending on its location and size. Common symptoms may include:
Pulsating Lump: A noticeable pulsating mass near the site of the affected artery.
Pain or Discomfort: Localized pain or tenderness in the area surrounding the pseudoaneurysm.
Swelling: Swelling or bruising may occur at the site of the pseudoaneurysm.
Changes in Skin Color: The skin over the pseudoaneurysm may appear discolored or warm to the touch.

diseases.name: Pseudobulbar Affect - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Pseudobulbar affect (PBA) is a condition in which patients may often display an exaggerated reaction to their emotions. This causes them to laugh or cry uncontrollably . This may be due to neurological injuries or disorders .
symptoms: Some of the common symptoms of PBA are,
Sudden, involuntary, uncontrollable episodes of laughter or crying as a response to an external event or self-triggered by the patient’s thoughts or emotions
Frequent intense or exaggerated emotional outbursts
Anger , frustration, depression , etc.
Mood incongruence
Exaggerated emotional responses
Among most of the patients that suffer from PBA, intense crying is more common than laughing, which often leads to misdiagnosis of depression.

diseases.name: Pseudocholinesterase Deficiency
diseases.description: Pseudocholinesterase (PCE) is an enzyme made in the liver and found in our blood plasma , which acts as a ghrelin regulator. Pseudocholinesterase deficiency results in the slower metabolism of medications used in anesthesia like succinylcholine, mivacurium, procaine, etc. . Normally, the anaesthetics used for medical procedures are metabolized by the body within a couple of minutes from being administered. When people who suffer from pseudocholinesterase deficiency are administered anaesthesia, their respiratory muscles relax excessively. They may not be able to move or breathe on their own for a while and may require mechanical ventilation.
symptoms: For most inviduals having pseudocholinesterase deficiency, no signs/symptoms of the condition occur until they are exposed to muscle relaxants mivacurium or succinylcholine used in anesthesia. If so, the muscle paralysis or muscle relaxation caused by such medications lasts for many hours, with the inability to breathe on the own and mechanical ventilation may be required for a while .
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals.

diseases.name: Pseudogout - Symptomsc Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Pseudogout is a medical condition that involves sudden , painful swelling and inflammation of one or more joints. The knee is commonly affected.
symptoms: Severe joint pain
Joint swelling
Buildup of fluid around the affected joint

diseases.name: Pseudomembranous Colitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Pseudomembranous colitis is a medical condition that involves the inflammation of the large intestine. It is related to antibiotic usage leading to proliferation of the bacterium called Clostridium difficile (C. diff.) in the lining of the intestines. This in turn causes the large intestine to swell.
symptoms: The symptoms of include the following:
Watery stool
Diarrhea
Cramps
Dehydration
Nausea
Loss of appetite
Tender feeling in your stomach
Bloody stool
Sepsis

There are numerous bacteria in your colon in a naturally healthy balance, but antibiotics and other medications can upset this balance. Pseudomembranous colitis occurs when certain bacteria — usually C. difficile outgrow other bacteria that normally keep them in check.
The following factors may upset the balance of the good vs harmful bacteria in the colon:
Antibiotics such as penicillin, clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, and cephalosporins.
Diseases such as Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis can increase the risk of developing Pseudomembranous Colitis.
Recent stay at a hospital

diseases.name: Pseudomonas Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pseudomonas infection is a significant health concern caused by the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa . This opportunistic pathogen is known for its resilience and ability to thrive in various environments, making it a common cause of infections, particularly in individuals with weakened immune systems. Understanding Pseudomonas infections is crucial, as they can lead to severe health complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Pseudomonas infections, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of a Pseudomonas infection can vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include:
Respiratory Infections: Cough, difficulty breathing, chest pain, and fever.
Urinary Tract Infections: Frequent urination, burning sensation during urination, and lower abdominal pain.
Skin Infections: Redness, swelling, and pus formation at the site of infection, often seen in burn wounds.
Bloodstream Infections: Fever, chills, rapid heartbeat, and confusion.

diseases.name: Pseudopregnancy (False Pregnancy) : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Pregnancy is usually an exciting time for parents who are expecting a baby. In rare cases, parents, especially women, believe they are pregnant, only to discover that their symptoms were caused not by pregnancy but entirely by other causes. It is called false pregnancy or pseudopregnancy.
symptoms: False pregnancy frequently bears a resemblance to pregnancy in every way. However, the baby is not present in a false pregnancy. In every case, women are sure that they are pregnant. The most common physical symptom of false pregnancy is a distended abdomen, similar to a baby bump. The woman’s belly can expand as it does during pregnancy. In a false pregnancy, the abdominal extension does not result from a baby. Instead, doctors believe that gas, fat, faeces, and urine buildup causes it.

The second most common physical symptom is an irregularity in a woman’s menstrual cycle. About 50 to 75 per cent of women who experience a false pregnancy describe the feeling of the baby moving. Many women also describe feeling the baby kick, even though the baby is not present. The other symptoms can be difficult to distinguish from those experienced during pregnancy. They can include the following:
Interruption of the menstrual period
Nausea and vomiting
Lactation
Weight gain
Labour pains
False labour
Increased appetite
Enlarged and tender breasts, changes in nipples, and sometimes even milk production
Swollen belly
Enlargement of the uterus
Softening of the cervix
The symptoms can last for a few weeks, nine months, or even years. A small percentage of women with false pregnancies arrive at the doctor’s office or hospital feeling labour pains.

diseases.name: Pseudotumor Cerebri - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Do you often have pain in your head starting from your eyes and then radiating towards your head, neck, shoulders, and back? Does this pain cause a whooshing sound in your head? These are a few of the obvious signs and symptoms that your body presents towards the disorder pseudotumor cerebri. Just as the name suggests, pseudotumor cerebri may have no reason for its occurrence. This is why it is also referred to as idiopathic intracranial hypertension , in which the pressure inside the brain increases for no obvious known reasons. If you are suffering from such type of pain, consult your doctor at the earliest and get yourself treated.
symptoms: The common signs and symptoms of pseudotumor cerebri include the following:
Severe headache originating at the back of the eye
The feeling of nausea vomiting and dizziness
Double vision or loss of vision
Blurred vision
Difficulty to see side objects
Having episodes of blindness that lasts for few seconds to few minutes affecting one or both the eyes
A whooshing sound echoing inside the head due to which there is an increase in heart rate and pulse rate
Radiating down towards the back of the neck, shoulder, and back
Ringing sound in the ear that is tinnitus
Vision problems like flashing
Sometimes the pain radiates to the lower back leading to pain in the lower limbs.

diseases.name: Psoriasis
diseases.description: Psoriasis is a chronic, autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the skin cell life cycle, causing cells to build up rapidly on the surface of the skin. The extra skin cells form scales and red patches that can be itchy and sometimes painful. Psoriasis tends to go through cycles, flaring for a few weeks or months, then subsiding.
symptoms: Red patches of skin covered with thick, silvery scales
Dry, cracked skin that may bleed or itch
Itching, burning, or soreness
Thickened, pitted, or ridged nails
Swollen and stiff joints (psoriatic arthritis)

diseases.name: Psoriasis In Ears - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that primarily affects the skin, leading to the rapid growth of skin cells and the formation of scales and red patches that can be itchy and sometimes painful. While psoriasis is commonly associated with areas like the elbows, knees, and scalp, it can also manifest in less typical locations, including the ears. Psoriasis in the ears can be particularly uncomfortable and may lead to complications if not properly managed. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective treatment and management.
symptoms: The symptoms of psoriasis in the ears can vary but typically include:
Red Patches: Inflamed, red areas of skin that may appear in and around the ears.
Scaling: Silvery-white scales that can flake off and may be itchy.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Discomfort in the affected areas.
Dryness: The skin in and around the ears may become dry and cracked.

diseases.name: Psoriasis On The Face - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that primarily affects the skin, leading to the rapid growth of skin cells and the formation of scales and red patches that can be itchy and sometimes painful. While psoriasis can occur anywhere on the body, psoriasis on the face presents unique challenges and considerations. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of psoriasis on the face, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective management and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of facial psoriasis can vary in severity and may include:
Red Patches: Inflamed areas of skin that may be itchy or painful.
Scales: Silvery-white scales that can flake off.
Dryness and Cracking: The skin may become dry and cracked, leading to discomfort.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Many individuals experience itching or a burning sensation in affected areas.

diseases.name: Psoriatic Arthritis
diseases.description: Psoriatic arthritis is a form of arthritis that affects some people who have psoriasis — a condition that features red patches of skin topped with silvery scales. Most people develop psoriasis first and are later diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis, but the joint problems can sometimes begin before skin patches appear.
symptoms: Swollen fingers and toes (dactylitis, 'sausage digits')
Foot pain (heel and sole)
Lower back pain
Joint stiffness and swelling
Nail changes (pitting, separation from nail bed)
Eye inflammation

diseases.name: Psychosomatic Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Psychosomatic disorder is a complex condition that intertwines the mind and body, illustrating how psychological factors can manifest as physical symptoms. This disorder is significant not only because it affects a person's quality of life but also because it challenges the traditional boundaries of medicine, emphasizing the importance of a holistic approach to health. Understanding psychosomatic disorders can lead to better management strategies, improved patient outcomes, and a greater appreciation for the mind-body connection.
symptoms: The symptoms of psychosomatic disorder can vary widely but often include:
Chronic Pain: Unexplained pain in various body parts, such as the back, neck, or joints.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Symptoms like nausea, diarrhea, or irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Headaches: Frequent tension headaches or migraines.
Cardiovascular Symptoms: Palpitations, chest pain, or shortness of breath without a clear medical cause.

diseases.name: Pubic Lice - Symptoms, risk Factors And Treatment
diseases.description: Pubic lice are about 1.8-millimeter long, lice found in the genital areas. They are different from head and body lice and look like sea crabs. Pubic lice spread from one person to another through sexual contact, but they can also get transmitted through shared towels, bedding and clothes.
symptoms: Itching is the most common sign of crab infestations which occurs about five days after the infestation. The itching is most intense during nighttime.
You get blue spots near the bites.
Dark brown or black powder-like louse droppings are present in the underwear.
You can get a mild fever .
You can get secondary infections from itch scratches.
Symptoms present in infected children include:
Eye itching
Eye irritation
Pink eye, conjunctivitis

diseases.name: Pudendal Neuralgia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pudendal neuralgia is a condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. It is characterized by chronic pain in the pelvic region, often affecting the genital area, perineum, and buttocks. This condition can be debilitating, leading to difficulties in daily activities, intimacy, and overall well-being. Understanding pudendal neuralgia is crucial for those who experience unexplained pelvic pain, as early diagnosis and treatment can lead to better outcomes.
symptoms: Pudendal neuralgia presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Chronic Pelvic Pain: A persistent, aching pain in the pelvic region that may worsen with sitting or certain activities.
Genital Pain: Discomfort or pain in the genital area, which may be sharp, burning, or throbbing.
Perineal Pain: Pain in the perineum, the area between the genitals and the anus.
Numbness or Tingling: Some individuals may experience numbness or a tingling sensation in the pelvic area.
Pain During Intercourse: Many individuals report pain during sexual activity, which can lead to emotional distress and relationship issues.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (PAP) is a rare lung disease characterized by the accumulation of surfactant proteins and lipids within the alveoli, the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs. This condition can significantly impair respiratory function, leading to various symptoms and complications. Understanding PAP is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can impact individuals' quality of life and overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of PAP can vary in severity and may include:
Shortness of Breath: Often the most prominent symptom, especially during physical activity.
Cough: A persistent cough that may produce sputum.
Fatigue: General tiredness and lack of energy.
Chest Discomfort: A feeling of tightness or pressure in the chest.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, indicating low oxygen levels.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Contusion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary contusion is a significant medical condition that involves bruising of the lung tissue, often resulting from blunt chest trauma. This injury can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding pulmonary contusion is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as it can arise from various situations, including car accidents, falls, or sports injuries. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of pulmonary contusion, providing a comprehensive overview of this important medical condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulmonary contusion can vary based on the severity of the injury. Common symptoms include:
Chest Pain: Pain at the site of injury, which may worsen with deep breathing or coughing.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of breathlessness, especially during physical activity.
Coughing: A persistent cough, which may produce blood-tinged sputum in more severe cases.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate as the body attempts to compensate for reduced lung function.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, particularly around the lips and fingertips, indicating low oxygen levels.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Edema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary edema is a serious medical condition characterized by the accumulation of fluid in the lungs, which can lead to severe breathing difficulties and other complications. This condition can arise from various underlying health issues and can significantly impact a person's quality of life. Understanding pulmonary edema is crucial for early detection and effective management, as timely intervention can prevent serious health consequences.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulmonary edema can vary in severity but often include:
Shortness of Breath: This may occur suddenly or gradually and can worsen with physical activity or when lying down.
Coughing: A persistent cough that may produce frothy or pink-tinged sputum.
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest, which may indicate an underlying heart issue.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate as the body attempts to compensate for reduced oxygen levels.
Feeling of Suffocation: A sensation of not being able to breathe adequately.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Embolism - Symptoms, Causes, Risks, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: When a blood clot blocks one of the arteries in your lung and prevents proper blood circulation, this condition is Pulmonary Embolism or PE.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of pulmonary embolism can differ from one person to the other. It mainly depends on the following factors –
The size of the blood clot
If or not you are suffering from a heart or lung disease
The portion of your lungs affected

Chest pain – You feel heaviness in your lungs that might resemble a heart attack. There might be shooting pain in your chest, especially on taking deep breaths. The situation might worsen when you cough and lean on something.
Shortness of breath – You might feel that you are gasping for air all of a sudden. It can get worse after doing a strenuous activity.
Cough – You might see blood-tinged sputum after coughing.
Excessive sweating
Irregular or fast heartbeat
Dizziness
Fever
Swelling in legs and calf
Pain in the legs
Discolored skin or bluish skin (cyanosis)
Chest Pain
Hemoptysis

The signs and symptoms of PE can appear all of a sudden. Therefore, it is a medical emergency. Go to your doctor immediately if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, bloody sputum with the cough.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Heart Disease - Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Pulmonary heart disease or Cor pulmonale is the enlargement and failure of the right ventricle of the heart due to increased vascular resistance or pulmonary hypertension. Pulmonary heart disease causes the right ventricle to enlarge and pump blood less effectively than normal, due to which the ventricle is then pushed to its limit and ultimately fails. Pulmonary heart disease is a complication of lung conditions like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and pulmonary embolism (PE).
symptoms: The early symptoms may go unnoticed, as they are quite similar to the feeling we get after hard work such as shortness of breath, tiredness, an increased heart rate etc. Over the time, these symptoms get worse. Visit your doctor immediately, if you have:
Swelling in the legs or feet
Shortness of breath
Dizziness
Wheezing and coughing
Excessive fatigue
Enlarged neck veins
Chest pain
Abdominal swelling
Cyanosis (bluish or purplish colour on the skin, lips or gums)

Pulmonary heart disease can be chronic or acute. It is usually caused by a lung disease. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is the most common cause for pulmonary heart disease, however there are other factors also. The condition becomes more severe if you have a pre-existing heart disease like arrhythmia (irregular heartbeat) or a history of heart attack.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Hypoplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary hypoplasia is a serious medical condition characterized by the underdevelopment of the lungs. This condition can significantly impact a person's ability to breathe and can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and managed appropriately. Understanding pulmonary hypoplasia is crucial for early detection and intervention, which can improve outcomes for affected individuals. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding pulmonary hypoplasia.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulmonary hypoplasia can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Difficulty Breathing: Infants may exhibit rapid or labored breathing, often requiring immediate medical attention.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially around the lips and fingertips, indicating low oxygen levels.
Poor Feeding: Infants may struggle to feed due to respiratory distress.
Recurrent Respiratory Infections: Children with pulmonary hypoplasia may be more susceptible to lung infections.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Nodules - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary nodules are small, round growths in the lungs that can be detected through imaging tests such as X-rays or CT scans. While they are often benign (non-cancerous), their presence can be a source of concern for both patients and healthcare providers. Understanding pulmonary nodules is crucial, as they can sometimes indicate more serious conditions, including lung cancer. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pulmonary nodules, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Most pulmonary nodules do not cause symptoms and are often discovered incidentally. However, some individuals may experience:
Cough: A persistent cough that does not go away.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded.
Wheezing: A whistling sound when breathing.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Sarcoidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulmonary sarcoidosis is a complex inflammatory disease that primarily affects the lungs but can also impact other organs in the body. It is characterized by the formation of tiny clumps of inflammatory cells, known as granulomas, which can disrupt normal lung function. Understanding pulmonary sarcoidosis is crucial, as it can lead to significant health complications if not diagnosed and managed appropriately. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of pulmonary sarcoidosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulmonary sarcoidosis can vary widely among individuals. Some may experience mild symptoms, while others may have more severe manifestations. Common symptoms include:
Cough: A persistent dry cough is often one of the first signs.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of breathlessness, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Fever: Low-grade fever may occur in some cases.
Night Sweats: Excessive sweating during the night.

diseases.name: Pulmonary Valve Disease - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The human heart is divided into four chambers. These are two atria and two ventricles. The smooth functioning of the atria and ventricles depends on valves that prevent the backflow of blood in the heart. These valves work like a one-way blood inlet at one side of the ventricle and a one-way outlet for blood on the other side of the ventricle. The four main valves in the human heart are, the mitral valve, tricuspid valve, aortic valve, and pulmonary valve. Any abnormal functioning of these valves could cause issues in the human circulatory system.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulmonary valve diseases vary depending on the severity of the obstruction in the valve. Persons with mild pulmonary valve diseases may not even have any symptoms. The symptoms might indicate issues in the regular functioning of the pulmonary valve includes:
Excessive fatigue with little physical activity
Chest pain
A turbulent flow of blood causes an abnormal whooshing sound that is heard using a stethoscope. It is called a heart murmur.
Shortness of breath especially using exertion or physical activity.
Sudden fainting or loss of consciousness

diseases.name: Pulmonary Valve Stenosis
diseases.description: The pulmonary valve is situated between the lower right heart chamber (right ventricle) and the pulmonary arteria’s Pulmonary valve stenosis is a medical condition wherein there is a narrowing of the pulmonary valve. This, in turn, reduces the blood flow. Pulmonary valve stenosis is caused by several factors such as genetic history, rheumatic fever, etc.
symptoms: The following are the symptoms of pulmonary valve stenosis :
Chest pain
A murmur in the heart
Fainting
Nausea
Fatigue
Trouble breathing
Prominent jugular vein
There are a few factors that are known to cause pulmonary valve stenosis . These are:
Genetic history of pulmonary valve stenosis
Other heart abnormalities
Rheumatic fever and carcinoid syndrome
Pulmonary valve replacement
Also Read About: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement

diseases.name: Pulpitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulpitis is a dental condition that affects the pulp, the innermost part of a tooth, which contains nerves and blood vessels. This condition is significant because it can lead to severe pain, infection, and even tooth loss if not treated promptly. Understanding pulpitis is crucial for maintaining oral health and preventing complications that can arise from untreated dental issues. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of pulpitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of pulpitis can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Toothache: A persistent, throbbing pain that may worsen with temperature changes or pressure.
Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to hot or cold foods and beverages.
Swelling: Swelling in the gums surrounding the affected tooth.
Discoloration: Darkening of the tooth, indicating possible necrosis of the pulp.
Foul Taste: A bad taste in the mouth due to infection.

diseases.name: Pulsatile Tinnitus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pulsatile tinnitus is a unique form of tinnitus characterized by a rhythmic sound that often coincides with the heartbeat. Unlike the more common type of tinnitus, which presents as a constant ringing or buzzing in the ears, pulsatile tinnitus is typically perceived as a pulsing sound. This condition can be distressing and may indicate underlying health issues, making it essential for individuals experiencing these symptoms to seek medical evaluation. Understanding pulsatile tinnitus is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers who aim to offer effective management strategies.
symptoms: The primary symptom of pulsatile tinnitus is the perception of rhythmic sounds that align with the heartbeat. Other associated symptoms may include:
A feeling of fullness in the ear
Hearing loss
Dizziness or balance issues
Headaches

diseases.name: Puppp Rash - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Puppp Rash, also known as Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy, is a common skin condition that affects pregnant women, particularly during the third trimester. This condition can cause significant discomfort and distress, making it essential for expectant mothers to understand its nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options. While Puppp Rash is not harmful to the baby, it can lead to considerable itching and skin irritation for the mother. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Puppp Rash, helping readers recognize its signs and seek appropriate care.
symptoms: Puppp Rash is characterized by several distinct symptoms, including:
Itchy Red Bumps: The rash typically begins as small, itchy red bumps that can develop into larger hives.
Plaques: These bumps may merge to form raised plaques on the skin.
Location: The rash usually starts on the abdomen and can spread to the thighs, buttocks, and sometimes the arms and legs.
Discomfort: Intense itching can lead to significant discomfort and may interfere with sleep.

diseases.name: Pustular Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pustular psoriasis is a chronic skin condition characterized by the presence of pus-filled blisters (pustules) on the skin. This form of psoriasis can be both physically and emotionally distressing, significantly impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding pustular psoriasis is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of pustular psoriasis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Pustular psoriasis presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Pustules: Small, white, pus-filled blisters that can be painful and itchy.
Red Skin: Areas surrounding the pustules may appear red and inflamed.
Scaling: The skin may become scaly as pustules dry out and peel.
Fever and Chills: In some cases, individuals may experience systemic symptoms like fever, chills, or fatigue, especially during acute flare-ups.

diseases.name: Pyelectasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pyelectasis is a medical condition characterized by the dilation of the renal pelvis, the area of the kidney that collects urine before it moves to the ureter. While it may sound alarming, pyelectasis is often a benign finding, particularly in fetuses and infants. However, its significance lies in the potential underlying causes that may require medical attention. Understanding pyelectasis is crucial for early detection and management, ensuring that any serious conditions are addressed promptly.
symptoms: Pyelectasis may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in mild cases. However, some individuals may experience:
Flank Pain: Discomfort or pain in the side or back, often associated with kidney issues.
Urinary Changes: Increased frequency of urination, urgency, or changes in urine color.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur if there is significant obstruction or infection.

diseases.name: Pyoderma Gangrenosum - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a rare condition in which large, painful ulcers develop on your skin, most often on your legs. It affects people between age 20 to 50. The cause is unknown but it is believed to be an autoimmune disease.
symptoms: Pyoderma gangrenosum mostly appears on the skin of the legs , ankles, neck or genitals. Usually, pyoderma gangrenosum starts with a small, red bump on the skin, which may resemble a spider bite. Often, they swell into open sores with a distinct blue or violet border. Within days, the bumps can develop into large, painful open sores. They are also characterized by by pathergy, the appearance of new lesions after local trauma .

Atypical or bullous pyoderma gangrenosum usually occurs as a superficial blister, and it appears on the hand and face. Vegetative Pyoderma gangrenosum ulcer appears as an ulcer, but it is painless. People who suffer from pyoderma gangrenosum may also experience joint pain, fever , localized tenderness, and tiredness.

diseases.name: Pyogenic Granuloma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pyogenic granuloma is a benign vascular lesion that often appears as a small, red bump on the skin or mucous membranes. While it is not cancerous, its rapid growth and distinctive appearance can cause concern for patients and healthcare providers alike. Understanding pyogenic granuloma is essential for timely diagnosis and effective management, as it can sometimes be mistaken for more serious conditions. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of pyogenic granuloma, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The primary symptom of pyogenic granuloma is the appearance of a small, red, raised lesion. Other characteristics include:
Size: Typically ranges from a few millimeters to a couple of centimeters in diameter.
Color: Bright red or purple due to the high vascularity of the lesion.
Texture: Smooth or lobulated surface, often with a shiny appearance.
Bleeding: The lesion may bleed easily, especially if bumped or irritated.

diseases.name: Pyomyositis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pyomyositis is a rare but significant condition characterized by the infection of skeletal muscles, leading to the formation of pus within the muscle tissue. This condition can result in severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding pyomyositis is crucial for both healthcare professionals and the general public, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding pyomyositis.
symptoms: The symptoms of pyomyositis can vary depending on the severity of the infection and the muscle group involved. Common symptoms include:
Localized Pain: Affected muscles may be painful, tender, and swollen.
Fever: Patients often experience a fever, which may be accompanied by chills.
Swelling and Redness: The skin over the infected muscle may appear red and swollen.
Limited Range of Motion: Patients may have difficulty moving the affected limb due to pain and swelling.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness and malaise are common.

diseases.name: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency (PKD) is a rare genetic disorder that affects red blood cells, leading to hemolytic anemia. This condition is significant because it can cause a range of health issues, from mild fatigue to severe complications that may require medical intervention. Understanding PKD is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Fatigue: Due to anemia, individuals often experience extreme tiredness and weakness.
Pallor: A noticeable paleness of the skin can occur as a result of reduced red blood cell count.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes may develop due to the breakdown of red blood cells.
Dark Urine: Hemoglobin released from destroyed red blood cells can lead to dark-colored urine.
Splenomegaly: An enlarged spleen may occur as the organ works harder to filter out damaged red blood cells.
Shortness of Breath: Individuals may experience difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.

diseases.name: Pyuria - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pyuria is a medical condition characterized by the presence of pus in the urine, which typically indicates an underlying infection or inflammation in the urinary tract. This condition is significant because it can be a symptom of various urinary tract disorders, including urinary tract infections (UTIs), kidney infections, and other serious health issues. Recognizing and understanding pyuria is crucial for timely diagnosis and treatment, which can prevent complications and promote better health outcomes.
symptoms: Cloudy Urine: The presence of pus can make urine appear cloudy or murky.
Foul-Smelling Urine: Infections often cause urine to have a strong, unpleasant odor.
Increased Urination: Individuals may experience a frequent urge to urinate, often with little urine produced.
Burning Sensation: A burning sensation during urination is a common symptom associated with urinary tract infections.
Lower Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen may occur, particularly if there is an infection.
Fever and Chills: In cases of severe infection, systemic symptoms such as fever and chills may be present.

diseases.name: Q Fever
diseases.description: Q fever is a bacterial infection caused by Coxiella burnetii, often linked to exposure to infected livestock or contaminated animal products. It can present as an acute flu-like illness or, in some people, progress to chronic complications.
symptoms: High fever and chills
Headache and muscle pain
Fatigue and malaise
Dry cough or chest discomfort
Nausea or abdominal pain

diseases.name: Quadrantanopia
diseases.description: Quadrantanopia is a visual field defect where vision is lost in one quarter of the field of view, typically due to damage in the optic pathways of the brain.
symptoms: Loss of vision in one visual quadrant
Difficulty reading or navigating spaces
Frequent bumping into objects on one side
Visual scanning difficulties

diseases.name: Rabies
diseases.description: Rabies is a viral disease that affects the central nervous system. It is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, but can be prevented with prompt post-exposure treatment.
symptoms: Fever and pain at bite site
Tingling or burning near the wound
Anxiety or agitation
Hydrophobia (fear of water)
Paralysis and coma in later stages

diseases.name: Rabies – Introduction, Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Immediately linked to the bite or scratch of a stray animal and all those injections in the stomach, Rabies is a serious viral infection. Generally, by the time the symptoms manifest, it is too late to save the infected individual. However, an individual who may have been exposed to rabies can generally be treated effectively if he/she seek help immediately.
symptoms: The symptoms and signs of rabies do not occur till late stages of the disease, by which time the virus has spread to the brain causing encephalitis , and death soon after. Rabies has an incubation period, which means that it is dormant in the person’s body for some days before the symptoms and signs appear. The early symptoms are headache , sore throat, fever and tingling at the spot where the bite is. Symptoms like excessive salivation, difficulty in swallowing, fear of water due to swallowing difficulty, anxiety, confusion, insomnia and even partial paralysis and sometimes coma indicate rabies. The person is intolerant to sound, light and even a cold current of air. Fear of air (aerophobia) is seen.

diseases.name: Radial Tunnel Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Radial Tunnel Syndrome (RTS) is a condition that affects the radial nerve, which runs down the arm and controls movement and sensation in the forearm and hand. This syndrome is significant because it can lead to pain, weakness, and functional limitations in the affected arm, impacting daily activities and quality of life. Understanding RTS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to regain their normal function and alleviate discomfort.
symptoms: The symptoms of Radial Tunnel Syndrome can vary in intensity and may include:
Pain: A dull ache or sharp pain in the outer part of the elbow, which may radiate down the forearm.
Weakness: Difficulty in extending the wrist or fingers, leading to a weakened grip.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations of numbness or tingling in the back of the hand and fingers.
Tenderness: Tenderness in the area around the elbow, particularly when pressure is applied.

diseases.name: Radiation Burns - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Radiation burns are a significant medical concern that can arise from exposure to various forms of radiation, including ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun, ionizing radiation from medical treatments, and environmental sources. These burns can lead to serious health complications, affecting the skin and underlying tissues. Understanding radiation burns is crucial for prevention, early detection, and effective treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of radiation burns, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of radiation burns can vary based on the severity of the burn and the type of radiation involved. Common symptoms include:
Redness and Inflammation: The affected area may appear red and swollen.
Pain and Tenderness: Patients often experience discomfort or pain in the burned area.
Blistering: Severe burns may lead to the formation of blisters filled with fluid.
Peeling Skin: As the burn heals, the skin may begin to peel.
Itching: The healing process can cause itching in the affected area.

diseases.name: Radiation Enteritis - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Radiation therapy is used widely to treat cancer, but it has side effects such as Radiation enteritis . Radiation enteritis is usually temporary and the inflammation usually subsides eventually, after treatment ends
symptoms: Symptoms can vary depending on the portion of the bowel that has undergone radiation. These may occur during or shortly after or long after radiation treatment. Some of the symptoms are:
Rectal bloating or passing mucus
Watery stools or diarrhea
Urge to defecate every now and then
Rectal pain, especially with intestinal motions
Appetite loss
Nausea and spasm of the abdomen
Symptoms can be more severe if:
You receive chemotherapy in conjunction with radiotherapy.
You get higher radiation doses.
A wider area of your gut is undergoing radition.
Most of the time, these symptoms improve within 2 to 3 months following the end of the radiation treatment. However, the disease may develop months or years after radiation therapy.

diseases.name: Radiation Sickness - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Radiation sickness is an illness resulting from a high exposure to ionizing radiation.
symptoms: Symptoms of this illness mostly vary depending on the amount of radiation you’ve absorbed in your body. The amount of radiation you absorb depends on the dose of the radiation energy, the extent of your susceptibilities and the distance between the patient and the origin of radiation.
Initial symptoms

There are a few significant early manifestations of radiation sickness , usually vomiting . The duration between exposure and the time of developing these symptoms indicates the extent of radiation absorbed .
After the initial symptoms are over, an individual having radiation sickness may have no noticeable illness for a short period of time.
Other symptoms will follow and these include:
Severe headache
Fever
Infections
Nausea and vomiting
Low blood pressure
Weakness and exhaustion
Hair loss
Diarrhea
Vomit with blood
Blood in stools

diseases.name: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome (RHS) - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Ramsay Hunt syndrome or herpes zoster oticus happens when a shingles outbreak affects your facial nerve near one of the ears. The virus that causes chickenpox causes Ramsay Hunt syndrome as well. The virus that still lives in your nerves after chickenpox clears up reactivates again.
symptoms: The two main symptoms of Ramsay Hunt syndrome are:
Painful red rash with fluid-filled blisters in, on, and around one of the ears
Facial paralysis or weakness on the same side as the affected ear
Other symptoms include :
Hearing loss
Ringing sound in your ear
Difficulty closing your eyes
Vertigo
A change in taste or smell
Feeling thirsty

diseases.name: Ranula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ranula is a type of cyst that forms in the mouth, specifically in the floor of the mouth, and is often associated with the sublingual salivary glands. While it is generally benign, its presence can lead to discomfort and complications if not addressed. Understanding ranula is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of ranula can vary depending on the size and location of the cyst. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: A noticeable swelling or lump under the tongue or in the floor of the mouth.
Discomfort: Mild to moderate discomfort, especially when eating or speaking.
Difficulty Swallowing: Larger ranulas may cause difficulty in swallowing or speaking.
Change in Taste: Some individuals may experience changes in taste sensation.

diseases.name: Rathke Cleft Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rathke Cleft Cyst (RCC) is a benign, fluid-filled sac that forms in the pituitary gland, specifically in the region known as Rathke's pouch. While these cysts are generally asymptomatic and often discovered incidentally during imaging studies for unrelated issues, they can sometimes lead to significant health problems if they grow large enough to exert pressure on surrounding structures. Understanding Rathke Cleft Cysts is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, especially for those who may experience symptoms.
symptoms: Rathke Cleft Cysts are often asymptomatic, but when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Headaches: Persistent or severe headaches that do not respond to typical pain relief methods.
Vision Problems: Blurred or double vision, or loss of peripheral vision, due to pressure on the optic nerves.
Hormonal Imbalances: Symptoms related to hormonal deficiencies, such as fatigue, weight changes, or menstrual irregularities.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may arise if the cyst exerts pressure on surrounding structures.

diseases.name: Raynaud's Disease (Primary Raynaud's)
diseases.description: Raynaud's disease (primary Raynaud's phenomenon) refers to episodes of reduced blood flow to the fingers (and sometimes toes, ears, nose, and lips) triggered by cold or emotional stress. Unlike secondary Raynaud's (which is associated with another disease), primary Raynaud's occurs without an underlying condition. It is generally less severe than secondary forms.
symptoms: Fingers (and possibly toes) turning white or blue in response to cold or stress
Affected areas turning red when blood flow returns
Numbness, tingling, or stinging pain during episodes
Color changes that occur in phases: white → blue → red
Episodes lasting minutes to hours

diseases.name: Raynaud's Phenomenon
diseases.description: Raynaud's phenomenon is a condition that causes some areas of the body — such as fingers and toes — to feel numb and cold in response to cold temperatures or stress. In Raynaud's disease, smaller arteries that supply blood to the skin narrow, limiting blood flow to affected areas. It can be primary (Raynaud's disease) or secondary to another condition.
symptoms: Cold fingers or toes
Color changes in skin (white, blue, red) in response to cold or stress
Numbness, prickling, or stinging pain when warming up or stress relief

diseases.name: Reactive Airway Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Reactive Airway Disease (RAD) is a term often used to describe a condition characterized by increased sensitivity of the airways to various stimuli, leading to symptoms similar to asthma. It is significant because it affects a substantial number of individuals, particularly children, and can lead to chronic respiratory issues if not properly managed. Understanding RAD is crucial for effective treatment and prevention, as it can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Reactive Airway Disease include:
Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound during breathing, particularly when exhaling.
Coughing: Persistent cough, especially at night or after physical activity.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or a feeling of tightness in the chest.
Chest Tightness: A sensation of pressure or constriction in the chest area.

diseases.name: Reactive Arthritis
diseases.description: Reactive arthritis is joint pain and swelling triggered by an infection in another part of the body, most often the intestines, genitals, or urinary tract. The condition most commonly targets the knees and the joints of the ankles and feet. It is also known as Reiter's syndrome.
symptoms: Joint pain and swelling
Eye inflammation (conjunctivitis)
Urinary problems
Skin rash (especially on palms and soles)
Mouth sores
Heel pain

diseases.name: Reactive Attachment Disorder - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Reactive attachment disorder (RAD) is when an baby or a child fails to form a secure attachment with their primary caretaker. As a result, these children face problems in managing emotions and find establishing and maintaining relationships difficult. Children between 9 months to 5 years of age who have experienced neglect or abuse are more likely to develop this disorder.
symptoms: Some of the prevalent symptoms of reactive attachment disorder are,
The child fails to show a range of emotions
The child doesn’t seek attention when in discomfort/distressed
The child avoids eye contact or physical touch of people, especially caregivers
The child expresses unusual anger, throws tantrums, indulges in arguments, acts disobediently, etc.
The child shows preference and affection to strangers and avoids caregiver/family members
The child avoids interactive games like peekaboo
The child is frequently seen as sad or seems depressed
The child withdraws from social situations

diseases.name: Rebound Headaches - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rebound headaches, also known as medication-overuse headaches, are a prevalent yet often misunderstood condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. These headaches occur when pain relief medications are used too frequently, leading to a cycle of pain and dependence on medication. Understanding rebound headaches is crucial for effective management and prevention, as they can exacerbate existing headache disorders and lead to chronic pain. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of rebound headaches, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Rebound headaches can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Dull, persistent pain: Often described as a constant ache that can vary in intensity.
Worsening pain: The headache may intensify as the effects of the medication wear off.
Nausea and vomiting: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal symptoms alongside their headaches.
Sensitivity to light and sound: Increased sensitivity can accompany the headache, similar to migraine symptoms.
Fatigue: Chronic pain can lead to feelings of exhaustion and decreased energy levels.

diseases.name: Rectal Cancer - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Rectal cancer is a type of cancer in which malignant (cancerous) cells develop in the rectal tissues. The large intestine, also known as the large bowel, comprises the rectum and the colon. The rectum is the big bowel’s final six inches, connecting the colon to the anus. It develops when cells in the rectum change and proliferate uncontrollably. The illness can also occur when polyps on the inner wall of the rectum expand and become cancerous. Cancer inside the rectum and cancer inside the colon are often referred to together as “ colorectal cancer .
symptoms: In the early stages, there may be no apparent symptoms. Symptoms of the illness include changes in bowel habits, rectal bleeding , and thin, ribbon-like feces. Other symptoms are as follows:
Fatigue
Loss of weight
Blood traces in the feces
Constipation or diarrhea
Pain in the abdomen
Bloating

diseases.name: Rectovaginal Fistula - Symptoms, Causes and Treatments
diseases.description: When an abnormal connection develops between the rectum and the vagina of a woman, it is termed a rectovaginal fistula. While rectovaginal fistula is not a life-threatening condition, it causes discomfort to the patient.
symptoms: Emission of gas or stool from the vaginal opening
Foul smell emitting from the normal vaginal discharge
Frequent repetition of infections in the vaginal or urinary tract
Feeling of immense pain during sexual intercourse
Abnormal pain persisting in the vagina and the space between the vagina and anus

diseases.name: Rectus Sheath Hematoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rectus sheath hematoma (RSH) is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of blood within the rectus sheath, a fibrous structure that encases the rectus abdominis muscle in the abdominal wall. This condition can arise from various causes, including trauma, anticoagulant therapy, or spontaneous bleeding. Understanding RSH is crucial, as it can lead to significant complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of rectus sheath hematoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Abdominal Pain: The most common symptom, often localized to the area of the hematoma.
Swelling or Mass: A palpable mass may be felt in the abdominal wall.
Bruising: Discoloration of the skin over the hematoma may occur.
Nausea or Vomiting: Some patients may experience gastrointestinal symptoms.
Fever: In cases where infection is present, fever may be a symptom.

diseases.name: Recurrent Breast Cancer - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Breast cancer that returns after treatments is known as recurrent breast cancer. Although the initial treatment is intended to eliminate all cancer cells, some may have evaded treatment and survived. These cancer cells multiply undetected, leading to recurrent breast cancer.

diseases.name: Red Blood Cell Count High (RBC): Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Red blood cells (RBCs) are the bright, red-colored cells of the blood. They are also called erythrocytes.
symptoms: Polycythemia does not always show symptoms, some people show no symptoms at all. Mostly, polycythemia itself is a symptom of an underlying disease. However, some of the most common symptoms of the condition are:
Headaches
Tiredness
Blurry vision
Shortness of breath
Sleep disorders
Itchy skin
Tingling and/or numbness
Joint pain
Nosebleeds
At times, people with high red blood cell count do not develop any symptoms at all.

diseases.name: Refeeding Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Refeeding Syndrome is a potentially life-threatening condition that can occur when feeding is restarted in individuals who have been malnourished or in a state of starvation. This syndrome is significant because it can lead to severe metabolic disturbances, including electrolyte imbalances, which can have serious consequences if not recognized and managed promptly. Understanding Refeeding Syndrome is crucial for healthcare providers, caregivers, and patients alike, as it emphasizes the importance of careful nutritional management in vulnerable populations.
symptoms: The symptoms of Refeeding Syndrome can vary but often include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Muscle Weakness: Difficulty in performing physical tasks due to muscle fatigue.
Confusion or Delirium: Changes in mental status, including confusion or altered consciousness.
Seizures: In severe cases, electrolyte imbalances can lead to seizures.
Cardiac Arrhythmias: Irregular heartbeats due to electrolyte disturbances.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may arise as the body adjusts to refeeding.

diseases.name: Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy (RSD): Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment
diseases.description: Imagine experiencing sharp pain while performing daily activities like showering or wearing clothes. We may wince at the thought of it, but it could be a sign of a condition known as Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy Syndrome (RSD).
symptoms: When you have RSD, your symptoms can take time to manifest. Pain may progressively worsen. At first, you might not be aware that your discomfort is abnormal. But RSD most frequently appears in the arm, shoulder, leg, or hip. Usually, the pain radiates from the place of your injury. In some circumstances, symptoms may even spread to other body areas.

RSD may also impact your immune system, leading to redness, inflammation, and warm skin near the injury. When you have RSD, your pain is typically intense and ongoing. Patients describe the RSD pain as burning, aching, deep and throbbing. If you have RSD, the actions that don’t bother you otherwise, like taking a shower or wearing clothes, may cause intense pain.
changes in your skin’s texture or hair and nail growth
excessive sweating in specific body parts
muscles that are weak and spasm frequently
rigid joints
difficulty moving the affected area
changes in skin colour. It may turn into a white, red, or blue

diseases.name: Refsum Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Refsumm Disease is a rare genetic disorder that affects the metabolism of certain fats in the body, leading to a buildup of phytanic acid. This accumulation can cause a range of neurological and physical symptoms, significantly impacting the quality of life for those affected. Understanding Refsum Disease is crucial not only for patients and their families but also for healthcare providers who may encounter this condition in their practice. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Refsum Disease, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Refsumm Disease can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Neurological Symptoms: These may include peripheral neuropathy, ataxia (loss of coordination), and vision problems, such as retinitis pigmentosa.
Cardiac Symptoms: Some individuals may experience arrhythmias or other heart-related issues.
Skeletal Symptoms: Bone abnormalities, such as shortening of the bones in the hands and feet, may occur.
Skin Symptoms: Some patients develop ichthyosis, a condition characterized by dry, scaly skin.

diseases.name: Reinkes Edema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Reinke's edema is a medical condition that affects the vocal cords, leading to significant changes in voice quality and function. This condition is characterized by the accumulation of fluid in the Reinke's space, a layer of the vocal cords. Understanding Reinke's edema is crucial for individuals who rely on their voice for professional or personal reasons, as it can impact communication and overall quality of life. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Reinke's edema.
symptoms: The symptoms of Reinke's edema can vary in severity but typically include:
Hoarseness: A raspy or strained voice is one of the most common symptoms.
Lower Pitch: The voice may sound deeper than usual.
Vocal Fatigue: Individuals may experience tiredness or strain when speaking.
Difficulty Projecting Voice: It may become challenging to speak loudly or clearly.
Throat Discomfort: Some individuals report a sensation of fullness or discomfort in the throat.

diseases.name: Reiters Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Reiter's Syndrome, also known as reactive arthritis, is a rare inflammatory condition that affects the joints, eyes, and urinary tract. Although its exact cause is not fully understood, it is often triggered by infections in other parts of the body. This article provides an in-depth look at Reiter's Syndrome, explaining its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, and more. Designed for a general audience with minimal medical knowledge, this guide aims to provide comprehensive and easily understandable information for anyone seeking to understand the condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of Reiter's Syndrome can vary in severity and may affect different parts of the body. The classic symptoms include:
Joint pain and inflammation: The most common symptom is arthritis, which often affects the knees, ankles, and feet. Joint swelling, pain, and stiffness are typical signs.
Urethritis: Inflammation of the urethra, leading to painful urination, discharge, and frequent need to urinate.
Conjunctivitis: Inflammation of the eyes, causing redness, irritation, and discharge.
Skin lesions: Some individuals develop rashes or sores on the skin, especially on the soles of the feet or palms of the hands.
In more severe cases, Reiter's Syndrome can also lead to complications such as inflammation in the tendons (tendinitis), the lower back (spondylitis), and the heart (aortic insufficiency).

diseases.name: Relapsing Polychondritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Relapsing Polychondritis (RP) is a rare autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent inflammation of cartilage and other connective tissues. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to pain, discomfort, and potential complications if not managed properly. Understanding RP is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can help mitigate its effects and improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Relapsing Polychondritis can vary widely among individuals and may include:
Ear Pain and Inflammation: One of the hallmark symptoms, often presenting as redness and swelling of the ear cartilage.
Nasal Cartilage Inflammation: This can lead to a "saddle nose" deformity due to the collapse of the nasal bridge.
Joint Pain: Inflammation of joints can cause pain and swelling, resembling arthritis.
Respiratory Issues: Inflammation of the trachea and bronchi can lead to breathing difficulties.
Skin Rashes: Some patients may develop rashes or skin lesions.
Fatigue and Fever: General malaise, fatigue, and low-grade fever may accompany flare-ups.

diseases.name: Renal Agenesis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal agenesis is a medical condition characterized by the absence of one or both kidneys at birth. This congenital anomaly can have significant implications for an individual's health and quality of life. Understanding renal agenesis is crucial for early diagnosis, management, and support for affected individuals and their families. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions related to renal agenesis.
symptoms: The symptoms of renal agenesis can vary significantly depending on whether one or both kidneys are absent:
Unilateral Renal Agenesis: Many individuals may be asymptomatic and lead normal lives. However, some may experience: High blood pressure Urinary tract infections Kidney stones
High blood pressure
Urinary tract infections
Kidney stones

Bilateral Renal Agenesis: This condition is more severe and typically presents with: Oligohydramnios (low amniotic fluid) during pregnancy Respiratory distress in newborns Abnormal facial features (part of Potter's sequence) Inability to produce urine, leading to severe complications shortly after birth
Oligohydramnios (low amniotic fluid) during pregnancy
Respiratory distress in newborns
Abnormal facial features (part of Potter's sequence)
Inability to produce urine, leading to severe complications shortly after birth

diseases.name: Renal Angiomyolipoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal Angiomyolipoma (AML) is a benign tumor that primarily affects the kidneys. Although it is non-cancerous, its presence can lead to significant health issues, including kidney damage and bleeding. Understanding renal angiomyolipoma is crucial for early detection and management, as it can impact kidney function and overall health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of renal angiomyolipoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many individuals with renal angiomyolipoma may not experience any symptoms, especially if the tumor is small. However, as the tumor grows, it can lead to various symptoms, including:
Flank Pain: Discomfort or pain in the side or back, often due to the tumor's size or pressure on surrounding tissues.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which can be a sign of bleeding from the tumor.
Palpable Mass: In some cases, a large tumor may be felt as a lump in the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur if the tumor causes kidney dysfunction or obstruction.

diseases.name: Renal Artery Stenosis - Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Renal artery stenosis narrows one or more blood-carrying arteries to your kidneys. Normal quantities of blood that are rich in oxygen cannot reach your kidneys due to this artery narrowing.
symptoms: Unexpectedly high blood pressure that develops without warning
Difficulty controlling high blood pressure
When blood flows through a narrowed artery, your doctor will hear a whooshing sound using a stethoscope positioned over your kidneys.
Abnormally high urine protein levels or other indications of abnormal function of the kidneys
Worsening renal function with high blood pressure
Fluid excess and swelling of tissue in your body
Heart failure resistant to treatment

diseases.name: Renal Cell Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Renal cell cancer is the most common type of kidney cancer in adults, developing in the tiny filtering units of the kidney. Because its early symptoms are often subtle or mistaken for other conditions, it may go unnoticed until later stages. This guide offers clear and trustworthy information about renal cell cancer—its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what patients and families can expect. With patient-friendly language and practical insights, our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and confident as you navigate this condition.
symptoms: In its earliest stages, renal cell cancer often does not cause any symptoms. This is why many tumors are found by chance. When symptoms do appear, they can be vague and are often a sign of a larger or more advanced tumor.
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Unexplained Fever: A persistent, unexplained fever that comes and goes.
Extreme Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
Anemia: A low red blood cell count, which can also cause fatigue and weakness.
Leg Swelling or Bone Pain: If the cancer has spread to other parts of the body.
If you have any of these persistent symptoms, especially blood in the urine, it is crucial to see a doctor for a proper evaluation. Early diagnosis is the key to a better outcome.

diseases.name: Renal Colic - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal colic is a term that describes the intense pain caused by kidney stones as they move through the urinary tract. This condition is significant not only due to the severe discomfort it causes but also because it can lead to complications if not properly managed. Understanding renal colic is essential for anyone who may be at risk, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Severe Pain: Sudden onset of intense pain in the back, side, or lower abdomen.
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate to the groin or inner thigh.
Nausea and Vomiting: Often accompanies the pain.
Changes in Urination: Increased frequency, urgency, or pain during urination.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine may occur.

diseases.name: Renal Oncocytoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal oncocytoma is a rare type of kidney tumor that arises from the cells of the renal tubules. While it is generally considered benign, its presence can lead to significant health concerns if not properly diagnosed and managed. Understanding renal oncocytoma is crucial for early detection and effective treatment, as it can mimic more aggressive forms of kidney cancer. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of renal oncocytoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Renal oncocytomas are often asymptomatic in their early stages. However, as they grow, they may present with the following symptoms:
Flank Pain: Discomfort or pain in the side or back, which may be persistent or intermittent.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which can be visible or detected through laboratory tests.
Abdominal Mass: A palpable mass in the abdomen may be felt during a physical examination.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss may occur in some patients.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness or weakness.

diseases.name: Renal Osteodystrophy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal osteodystrophy is a significant medical condition that affects individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD). It is characterized by bone abnormalities resulting from imbalances in calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D metabolism due to impaired kidney function. As the kidneys fail to adequately filter waste and maintain mineral balance, patients may experience weakened bones, increased risk of fractures, and other complications. Understanding renal osteodystrophy is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and management can significantly improve quality of life and reduce the risk of severe complications.
symptoms: Patients with renal osteodystrophy may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Bone Pain: Persistent pain in the bones, particularly in the lower back, hips, and legs.
Fractures: Increased susceptibility to fractures due to weakened bones.
