Muscle Weakness: Generalized weakness and fatigue.
Joint Pain: Discomfort in the joints, which may be mistaken for arthritis.
Deformities: Changes in bone structure, leading to deformities in severe cases.

diseases.name: Renal Papillary Necrosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Renal Papillary Necrosis (RPN) is a medical condition that affects the kidneys, specifically the renal papillae, which are the tips of the renal pyramids where urine is collected before it moves to the bladder. This condition is significant because it can lead to serious complications, including kidney failure, if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding RPN is crucial for early detection and management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Renal Papillary Necrosis can vary, but common signs include:
Flank Pain: Pain in the side or back, often severe.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which may appear pink or red.
Dysuria: Painful urination or difficulty urinating.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little output.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to kidney dysfunction.

diseases.name: Repetitive Strain Injury - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) is a term that encompasses a range of conditions resulting from repetitive motion or overuse of specific body parts, particularly the muscles, tendons, and nerves. As our world becomes increasingly digital, the prevalence of RSI has surged, affecting millions of individuals engaged in activities such as typing, playing musical instruments, or performing manual labor. Understanding RSI is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for employers, healthcare providers, and anyone involved in physical activities. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of RSI, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of RSI can vary depending on the affected area but often include:
Pain: A dull ache or sharp pain in the affected area, which may worsen with activity.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness in the muscles or joints.
Swelling: Inflammation and swelling around the affected area.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations of numbness or tingling, particularly in the hands or fingers.
Weakness: A feeling of weakness in the affected muscles, making it difficult to perform tasks.

diseases.name: Resistant Hypertension - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Resistant hypertension is a significant health concern that affects millions of individuals worldwide. It is defined as high blood pressure that remains elevated despite the use of three or more antihypertensive medications, including a diuretic. This condition is not just a simple case of stubborn blood pressure; it can lead to severe health complications, including heart disease, stroke, and kidney failure. Understanding resistant hypertension is crucial for effective management and prevention of these serious outcomes.
symptoms: Many individuals with resistant hypertension may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some common symptoms include:
Headaches: Frequent or severe headaches can be a sign of elevated blood pressure.
Dizziness: Feeling lightheaded or dizzy may occur, especially when standing up quickly.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing can indicate heart strain due to high blood pressure.
Chest Pain: This may signal a more serious condition and should be evaluated immediately.

diseases.name: Respiratory Acidosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Respiratory acidosis is a medical condition that occurs when the lungs cannot remove enough carbon dioxide (CO2) from the body. This buildup of CO2 leads to a decrease in blood pH, making it more acidic. Understanding respiratory acidosis is crucial because it can indicate underlying health issues and may lead to serious complications if not addressed promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of respiratory acidosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of respiratory acidosis can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling breathless, especially during physical activity.
Confusion or Drowsiness: Increased CO2 levels can affect brain function, leading to confusion or lethargy.
Headache: Elevated CO2 levels can cause headaches due to increased pressure in the brain.
Rapid Breathing: The body may attempt to compensate for acidosis by increasing the breathing rate.
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, especially around the lips and fingertips, indicating low oxygen levels.

diseases.name: Respiratory Alkalosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Respiratory alkalosis is a condition that occurs when the body’s pH level becomes elevated due to a decrease in carbon dioxide (CO2) levels in the blood. This imbalance can lead to various physiological disturbances and may indicate underlying health issues. Understanding respiratory alkalosis is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely diagnosis and management can prevent complications and improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of respiratory alkalosis can vary in severity and may include:
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: A common symptom due to reduced blood flow to the brain.
Tingling Sensations: Often felt in the fingers, toes, or around the mouth, caused by changes in calcium levels.
Muscle Cramps or Spasms: Resulting from electrolyte imbalances.
Palpitations: An increased heart rate may occur as the body attempts to compensate for the imbalance.
Shortness of Breath: Although paradoxical, some individuals may feel breathless despite hyperventilating.

diseases.name: Restless Legs Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) is a neurological disorder characterized by an uncontrollable urge to move the legs, often accompanied by uncomfortable sensations. This condition can significantly impact sleep quality and overall quality of life. Understanding RLS is crucial, as it affects millions of people worldwide, yet it remains underdiagnosed and misunderstood. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of RLS, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Restless Legs Syndrome include:
An overwhelming urge to move the legs, often accompanied by uncomfortable sensations.
Symptoms that worsen during periods of inactivity, such as sitting or lying down.
Relief of symptoms through movement, such as walking or stretching.
Symptoms that typically occur in the evening or at night, disrupting sleep.

diseases.name: Retained Products Of Conception - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Retained Products of Conception (RPOC) is a medical condition that occurs when tissue from a pregnancy remains in the uterus after a miscarriage, abortion, or childbirth. This condition can lead to various complications, including infection and prolonged bleeding, making it a significant concern for women’s health. Understanding RPOC is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that women receive the care they need to recover fully.
symptoms: The symptoms of RPOC can vary depending on the amount of retained tissue and the individual’s overall health. Common symptoms include:
Heavy Bleeding: Prolonged or heavy vaginal bleeding after a miscarriage or delivery.
Severe Abdominal Pain: Cramping or pain that may be more intense than typical post-pregnancy discomfort.
Fever: A fever may indicate an infection, which can occur if tissue is retained.
Foul-Smelling Discharge: Unusual vaginal discharge that has a strong odor can be a sign of infection.

diseases.name: Retinal Detachment - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Retinal Detachment is a medical emergency that can lead to permanent blindness. There is an increased risk of losing vision if this eye problem is not treated at the right time.
symptoms: Abrupt presence of many floaters
The sudden appearance of light flashes in eyes
Blurred vision
Progressively reducing side vision
Dark curtain-like shadow effect around your visual field

diseases.name: Retinal Hemorrhage - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Retinal hemorrhage is a serious medical condition that occurs when blood leaks into the retina, the light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye. This condition can lead to significant vision problems and, in severe cases, permanent vision loss. Understanding retinal hemorrhage is crucial for early detection and treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of retinal hemorrhage.
symptoms: The symptoms of retinal hemorrhage can vary depending on the severity and location of the bleeding. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Vision Loss: This can range from partial to complete loss of vision in one eye.
Floaters: Patients may notice small specks or spots that float across their field of vision.
Flashes of Light: Some individuals may experience flashes or streaks of light.
Blurred Vision: Vision may become hazy or distorted.

diseases.name: Retinoblastoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Retinoblastoma is a rare type of eye cancer that most commonly affects young children, developing in the retina—the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. Because its early symptoms, such as a white reflection in the pupil or vision problems, can be easy to overlook, understanding the condition is especially important. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about retinoblastoma—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what to expect throughout the journey. Our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of retinoblastoma can be subtle, and a diagnosis often begins when a parent or pediatrician notices a change in the child's eye. Because it is a fast-growing cancer, early detection is critical for saving the child's life and vision.
If the tumor grows large or spreads, other symptoms may appear:
Red, Irritated Eye: The eye may be red, inflamed, and painful.
A Bulging Eyeball: The eyeball may appear to be sticking out (proptosis).
A Change in the Color of the Iris: The colored part of the eye may change color.
If you notice a white glow in your child's eye in a photograph or in low light, or any other of these persistent symptoms, it is crucial to consult a doctor right away for an accurate diagnosis.

diseases.name: Retinoschisis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Retinoschisis is a condition that affects the retina, the light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye. This condition is characterized by the splitting of the retina into two layers, which can lead to vision problems. Understanding retinoschisis is crucial, as it can have significant implications for an individual's vision and overall eye health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of retinoschisis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of retinoschisis can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Blurred Vision: Individuals may experience a gradual or sudden decrease in visual clarity.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or distorted.
Difficulty Seeing in Low Light: Night vision may be impaired.
Floaters: Small specks or spots may appear in the field of vision.

diseases.name: Retrograde Ejaculation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Retrograde ejaculation is a condition that affects a man's ability to ejaculate normally. Instead of the semen being expelled through the urethra during orgasm, it flows backward into the bladder. This phenomenon can be disconcerting and may raise concerns about fertility and sexual health. Understanding retrograde ejaculation is crucial for those affected, as it can have implications for sexual function, emotional well-being, and reproductive health.
symptoms: Dry Orgasm: The most noticeable symptom is the absence of semen during orgasm.
Urine Changes: After orgasm, some men may notice cloudy urine due to the presence of semen.
Reduced Sexual Satisfaction: The experience of orgasm may feel different, leading to decreased sexual satisfaction.

diseases.name: Retrolisthesis : Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Lumbar retrolisthesis occurs when parts of your backbone are slipping backwards on one another. Although this condition generally causes few symptoms, there’s evidence that lumbar retrolisthesis can lead to back pain and impaired back function. Retrolisthesis is an uncommon dysfunction and usually develops in the neck and shoulder area (the cervical spine) or the lower back (the lumbar spine).
symptoms: The symptoms of retrolisthesis differ from each individual and vary from mild to severe. They can include any combination of the following:
Back pain
Uneasiness in one specific area of the back
Limited range of motion
Pain in the area of dislocation
Sharp pinching pain
A bulge in the spine
The symptoms can extend beyond the back. Certain patients experience numbness or tingling in the buttocks, thighs, arms, hips, legs, shoulders, and neck.

diseases.name: Retropharyngeal Abscess - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Retropharyngeal abscess is a serious medical condition that can arise from various infections, particularly in the throat area. This condition is characterized by the accumulation of pus in the retropharyngeal space, which is located behind the pharynx. Understanding retropharyngeal abscess is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of retropharyngeal abscess, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of a retropharyngeal abscess can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Sore throat: A persistent and severe sore throat is often one of the first signs.
Difficulty swallowing: Patients may experience pain or discomfort while swallowing.
Fever: A high fever is common as the body fights the infection.
Neck stiffness: Patients may have difficulty moving their neck due to pain and swelling.
Muffled voice: Changes in voice quality, often described as "hot potato voice," can occur.
Swelling: Visible swelling in the neck area may be present.

diseases.name: Retroverted Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A retroverted uterus, also known as a tilted or tipped uterus, is a condition where the uterus is positioned backward, tilting towards the spine instead of the abdomen. While this anatomical variation is common and often harmless, it can sometimes lead to discomfort or complications. Understanding the implications of a retroverted uterus is essential for women’s health, as it can affect menstrual cycles, fertility, and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of retroverted uterus, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Many women with a retroverted uterus experience no symptoms. However, some may encounter the following:
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic region, especially during menstruation or intercourse.
Back Pain: Some women report lower back pain, which may be related to the position of the uterus.
Menstrual Irregularities: Changes in menstrual flow or cycle regularity can occur.
Difficulty with Conception: While a retroverted uterus does not typically affect fertility, some women may experience challenges.

diseases.name: Rett Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Rett syndrome is one of the rarest neurological disorders causing progressive loss of speech and motor activity in children. The syndrome affects girls, and the symptoms appear during the first two years of their life. Babies are born normal with this disorder and also grow normally for the first 6-18 months, followed by progressive loss of function.
symptoms: Slowed body, muscle, and brain development
Cognitive disability
Loss of normal movement and coordination
Muscle and bone weakness
Loss of communication abilities
Breathing problems including breath-holding, hyperventilating, forceful exhalation of air or saliva, and swallowing air
Irritability, screaming, and crying
Sudden, odd facial expressions and long bouts of laughter
Hand licking
Grasping of hair or clothing
Abnormal curvature of the spine
Weak, fragile, and thin bones prone to fractures
Problems with chewing and swallowing
Problems with bowel function
Teeth grinding
Abnormal hand movements like hand wringing, clapping, tapping, rubbing, or squeezing
Irregular heartbeat
Sleep disturbances
Fears and anxiety
Abnormal eye movements including crossed eyes, blinking, intense staring, or closing one eye at a time
Seizures
Small hands that get cold all the time

diseases.name: Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (RCVS) is a rare but significant neurological condition characterized by the temporary narrowing of blood vessels in the brain. This condition can lead to severe headaches and other neurological symptoms, making it crucial for both patients and healthcare providers to understand its implications. RCVS is often misdiagnosed or overlooked, which can lead to serious complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of RCVS, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of RCVS is a sudden, severe headache, often described as a "thunderclap headache." Other common symptoms may include:
Nausea and Vomiting: Often accompanying severe headaches.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or temporary loss of vision.
Seizures: In some cases, patients may experience seizures.
Neurological Deficits: Weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking.

diseases.name: Reyes Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Reyes Syndrome is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that primarily affects children and teenagers. It is characterized by a sudden onset of severe liver dysfunction and neurological symptoms, often following a viral infection. The significance of Reyes Syndrome lies in its association with the use of aspirin during viral illnesses, particularly influenza and chickenpox. Understanding Reyes Syndrome is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure early recognition and prompt treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Reyes Syndrome can present with a variety of symptoms, which may develop suddenly. Common symptoms include:
Vomiting: Often one of the first signs, it can be persistent and severe.
Confusion or Disorientation: Changes in mental status can occur, leading to confusion or altered consciousness.
Seizures: Neurological symptoms may escalate to seizures.
Lethargy: Affected individuals may become unusually tired or lethargic.
Irritability: Children may exhibit increased irritability or behavioral changes.
Loss of Appetite: A sudden decrease in appetite is common.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes may occur due to liver dysfunction.

diseases.name: Rhabdomyosarcoma
diseases.description: Rhabdomyosarcoma is a type of cancer that occurs in soft tissues. These cancers are one of the rarest forms and affect the skeletal tissues or sometimes hollow organs like the uterus and bladder. It is common in children, but the disorder can affect people at any age.

diseases.name: Rheumatic Fever - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Rheumatic fever is an inflammatory condition, which occurs as a complication when strep throat or scarlet fever is not treated completely ,
symptoms: The signs and symptoms, which result from inflammation in the central nervous system, heart, joints or skin may include:
Chills and fever
Pain and tenderness in joints, mostly on ankles, elbows, knees and wrists
Pain in a joint that travels to another joint
Red, hot or swollen joints
Small, painless bumps beneath the skin
Chest pain
Fatigue
Heart murmur or Heart palpitations
Slightly raised or flat, painless rash with a ragged edge
Migrating pain from one joint to another
Red rashes on body
Nose bleeding
Stomach pain
Small and painless bumps under the skin
Jerky, uncontrollable face and limb movements (Sydenham chorea)
Outbursts of unusual behavior like crying or inappropriate laughing, which accompanies Sydenham chorea

diseases.name: Rheumatic Heart Disease & Fever
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Rheumatic fever symptoms show up after 2 or 3 weeks of a strep throat diagnosis. Check your child for the following symptoms and get a strep test done –
Sore throat
Sore throat with tender and swollen lymph nodes
Red rash
Difficulty in swallowing
Very thick discharge from nose, sometimes bloody
Temperature of 101°F and a fever which lasts more than 3 days
Red and swollen tonsils
White patches or pus in tonsils
Small, red spots on the roof of their mouth
Headache
Nausea/vomiting
Someone with rheumatic fever could experience a few, some or most of the following symptoms:
Fever
Muscle aches
Swollen and painful joints. In this condition, knees, ankles, elbows, and wrists become swollen and very often the pain migrates from one joint to another.
A red, lattice-like rash — typically begins two to four weeks after a bout of strep.

The most severe complication is the damage it can do to the heart. In more than half of all cases, rheumatic fever can cause scarring of the valves of the heart, and cause a serious condition known as rheumatic heart disease, which will lead to heart failure
Sydenham’s chorea is a temporary nervous system disorder where rapid, jerky, involuntary movements of the body happen. The muscles of the arms, legs, or face tend to twitch uncontrollably.

diseases.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
diseases.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disorder that can affect more than just the joints. In some people, the condition can damage a wide variety of body systems, including the skin, eyes, lungs, heart, and blood vessels. RA is an autoimmune disease that occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues.
symptoms: Tender, warm, swollen joints
Joint stiffness that is usually worse in the mornings and after inactivity
Fatigue, fever, and loss of appetite
Symmetrical joint involvement
Rheumatoid nodules under the skin
Organ involvement (lungs, heart, eyes, blood vessels)

diseases.name: Rhinitis Medicamentosa - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rhinitis Medicamentosa (RM) is a condition that arises from the overuse of nasal decongestant sprays, leading to a cycle of dependency and worsening nasal congestion. This condition is significant because it can severely impact a person's quality of life, leading to chronic nasal obstruction, discomfort, and a reliance on medications that can exacerbate the problem. Understanding RM is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers to ensure effective management and prevention strategies are in place.
symptoms: The symptoms of RM can be distressing and may include:
Persistent Nasal Congestion: A feeling of blockage in the nasal passages that does not improve with decongestant use.
Rhinorrhea: A runny nose that may accompany the congestion.
Sneezing: Frequent sneezing episodes may occur, especially if there is an underlying allergic component.
Postnasal Drip: Mucus accumulation in the throat can lead to coughing or throat irritation.

diseases.name: Rickets: All You Wanted to Know
diseases.description: Rickets can be thought of as a skeletal disorder or a bone condition that happens mostly in children due to the lack of Vitamin D, calcium, and phosphate. These are the essential nutrients for the development of strong and healthy bones. People with Rickets tend to have bones that soften and become prone to fractures and irregularities, even skeletal deformities in the most severe cases. A survey was conducted for 337.68 million people present in 0.39 million villages spread across 22 states in India between 1963 to 2005. Out of 411,744 patients recognized with a bone disorder and mineral metabolism, Rickets was one of the most common disorders found. Vitamin D assumes a pivotal role in the absorption of calcium, and so low Vitamin D levels can lead to lower calcium levels. This causes the developing bones to become weak and irregular. Let us discuss the symptoms, causes, treatments, and everything else related to Rickets.
symptoms: The symptoms of Rickets are often detected in children, and they are listed below.
Pain or softness in the bones of the arms, legs, pelvis, or even the spine.
Restriction in the growth or short stature of the child.
If there are bones detected which are soft and break easily.
The slow growth of bones and bowed legs.
If a child experiences muscle cramps and fractures present.
If a child has deformities in the teeth, including delayed tooth formation, holes found in the enamel, abscesses, defects found in the tooth structure, and an increase in the number of cavities.
If someone has skeletal deformities such as their skull-shaped in an odd way or bumps in their ribcage or a protruding breastbone or a curved spine.
If a child has an enormous forehead and abdomen.

diseases.name: Right Bundle Branch Block - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB) is a condition that affects the electrical conduction system of the heart. It occurs when there is a delay or blockage in the electrical impulses traveling through the right bundle branch of the heart's conduction system. This can lead to changes in the heart's rhythm and function, which may have significant implications for overall cardiovascular health. Understanding RBBB is crucial for early detection and management, as it can be associated with various underlying heart conditions.
symptoms: RBBB may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in mild cases. However, some common symptoms include:
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Feeling faint or unsteady, particularly during physical activity.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during exertion.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.

diseases.name: Road Traffic Accident | Traffic Injuries
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE

diseases.name: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever
diseases.description: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a bacterial disease that gets transmitted through the bite of ticks. RMSF requires prompt medical attention to prevent severe damage to internal organs.
symptoms: You will notice the first symptoms of Rocky Mountain spotted fever within two to fourteen days after getting a tick bite.

The chief symptom associated with the disease is a non-itchy rash that starts on your wrist and ankles. Later, the rash spreads up to your arms and legs until it reaches the torso. It can also cover your palms and soles. The rash begins two to five days after the fever and looks like small red spots. Subsequently, the rash turns purple and red, indicating that the disease has progressed.
Other symptoms observed in RMSF are:
High fever that persists for two to three weeks
Chills
Muscle aches
Vomiting
Severe headache
Fatigue
Poor appetite
Abdominal pain
Nausea
Sore throat
Neurological symptoms like confusion

In RMSF, headache and fever are usually the first symptoms to develop. The rash starts three to five days after the fever. An infected person should get treatment before the rash turns darker in color.

diseases.name: Rosai Dorfman Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rosai Dorfman Disease (RDD) is a rare and often misunderstood condition that primarily affects the lymphatic system. Named after the pathologists Dr. Rosai and Dr. Dorfman, who first described it in 1969, this disease is characterized by an overproduction of a type of white blood cell known as histiocytes. While RDD is generally considered benign, its symptoms can significantly impact a patient's quality of life, making awareness and understanding of the disease crucial. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Rosai Dorfman Disease, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Rosai Dorfman Disease can vary widely depending on the organs involved. Common symptoms include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: The most characteristic symptom, often painless and located in the neck, armpits, or groin.
Fever: Persistent low-grade fever may occur.
Night Sweats: Patients may experience excessive sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can be a concerning symptom.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue and malaise are common complaints.
Skin Lesions: In some cases, RDD can cause skin lesions that may appear as raised, reddish-brown bumps.

diseases.name: Roseola Infantum: Symptoms, Treatment and More
diseases.description: Roseola is a contagious viral infection commonly seen in infants and toddlers. Usually, this infection is not severe and resolves on its own. This article may help you learn more about the symptoms, causes, treatment, and much more.
symptoms: If your kid gets exposed to the infection, it could take five to fifteen days for the symptoms to appear. Your child can also be asymptomatic despite being affected by the virus. Moreover, some children might suffer from symptoms mild enough to get unnoticed. Roseola symptoms commonly include:
High fever – If your child’s temperature goes above 39.5 ℃, then it’s considered a high fever. The fever typically lasts three to seven days.

Rash – A pink rash develops within 12 to 24 hours after the fever goes away. It might be flat or raised. This pink rash is a characteristic sign of roseola and indicates the end of the infection’s course. There can be a white ring around some of the spots. Usually, the rash starts on the back, chest and abdomen, and and later spreads to arms and the neck. It may or may not reach your legs and face. Sometimes there may not be any rash.
Other signs and symptoms of roseola in a child are:
Irritability
Ear pain
Decreased appetite
Swollen glands
Mild diarrhea
Mild cough or sore throat
Eyelid swelling
Convulsions due to high fever

diseases.name: Rotator Cuff Injuries
diseases.description: The rotator cuff is a group of four muscles and their tendons that stabilize the shoulder joint and allow the shoulder to rotate and move. Injuries range from inflammation (tendinitis) and partial tears to complete tears of one or more tendons. Rotator cuff injuries are one of the most common causes of shoulder pain and disability.
symptoms: A dull ache deep in the shoulder
Disturbed sleep, particularly if lying on the affected shoulder
Arm weakness
Difficulty reaching behind the back
Crackling sensation with movement

diseases.name: Rotator Cuff Injury - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Rotator cuff injuries are among the most common musculoskeletal disorders affecting the shoulder. They can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, limiting mobility and causing persistent pain. Understanding rotator cuff injuries is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can lead to better outcomes and a return to normal activities. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding rotator cuff injuries.
symptoms: Shoulder Pain: Often described as a dull ache, pain may worsen at night or with overhead activities.
Weakness: Difficulty lifting objects or performing overhead tasks may indicate muscle weakness.
Limited Range of Motion: Stiffness in the shoulder can restrict movement, making daily activities challenging.
Clicking or Popping Sounds: Some individuals may experience audible sounds during shoulder movement.

diseases.name: Rotator Cuff Tendinitis
diseases.description: The rotator cuff is a group of tendons and muscles in the shoulder, connecting the upper arm (humerus) to the shoulder blade (scapula).
symptoms: The early symptoms of Rotator Cuff Tendinitis are mild but get worse over time and may persist for years to come, unless treated and managed in the right way. The following are the most common symptoms of Rotator Cuff Tendinitis:
Pain caused by lowering or raising your arm
Clicking sound while raising your arm
Pain, swelling on the front of your shoulder
Pain, swelling in the side of your arm
Pain forcing you to wake from sleep
Stiffness of the joint
Loss of mobility in the affected area
Pain while reaching behind your back

diseases.name: Rotavirus - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Rotavirus is a virus that causes diarrhea . Before developing the rotavirus vaccine, many children were infected by this contagious virus at least once before 5 years of age. It can be treated at home with adequate fluids to prevent dehydration and maintain good hygiene.
symptoms: The incubation period for rotavirus infection is about two days after being exposed to the virus. The initial symptoms are fever and vomiting , which is then followed by four to eight days of watery diarrhea. Rotavirus infection can also cause abdominal pain. It can even lead to death if there is untreated and severe dehydration. The symptoms of rotavirus vary in children and adults.
Excessive fatigue
Vomiting
High fever
Irritability
Dehydration
Pain in the abdomen

Of all the symptoms, dehydration is the most concerning in children, as it is caused by the fact that this age group is more liable to a drop in fluid and electrolytes through vomiting and diarrhea because they have less body weight. It is important to look out for indications of dehydration in children , like:
Dry mouth
Cool skin
Absence of tears when crying
Sunken eyes
Decreased frequency in urination
Healthy adults experience the symptoms to a smaller degree, while some can be asymptomatic also.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Rotavirus Infection
diseases.description: Rotavirus is a common cause of severe diarrhea and vomiting in infants and young children, which can lead to dehydration.
symptoms: Watery diarrhea
Vomiting
Fever
Stomach pain
Dehydration

diseases.name: Rule Out Heart Palpitations Before They Lead to Other Cardiac Complications
diseases.description: Heart palpitations are when your heart starts beating irregularly and unexpectedly fast. These heart palpitations usually arise as a result of stress, anxiety, or too much consumption of caffeine, nicotine, or alcohol. You can feel these sensations in your chest, neck, or throat. Heart palpitations are usually harmless and often go away on their own. But, in some rare cases, they can lead to serious heart conditions such as heart attack, coronary artery disease, heart failure , heart valve problems, and heart muscle problems. Having a basic knowledge of heart palpitations and its complications can help you rule out all such diseases related to them.
symptoms: The symptoms of heart palpitations are
Heart skipping beats
Heart pounding
Heart beating too fast
Flip-flopping
Heart throbbing
Heart fluttering rapidly
In case you have a serious heart condition, heart palpitations will be accompanied by
Breath shortness
Dizziness
Chest pain
Fainting
In such severe cases, you should seek medical attention immediately. If you’re experiencing one or many of the symptoms mentioned above, they might be brought along by the following risk factors.

diseases.name: Rumination Syndrome
diseases.description: Rumination syndrome causes patients to accidentally regurgitate or bring up unprocessed or poorly digested food, chew it again, and then swallow or spit out the food. Since this food does not get metabolized, it’s supposed to taste natural and not acidic like vomit. Rumination happens after each meal, generally immediately.
symptoms: The symptoms of rumination syndrome may include some or all of the following:
Regurgitation without effort, usually within 10 minutes after eating
Regurgitation relieves abdominal discomfort or pressure
A sense of fullness
Peculiar oral odor
Nausea
Unintentional weight loss

diseases.name: Ruptured Eardrum (Perforated Eardrum)
diseases.description: An opening or tear in the fragile tissue that separates your ear channel from your central ear is called a ruptured eardrum (tympanic membrane perforation). A ruptured eardrum can cause hearing loss and can also make your middle ear prone to infections.
symptoms: A punctured eardrum can cause the following symptoms and negative effects:
Earache that may come and go away quickly
Pus or blood-like discharge from the ear
Hearing issues
Tinnitus
Vertigo
Dizziness along with a feeling of queasiness or vomiting

diseases.name: Ruptured Spleen: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, and Recovery
diseases.description: The Spleen is an organ in our body located right under the left rib cage and at the upper left part of the abdomen. This organ is responsible for recycling the blood cells and fighting certain bacteria that can cause serious health problems such are meningitis and pneumonia. It also acts as a storehouse for white blood cells and platelets.
symptoms: A ruptured spleen causes pain in the area along with symptoms of blood loss. The main symptoms are:
• Dizziness
• Confusion
• Fainting
• Lightheadedness
• Anxiety and restlessness
• Pain in the left shoulder
• Pain and tenderness at the upper left abdomen or below the left rib cage

As already mentioned, a ruptured spleen is a medical emergency. Therefore, if you suspect a ruptured or injured spleen, you should seek emergency care. Head to the nearest emergency room or dial 1066 for an ambulance .
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: Russell Silver Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Russell Silver Syndrome (RSS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by growth retardation and distinctive physical features. First described in the 1950s, this condition is significant not only for its impact on physical development but also for the psychological and social challenges it poses to affected individuals and their families. Understanding Russell Silver Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of Russell Silver Syndrome can vary widely among individuals, but common features include:
Short Stature: Height significantly below the average for age and sex.
Asymmetry: Uneven growth of limbs or facial features.
Triangular Face: A distinctive facial shape with a prominent forehead and narrow chin.
Low Birth Weight: Many affected individuals are born with a lower-than-average birth weight.
Delayed Development: Some children may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones.
Feeding Difficulties: Infants may have trouble feeding, leading to further growth challenges.

diseases.name: Sacral Dimple - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A sacral dimple is a small indentation or pit located at the lower back, specifically in the sacral region, which is the triangular bone at the base of the spine. While often benign and harmless, the presence of a sacral dimple can sometimes indicate underlying conditions that may require medical attention. Understanding what a sacral dimple is, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and potential complications is essential for parents and caregivers, especially when it comes to the health of infants and young children.
symptoms: Most sacral dimples are asymptomatic and do not cause any discomfort. However, they may be associated with the following:
Visible Dimple: A small pit or indentation on the lower back.
Hair Tufts: In some cases, hair may grow around the dimple.
Pigmentation Changes: The skin around the dimple may appear darker or lighter than the surrounding area.

diseases.name: Sacral Fracture : Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The sacrum is the lower part of the spine, below the lumbar spine and above the coccyx or tailbone. It is made up of five fused vertebrae called sacral vertebrae. Fracture of these vertebrae is called a sacral fracture. The sacrum anchors the spine firmly to a bony structure called pelvic girdle between the two hip bones.
symptoms: Severe lower back pain
Tingling or numbness
Urinary incontinence , faecal incontinence (inability to control the passage of stools)
Sexual problems

diseases.name: Sacroiliitis : Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, Home Remedies & Exercises
diseases.description: The sacroiliac joints connect the pelvis and the lower spine. Sacroiliitis is the swelling of either one or both sacroiliac joints, causing pain in the buttocks or lower back and spreading to either or both legs. The treatment methods for sacroiliitis include physical therapy, radio frequency ablation, and steroid injections into the sacroiliac joint.
symptoms: Sacroiliitis symptoms can be similar to that of other lower back issues. Its most common symptom is a pain in the hip , buttocks, lower back, and down the legs. Sometimes a low-grade fever accompanies these symptoms. The pain generally worsens after standing for long periods, going up and down the stairs, and running or walking with long strides.

diseases.name: Saddle Nose - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Saddle nose, also known as saddle nose deformity, is a condition characterized by a noticeable depression or collapse of the nasal bridge, giving the nose a "saddle-like" appearance. This condition can significantly impact an individual's appearance and self-esteem, and it may also lead to functional issues such as breathing difficulties. Understanding saddle nose is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can arise from various underlying causes, including infections, genetic factors, and autoimmune diseases.
symptoms: The primary symptom of saddle nose is the visible deformity of the nasal bridge. Other associated symptoms may include:
Nasal Congestion: Difficulty breathing through the nose due to structural changes.
Nasal Obstruction: Blockage of airflow, leading to discomfort.
Sinus Infections: Increased susceptibility to sinusitis due to altered nasal anatomy.
Nasal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the nasal area, especially if associated with underlying conditions.

diseases.name: Salivary Gland Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Salivary gland cancer starts in the glands that make saliva---most commonly the parotid (in front of the ear), submandibular (under the jaw), and sublingual (under the tongue) glands, as well as hundreds of tiny "minor" salivary glands lining the mouth, nose, sinuses, and throat. Unlike many head and neck cancers that are linked to tobacco or alcohol, salivary gland cancers are diverse, relatively uncommon, and driven by tumorspecific biology. The encouraging news: with precise surgery, modern radiation techniques, and tailored systemic therapies, many people achieve longterm control with excellent quality of life. This comprehensive article explains what salivary gland cancer is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, evidencebased treatments (surgery, reconstruction, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted and immune therapies, and proton therapy in select cases), prognosis, and prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on the gland and proximity to nerves and nearby structures.

diseases.name: Salmonella - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Salmonella is a type of bacteria that can cause foodborne illness, commonly known as salmonellosis. This infection is significant due to its prevalence and potential severity, affecting millions of people worldwide each year. Understanding Salmonella is crucial for prevention and management, as it can lead to serious health complications if not addressed promptly.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Salmonella infection include:
Diarrhea
Abdominal cramps
Fever
Nausea
Vomiting
Symptoms typically appear 6 hours to 6 days after exposure and can last 4 to 7 days. Warning signs that require immediate medical attention include:
Severe dehydration
High fever (over 102°F)
Blood in stool
Prolonged vomiting

diseases.name: Sandifer Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sandifer Syndrome is a rare neurological condition that primarily affects infants and young children. It is characterized by a combination of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and abnormal posturing, which can often be mistaken for seizures or other neurological disorders. Understanding Sandifer Syndrome is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early recognition and appropriate management can significantly improve the quality of life for affected children. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Sandifer Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of Sandifer Syndrome can vary from child to child, but they typically include:
Abnormal Posturing: This is the hallmark of Sandifer Syndrome. Children may exhibit arching of the back, twisting of the neck, or other unusual movements during episodes.
Gastroesophageal Reflux Symptoms: These may include vomiting, regurgitation, irritability, and feeding difficulties.
Coughing or Choking: Some children may cough or choke during or after feeding due to reflux.
Sleep Disturbances: Children may have trouble sleeping due to discomfort from reflux.

diseases.name: Sanfilippo Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sanfilippo Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects children, leading to severe neurological decline and a range of debilitating symptoms. Named after Dr. Sylvio Sanfilippo, who first described the condition in the 1960s, this syndrome is classified as a type of mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS), a group of inherited metabolic disorders. Understanding Sanfilippo Syndrome is crucial not only for affected families but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Sanfilippo Syndrome manifests through a variety of symptoms that worsen over time. Common symptoms include:
Developmental Delays: Children may experience delays in speech and motor skills.
Behavioral Issues: Hyperactivity, aggression, and sleep disturbances are common.
Cognitive Decline: Progressive loss of cognitive abilities, including memory and problem-solving skills.
Physical Symptoms: Enlarged liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly), joint stiffness, and skeletal abnormalities.
Seizures: Many children with Sanfilippo Syndrome may develop seizures as the disease progresses.

diseases.name: Sarcoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that develops in the bones, muscles, fat, or connective tissues. Because it can occur in many different parts of the body and present in various ways, understanding sarcoma can feel particularly challenging. This comprehensive guide provides clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about sarcoma—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what to expect throughout your journey. Our aim is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: Sarcomas often grow silently in the early stages, which can make them difficult to detect. This is because they can form in flexible tissues and may not cause pain until they are quite large.
As the tumor grows, it may press on nearby nerves or muscles, leading to more noticeable symptoms.
Pain: The lump or bone may become painful if it's pressing on a nerve.
Numbness, tingling, or a limp: This can happen if the tumor is affecting a nerve or is near a joint.
Abdominal Pain: If the sarcoma is in the abdomen, it can cause a feeling of fullness, abdominal pain, or a noticeable mass.
Unexplained Weight Loss or Fatigue: These can be signs of more advanced disease.

If you find a new lump on your body, particularly one that is growing or is larger than a golf ball, it is crucial to see a doctor promptly. While most lumps are benign (non-cancerous), a timely evaluation is the best way to ensure an accurate diagnosis and the most effective treatment.

diseases.name: Sarcomatoid Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sarcomatoid carcinoma is a rare and aggressive form of cancer that exhibits characteristics of both sarcomas and carcinomas. This hybrid nature makes it particularly challenging to diagnose and treat. Understanding sarcomatoid carcinoma is crucial for early detection and effective management, as it can significantly impact patient outcomes. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding sarcomatoid carcinoma.
symptoms: The symptoms of sarcomatoid carcinoma can vary depending on the location of the tumor. Common symptoms may include:
Unexplained Weight Loss: Significant weight loss without trying can be a warning sign.
Persistent Cough: A chronic cough that does not improve may indicate lung involvement.
Pain: Localized pain in the affected area, such as the chest or abdomen.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness that does not improve with rest.
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the affected area, particularly in soft tissue sarcomas.

diseases.name: Sarcopenia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sarcopenia is a condition characterized by the progressive loss of muscle mass and strength, primarily associated with aging. It is a significant health concern, particularly for older adults, as it can lead to increased frailty, falls, and a decline in overall quality of life. Understanding sarcopenia is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers and healthcare providers, as early recognition and intervention can greatly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Muscle Weakness: A noticeable decrease in strength, making daily activities more challenging.
Decreased Endurance: Fatigue during physical activities that were previously manageable.
Weight Loss: Unintentional loss of muscle mass, often accompanied by a decrease in overall body weight.
Impaired Mobility: Difficulty walking, climbing stairs, or performing routine tasks.
Increased Risk of Falls: A higher likelihood of falling due to weakened muscles and balance issues.

diseases.name: Scabies: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment
diseases.description: Scabies is an itchy skin condition that is caused by Sarcoptes scabiei, a tiny burrowing mite. People with scabies experience severe itching in the area where the mite burrows.

diseases.name: Scalp Folliculitis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Folliculitis is a condition in which the hair follicles get inflamed. It can occur anywhere in the body where there is hair.
symptoms: Folliculitis signs and symptoms include:
White-headed pimples, or clusters of small red bumps which develop around hair follicles
Burning, itchy skin
A large swollen bump or mass
Painful, tender skin
Pus-filled blisters which breaks open and crust over

People with folliculitis might feel itchy and would want to scratch. This urge may be uncontrollable and when scratched the bumps break and bleed leading to severe infection on the spots. This apparently worsens the condition and damages the hair follicles permanently.

With folliculitis, there is a high risk of the bumps getting spread all over the scalp. Scratching on the results of the bump in spreading. When there is a bump on a particular spot, it spreads to the other follicles and increases in size. The bumps after spreading may also get more inflamed.
Since the condition often starts along the hairline, most patients experience severe hair fall.
Yellowish-brown sores
Itching
Scarring
Burning or stinging sensation on the affected spots
Pain or tenderness on the scarred spots
Pus formation on the breakouts

Warm compress – A warm, damp cloth can be applied on the affected spots for at least 3 or 4 times a day. This will help to reduce the inflammation and pacify the itching or burning sensation. It can also help to drain the pus. However, treatment with too hot a compress needs to be avoided, as it may worsen the bumps.

Using antibacterial soap – Gently washing the skin twice a day with an antibacterial soap will help to reduce the infection on the scalp. This can be done when the folliculitis is developed along the hairline. It is also important to dry the area with a clean towel after washing with the soap, as any traces of the soap left should be wiped off.

Using anti-dandruff shampoo – Washing the scalp with an anti dandruff shampoo helps to kill the infection-causing organisms on the follicles. Shampoos that contain anti-fungal properties such as ketoconazole, ciclopirox or tea tree oil are preferred. If after using the shampoo, any side effects are experienced, it is important to consult the dermatologist immediately.

Applying cortisone cream – A cortisone cream can be applied on the affected spots to help reduce the inflammation and get rid of itching. It will also help to reduce the burning sensation on the scalp.

Using antibiotic ointments – When the scalp folliculitis is developed due to bacteria, applying an antibiotic ointment like Neosporin on the affected spots can help to kill the organism and gradually reduce the infection.

Avoid hot water – Washing the hair or scalp with hot water may worsen the symptoms. Hence, it is advisable to use lukewarm water to wash the scalp. This can help to reduce the irritation on the affected spots.

Avoid shaving frequently – Shaving the head frequently needs to be avoided. The individual can try switching to an electric shaver instead of hand razors as electric ones may be effective and less painful. After shaving lotion that doesn’t contain any chemical formulations can be applied on the scalp after shaving.

Using clean towels and combs – Keeping the towel, comb, hats, pillows, etc that come in contact with your scalp clean is essential. Washing these items regularly is necessary to avoid developing the symptoms further.

Keeping the scalp clean – Washing the scalp properly after using any product or oil on the scalp is important. This helps to clear off any remains of the products that can potentially lead to problems.
In addition to the above remedies, it is important to follow proper scalp hygiene after the condition is sorted.

diseases.name: Scalp Psoriasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scalp psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that affects millions of people worldwide. It is characterized by the rapid growth of skin cells on the scalp, leading to red, scaly patches that can be itchy and uncomfortable. While it may seem like a cosmetic issue, scalp psoriasis can significantly impact a person's quality of life, causing emotional distress and social anxiety. Understanding this condition is crucial for effective management and treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of scalp psoriasis can vary in severity and may include:
Red Patches: Raised, inflamed areas of skin covered with silvery-white scales.
Itching and Burning: The affected areas can be itchy and may cause discomfort.
Dry Scalp: Flaking skin that resembles dandruff.
Hair Loss: In severe cases, hair may fall out due to inflammation.

diseases.name: Scarlet fever - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Scarlet fever is an infection characterized by rashes, a sore throat, and high fever. It is now treatable with antibiotics and is not considered as deadly as it was in past centuries. The infection is highly contagious that spreads from one person to another via droplets expelled when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
symptoms: Rashes : The primary symptom is the rash. Red rashes that look similar to sunburns appear on your body with a texture like sandpaper. It begins typically on the neck or face and spreads to the trunk, arms and legs. If pressure is applied to the reddened skin, it will turn pale. The folds of skin on your armpits, groin, knees, elbows, and neck are usually a deeper red than the surrounding rashes. You might also notice a pale ring around the mouth on your flushed face. Your tongue will be red, bumpy and sometimes, covered with a white coating, and this condition is called a strawberry tongue. These symptoms are what give scarlet fever its name. These rashes subside within a week, and your skin begins peeling in the affected areas.
A high fever, usually at 101 °F ( 38.3 °C)
Chills
A sore and red throat often gets accompanied by white or yellow patches.
Headache
Difficulty swallowing
Nausea and vomiting
Enlarged glands in your neck.

diseases.name: Scarring Alopecia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scarring alopecia, also known as cicatricial alopecia, is a group of hair loss disorders characterized by the destruction of hair follicles and replacement with scar tissue. This condition can lead to permanent hair loss and can significantly impact an individual's self-esteem and quality of life. Understanding scarring alopecia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can be associated with various underlying health issues. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of scarring alopecia.
symptoms: The symptoms of scarring alopecia can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Hair Loss: Gradual or sudden loss of hair in patches or diffuse thinning.
Itching or Burning: Some individuals may experience discomfort in the affected areas.
Redness and Inflammation: The scalp may appear red or inflamed.
Changes in Skin Texture: The skin on the scalp may become shiny or scarred.

diseases.name: Schistosomiasis
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms for schistosomiasis surface within days after the infection and continue till months. Note that the symptoms are caused by the body’s reaction to the eggs produced by worms, not by the worms themselves. Below are the signs and symptoms of schistosomiasis:
Developing a rash or having itchy skin
Fever
Chills
Muscle pain
Cough
More rare but severe symptoms for schistosomiasis include:
Paralysis
Seizures
Spinal cord inflammation
Liver damage
Intestine damage
Lung damage
Bladder damage

diseases.name: Schizencephaly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Schizencephaly is a rare and complex neurological condition that affects brain development. It is characterized by abnormal clefts or slits in the cerebral hemispheres, which can lead to a range of neurological impairments. Understanding this condition is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for families, caregivers, and healthcare professionals involved in the management of affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of schizencephaly, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of schizencephaly can vary widely based on the severity of the condition and the extent of brain involvement. Common symptoms include:
Developmental Delays: Children with schizencephaly may experience delays in reaching developmental milestones, such as walking and talking.
Seizures: Many individuals with schizencephaly experience seizures, which can range from mild to severe.
Muscle Weakness: Weakness or paralysis on one side of the body (hemiparesis) is common, particularly in cases of unilateral schizencephaly.
Cognitive Impairments: Some individuals may have learning disabilities or intellectual disabilities.
Speech and Language Difficulties: Communication challenges are common, and speech therapy may be necessary.

diseases.name: Schizoid Personality Disorder: Symptoms, Causes, and Diagnosis
diseases.description: A schizoid personality disorder is a mental health condition that begins in early adulthood. It is characterized by a lack of social interaction, even with family and friends. It is a common disorder that usually lasts a lifetime. The exact cause of this disorder is unknown, but it can be managed with medications.
symptoms: People who have schizoid personality disorder exhibit the following symptoms:
They prefer being alone and spending their work, leisure, and study time alone.
They do not form close relationships, even with family.
They desire little to no sexual relationships, even with their partner.
They feel like they cannot feel pleasure.
They have difficulty in feeling and understanding emotion.
They do not know how to react to situations appropriately.
They appear cold, distant, humourless, and emotionless to other people.
They do not have any goals or motivation.
They do not react to praise or criticism with suitable responses

diseases.name: Schizophrenia
diseases.description: Schizophrenia is a mental illness characterized by abnormal social behaviour and inability to understand reality. Symptoms of schizophrenia include confused thinking, hallucinations, false beliefs, lack of motivation and decreased social life. Mental health issues like anxiety and depression are common in individuals with schizophrenia. Often, schizophrenic patients are prone to substance abuse.

diseases.name: Schizophreniform Disorder - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: The doctor may diagnose a patient to be suffering from the schizophreniform disorder if they show symptoms of schizophrenia such as hallucinations, delusions, and chaotic behaviour. These symptoms lasts anywhere between 1 to 6 months. For example, when they are alone in a room, they may hear others talking or calling out to them when none of such people exist.
symptoms: Like schizophrenia, the symptoms might include the following:
Delusions : False beliefs that people refuse to give up, even after presenting factual information showing that their belief is untrue
Hallucinations : Seeing, hearing, or feeling things that are untrue
Disorganized speech : Making illogical statements and quickly skipping from one topic to another
Odd or strange behaviour : Constantly pacing, writing, or walking in circles

Other symptoms : Patients may also present the following symptoms: Poor hygiene and grooming habits Lack of energy Loss of interest in life Withdrawal from friends, family, and other social activities
Poor hygiene and grooming habits
Lack of energy
Loss of interest in life
Withdrawal from friends, family, and other social activities

diseases.name: Schizotypal personality disorder - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: A schizotypal personality disorder is a personality disorder characterized by odd and eccentric behavior and discomfort with close relationships. The pattern of cognitive distortion of behavior typically begins by early adulthood and is likely to endure across the lifespan.
symptoms: Typically, STPD includes five or more of these signs and symptoms:
Flat emotions inappropriate emotional responses
Being a loner and lacking friends
Persistent social anxiety
Incorrect interpretation of events
Peculiar, eccentric mannerisms or beliefs
Praniod or suspicious thoughts and constant doubts about others’ loyalty
Belief in special powers
Unusual perceptions or having illusions
Dressing in peculiar ways
Peculiar style of speech

diseases.name: Schwannoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Schwannoma, also known as neurilemmoma, is a type of tumor that arises from Schwann cells, which are responsible for the formation of the myelin sheath that insulates nerves. While schwannomas are generally benign (non-cancerous), they can lead to significant health issues depending on their size and location. Understanding schwannomas is crucial for early detection and effective management, as they can affect various nerves throughout the body, leading to a range of symptoms and complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of schwannoma can vary widely depending on the tumor's location and size. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Localized pain in the area where the tumor is located.
Numbness or Tingling: Affected nerves may lead to sensations of numbness or tingling in the corresponding body part.
Weakness: Muscle weakness may occur if the tumor compresses motor nerves.
Balance Issues: Vestibular schwannomas can cause dizziness and balance problems.
Hearing Loss: Schwannomas on the auditory nerve can lead to hearing impairment.

diseases.name: Schwannomas - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: A schwannoma is a type of nerve sheath tumor that develops from Schwann cells, which normally protect and insulate nerves. Most schwannomas are benign (non-cancerous), meaning they grow slowly and usually don’t spread to other parts of the body. However, their growth can press on surrounding nerves and tissues, causing pain, numbness, or other symptoms. Rarely, a schwannoma can become malignant (cancerous) and is then called a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST).
symptoms: Schwannomas grow slowly, and symptoms often depend on their size and location.
Common early symptoms include:
A painless lump under the skin
Numbness, tingling, or weakness in the affected area
Mild discomfort or shooting nerve pain
Advanced symptoms may include:
Hearing loss or ringing in the ear (vestibular schwannoma)
Balance problems or dizziness
Persistent back pain (spinal schwannoma)
Difficulty moving an arm or leg
Facial weakness or numbness (if near facial nerves)
If a tumor presses on nearby organs, symptoms may mimic other medical conditions, which is why medical evaluation is essential.

diseases.name: Scimitar Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scimitar Syndrome is a rare congenital heart defect characterized by an abnormal connection between the pulmonary veins and the right atrium. This condition is significant not only due to its unique anatomical features but also because of its potential complications if left untreated. Understanding Scimitar Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Symptoms of Scimitar Syndrome can vary widely depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Cyanosis: A bluish tint to the skin, lips, and nails due to low oxygen levels in the blood.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or weakness.
Frequent Respiratory Infections: Increased susceptibility to lung infections.
Poor Growth: In infants and children, failure to thrive or gain weight appropriately.

diseases.name: Scleritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scleritis is a serious inflammatory condition affecting the sclera, the white outer coating of the eyeball. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and, in severe cases, vision loss. Understanding scleritis is crucial not only for those who may be affected but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of scleritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of scleritis can vary depending on the severity and type of inflammation. Common symptoms include:
Eye Pain: Often described as deep, aching, or throbbing pain that may worsen with eye movement.
Redness: The affected eye may appear red or inflamed.
Sensitivity to Light: Photophobia, or sensitivity to light, is a common symptom.
Vision Changes: Blurred vision or other visual disturbances may occur.
Tearing: Increased tear production can be a symptom.

diseases.name: Scleroderma (Systemic Sclerosis)
diseases.description: Scleroderma, also known as systemic sclerosis, is a group of rare diseases that involve the hardening and tightening of the skin and connective tissues. Some types can also harm the blood vessels, internal organs, and the digestive tract. It is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system triggers excessive collagen production.
symptoms: Hardening and tightening of skin
Raynaud's phenomenon
CREST syndrome features (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia)
Digestive problems
Heart, lung, kidney involvement
Joint pain

diseases.name: Sclerosing Mesenteritis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Sclerosing Mesenteritis, also known as mesenteric panniculitis, occurs when mesentery (the tissue) that holds small intestines in place becomes inflamed and forms a scar tissue. Sclerosing Mesenteritis is a rare condition, and it’s not clear what causes it.
symptoms: The symptoms of Sclerosing Mesenteritis vary from person to person. Some of the most prominent symptoms of Sclerosing Mesenteritis include:
Abdominal pain
Gastric discomfort
Bloating of the stomach
Nausea
Vomiting
Irregular bowel movement
Weight loss
Fever
Loss of appetite

diseases.name: Scoliosis
diseases.description: Scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine that occurs most often during the growth spurt just before puberty. While scoliosis can be caused by conditions such as cerebral palsy and muscular dystrophy, the cause of most scoliosis is unknown. Most cases of scoliosis are mild, but some children develop spine deformities that continue to get more severe as they grow.
symptoms: Uneven shoulders
One shoulder blade appears more prominent than the other
Uneven waist
One hip higher than the other
One side of the rib cage jutting forward
Back pain in adults

diseases.name: Scorpion Sting
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Scorpion stings symptoms are:
Intense pain
Tingling and numbness in the area around the sting
Swelling around the sting area
If a bark scorpion bites, severe symptoms are visible, which are as follows:
Unusual head, neck and eye movements
Muscle twitching or thrashing
Sweating
Drooling
Vomiting
Accelerated heart rate or irregular heartbeat
High or low blood pressure levels
Restlessness or anxiety or crying profusely (in children)
If a child is stung by a scorpion, immediately get medical help. If adults manifest a variety of symptoms, seek medical attention right away.

diseases.name: Scotoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scotoma is a term that may not be familiar to many, but it plays a significant role in understanding various visual impairments. It refers to a partial loss of vision or a blind spot in an otherwise normal visual field. This condition can affect one or both eyes and can be caused by a variety of factors, ranging from eye diseases to neurological disorders. Understanding scotoma is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers, as it can significantly impact daily life and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of scotoma can vary widely depending on its cause and location. Common symptoms include:
Blind Spots: Areas in the visual field where vision is absent.
Distorted Vision: Objects may appear warped or bent in the affected area.
Difficulty Reading: Individuals may struggle to read text, especially if the scotoma is located in the central vision.
Flashes of Light: Some may experience visual disturbances, such as flashes or floaters.

diseases.name: Scrofula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Scrofula, often referred to as "king's evil," is a term that has historically been associated with a specific type of lymphadenitis, particularly affecting the cervical lymph nodes. This condition has significant historical and cultural implications, as it was once believed that royal touch could cure it. In modern medicine, scrofula is recognized primarily as a manifestation of tuberculosis (TB) or other infections, and understanding its causes, symptoms, and treatment options is crucial for effective management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of scrofula, its implications, and how it can be addressed in today's medical landscape.
symptoms: The symptoms of scrofula primarily revolve around the swelling of lymph nodes in the neck. Common symptoms include:
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Enlarged, tender lymph nodes, particularly in the cervical region.
Fever: Low-grade fever may accompany the swelling.
Night Sweats: Patients may experience excessive sweating during the night.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss can occur due to the underlying infection.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness and malaise are common.

diseases.name: Scurvy
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE

diseases.name: Sebaceous Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sebaceous cysts, also known as epidermoid cysts, are common skin growths that can occur anywhere on the body. While they are generally harmless, their presence can lead to discomfort, embarrassment, or complications if not properly managed. Understanding sebaceous cysts is essential for recognizing their symptoms, causes, and treatment options. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of sebaceous cysts, helping readers gain a better understanding of this condition.
symptoms: Sebaceous cysts are usually painless and may not cause any symptoms. However, some common signs include:
A small, round lump beneath the skin
A visible opening or punctum on the skin's surface
A thick, yellowish substance that may drain from the cyst
Redness or swelling if the cyst becomes inflamed or infected

diseases.name: Sebaceous Filaments - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sebaceous filaments are a common yet often misunderstood skin condition that can affect individuals of all ages. While they are often mistaken for blackheads or acne, sebaceous filaments serve a unique purpose in maintaining skin health. Understanding what sebaceous filaments are, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options can empower individuals to manage their skin better and maintain a healthy complexion. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of sebaceous filaments, ensuring that readers are well-informed about this skin phenomenon.
symptoms: Sebaceous filaments are typically asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause pain or discomfort. However, they can appear as small, yellowish or grayish dots on the skin's surface, particularly in areas with a high concentration of oil glands. They may become more noticeable when the skin is oily or when makeup is applied.

diseases.name: Sebaceous Hyperplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sebaceous hyperplasia is a common skin condition that often goes unnoticed but can be a source of concern for many individuals. It manifests as small, painless bumps on the skin, primarily on the face, particularly in areas where sebaceous (oil) glands are abundant. While sebaceous hyperplasia is generally benign and not harmful, understanding its significance is crucial for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of sebaceous hyperplasia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Sebaceous hyperplasia is characterized by the following symptoms:
Small Bumps: Soft, yellowish bumps that are typically painless.
Size: Each bump usually measures between 1 to 5 millimeters in diameter.
Location: Commonly found on the face, particularly on the forehead, cheeks, and nose.

diseases.name: Seborrheic Dermatitis - Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Dermatitis is a skin condition that is characterized by dryness and inflammation. Seborrheic dermatitis is a commonly occurring condition of the scalp characterized by scaly, red patches, and stubborn dandruff . Not just your scalp, but this condition can affect other parts of your body where the skin tends to get oily such as your eyebrows, face, chest, eyelids, etc.
symptoms: Commonly observed signs and symptoms of seborrheic dermatitis that you should pay attention to are::
Scaly patches on the scalp
Dandruff on the scalp, hair, eyelashes, eyebrows
Diffuse patches of oily or greasy skin covered by whitish-yellow flaky scales on the scalp, face, eyelids, eyebrows, chest, armpits, groin, etc.,
Itching
Redness and inflammation on the skin in certain areas
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Seborrheic Keratosis : Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Seborrheic keratosis is a type of non-cancerous skin growth. These usually indicate skin ageing. They appear gradually in variable numbers, commonly on the neck, chest, face, or shoulders. They are easily diagnosed and treated.
symptoms: The visual appearance of Seborrheic keratosis looks like moles, warts, barnacles, or skin tumors. They seem stuck onto the skin and appear waxy. These skin warts are usually not painful but sometimes may be associated with skin irritation or itchiness. Lesions are degenerative and tend to increase in number as time passes.
The size of keratosis ranges from tiny to 1 inch across. Four aspects usually describe the physical attributes of seborrheic keratosis:
