Location: The lesions usually are found on the scalp, shoulder, face, chest, abdomen, or back. They are most commonly found on skin folds but never on the soles of the feet or palms.
Texture: During the initial stages, they appear as small rough bumps. But gradually, they get thicker and tend to develop warty surfaces with a waxy and stuck-on appearance.
Shape: The shape of lesions varies from round to oval. They look like a flat or raised papule.
Color: Skin lesions can appear brown, or they can also get pigmented as yellow, black, or white warts.
Depending on the location of the lesions, sometimes they can be very annoying. It is recommended not to scratch the lesions as it may cause bleeding, swelling, or even infection.

diseases.name: Secondary Hypertension - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The single most highest contributor to the world’s disease burden is hypertension. A large majority of patients with hypertension suffer from primary hypertension, which has an unknown cause. The remaining patients have secondary hypertension, a condition where an underlying disease is responsible for the elevated blood pressure (BP).
symptoms: There are many causes:
Renal : Injuries to the kidney or narrowing of its arteries can result in poor blood flow. It can lead to increased production of a hormone called renin, which can increase blood pressure.

diseases.name: Secondary Infertility - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Infertility is a complex and often distressing issue that affects many couples worldwide. While primary infertility refers to the inability to conceive after one year of unprotected intercourse without a previous pregnancy, secondary infertility is a different challenge. Secondary infertility is defined as the inability to conceive after having one or more successful pregnancies. This condition can be particularly frustrating for couples who have previously experienced the joy of parenthood. Understanding secondary infertility is crucial, as it can have significant emotional, psychological, and social implications for those affected.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of secondary infertility is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Irregular Menstrual Cycles: Changes in menstrual patterns can indicate underlying reproductive issues.
Painful Periods: Severe menstrual cramps may suggest conditions like endometriosis.
Changes in Sexual Function: Decreased libido or discomfort during intercourse can be signs of fertility issues.
Previous Pregnancy Complications: History of miscarriages or ectopic pregnancies may indicate potential fertility challenges.

diseases.name: Segmental Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A segmental fracture is a specific type of bone fracture characterized by the presence of two or more fracture lines that create a "segment" of bone that is completely separated from the rest of the bone structure. This type of fracture is significant because it often results from high-energy trauma and can lead to serious complications if not treated properly. Understanding segmental fractures is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly impact recovery outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of a segmental fracture can vary depending on the location and severity of the injury. Common symptoms include:
Severe Pain: Intense pain at the fracture site, which may worsen with movement.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling around the affected area, often accompanied by bruising.
Deformity: Visible deformity or abnormal positioning of the limb.
Inability to Move: Difficulty or inability to move the affected limb.

diseases.name: Selective IgA Deficiency : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Selective IgA deficiency is an immunodeficiency disease. Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is an antibody blood protein found in mucous membranes, particularly in the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts. It also is found in breast milk, saliva, and tears. The body makes IgA and other types of antibodies to fight off illness. An IgA deficiency is when the body contains very little or no IgA.
symptoms: About 85 to 90% of IgA-deficient individuals are asymptomatic. Some patients with IgA deficiency tend to develop respiratory infections and diseases such as asthma and pneumonia .
Gastrointestinal infections and associated disorders, such as giardiasis malabsorption, lactose intolerance , celiac disease, ulcerative colitis, and nodular lymphoid hyperplasia may also develop.
IgA Deficiency also contributes to allergic disorders.
Several autoimmune diseases are caused by IgA deficiency, such as chronic inflammatory bowel disease, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis .
One in five cases of IgA deficiency are hereditary and passed down through family members who have IgA deficiency or similar disorders.

diseases.name: Selective Mutism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Selective Mutism is a complex childhood anxiety disorder characterized by a child's inability to speak in certain social situations, despite being able to communicate comfortably in other settings, such as at home. This condition can significantly impact a child's social interactions, academic performance, and overall quality of life. Understanding Selective Mutism is crucial for parents, educators, and healthcare providers to ensure that affected children receive the support they need to thrive.
symptoms: The symptoms of Selective Mutism can vary from child to child but generally include:
Inability to speak in specific social situations, such as school or public settings.
Consistent silence in these situations, despite being able to communicate verbally in familiar environments.
Excessive shyness or fear of social interactions.
Physical symptoms of anxiety, such as sweating, trembling, or stomachaches when faced with speaking situations.

diseases.name: Self-injury/cutting - Warning Signs, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Non-suicidal Self-injury/cutting is the term used to explain deliberately harming your own body, like cutting or burning yourself. It is done to cope with emotional traumas, anger, and frustration and it is usually not done with the intention of committing suicide .
symptoms: Symptoms of self-injury may include:
Scars
Bruises, scratches, or similar wounds
Keeping sharp objects in hand
Frequent accidental injuries
Emotional instability
Impulsive behavior
Feelings of hopelessness

diseases.name: Sensory Overload: Causes and Effects
diseases.description: Everyone may have experienced a feeling of confusion and irritation while being in a crowded place. It may be due to our brain’s incapability to simultaneously process all the sensory information. Sensory overload is an issue several people face, and it is crucial to know about it. This blog focuses on addressing what sensory overload is and various ways to manage it.

diseases.name: Separation Anxiety - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Separation anxiety is a common psychological condition that affects individuals of all ages, though it is most frequently observed in children. It is characterized by excessive fear or distress when separated from a primary caregiver or attachment figure. Understanding separation anxiety is crucial, as it can significantly impact a person's daily functioning, relationships, and overall quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of separation anxiety, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Symptoms of separation anxiety can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Excessive worry about losing a primary attachment figure
Persistent fear of being alone or without the attachment figure
Nightmares involving separation
Physical symptoms such as headaches, stomachaches, or nausea when anticipating separation
Clinginess or refusal to go to school or participate in activities without the attachment figure

diseases.name: Separation anxiety disorder & Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Separation anxiety disorder is a condition in which toddlers and children experience severe anxiety when separated from their parents. Separation anxiety is common among most kids. However, when this anxiety is prolonged and more serious, the child is diagnosed with separation anxiety disorder. Read on to learn more about separation anxiety, its symptoms, its causes, and treatments.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms that may indicate that your child are:
Recurrent, prolonged, and excessive distress about being away from home or loved ones, especially parents.
Constant, unusually excessive worry about losing a loved one to a disease, accident, or disaster.
Constant and excessive worry that something will happen to separate your child from its loved ones, such as a kidnapping.
Refusing to leave the house for school, work, play, trips, etc., due to the fear of being separated from the parents or other loved ones.
Not wanting to be alone without a parent or loved one.
Refusing to sleep away from home without a loved one nearby
Recurrent nightmares about separation.
Stomach aches, headaches , and other physical symptoms when your child gets separated from its loved ones.
Panic attacks when thinking about being away from a loved one.

diseases.name: Sepsis In Newborns - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sepsis in newborns is a critical medical condition that requires immediate attention. It occurs when the body’s response to an infection leads to widespread inflammation, potentially resulting in organ failure and death. Newborns, particularly those born prematurely or with low birth weight, are at a heightened risk for sepsis due to their immature immune systems. Understanding sepsis in newborns is vital for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment, ultimately improving outcomes for affected infants.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of sepsis in newborns is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Temperature Instability: Fever or hypothermia (low body temperature).
Respiratory Distress: Rapid breathing, grunting, or difficulty breathing.
Poor Feeding: Refusal to eat or difficulty feeding.
Lethargy: Unusual sleepiness or decreased responsiveness.
Irritability: Increased fussiness or inconsolable crying.
Skin Changes: Rash, jaundice, or mottled skin.

diseases.name: Septate Hymen - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The hymen is a thin membrane that partially covers the vaginal opening in females. While often associated with virginity and sexual activity, the hymen can take various forms, one of which is the septate hymen. This condition, characterized by a band of tissue that divides the vaginal opening, can have significant implications for a woman's health and well-being. Understanding septate hymen is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and potential complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of septate hymen, making it accessible for a general audience.
symptoms: Menstrual Issues: Women with a septate hymen may experience difficulty with menstrual flow, leading to painful periods or menstrual retention.
Pain During Intercourse: The presence of a septum can cause discomfort or pain during sexual activity.
Vaginal Discomfort: Some individuals may experience general discomfort in the vaginal area.
Difficulty with Tampons: Inserting tampons may be challenging due to the obstructed vaginal canal.

diseases.name: Septate Uterus : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: A woman’s uterus is divided into two parts due to a membrane called a septum, which is known as septate uterus. The membrane is made up of fibrous and muscular tissue that can be thin or thick. The condition is a birth anomaly, meaning the septate uterus develops when a fetus grows in the womb. Women with this condition are at a greater risk of miscarriage, preterm labour, pregnancy loss, and fetal malpresentation – a medical condition when the baby is not facing downwards when it’s being formed in the womb.
symptoms: Most women with a septate uterus are asymptomatic, meaning they do not display symptoms. Women typically become aware of the condition if doctors begin to examine the cause of repeated miscarriages. Sometimes doctors can discover it during a routine pelvic exam when the septum expands beyond the uterus to include the cervix and the vagina. The potential symptoms of a septate uterus include frequent miscarriages, painful menstruation and pelvic pain.

diseases.name: Septic Arthritis - Causes, Symptoms an Treatment
diseases.description: Septic arthritis is a painful infection that affects the joint fluid and tissues of a specific joint of your body. Germs, which travel from other parts of your body through your bloodstream, can cause this infection.
symptoms: The symptoms of septic arthritis differ from person to person. Signs and symptoms include:
Sudden joint pain
Redness and swelling in the knee and around the joint
Running a high fever
Due to stiffness, you find it difficult to move or put pressure on the joint
The skin over the particular joint feels hot
Low appetite and irritability

diseases.name: Septic Shock - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Septic shock is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body’s response to an infection leads to dangerously low blood pressure and organ failure. It is a critical medical emergency that requires immediate attention. Understanding septic shock is essential not only for healthcare professionals but also for the general public, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding septic shock.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of septic shock is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Fever or Hypothermia: A high fever or a body temperature below normal can indicate an infection.
Rapid Heart Rate: An increased heart rate is a common response to infection and low blood pressure.
Rapid Breathing: Increased respiratory rate may occur as the body attempts to compensate for low oxygen levels.
Confusion or Disorientation: Changes in mental status can indicate reduced blood flow to the brain.
Cold, Clammy Skin: Poor circulation can lead to cool, pale skin.
Decreased Urine Output: Reduced kidney function may result in less urine production.

diseases.name: Septicemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Septicemia, often referred to as blood poisoning, is a serious medical condition that arises when bacteria enter the bloodstream, leading to a systemic inflammatory response. This condition is significant because it can rapidly progress to sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body’s response to infection. Understanding septicemia is crucial for early detection and treatment, which can significantly improve outcomes and reduce the risk of severe complications.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of septicemia is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Fever: A high fever is often one of the first signs.
Chills: Patients may experience severe chills and shivering.
Rapid Heart Rate: An increased heart rate is common as the body attempts to fight the infection.
Confusion or Disorientation: Changes in mental status can occur, especially in severe cases.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing may arise as the condition progresses.
Low Blood Pressure: This can lead to shock, a critical condition requiring immediate medical attention.

diseases.name: Serotonin Syndrome: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Serotonin syndrome , also known as serotonin toxicity, arises due to the accumulation of chemical serotonin in your body. The intake of certain medications can cause this drug reaction.
symptoms: You may get the symptoms within minutes or hours of taking a specific medicine or when you increase the dosage of current medications.
The symptoms can be:
Disorientation
Confusion
Anxiety
Irritability
Muscle spasms and stiffness
Loss of muscle control
Tremors
Shivering
Nausea
Vomiting
Headache
Diarrhea
High blood pressure
Rapid heartbeat or tachycardia
Hallucinations
Heavy sweating
Dilated pupils
Hyperreflexia or overactive reflexes, or hyperreflexia

diseases.name: Serum Sickness - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Serum sickness is a type of immune response that occurs when the body reacts to certain medications or antigens, leading to a range of symptoms that can affect various systems. While it is often associated with the administration of antiserum or monoclonal antibodies, serum sickness can also arise from other sources. Understanding serum sickness is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as timely recognition and management can prevent complications and improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of serum sickness typically appear 7 to 14 days after exposure to the triggering substance and can include:
Fever: A mild to moderate fever is common.
Rash: A rash may develop, often resembling hives or urticaria.
Joint Pain: Arthralgia or joint swelling can occur, affecting mobility.
Fatigue: Generalized fatigue and malaise are frequent complaints.
Swollen Lymph Nodes: Lymphadenopathy may be present as the immune system responds.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms can also manifest.

diseases.name: Sesamoiditis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sesamoiditis is a condition that affects the small, round bones known as sesamoids, which are embedded within tendons. These bones play a crucial role in the function of the foot, particularly in the big toe, where they help to absorb shock and facilitate movement. Understanding sesamoiditis is significant not only for athletes and active individuals but also for anyone who experiences foot pain. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook of sesamoiditis, providing a comprehensive overview for those seeking to understand this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of sesamoiditis can vary in intensity but typically include:
Pain: A sharp or aching pain in the ball of the foot, particularly when pushing off during walking or running.
Swelling: Inflammation around the sesamoid bones, leading to visible swelling.
Tenderness: Increased sensitivity in the area beneath the big toe.
Difficulty Moving: Pain may limit the range of motion in the big toe, making it challenging to walk or engage in physical activities.

diseases.name: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS)
diseases.description: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome or SARS is a respiratory viral infection caused by SARS-associated coronavirus (SARS-CoV virus). The virus outbreak occurred in 2003, infecting over 8,000 people and claiming 774 lives. The good news is that the outbreak was over by July 2003, and since then, there have been no reported cases. SARS-CoV is a severe form of pneumonia that causes breathing problems, high fever, and body aches. SARS is contagious and spreads through air droplets if you come in close contact with the infected person.
symptoms: SARS-associated coronavirus may cause Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome. The initial symptoms are similar to common cold and flu, which may further lead to breathing issues. A person suffering from SARS may show the following symptoms:
High fever (body temperature over 100.4 F/38 C)
Body aches and muscle pains
Headache
Diarrhea
Dry cough and sore throat
Breathing problem leading to shortness of breath
Loss of appetite
Drop in the blood oxygen level.

diseases.name: Shaken Baby Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The shaken baby syndrome is a severe brain injury caused by forceful shaking of a toddler or infant that damages the infant’s brain cells preventing the child’s brain from receiving adequate oxygen. The shaken baby syndrome is medical negligence or abuse that may result in permanent damage to the brain or even lead to death.
symptoms: Since shaken baby syndrome damages the brain, outer injuries do not get seen. However, you can identify the condition through these symptoms:
Constant irritability or extreme fussiness.
Sleeping for prolonged periods than usual and facing difficulty and irritation in staying awake.
Respiratory problems and decreased appetite.
Nausea or skin turns blue or pale.
Paralysis , convulsions, or seizures .
Coma.
Sometimes, brain damage may show its repercussions on the outer body, too, such as:
Bleeding in eyes or ears.
Unexplained bruises on the face.
Damage of spinal cord or ribs.
Fracture of ribs, skull, legs, or other bones.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Sheehan's syndrome - Symptoms, Treatment and Causes
diseases.description: In Sheehan’s syndrome, women lose drastic amounts of blood while giving birth to a child or have low blood pressure reducing the oxygen supply to the woman. The deprivation of oxygen damages the pituitary gland. It is called Sheehan’s syndrome.
symptoms: It is difficult to notice symptoms of Sheehan’s syndrome in the initial days as they develop slowly. However, look out for the below:
Difficulty while breastfeeding .
Irregular menstruation.
Reduced growth of pubic hair.
Hypothyroidism : It occurs when thyroid glands don’t produce and release adequate thyroid hormones into your bloodstream. It slows down your body’s metabolic functioning.
Ineffective cognitive abilities.
Weight gain.
Low blood pressure .
Low body temperature.
Fatigue
Abnormal heartbeat.
Severely low blood sugar levels.
Shrinking breasts.

diseases.name: Shigella Infection - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Shigella infection is an infection caused by a family of bacteria known as Shigella. This bacteria affects the intestines and is very contagious. It can occur at any age and often infects children.
symptoms: Symptoms typically appear 1 or 2 days after you contract the bacteria. A few symptoms associated with it are:
Blood in stools
Diarrhea
Severe stomach pains or cramps
Fever or chills
Nausea or vomiting
Weight loss or dehydration
Symptoms may last for a week after you contract the infection. Some people may notice no symptoms, but their feces may still carry the infection.

diseases.name: Shigellosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shigellosis is a highly contagious bacterial infection that primarily affects the intestines, leading to severe diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. It is caused by a group of bacteria known as Shigella , which can be transmitted through contaminated food, water, or direct person-to-person contact. The significance of shigellosis lies in its potential to cause outbreaks, particularly in crowded settings such as daycare centers, schools, and refugee camps. Understanding shigellosis is crucial for prevention and effective management, especially in vulnerable populations.
symptoms: The symptoms of shigellosis typically appear 1 to 3 days after exposure to the bacteria and can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Diarrhea: Often watery at first, it can become bloody and accompanied by mucus.
Abdominal Pain and Cramps: Cramping can be severe and may be accompanied by a feeling of urgency to have a bowel movement.
Fever: A moderate fever is common, often accompanied by chills.
Tenesmus: A painful sensation of needing to pass stool, even when the bowels are empty.

diseases.name: Shin Splints (Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome)
diseases.description: Shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome) refers to pain along the inner edge of the shinbone (tibia). It is a common overuse injury affecting runners, dancers, and military recruits. Shin splints result from excessive stress on the shinbone and the connective tissues attaching muscles to bone.
symptoms: Tenderness, soreness, or pain along the inner side of the lower leg
Mild swelling of the lower leg
Pain that begins during exercise but may progress to pain at rest
Pain worsens with continued activity

diseases.name: Shingles (Herpes Zoster): Symptoms And Treatment
diseases.description: Commonly known as shingles, herpes zoster is a viral infection that causes a painful rash and blisters, caused by varicella-zoster, a virus causing chickenpox. After a person suffered chickenpox, the virus lies inactive in nerve tissue near the spinal cord and brain. After some time (years later), the virus may reactivate as shingles. Shingles typically appear in a stripe or group in a limited area on one side of the body. Rashes and blisters caused by shingles heal within 2-4 weeks, but in some cases, the pain stays on for long after the rashes go. This condition is called post-herpetic neuralgia in medical language.
symptoms: Shingles occur in phases.
The first stage of shingles before rashes and blisters appear is a burning or tingling sensation or itchy, sensitive skin — accompanied by fever, headache and a general feeling of discomfort.

The second stage starts a day or two later. In this stage, one will notice rashes that over time can become fluid-filled blisters. The blisters spread on the path of nerves that come out of the spinal cord.
The third stage is when the blisters burst to form small ulcers.
In the final stage, these ulcers dry and form crusts to heal the infected area.

diseases.name: Short Bowel Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: The bowels in the human body are made up of the small and large intestine. Most of the consumed nutrients are absorbed into the body during digestion in the small intestine. Short bowel syndrome, also known as a short gut syndrome, occurs when the body is incapable of absorbing adequate nutrients from the foods consumed because the patient does not have enough length of small intestine.
symptoms: Some of the common signs and symptoms of the short bowel syndrome include:
Diarrhea
Greasy, foul-smelling stools
Fatigue
Weight loss
Malnutrition
Swelling in the lower extremities

diseases.name: Shoulder Arthritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shoulder arthritis is a prevalent condition that affects many individuals, particularly as they age. It can significantly impact daily activities, leading to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility. Understanding shoulder arthritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain a better quality of life. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of shoulder arthritis, providing a comprehensive overview for those affected by this condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of shoulder arthritis can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Pain: A persistent ache or sharp pain in the shoulder, which may worsen with movement or at night.
Stiffness: Difficulty in moving the shoulder, especially after periods of inactivity.
Swelling: Inflammation around the joint may cause visible swelling.
Reduced Range of Motion: Limited ability to raise the arm or perform overhead activities.
Grinding or Popping Sensations: A feeling of grinding or popping when moving the shoulder.

diseases.name: Shoulder Dystocia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shoulder dystocia is a critical obstetric emergency that occurs during childbirth when a baby's shoulder becomes lodged behind the mother's pelvic bone. This condition can lead to serious complications for both the mother and the baby if not managed promptly and effectively. Understanding shoulder dystocia is essential for expectant parents, healthcare providers, and anyone involved in maternal and child health. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of shoulder dystocia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Shoulder dystocia is primarily identified during labor and delivery. The following symptoms may indicate its occurrence:
Difficulty Delivering the Shoulders: The most apparent sign is the inability to deliver the baby's shoulders after the head has emerged.
Turtle Sign: The baby's head retracts back into the birth canal after delivery, resembling a turtle retracting into its shell.
Prolonged Labor: Labor may be prolonged, and the mother may experience increased pain and pressure.
Fetal Heart Rate Changes: Abnormal fetal heart rate patterns may be observed, indicating fetal distress.

diseases.name: Shoulder Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shoulder fractures are a common injury that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. The shoulder is a complex joint that allows for a wide range of motion, making it susceptible to injuries, especially during falls or accidents. Understanding shoulder fractures is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective treatment, which can help prevent long-term complications and restore function. This article will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding shoulder fractures.
symptoms: Common symptoms of a shoulder fracture may include:
Severe Pain: Immediate and intense pain in the shoulder area.
Swelling and Bruising: Swelling around the shoulder joint and discoloration of the skin.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the arm or shoulder, often accompanied by a feeling of instability.
Deformity: In some cases, the shoulder may appear out of place or misaligned.

diseases.name: Shoulder Tendonitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shoulder tendonitis is a common condition that affects many individuals, particularly those who engage in repetitive overhead activities. It occurs when the tendons in the shoulder become inflamed, leading to pain and discomfort. Understanding shoulder tendonitis is crucial, as it can significantly impact daily activities and quality of life. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of shoulder tendonitis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of shoulder tendonitis can vary in intensity and may include:
Pain: A dull ache in the shoulder, often worsening with overhead activities.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion, making it difficult to lift the arm.
Swelling: Inflammation around the shoulder joint.
Tenderness: Sensitivity when touching the shoulder area.
Weakness: Difficulty in performing tasks that require shoulder strength.

diseases.name: Shwachman Diamond Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Shwachman Diamond Syndrome (SDS) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the bone marrow, pancreas, and skeletal system. It is characterized by a combination of bone marrow failure, pancreatic insufficiency, and skeletal abnormalities. Understanding SDS is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and families, as early diagnosis and management can significantly improve quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Shwachman Diamond Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Shwachman Diamond Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Bone Marrow Failure: This can lead to anemia, increased susceptibility to infections, and easy bruising or bleeding due to low platelet counts.
Pancreatic Insufficiency: Symptoms may include poor weight gain, diarrhea, and fatty stools (steatorrhea) due to malabsorption of nutrients.
Skeletal Abnormalities: These may include short stature, skeletal dysplasia, and other bone-related issues.
Dental Problems: Delayed tooth eruption and other dental anomalies are common.
Immune Deficiencies: Increased risk of infections due to compromised immune function.

diseases.name: Sialolithiasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sialolithiasis, commonly known as salivary gland stones, is a condition that affects the salivary glands, leading to painful swelling and discomfort. These stones can obstruct the flow of saliva, causing various complications if left untreated. Understanding sialolithiasis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of sialolithiasis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of sialolithiasis can vary depending on the size and location of the stone. Common symptoms include:
Pain and Swelling: Pain in the affected gland, especially during meals when saliva production increases.
Dry Mouth: Reduced saliva flow can lead to a dry mouth, making it difficult to swallow or speak.
Difficulty Opening the Mouth: Swelling and pain may restrict jaw movement.
Foul Taste or Bad Breath: Infection or inflammation can lead to unpleasant tastes or odors.

diseases.name: Sick Sinus Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sick Sinus Syndrome (SSS) is a heart condition that affects the heart's natural pacemaker, known as the sinus node. This syndrome is significant because it can lead to various heart rhythm problems, which may result in serious health complications if left untreated. Understanding SSS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that individuals can maintain a healthy heart rhythm and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of Sick Sinus Syndrome can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Often due to inadequate blood flow to the brain.
Palpitations: A sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeats.
Fainting or Near-Fainting: Episodes of syncope can occur, especially during physical activity.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, particularly during exertion.

diseases.name: Sickle Cell Anemia: Symptoms, Causes And Treatment
diseases.description: Sickle cell anemia is an inherited blood disorder that causes chronic destruction of red blood cells, episodes of intense pain, vulnerability to infections, organ damage, and, in some cases, early death. Sickle cell anemia is most common in people whose ancestors came from parts of Africa, Saudi Arabia, India and the Mediterranean region. To have a fully developed case of sickle cell anemia, one gene for the illness must be inherited from both parents. When a person inherits only one sickle cell gene from one parent, that person is said to have sickle cell “trait” rather than sickle cell anemia . People with sickle cell trait usually have no symptoms of sickle cell anemia, but they can pass the gene for sickle cell hemoglobin to their children.
symptoms: Symptoms of sickle cell anemia include:
Symptoms of anemia, including fatigue, shortness of breath, pale skin and fingernails
Jaundice , yellowing of skin and whites of eyes
Slowed growth and delayed puberty in children
Frequent infections
Eye problems, including blindness
Stroke

diseases.name: Sideroblastic Anemia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sideroblastic anemia is a type of blood disorder characterized by the body’s inability to properly incorporate iron into hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. This condition can lead to a variety of health issues, including fatigue, weakness, and more severe complications if left untreated. Understanding sideroblastic anemia is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of sideroblastic anemia can vary in severity and may include:
Fatigue: A common symptom due to reduced oxygen delivery to tissues.
Weakness: Generalized weakness and decreased exercise tolerance.
Pale Skin: A noticeable paleness due to reduced red blood cell count.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during physical activity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Especially when standing up quickly.
Cold Hands and Feet: Poor circulation can lead to feelings of coldness in extremities.

diseases.name: Signet Ring Cell Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Signet Ring Cell Carcinoma (SRCC) is a rare and aggressive form of cancer characterized by the presence of signet ring-shaped cells. These cells are named for their distinctive appearance, which resembles a signet ring due to the large vacuole that pushes the nucleus to one side. SRCC is most commonly associated with gastric (stomach) cancer but can also occur in other organs, including the breast, colon, and pancreas. Understanding SRCC is crucial due to its unique characteristics, aggressive nature, and the challenges it presents in diagnosis and treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of Signet Ring Cell Carcinoma can vary depending on the location of the tumor but may include:
Abdominal Pain: Persistent or severe pain in the abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Frequent feelings of nausea or episodes of vomiting.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can be a significant indicator.
Loss of Appetite: A noticeable decrease in appetite or early satiety.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or bloating after eating small amounts of food.
Dysphagia: Difficulty swallowing, particularly if the cancer is located in the esophagus or stomach.

diseases.name: Signs and Symptoms of Low Blood Pressure
diseases.description: Simply said, blood pressure is the pressure with which the blood flows through your blood vessels. When this pressure of the blood flow decreases beyond a certain level, you are said to be having low blood pressure .
symptoms: Among the various conditions people may experience, these are the most frequently observed symptoms of low blood pressure (hypotension):
Fatigue. Fatigue is a general overall feeling of tiredness and lack of energy.

Lightheadedness. It is the feeling that you might faint and that feeling that you are not getting enough blood in your head which feels light. It is one of the clearest symptoms of low blood pressure. Lightheadedness may be accompanied by clouded vision and dizziness, which increases the chance of a fall. Necessary precautions should be taken to prevent falls.
Dizziness. Dizziness is often accompanied by and is very closely related to lightheadedness. It might lead to fainting due to a loss of balance.

Nausea . Nausea is uneasiness in the stomach with a feeling to vomit. Nausea is usually succeeded by throwing up the contents of the stomach. Once nausea subsides, dehydration should be minimized by rehydrating.
Clammy skin. It means skin wet and sweaty skin.
Unconsciousness.
Blurred vision.
If low blood pressure is expected, it is suggested to try some simple ways to prevent symptoms like dizziness.
Increase water intake
Reduce or completely avoid alcohol consumption
Limit or avoid caffeine
In case you feel dizzy or lightheaded:
Lie down for a few minutes
Sit down and put your head between the knees
This will help your blood pressure go back to normal and help your symptoms go away.

diseases.name: Silent Heart Attack - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A silent heart attack, often overlooked and misunderstood, is a significant health concern that can have serious implications for individuals and their families. Unlike a typical heart attack, which presents with clear and alarming symptoms, a silent heart attack may occur without any noticeable signs. This article aims to shed light on what a silent heart attack is, its causes, risk factors, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook. Understanding this condition is crucial for early detection and effective management, ultimately saving lives.
symptoms: Silent heart attacks may not present with the classic symptoms, but some individuals may experience subtle signs, including:
Fatigue: Unexplained tiredness or fatigue that lasts for days.
Discomfort: Mild discomfort or pressure in the chest, back, neck, or jaw.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing during normal activities or at rest.
Nausea or Indigestion: Feelings of nausea, indigestion, or heartburn that may be mistaken for gastrointestinal issues.

diseases.name: Silent Hypoxia or Happy Hypoxia in COVID-19 Patients
diseases.description: As doctors and healthcare workers are busy treating people for COVID-19 owing to the second wave of the pandemic, many patients have reported a condition called ‘silent’ or ‘happy’ hypoxia. In happy hypoxia, patients have extremely low levels of oxygen in the blood, and yet do not show signs of breathlessness.
symptoms: Although the symptoms of Silent Hypoxia can vary from person to person, the most common symptoms include:
Cough
Confusion
Sweating
Wheezing
Shortness of breath
Rapid breathing
Fast heart rate or slow heart rate
Change of the colour of lips from natural tone to blue
Changes in the color of skin (from purple to red)
Apart from the COVID-19 symptoms , if an individual has ‘silent’ or happy hypoxia, he or she may display the following additional symptoms:
Dis-colouration of skin to red or purple tone
Profuse sweating even when not doing hard physical work

diseases.name: Silent Sinus Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Silent Sinus Syndrome (SSS) is a rare but significant condition that affects the paranasal sinuses, particularly the maxillary sinus. Unlike typical sinusitis, which presents with clear symptoms such as nasal congestion, facial pain, and fever, Silent Sinus Syndrome often goes unnoticed until it leads to more severe complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Silent Sinus Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. Understanding this condition is crucial for early detection and effective management, ultimately improving patient outcomes.
symptoms: Silent Sinus Syndrome is often asymptomatic, which is why it can go unnoticed for long periods. However, some individuals may experience:
Facial Swelling: A subtle swelling around the eyes or cheeks may occur due to the collapse of the sinus.
Vision Changes: Blurred or double vision can result from pressure on the optic nerve.
Nasal Congestion: Some patients may report a feeling of fullness or pressure in the nasal passages.
Headaches: Mild headaches may occur, although they are often not severe.

diseases.name: Silicosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Silicosis is a serious lung disease caused by the inhalation of fine silica dust, a common mineral found in various materials such as sand, rock, and clay. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on respiratory health but also due to its preventable nature. As industries such as construction, mining, and manufacturing continue to expose workers to silica dust, understanding silicosis becomes crucial for both prevention and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of silicosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of silicosis may not appear until years after exposure to silica dust. Common symptoms include:
Chronic Cough: A persistent cough that may worsen over time.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during physical activity.
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area.
Fatigue: General tiredness and lack of energy.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss may occur in advanced stages.

diseases.name: Sinus Tarsi Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sinus Tarsi Syndrome (STS) is a condition that affects the foot, specifically the sinus tarsi, a small cavity located on the outer side of the ankle. This syndrome is significant because it can lead to chronic pain and discomfort, impacting mobility and quality of life. Understanding STS is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to regain their normal activities and prevent further complications.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Sinus Tarsi Syndrome include:
Localized Pain: Pain on the outer side of the ankle, which may worsen with activity.
Swelling: Inflammation around the sinus tarsi area.
Tenderness: Sensitivity when pressure is applied to the sinus tarsi.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the ankle joint.
Instability: A feeling of weakness or instability in the ankle.

diseases.name: Sinusitis
diseases.description: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinus lining, often following a cold or allergies, leading to facial pain and congestion.
symptoms: Facial pain or pressure
Nasal congestion
Thick nasal discharge
Cough
Fever in some cases

diseases.name: Sinusitis – Types, Causes, Symptoms and Complications
diseases.description: Those who suffer from inflamed sinuses can give evidence as to how painful the condition can be. Find out more about sinuses and what causes them to get inflamed , leading to a condition called sinusitis.
symptoms: Symptoms of acute sinusitis:
Fever and body ache
Headache – a pressure-like pain and pain behind the eyes or above lips or tenderness of the face
Cough which gets worse at night
Nasal discharge and stuffiness
Sore throat and postnasal drip
Symptoms of chronic sinusitis: In chronic sinusitis, the symptoms are the same, but milder.

diseases.name: Situs Inversus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Situs inversus is a fascinating medical condition characterized by the reversal of the internal organs in the thoracic and abdominal cavities. While it may sound alarming, many individuals with situs inversus lead normal, healthy lives. Understanding this condition is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can have implications for diagnosis and treatment. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding situs inversus.
symptoms: Many individuals with situs inversus are asymptomatic and may not even be aware of their condition until imaging studies are performed for unrelated reasons. However, some may experience symptoms related to associated conditions or complications, including:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the abdomen may occur, particularly if there are associated gastrointestinal issues.
Respiratory Issues: Individuals with situs inversus may experience respiratory problems if they have associated conditions like Kartagener syndrome.
Digestive Problems: Some may have issues with digestion or bowel movements due to the unusual positioning of organs.

diseases.name: Sjogren’s syndrome – Symptoms and causes
diseases.description: Sjogren’s Syndrome is an autoimmune disorder that affects the salivary glands in your mouth and the tear glands in your eyes, causing them to dry up. The decrease in the production of tears and the saliva is the main identification factor for Sjogren’s syndrome.
symptoms: Sjogren’s syndrome is characterized by dry mouth and dry eyes , which form the identifying symptoms of the condition.
Dry mouth: You may feel like your throat is stuffed with cotton making it difficult to swallow or speak. Some people complain to have a chalky feeling in the mouth.
Dry eyes: The eyes will have a burning and itchy feeling, associated with grittiness. This increases the risk of infections in and around the eyes.

Apart from the main symptoms, there are few other symptoms associated that one might experience. It is important to note that this condition can also affect other parts of your body, followed by these symptoms.
Dryness of nose, lips and mouth and skin.
Inflammation of glands in your face and neck, particularly the ones behind your jaw and in front of your ears.
Vaginal dryness & Pelvic pain in women.
The decrease in the production of saliva can cause the formation of cavities and tooth decay.
Dry mouth can lead to inflammation of gums causing gingivitis.
Yeast infections in the mouth due to dryness.
Swelling, pain, and stiffness in joints, similar to Rheumatoid arthritis .
A dry cough that won’t go away.
Feeling tired all the time along with tingling sensations in hand and feet, from time to time.
Cancer treatment of the lungs, liver , and kidneys.
Some people complain of a burning sensation that travels from the stomach to the chest.
In some people, Sjogren’s syndrome is associated with cancer of lymph glands called lymphoma.

diseases.name: Sjögren's Syndrome
diseases.description: Sjögren's syndrome is a disorder of the immune system identified by its two most common symptoms — dry eyes and a dry mouth. The condition often accompanies other immune system disorders, such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus. The immune system mistakenly attacks the glands that produce tears and saliva.
symptoms: Dry eyes (feeling of grit in eyes)
Dry mouth (difficulty swallowing or speaking)
Joint pain, swelling, and stiffness
Swollen salivary glands
Skin rashes or dry skin
Vaginal dryness
Persistent dry cough
Prolonged fatigue
Neuropathy

diseases.name: Skin Allergy – Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: When the immune system reacts to something harmless, causing an allergic reaction is a skin allergy. Different allergens can cause allergies, such as pollen, plants, food, certain medications, etc. Itching, bumps, redness, and other skin conditions are common. Sometimes, their cause may not be easily identifiable. Sometimes, it can be due to medical conditions like chickenpox or measles . An allergist can diagnose the cause of an allergy. There are many preventive methods and treatment options available to treat allergies.
symptoms: Some of the symptoms of hives include:
The dermis (the deeper layer of the skin) becomes swollen due to the expansion of blood vessels.
Lips get swollen
Itching is common
May notice respiratory symptoms, such as a runny nose, wheezing, and breathing difficulty along with skin manifestations.
May notice heaviness in the chest and abdominal pain

Dry, itchy, and red skin constitute the most common symptoms. A person with atopic dermatitis experiences severe itching. Scratching in response to it only worsens the skin inflammation, in addition to worsening the itch itself.
In infants, acute eczema characterized by reddish raised lesions, crusting, and weeping is seen on the face, scalp, chest, and limbs. In severe cases, it extends to other areas too.
In children, acute eczema with skin pigmentation usually occurs, especially behind the knees and elbows.
In adolescents and adults, chronic eczematous lesions like thickening and prominent markings are seen.
The symptoms may be acute or chronic (long-standing)
As a rule, it affects the hands and the back of the fingers, and hands are more affected than the palms. Other exposed areas like the face, feet, and underarms may also be affected.
Itching
Redness and inflammation of the exposed area
Skin lesions or rash

diseases.name: Skin Cancer: Symptoms, Types And Treatment
diseases.description: Skin cancer is not just a cancer of the West. Know the facts so you may prevent it. As the name suggests, skin cancer attacks the skin tissue and refers to a condition wherein abnormal skin cells start growing uncontrollably. Skin cancer is amongst the fastest growing cancer types of recent times and we need to be aware of this potentially life threatening condition.
symptoms: The skin can appear to be shiny, small, waxy, rough, crusty and red. Some symptoms of this disease are:
Change in the size of a mole – When a mole’s diameter increases beyond 6mm or there’s the formation of new skin with bumps and nodes.
Change in the colour of a mole – When the infected skin completely loses its colour or becomes darker than the surrounding normal skin.
Change in the sensation of a mole – When the area becomes itchy, painful or tender.
When the borders of moles becoming irregular, notched and ragged
When an ulcer refuses to heal
When one half of the mole area becomes asymmetrically improportionate to the other half

diseases.name: Skin Diseases
diseases.description: The Skin is the largest organ of your body. There are various skin conditions that affect humans but many of the common skin conditions exhibit similar symptoms. However, it is important to understand the differences between them. Consult with Best Dermatologist will diagnose and treat your skin condition so that your lifestyle may not get disturbed. Listed below are some of the common skin conditions.

diseases.name: Skin Fungus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Skin fungus, often referred to as fungal skin infections, is a common yet often misunderstood condition that affects millions of people worldwide. These infections can range from mild irritations to severe conditions that require medical intervention. Understanding skin fungus is crucial not only for effective treatment but also for prevention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of skin fungus, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of skin fungus can vary depending on the type of infection but often include:
Itching: A common symptom that can range from mild to severe.
Redness and Inflammation: Affected areas may appear red and swollen.
Rash: Fungal infections often present as a rash, which can be scaly or flaky.
Blisters or Pustules: In some cases, blisters may form, leading to oozing or crusting.
Foul Odor: Certain fungal infections, particularly those caused by Candida, may produce a noticeable odor.

diseases.name: Skincare Tips for Combating Rosacea
diseases.description: Rosacea is a common skin condition where your face appears rather red on the cheeks , which may also produce small, red, pus-filled bumps. Symptoms of rosacea may remain for weeks and even months on end, eventually disappearing for a while only to resurface.
symptoms: The symptoms and signs of rosacea are as follows:
● Facial redness: Generally, rosacea causes a persistent redness in the central part of the face. Small blood vessels on our cheeks and nose swell often and become visible.
● Swollen, Red bumps: Most of the individuals with rosacea may also develop pimples on their face that look like acne . Such bumps contain pus sometimes. The skin may feel tender and hot.
● Eye problems: Most individuals with rosacea may also experience irritated, dry, swollen eyes including red, swollen eyelids.
● Enlarged nose: Rosacea, over time, can thicken your skin on the nose, causing the nose to appear bulbous (rhinophyma). This often occurs more in men than in women.
You need to consult your doctor to manage your rosacea; else, it might worsen

diseases.name: Skull Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A skull fracture is a serious medical condition that involves a break in one or more of the bones that make up the skull. The significance of a skull fracture cannot be overstated, as it can lead to severe complications, including brain injury, bleeding, and infection. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies for skull fractures is crucial for both patients and caregivers. This comprehensive guide aims to provide clear and accurate information about skull fractures, making it accessible to a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of a skull fracture can vary depending on the severity and type of fracture. Common symptoms include:
Headache: A persistent or severe headache is often reported.
Swelling or Bruising: Swelling or bruising around the site of the fracture may occur.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can indicate increased intracranial pressure.
Dizziness or Confusion: Changes in mental status may occur, especially if there is brain involvement.
Clear Fluid Drainage: Clear fluid leaking from the nose or ears may indicate a cerebrospinal fluid leak.

diseases.name: Slap Tear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A SLAP tear, or Superior Labrum Anterior to Posterior tear, is a common shoulder injury that affects the labrum, a ring of cartilage that surrounds the shoulder socket. This injury can lead to significant pain and dysfunction, impacting daily activities and athletic performance. Understanding SLAP tears is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, allowing individuals to regain full shoulder function and prevent long-term complications.
symptoms: Common symptoms of a SLAP tear include:
Shoulder Pain: A deep, aching pain in the shoulder, often exacerbated by overhead activities.
Clicking or Popping Sensation: A feeling of catching or popping in the shoulder joint during movement.
Weakness: Reduced strength in the shoulder, making it difficult to lift objects or perform overhead tasks.
Limited Range of Motion: Difficulty moving the shoulder through its full range of motion.

diseases.name: Sleep Deprivation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sleep is a fundamental aspect of human health, playing a crucial role in physical, mental, and emotional well-being. Sleep deprivation, a condition characterized by insufficient sleep, can have significant implications for overall health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of sleep deprivation, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis. By understanding sleep deprivation, individuals can take proactive steps to improve their sleep quality and overall health.
symptoms: Sleep deprivation can manifest in various ways, including:
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy.
Irritability: Increased mood swings and emotional instability.
Cognitive Impairment: Difficulty concentrating, memory problems, and decreased decision-making abilities.
Physical Symptoms: Headaches, muscle tension, and gastrointestinal issues.
Sleep Disorders: Increased likelihood of insomnia or other sleep-related issues.

diseases.name: Sleep Disorders
diseases.description: Sleep is a must for maintaining good health. Several disorders and disturbances may affect the duration and depth of your sleep. Sleep disorders are the sleep disturbances that interrupt the person’s capability to sleep well on a regular basis. These disorders result in inadequate sleep or excess sleep, causing numerous behavioral and cognitive problems.

diseases.name: Sleep Paralysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sleep paralysis is a phenomenon that many people experience at least once in their lives, yet it remains shrouded in mystery and misunderstanding. This condition can be both frightening and disorienting, often leaving individuals feeling helpless and confused. Understanding sleep paralysis is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for their loved ones and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of sleep paralysis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of sleep paralysis can vary from person to person, but they typically include:
Inability to Move: The most prominent symptom is the inability to move or speak, which can last from a few seconds to a couple of minutes.

Hallucinations: Many individuals report experiencing vivid hallucinations, which can be visual, auditory, or tactile. These hallucinations can be frightening and may involve the sensation of a presence in the room.
Chest Pressure: A common sensation during sleep paralysis is a feeling of pressure on the chest, often described as being unable to breathe or feeling suffocated.
Fear and Anxiety: The experience can provoke intense feelings of fear and anxiety, which may linger even after the episode has passed.

diseases.name: Sleep-related eating disorders - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: In sleep-related eating disorders, you suffer from uncontrollable eating and drinking while you are asleep. You may or may not be fully aware of your eating habits in your state of sleep, and you may not necessarily remember these actions after you wake up. Sleep-related eating disorders are linked with some medications or other kinds of sleeping disorders .
symptoms: A sleep-related eating disorder is an abnormal activity that happens while you are asleep or half asleep. The symptoms include:
Uncontrollable eating during nights, especially when you are sleeping or partially asleep
Diminished consciousness while eating.
Forgetting about the abnormal behavior by morning
Eating unhealthy food that is high in fats and drinking highly carbonated drinks
Consuming inedible items or even toxic substances
Not being able to wake up while eating
Change in eating habits
Drastic weight changes

diseases.name: Slipped Disc Exercises for Pain Relief and Treatment
diseases.description: A slipped disc, also known as a herniated, bulged, or ruptured disc, causes excruciating pain. The human spine is built to withstand a lot of bending and flexing, but it could eventually cause problems. Shock-absorbing discs surround each bone in the spine, and any issues concerning these discs are the reason for the pain. Knowing ways to handle pain is essential in cases of slipped discs. So, this blog focuses on pain relief exercises and treatment for people with slipped discs.

diseases.name: Small Bowel Prolapse or Enterocele - Symptoms, Causes, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Small bowel prolapse, also called enterocele, is an abnormal condition where the small intestine slides into the lower pelvic cavity making a bulge on the top part of the vagina. Although self-care measures can reduce the probability of small bowel prolapse, once it occurs, it needs to be treated.
symptoms: Mild enterocele doesn’t show any symptoms. However, you can lookout for the following symptoms in case of considerable prolapse:
Feeling heavy in your pelvic region or pulling sensation, but it dies down during sleeping.
Pressure, burning sensation , or pain in the pelvic region.
Feeling of fullness in the pelvic region.
You can also observe bulging of your outer vaginal area.
Lower back pain .
Painful intercourse or pain while urinating .
Feeling discomfort in the vagina.

diseases.name: Small Fiber Neuropathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Small Fiber Neuropathy (SFN) is a condition that affects the small nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system, which are responsible for transmitting pain and temperature sensations, as well as autonomic functions such as sweating and blood pressure regulation. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to chronic pain, discomfort, and other debilitating symptoms. Understanding SFN is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can often be overlooked or misdiagnosed due to its subtle and varied symptoms.
symptoms: The symptoms of Small Fiber Neuropathy can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Pain: A burning, stabbing, or tingling sensation, often in the feet and hands.
Numbness: Loss of sensation in the extremities, which can lead to difficulty with balance and coordination.
Temperature Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to heat or cold, which can cause discomfort.
Autonomic Symptoms: Issues such as excessive sweating, changes in heart rate, or gastrointestinal problems.

diseases.name: Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL): Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Every person has a type of white blood cell known as a lymphocyte that helps fight infections. But when cancer develops in these lymphocytes, it is known as small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). It is a slow-progressing cancer of the immune system. You may produce several ineffective lymphocytes that multiply in your lymph nodes.
symptoms: You may not show symptoms for several years. However, when you start to exhibit signs, they are as follows:
Painless swelling in the neck, armpits, and groin
Extreme fatigue
Unexpected weight loss
Fever
Night sweats
Swollen, tender belly
A feeling of fullness
Easily bruising and skin lesions
Loss of appetite
Shortness of breath

diseases.name: Small pox - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Smallpox is a highly contagious and deadly disease caused by the variola virus. It has played a significant role in human history, leading to widespread outbreaks and millions of deaths before its eradication in 1980. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared smallpox eradicated after a successful global vaccination campaign, making it the first disease to be eliminated by human effort. Understanding smallpox is crucial not only for historical context but also for recognizing the importance of vaccination and public health measures in controlling infectious diseases.
symptoms: The symptoms of smallpox typically appear 7 to 17 days after exposure to the virus and can be divided into several stages:
Incubation Period: No symptoms are present, and the person is not contagious.
Prodromal Stage: This stage lasts 2 to 4 days and includes: High fever Fatigue Headache Backache Vomiting
High fever
Fatigue
Headache
Backache
Vomiting

Rash Stage: After the prodromal stage, a rash develops, which progresses through several stages: Macules: Flat red spots appear on the face, arms, and legs. Papules: The spots become raised bumps. Vesicles: Fluid-filled blisters form. Pustules: Blisters fill with pus and become crusted over.
Macules: Flat red spots appear on the face, arms, and legs.
Papules: The spots become raised bumps.
Vesicles: Fluid-filled blisters form.
Pustules: Blisters fill with pus and become crusted over.
Scabbing: After about a week, the pustules scab over and eventually fall off, leaving scars.

diseases.name: Smith Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A Smith fracture is a specific type of wrist fracture that occurs when the distal radius bone in the forearm breaks. This injury is significant not only because of its impact on the wrist's functionality but also due to its association with various activities and risk factors. Understanding Smith fractures is crucial for both prevention and effective treatment, as they can lead to long-term complications if not managed properly.
symptoms: Pain: Severe pain in the wrist, especially when moving the hand or wrist.
Swelling: Swelling around the wrist joint.
Deformity: Visible deformity or abnormal positioning of the wrist.
Bruising: Discoloration around the fracture site.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty in moving the wrist or hand.

diseases.name: Smith Magenis Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Smith Magenis Syndrome (SMS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects multiple systems in the body, leading to a variety of physical, behavioral, and cognitive challenges. First identified in the early 1980s, this syndrome is characterized by distinctive facial features, developmental delays, and a range of behavioral issues. Understanding SMS is crucial not only for those directly affected but also for healthcare providers, educators, and families who support individuals with this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Smith Magenis Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Smith Magenis Syndrome presents a wide range of symptoms that can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Distinctive Facial Features: Individuals with SMS often have a broad forehead, deep-set eyes, a flat nasal bridge, and a prominent jaw.
Developmental Delays: Many children with SMS experience delays in speech and motor skills.
Behavioral Issues: Common behavioral challenges include aggression, self-injurious behavior, and sleep disturbances.
Sleep Disorders: Individuals with SMS often have difficulty sleeping, which can exacerbate other symptoms.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals may experience hearing impairments.
Skeletal Abnormalities: There may be issues with bone development, leading to scoliosis or other skeletal problems.

diseases.name: Smv Thrombosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: SMV Thrombosis, or superior mesenteric vein thrombosis, is a serious medical condition that occurs when a blood clot forms in the superior mesenteric vein, which drains blood from the intestines. This condition can lead to significant complications, including intestinal ischemia, which is a reduction in blood flow to the intestines, potentially resulting in tissue death. Understanding SMV thrombosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of SMV thrombosis can vary widely, but common signs include:
Abdominal Pain: Often sudden and severe, typically located in the middle or lower abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Accompanying the abdominal pain, these symptoms may indicate intestinal distress.
Diarrhea or Constipation: Changes in bowel habits can occur due to reduced blood flow to the intestines.
Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Fever: May occur if there is an associated infection or inflammation.

diseases.name: Snake Bites
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: You will know immediately when a snake has bitten you. Typical symptoms that accompany a snake bite are:
Two fang marks or wounds that look punctured
Bleeding from the wound
Localised Inflammation, burning and redness around the bite
Tremendous pain around the bite
Change in skin color
Diarrhoea and fever
Stomach ache and headache
Difficulty in breathing
Nausea and vomiting
Shock and Convulsions
Allergic reactions
Vision going blurry
Increased perspiration and salivation
Numbness and tingling in the limbs and the face, and drooping eyelids
Paralysis
Rapid pulse
Tiredness and muscle weakness
Thirst
Low Blood pressure

diseases.name: Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia)- Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: It is entirely normal to feel a little nervous in some social situations. But social anxiety disorder causes significant anxiety, embarrassment and self-consciousness in everyday social situations. Therefore, a social anxiety disorder is a definitive psychological disorder.
symptoms: A feeling of discomfort or shyness may not necessarily be a symptom of social anxiety disorder . The common signs and symptoms of a social anxiety disorder include:
Physical symptoms
Fast heartbeat
Trembling
Sweating
Lightheadedness
Nausea
Behavioral and emotional symptoms
Constantly worrying about humiliating or embarrassing yourself
Fear of certain situations where others may judge you
Extreme fear of interacting with new people
Avoiding interacting with new people out of a fear of embarrassment or humiliation
Avoiding being in situations where you may be the center of attention

diseases.name: Soft Palate Cancer- Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Your soft palate is situated at the upper portion of the back of your mouth, behind your teeth Soft palate cancer develops in the cells of the soft palate. It can affect individuals of all age groups. However, some people may be at a higher risk of developing soft palate cancer than others. The treatment options for soft palate cancer are the same as those for other oral cancer types – chemotherapy , radiation therapy or surgery.
symptoms: Difficulty swallowing food or liquids
Bad breath
Loose teeth
Bleeding
Difficulty speaking
Pain in the ear
Sores or ulcers in your mouth for a prolonged time
Swelling in your neck region
Mouth pain
White patches in your mouth that do not go away
Weight loss

diseases.name: Solar Retinopathy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Solar retinopathy is a serious eye condition that can result from direct exposure to sunlight, particularly during activities such as solar viewing or looking at the sun without proper eye protection. This condition is significant because it can lead to permanent vision loss if not recognized and treated promptly. In this article, we will explore solar retinopathy in detail, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: The symptoms of solar retinopathy can vary in severity and may include:
Blurred Vision: Difficulty seeing clearly, especially in bright light.
Central Vision Loss: A dark or blind spot in the center of the visual field.
Distorted Vision: Straight lines may appear wavy or bent.
Color Perception Changes: Difficulty distinguishing colors or changes in color perception.

diseases.name: Solitary Fibrous Tumors - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Solitary Fibrous Tumors (SFTs) are rare tumors that can arise in various tissues throughout the body, most commonly in the pleura, which is the lining of the lungs. Although they are classified as soft tissue tumors, their behavior can vary significantly, ranging from benign to malignant. Understanding SFTs is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as they can sometimes mimic other conditions, leading to delays in treatment. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of solitary fibrous tumors, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of solitary fibrous tumors can vary widely depending on their location and size. Common symptoms may include:
Chest Pain: Often associated with pleural SFTs, chest pain can be a significant symptom.
Cough: A persistent cough may occur, especially if the tumor is located in the lungs.
Shortness of Breath: Larger tumors can compress the lungs or airways, leading to difficulty breathing.
Fatigue: General fatigue may be experienced, particularly if the tumor is causing systemic effects.
Weight Loss: Unexplained weight loss can occur in some cases, particularly with malignant tumors.

diseases.name: Solitary Rectal Ulcer Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome is a rare medical condition that you develop when you get one or more ulcers in your rectum. Though the condition is called solitary rectal ulcer syndrome , more than one ulcer can form .Even though it is a rare condition, it can occur in individuals of any age group. It can be treated by making changes in your diet and lifestyle. However, doctors may recommend surgery in severe cases.
symptoms: The common symptoms are:
Rectal bleeding
Constipation
Rectal pain
Passing mucus from your rectum
Strain while passing stool
Pain in your pelvic region
Fecal incontinence
In some cases, you may not experience any symptoms .

diseases.name: Somatic Symptom Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Somatic Symptom Disorder (SSD) is a complex mental health condition characterized by an intense focus on physical symptoms that cause significant distress or impairment. These symptoms may or may not have a clear medical explanation, but the emotional and psychological impact on the individual can be profound. Understanding SSD is crucial, as it can affect anyone, regardless of age or background, and can lead to unnecessary medical interventions, increased healthcare costs, and a diminished quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Somatic Symptom Disorder, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Somatic Symptom Disorder is defined as a mental health condition where an individual experiences one or more physical symptoms that are distressing and significantly disrupt daily life. These symptoms can include pain, fatigue, or gastrointestinal issues, among others. Importantly, the symptoms are not intentionally produced or feigned, and the individual genuinely believes that they are experiencing these physical issues. The focus on these symptoms can lead to excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to the symptoms, which can exacerbate the condition and complicate treatment.
The symptoms of Somatic Symptom Disorder can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Chronic Pain: Persistent pain in various body parts without a clear medical cause.
Fatigue: Extreme tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Symptoms such as nausea, bloating, or changes in bowel habits.
Neurological Symptoms: Dizziness, headaches, or numbness that cannot be explained by medical conditions.
Sleep Disturbances: Insomnia or disrupted sleep patterns.
While not all cases of SSD can be prevented, certain strategies may help reduce the risk of developing the disorder:
Education: Increasing awareness about mental health and the mind-body connection can empower individuals to seek help early.
Healthy Lifestyle Choices: Encouraging regular physical activity, a balanced diet, and stress management techniques can promote overall well-being.
Social Support: Building strong social networks can provide emotional support and reduce feelings of isolation.

diseases.name: Somnambulism (Sleepwalking)
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms are:
Simply waking up in the middle of deep sleep
Sitting up and looking around
Walking around the house
Leaving the house in deep slumber
Driving long distances in a state of sleep
Talking (somniloquy) or screaming in sleep
Sleepiness during the day
No memory of the event
Associated injury
Inappropriate social behaviour like urinating in closets

diseases.name: Somniphobia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Somniphobia, often referred to as sleep anxiety or fear of sleep, is a condition that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. This phobia is characterized by an intense fear of falling asleep or the act of sleeping itself.
