While it may seem trivial to some, the implications of somniphobia can be profound, leading to insomnia, anxiety disorders, and other mental health issues. Understanding somniphobia is crucial for those affected, as well as for their families and healthcare providers, to ensure effective management and support.
symptoms: Individuals with somniphobia may experience a range of symptoms, including:
Intense Anxiety: A feeling of dread or panic at the thought of sleeping.
Physical Symptoms: Increased heart rate, sweating, trembling, or nausea when faced with the prospect of sleep.
Avoidance Behaviors: Staying awake for extended periods or using stimulants to prevent sleep.
Sleep Disturbances: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep, leading to chronic fatigue.

diseases.name: Somogyi Effect - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The Somogyi Effect, also known as the "rebound hyperglycemia," is a phenomenon that can occur in individuals with diabetes, particularly those who use insulin. It is characterized by a cycle of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) followed by a spike in blood sugar (hyperglycemia). Understanding the Somogyi Effect is crucial for effective diabetes management, as it can lead to significant fluctuations in blood glucose levels, complicating treatment and increasing the risk of long-term complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the Somogyi Effect, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of the Somogyi Effect can vary but typically include:
Hypoglycemia Symptoms: These may include sweating, shaking, irritability, confusion, and dizziness, which occur during the low blood sugar phase.
Hyperglycemia Symptoms: Following the rebound effect, symptoms may include increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, and blurred vision.

diseases.name: Sotos Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sotos Syndrome, also known as cerebral gigantism, is a rare genetic disorder characterized by excessive growth during childhood, distinctive facial features, and developmental delays. Understanding Sotos Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for families, caregivers, and healthcare professionals involved in the management of this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Sotos Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Excessive Growth: Children with Sotos Syndrome often experience rapid growth in height and head circumference, typically exceeding the 97th percentile for their age.
Distinctive Facial Features: These may include a long face, prominent forehead, and pointed chin.
Developmental Delays: Many children face challenges in speech and motor skills, leading to delays in reaching developmental milestones.
Cognitive Impairments: Some individuals may experience learning difficulties or intellectual disabilities.
Behavioral Issues: Children may exhibit behavioral problems, including anxiety and social challenges.

diseases.name: Spasmodic Dysphonia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spasmodic Dysphonia (SD) is a rare but impactful voice disorder that affects the ability to speak clearly and fluently. Characterized by involuntary spasms of the vocal cords, this condition can significantly disrupt communication, leading to frustration and social withdrawal for those affected. Understanding spasmodic dysphonia is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for their families, friends, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of spasmodic dysphonia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of spasmodic dysphonia can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Strained or Stuttered Voice: Individuals may experience difficulty initiating speech, leading to a strained or stuttered voice quality.
Breathiness: Some may notice a breathy quality to their voice, making it sound weak or soft.
Voice Breaks: Sudden breaks in the voice can occur, making it challenging to maintain a steady flow of speech.
Tension in the Neck and Throat: Many individuals report feeling tension or discomfort in the neck and throat area while speaking.

diseases.name: Specific Phobias - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Specific phobias are intense, irrational fears of specific objects, situations, or activities that pose little to no actual danger. These fears can significantly impact an individual's daily life, leading to avoidance behaviors that can interfere with work, social interactions, and overall quality of life. Understanding specific phobias is crucial not only for those who suffer from them but also for their families, friends, and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of specific phobias, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Individuals with specific phobias may experience a range of symptoms when confronted with their fear, including:
Intense Anxiety: A sudden surge of fear or panic when exposed to the phobic stimulus.
Physical Symptoms: These may include sweating, trembling, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, dizziness, or nausea.
Avoidance Behavior: Actively avoiding situations or objects that trigger fear, which can lead to significant lifestyle limitations.
Emotional Distress: Feelings of helplessness, embarrassment, or shame about the phobia.

diseases.name: Spermatocele - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spermatocele is a condition that affects the male reproductive system, specifically the epididymis, which is a coiled tube located at the back of the testicle. This condition is characterized by the formation of a fluid-filled cyst that can vary in size and may contain sperm. While spermatocele is generally benign and often asymptomatic, understanding its significance is crucial for men’s health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of spermatocele, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Most cases of spermatocele are asymptomatic, meaning they do not present any noticeable symptoms. However, some individuals may experience:
A painless lump or swelling in the scrotum
Discomfort or a feeling of heaviness in the affected testicle
Changes in the size of the cyst over time

diseases.name: Spider Angioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spider angioma, also known as spider nevus, is a common vascular lesion characterized by a central red spot with radiating blood vessels resembling a spider's legs. While often benign and asymptomatic, spider angiomas can indicate underlying health issues, particularly related to liver function. Understanding spider angiomas is essential for recognizing their significance in both cosmetic and medical contexts.
symptoms: Spider angiomas are typically asymptomatic, meaning they do not cause pain or discomfort. However, they can present with the following characteristics:
Appearance: A central red spot with radiating vessels, resembling a spider.
Location: Commonly found on the face, neck, and upper body.
Size: Can range from a few millimeters to several centimeters in diameter.

diseases.name: Spina Bifida Occulta - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spina Bifida Occulta is a form of spina bifida, a neural tube defect that occurs when the spine does not close completely during fetal development. Unlike its more severe counterparts, Spina Bifida Occulta often goes unnoticed and may not present any significant symptoms. However, understanding this condition is crucial, as it can lead to complications if left unmanaged. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Spina Bifida Occulta, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many individuals with Spina Bifida Occulta may not experience any symptoms. However, some common symptoms can include:
Back Pain: Chronic pain in the lower back may occur, especially in adulthood.
Skin Changes: Signs such as a tuft of hair, pigmented lesions, or dimples over the defect site may be present.
Neurological Symptoms: In some cases, individuals may experience numbness, weakness, or tingling in the legs.

diseases.name: Spinal Cord Injury
diseases.description: Spinal cord injury can be one of the most perilous injuries that can happen to a person. Depending upon its location and completeness, spinal cord injury may lead to paralysis and can even be life-threatening. Injuries in the cervical spine of the spinal cord are the most severe and can lead to complete tetraplegia. Tetraplegia, also called quadriplegia, is paralysis caused by injury or disease that results in partial or total loss of use of all four limbs including the torso.

diseases.name: Spinal Fractures - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spinal fractures are a significant medical concern that can lead to severe complications if not addressed promptly. The spine, composed of vertebrae, is crucial for supporting the body, protecting the spinal cord, and facilitating movement. When a fracture occurs in this vital structure, it can result in pain, mobility issues, and even neurological deficits. Understanding spinal fractures, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is essential for anyone looking to maintain spinal health and overall well-being.
symptoms: The symptoms of spinal fractures can vary depending on the severity and location of the fracture. Common symptoms include:
Severe Back Pain: Often sudden and intense, pain may worsen with movement or pressure.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty in bending, twisting, or standing up straight.
Numbness or Tingling: May occur if the spinal cord or nerves are affected.
Muscle Weakness: Weakness in the legs or arms, depending on the location of the fracture.
Deformity: Visible changes in posture, such as a hunched back.

diseases.name: Spinal Hemangioma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spinal hemangiomas are benign tumors that occur in the spine, often discovered incidentally during imaging studies for unrelated issues. While they are generally asymptomatic and do not require treatment, understanding their significance is crucial for early detection and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of spinal hemangiomas, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Spinal hemangiomas are often asymptomatic, meaning many people may not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Localized Pain: This is the most common symptom, often described as a dull ache in the back.
Neurological Symptoms: If the hemangioma compresses nearby nerves or the spinal cord, symptoms may include numbness, weakness, or tingling in the limbs.
Fractures: In rare cases, a hemangioma can weaken the vertebra, leading to fractures, which may cause severe pain and instability.

diseases.name: Spinal Muscular Atrophy Sma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is a rare genetic disorder that affects the motor neurons in the spinal cord, leading to progressive muscle weakness and atrophy. This condition is significant not only because of its impact on individuals and families but also due to its implications for public health and medical research. Understanding SMA is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: The symptoms of SMA can vary based on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Weakness: This is the hallmark symptom, often starting in the legs and spreading to other muscle groups.
Atrophy: Muscles may shrink in size due to lack of use.
Difficulty with Movement: Individuals may struggle with crawling, walking, or holding up their head.
Respiratory Issues: Weakness in the muscles that control breathing can lead to respiratory complications.
Swallowing Difficulties: Some individuals may experience problems with swallowing, leading to nutritional challenges.

diseases.name: Spiral Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A spiral fracture is a specific type of bone fracture characterized by a helical or spiral pattern along the bone. This type of fracture is significant not only because of its unique shape but also due to the mechanisms that typically cause it. Spiral fractures often occur in long bones, such as the femur or tibia, and can result from high-impact trauma or twisting forces. Understanding spiral fractures is crucial for both prevention and effective treatment, as they can lead to complications if not managed properly.
symptoms: The symptoms of a spiral fracture can vary depending on the severity of the injury but typically include:
Pain: Severe pain at the site of the fracture, which may worsen with movement.
Swelling: Swelling and bruising around the affected area.
Deformity: Visible deformity or abnormal positioning of the limb.
Inability to Use the Affected Limb: Difficulty or inability to bear weight or use the affected limb.

diseases.name: Spitz Nevus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spitz Nevus, often referred to as a Spitz mole, is a type of skin lesion that can be a source of confusion for both patients and healthcare providers. While it is generally considered benign, its appearance can sometimes mimic that of melanoma, a serious form of skin cancer. Understanding Spitz Nevus is crucial for early detection and appropriate management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Spitz Nevus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Spitz Nevi typically present with the following characteristics:
Color: They can be pink, red, or brown.
Shape: Usually dome-shaped and raised.
Size: They can vary in size, often measuring between 5 mm to 10 mm in diameter.
Surface: The surface may be smooth or slightly scaly.

diseases.name: Splenomegaly (Enlarged Spleen): Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Splenomegaly refers to a condition where a person’s spleen gets enlarged. The spleen is a small organ that produces white blood cells and antibodies and is located right behind the left rib cage. Splenomegaly may occur for several reasons and lead to severe complications if left untreated.
symptoms: Generally, splenomegaly shows no prior indicators. But in some cases, the patients may have frequent infections, bleeding, feeling of fullness without eating, pain in the upper belly that spreads to the left shoulder and low red blood cell count.

diseases.name: Splinter Hemorrhage - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Splinter hemorrhage is a medical term that refers to small, linear streaks of blood that appear under the nails, resembling splinters. These hemorrhages can be a sign of various underlying health issues, ranging from benign to serious conditions. Understanding splinter hemorrhage is crucial, as it can serve as an important indicator of systemic health problems, particularly those related to the cardiovascular system. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of splinter hemorrhage, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The primary symptom of splinter hemorrhage is the appearance of red or brown streaks under the nails. These streaks can vary in size and may be accompanied by other symptoms, depending on the underlying cause. Common symptoms associated with splinter hemorrhages include:
Nail discoloration: The streaks may appear alongside other nail changes, such as discoloration or brittleness.
Pain or discomfort: In some cases, individuals may experience pain or discomfort in the affected nail.
Swelling: There may be localized swelling around the nail bed.

diseases.name: Spondyloarthritis: Types, Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Spondyloarthritis (or spondyloarthropathy) is a group of inflammatory rheumatic conditions that cause arthritis. Spondyloarthritis differs from other types of arthritis as it involves the sites where ligaments and tendons attach to bones called ‘entheses’.
symptoms: The different types of spondyloarthritis can cause the following symptoms:
Back pain
Tiredness
Pain or swelling in the joints, including the hips, hands, wrists, elbows, shoulders, swelling in the knee , ankles, and feet
Swelling in the tendons of the toes or the fingers
Other problems can happen in patients with spondyloarthritis. These can include:
Osteoporosis
Psoriasis
Inflammation of the heart’s aortic valve
Inflammation of part of the eye, known uveitis , occurs in about 40% of those with spondyloarthritis.
Intestinal inflammation

diseases.name: Spondylolisthesis – Types, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: This tongue- twister called spondylolisthesis is derived from Greek words spondylos, meaning ‘spine’ or ‘vertebra’ (spinal bone), and listhesis, meaning ‘to slip’ or ‘to slide’. Spondylolisthesis is a type of spinal deformity where one vertebra (spinal bone) is displaced over the one below it.
symptoms: The most important symptom is pain in the lower back which gets worse after exercises, especially those which cause over-extension of the lower spine.
There may be a decrease in the range of motion of the lower back and tightness of the hamstrings.
Neurological symptoms like pain, numbness, tingling and weakness in the legs due to nerve compression.
In some severe cases there may be loss of bladder or bowel control.

diseases.name: Spondylolysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spondylolysis is a condition that affects the spine, particularly the lower back, and is characterized by a defect or fracture in a specific part of the vertebra called the pars interarticularis. This condition is significant because it can lead to chronic pain, reduced mobility, and, in some cases, more severe spinal issues if left untreated. Understanding spondylolysis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain an active lifestyle and prevent complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of spondylolysis can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Lower Back Pain: This is the most prevalent symptom, often described as a dull ache or sharp pain that may worsen with activity.
Muscle Spasms: Involuntary contractions of the muscles surrounding the spine can occur.
Stiffness: A feeling of tightness or reduced flexibility in the lower back.
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate down the legs, especially if nerve roots are affected.

diseases.name: Spondylosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Spondylosis is a term that refers to the degeneration of the spine, often associated with aging. It is significant because it can lead to chronic pain, reduced mobility, and a decrease in quality of life. Understanding spondylosis is crucial for early detection and effective management, allowing individuals to maintain their daily activities and overall well-being.
symptoms: Common symptoms of spondylosis include:
Chronic neck or back pain
Stiffness in the spine
Numbness or tingling in the arms or legs
Muscle weakness
Reduced range of motion

diseases.name: Sports Hernia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sports hernia, often misunderstood and misdiagnosed, is a condition that affects athletes and active individuals. It is characterized by chronic groin pain resulting from a tear or strain in the muscles or tendons of the lower abdomen or groin area. Unlike traditional hernias, which involve a protrusion of tissue through a weak spot in the abdominal wall, a sports hernia does not typically result in a visible bulge. Understanding sports hernia is crucial for athletes, coaches, and healthcare providers, as early recognition and appropriate management can significantly impact recovery and return to sports.
symptoms: The symptoms of sports hernia can vary in intensity and may include:
Chronic Groin Pain: A deep, aching pain in the groin that worsens with physical activity, especially during twisting or turning movements.
Pain During Exercise: Discomfort that increases during sports activities, particularly those involving sprinting, kicking, or sudden changes in direction.
Pain Relief at Rest: Symptoms may improve with rest but can return with activity.
Swelling or Bruising: In some cases, there may be mild swelling or bruising in the groin area.

diseases.name: Sports Injuries
diseases.description: Sports injuries are injuries that occur during athletic activities or exercise. They can result from accidents, inadequate training, improper use of protective devices, or insufficient warm-up and stretching exercises. The most common sports injuries are sprains and strains, knee injuries, swollen muscles, Achilles tendon injuries, pain along the shin bone, rotator cuff injuries, fractures, and dislocations.
symptoms: Pain
Swelling
Reduced range of motion
Bruising
Weakness
Inability to bear weight
Deformity in case of fracture

diseases.name: Sprained Thumb
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: The symptoms of sprained thumb include:
Swelling, tenderness and bruising on the joint
Excessive pain
Unable to grasp things
Instability in the joint

diseases.name: Sprains and Strains
diseases.description: A sprain is a stretching or tearing of ligaments (the tough bands of fibrous tissue that connect bones in a joint). A strain is a stretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon. Both are very common injuries, often occurring during sports or other physical activities. The ankle is the most commonly sprained joint; the back and hamstring are commonly strained.
symptoms: Pain
Swelling
Bruising
Limited ability to move the affected joint
Hearing or feeling a 'pop' in the joint at time of injury (sprain)
Muscle spasm
Weakness

diseases.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is the second most common type of skin cancer, often developing in areas frequently exposed to the sun, such as the face, lips, ears, and hands. While many cases can be treated successfully, SCC can sometimes grow more aggressively than other skin cancers, making early detection especially important. This guide provides clear and trustworthy information about SCC—its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, treatment options, and what you can expect along the way. Written in simple, patient-friendly language, our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and confident as you take steps to protect your skin and overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of squamous cell carcinoma can be subtle and are often mistaken for other common skin conditions. A key characteristic to look for is a spot that does not heal, or that bleeds and then scabs over and then bleeds again.

diseases.name: Squamous Metaplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Squamous metaplasia is a medical condition characterized by the abnormal transformation of one type of epithelial cell into squamous cells, which are flat and scale-like. This process can occur in various tissues throughout the body, including the respiratory tract, cervix, and urinary bladder. Understanding squamous metaplasia is crucial because it can be a precursor to more serious conditions, including cancer. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of squamous metaplasia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of squamous metaplasia can vary depending on the affected area. Common symptoms may include:
Respiratory Symptoms: Chronic cough, wheezing, or difficulty breathing may occur if the respiratory tract is affected.
Cervical Symptoms: Abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge may be present in cases of cervical squamous metaplasia.
Urinary Symptoms: Increased frequency of urination or discomfort may indicate squamous metaplasia in the urinary bladder.

diseases.name: Squamous Neck Cancer with Occult Primary - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Squamous neck cancer with occult primary is a unique head and neck cancer scenario where squamous cell carcinoma is found in the lymph nodes of the neck, but the original (primary) tumor cannot be located despite thorough testing. This situation can feel confusing and stressful. The good news is that there are proven, effective treatment paths designed specifically for this presentation, and outcomes are often strong with coordinated, expert care. This article explains symptoms, diagnosis, staging considerations, treatment options (surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiation, and proton therapy), recovery, prognosis, and prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: The most common first sign is a neck lump that persists. Symptoms can be subtle because the original tumor is small or hidden.
Common early signs:
A painless lump in the neck that doesn't resolve in 2-3 weeks
One-sided throat pain or ear pain (referred pain)
A feeling of something "stuck" when swallowing (dysphagia)
Advanced or additional symptoms:
Increasing difficulty swallowing, choking or coughing during meals
Unexplained weight loss and fatigue
Persistent sore throat, bad breath, or blood-streaked saliva
Noisy breathing or shortness of breath in more extensive cases
Voice changes (uncommon unless the larynx is involved, since most occult primaries are oropharyngeal)
Any neck mass that doesn't go away deserves prompt evaluation by an ENT or head and neck cancer specialist.

diseases.name: Staghorn Calculus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Staghorn calculus is a type of kidney stone that can significantly impact a person's health and quality of life. Unlike regular kidney stones, which are typically small and can pass through the urinary tract with relative ease, staghorn calculi are large, branching stones that can fill the renal pelvis and extend into the calyces of the kidney. Their size and shape can lead to serious complications, making it essential to understand their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of staghorn calculus, ensuring that readers are well-informed about this medical condition.
symptoms: Staghorn calculi can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Flank Pain: Severe pain in the back or side, often radiating to the lower abdomen.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which may appear pink, red, or brown.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often accompanied by discomfort.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to pain or obstruction.
Fever and Chills: Indicating a possible infection associated with the stone.

diseases.name: Staph Infections: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment
diseases.description: Staph Infections are caused by a group of bacteria called staphylococcui that can affect various parts of the body. They are generally found on the skin or in the nose of even healthy people. Most of the time, such bacteria cause no issues or result in relatively minor skin infections.

diseases.name: Stargardt Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stargardt Disease is a genetic eye disorder that primarily affects the retina, leading to progressive vision loss. It is one of the most common forms of inherited macular degeneration, particularly in children and young adults. Understanding Stargardt Disease is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for their families and caregivers, as it can significantly impact daily life and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Stargardt Disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Stargardt Disease can vary from person to person but often include:
Blurry or Distorted Vision: Individuals may notice that their central vision becomes blurry or distorted, making it difficult to read or recognize faces.
Difficulty Seeing in Low Light: Night vision may be impaired, making it challenging to see in dimly lit environments.
Blind Spots: Some individuals may develop blind spots in their central vision, known as scotomas.
Color Vision Changes: There may be difficulty distinguishing between colors, particularly in low light.

diseases.name: Status Epilepticus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Status Epilepticus (SE) is a serious medical condition characterized by prolonged seizures or a series of seizures without recovery in between. It is considered a neurological emergency that requires immediate medical attention. The significance of Status Epilepticus lies in its potential to cause lasting brain damage, cognitive impairment, and even death if not treated promptly. Understanding SE is crucial for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of Status Epilepticus can vary depending on the type of seizure but may include:
Convulsive Seizures: Characterized by violent shaking, loss of consciousness, and muscle rigidity.
Non-Convulsive Seizures: May present as confusion, staring spells, or unresponsiveness.
Postictal State: After a seizure, individuals may experience confusion, fatigue, or headache.

diseases.name: Status Migrainosus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Status Migrainosus is a severe and debilitating form of migraine that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Unlike typical migraines, which may last for a few hours to a couple of days, Status Migrainosus can persist for 72 hours or longer. This condition not only causes intense pain but can also lead to various complications if not managed properly. Understanding Status Migrainosus is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and effective management.
symptoms: The symptoms of Status Migrainosus can be debilitating and may include:
Severe Headache: The hallmark symptom is a throbbing or pulsating headache, often localized to one side of the head.
Nausea and Vomiting: Many individuals experience gastrointestinal symptoms, including nausea and vomiting.
Sensitivity to Light and Sound: Photophobia (sensitivity to light) and phonophobia (sensitivity to sound) are common.
Aura: Some individuals may experience visual disturbances, such as flashing lights or blind spots, prior to the onset of the headache.

diseases.name: STD (Sexually Transmitted Diseases) : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: An infection that is sexually transmitted is known as a sexually transmitted disease. Bacteria, viruses, and parasites cause some of these infections, which get transmitted through semen, vaginal fluid, blood, or other fluids secreted from the body. Sexually transmitted diseases are also commonly referred to as sexually transmitted infections.
symptoms: Sometimes, sexually transmitted diseases may go unnoticed due to asymptomatic cases, but most commonly, below are the symptoms that you can identify sexually transmitted infections with:
Bumps and pus-filled sores in private areas or genitals.
Difficulty or inflammation during urinating.
Discharge from vagina or penis.
Pain or discomfort during sex.
Bleeding in the vagina or penis.
Swelling in genitals.
Fever
Rashes and itching don’t go away.
Unusually smelling discharge in the penis or vagina

diseases.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) is a rare but serious condition that affects the skin and mucous membranes. It is characterized by the sudden onset of painful rashes, blisters, and peeling skin, often leading to severe complications. Understanding SJS is crucial not only for those who may be affected but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. Early recognition and prompt treatment can significantly improve outcomes and reduce the risk of long-term complications.
symptoms: The symptoms of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome can vary in severity and may develop rapidly. Common symptoms include:
Fever: Often the first sign, indicating an underlying infection or reaction.
Sore Throat: A painful throat may accompany the fever.
Skin Rash: A red or purplish rash that spreads and blisters, often resembling a burn.
Mucous Membrane Involvement: Painful sores in the mouth, eyes, and genital areas.
Flu-like Symptoms: Fatigue, malaise, and body aches.

diseases.name: Stickler Syndrome
diseases.description: Stickler Syndrome is a serious health disorder. It is also known us as hereditary progressive arthro-ophthalmopathy. Joint, vision, and hearing problems are some common issues associated with stickler syndrome.
symptoms: The symptoms of stickler syndrome vary from person to person. The standard symptoms of this disease are;
Eye problems. Apart from having a severe nearsightedness, children with Stickler syndrome often experience retinal detachments, glaucoma and cataracts.
Hearing difficulties are also common with people who have stickler syndrome. Many people experience problems hearing sounds at high frequency.
Affected children have over flexible joints and can get abnormal curvatures of the spine, such as scoliosis . Osteoarthritis can also occur.

Children with Stickler syndrome may often have distinctive facial features, such as a receding chin, prominent eyes and a small nose with scooped-out facial appearance. They are often born with a cleft palate.

diseases.name: Still's Disease (Adult-Onset Still's Disease)
diseases.description: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare form of inflammatory arthritis that features high fevers, rash, and joint pain. It is considered by many to be a spectrum of conditions related to systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, but occurring in adults. The condition may be self-limited, intermittent, or chronic.
symptoms: Quotidian fever spikes (high fever once or twice daily)
Salmon-colored skin rash appearing with fever
Joint pain and arthritis
Sore throat
Lymph node enlargement
Enlargement of liver or spleen
Elevated ferritin

diseases.name: Stillbirth : Types, Symptoms, Causes, Treatment and Risk Factors
diseases.description: When women lose their baby between the 20th week of pregnancy and birth, it is known as a stillbirth. If they lose the baby before the 20th week, it is typically known as a miscarriage. Stillbirths can be distressing for parents since many of them occur in normal pregnancies. The causes are unknown for about a third of the cases. Placenta or umbilical cord problems, infections, high blood pressure , congenital disabilities, or a poor lifestyle can cause stillbirths. Most women who suffer a stillbirth can have a healthy baby in their subsequent pregnancy.
symptoms: A stillbirth typically has no warning signs. However, the following symptoms could suggest a problem.

Vaginal bleeding, particularly in the second half of pregnancy, can indicate a problem with the baby. If women suffer bleeding, they must consult the doctor immediately. However, many women who suffer vaginal bleeding in their pregnancy go on to have a successful pregnancy.
Lack of movement or an alteration in the baby’s regular activity.

diseases.name: Stokes Adams Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stokes Adams Syndrome, often referred to simply as Adams-Stokes syndrome, is a medical condition characterized by sudden episodes of fainting or loss of consciousness due to a temporary interruption in the heart's electrical activity. This syndrome is significant not only because of its immediate effects on an individual's health but also due to its potential to indicate underlying heart conditions that may require urgent medical attention. Understanding Stokes Adams Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Stokes Adams Syndrome can vary in intensity and frequency. Common symptoms include:
Syncope (Fainting): Sudden loss of consciousness, often without warning.
Near-Syncope: Feeling faint or lightheaded without actually losing consciousness.
Palpitations: An awareness of irregular heartbeats or a racing heart.
Dizziness: A sensation of spinning or loss of balance.
Fatigue: Unusual tiredness or weakness, especially after physical exertion.

diseases.name: Stomach Cancer
diseases.description: The stomach as an organ receives and contains food before breaking down and digesting it. Stomach cancer begins when cancer cells form in the inner lining of your stomach. These cells can grow into a tumor. Also called gastric cancer, the disease usually grows slowly over many years.
symptoms: The following are the typical signs and symptoms:
Fatigue
Feeling bloated after eating
Feeling full even after eating little
Severe and persistent heartburn
Severe and unrelenting indigestion
Persistent and unexplained Nausea and Vomiting
Unexplained Stomach pain
Unexplained Weight loss

diseases.name: Stomach Polyps - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stomach polyps, also known as gastric polyps, are abnormal growths that form on the lining of the stomach. While many stomach polyps are benign (non-cancerous), some can develop into cancer over time. Understanding stomach polyps is crucial for early detection and management, as they can lead to serious health complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of stomach polyps, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Stomach polyps often do not cause noticeable symptoms, especially when they are small. However, larger polyps or those that cause complications may lead to the following symptoms:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the upper abdomen.
Nausea and Vomiting: Feelings of nausea or actual vomiting, which may include blood.
Gastrointestinal Bleeding: This can manifest as black or tarry stools or bright red blood in vomit.
Loss of Appetite: A decrease in appetite or unexplained weight loss.

diseases.name: Stomach Ulcers
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: In a lot of cases, ulcers may not have symptoms at all, but most noticeable symptoms may include:
Heartburn
Bloating
Nausea
Severe pain in the abdomen between meals
Vomiting blood
Weight-loss
Dark or black stool

If you feel any of the above symptoms, consult your doctor immediately. While in most cases, stomach ulcers are easily treatable, if ignored they may cause serious risk to your health such as bleeding, perforation of the heart and/or gastric obstruction.

diseases.name: Strawberry Hemangiomas - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Strawberry hemangiomas, also known as infantile hemangiomas, are benign vascular tumors that commonly appear in infants. These growths are characterized by their bright red color and raised appearance, resembling a strawberry, hence the name. While they are generally harmless and often resolve on their own, understanding their nature, causes, symptoms, and treatment options is crucial for parents and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of strawberry hemangiomas, ensuring that readers are well-informed about this common condition.
symptoms: Strawberry hemangiomas typically present with the following symptoms:
Appearance: Bright red, raised lesions that may feel warm to the touch.
Location: Commonly found on the face, scalp, neck, and sometimes on the trunk or limbs.
Growth Phase: Rapid growth during the first few months, followed by a gradual involution phase where the hemangioma shrinks and fades.

diseases.name: Strep Throat - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Strep throat is a bacterial infection which affects the throat, causing inflammation and making your throat feel sore and scratchy. This infection is commonly caused by group A Streptococcus bacterium.
symptoms: The following are some of the signs and symptoms:
Sudden and severe throat pain
Difficulty swallowing
Tonsils that appear red and inflamed, with white spots or pus stains.
Bright red patches on the upper jaw
Fever and dizziness
Severe headache
Irritation and rashes
Body pain and tiredness
Feeling nauseous and vomiting in younger age groups
Appetite loss

A dry throat is the most common symptom of a strep infection in any individual. Sore throats can also be caused by colds and other viruses. However, a virus will generally cause a runny nose, which is one method to identify the difference.

diseases.name: Stress - Types, Symptoms, Causes, Effects, Prevention & Management
diseases.description: A blood test, going on a solo trip, or meeting an investor for a start-up venture are all situations that may cause sweating, increased heart rate, and a decrease in appetite. It indicates signs of stress.

diseases.name: Stress Fractures
diseases.description: Stress fractures are tiny cracks in a bone caused by repetitive force or overuse, often from jumping or running long distances. They can also develop from normal use of a bone that has been weakened by osteoporosis. Stress fractures most commonly occur in the weight-bearing bones of the lower leg and foot.
symptoms: Pain that develops gradually and worsens with activity
Pain that diminishes with rest
Swelling on the outside of the ankle or foot
Bruising
Tenderness to touch at the fracture site

diseases.name: Stress Incontinence - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stress incontinence is a common yet often misunderstood condition that affects millions of individuals worldwide. It is characterized by the involuntary leakage of urine during physical activities that put pressure on the bladder, such as coughing, sneezing, laughing, or exercising. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to embarrassment, social withdrawal, and emotional distress. Understanding stress incontinence is crucial for those affected, as it can help in seeking appropriate treatment and support.
symptoms: The primary symptom of stress incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine during activities that increase abdominal pressure. Other common symptoms may include:
A feeling of urgency to urinate
Frequent urination, especially during the day
Leakage during physical activities, such as exercise or lifting

diseases.name: Stridor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stridor is a medical term that refers to a high-pitched, wheezing sound made while breathing, often indicative of an obstruction in the airway. This sound can be alarming, especially for parents of young children, as it may signal a serious underlying condition. Understanding stridor is crucial for recognizing when to seek medical attention and for managing the potential causes effectively. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding stridor.
symptoms: The primary symptom of stridor is the characteristic high-pitched sound during breathing. Other associated symptoms may include:
Difficulty Breathing: Patients may exhibit labored breathing or a sense of breathlessness.
Coughing: A barking cough may accompany stridor, especially in cases of croup.
Hoarseness: Changes in voice quality can occur due to laryngeal involvement.
Fever: In cases of infection, a fever may be present.

diseases.name: Stroke
diseases.description: A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a blood vessel breaks, causing brain cells to die quickly.
symptoms: Sudden weakness of face, arm, or leg
Trouble speaking or understanding speech
Sudden vision problems
Loss of balance or coordination
Severe sudden headache

diseases.name: Strongyloidiasis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection caused by the roundworm Strongyloides stercoralis . This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause severe health issues but also due to its often overlooked nature in many parts of the world. While it is endemic in tropical and subtropical regions, it can also affect individuals in non-endemic areas, particularly those who have traveled to or lived in affected regions. Understanding strongyloidiasis is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective treatment.
symptoms: Many individuals infected with Strongyloides stercoralis may remain asymptomatic. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Abdominal Pain: Often crampy and may be accompanied by diarrhea.
Diarrhea: Can be intermittent and may vary in severity.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms can occur, particularly during acute infections.
Skin Rash: A rash may develop at the site of larval penetration, often described as a pruritic (itchy) rash.
Fatigue: General malaise and fatigue are common complaints.

diseases.name: Sturge Weber Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sturge-Weber Syndrome (SWS) is a rare neurological disorder that primarily affects the skin and brain. Characterized by a distinctive facial birthmark and neurological abnormalities, SWS can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected. Understanding this condition is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can help mitigate its complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Sturge-Weber Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Sturge-Weber Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary significantly from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Port-Wine Stain: A flat, reddish-purple birthmark on the face, typically following the distribution of the trigeminal nerve.
Seizures: Many individuals with SWS experience seizures, which can begin in infancy or early childhood.
Developmental Delays: Children with SWS may have delays in reaching developmental milestones, including speech and motor skills.
Cognitive Impairments: Some individuals may experience learning disabilities or cognitive challenges.
Vision Problems: Glaucoma and other eye issues can occur due to increased pressure in the eye.
Hemiparesis: Weakness on one side of the body may develop due to brain involvement.

diseases.name: Stuttering - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Stuttering, also known as stammering, is a speech disorder that affects the fluency of speech. It is characterized by disruptions in the flow of speech, which can manifest as repetitions of sounds, syllables, or words, prolongations of sounds, or interruptions known as blocks. Stuttering is not just a speech issue; it can significantly impact an individual's social interactions, self-esteem, and overall quality of life. Understanding stuttering is crucial for early intervention and effective management, making it a significant topic in the field of speech-language pathology and general health.
symptoms: Stuttering can present in various ways, including:
Repetitions: Repeating sounds, syllables, or words (e.g., "I w-w-want a cookie").
Prolongations: Stretching out sounds (e.g., "I wwwwant a cookie").
Blocks: Pausing or struggling to produce sounds or words.
Secondary Behaviors: Physical movements or facial expressions that accompany stuttering, such as eye blinking or head jerking.

diseases.name: Stye - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A stye, also known as a hordeolum, is a common eye condition that can cause discomfort and concern for those affected. While often benign, styes can lead to complications if not properly managed. Understanding what a stye is, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for anyone who may experience this condition. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of styes, helping readers recognize the signs, understand the underlying causes, and know when to seek medical attention.
symptoms: The symptoms of a stye can vary but typically include:
A red, swollen bump on the eyelid
Tenderness or pain at the site of the bump
Increased sensitivity to light
Tearing or watery eyes
Crustiness around the eyelid, especially upon waking

diseases.name: Subacute Cutaneous Lupus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subacute Cutaneous Lupus (SCLE) is a form of lupus erythematosus, a chronic autoimmune disease that primarily affects the skin. It is characterized by specific skin lesions that can be triggered by various factors, including sunlight exposure. Understanding SCLE is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and the general public, as early recognition and management can significantly improve quality of life. This article aims to provide a thorough overview of SCLE, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of SCLE primarily manifest as skin lesions, which can vary in appearance. Common symptoms include:
Red, Scaly Patches: These lesions often appear on sun-exposed areas and may be ring-shaped or have a raised border.
Photosensitivity: Increased sensitivity to sunlight, leading to exacerbation of skin lesions after sun exposure.
Itching or Burning Sensation: Some individuals may experience discomfort associated with the skin lesions.

diseases.name: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
diseases.description: The subarachnoid space (SAS) refers to the space between arachnoid and the pia mater – innermost membrane that surrounds the central nervous system. The arachnoid is named for its delicate, spider-web-like filaments that extend from its undersurface. A subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding in this space between your brain and the surrounding membrane. Bleeding usually results from the rupture of an abnormal bulge in a blood vessel (aneurysm) in your brain. If this goes untreated, it may result in permanent brain damage or even death.
symptoms: When subarachnoid hemorrhage develops, you may experience numerous symptoms. A sudden and severe headache is the primary symptom. It is more intense at the base of the skull. Those who have experienced it describe it as the worst headache they have ever had. Similarly, you may also experience a popping sensation in your head before the hemorrhage starts. You may also experience the following symptoms:
· Numbness throughout the body
· Seizures
· Irritability
· Decreased vision
· Neck pain
· Shoulder pain
· Sensitivity to light
· Double vision
· Vomiting
· Confusion
· Nausea
· Quick loss of alertness

diseases.name: Subclavian Steal Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subclavian Steal Syndrome (SSS) is a vascular condition that occurs when blood flow is reversed in the subclavian artery, typically due to a blockage or narrowing (stenosis) in the artery. This condition is significant because it can lead to various neurological symptoms and complications, particularly affecting the brain and upper extremities. Understanding SSS is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as untreated cases can lead to serious health issues.
symptoms: The symptoms of Subclavian Steal Syndrome can vary widely among individuals, but common symptoms include:
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Often due to reduced blood flow to the brain.
Weakness in the Arm: Affected individuals may experience weakness or fatigue in the arm on the side of the blockage.
Coldness or Numbness: The affected arm may feel colder or numb compared to the other arm.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or transient visual loss can occur due to reduced cerebral blood flow.
Headaches: Some individuals report headaches, particularly in the back of the head.

diseases.name: Subclinical Hyperthyroidism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subclinical hyperthyroidism is a condition that often goes unnoticed, yet it can have significant implications for overall health. It is characterized by mildly elevated thyroid hormone levels without the overt symptoms typically associated with hyperthyroidism. Understanding this condition is crucial, as it can lead to various health issues if left untreated. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding subclinical hyperthyroidism.
symptoms: Subclinical hyperthyroidism often presents with few or no symptoms, making it challenging to diagnose without routine testing. However, some individuals may experience:
Mild weight loss
Increased heart rate or palpitations
Anxiety or nervousness
Fatigue or muscle weakness
Difficulty sleeping
Increased sensitivity to heat
Changes in menstrual patterns

diseases.name: Subclinical Hypothyroidism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subclinical hypothyroidism is a condition that often goes unnoticed, yet it can have significant implications for overall health. It is characterized by an underactive thyroid gland that does not produce enough hormones, but the symptoms may be subtle or absent. Understanding subclinical hypothyroidism is crucial, as it can lead to more severe thyroid dysfunction if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of subclinical hypothyroidism, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Subclinical hypothyroidism often presents with vague or mild symptoms, which can make diagnosis challenging. Common symptoms may include:
Fatigue or low energy
Weight gain or difficulty losing weight
Cold intolerance
Dry skin and hair
Constipation
Muscle weakness
Depression or mood changes

diseases.name: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage (Broken Blood Vessel in Eye)
diseases.description: A subconjunctival haemorrhage is a bleed that happens when a tiny blood vessel breaks just underneath the eye’s clear surface (conjunctiva). Most of the time, it does not require treatment. While the symptoms might be worrying, it is a harmless condition. It often goes away within two weeks or so.
symptoms: A bright red patch on sclera (the white) of your eye is the most obvious sign of a subconjunctival hemorrhage. Even though your eye may appear to be bloody, a subconjunctival hemorrhage should not cause any change in your vision. Similarly, there usually isn’t any pain or discharge from the eye.
The only feeling of discomfort may be a scratchy feel in your eye. The red spot may grow over one or two days. After that, it will gradually turn yellow as your eyes will start absorbing the blood.

If the condition continues for over two weeks or you are experiencing any pain or vision problems, you must consult a doctor. Similarly, if you notice any blood inside the iris (colored part of the eye, it is best to take medical help.

diseases.name: Subdural Hematoma
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Typical symptoms of a subdural hematoma are very similar to the symptoms of dementia, stroke, tumors or other brain-related problems like the following:
Speech slurring
Loss of consciousness, fainting or going into coma
Seizures
Numbness
Weakness
Severe headaches
Vision problems

diseases.name: Subgaleal Hemorrhage - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subgaleal hemorrhage is a medical condition that involves bleeding in the subgaleal space, which is located between the outer layer of the skull and the galea aponeurotica, a fibrous tissue that covers the skull. This condition is particularly significant in newborns, especially those who have experienced traumatic deliveries. Understanding subgaleal hemorrhage is crucial for parents, caregivers, and healthcare professionals, as early recognition and intervention can significantly impact outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of subgaleal hemorrhage can vary depending on the severity of the bleeding. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: A noticeable swelling on the head, particularly in the area of the scalp.
Bruising: Discoloration of the skin may be present.
Lethargy: The newborn may appear unusually tired or less responsive.
Poor Feeding: Difficulty in feeding or a lack of interest in feeding can be observed.
Rapid Heart Rate: Increased heart rate may indicate significant blood loss.

diseases.name: Subglottic Stenosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subglottic stenosis is a medical condition characterized by the narrowing of the airway just below the vocal cords, in the subglottic region of the larynx. This condition can significantly impact breathing and voice quality, making it a critical area of concern for both patients and healthcare providers. Understanding subglottic stenosis is essential, as it can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of subglottic stenosis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of subglottic stenosis can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Stridor: A high-pitched wheezing sound during breathing, especially when inhaling.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, particularly during physical activity.
Coughing: A persistent cough that may worsen with exertion.
Hoarseness: Changes in voice quality, including a raspy or weak voice.
Difficulty Swallowing: In some cases, patients may experience trouble swallowing.

diseases.name: Submucous Cleft Palate - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Submucous cleft palate is a congenital condition that affects the structure of the palate, which is the roof of the mouth. Unlike a complete cleft palate, where there is a visible gap in the palate, a submucous cleft palate is characterized by a hidden defect beneath the mucous membrane. This condition can lead to various complications, including speech difficulties, feeding problems, and ear infections. Understanding submucous cleft palate is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, ensuring that affected individuals can lead healthy, fulfilling lives.
symptoms: The symptoms of submucous cleft palate can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Speech difficulties: Children may have trouble articulating certain sounds, leading to speech delays or unclear speech.
Feeding problems: Infants may struggle with breastfeeding or bottle-feeding due to difficulty creating a proper seal in the mouth.
Nasal regurgitation: Food or liquid may come out of the nose during feeding, indicating a problem with the palate's structure.
Frequent ear infections: Dysfunction of the Eustachian tubes can lead to fluid buildup in the middle ear, resulting in recurrent ear infections.

diseases.name: Subungual Melanoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Subungual melanoma is a rare but serious form of skin cancer that occurs under the nails. While melanoma is often associated with sun exposure and skin lesions, subungual melanoma presents unique challenges due to its location and the difficulty in early detection. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of subungual melanoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies. Understanding this condition is crucial for early detection and effective management, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Subungual melanoma can present with various symptoms, which may include:
Dark streaks or spots: A common early sign is a dark line or spot under the nail, which may be mistaken for a bruise.
Nail discoloration: Changes in the color of the nail, including black, brown, or red hues.
Nail deformity: The nail may become distorted or grow irregularly.
Pain or tenderness: Some individuals may experience discomfort or pain in the affected area.
Swelling: Swelling around the nail bed may occur.

diseases.name: Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS)
diseases.description: Parents of newborn babies try their best to keep them healthy. However, sometimes, a baby may die due to unclear reasons even though they seemed perfectly fine. When this occurs when an infant is under the age of one, we call it Sudden Infant Death Syndrome SIDS . It often occurs when the baby is sleeping and is tough to predict.
symptoms: There are no noticeable symptoms when it comes to SIDS. It occurs suddenly and unexpectedly. A combination of physical as well as sleep environmental factors can make an infant more vulnerable to SIDS.
Physical factors
Physical factors associated with SIDS include:
Brain defects . The portion of the brain that controls breathing and arousal from sleep is defective or immature.
Low birth weight . Premature birth or being part of a multiple birth may cause baby’s brain to have not matured completely, with less control on automatic processes as breathing and heart rate.
Respiratory infection . These might contribute to breathing problems.
Sleep environmental factors
Examples include:
Sleeping on the stomach or side
Sleeping on a soft surface
Sharing a bed with parent or sibling may lead to inadvertent smothering
Overheating. Being too warm may increase a baby’s risk of SIDS

diseases.name: Suicide and Suicidal Thoughts
diseases.description: Suicide is said to be an act of taking one’s own life. Suicidal thoughts refer to having thoughts about taking one’s life. As per the World Health Organization (WHO), 700,000 people die because of suicide every year.

diseases.name: Sun Allergy - Types, Causes, Symptoms, Disgnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: A sun allergy is most commonly used to describe several skin conditions wherein an itchy rash, blister, or hives occur on the sun-exposed part of the skin. It is usually seen in people with sun sensitivity and most often occurs during spring and early summer. This article dives deep into the different aspects of sun allergy, types, causes, symptoms, treatment, and associated risk factors.
symptoms: The symptoms of sun allergy can vary widely, depending on the cause of the problem. Signs and symptoms may include redness, itchiness or pain, tiny bumps that may merge into raised patches, blisters or hives, and scaling, crusting, or bleeding.
Actinic prurigo : Individuals experience very itchy, crusted bumps (nodules).
PMLE and photoallergic reaction : In this, within two hours of sun exposure, the person may get a burning or itchy rash and fluid-filled blisters.

Solar urticaria : Individuals notice hives a few minutes after sun exposure. At first, a burning and stinging sensation may occur. The rashes fade slowly over days or weeks. Sometimes, the skin may darken after the reaction.
Signs and symptoms usually occur only on skin that has been exposed to the sun and typically develops within minutes to hours after sun exposure.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Sunburn-related Illness
diseases.description: Sunburn is skin damage caused by overexposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun or tanning sources.
symptoms: Red, painful skin
Warm or tender skin
Blistering in severe cases
Fever or chills in severe cases

diseases.name: Superfetation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Superfetation is a fascinating and rare reproductive phenomenon that occurs when a woman conceives a second fetus while already pregnant. This unusual occurrence raises questions about human reproduction and the complexities of gestation. While it is extremely rare in humans, understanding superfetation is significant for both medical professionals and expectant parents. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding superfetation.
symptoms: The symptoms of superfetation can be similar to those of a typical pregnancy, making it challenging to identify without medical intervention. Common symptoms include:
Nausea and Vomiting: Often referred to as morning sickness, these symptoms can occur in both pregnancies.
Fatigue: Increased tiredness is common during pregnancy and may be exacerbated in cases of superfetation.
Breast Tenderness: Hormonal changes can lead to breast sensitivity and tenderness.
Abdominal Discomfort: As the uterus expands, women may experience cramping or discomfort.

diseases.name: Superficial Thrombophlebitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Superficial thrombophlebitis is a condition that affects the veins just beneath the skin's surface, leading to inflammation and clot formation. While it may seem minor compared to other vascular conditions, its significance lies in its potential to cause discomfort and, in some cases, complications. Understanding superficial thrombophlebitis is crucial for early recognition and effective management, ensuring that individuals can maintain their quality of life.
symptoms: Common symptoms of superficial thrombophlebitis include:
Pain and Tenderness: Affected areas may feel painful or tender to the touch.
Redness and Swelling: The skin over the inflamed vein may appear red and swollen.
Warmth: The area may feel warm compared to surrounding skin.
Hardening of the Vein: The affected vein may feel firm or cord-like.

diseases.name: Superior Canal Dehiscence Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Superior Canal Dehiscence Syndrome (SCDS) is a rare but significant condition that affects the inner ear, leading to a range of auditory and vestibular symptoms. This syndrome occurs when there is a thinning or absence of bone overlying the superior semicircular canal, a crucial component of the vestibular system responsible for balance. Understanding SCDS is essential not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and appropriate management can significantly improve quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of Superior Canal Dehiscence Syndrome can vary widely among individuals but commonly include:
Hearing Changes: Patients may experience conductive hearing loss, which can be temporary or permanent.
Vertigo: A sensation of spinning or dizziness, often triggered by loud noises or changes in head position.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears, which can be persistent or intermittent.
Aural Fullness: A feeling of pressure or fullness in the affected ear.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance, particularly in challenging environments.

diseases.name: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome (SVCS) is a serious medical condition that arises when the superior vena cava (SVC)—a large vein that carries blood from the head, neck, upper body, and arms back to the heart—becomes obstructed. This obstruction can lead to a range of symptoms that significantly impact a person's quality of life and can even be life-threatening if not addressed promptly. Understanding SVCS is crucial for early detection and effective management, making it a significant topic in the field of medicine.
symptoms: The symptoms of Superior Vena Cava Syndrome can vary in severity and may develop gradually or suddenly. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: Noticeable swelling in the face, neck, and upper extremities due to increased venous pressure.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing, especially when lying down, as blood flow is compromised.
Coughing: A persistent cough may occur, sometimes accompanied by hemoptysis (coughing up blood).
Chest Pain: Discomfort or pain in the chest area, which may worsen with deep breaths.
Headaches: Increased intracranial pressure can lead to headaches.
Dizziness: Lightheadedness or fainting spells due to reduced blood flow to the brain.

diseases.name: Supraventricular Tachycardia - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Supraventricular tachycardia is an abnormal heart rhythm in which your heart beats faster than usual. The term has Latin roots. “Supra” means above, and “ ventricular ” refers to the lower chambers of your heart. Thus “supraventricular” means above your ventricles.
symptoms: Symptoms occur because your heart does not have adequate time to refill and push blood to your body. Following signs are seen in supraventricular tachycardia.
Rapid heartbeat
Chest pain
Pounding in your chest (palpitations)
Dizziness
Fatigue
Shortness of breath
Sweating
Near fainting or fainting ( syncope )

diseases.name: Susac Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Susac Syndrome is a rare and complex neurological disorder that primarily affects the brain, eyes, and inner ear. It is characterized by a triad of symptoms: encephalopathy (brain dysfunction), hearing loss, and vision problems. This syndrome is significant not only because of its unique presentation but also due to its potential for misdiagnosis and the challenges it poses in treatment. Understanding Susac Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Encephalopathy: This may present as confusion, memory loss, or cognitive difficulties.
Hearing Loss: Patients often experience sudden or progressive hearing loss, which can affect one or both ears.
Vision Problems: Visual disturbances, including blurred vision or central scotomas (blind spots), are common.
Headaches: Frequent headaches, often severe, can occur.
Balance Issues: Dizziness or problems with balance may arise due to inner ear involvement.

diseases.name: Sweet's syndrome - Symptoms,causes & types
diseases.description: While the name ‘ Sweet’s Syndrome’ is quite deceptive, it is one of the rare conditions that cause severe discomfort to a person. Unlike the name, Sweet’s syndrome is a skin condition that occurs on the arms, neck and the trunk of the body. It appears in red or purple colored patches on the body which are tender in nature that may ulcerate. Clinically this skin condition is known as ‘acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis’, or ‘Gomm – Button Disease’ . There isn’t any specific reason for Sweet’s syndrome to occur, but in most people, it can be triggered due to certain infections, fevers, inflammatory bowel disease , or as a side effect of certain medications. Sometimes it also occurs during pregnancy. In some rare cases, Sweet’s syndrome may also occur due to certain types of cancers, one of which is acute myelogenous leukemia .
symptoms: Itchy skin rash that appears shortly after a fever
Ulcers in the mouth
Small reddish bumps on the body that grow very rapidly, spreading into clusters which are painful
High fever
Fatigue
Basel cell carcinoma
Sore or swollen eyes
Joint and muscle pain

Diagnosis Sweet’s syndrome appears like a rash which rapidly increases and reaches an inflammatory stage. The condition is usually diagnosed to be abnormal when reddish clusters of bumpy skin rash start spreading all over the neck, arms and the trunk of the body. This occurs when the white blood cells (neutrophils) present in the upper layers of the skin increase. Doctors may suggest various tests to confirm the condition which includes the following:
Blood tests – To determine the level of neutrophils in the bloodstreams.
Skin biopsy – This is a test done under a microscope. A small piece of the abnormal skin is taken from the patient’s body and is tested to confirm the condition.
CT-Scans and X-Rays – These are recommended apart from the blood tests, to determine any underlying conditions leading to Sweet’s syndrome.

diseases.name: Swimmer's Ear - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Swimmer's Ear , medically known as otitis externa, is an infection of the outer ear canal that can cause discomfort and pain. It is particularly significant for those who frequently swim or engage in water-related activities, as moisture in the ear canal can create an environment conducive to bacterial growth. Understanding Swimmer's Ear is essential for prevention and effective management, especially for individuals at higher risk.
symptoms: Common symptoms of Swimmer's Ear include:
Itching in the ear canal
Redness and swelling of the outer ear
Pain, which may worsen when pulling on the ear
Discharge of fluid, which may be clear, yellow, or foul-smelling
Hearing loss, if the ear canal is swollen or blocked

diseases.name: Swimmers Shoulder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Swimmer's shoulder is a term that refers to a collection of shoulder injuries and conditions that are common among swimmers and other athletes who engage in repetitive overhead motions. This condition can significantly impact an athlete's performance and quality of life, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, and treatment options. In this article, we will explore swimmer's shoulder in detail, providing a comprehensive overview that is easy to understand for the general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of swimmer's shoulder can vary depending on the specific condition affecting the shoulder. Common symptoms include:
Pain: A dull ache or sharp pain in the shoulder, especially during overhead activities.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the shoulder joint.
Swelling: Inflammation around the shoulder joint.
Weakness: Difficulty lifting the arm or performing daily activities.

diseases.name: Swimmer’s Ear (Otitis Externa): Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Do you complain of having pain and irritation inside your ear? Did you notice any redness or discomfort after frequently using cotton swabs to clean your ear? These may be the signs of a swimmer’s ear, one of the most common bacterial infections of the ear. Visit an ENT specialist if you have any such problems and get yourself treated before the infection spreads to deeper parts of the ear.
symptoms: Some of the most common causes of swimmer’s ear are
Putting objects inside the ear like cotton swabs, ear pins, pen caps, fingers, etc., to clean the ears causes scratches or abrasions inside the ear canal.
Trapped moisture inside the ear while swimming, showering or bathing causes bacterial infection.
Sweat can also cause a swimmer’s ear.
People with narrow ear canal.
Age factor- can be seen in all age groups but is most common in children.
Skin problems like eczema and psoriasis can cause a swimmer’s ear, and so can cosmetic products or jewellery causing sensitivity reactions.
People suffering from swimmer’s ear often complain of the following symptoms-
Itching inside the ear
Irritation and discomfort
Pain, when left untreated, can become severe.
Difficulty in hearing .
Perception of sound may seem as muffled due to swelling of the ear canal.
Oozing pus or fluid from the ear canal
A feeling of fullness inside the ear may lead to partially blocking the ear canal.
In severe conditions, pain radiates towards the face, neck, and on the sides of the head and may even cause complete blockage of the ear canal, swelling of the lymph nodes of the neck.

diseases.name: Swimmer’s Itch - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Swimmer’s itch, otherwise known as cercarial dermatitis, is a rash caused by an allergy to certain parasites. These parasites typically get transmitted by infected snails into water bodies such as lakes and ponds. An interesting fact about these parasites is that humans are not suitable hosts for them. They tend to die after a few days of living on human skin.
symptoms: The primary symptom of a swimmer’s itch is a set of rashes on your skin, especially right after a swim in an unpurified water body such as a lake, pond, or sea. These rashes look like blisters or pimples and are red. They usually appear on exposed skin, that is, parts not covered by clothing or protective material. These symptoms can worsen if the exposure is regular.

diseases.name: Swine Flu - The Rising Pandemic Disease of the 21st Century
diseases.description: Swine Flu, also called A (H1N1) pdm09 Influenza Virus, is witnessing a sudden surge in most part of India, especially the western and southern states. India witnessed worst outbreak of Swine Flu in 2009-10 when nearly 50,000 people were affected and more than 2,700 losing their lives across the country. This year, there is an alarming rise in Swine Flu cases as many people have already lost their lives across the country.
symptoms: People affected with Swine Flu may experience:
Fever (but not always)
Weakness
Extreme breathlessness
Headache or sore throat
Body aches – pain in the muscles
Lethargy
Loss of appetite
Nausea/vomiting
Cough – can be dry
Malaise or high fever (101 Fahrenheit for more than 3 days)
Chills
Sneezing or runny nose

diseases.name: Swyer Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Swyer Syndrome, also known as 46,XY Gonadal Dysgenesis, is a rare genetic condition that affects sexual development. It is characterized by the presence of XY chromosomes, typically associated with male development, but results in female physical characteristics due to the underdevelopment or absence of functional gonads. This condition is significant not only for its medical implications but also for its psychological and social impact on those affected.
