Understanding Swyer Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, appropriate management, and support for individuals and families navigating this complex condition.
symptoms: Individuals with Swyer Syndrome may experience a range of symptoms, primarily related to sexual development:
Absence of Menstruation: Most individuals do not experience menstruation (amenorrhea) due to the lack of functional ovaries.
Underdeveloped Breasts: Breast development may be minimal or absent.
Short Stature: Some individuals may have a shorter than average height.
Lack of Secondary Sexual Characteristics: There may be a lack of typical female secondary sexual characteristics, such as body hair.
Infertility: Due to the absence of functional ovaries, individuals are typically infertile.

diseases.name: Sydenham Chorea - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Sydenham Chorea, also known as St. Vitus' dance, is a neurological disorder characterized by involuntary movements, emotional disturbances, and muscle weakness. It primarily affects children and adolescents, often following a streptococcal infection, such as rheumatic fever. Understanding Sydenham Chorea is crucial not only for those affected but also for parents, educators, and healthcare providers, as early recognition and intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of Sydenham Chorea can vary in severity and may include:
Involuntary Movements: Rapid, irregular movements of the arms, legs, and face.
Emotional Disturbances: Mood swings, irritability, and anxiety.
Muscle Weakness: Difficulty with coordination and balance.
Speech Changes: Slurred speech or difficulty articulating words.
Facial Grimacing: Uncontrollable facial expressions.

diseases.name: Symbrachydactyly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Symbrachydactyly is a rare congenital condition characterized by the underdevelopment or absence of fingers and/or toes. This condition can significantly impact an individual's daily life, affecting their ability to perform tasks that require fine motor skills. Understanding symbrachydactyly is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can improve the quality of life for those affected. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding symbrachydactyly.
symptoms: The symptoms of symbrachydactyly can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Underdeveloped Fingers or Toes: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of short or absent digits.
Limited Range of Motion: Individuals may experience difficulty moving their fingers or toes due to the underdevelopment of the associated structures.
Functional Limitations: Tasks requiring fine motor skills, such as writing or buttoning clothes, may be challenging.

diseases.name: Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD) is a condition that affects many individuals, particularly during pregnancy. It involves pain and discomfort in the pelvic region due to instability or dysfunction of the symphysis pubis, a joint located at the front of the pelvis. Understanding SPD is crucial, as it can significantly impact daily activities, quality of life, and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of SPD, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Pelvic Pain: The most common symptom, often described as a sharp or aching pain in the front of the pelvis.
Pain During Movement: Activities such as walking, climbing stairs, or turning in bed may exacerbate the pain.
Difficulty with Daily Activities: Simple tasks like dressing or lifting objects can become challenging.
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate to the lower back, hips, or thighs.

diseases.name: Symptoms and Treatment of Rectal Prolapse
diseases.description: The rectum is the lowest part of the human digestive tract. It may slip out of its actual position and drop further down. The rectum then tends to hang out through the anal opening. It looks like a small reddish, fleshy mass protruding out of the anus. This condition is not dangerous, but it makes bowel movements very troublesome. It is more common in elderly women above the age of 50.
symptoms: The feeling of something trying to bulge out of the anus, mainly during the bowel movement
A small, red mass is noticed hanging out of the anus, which can be pushed back by hand.
Continuous pain in the rectum and anus
Traces of blood or mucus in the feces, due to bleeding from the rectum.
Fecal incontinence (inability to control bowel movements)
Constipation or diarrhea
Feeling that your rectum isn’t empty after a bowel movement

diseases.name: Symptoms, causes and cure for Bird Flu
diseases.description: Bird flu belongs to a group of infectious diseases which primarily infects birds. But these conditions are also capable of infecting humans. One particularly deadly and most common sub type of this category is the H5N1 virus. Also known as avian influenza , it is quite deadly to poultry. This disease can be passed on to humans and other animals which come in contact with a carrier. Bird flu has been significantly found in nations like Bangladesh, India, China, Indonesia, Egypt and Vietnam. According to the World Health Organization, this disease is fatal for 60% of people affected. So, it is important to know the whys and hows of this serious disease.
symptoms: A person infected with the H5N1 virus is bound to develop certain serious symptoms. The incubation period generally ranges from 2 to 8 days, and could continue till 17 days, depending upon the type. You tend to suffer from typical flu signs and symptoms which include:
Dry cough
High fever , over 38 degrees centigrade
Pain in bones, joints and muscles
Hoarse voice
Blocked and runny noise
Bleeding nose
Extreme fatigue
Chest pain
Cold sweats and chills
Loss of appetite
Headache
Upset stomach, even diarrhea
Trouble sleeping
Malaise
Bleeding gums
Breathing difficulties
Pneumonia
Bloody sputum
Nausea and vomiting
Conjunctivitis
Multiple organ failure

diseases.name: Synovitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Synovitis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the synovial membrane, which lines the joints and produces synovial fluid. This fluid is essential for lubricating joints, allowing for smooth movement and reducing friction between the cartilage surfaces. The significance of synovitis lies in its potential to cause pain, swelling, and stiffness in the affected joints, which can severely impact a person's quality of life. Understanding synovitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as untreated synovitis can lead to joint damage and chronic conditions.
symptoms: The symptoms of synovitis can vary depending on the severity and underlying cause but typically include:
Swelling: The affected joint may appear swollen due to increased synovial fluid.
Pain: Pain in the joint, which may worsen with movement or pressure.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness, especially in the morning or after periods of inactivity.
Warmth: The skin over the affected joint may feel warm to the touch.
Redness: The skin may appear red or inflamed around the joint.

diseases.name: Syphilis: Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment and Prevention
diseases.description: Syphilis is an infectious illness caused by the pathogen Treponema pallidum . This sexually transmitted disease (STD) can spread via direct contact during vaginal, anal, or oral sex. The disease is highly contagious and can spread with sores of syphilis during direct sexual contact. Congenital syphilis can be transmitted from an infected mother to the fetus during pregnancy. After initial infection, the syphilis bacteria may remain inactive in your body for decades before getting active again. Sometimes, early syphilis can be cured with a single shot (injection) of penicillin.
symptoms: This disease is categorized into four distinct stages, namely, primary, secondary, tertiary, and latent. The signs and symptoms of syphilis vary, depending on the stage of illness.

Primary syphilis: A small sore called a chancre is the first sign of syphilis.The sore may appear at the place where the bacteria entered the body. There may be one or many .Usually, the chancre develops about 3 weeks after exposure. Many people with syphilis don’t notice the chancre because it’s usually painless and may be hidden within the rectum or vagina. Chancre heals on its own within 3 – 6 weeks

Secondary syphilis: The disease spreads to the skin, lymph nodes, and mucous membranes. Reddish-pink, symmetrical, and non-itchy rashes may appear on the trunk and extremities of the body, including your soles and palms. It begins within six weeks to six months of the infection and may last up to three months. The other symptoms of secondary syphilis are fatigue, headache , pain in joints, fever , weight loss , and swelling in the lymph nodes. These symptoms might disappear within some weeks or come and go repeatedly for as long as a year.

Latent syphilis: The third and hidden stage of syphilis often involves an absence of symptoms noted in the primary and secondary stages. This stage may be observed for several years before the complications of tertiary syphilis are observed.

Tertiary syphilis: Said to be the last stage of infection, tertiary syphilis can occur several years after the initial infection. This is a life-threatening stage of the illness generally associated with adverse health outcomes.

diseases.name: Syringoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Syringoma is a benign skin condition characterized by small, flesh-colored or yellowish bumps that typically appear around the eyes, on the cheeks, and on the upper chest. While syringomas are not harmful and do not pose any serious health risks, they can be a cosmetic concern for many individuals. Understanding syringoma is essential for those affected, as well as for healthcare providers who may encounter patients with this condition. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of syringoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Syringomas are characterized by the following symptoms:
Small Bumps: The most noticeable symptom is the presence of small, firm, flesh-colored or yellowish bumps on the skin.
Location: Syringomas commonly appear around the eyes, on the cheeks, and on the upper chest, but they can occur anywhere on the body.
Asymptomatic: In most cases, syringomas do not cause pain, itching, or discomfort.

diseases.name: Syringomyelia: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, Complications
diseases.description: Syringomyelia develops when a fluid-filled cyst forms within the spinal cord. Progressively, the cysts enlarge, damaging the spinal cord and leading to pain, weakness, stiffness, and other symptoms. It is also known as hydromyelia, syringohydromyelia, or Morvan disease.
symptoms: The syringomyelia symptoms gradually develop over time, depending on the size and location. If syringomyelia is due to Chiari malformation, the symptoms appear between ages 25 to 40. In certain instances, coughing and straining trigger the symptoms of the condition, but neither causes the development of syringomyelia. It can occur suddenly, too, due to accidents or falls.
The symptoms that can affect the different body parts, such as the back, shoulders, arms, and legs, are as follows:
Weakness in the muscle
Muscle atrophy
Loss of reflexes
Decreased or loss of sensitivity to pain and temperature
Headaches
Stiffness in the neck , back, arms, and legs
Pain in the neck, back, and shoulders
Curvature in the spine called scoliosis
Change or loss of bowel and bladder control
Sweating profusely
Numbness, tingling, burning, or piercing sensation
Paralysis , in extreme cases
Sexual issues
Irregular blood pressure levels
Involuntary and uncoordinated muscle movements

A patient suffering facial nerve damage can develop eye and face issues, which may lead to Horner syndrome. It leads to droopy eyelids, a narrow opening between the eyelids, reduced pupil size, and decreased sweating in the affected facial area.

diseases.name: Systemic Capillary Leak Syndrome - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Systemic capillary leak syndrome, also referred to as Clarkson’s disease, is a condition wherein your plasma from the blood leaks into adjacent body muscles and cavities that in turn may lead to a sharp drop in blood pressure that may lead to organ failure, or even death. Although it is a life-threatening situation, early identification and timely intervention can reduce the mortality rate.
symptoms: Systemic capillary leak syndrome manifests after an initial couple of days after non-specific symptoms like:
Irritability
Fatigue
Abdominal pain
Nausea
Muscle aches
Increased thirst
Sudden increase in body weight
This is followed by a leakage of plasma from blood vessels into body cavities leading to sudden drop in blood pressure and organ damage .

diseases.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
diseases.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the most common and severe form of lupus. It is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system produces antibodies that attack the body's own healthy tissue, causing widespread inflammation and damage in multiple organ systems including joints, skin, kidneys, heart, lungs, blood vessels, and brain.
symptoms: Butterfly (malar) rash across cheeks and nose
Photosensitivity
Oral ulcers
Non-scarring hair loss
Arthritis
Serositis (pleuritis, pericarditis)
Renal disorder (lupus nephritis)
Neuropsychiatric symptoms
Hematologic abnormalities
Fatigue

diseases.name: Systemic Mastocytosis - Symptoms, Causes, Complications and Treatment
diseases.description: Systemic Mastocytosis is a rare health condition where mast cells accumulate in your digestive tract, skin, bone marrow , and other body parts. The buildup of excessive mast cells can cause allergic reactions and inflammation, leading to organ damage.
symptoms: Mast cells can build up in your intestines, bone marrow, skin, spleen or liver. Less commonly, other organs like lungs, heart or brain also may be affected.
Signs and symptoms of systemic mastocytosis might include:
Itching, lushing or hives
Abdominal pain , vomiting , diarrhea , or nausea
Bleeding disorders or anemia
Muscle pain and bone
Lymph nodes , enlarged liver or spleen
Depression , mood changes

diseases.name: Systolic Heart Failure - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Systolic heart failure (SHF) is a significant health concern that affects millions of people worldwide. It occurs when the heart's ability to pump blood effectively is compromised, leading to inadequate blood flow to meet the body's needs. This condition can result in a range of symptoms and complications, making it crucial for individuals to understand its implications. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding systolic heart failure.
symptoms: Individuals with systolic heart failure may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Shortness of Breath: This may occur during physical activity or even at rest, particularly when lying down.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy is common.
Swelling: Fluid retention can lead to swelling in the legs, ankles, and abdomen.
Rapid or Irregular Heartbeat: Palpitations or a racing heart may be experienced.
Coughing or Wheezing: This may occur due to fluid buildup in the lungs.
Decreased Exercise Tolerance: Individuals may find it difficult to engage in physical activities they once enjoyed.

diseases.name: Sézary Syndrome - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Sézary syndrome is a rare and complex type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) that affects both the skin and the blood. Because its symptoms—such as persistent redness, itching, or skin changes—can resemble more common conditions like eczema or psoriasis, it is often difficult to recognize in the early stages. This comprehensive guide is designed to provide clear, compassionate, and easy-to-understand information about Sézary syndrome—covering its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, available treatments, and what to expect on your journey. Our goal is to help you feel informed, supported, and empowered to face this condition with confidence and hope.
symptoms: The symptoms of Sézary syndrome are often pronounced and can be debilitating. They are caused by the widespread presence of cancerous T-cells in the skin and blood.
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
Unexplained Fever: A persistent, unexplained fever.
Night Sweats: Drenching night sweats.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing weight without trying.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
If you have a persistent, widespread, and intensely itchy rash that does not respond to standard treatments, it is important to see a dermatologist for a proper evaluation.

diseases.name: T-Cell Lymphoma - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: T-cell lymphoma is a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that begins in T-cells, an important part of the body’s immune system. Because its symptoms can resemble those of more common conditions, it may be difficult to recognize at first. This guide provides clear and reliable information about T-cell lymphoma—its symptoms, how it is diagnosed, available treatment options, and what patients and families can expect. Understanding the condition can help you feel more informed and supported throughout the journey.
symptoms: The symptoms of T-cell lymphoma can be vague and are often mistaken for other, less serious conditions. However, if you experience these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
A Persistent Rash: In its early stages, MF often looks like a red, scaly rash that can resemble eczema or psoriasis.
Itching: The rash or skin lesions are often intensely itchy.
Light or Dark Spots: The affected skin may appear lighter or darker than the surrounding skin.
Plaques and Tumors: In advanced stages, the rash can turn into raised, thickened patches (plaques) and then into large, tumorous growths.
1. Swollen, Painless Lymph Nodes: The most common sign is a swollen lymph node, often in the neck, armpit, or groin.
2. "B" Symptoms: These are a group of systemic symptoms that are a major red flag for lymphoma.
Unexplained Fever: A fever that comes and goes for no apparent reason.
Drenching Night Sweats: Sweating so much at night that you have to change your clothes or bedsheets.
Unexplained Weight Loss: Losing more than 10% of your body weight in six months without trying.
3. Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
If you have a swollen lymph node that doesn't go away, or a persistent rash that doesn't respond to standard treatments, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.

diseases.name: Takayasu’s Arteritis
diseases.description: Takayasu’s arteritis is a rare vasculitis, a group of disorders that causes blood vessel inflammation. the inflammation damages the aorta including its main branches in Takayasu’s arteritis.
symptoms: Depending on the symptoms seen, a doctor can categorize Takayasu’s arteritis into three different stages.
Stage 1 symptoms:
Fatigue
Unexplained weight loss
Muscle pain
Joint pain
Low-grade fever
These are common symptoms and are not that conclusive.The damage to the arterial walls could go on for years before it is noticed .
Stage 2 symptoms:
Pain or weakness in your limbs while using
A weak pulse – difficulty getting blood pressure or difference in blood pressure between the arms
High blood pressure
Dizziness, painting or lightheadedness
Trouble thinking or memory problems
Visual changes or headaches
Shortness of breath or chest pain
Anemia (too few red blood cells)
Diarrhea or blood in your stool
These symptoms denote a more advanced stage resulting from obstructed blood flow from the heart to other parts of the body.
When do you need to see a doctor?

Immediate medical care should be sought if you are having pain in your arms and chest with shortness of breath. Also look out for symptoms of stroke like arm weakness, difficulty in speaking or face drooping. Earlier the detection more effective the treatment will be. If you already have been diagnosed with Takayasu’s arteritis , observe the types of symptoms you are experiencing. Keeping a track of all these will help your doctor to treat you effectively.

Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: Talus Fracture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A talus fracture is a break in one of the bones that make up the ankle joint, specifically the talus bone. This bone plays a crucial role in connecting the leg to the foot and is essential for proper movement and weight-bearing. Talus fractures are significant because they can lead to complications such as chronic pain, arthritis, and impaired mobility if not treated properly. Understanding the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options for talus fractures is vital for anyone who may be at risk or experiencing related symptoms.
symptoms: Pain: Severe pain in the ankle or foot, especially when bearing weight.
Swelling: Swelling around the ankle joint.
Bruising: Discoloration of the skin around the injury site.
Limited Mobility: Difficulty moving the ankle or foot.
Deformity: In some cases, the foot may appear deformed or out of alignment.

diseases.name: Tapeworm Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tapeworm infection , also known as taeniasis, is a parasitic disease caused by flat, segmented worms belonging to the class Cestoda. These infections are significant due to their potential to cause various health issues, ranging from mild gastrointestinal discomfort to severe complications if left untreated. Understanding tapeworm infections is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective treatment.
symptoms: Common symptoms of tapeworm infection may include:
Abdominal pain or discomfort
Nausea and vomiting
Diarrhea or constipation
Unexplained weight loss
Fatigue
Visible segments of the tapeworm in stool
Warning Signs: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or signs of intestinal obstruction, such as severe bloating or inability to pass gas.

diseases.name: Tarlov Cyst - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tarlov cysts, also known as perineural cysts, are fluid-filled sacs that develop on the nerve roots of the spine, particularly in the sacral region. While many individuals with Tarlov cysts remain asymptomatic, these cysts can lead to significant discomfort and neurological issues in some cases. Understanding Tarlov cysts is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, especially for those experiencing symptoms. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Tarlov cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many individuals with Tarlov cysts do not experience symptoms. However, when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Pain: Localized pain in the lower back or sacral region.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations in the legs, buttocks, or pelvic area.
Weakness: Muscle weakness in the lower extremities.
Bowel or Bladder Dysfunction: Issues such as incontinence or difficulty urinating.
Sexual Dysfunction: Changes in sexual function or sensation.

diseases.name: Tarsal Coalition - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tarsal coalition is a condition that affects the bones in the foot, specifically the tarsal bones, which are located in the midfoot. This condition can lead to significant discomfort and mobility issues, making it essential for individuals to understand its implications. Tarsal coalition is often overlooked, yet it can have a profound impact on a person's quality of life. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding tarsal coalition.
symptoms: Foot Pain: The most common symptom, often localized to the midfoot or heel.
Stiffness: Limited range of motion in the foot, particularly during activities.
Swelling: Inflammation around the affected area may occur.
Flatfoot: A flatfoot deformity may develop due to the coalition.
Difficulty Walking: Pain and stiffness can lead to an altered gait.

diseases.name: Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome (TTS) is a condition that affects the foot, specifically the area around the tarsal tunnel, a narrow space located on the inside of the ankle. This syndrome occurs when the posterior tibial nerve, which runs through the tarsal tunnel, becomes compressed or irritated. Understanding Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome is crucial, as it can lead to significant discomfort and mobility issues if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of TTS, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of Tarsal Tunnel Syndrome can vary in intensity and may include:
Pain: A sharp or burning pain in the heel, arch, or toes.
Tingling or Numbness: A sensation of pins and needles, often felt in the foot or toes.
Weakness: Difficulty in moving the toes or foot.
Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to touch in the affected area.

diseases.name: Tartar - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tartar, also known as dental calculus, is a hardened form of dental plaque that forms on teeth when plaque is not removed through regular brushing and flossing. It is significant because it can lead to various dental issues, including gum disease, cavities, and bad breath. Understanding tartar is essential for maintaining oral health and preventing more severe complications.
symptoms: Visible Deposits: Yellow or brownish deposits on teeth, especially near the gum line.
Bad Breath: Persistent bad breath can be a sign of tartar buildup and associated gum disease.
Gum Inflammation: Red, swollen gums that may bleed during brushing or flossing.
Tooth Sensitivity: Increased sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods and beverages.

diseases.name: Tattoo Infection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tattoos have become a popular form of self-expression, with millions of people around the world choosing to adorn their bodies with intricate designs and meaningful symbols. However, while tattoos can be a beautiful addition to one’s appearance, they also come with certain risks, one of the most concerning being tattoo infection. Understanding tattoo infection is crucial for anyone considering getting a tattoo, as well as for those who already have one. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of tattoo infections, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of a tattoo infection is crucial for early intervention. Common symptoms include:
Redness: The area around the tattoo may become red and inflamed.
Swelling: The skin may swell, indicating an inflammatory response.
Pain: Increased sensitivity or pain at the tattoo site can be a sign of infection.
Pus or Discharge: The presence of yellow or green pus is a clear indicator of infection.
Fever: In some cases, a systemic infection may lead to fever and chills.

diseases.name: Tay-Sachs Disease
diseases.description: Tay-Sachs disease i s a genetic disorder, which is passed on to children from parents. It leads to improper functioning of the nerves.
symptoms: If a child has Tay-Sachs disease, he/she will begin showing the symptoms from a very early age. The common symptoms are:
Vision loss
Hearing disability
Seizures
Muscle weakness
Loss of motor skills
Exaggerated reaction to loud noises
Cherry red spots in the eye
Movement issues
Unable to crawl
Unable to sit up
Unable to turn over in the bed

diseases.name: TBE - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infection that primarily affects the central nervous system, leading to inflammation of the brain and its surrounding tissues. This condition is significant not only due to its potential severity but also because of its increasing prevalence in certain regions, particularly in Europe and Asia. Understanding TBE is crucial for prevention, early diagnosis, and effective management, especially for those living in or traveling to endemic areas.
symptoms: The symptoms of TBE can vary widely, ranging from mild to severe. Common symptoms include:
Fever: Often the first sign, it may be accompanied by chills.
Headache: A severe headache is common and can be debilitating.
Muscle Pain: Generalized muscle aches and fatigue.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may occur.
Confusion or Disorientation: Neurological symptoms can develop, including confusion or altered mental status.
Seizures: In severe cases, seizures may occur.

diseases.name: Telecanthus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Telecanthus is a medical condition characterized by an abnormal distance between the inner corners of the eyes, known as the canthi. This condition can have significant implications for an individual's appearance and may be associated with various underlying health issues. Understanding telecanthus is essential for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can impact both physical and psychological well-being.
symptoms: The primary symptom of telecanthus is the increased distance between the inner corners of the eyes. Other associated symptoms may include:
Altered Eye Appearance: The eyes may appear wider set, which can affect facial aesthetics.
Strabismus: Some individuals may experience misalignment of the eyes.
Vision Problems: Depending on the underlying cause, individuals may have associated vision issues.

diseases.name: Telogen Effluvium - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Hair loss can be a distressing experience for many individuals, and one of the most common forms of hair loss is Telogen Effluvium. This condition, while often temporary, can significantly impact a person's self-esteem and emotional well-being. Understanding Telogen Effluvium is crucial for those experiencing hair loss, as it can help demystify the condition and guide individuals toward effective management strategies. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding Telogen Effluvium.
symptoms: The primary symptom of Telogen Effluvium is noticeable hair shedding. Individuals may observe:
Increased hair loss during washing or brushing.
Thinning of hair across the scalp rather than in patches.
A widening part or visible scalp.

diseases.name: Temporal Lobe Seizure
diseases.description: Temporal lobe seizures originate in the temporal lobes of your brain, responsible for emotions and short-term memory. The exact cause of temporal lobe seizure remains unknown. They are usually focal seizures with impaired awareness.

diseases.name: Temporomandibular Joints (TMJ Disorder): Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is a sliding hinge joint present on each side of the jaw. It connects the mandible(lower jaw bone) to the skull.
symptoms: Symptoms of TMJ disorders include:
Tenderness and pain in the TMJ joints
Pain in the mandible
Aching pain around or in the ear
Facial pain
Difficulty in chewing
Locking of TMJ joint
Unable to open or close the mouth.

diseases.name: Tendinitis
diseases.description: Tendinitis is an inflammation or irritation of a tendon — any one of the thick fibrous cords that attaches muscle to bone. The condition causes pain and tenderness just outside a joint. Tendinitis can occur in any tendon. It is most common around the shoulders, elbows, wrists, knees, and heels.
symptoms: Pain described as a dull ache, especially when moving the affected limb or joint
Tenderness
Mild swelling

diseases.name: Tendinopathy
diseases.description: Tendinopathy is a broad term encompassing painful conditions occurring in and around tendons in response to overuse. It includes both inflammatory tendinitis and degenerative tendinosis. Common locations include the Achilles tendon, patellar tendon (jumper's knee), rotator cuff, lateral elbow (tennis elbow), and medial elbow (golfer's elbow).
symptoms: Localized tendon pain, especially with activity
Stiffness after periods of inactivity
Tenderness on palpation
Pain that is worse at the start of exercise and improves
Gradual onset in overuse cases

diseases.name: Tendinosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tendinosis is a common yet often misunderstood condition that affects the tendons, the fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones. Unlike tendinitis, which is characterized by inflammation, tendinosis involves the degeneration of the tendon’s collagen in response to chronic overuse. This condition can lead to pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility, significantly impacting an individual's quality of life. Understanding tendinosis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, allowing individuals to return to their daily activities with minimal discomfort.
symptoms: The symptoms of tendinosis can vary depending on the affected tendon but generally include:
Chronic Pain: A persistent ache or pain in the affected area, often worsening with activity.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion and stiffness, particularly after periods of inactivity.
Swelling: Mild swelling may occur around the affected tendon, although it is less pronounced than in tendinitis.
Tenderness: The area around the tendon may be tender to the touch.
Crepitus: A grating sensation or sound may be felt or heard when moving the affected joint.

diseases.name: Tendon and Ligament Injuries
diseases.description: Tendons connect muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones to other bones. Both structures can be injured through acute trauma or overuse. Common tendon injuries include tendinitis, tendinosis, and tendon tears. Common ligament injuries include sprains. These injuries are among the most common musculoskeletal problems.
symptoms: Pain at the site of injury
Swelling
Bruising
Weakness
Limited range of motion
Instability (with ligament tears)

diseases.name: Tennis Elbow (Lateral Epicondylitis)
diseases.description: Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) is a painful condition caused by overuse of the elbow, particularly the tendons of the forearm muscles that attach to the lateral epicondyle — the bony bump on the outside of the elbow. Despite the name, most cases occur in people who do not play tennis.
symptoms: Pain and tenderness on the outer part of the elbow
Pain that radiates into the forearm
Weak grip strength
Pain when shaking hands, turning a doorknob, or lifting a cup
Pain that worsens with wrist and hand activities

diseases.name: Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumor (TGCT) is a rare, benign tumor that primarily affects the synovial tissue surrounding joints and tendons. While it is not cancerous, its presence can lead to significant discomfort and functional impairment. Understanding TGCT is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can impact the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of TGCT, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of TGCT can vary depending on the tumor's location and size. Common symptoms include:
Swelling: A noticeable lump or swelling around the affected joint or tendon.
Pain: Localized pain that may worsen with movement or pressure.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the affected joint.
Tenderness: Sensitivity to touch around the tumor site.

diseases.name: Tenosynovitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tenosynovitis is a condition that affects the tendons and their protective sheaths, leading to inflammation and pain. This condition can significantly impact a person's quality of life, making everyday activities challenging. Understanding tenosynovitis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can prevent complications and promote recovery. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of tenosynovitis.
symptoms: The symptoms of tenosynovitis can vary depending on the location and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Pain: A sharp or aching pain near the affected tendon, which may worsen with movement.
Swelling: Inflammation around the tendon, leading to visible swelling.
Stiffness: Reduced range of motion in the affected area, making it difficult to perform daily activities.
Tenderness: Sensitivity to touch around the inflamed tendon.
Crepitus: A grating sensation or sound when moving the affected tendon.

diseases.name: Tension Headaches - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tension headaches are one of the most common types of headaches, affecting millions of people worldwide. They can significantly impact daily life, work productivity, and overall well-being. Understanding tension headaches is crucial for effective management and prevention. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of tension headaches, providing a comprehensive resource for those seeking to understand this prevalent condition.
symptoms: Tension headaches are characterized by the following symptoms:
Dull, aching head pain
Sensation of tightness or pressure across the forehead or on the sides and back of the head
Tenderness in the scalp, neck, and shoulder muscles
Mild sensitivity to light or sound (less common than in migraines)

diseases.name: Teratoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Teratoma is a type of tumor that can contain a variety of tissues, including hair, muscle, and even organs. These tumors are fascinating yet complex, often raising questions about their origins, implications, and treatment options. Teratomas can occur in various parts of the body, including the ovaries, testes, and even the spine. Understanding teratomas is crucial not only for those diagnosed with them but also for their families and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of teratomas, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of teratoma can vary depending on the tumor's location and whether it is benign or malignant. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: This is often the most common symptom, especially for ovarian teratomas.
Swelling or Mass: A noticeable lump or swelling in the abdomen or groin area.
Changes in Menstrual Cycle: In females, teratomas can cause irregular menstrual cycles or other hormonal changes.
Testicular Swelling: In males, teratomas may present as a lump or swelling in the testicle.
Nerve Symptoms: If the teratoma is located near the spine, it may cause nerve-related symptoms such as weakness or numbness.

diseases.name: Terriens Marginal Degeneration - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Terriens Marginal Degeneration (TMD) is a rare, progressive eye condition that primarily affects the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye. This condition is characterized by a thinning of the corneal margin, leading to various visual disturbances and potential complications. Understanding TMD is crucial for early diagnosis and management, as it can significantly impact a person's quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Terriens Marginal Degeneration, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: The symptoms of TMD can vary from person to person, but common signs include:
Blurred Vision: As the cornea thins and becomes irregular, vision may become increasingly blurred.
Distorted Vision: Patients may experience visual distortions, making it difficult to focus on objects.
Sensitivity to Light: Increased sensitivity to bright lights or glare can occur.
Eye Discomfort: Some individuals may experience mild discomfort or a sensation of dryness in the eyes.

diseases.name: Testicular Cancer
diseases.description: Testicular cancer develops in the testicles (testes) that are located inside the scrotum. The scrotum looks like a loose bag located underneath the penis and produces sex hormones and sperm for reproduction. Testicular cancer is rare but is highly treatable depending on its stage and level, even if it has spread beyond the testicle area.

diseases.name: Tetanus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tetanus is a serious bacterial infection that affects the nervous system, leading to painful muscle stiffness and spasms. It is caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani , which is commonly found in soil, dust, and animal feces. The significance of tetanus lies in its potential to cause severe complications and even death if not treated promptly. Despite being preventable through vaccination, tetanus remains a public health concern, particularly in areas with low vaccination rates. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of tetanus, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of tetanus typically appear 7 to 10 days after infection, although they can develop as early as 3 days or as late as several weeks after exposure. Common symptoms include:
Muscle Stiffness: Often begins in the jaw (lockjaw) and can spread to the neck, back, and abdomen.
Muscle Spasms: Painful spasms can occur, triggered by stimuli such as noise, light, or touch.
Difficulty Swallowing: Stiffness in the throat muscles can make swallowing difficult.
Fever and Sweating: Patients may experience elevated body temperature and excessive sweating.
Rapid Heart Rate: Increased heart rate may occur due to muscle spasms and stress on the body.

diseases.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms of Tetralogy of Fallot may vary from person to person. These symptoms may include:
Loss of consciousness
Clubbing of fingers and toes
Shortness of breath
Bluish coloration in the skin
Weight gain
Heart murmur
Irritability
Prolonged crying
Tiring easily
Weakness
Seizures
Difficulty breathing
If your baby shows any/some/all of the above signs, immediate medical attention should be sought.

diseases.name: Thalassemia: Symptoms and Causes
diseases.description: Thalassemia is basically an inherited blood disorder. People suffering with thalassemia have abnormal levels of haemoglobin. Thalassemia contributes to excessive destruction of RBCs or red blood cells. This in turn leads to anaemia, a condition where the body does not have required amounts of red blood cells. It is a genetic blood disease and children inherit the disorder if one or both the parents carry the disease causing gene. A child’s risk of developing the disease is much higher if both parents have thalassemia. Though the symptoms of thalassemia are not visible, there are some prescribed medical tests to identify the disease. A ​ general physician ​may also be able to tell you about your condition but it is important to see a hemato oncologist, stem cell transplant surgeon or ​medical oncologist​ for proper diagnosis. https://youtu.be/4jKWKBLBJmE

diseases.name: Thanatophoric Dysplasia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thanatophoric Dysplasia (TD) is a rare and severe skeletal dysplasia that primarily affects bone development. This condition is characterized by significant abnormalities in the growth and structure of bones, leading to a range of health complications. The name "thanatophoric" is derived from the Greek word "thanatos," meaning death, and "phoros," meaning bearer, reflecting the serious nature of this disorder. Understanding TD is crucial not only for medical professionals but also for families affected by this condition, as it can have profound implications for health and quality of life.
symptoms: Thanatophoric Dysplasia presents a range of symptoms that can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Short Stature: Infants with TD are typically much shorter than their peers.
Disproportionately Short Limbs: The arms and legs are often shorter in proportion to the torso.
Narrow Chest: A narrow thoracic cavity can lead to respiratory difficulties.
Large Head: Infants may have a relatively large head compared to their body size.
Curved Spine: Scoliosis or kyphosis may develop due to abnormal spinal growth.
Bowed Legs: The legs may appear bowed due to abnormal bone growth.

diseases.name: The Facts about Silent Stroke
diseases.description: You had a stroke, but shockingly, you do not know about it. Is it even possible? Yes, a silent stroke is such where you unknowingly suffer a stroke. But, you either cannot remember anything about it or are completely unaware of it. When it comes to describing strokes, we generally think of the causative signs and symptoms. It includes numbness, blurry vision, mumbled speech, and facial paralysis , or body paralysis. However, a person does not experience any symptoms in a Silent Stroke at all. Therefore, the name – Silent Stroke or asymptomatic cerebral infarction . Similar to ischemic brain strokes, silent strokes occur when a portion of your brain suddenly stops receiving blood. It stops oxygen supply to the brain, causing considerable damage to the brain cells. However, a silent stroke is hard to understand because it breaks the blood supply to that part of your brain that has nothing to do with any of your visible functions, such as with ambulation, seeing, or speaking. Therefore, it goes unnoticed. So, what about Silent Stroke Diagnosis? In most cases, people get to find out about their stroke only when they undergo a CT scan or an MRI of the brain for any other health condition. That is when a doctor can identify that a small portion(s) of your brain has sustained some amount of damage. In light of the current scenario due to COVID-19, brain stroke is seen in around 5.9% of coronavirus infected patients. And if you take a look at the neurological complications of COVID-19, you will find that strokes make about 85% of it.

diseases.name: The Function and Importance of Kidneys: What Happens When There Is A Kidney Failure?
diseases.description: Kidneys are bean-shaped organs that are located on either side of your abdomen. These are two in number and are present at the lowest level of your rib cage. Each kidney consists of several functional units known as nephrons.

diseases.name: Things to Keep in Mind About Female Pattern Baldness
diseases.description: Female pattern baldness can be a tricky thing and a cause of emotional distress for many women, especially if they start balding while they are younger. Hair forms a vital element of a woman’s personality and style. Loss of hair could be damaging to a woman’s self-esteem.
symptoms: Here are some symptoms of female pattern baldness :

You might notice a gradual decrease in the volume of hair on the crown. This is more common in men. However, older women may also suffer from this. This is known as frontal fibrosing alopecia, which causes a gradual increase in the hairline to eyebrow distance.
There might be a sudden, unexplained loss of hair. Emotional, mental, or physical stress are some vital factors. This is a temporary symptom and regresses with a decrease in stress.
Sometimes, you may notice scaling on the scalp that might be in patches spread over the scalp.
On rare occasions, you may develop patchy, scattered pattern bald spots. This might happen to your eyebrows as well.
In extreme cases, especially if you are on chemotherapy, you might experience hair loss, followed by the rest of the body, including your eye-brows and facial hair.

diseases.name: Things You Should Know If You Are A Hypochondriac
diseases.description: Hypochondria is a health anxiety disorder, where the patient excessively worries about the possibility of falling acutely ill. A hypochondriac may not have physical symptoms, but considers minor symptoms- or regular sensations in the body as a sign of acute illness- even if a medical examination denies that existence of an underlying medical condition. Hence, it is the extreme anxiety in the person, rather than the symptoms, that result in immense distress that can disturb normal life.
symptoms: Here are the common symptoms of Hypochondria :
Excessive worrying about having contracted a critical health condition or disease
Troubled by regular body sensations or minor symptoms and regarding them indicative of a critical illness
Being extremely uneasy about your health situation
Inability to feel reassured despite negative test results or visits to the doctor with nothing detected
Excessive worrying about a certain medical condition or the possibility of feeling that you are at the risk of developing a certain disease/illness since it runs in the family
Being distressed about having contracted a possible illness, making it difficult for you to function normally
Frequently checking vital body stats to find signs of disease or illness
Constantly checking and rechecking your body for signs of illness or disease
Frequently taking doctor appointments to seek reassurance or avoiding medical attention altogether for fear of being diagnosed with a critical illness
Avoiding going to places, participating in activities or meeting people to prevent any risk to health
Frequently indulging in talk concerning your health and the possibility of contracting illnesses.
Regularly surfing the internet to search for possible illnesses and the causes behind symptoms

diseases.name: Third Nipple - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The human body is a marvel of biological engineering, and its variations can be both fascinating and perplexing. One such variation is the presence of a third nipple, medically known as "supernumerary nipple." While it may seem unusual, this condition is more common than many people realize. Understanding what a third nipple is, its causes, symptoms, and treatment options can help demystify this condition and provide reassurance to those who may have it.
symptoms: Most individuals with a third nipple do not experience any symptoms. However, some may notice:
A small, raised bump resembling a nipple
Hair growth around the area
Pigmentation that differs from surrounding skin

diseases.name: Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm
diseases.description: Depending on its location and size, a Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm is quite a serious disease. It can cause excessive internal bleeding that can be life-threatening. Surgery or other less invasive techniques are used to treat this disease.
symptoms: Detecting a thoracic aortic aneurysm is difficult because often, it does not show any symptoms but keeps growing. Some of these aneurysms might not rupture ever, some might stay small throughout your life, and some might increase in size over time. That is why detecting this disease is challenging for doctors. However, if these aneurysms grow, certain symptoms may be seen. They are:
Shortness of breath.
Back pain .
Hoarseness of voice
Cough.
Chest pain .
Tenderness in the chest.
Sharp and sudden pain in the upper back radiating downward.
Pain in jaw, arms, and neck .

diseases.name: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS)
diseases.description: Thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) is a group of disorders that occur when the blood vessels or nerves in the space between the collarbone and first rib (the thoracic outlet) become compressed. This can cause pain in the shoulders and neck and numbness in the fingers. There are three types: neurogenic (most common), venous, and arterial TOS.
symptoms: Numbness or tingling in the fingers (especially ulnar nerve distribution)
Neck, shoulder, and arm pain
Weak grip
Swelling of the arm (venous TOS)
Arm that changes color (venous/arterial TOS)
Blood clots in upper extremity veins (Paget-Schroetter syndrome)

diseases.name: Threatened Miscarriage - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pregnancy is a time of joy and anticipation, but it can also be fraught with anxiety, especially when complications arise. One such complication is a threatened miscarriage, a term that can evoke fear and uncertainty for expectant parents. Understanding what a threatened miscarriage is, its causes, symptoms, and management options can empower individuals to navigate this challenging experience with knowledge and support.
symptoms: The primary symptom of a threatened miscarriage is vaginal bleeding, which may vary in color from light pink to bright red. Other symptoms may include:
Mild cramping or abdominal pain
Lower back pain
Passage of small clots or tissue

diseases.name: Throat Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Throat cancer is a general term for cancers that start in the pharynx (throat) or larynx (voice box). The pharynx includes the nasopharynx (behind the nose), oropharynx (tonsils, base of tongue, soft palate), and hypopharynx (lower throat). The larynx sits just below, housing the vocal cords. Most throat cancers start in the thin lining of the throat or voice box, called the mucosa. With early detection and modern, team‑based care, many people are cured while preserving speech, swallowing, and quality of life. This comprehensive article explains what throat cancer is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, treatment options (surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiation, and proton therapy in select cases), prognosis, prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Symptoms depend on location and size. Any symptom that persists beyond 2--3 weeks deserves evaluation by an ENT/head and neck specialist.
Common early signs:
A mouth or throat sore that doesn't heal
Persistent hoarseness or voice change (especially for laryngeal cancers)
One‑sided throat or ear pain (referred otalgia)
Difficulty or pain when swallowing; sensation of food sticking
A neck lump (enlarged lymph node)
Persistent nasal blockage (one‑sided), nosebleeds (nasopharynx)
Additional or advanced symptoms:
Chronic cough, coughing up blood
Breathing noise (stridor) or shortness of breath
Jaw tightness (trismus), facial numbness or pain
Unexplained weight loss, fatigue
Vision changes or double vision (nasopharynx/skull base involvement)
Persistent hoarseness, a neck lump, one‑sided throat or ear pain, or one‑sided nasal symptoms should be checked promptly.

diseases.name: Throat Pain: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and When to See a Doctor
diseases.description: Throat pain, commonly known as a sore throat, is one of the most frequent health complaints affecting both children and adults. It can range from a mild, scratchy irritation to severe pain that makes swallowing, speaking, or even breathing uncomfortable. In most cases, throat pain is temporary and resolves on its own, but sometimes it may signal an underlying infection or medical issue that needs timely evaluation.
symptoms: Throat pain rarely occurs in isolation. Understanding throat pain symptoms along with associated signs can help narrow down the underlying cause. People often report combinations like dry cough and throat pain, throat pain and cough, or fever and throat pain, which can indicate infections, allergies, or irritation.
Common accompanying symptoms include:
Fever – Often points to an infection, especially when paired with severe throat pain or heavy throat pain.
Cough – Seen in viral infections, allergies, acid reflux, and may present as dry cough and throat pain.
Runny or Stuffy Nose – Suggestive of cold, flu, or allergies.
Swollen Lymph Nodes – Tender lumps in the neck may indicate infection or inflammation.
White Patches on Tonsils – Often seen in bacterial infections like strep throat.
Voice Changes (Hoarseness) – Can be due to laryngitis, vocal strain, or acid reflux.
Difficulty Swallowing – Many patients report “pain in my throat when I swallow”, throat pain when swallowing, or throat pain while swallowing.
This may be worse on one side, such as pain while swallowing on left side of throat.
Ear Pain – Because throat and ear nerves are connected, infections can cause throat and ear pain, including throat and ear pain right side or ear and throat pain on one side when swallowing.
Throat Pain While Talking – Hoarseness, vocal strain, and infections can cause throat discomfort when speaking.
Throat Pain While Yawning – Yawning may stretch inflamed throat tissues, increasing discomfort.
These symptoms help identify whether you're dealing with a simple viral infection, strep throat, tonsillitis, acid reflux, allergies, or another condition.
Yes. Throat pain can be an early symptom of COVID-19, often accompanied by fever, cough, fatigue, or loss of taste and smell. Testing is recommended if symptoms match COVID patterns.

diseases.name: Thrombocytopenia (Low Platelet Count) : Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
diseases.description: Thrombocytopenia is a condition wherein your blood platelet count is lower than normal . Thrombocytopenia may occur due to a bone marrow disorder like leukemia or an immune system condition or a side effect of some medicine.
symptoms: One of the first signs of a low platelet count is a cut or nose bleed that won’t stop. Other signs include:
Bleeding gums
Blood in your urine , stool or vomit
Unusually heavy menstruation (for women)
Rectal bleeding
Purpura (purple, red or brown bruises)
Petechiae (tiny purple or red dots on the leg resembling a rash)
Fatigue
Enlarged spleen
This condition can also lead to bleeding in the brain, but this is a rare occurrence.

diseases.name: Thrombocytosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thrombocytosis is a medical condition characterized by an elevated platelet count in the blood. Platelets, or thrombocytes, are small cell fragments that play a crucial role in blood clotting. While having a higher platelet count may seem beneficial, thrombocytosis can lead to serious health complications, including an increased risk of blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Understanding thrombocytosis is essential for early detection and effective management, making it a significant topic in the field of hematology.
symptoms: Thrombocytosis may not always present noticeable symptoms, especially in its early stages. However, some common symptoms include:
Headaches: Frequent or severe headaches can occur due to increased blood viscosity.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: This may result from reduced blood flow to the brain.
Chest Pain: Elevated platelet counts can lead to clot formation, causing chest discomfort.
Weakness or Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness may arise from the body’s efforts to manage the condition.
Numbness or Tingling: This can occur in the extremities due to blood flow issues.

diseases.name: Thrombophlebitis - Types, Symptoms, Causes, and Treatment
diseases.description: Thrombophlebitis (Thrombo + Phlebitis), wherein Thrombo refers to clot and Phlebitis means swelling of a vein, is an inflammatory condition in which a blood clot(s) forms in one or more veins resulting in pain and swelling. This ailment usually affects your leg, but it can also develop in your arms and other parts of the body.
symptoms: The symptoms of thrombophlebitis include – ● Pain and soreness in the affected area ● A feeling of warmth in the affected area ● Redness or discoloration of the skin ● Swelling in the leg or ankle ● A swollen vein that appears like a hard cord You should seek medical help immediately if – ● The pain gets worse upon touching the affected spot ● The affected leg or arm turns pale or cold followed by fever and chills ● You are unable to do your day to day activities ● You experience shortness of breath, shooting chest pain , and severe lightheadedness Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals. Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) is a rare but serious blood disorder characterized by the formation of small blood clots throughout the body, leading to a low platelet count (thrombocytopenia) and various complications. Understanding TTP is crucial, as early diagnosis and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of TTP, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of TTP can vary widely but often include:
Purpura: Small, purple spots on the skin due to bleeding under the skin.
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or weakness.
Anemia: Low red blood cell count, leading to paleness and shortness of breath.
Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes due to liver dysfunction.
Neurological Symptoms: Headaches, confusion, seizures, or changes in consciousness.

diseases.name: Thrush - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thrush, also known as oral candidiasis, is a common fungal infection that primarily affects the mucous membranes of the mouth and throat. It is caused by an overgrowth of the Candida species, particularly Candida albicans, which is a type of yeast that naturally resides in the body. While thrush is often considered a minor health issue, it can lead to significant discomfort and complications, especially in individuals with weakened immune systems. Understanding thrush is essential for effective prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.
symptoms: The symptoms of thrush can vary in severity and may include:
White Patches: Creamy white lesions on the tongue, inner cheeks, gums, or tonsils.
Soreness: Pain or discomfort in the mouth, which may make eating or swallowing difficult.
Redness and Inflammation: Areas of redness and swelling in the mouth.
Cracking: Cracks at the corners of the mouth (angular cheilitis).

diseases.name: Thumb Arthritis - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Thumb arthritis is an age-related problem. It occurs when the cartilage wears off from the base bones of the thumb that form the carpometacarpal (CMC) joint.
symptoms: Signs and symptoms include:
Severe pain at the base of the thumb
Difficulty in picking or grasping an object
Unable to apply force with your thumb
Decreased mobility in the thumb
Enlargement of joint at the base of your thumb

diseases.name: Thyroglossal Duct Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thyroglossal duct cysts (TGDCs) are the most common type of congenital neck mass found in children, although they can also occur in adults. These cysts arise from remnants of the thyroglossal duct, a structure that forms during the development of the thyroid gland. Understanding thyroglossal duct cysts is significant not only for their prevalence but also for their potential complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of thyroglossal duct cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Thyroglossal duct cysts may present with the following symptoms:
Painless Swelling: A noticeable lump in the midline of the neck, often just below the hyoid bone.
Redness and Tenderness: If the cyst becomes infected, it may become red, swollen, and tender to the touch.
Discharge: Infected cysts may drain pus or fluid.
Difficulty Swallowing or Breathing: In rare cases, large cysts may compress surrounding structures, leading to difficulty swallowing or breathing.

diseases.name: Thyroid Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Thyroid cancer is a type of cancer that starts in the thyroid gland, a small butterfly-shaped gland located in the front of your neck. The thyroid plays an important role in controlling metabolism, body temperature, heart rate, and energy levels through the release of hormones.
symptoms: Thyroid cancer often doesn’t cause symptoms in its early stages. Many cases are discovered during routine health checks or imaging tests done for other reasons.
A lump or swelling in the neck that doesn’t go away.
Changes in voice, including hoarseness.
Trouble swallowing or breathing.
Persistent cough not related to a cold.
Pain in the neck or throat.
Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck.
Difficulty breathing due to airway compression.
Bone pain (if cancer spreads).
Unexplained weight loss.

diseases.name: Thyroid Nodule - Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Thyroid is the gland located at the base of the neck. Thyroid nodules are an unusual growth or lump in the thyroid gland. These are fluid-filled or solid, and most of them are not severe or cause serious symptoms. Only a small percentage of these nodules turn cancerous and should be treated immediately.
symptoms: There are no symptoms caused by most thyroid nodules, but some nodules can show the following signs:
Can be felt
Can be seen
Cause shortness of breath
Cause difficulty in swallowing
In addition to this, some of the thyroid nodules can overproduce the hormone thyroxine, which produces other symptoms such as:
Weight loss
Tremors
Nervousness
Irregular heartbeat
Increased sweating

diseases.name: Thyroid Storm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thyroid storm is a rare but life-threatening condition that occurs in individuals with hyperthyroidism, particularly those with untreated or poorly managed Graves' disease. It is characterized by an extreme overproduction of thyroid hormones, leading to a hypermetabolic state that can affect multiple organ systems. Recognizing and treating thyroid storm promptly is crucial, as it can lead to severe complications and even death. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of thyroid storm, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of thyroid storm can vary but often include:
High Fever: A significant increase in body temperature, often exceeding 101°F (38.3°C).
Rapid Heart Rate: Tachycardia, or a heart rate exceeding 140 beats per minute, is common.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may occur, leading to dehydration.
Agitation or Confusion: Altered mental status, including anxiety, confusion, or delirium.
Tremors: Fine tremors in the hands or fingers.
Increased Sweating: Profuse sweating and heat intolerance.
Shortness of Breath: Difficulty breathing or rapid breathing.

diseases.name: Thyroiditis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thyroiditis is an inflammation of the thyroid gland, a butterfly-shaped organ located at the base of the neck. This condition is significant because the thyroid plays a crucial role in regulating metabolism, energy levels, and overall hormonal balance in the body. When the thyroid becomes inflamed, it can lead to a variety of health issues, including hormonal imbalances that affect numerous bodily functions. Understanding thyroiditis is essential for early detection, effective management, and maintaining overall health.
symptoms: The symptoms of thyroiditis can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness or lack of energy.
Weight Changes: Unexplained weight gain or loss.
Mood Swings: Increased irritability, anxiety, or depression.
Sensitivity to Temperature: Increased sensitivity to cold or heat.
Swelling: Enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as a goiter.
Difficulty Concentrating: Cognitive issues or "brain fog."

diseases.name: Thyrotoxicosis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Thyrotoxicosis is a medical condition characterized by an excess of thyroid hormones in the bloodstream. This condition can lead to a range of symptoms and complications, making it significant for both individual health and public awareness. Understanding thyrotoxicosis is crucial, as it can affect various bodily functions and overall well-being. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of thyrotoxicosis, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Thyrotoxicosis can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Increased Heart Rate: Palpitations or a racing heart are common.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss despite normal or increased appetite.
Nervousness and Anxiety: Feelings of anxiety, irritability, or restlessness.
Heat Intolerance: Increased sensitivity to heat and excessive sweating.
Tremors: Fine shaking, particularly in the hands.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness or muscle weakness.
Changes in Menstrual Patterns: Irregularities in menstrual cycles for women.
Goiter: An enlarged thyroid gland, which may be visible at the base of the neck.

diseases.name: Tietze Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tietze Syndrome is a rare inflammatory condition that affects the cartilage connecting the ribs to the breastbone (sternum). While it is often confused with costochondritis, Tietze Syndrome is characterized by swelling and tenderness in the affected area, which can lead to significant discomfort. Understanding Tietze Syndrome is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective management, as it can mimic other more serious conditions. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Tietze Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark symptoms of Tietze Syndrome include:
Localized Chest Pain: Pain is typically sharp and may worsen with movement, deep breathing, or coughing.
Swelling: Noticeable swelling at the costosternal, costochondral, or costovertebral junctions.
Tenderness: The affected area is often tender to the touch.
Radiating Pain: Pain may radiate to the shoulders, back, or arms, mimicking heart-related issues.

diseases.name: Tinea Capitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tinea Capitis, commonly known as scalp ringworm, is a fungal infection that affects the scalp and hair follicles. This condition is significant not only because of its prevalence, especially among children, but also due to its potential to cause discomfort, hair loss, and psychological distress. Understanding Tinea Capitis is crucial for effective management and prevention, as it can lead to complications if left untreated.
symptoms: The symptoms of Tinea Capitis can vary, but common signs include:
Scaly Patches : Red, scaly patches on the scalp that may be itchy.
Hair Loss : Patches of hair loss, often with broken hair shafts.
Black Dots : Small black dots on the scalp where hair has broken off.
Inflammation : Swelling and redness in the affected areas.
Fever : In some cases, a mild fever may accompany the infection.

diseases.name: Tinea Manuum - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tinea Manuum, commonly referred to as "ringworm of the hand," is a fungal infection that affects the skin on the hands. This condition is significant not only because of its discomfort and potential for spreading but also due to its impact on daily activities and quality of life. Understanding Tinea Manuum is essential for effective management and prevention, especially for those at higher risk.
symptoms: The symptoms of Tinea Manuum can vary but typically include:
Red, scaly patches: These may appear on the palms, fingers, or back of the hands.
Itching and irritation: A common complaint among those affected, which can lead to scratching and further skin damage.
Blisters or pustules: In some cases, small blisters may form, leading to oozing or crusting.
Peeling skin: The affected areas may exhibit peeling or flaking skin.

diseases.name: Tinea pedis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Tinea pedis, commonly known as athlete's foot, is a fungal infection that affects the skin on the feet. Though often overlooked, it is one of the most common skin infections worldwide. It typically presents as an itchy, red, scaly rash between the toes or on the soles of the feet. While it is usually not a serious condition, if left untreated, Tinea pedis can lead to complications and discomfort. This article will provide an in-depth look at Tinea pedis, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Tinea pedis can vary depending on the severity of the infection. Common symptoms include:
Itching: The most common symptom, often occurring between the toes.
Redness and Inflammation: A red, inflamed rash on the affected areas.
Peeling and Cracking Skin: The skin may become dry and flaky, particularly between the toes.
Blisters: Small fluid-filled blisters may appear, causing discomfort and pain.
Foul Odor: Infected feet may emit a strong, unpleasant smell due to the fungal infection.

diseases.name: Tinea Versicolor: Good Hygienic Routines to Follow
diseases.description: Introduction
symptoms: Discoloration or pigmentation of the skin is one of the most common symptoms of Tinea Versicolor . The discolored patches may be:
Itchy, dry, or scaly
Lighter or darker than the surrounding skin
Brown, pink, red, or tan
Prone to disappear in less humid weather
More prominent with tanning
The discolored patches may get worse during humid and warm weather. The condition may get better during cold and less humid weather.
If you notice any discolored patches on your skin without any possible causes, immediately seek medical assistance.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: Tomato Flu – All You Need to Know
diseases.description: Just when it seems that the COVID-19 scenario is settling down, and we may get some respite from irritating viruses, another viral disease, “Tomato Flu”, has crept its way into Kerala!
symptoms: The primary symptoms of the disease include:
Large blisters, the size of tomatoes that are red in colour
Rashes
Skin irritation
High fever
Dehydration
Body aches
Joint swelling.
Some other symptoms include:
Discoloration of hands, knees and buttocks
Nausea
Vomiting
Abdominal cramps
Fatigue
Coughing
Sneezing
Runny nose

diseases.name: Tongue Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Tongue cancer is a type of head and neck cancer that begins in the tongue. Most cases start in the front two‑thirds of the tongue (oral tongue), which is part of the oral cavity. Less commonly, cancers start at the base of the tongue (part of the oropharynx). The majority are squamous cell carcinomas that arise from the thin mucosal lining. In India and South Asia, oral tongue cancers linked to tobacco and betel quid are more common, while in Western countries, base-of-tongue cancers related to HPV are increasingly seen. With early detection and expert, multidisciplinary care, many people are cured while preserving speech, taste, and swallowing. This comprehensive article explains what tongue cancer is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, modern treatments (surgery, reconstruction, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and proton therapy in select cases), recovery, prevention at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: If a sore, ulcer, or patch in your mouth does not heal within 2–3 weeks, it's important to see a doctor. Early detection makes treatment simpler and recovery faster. Any symptom lasting more than 2--3 weeks should be evaluated promptly.
Tongue stiffness or reduced mobility; slurred speech
Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) or pain with swallowing (odynophagia)
Jaw tightness (trismus)
Numbness or altered sensation of the tongue
A lump in the neck (enlarged lymph node)
Unintended weight loss, fatigue, or drooling
Base‑of‑tongue cancers may present first with a neck lump or persistent sore throat.

diseases.name: Tongue-tie (Ankyloglossia)
diseases.description: The tongue is a muscular organ that helps us speak and also swallow the food. With tongue-tie, an remarkably short, tight or thick band of tissue ties the bottom of the tip of your tongue to the floor of the mouth. Tongue-tie may also affect the way a child speaks, eats and swallows.

diseases.name: Tonsil Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Tonsil cancer is a type of head and neck cancer that starts in the palatine tonsils, which sit on either side at the back of the mouth. Most tonsil cancers are squamous cell carcinomas that arise from the mucosal lining. In many countries, a growing number of cases are linked to human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV‑16. The encouraging news: tonsil cancer is highly treatable. With early diagnosis and expert, multidisciplinary care, many people are cured while preserving swallowing, speech, and appearance. This comprehensive article explains what tonsil cancer is, who is at risk, symptoms to watch for, how doctors diagnose and stage it, modern treatments (transoral surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted and immune therapies, and proton therapy in select cases), recovery and rehabilitation, prevention, international patient support at Apollo Hospitals, and answers to common questions.
symptoms: Any symptom that persists beyond 2--3 weeks should be evaluated by an ENT/head and neck specialist.
Tonsil asymmetry or a visible mass/ulcer on the tonsil
Muffled voice ("hot potato" voice) or speech changes
Bad breath, blood‑streaked saliva
Unintentional weight loss, fatigue
