diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: We all forget things, all the more as we age. A certain degree of forgetfulness is normal for every age group, especially in the elderly. That is not dementia. Some people are naturally bad with names, telephone numbers or addresses, as the case may be. That is ‘normal’ for them and is not dementia either. Ask their families and you will find that they have always been like that. The worry is, when the memory loss exceeds what is normal for the person’s age, education or nature. In such situations, a decline in dayto- day function may also be noticed. Appointments may be forgotten and memos may need to be kept. Shopping lists may be difficult to remember. Things may be misplaced and lost a bit too frequently. There may be difficulty remembering names and even recognising people not seen for a few years. Objects that have not been used recently may also be forgotten. Wrong names may be used. Some may start losing their way, initially in unfamiliar and later in familiar places. They may have great difficulty in locating their seats in a train or in flight, for example. And gradually, even forget the way to their own home. Conversation may be affected in many. Some cannot stop speaking while others sit quietly by themselves with almost nothing to say. Some speak with stutters and trip over words. Finding the right words may be difficult for many of them. Reading and handwriting may be affected; pronunciation and spelling errors may be prominent. Signing a cheque could become a harrowing experience. Dressing, cooking, handling a remote control, a mobile phone or a push-button telephone may become difficult. While any or all of these symptoms may be seen in Alzheimer’s disease, loss of memory is typically the most prominent. Very often it is this loss of memory that draws the attention of the caregivers and other close relatives. At other times, a worried patient himself rings the doctor first.

diseases.name: Understanding COVID-19 Variants In View of Sharp Rise of Coronavirus Infections in India
diseases.description: After a brief lull, the number of COVID-19 cases is once again rising in India, signaling that the country maybe on the verge of a second wave of infection.

diseases.name: Understanding Pheochromocytoma - A Tumor that can Trigger High BP
diseases.description: The human body is composed of various endocrine glands. The function of these glands is to secrete hormones to maintain a regulatory mechanism. One of the important endocrine glands in humans is the supra-renal gland, also called the adrenal gland. These are triangle-shaped glands located above both kidneys.
symptoms: In Pheochromocytoma, there are high levels of adrenaline and noradrenaline produced. The symptoms occur in spells ; they may lead to a paroxysmal increase in blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, etc
Common symptoms associated with Pheochromocytoma can be-
● High blood pressure
● Headache
● Heavy sweating
● Rapid heartbeat
● Tremors
● Paleness in the face
● Shortness of breath
● Panic attack -type symptoms

diseases.name: Understanding Prostate Disorders
diseases.description: The prostate is a small gland in men. It is part of the male reproductive system. The prostate is about the size and shape of a walnut. It sits low in the pelvis, below the bladder and just in front of the rectum. The prostate helps make semen, the milky fluid that carries sperm from the testicles through the penis when a man ejaculates. The prostate surrounds part of the urethra, a tube that carries urine out of the bladder and through the penis.

diseases.name: Understanding Sarcoidosis- And ways to Avoid Triggering It
diseases.description: Sarcoidosis is a chronic inflammatory disease commonly seen in the lungs and lymph nodes, but may occur in any organ of the body. Granulomas (or clumps of inflammatory cells) form in various organs which results in organ inflammation. Sarcoidosis may be triggered by the body’s immune system responding to foreign substances like bacteria, viruses, or chemicals. The cause is unknown, and it can suddenly appear and disappear or develop symptoms that can stay for a lifetime. The disease is neither contagious nor it is inherited. Although there is no cure for sarcoidosis , most people do well without any treatment or medical help.
symptoms: Sarcoidosis is often challenging to diagnose and is sometimes confused with other diseases. The symptoms vary from person to person and mainly depend on the area of the body that has been affected. However, the general symptoms include –
Swollen lymph nodes
Fatigue
A sense of illness and discomfort
Fever
Swelling in the joints and pain
Depression
Weight loss
If your lungs have been affected by this disease, you may observe some respiratory symptoms such as :
Wheezing
Pain in the chest area
Persistent dry cough
Shortness of breath
If your skin has been affected, you may see the following symptoms –
Raised bumps on the skin surface
Skin rashes
Lesions on the cheeks, ears, and nose
Sarcoidosis affecting the eyes shows symptoms such as :
Dryness of the eyes
Sensitivity to light
Severe redness
Irritation and blurry vision
Signs of cardiac sarcoidosis may include –
Irregular heartbeat, also known as arrhythmias
Swelling of the body due to surplus fluid
Palpitations
Fainting
Some people may experience sudden symptoms that will appear and disappear quickly, while others may not show any symptoms.

diseases.name: Understanding the Global Development Delay (GDD) in Children
diseases.description: As babies and toddlers grow older, they typically develop basic motor and social abilities like sitting up, rolling over, crawling, walking, babbling (creating initial speech sounds), talking, and toilet training.
symptoms: A child should start reaching his/her development skills at a certain age. For example: a baby can start rolling and undertake associated movements by four or five months or maybe a little before or after. But if a baby cannot roll much past the defined milestone, or cannot hold his/her heads up or is still not “babbling”, it could be the first signs of global development delay.
Here is a checklist that will help compare your child’s development with normal development milestones:
3 – 4 months:
Baby should respond to loud noises
Should babble and imitate sounds
7 months:
Baby should start responding to sounds
1 year:
Baby should start using simple words like ‘mama’
2 years:
Baby should be able to speak 15 words or so.
Should be able to speak phrases, generally two words without imitating or repeating others
Should generally communicate their needs through speech than actions.

diseases.name: Understanding Toxoplasmosis: Symptoms, Causes and Diagnosis and Treatment Options
diseases.description: Toxoplasmosis is an infection caused by a parasite called Toxoplasma gondii. It is one of the world’s most common parasites and is primarily caused by ingesting undercooked meat (such as venison, lamb, and pork) and being exposed to infected cat feces. It can also be spread from an infected mother to her child during pregnancy.

diseases.name: Undescended Testicle: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Risk Factors
diseases.description: An undescended testicle, also known as cryptorchidism, is a testicle that has not moved into a proper position in the scrotum (bag of skin hanging below the penis) before birth.
symptoms: Testicles are present in the scrotum. Scrotums are the bags of skin that hang below the penis. If you do not see or feel a testicle in the scrotal sacs , it can indicate undescended testicles.
There is a tubelike passage in the groin that connects the abdomen and scrotum. The testicles travel through this passage. If this process is delayed or stops, it results in undescended testicles.

diseases.name: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease (UCTD)
diseases.description: Undifferentiated connective tissue disease (UCTD) is an autoimmune condition that has features suggestive of a systemic rheumatic disease, but does not fulfill the criteria for a specific defined connective tissue disease such as lupus, scleroderma, or Sjögren's syndrome. Many patients with UCTD remain in this undifferentiated state, while some eventually evolve into a defined disease.
symptoms: Raynaud's phenomenon
Arthritis or arthralgia
Photosensitivity
Oral ulcers
Dry eyes or dry mouth
Fatigue
Positive ANA

diseases.name: Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma: Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Sarcoma is a rare kind of tumour that can develop on any organ or part of the body. It is an umbrella term for a wide variety of cancers that occur in the soft tissues. The sarcomas develop around tissues that connect or support different organs like muscles, tendons, blood vessels or the linings of joints.
symptoms: The symptoms of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma depend on its location (where it has grown) and the size of the lump. It generally affects the arms and legs but may occur in any part of the body. Some of the symptoms that may appear are:
Growing lump or swelling in the area affected
Pain, tingling or numbness where the cancer is growing
Loss of appetite
Diarrhea or constipation if it occurs in the abdominal region
Fever and chills
Unexpected weight loss
Pain in the bones

diseases.name: Unexplained Infertility - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Infertility is a complex and often distressing issue that affects many couples worldwide. Among the various types of infertility, unexplained infertility stands out as particularly challenging. This condition is defined as the inability to conceive after one year of regular, unprotected intercourse, despite normal test results for both partners. The significance of unexplained infertility lies in its emotional toll and the uncertainty it brings to couples who are eager to start a family. Understanding this condition is crucial for those affected, as it can guide them toward appropriate treatment options and support.
symptoms: The primary symptom of unexplained infertility is the inability to conceive after one year of trying. However, other symptoms may accompany this condition, including:
Irregular menstrual cycles
Painful periods
Changes in sexual desire
Unexplained weight gain or loss

diseases.name: Unicornuate Uterus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Unicornuate uterus is a rare congenital anomaly of the female reproductive system, characterized by the presence of a single, horn-shaped uterus. This condition arises during fetal development when the Müllerian ducts, which form the uterus, fail to develop properly. Understanding unicornuate uterus is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and individuals interested in reproductive health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of unicornuate uterus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many women with a unicornuate uterus may be asymptomatic and unaware of their condition until they experience reproductive issues. However, some common symptoms may include:
Irregular Menstrual Cycles: Women may experience abnormal bleeding patterns.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic region may occur, particularly if a rudimentary horn is present.
Infertility: Difficulty conceiving is a common concern for women with this condition.
Pregnancy Complications: Women may face challenges during pregnancy, including increased risk of miscarriage, preterm labor, and ectopic pregnancy.

diseases.name: Urachal Remnant - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urachal remnant is a medical condition that arises from the incomplete closure of the urachus, a tubular structure that connects the bladder to the umbilical cord during fetal development. While it is a relatively rare condition, understanding its implications is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of urachal remnants, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Symptoms of a urachal remnant can vary depending on the type of remnant present. Common symptoms include:
Abdominal Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen may occur.
Urinary Symptoms: Increased frequency of urination, urgency, or pain during urination can be indicative of a urachal remnant.
Discharge: A discharge from the umbilicus or urinary tract may be observed, especially in cases of urachal sinus or cyst.
Infection Signs: Fever, chills, and malaise may indicate an infection associated with the remnant.

diseases.name: Urea Cycle Disorder - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urea Cycle Disorder (UCD) is a group of genetic conditions that affect the body's ability to remove ammonia from the bloodstream. Ammonia is a toxic byproduct of protein metabolism, and its accumulation can lead to severe neurological damage and even death if not managed properly. Understanding UCD is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, which can significantly improve the quality of life for affected individuals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Urea Cycle Disorder, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of Urea Cycle Disorder can vary widely depending on the specific type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Lethargy : Unusual tiredness or lack of energy.
Vomiting : Frequent episodes of vomiting, especially after protein intake.
Irritability : Increased fussiness or irritability in infants.
Seizures : Neurological symptoms such as seizures can occur due to high ammonia levels.
Confusion : Cognitive impairment or confusion, particularly in older children and adults.
Coma : In severe cases, untreated hyperammonemia can lead to coma.

diseases.name: Uremia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uremia is a serious medical condition that arises when the kidneys are unable to filter waste products from the blood effectively. This condition is significant because it can lead to a buildup of toxins in the body, resulting in severe health complications. Understanding uremia is crucial for early detection and management, which can significantly improve patient outcomes. In this article, we will explore uremia in detail, covering its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Uremia presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Fatigue: A general feeling of tiredness and lack of energy.
Nausea and Vomiting: Often due to the buildup of toxins in the body.
Loss of Appetite: A decreased desire to eat, which can lead to weight loss.
Itching: Persistent itching, often due to the accumulation of waste products.
Swelling: Edema in the legs, ankles, or around the eyes due to fluid retention.
Shortness of Breath: Can occur if fluid builds up in the lungs.
Confusion or Difficulty Concentrating: Cognitive changes due to toxin buildup.

diseases.name: Ureteral Cancer: Causes, Symptoms, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: Ureteral cancer is the abnormal growth of cells on the inner lining of the ureters. Ureters are the two tubes that connect your kidneys and bladder and carry your urine to the urinary bladders. This type of cancer is rare and increases the risk for bladder cancer. The same kind of cancer cells grow in the ureters and bladder; hence, one can pose an increased risk for cancer of the other. Also, it usually affects older people.
symptoms: Symptoms of ureteral cancer may include:
Blood or blood clots in urine
Weight loss
Fatigue
Back pain
Pain while urinating
Frequent urination
Dark urine
If you experience any of these symptoms, you should seek medical help from a Urologist.

diseases.name: Ureteral Obstruction: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The ureters are tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder. Two (2) ureters are present in our body, one attached to each kidney. The upper portion of each ureter is in the abdomen, and the bottom half is in the pelvic region. In an average adult, the length of the ureter is about 10 to 12 inches.
symptoms: Signs and symptoms depend on where and how quickly the obstruction develops, whether it affects one or both kidneys. The symptoms may be mild at first but can quickly become worse in some cases. These might include:
Abdominal pain (on one or both sides)
Reduced urine output
Having difficulty urinating
Blood in the urine
High blood pressure or hypertension
Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs)
Swollen leg(s)
You should seek immediate medical attention if you have:
Severe pain that does not allow you to sit still or find a comfortable position
Pain accompanied by fever and chills
Pain accompanied by nausea and vomiting
Difficulty passing urine
Blood in your urine
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Ureteral Stones - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ureteral stones, also known as ureteral calculi, are hard mineral deposits that form in the urinary tract, specifically in the ureters—the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder. These stones can cause significant discomfort and lead to serious health complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding ureteral stones is crucial for prevention, early detection, and effective management, making it a significant topic in urology and general health.
symptoms: Ureteral stones can cause a range of symptoms, which may vary depending on the size and location of the stone. Common symptoms include:
Severe Pain: Often described as sharp or cramping, pain typically occurs in the lower back or side and may radiate to the abdomen or groin.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which may appear pink, red, or brown.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may accompany the pain.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little urine output.
Painful Urination: Discomfort or burning sensation during urination.

diseases.name: Ureterocele - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ureterocele is a medical condition that affects the urinary system, specifically the ureters, which are the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder. This condition occurs when a portion of the ureter bulges or forms a sac-like structure at its opening into the bladder. While ureterocele can occur in individuals of any age, it is most commonly diagnosed in infants and children. Understanding ureterocele is crucial, as it can lead to various complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of ureterocele, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of ureterocele can vary depending on the severity of the condition and whether it is causing any obstruction. Common symptoms include:
Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Frequent UTIs may occur due to urine retention.
Painful Urination: Discomfort or pain during urination can be a sign of obstruction.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine may indicate irritation or injury to the urinary tract.
Abdominal Pain: Pain in the lower abdomen may occur, especially if there is significant obstruction.
Enlarged Bladder: In severe cases, the bladder may become distended due to urine retention.

diseases.name: Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction (UPJO) is a medical condition that affects the urinary system, specifically the area where the ureter meets the renal pelvis. This obstruction can lead to significant complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding UPJO is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can impact kidney function and overall health. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding UPJO.
symptoms: The symptoms of UPJO can vary depending on the severity of the obstruction and whether it is acute or chronic. Common symptoms include:
Flank Pain: Pain in the side or back, often severe and intermittent.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to the buildup of urine and pressure in the kidney.
Urinary Changes: Changes in urine output, such as decreased urine production or difficulty urinating.
Blood in Urine: Hematuria may occur, indicating irritation or damage to the urinary tract.
Frequent Urination: Increased urgency or frequency of urination may be experienced.

diseases.name: Urethral Caruncle - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urethral caruncle is a benign growth that occurs at the urethral opening, primarily affecting women. While it is not a life-threatening condition, understanding its significance is crucial for early detection and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of urethral caruncles, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more. By the end of this article, readers will have a clearer understanding of this condition and when to seek medical attention.
symptoms: Urethral caruncles are often asymptomatic, but when symptoms do occur, they may include:
Pain or Discomfort: Some women may experience pain during urination or sexual intercourse.
Bleeding: Light bleeding or spotting may occur, especially after sexual activity.
Swelling or Irritation: The area around the urethral opening may appear swollen or irritated.

diseases.name: Urethral Stricture - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Urethral stricture occurs when scarring narrows the tube that carries urine out of your body (urethra), preventing the flow of urine through it freely. This medical condition occurs more commonly in men.
symptoms: There can be numerous symptoms of a stricture, ranging in severity,. They are as follows:
A reduction in urine flow
Experiencing burning or pain during urination
Sudden urges to urinate
Incontinence (inability to control urinating)
Pain in the lower abdominal area
Darkening of urine
Blood in urine or semen
Penile swelling (in men)
Another effect could be the inability to urinate. It is a severe condition and requires immediate medical attention.

diseases.name: Urethritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urethritis is a medical condition characterized by inflammation of the urethra, the tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body. This condition can affect both men and women, although the causes and symptoms may vary between genders. Urethritis is significant not only because of its discomforting symptoms but also due to its potential to lead to more serious health issues if left untreated. Understanding urethritis is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, which can significantly improve a patient's quality of life.
symptoms: The symptoms of urethritis can vary based on the underlying cause but commonly include:
Pain or burning sensation during urination: This is often the most noticeable symptom.
Increased frequency or urgency to urinate: Patients may feel the need to urinate more often than usual.
Discharge from the urethra: This may be clear, cloudy, or colored, depending on the cause.
Swelling or redness around the urethral opening: Inflammation can lead to visible changes.
Pain during sexual intercourse: This can occur in both men and women.

diseases.name: Uric Acid Stones - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uric acid stones are a type of kidney stone that form when there is an excess of uric acid in the urine. These stones can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not addressed promptly. Understanding uric acid stones is crucial for prevention and effective management, especially for individuals at risk. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook for uric acid stones.
symptoms: Uric acid stones can cause a range of symptoms, which may vary in intensity. Common symptoms include:
Severe Pain: Often described as sharp or cramping, pain typically occurs in the back, side, or lower abdomen and may radiate to the groin.
Hematuria: Blood in the urine, which may appear pink, red, or brown.
Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often accompanied by discomfort.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may occur due to the pain or as a response to the body’s stress.
Cloudy or Foul-Smelling Urine: Changes in urine appearance can indicate the presence of stones.

diseases.name: Urinary fistula in women - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urinary fistula in women is a serious and distressing medical condition that significantly impacts a woman’s physical and emotional well-being. A urinary fistula is an abnormal connection or passage that forms between the urinary tract (including the bladder, ureters, or urethra) and other organs, such as the vagina, uterus, or rectum. This condition can result in continuous, uncontrolled leakage of urine and, if left untreated, can lead to infections, social isolation, and diminished quality of life. Understanding the causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for prompt diagnosis and effective management.
symptoms: Continuous leakage of urine from the vagina
Irritation or soreness in the vaginal area
Foul-smelling discharge
Frequent urinary tract infections
Pain during intercourse (dyspareunia)
Wetness and skin breakdown around the genital area

diseases.name: Urinary Incontinence - Causes, Symptoms and Prevention
diseases.description: When you cannot control urination, you might have a pathological condition known as ‘Urinary Incontinence’. This condition is also known as “Leaky Bladder or Enuresis.”

diseases.name: Urinary Incontinence in Elderly
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Aging itself does not cause urinary incontinence, but changes that occur with aging can increase the risk of developing urinary incontinence by interfering with a person’s ability to control urination. For example, the maximum amount of urine that the bladder can hold (bladder capacity) decreases. The ability to postpone urination decreases. More urine remains in the bladder after urination (residual urine), partly due to less effective squeezing of the bladder muscle. In postmenopausal women, the urinary sphincter does not hold back urine in the bladder as effectively, because the decrease in estrogen levels after menopause leads to shortening of the urethra and thinning and fragility (atrophy) of its lining. Also, urine flow through the urethra slows. In men, urine flow through the urethra may be impeded by an enlarged prostate gland, eventually leading to bladder enlargement. Urinary incontinence has many possible causes. Some causes, such as a bladder infection, a broken hip, or delirium, can bring on incontinence suddenly and abruptly. Other causes, such as an enlarged prostate in men or dementia, gradually interfere with control of urination until incontinence results. Incontinence may resolve and never recur. Alternatively, it may persist, recurring sporadically or, in some cases, frequently.

diseases.name: Urinary Incontinence in Women - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urinary incontinence in women is a medical condition that can significantly impact daily life. It refers to the involuntary leakage of urine, which can occur due to a variety of reasons. This condition is more common than many may realize, affecting women of all ages. Understanding urinary incontinence is important not only for those affected but also for healthcare professionals and caregivers who can provide the right support. The stigma surrounding the condition often leads to underreporting, but awareness is crucial for early intervention and effective treatment.
symptoms: The most common symptoms of urinary incontinence in women include:
Urgency: A strong, sudden urge to urinate that is difficult to control.
Frequency: Urinating more often than usual, often in small amounts.
Leakage: Involuntary urine leakage when sneezing, coughing, laughing, or exercising.
Nocturia: Waking up multiple times during the night to urinate.
Dribbling: Small amounts of urine leakage that occurs after urinating.
Warning signs that require immediate medical attention may include:
Severe pain or discomfort during urination.
Blood in the urine.
Inability to urinate, or an extreme reduction in urine output.
Sudden onset of incontinence in previously healthy individuals.

diseases.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI): Symptoms, Causes, Prevention & Treatment for Men and Women
diseases.description: A urine infection, more commonly referred to as a urinary tract infection (UTI), is an infection that affects any part of the urinary system. This system includes:
symptoms: Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) can show up in different ways depending on your age, gender, and overall health condition. Recognizing these early signs is important — because prompt treatment can prevent complications like kidney infection.
Let’s break down the symptoms for men, women, children, and the elderly.
Regardless of gender, these are the classic signs of a urinary tract infection:
Burning sensation or pain while urinating (called dysuria )
Frequent urge to urinate, even if little comes out
Cloudy or foul-smelling urine
Lower abdominal or pelvic pain
Blood in urine (hematuria)
Fever or chills (may signal the infection has reached the kidneys)
Feeling tired or generally unwell
Note : These symptoms may vary slightly depending on which part of the urinary tract is affected.
Women are up to 30 times more likely to get UTIs than men due to a shorter urethra and anatomical proximity to the anus.
Key symptoms in women include:
Strong urge to urinate, often with little output
Sharp pelvic or lower abdominal pain
Burning while peeing
Vaginal irritation or discharge (if a vaginal infection co-exists)
Discomfort during or after sex
Special attention should be paid by pregnant women, as untreated UTIs during pregnancy can lead to complications like premature labor or kidney infection.
Though less common, UTIs in men often occur due to prostate problems, poor hygiene, diabetes, or catheter use.
Key symptoms in men include:
Burning or stinging sensation during urination
Frequent urination (especially at night)
Discharge from the penis
Pain in the lower back, lower abdomen, or around the testicles
Weak or interrupted urine stream (if prostate is involved)
Men with persistent or recurrent symptoms should be evaluated for prostatitis, urethritis, or enlarged prostate.
Young children and babies can get UTIs too — especially girls under age 5 or uncircumcised boys under 1 year.
Symptoms in children may include:
Fever without a known cause
Vomiting or poor feeding (in babies)
Irritability or constant crying
Bedwetting (in a child who was previously dry)
Foul-smelling or cloudy urine
Abdominal pain
Important : Infants under 3 months with fever should be evaluated for UTI as a medical emergency.
In elderly individuals, UTI symptoms may be non-typical or mistaken for other issues like dementia or general fatigue.
Signs to look out for in seniors:
Sudden confusion or disorientation (delirium)
Change in behavior or mood
Loss of appetite
Urinary incontinence or increased accidents
Weakness or falls
Caregivers’ tip : If an elderly person suddenly becomes confused, sleepy, or “not themselves,” consider a possible UTI — even in the absence of classic symptoms.
Depending on where the infection is located in the urinary tract, symptoms can be mild or severe.
1. Lower UTI (Bladder and Urethra) — Common, milder
Frequent urination
Burning sensation while urinating
Urgency or incomplete voiding
Lower belly discomfort
2. Upper UTI (Kidneys or Ureters) — Serious, needs immediate care
High fever with chills
Pain in the sides or lower back (flank pain)
Nausea or vomiting
Fatigue, confusion, or sepsis (in severe cases)
Kidney infections ( pyelonephritis ) can spread to the bloodstream if untreated — making early detection critical.

diseases.name: Urinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urinoma is a medical condition characterized by the accumulation of urine in the surrounding tissues, typically resulting from a rupture or obstruction in the urinary system. This condition can lead to significant complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Understanding urinoma is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as early intervention can prevent serious health issues. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of urinoma, providing a comprehensive overview for a general audience.
symptoms: The symptoms of urinoma can vary depending on the location and extent of the urine accumulation. Common symptoms include:
Pain: Patients may experience localized pain in the abdomen or flank area, often worsening with movement.
Swelling: The affected area may appear swollen or distended due to the accumulation of urine.
Fever: In cases where infection is present, fever may accompany other symptoms.
Nausea and Vomiting: Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal symptoms as a result of the underlying condition.

diseases.name: Urogenital Sinus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: The urogenital sinus is a crucial anatomical structure that plays a significant role in the development of the urinary and reproductive systems. Understanding its function, potential complications, and management options is essential for both healthcare providers and patients. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the urogenital sinus, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Symptoms associated with urogenital sinus abnormalities can vary widely depending on the specific condition. Common symptoms may include:
Urinary Issues: Frequent urination, difficulty urinating, or urinary incontinence.
Reproductive Symptoms: Abnormal menstrual cycles, pelvic pain, or issues with sexual function.
Congenital Anomalies: In newborns, signs may include ambiguous genitalia or other visible abnormalities.

diseases.name: Urosepsis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urosepsis is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition that arises from a urinary tract infection (UTI) that has spread to the bloodstream. It is a critical medical emergency that requires immediate attention. Understanding urosepsis is essential not only for those at risk but also for the general public, as early recognition and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions regarding urosepsis.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of urosepsis is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Fever : A high fever is often one of the first signs.
Chills : Accompanying fever, chills may indicate a systemic infection.
Rapid Heart Rate : Increased heart rate can be a response to infection.
Confusion or Disorientation : Changes in mental status may occur, especially in older adults.
Pain or Discomfort : Pain in the lower abdomen or back may be present.
Frequent Urination : An increased urge to urinate, often accompanied by pain or burning.
Nausea and Vomiting : Gastrointestinal symptoms may also occur.

diseases.name: Usher Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Usher Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects both hearing and vision, leading to significant challenges in daily life. It is the most common condition that causes combined deafness and blindness, impacting individuals and their families profoundly. Understanding Usher Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis, effective management, and improving the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Usher Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Hearing Loss: Varies from mild to profound, often present at birth or develops in early childhood.
Vision Loss: Progressive vision loss due to retinitis pigmentosa, leading to night blindness and peripheral vision loss.
Balance Issues: Individuals with Type 1 Usher Syndrome may experience balance problems due to inner ear dysfunction.

diseases.name: Uterine Atony - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterine atony is a significant medical condition that can have serious implications for women, particularly during and after childbirth. It refers to the failure of the uterus to contract effectively after delivery, which can lead to excessive bleeding, known as postpartum hemorrhage. Understanding uterine atony is crucial for both healthcare providers and patients, as timely recognition and management can save lives. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of uterine atony, providing a comprehensive overview for a general audience.
symptoms: The primary symptom of uterine atony is excessive bleeding after childbirth. Other symptoms may include:
Rapid Heart Rate: As the body loses blood, the heart may race to compensate.
Low Blood Pressure: Significant blood loss can lead to hypotension.
Dizziness or Fainting: Women may feel lightheaded or faint due to blood loss.
Pale Skin: A noticeable pallor may occur as the body struggles to maintain blood volume.

diseases.name: Uterine Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Uterine cancer is a general term for cancers that start in the uterus (womb), the organ where a pregnancy grows. Most uterine cancers begin in the lining of the uterus (the endometrium) and are called endometrial cancers. Less commonly, cancers can arise in the uterine muscle (myometrium); these are called uterine sarcomas and behave differently. Because abnormal uterine bleeding often occurs early, many uterine cancers are found at a curable stage. This article explains what uterine cancer is, its common symptoms, how it is diagnosed and staged, today's treatments (surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy), recovery and prevention.
symptoms: The most important warning sign is any bleeding after menopause. This should always be checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Uterine Fibroids: Causes, Symptoms, Types, and Treatment Options
diseases.description: Uterine fibroids, also known as fibroid in the uterus, fibroids in uterus, myomas, or uterine myomas, are non-cancerous (benign) growths in the uterus made up of smooth muscle and fibrous connective tissue. These growths—sometimes described as a mass in the uterus—can range in size from tiny, pea-sized nodules to large tumors that distort the shape of the uterus.
symptoms: Uterine fibroids can present very differently from one woman to another. In fact, up to 50% of women with fibroids may have no symptoms at all, and the growths are often discovered only during a routine pelvic exam or ultrasound. When symptoms do appear, they can range from mild discomfort to significant, life-disrupting issues. The size, number, and location of the fibroid determine most fibroid in uterus symptoms.
Below are the most common uterus fibroid symptoms, also described as symptoms of fibroids, fibroids symptoms, or myoma symptoms (symptoms of myoma).
Fibroids can sometimes interfere with conception.
During pregnancy, fibroids may increase the risk of miscarriage, preterm birth, breech positioning, or the need for a C-section.
Important Note The severity of uterus fibroid symptoms does not always correlate with fibroid size. A small fibroid in a sensitive location may cause more symptoms than a large fibroid elsewhere.
Keep a menstrual diary noting bleeding patterns, pain levels, and other changes.
Report worsening symptoms to your doctor promptly.

Common fibroid in uterus symptoms include heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, abdominal bloating, urinary frequency, constipation, back pain, and fertility problems. Symptoms vary depending on the type, such as subserosal fibroid, intramural fibroid, or submucosal fibroid.

diseases.name: Uterine Inversion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterine inversion is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that occurs when the uterus turns inside out, either partially or completely, following childbirth. This condition can lead to severe complications, including hemorrhage and shock, making it a significant concern for healthcare providers and new mothers alike. Understanding uterine inversion is crucial for recognizing its symptoms, identifying risk factors, and seeking timely medical intervention.
symptoms: The symptoms of uterine inversion can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Severe Abdominal Pain: Sudden and intense pain in the lower abdomen.
Vaginal Bleeding: Heavy bleeding that may be life-threatening.
Shock Symptoms: Signs of shock, such as rapid heartbeat, low blood pressure, and confusion.
Prolapse of Uterine Tissue: Visible tissue protruding from the vagina.

diseases.name: Uterine Polyps - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterine polyps are growths that occur on the inner lining of the uterus, known as the endometrium. These polyps can vary in size and number, and while they are often benign (non-cancerous), they can lead to various symptoms and complications if left untreated. Understanding uterine polyps is crucial for women’s health, as they can affect menstrual cycles, fertility, and overall reproductive health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of uterine polyps, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Uterine polyps may not always cause noticeable symptoms, but when they do, they can include:
Irregular Menstrual Bleeding: This can manifest as heavy periods, bleeding between periods, or prolonged menstrual cycles.
Spotting After Menopause: Any bleeding after menopause should be evaluated by a healthcare provider.
Pelvic Pain: Some women may experience discomfort or pain in the pelvic region.
Fertility Issues: Uterine polyps can interfere with implantation and may contribute to infertility.

diseases.name: Uterine Prolapse
diseases.description: Uterine prolapse happens when ligaments and pelvic floor muscles stretch and weaken no longer providing enough support for the uterus. Consequently, uterus slips down into, or protrudes out of the vagina. Let us discuss its causes, symptoms, and remedies, respectively.
symptoms: Mild uterine prolapse does not show any prominent symptoms and can often go unnoticed. However, if the becomes severe, it certainly shows symptoms like;
You might feel a sensation of pulling or heaviness in your pelvic muscles.
Tissues will protrude from the vagina
You might face problems in your urinary tract, such as urine leakage or the inability to empty your bladder in one go.
Your bowel movement will suffer.
You might feel that something is falling out of your vagina.
You might also feel sexual concerns because you can feel a sense of looseness in your vaginal tissues.

diseases.name: Uterine Rupture - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterine rupture is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition that occurs when the muscular wall of the uterus tears during pregnancy or labor. This event can lead to severe complications for both the mother and the baby, making it a significant concern in obstetric care. Understanding uterine rupture, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is crucial for expectant mothers and healthcare providers alike. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of uterine rupture, ensuring that readers are well-informed about this critical medical issue.
symptoms: Recognizing the symptoms of uterine rupture is crucial for timely intervention. Common symptoms include:
Sudden Abdominal Pain: A sharp, intense pain that may be localized or diffuse.
Vaginal Bleeding: Heavy bleeding may occur, which can be a sign of rupture.
Fetal Heart Rate Changes: Abnormal fetal heart rate patterns may indicate distress.
Loss of Fetal Movement: A sudden decrease in fetal movement can be a warning sign.
Signs of Shock: Symptoms such as rapid heartbeat, low blood pressure, and fainting may indicate internal bleeding.

diseases.name: Uterus Didelphys - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterus didelphys is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two uteri, two cervices, and often a vaginal septum. This condition arises during fetal development when the Müllerian ducts, which form the female reproductive tract, fail to fuse properly. While many women with uterus didelphys may lead normal lives and experience successful pregnancies, understanding this condition is crucial for proper diagnosis and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of uterus didelphys, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Many women with uterus didelphys may be asymptomatic and unaware of their condition until they undergo imaging for other reasons. However, some common symptoms may include:
Menstrual Irregularities: Women may experience heavy or painful periods due to the presence of two uteri.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic region may occur, particularly during menstruation or sexual activity.
Reproductive Challenges: Some women may face difficulties conceiving or carrying a pregnancy to term.

diseases.name: Uterus Involution - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uterus involution is a crucial physiological process that occurs after childbirth, where the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size and condition. This process is significant not only for the physical recovery of the mother but also for her overall health and well-being. Understanding uterus involution can help new mothers recognize what to expect during their postpartum recovery and when to seek medical attention if complications arise.
symptoms: During the involution process, women may experience several symptoms, including:
Cramping: As the uterus contracts, women may feel cramping similar to menstrual cramps.
Vaginal Discharge: Postpartum bleeding, known as lochia, is common as the body sheds the uterine lining.
Breast Changes: Hormonal changes can lead to breast engorgement and tenderness.

diseases.name: Uti During Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) are common during pregnancy and can pose significant health risks to both the mother and the developing fetus. Understanding UTIs, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies is crucial for expectant mothers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of UTIs during pregnancy, ensuring that readers are well-informed about this important health issue.
symptoms: Frequent Urination: An increased urge to urinate, often with little urine produced.
Burning Sensation: A painful or burning feeling during urination.
Cloudy or Foul-Smelling Urine: Changes in urine appearance or odor.
Pelvic Pain: Discomfort or pain in the lower abdomen or pelvic area.
Fatigue: General tiredness or malaise.

diseases.name: UV Treatment for Vitiligo and Why it Works
diseases.description: Vitiligo is a skin disease resulting in white patches all over the body. This skin condition can also affect hair and even the internal wall of the mouth. In most cases, these patches grow bigger with time. Though it is not contagious or life-threatening, the loss of pigment from prominent body parts can cause stress among the people affected.
symptoms: Symptoms of vitiligo include:
Loss of skin color in patches. Vitiligo initially appears on the face, hands, genitals, and skin near the body openings and then progresses further.
Premature graying of scalp hair, eyebrows, eyelashes, and beard.
Loss of color on the inner lining of the mouth and nose. Here melanocytes in the mucous membrane get affected.

diseases.name: Uveitis : Types, Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Uveitis is the inflammation of the eye that affects the eye’s middle layer. The middle layer is known as the uvea. The uvea is the middle layer of tissue in the wall of an eye, which consists of the choroid, ciliary body and the iris . When you see your eye in the mirror, you will see the iris (coloured part of the eye) and the sclera (white part of the eye ).
symptoms: The symptoms depend on the part of the uvea that is inflamed. Some symptoms may occur suddenly and cause damage very quickly. In other cases, the symptoms may develop gradually. It can affect one or both eyes. Some signs and symptoms that you may have uveitis are:
Redness in the eye
Pain in the eye
Blurred or cloudy vision
Light sensitivity
Headaches
Decreased vision
Floating spots in your vision

Intermediate uveitis usually does not cause any pain and causes blurred vision and floaters in your vision. Some types of this condition do not show any symptoms and can only be detected during regular eye examinations. These can not be left untreated as they may lead to permanent vision loss in the future and affect your life adversely.

diseases.name: Uvulitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Uvulitis is a medical condition characterized by the inflammation of the uvula, the small, fleshy structure that hangs at the back of the throat. While it may seem like a minor issue, uvulitis can lead to significant discomfort and complications if not addressed properly. Understanding uvulitis is essential for recognizing its symptoms, causes, and treatment options, which can help individuals seek timely medical attention and improve their quality of life.
symptoms: Uvulitis can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Swelling of the Uvula: The most noticeable symptom is the enlargement of the uvula, which may appear red and inflamed.
Sore Throat: Individuals may experience pain or discomfort in the throat, especially when swallowing.
Difficulty Swallowing: Swelling can make it challenging to swallow food or liquids.
Gagging or Choking Sensation: The enlarged uvula may trigger a gag reflex or a feeling of something being stuck in the throat.
Foul Breath: Inflammation can lead to bad breath due to bacterial overgrowth.
Voice Changes: Swelling may affect speech, leading to a muffled or nasal voice.

diseases.name: Vaginal Atrophy: Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Vaginal atrophy is commonly found in women after menopause. Inflammation, dryness, and thinning of vaginal walls are some common symptoms. Apart from pain and irritation, your body starts to experience signs of low estrogen levels as an effect of menopause.
symptoms: Following are some common symptoms you may experience during vaginal atrophy.
Dryness of vagina
Irritation or sense of burning
Itching around your genitals
Frequent episodes of yeast infections
Frequent urinary tract infections (UTIs)
The frequent urge of urination
Painful intercourse
Pain after or during the intercourse
Loss of lubrication
Feeling of discomfort after sex
Bleeding after intercourse
Presence of abnormal vaginal discharge

diseases.name: Vaginal Boil - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vaginal boils, also known as vulvar abscesses, are painful lumps that can develop in the vaginal area. They are often filled with pus and can be a source of discomfort and concern for those affected. Understanding vaginal boils is crucial, as they can indicate underlying health issues and may require medical intervention. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vaginal boils, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of vaginal boils can vary but typically include:
A painful lump or swelling in the vaginal area
Redness and warmth around the boil
Discharge of pus or fluid from the boil
Itching or irritation in the affected area
Pain during sexual intercourse or while sitting

diseases.name: Vaginal Cancer
diseases.description: Cancer means an uncontrolled growth of cells in any tissue or organ in our body. When there is an uncontrolled growth of cells in the vagina, also called the birth canal of a woman’s body, it is vaginal cancer. Cancer can be of many types and can spread from some other part of the body or start in the vagina. It is more common in women over the age of 60.

diseases.name: Vaginal Cysts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vaginal cysts are fluid-filled sacs that can develop in the vaginal area. While they are often benign and asymptomatic, understanding their nature, causes, and potential complications is crucial for women's health. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vaginal cysts, including their definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies. By increasing awareness, we hope to empower women to seek timely medical advice and maintain their reproductive health.
symptoms: Many vaginal cysts are asymptomatic and may go unnoticed. However, when symptoms do occur, they can include:
Pain or Discomfort: This may be felt during intercourse or physical activity.
Swelling or Lumps: A noticeable lump or swelling in the vaginal area.
Discharge: Unusual vaginal discharge that may be accompanied by an odor.
Irritation or Itching: Persistent irritation or itching in the vaginal area.

diseases.name: Vaginal Dryness: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment & Prevention
diseases.description: Vaginal dryness is a widespread health concern in older women. It is the feeling of dryness and itchiness inside and around your vagina. Usually, this occurs due to low estrogen levels just before and after menopause.
symptoms: The dryness of the vaginal lining causes the following symptoms:
Mild bleeding after intercourse
Pain or discomfort during sexual intercourse (penetration)
Soreness of the vaginal wall
Itching in and around the vagina
Burning sensation

diseases.name: Vaginal Odor : Causes, Symptoms, Treatment and Remedies
diseases.description: Vaginal discharge is crucial for the proper functioning of the female reproductive system. It is normal for your vagina to give off a slight odor. But a strong smell may indicate a problem. Vaginal odor is caused due to several reasons.
symptoms: The following symptoms, when accompanied by vaginal odor, may be a threat to your health.
Burning
Itching
Irritation
Irregular discharge

diseases.name: Vaginal Yeast Infection - Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Vaginal yeast infections are a common concern for women worldwide, including millions of Indian women each year. Despite being highly treatable, the discomfort, embarrassment, and misconceptions associated with this condition can leave many women worried or even hesitant to seek help. Understanding vaginal yeast infections, their causes, how to recognize them, and when to get professional advice is crucial for women’s comfort, well-being, and overall health.
symptoms: Vaginal yeast infection symptoms can range from mild discomfort to severe irritation, depending on the severity of the infection.. Common signs include:
Intense itching or burning in or around the vagina and vulva
Thick, white, “cottage cheese-like” discharge, usually odorless
Redness, swelling, or soreness of the vaginal and vulvar tissues
Rash or small red spots on the vulva
Burning sensation during urination, especially when urine touches inflamed skin
Pain or discomfort during sexual intercourse
Watery Vaginal discharge (less common, but can occur in some cases)

diseases.name: Vaginitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vaginitis is a common condition that affects many women at some point in their lives. It refers to the inflammation of the vagina, which can lead to discomfort, unusual discharge, and other symptoms. Understanding vaginitis is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers and caregivers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vaginitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of vaginitis can vary depending on the underlying cause but often include:
Itching or irritation: This is a common symptom that can range from mild to severe.

Abnormal discharge: The color, consistency, and odor of vaginal discharge can change. For example, bacterial vaginosis may produce a fishy odor, while a yeast infection may result in a thick, white discharge.
Burning sensation: This may occur during urination or sexual intercourse.
Redness and swelling: The vaginal area may appear inflamed or swollen.

diseases.name: Valley Fever
diseases.description: Valley fever is a fungal infection. It is caused by coccidioides organisms, especially two coccidioides fungi species. These fungi are usually found in the soil in certain regions. The spores of this fungi can be stirred into air by anything that disrupts the soil like farming, construction and wind.
symptoms: People who get exposed can show a series of symptoms. The symptoms can go from acute and mild to chronic and severe if left untreated . The symptoms occur after one to three weeks after the exposure. Mild symptoms are-
Fever
Cough
Fatigue
Shortness of breath or difficulty in breathing
Headache
Chills
Night sweats
Body aches, joint ache
Soreness in muscles
Rashes on the whole body.

The infection can go unnoticed if it is mild. It can get diagnosed later as nodules on chest X-Ray or through a blood test. However, if the infection turns out to be severe, one can take months to recover. The body pain and joint pain may last for quite a long time. Depending upon the person’s immunity and overall health, the infection converts from mild to severe.
People with diabetes or pregnant women are at high risk. Chronic symptoms are-
Blood tinged sputum
Nodules in lungs
Cough and cold
Chest pain
Weight loss
Low-grade fever

If the infection is not treated, the symptoms turn into chronic pneumonia . A disseminated form of valley fever is where the infection spreads to other body parts like skin, bones, liver, kidney, heart, brain, etc. Symptoms associated with this form of valley fever are-
Lesions on the skin (more kind of ulcers and nodules rather than a rash)
Lesions on bones, spine, etc
Meningitis
Swollen joints, especially on knees and ankles

diseases.name: Van Der Woude Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Van Der Woude Syndrome (VDWS) is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the development of the face and mouth. It is characterized by the presence of cleft lip and/or cleft palate, along with distinctive pits or depressions in the lower lip. Understanding Van Der Woude Syndrome is crucial not only for those directly affected but also for healthcare providers, as early diagnosis and intervention can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Van Der Woude Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Cleft Lip and/or Cleft Palate: The most prominent feature of VDWS, which can range from a small notch in the lip to a complete separation of the lip and palate.
Lip Pits: Small indentations or pits on the lower lip, which can be present in varying numbers and sizes.
Dental Anomalies: Individuals may experience missing teeth, misaligned teeth, or other dental issues.
Speech Difficulties: Due to the presence of cleft lip and palate, affected individuals may have challenges with speech development.
Hearing Loss: Some individuals may experience hearing issues due to middle ear problems associated with cleft palate.

diseases.name: Vanishing Twin Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vanishing Twin Syndrome (VTS) is a term that describes a phenomenon occurring in multiple pregnancies, particularly in cases where twins are conceived. It refers to the loss of one twin during the early stages of pregnancy, often before the mother is even aware that she is carrying more than one fetus. This condition can have significant emotional and physical implications for the mother and the surviving twin. Understanding Vanishing Twin Syndrome is crucial for expectant parents, healthcare providers, and anyone interested in reproductive health.
symptoms: In many cases, Vanishing Twin Syndrome may not present any noticeable symptoms. However, some women may experience:
Vaginal Bleeding: Light spotting or bleeding can occur, which may be mistaken for a normal part of pregnancy.
Cramping: Mild cramping may be experienced as the body adjusts to the loss of one twin.
Changes in Pregnancy Symptoms: A sudden decrease in pregnancy symptoms, such as nausea or breast tenderness, may indicate a problem.

diseases.name: Varicella Zoster Virus - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) is a member of the herpesvirus family and is responsible for two distinct diseases: chickenpox (varicella) and shingles (herpes zoster). Understanding VZV is crucial not only for recognizing its symptoms and treatment options but also for implementing effective prevention strategies. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of VZV, its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Chickenpox (Varicella): Itchy, blister-like rash Fever Fatigue Loss of appetite Headache
Itchy, blister-like rash
Fever
Fatigue
Loss of appetite
Headache
Shingles (Herpes Zoster): Painful rash, often localized to one side of the body Burning or tingling sensation Fever Fatigue Sensitivity to light
Painful rash, often localized to one side of the body
Burning or tingling sensation
Sensitivity to light

diseases.name: Varicose Veins
diseases.description: Many individuals in India (around 30%) have varicose veins of the legs. while this can cause pain and discomfort for some people, for others this can just be a cosmetic concern.

diseases.name: Varicose Veins In Pregnancy - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Pregnancy is a beautiful journey, but it can also bring about various physical changes and challenges. One common issue that many expectant mothers face is the development of varicose veins. Varicose veins in pregnancy are not just a cosmetic concern; they can lead to discomfort and, in some cases, serious complications. Understanding what varicose veins are, their causes, symptoms, and treatment options is essential for managing this condition effectively.
symptoms: Visible Veins: Enlarged, twisted veins that are visible under the skin, often in the legs.
Pain or Discomfort: A feeling of heaviness, aching, or throbbing in the legs, especially after prolonged standing or sitting.
Swelling: Swelling in the legs, ankles, or feet, particularly at the end of the day.
Itching: Itching or irritation around the affected veins.
Skin Changes: Changes in skin color or texture around the varicose veins.

diseases.name: Various Colon Infections
diseases.description: The colon, also known as the large intestine, is a part of the digestive tract.
symptoms: Although the symptoms may vary based on the cause of infection, they typically include:
Watery diarrhea
Fever
Abdominal cramps
Pain and tenderness in the region of infection
Nausea
Vomiting
Severe infection may also present with:
Diarrhea for more than ten to fifteen times a day
Dehydration
Blood or pus in the stool
Kidney failure

diseases.name: Vasa Previa - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vasa previa is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that can occur during pregnancy. It involves the presence of fetal blood vessels running across or near the internal cervical os, which can lead to serious complications during labor and delivery. Understanding vasa previa is crucial for expectant parents and healthcare providers alike, as early detection and management can significantly improve outcomes for both the mother and the baby. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vasa previa, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: Vasa previa may not present with obvious symptoms, making it challenging to diagnose without proper imaging. However, some potential signs include:
Vaginal bleeding: This can occur if the vessels rupture, leading to a medical emergency.
Fetal heart rate abnormalities: Changes in the fetal heart rate may indicate distress, often detected during routine monitoring.
Preterm labor: In some cases, vasa previa may lead to premature contractions.

diseases.name: Vascular Dementia
diseases.description: Vascular dementia is the most common form of dementia after Alzheimer’s disease. It affects one’s memory and thought process due to blockage in supply of blood to the brain. Vascular dementia can occur from stroke as well as other conditions that damage the blood vessels and reduce blood circulation, depriving your brain of vital nutrients and oxygen.
symptoms: The symptoms arising from vascular dementia depend on the part of the brain affected by blockage of blood or stroke . These symptoms can be relatively mild in the beginning. These include:
Short-term memory problems.
Wandering around in familiar surroundings.
Loss of emotional control, with laughing or crying at inappropriate times.
Difficulty focusing or planning a process.
Difficulty speaking or understanding things.
Difficulty keeping track of things.
Inability to follow instructions.
Loss of bladder control.
Loss of bowel control.
Loss of motor control with an unsteady walk.
Physical symptoms, such as sudden headaches.
Paralysis on one side of body or face
Delusions.
Confusion.
The inability to analyze a situation.
Inability to decide what to do next
Restlessness and agitation.
Depression .
Mood changes.
Personality changes.

A stroke happens when the blood carrying oxygen and other nutrients to the brain is suddenly cut off. Not all strokes are major. The piling up of small strokes over a period of time can also cause disability. Such strokes are called silent strokes and show delayed symptoms. Another cause is the narrowing of blood vessels causing damage to the brain. The narrowing of blood vessels is generally related to aging, high blood pressure, atherosclerosis, diabetes , etc. Other factors or conditions that can cause vascular dementia are:
Smoking.
Heart complications.
Diabetes .
Obesity .
High cholesterol .
High alcohol consumption.

diseases.name: Vasculitis
diseases.description: Vasculitis is a group of disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation. Both arteries and veins can be affected. Lymphangitis is sometimes considered a type of vasculitis. It can affect any blood vessel in the body. Depending on which vessels are affected and the severity of inflammation, vasculitis can range from minor to life-threatening.
symptoms: Fever
Fatigue
Weight loss
Muscle and joint pain
Night sweats
Rashes
Nerve problems (numbness, weakness)
Organ-specific symptoms depending on which vessels are affected

diseases.name: Vasodilation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vasodilation is a crucial physiological process that plays a significant role in maintaining the body’s homeostasis. It refers to the widening of blood vessels, which leads to increased blood flow and decreased blood pressure. This process is essential for various bodily functions, including regulating temperature, delivering oxygen and nutrients to tissues, and removing waste products. Understanding vasodilation is vital for recognizing its implications in health and disease, as well as its potential impact on overall well-being.
symptoms: Vasodilation itself may not always present noticeable symptoms, but when it leads to changes in blood flow, several symptoms can arise, including:
Flushing: A sudden reddening of the skin, often seen in the face and neck.
Headaches: Increased blood flow to the brain can lead to headaches or migraines.
Dizziness or Lightheadedness: Rapid vasodilation can cause a drop in blood pressure, leading to feelings of dizziness.
Increased Heart Rate: The heart may pump faster to accommodate increased blood flow.

diseases.name: Vasospasm - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vasospasm is a medical condition characterized by the sudden constriction of blood vessels, which can lead to reduced blood flow to various organs and tissues. This phenomenon is significant because it can result in serious health complications, including ischemia (insufficient blood supply) and, in severe cases, stroke or organ damage. Understanding vasospasm is crucial for early detection and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of vasospasm can vary depending on the location and severity of the blood vessel constriction. Common symptoms include:
Headaches: Often severe and sudden, particularly in cases of cerebral vasospasm.
Numbness or Tingling: This may occur in the extremities if peripheral vessels are affected.
Weakness: Sudden weakness on one side of the body can indicate cerebral vasospasm.
Coldness in Extremities: Affected areas may feel colder than surrounding tissues.
Vision Changes: Blurred or double vision can occur with cerebral vasospasm.

diseases.name: Vasovagal Syncope: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Prevention & Treatment
diseases.description: Vasovagal syncope is a medical condition when a person faints due to a specific trigger. Vasovagal syncope, also known as neurocardiogenic syncope, is the most common cause of fainting. Usually, it is not harmful and not a sign of a more serious condition.
symptoms: While fainting is the most prominent symptom of vasovagal syncope, here are a few other symptoms that you may observe:
Paleness of skin.
Feeling lightheaded.
Experiencing tunnel vision in which the vision area narrows down such that you only see whatever is in front of you
Nauseated feeling.
Feeling warm or hot.
Feeling cold and clammy and sweating .
Blurred Vision.
If you experience a vasovagal syncope episode, people around you can recognize it by the following symptoms:
Jerky and abnormal movements.
A slow and weak pulse rate.
Dilated pupils.
The recovery process after a vasovagal episode generally begins within a minute. But if you stand up suddenly or too soon after fainting, you are at risk of fainting again.

diseases.name: Vater Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vater Syndrome, also known as VACTERL association, is a rare congenital condition characterized by a combination of birth defects that affect various systems in the body. The significance of Vater Syndrome lies in its multifaceted nature, as it can impact the development of the vertebrae, anus, cardiovascular system, trachea, esophagus, kidneys, and limbs. Understanding this syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly improve the quality of life for affected individuals.
symptoms: The symptoms of Vater Syndrome can vary widely depending on the specific anomalies present. Common symptoms include:
Vertebral Defects: Abnormalities in the spine, which may lead to scoliosis or other spinal deformities.
Anal Atresia: A condition where the anus is malformed or absent, requiring surgical intervention.
Tracheoesophageal Fistula: An abnormal connection between the trachea and esophagus, which can cause feeding difficulties and respiratory issues.
Renal Anomalies: Abnormalities in the kidneys, such as agenesis (absence of a kidney) or dysplasia (malformed kidneys).
Limb Abnormalities: These may include missing or malformed limbs, such as polydactyly (extra fingers or toes) or syndactyly (fused fingers or toes).

diseases.name: Velamentous Cord Insertion - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Velamentous cord insertion is a rare but significant condition that can occur during pregnancy. It involves the abnormal attachment of the umbilical cord to the fetal membranes rather than directly to the placenta. This condition can lead to serious complications for both the mother and the fetus, making it essential for expectant parents and healthcare providers to understand its implications. In this article, we will explore velamentous cord insertion in detail, covering its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Many women with velamentous cord insertion may not experience noticeable symptoms. However, some potential signs and symptoms may include:
Abnormal Fetal Heart Rate: Changes in the fetal heart rate may indicate distress, which can be associated with cord complications.
Vaginal Bleeding: Any unexplained vaginal bleeding during pregnancy should be evaluated by a healthcare provider.
Preterm Labor: Signs of preterm labor, such as regular contractions or lower back pain, may occur.

diseases.name: Venous Stasis Dermatitis - Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Venous stasis dermatitis, otherwise called Venous eczema or stasis dermatitis, is a condition when the veins, especially in the lower legs, block the blood from flowing freely. Some blood leaks out of the veins and into the skin when the liquids and pressure build up.
symptoms: The first symptom that can be noticed is swelling around the ankles . It can seem better when sleeping and might again become severe during the day time.
When the person stands or walks, the legs might feel sluggish and the person might find it difficult to move.
Some of the signs and symptoms seen are:
Skin turning reddish , brownish or yellowish in color around the ankles
Varicose veins , that appear to be bulging, twisted and dark blue or purple in color
Sore formation, that itches, oozes, crusts, or becomes scaly
Skin around the ankles and shins becomes thick
Ankle and shin hair loss
Severe pain or discomfort

diseases.name: Venous Thromboembolism - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) is a serious medical condition that encompasses two related disorders: deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). DVT occurs when a blood clot forms in a deep vein, usually in the legs, while PE happens when a clot breaks loose and travels to the lungs, potentially causing life-threatening complications. The significance of VTE lies in its prevalence and potential severity; it affects millions of people worldwide and can lead to significant morbidity and mortality if not diagnosed and treated promptly. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of VTE, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of VTE can vary depending on whether a person has DVT or PE:
DVT Symptoms: Swelling in one leg (or arm) Pain or tenderness in the affected area, often described as a cramp or soreness Red or discolored skin Warmth in the affected area
Swelling in one leg (or arm)
Pain or tenderness in the affected area, often described as a cramp or soreness
Red or discolored skin
Warmth in the affected area
PE Symptoms: Sudden shortness of breath Chest pain that may worsen with deep breathing or coughing Rapid heart rate Coughing up blood or blood-streaked sputum
Sudden shortness of breath
Chest pain that may worsen with deep breathing or coughing
Rapid heart rate
Coughing up blood or blood-streaked sputum

diseases.name: Venous Ulcer - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Venous ulcers are a common yet often misunderstood condition that can significantly impact a person's quality of life. These open sores typically develop on the lower legs and are primarily caused by poor blood circulation due to venous insufficiency. Understanding venous ulcers is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers and healthcare professionals. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of venous ulcers, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Venous ulcers can present with a variety of symptoms, including:
Open Sores: Typically located on the lower legs, these sores may be shallow or deep.
Swelling: The affected leg may appear swollen due to fluid accumulation.
Pain: Ulcers can be painful, especially when standing or walking.
Skin Changes: The skin around the ulcer may appear discolored, dry, or flaky.
Itching or Burning: Many individuals report discomfort in the area surrounding the ulcer.

diseases.name: Ventral Hernia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: A ventral hernia is a common medical condition that occurs when an internal organ or tissue protrudes through a weak spot in the abdominal wall. This condition can affect individuals of all ages and backgrounds, making it a significant health concern. Understanding ventral hernias is crucial for early detection and effective management, as untreated hernias can lead to serious complications. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of ventral hernias.
symptoms: The most common symptom of a ventral hernia is a noticeable bulge or swelling in the abdominal area. Other symptoms may include:
Discomfort or pain at the site of the hernia, especially when lifting or straining.
A feeling of heaviness or pressure in the abdomen.
