Changes in bowel habits, such as constipation or difficulty passing stool.

diseases.name: Ventricular Fibrillation - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ventricular fibrillation (VF) is a life-threatening heart condition characterized by rapid and chaotic electrical activity in the heart's ventricles. This erratic rhythm prevents the heart from effectively pumping blood, leading to a sudden loss of consciousness and, if not treated immediately, can result in death. Understanding ventricular fibrillation is crucial not only for healthcare professionals but also for the general public, as awareness can lead to quicker responses in emergencies, potentially saving lives.
symptoms: Ventricular fibrillation often occurs suddenly and without warning. Common symptoms include:
Loss of Consciousness: The most immediate and alarming symptom, often leading to collapse.
No Pulse: VF prevents effective blood circulation, resulting in the absence of a detectable pulse.
Seizures: In some cases, the lack of blood flow to the brain can cause seizures.
Shortness of Breath: This may occur prior to the onset of VF, especially in individuals with underlying heart conditions.

diseases.name: Ventricular Septal Defect
diseases.description: BOOK DOCTOR APPOINTMENT CONSULT DOCTOR ONLINE
symptoms: Symptoms of Ventricular Septal Defect can be seen in a child over the first few days, weeks or even years. These symptoms include:
Poor appetite
Breathlessness
Easy tiring
Not gaining weight
Weakness
Fatigue
Rapid or irregular heartbeat
If you or your baby have any/some/all of the above symptoms, visit your doctor immediately.
If the opening is small, it won’t cause symptoms because the heart and lungs don’t have to work harder. The only abnormal finding is a loud murmur (noise heard with a stethoscope).

If the opening is large, the child may breathe faster and harder than normal. Infants may have trouble feeding and growing at a normal rate. Symptoms may not occur until several weeks after birth. High pressure may occur in the blood vessels in the lungs because more blood than normal is being pumped there. Over time this may cause permanent damage to the lung blood vessels.

diseases.name: Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD)
diseases.description: Ventricular Septal Defect or VSD is a condition in which there is a defect or hole in the heart. The defect is in the wall or the ventricular septum. The septum acts as a barrier between the lower chambers of your heart. A VSD allows the blood to pass from the left to the right side of your heart causing oxygen-rich blood to be pumped back into your lungs instead of moving through your body, making your heart work harder and increasing the pressure on it. It is a common defect of the heart present at birth (congenital).
symptoms: The prominent signs and symptoms of a serious heart defect start appearing in the first few days, weeks, or months after a child’s birth.
Some vital symptoms of Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD) in a baby are:
Poor dietary intake and weakness
Breathlessness
Getting tired easily

diseases.name: Ventricular Tachycardia- Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Ventricular tachycardia is a heart disorder that is related to the rhythm of the heart and created by the irregular electrical signals in the ventricles (the lower chambers of the heart). Your heart pulsation is determined by the electrical signals sent to the heart tissues. The heartbeat of a healthy person is about 60 to 80 beats per minute when the individual is at rest and is measured by the signals originating from the upper chambers of the heart called atria. When a person experiences ventricular tachycardia, the occurrence of abnormal electrical signals in the lower chambers cause the heart to beat faster than the normal pace and completely is out of sync with the atria. If this situation occurs, your heart would not be able to pump out enough blood to the other organs of the body due to irregular pulsation of heart chambers and the lack of sync between each other. Ventricular tachycardia can be brief, lasting only for a couple of seconds, and may not cause any symptoms. Or else, it can occur for a longer duration causing symptoms like dizziness, palpitations, lightheadedness and loss of consciousness. In certain cases, ventricular tachycardia may result in a sudden halt of your heart ( cardiac arrest ), a life-threatening medical emergency. This condition can occur in people with a history of a previous heart attack , if the heart is weak and is not being able to pump efficiently, due to cardiovascular diseases and other heart complications.
symptoms: Dizziness
Shortness of breath
Irregular heartbeat
Lightheadedness
Feeling of palpitations
Chest pain (angina)
Seizures or strokes
Heartburn
Fainting or Loss of consciousness
Cardiac arrest (sudden death)
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals

diseases.name: Ventriculomegaly - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Ventriculomegaly is a medical condition characterized by the enlargement of the brain's ventricles, which are fluid-filled spaces that help cushion and protect the brain. This condition can be a significant indicator of underlying neurological issues and may affect individuals of all ages, from fetuses to adults. Understanding ventriculomegaly is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: Symptoms of ventriculomegaly can vary depending on the age of the individual and the severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
In Infants: Increased head size, irritability, poor feeding, and developmental delays.
In Children and Adults: Headaches, nausea, vomiting, balance issues, and cognitive difficulties.

diseases.name: Verrucous Carcinoma - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Verrucous carcinoma is a rare form of squamous cell carcinoma characterized by its warty appearance and slow growth. This type of cancer primarily affects the skin and mucous membranes, often presenting as a thickened, wart-like lesion. Understanding verrucous carcinoma is crucial, as early detection and treatment can significantly improve outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of verrucous carcinoma, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Verrucous carcinoma presents with distinct symptoms that can vary based on its location. Common symptoms include:
Warty Lesions: The most characteristic feature is the presence of thick, wart-like growths that may be white, gray, or flesh-colored.
Pain or Discomfort: Depending on the location, lesions may cause pain, especially if they are irritated or infected.
Bleeding or Ulceration: In some cases, the lesions may bleed or develop ulcers, indicating a need for medical evaluation.
Difficulty Swallowing or Breathing: If the carcinoma affects the larynx or esophagus, it may lead to difficulty swallowing or breathing.

diseases.name: Vertebral Artery Dissection - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vertebral artery dissection (VAD) is a serious medical condition that occurs when there is a tear in the inner lining of the vertebral artery, which supplies blood to the brain. This condition can lead to significant complications, including stroke, and is often underdiagnosed due to its varied symptoms. Understanding vertebral artery dissection is crucial for early detection and effective management, as timely intervention can significantly improve outcomes.
symptoms: The symptoms of vertebral artery dissection can vary widely, but common signs include:
Neck Pain: Often described as sudden and severe, this pain may be localized or radiate to the head or shoulders.
Headaches: These can be intense and may resemble migraines or tension headaches.
Dizziness or Vertigo: Patients may experience a spinning sensation or loss of balance.
Visual Disturbances: Blurred vision or double vision can occur due to compromised blood flow to the brain.
Nausea and Vomiting: These symptoms may accompany headaches or dizziness.
Neurological Symptoms: Weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking may indicate a stroke.

diseases.name: Vertex Presentation : Types, Positions, Complications and Risks
diseases.description: When babies are about to enter the world, they are either in a vertex, breech, or transverse position. A vertex position means the baby is head-down in the pelvic region, which is the position a baby is required to be during vaginal delivery.

diseases.name: Vertical Transmission - An Overview
diseases.description: Everyone knows that becoming a mother is a blessing. The life growing inside a woman should be treated with care. A baby deserves utmost care, from nurturing it to eating the most nutritious food, taking care of your diet, and sleeping well. An expecting mother should also take care of her mental and physical health as it impacts the baby. It is also important for her to protect herself from contracting diseases because if she gets infected, it may affect the baby.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms may vary as per the disease conditions acquired.
● In the initial stage, there might be a total absence of symptoms or the presence of generalized symptoms such as weakness, lethargy, fever , and loss of appetite.
● As the disease progresses, symptoms like petechial rashes and reddish or purplish patches on the skin may appear.
● Enlargement of liver and spleen
● Jaundice might occur, though it is rare

diseases.name: Vertigo
diseases.description: Vertigo is a condition that makes the person feel that themselves or the environment around is moving or spinning. It varies from dizziness in that vertigo represents an illusion of movement. When the subject feels that they themselves are moving, it is called subjective vertigo. The perception that surroundings are moving, it is called objective vertigo. Unlike nonspecific lightheadedness or dizziness, vertigo has relatively few causes.

diseases.name: Vesicoureteral Reflux
diseases.description: Urine is the waste produced by your body at the end of various reactions happening inside your body. The normal course of movement that urine follows in your body is from the kidneys, where the urine is produced through the ureters , to your urinary bladder. It is finally excreted through your urethra.
symptoms: A common complication of vesicoureteral reflux is Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs). Though signs and symptoms of UTIs might not be noticeable at first, some symptoms include:
Fever .
Pain while urinating.
A burning sensation while urinating
A strong and continuous urge to urinate.
Pain in the side of your abdomen.
Cloudy urine.
The urge to pass small amounts of urine.
If left untreated, vesicoureteral reflux might cause the following symptoms:
Frequent bedwetting.
Hypertension ( high blood pressure ).
Presence of protein in the urine.

diseases.name: Vestibular Disorders : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: One may have wondered how humans maintain balance while getting out of bed or walking on uneven terrain. This becomes possible due to a connection between the inner ear and the brain, called the vestibular system. Multiple diseases may affect the vestibular system. It’s crucial to be aware of them to look out for the symptoms and administer medical intervention as early as possible. This blog is a comprehensive guide on various vestibular disorders.

diseases.name: Vestibular Migraine - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vestibular migraine is a condition that combines the symptoms of migraine headaches with vestibular (balance-related) disturbances. This often debilitating disorder can significantly impact a person's quality of life, leading to dizziness, vertigo, and other balance issues. Understanding vestibular migraine is crucial for effective management and treatment, as it can often be misdiagnosed or overlooked. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vestibular migraine, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of vestibular migraine can vary widely among individuals but often include:
Vertigo: A spinning sensation that can last from seconds to days.
Dizziness: A feeling of lightheadedness or unsteadiness.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance, which can lead to falls.
Nausea and Vomiting: Often accompanying the dizziness and vertigo.
Sensitivity to Motion: Increased sensitivity to movement, which can exacerbate symptoms.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears may occur in some patients.

diseases.name: Vestibular Neuritis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vestibular neuritis is a condition that affects the inner ear and the vestibular nerve, which is responsible for sending signals to the brain about balance and spatial orientation. This condition can lead to sudden and severe vertigo, impacting a person's ability to maintain balance and perform daily activities. Understanding vestibular neuritis is crucial not only for those who experience its symptoms but also for healthcare providers and caregivers who may encounter this condition in their practice. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vestibular neuritis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The hallmark symptom of vestibular neuritis is sudden, intense vertigo, which may last for several days. Other common symptoms include:
Dizziness: A feeling of lightheadedness or unsteadiness.
Nausea and Vomiting: Often accompanying the vertigo.
Balance Issues: Difficulty maintaining balance, especially when walking or standing.
Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing in the ears, although this is less common.

diseases.name: Vestigial (Human) Tail : Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: If a tail grows in humans, it is called a human tail or vestigial tail. Many experts believe that human ancestors had a vestigial tail and, at some point, needed it. However, as humans evolved as species, the requirement for such an organ ended, which is why Humans no longer grow them.

diseases.name: Viral Exanthem Rash - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Viral exanthem rash, often simply referred to as a viral rash, is a common skin condition that arises as a result of viral infections. These rashes can manifest in various forms and are typically characterized by their sudden appearance, often accompanying other systemic symptoms. Understanding viral exanthem rashes is significant not only for recognizing the underlying viral infections but also for managing symptoms effectively and preventing complications. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of viral exanthem rashes, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of a viral exanthem rash can vary depending on the underlying virus but typically include:
Rash: The hallmark of viral exanthems, which may appear as red spots, blotches, or hives.
Fever: Often mild to moderate, accompanying the rash.
Fatigue: Generalized tiredness and malaise.
Sore Throat: Common in infections like measles and rubella.
Cough: Frequently seen in conjunction with respiratory viral infections.
Lymphadenopathy: Swollen lymph nodes, particularly in the neck and behind the ears.

diseases.name: Viral Fever
diseases.description: Viral fever is a general term for fever caused by viral infections. It is common and usually self-limited, but can be more severe in vulnerable groups.
symptoms: Fever
Body aches
Fatigue
Headache
Sore throat or cough
Runny nose

diseases.name: Viral Gastroenteritis
diseases.description: Viral Gastroenteritis, also known as stomach flu, is an infection of the intestines affects people all over the world. Symptoms of viral gastroenteritis include abdominal cramps, watery diarrhea, nausea or vomiting and fever sometimes. Also known viral gastroenteritis.

diseases.name: Viral Hemorrhagic Fever: Symptoms, Causes, Remedies, and Treatment
diseases.description: Viral Hemorrhagic Fever is a multisystem syndrome that affects multiple organs of the human body. It is caused by several viruses. Typically, the overall vascular system is damaged, and there is also hemorrhage (bleeding). However, the bleeding is itself rarely a life-threatening situation. While certain types of hemorrhagic fever viruses cause relatively mild illnesses, many of such viruses can cause severe, life-threatening condition.

diseases.name: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers (VHFs) are a group of illnesses caused by several distinct viruses that can lead to severe, often fatal, symptoms. These diseases are characterized by fever, bleeding disorders, and multi-organ dysfunction. The significance of VHFs lies not only in their potential for high mortality rates but also in their ability to cause outbreaks that can affect large populations, particularly in regions with limited healthcare resources. Understanding VHFs is crucial for public health, especially in areas where these viruses are endemic.
symptoms: The symptoms of Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers can vary depending on the specific virus but generally include:
Fever: A sudden onset of high fever is often the first symptom.
Fatigue: Severe tiredness and weakness are common.
Muscle Pain: Many patients report significant muscle aches.
Headache: Intense headaches can occur.
Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain are frequent.
Bleeding: This can manifest as bleeding from the gums, nose, or in severe cases, internal bleeding.

diseases.name: Viral Meningitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Viral meningitis is a significant health concern that affects the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, known as the meninges. While it is often less severe than bacterial meningitis, understanding viral meningitis is crucial for early detection and management. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of viral meningitis, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis.
symptoms: The symptoms of viral meningitis can vary but often include:
Fever: A common sign of infection.
Headache: Often severe and persistent.
Stiff Neck: Difficulty in bending the neck forward.
Sensitivity to Light: Discomfort in bright environments.
Nausea and Vomiting: Gastrointestinal symptoms may accompany the illness.
Fatigue: General feelings of tiredness and malaise.
Rash: In some cases, a rash may develop, particularly with certain viral infections.

diseases.name: Virilization - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Virilization is a medical condition characterized by the development of male physical characteristics in individuals who typically do not exhibit these traits. This phenomenon can occur in both males and females, often leading to significant psychological and physical implications. Understanding virilization is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can be indicative of underlying health issues, particularly hormonal imbalances. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of virilization, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of virilization can vary depending on the underlying cause and the individual's sex. Common symptoms include:
Hirsutism: Excessive hair growth in areas typically associated with male patterns, such as the face, chest, and back.
Acne: Increased oil production can lead to acne outbreaks.
Menstrual Irregularities: Women may experience changes in their menstrual cycle, including missed periods or heavy bleeding.
Voice Changes: Deepening of the voice is more common in females experiencing virilization.
Clitoral Enlargement: In females, the clitoris may become enlarged due to increased androgen levels.
Increased Muscle Mass: Individuals may notice a significant increase in muscle strength and size.

diseases.name: Visceral Fat - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Visceral fat, often referred to as "hidden fat," is a type of body fat that is stored within the abdominal cavity, surrounding vital organs such as the liver, pancreas, and intestines. Unlike subcutaneous fat, which is located just beneath the skin, visceral fat poses a significant health risk due to its association with various metabolic disorders and chronic diseases. Understanding visceral fat is crucial for maintaining overall health and preventing conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, and certain cancers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of visceral fat, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Visceral fat often does not present obvious symptoms, making it a silent health risk. However, some signs may indicate its presence:
Increased Waist Circumference: A waist measurement greater than 40 inches in men and 35 inches in women is often indicative of excess visceral fat.
Abdominal Distension: A protruding abdomen may suggest the accumulation of visceral fat.
Fatigue: Individuals with high levels of visceral fat may experience fatigue and low energy levels.
Difficulty Losing Weight: Those with excess visceral fat may find it challenging to lose weight despite diet and exercise efforts.

diseases.name: Visual Agnosia - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Visual agnosia is a fascinating yet complex neurological condition that affects an individual's ability to recognize and interpret visual stimuli, despite having intact vision. This condition can significantly impact daily life, making it challenging for individuals to identify objects, faces, or even places. Understanding visual agnosia is crucial not only for those affected but also for caregivers, healthcare professionals, and the general public. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of visual agnosia, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of visual agnosia can vary widely depending on the specific type and severity of the condition. Common symptoms include:
Inability to Recognize Objects: Individuals may struggle to identify common objects, even if they can describe their features.
Difficulty Recognizing Faces: A specific type of visual agnosia, known as prosopagnosia, affects the ability to recognize familiar faces.
Challenges with Spatial Awareness: Some individuals may have difficulty understanding the spatial relationships between objects.
Visual Hallucinations: In some cases, individuals may experience visual distortions or hallucinations.

diseases.name: Visual Snow Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Visual Snow Syndrome (VSS) is a rare neurological condition that affects how individuals perceive visual stimuli. Those who suffer from this syndrome often describe a persistent visual disturbance that resembles the static seen on a television screen. While it may seem like a minor inconvenience, VSS can significantly impact daily life, leading to anxiety, depression, and difficulties in concentration. Understanding Visual Snow Syndrome is crucial for both patients and healthcare providers, as it can often be misdiagnosed or overlooked.
symptoms: Visual Snow Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary in intensity and duration. Common symptoms include:
Visual Snow: A persistent static or "snow" effect that covers the entire visual field.
Light Sensitivity (Photophobia): Increased sensitivity to bright lights, which can lead to discomfort or pain.
Afterimages: The sensation of seeing an image after it has been removed from view.
Visual Distortions: This may include seeing halos around objects, trailing images, or other distortions.
Nyctalopia: Difficulty seeing in low-light conditions or at night.

diseases.name: Vitamin A Deficiency - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vitamin A deficiency is a significant public health issue that affects millions of people worldwide, particularly in developing countries. This essential nutrient plays a crucial role in maintaining various bodily functions, including vision, immune response, and skin health. Understanding vitamin A deficiency is vital for recognizing its implications on health and well-being. In this article, we will explore the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis related to vitamin A deficiency.
symptoms: Vitamin A deficiency can manifest through a variety of symptoms, which may vary in severity. Common symptoms include:
Night Blindness: Difficulty seeing in low light or darkness is often one of the first signs of vitamin A deficiency.
Dry Eyes: A lack of vitamin A can lead to xerophthalmia, a condition characterized by dry, thickened conjunctiva and cornea.
Skin Issues: Dry, rough skin and keratosis pilaris (small bumps on the skin) can occur due to impaired skin health.
Frequent Infections: A weakened immune system can lead to increased susceptibility to infections, particularly respiratory and gastrointestinal infections.
Delayed Wound Healing: Vitamin A is essential for skin health and repair, and deficiency can slow down the healing process.

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.description: Vitamin B12 deficiency can lead to anemia and nerve problems due to insufficient B12 intake or absorption.
symptoms: Fatigue
Weakness
Numbness or tingling
Memory problems
Pale skin

diseases.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
diseases.description: Vitamin D deficiency means the body is not getting enough vitamin D to maintain healthy bones, muscles, and immune function.
symptoms: Bone pain
Muscle weakness
Fatigue

diseases.name: Vitamin Deficiency Anemia - Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Vitamins and minerals are crucial for the balance of our bodies. If you have a lower than a particular threshold of vitamins or minerals in your body, it could lead to vitamin deficiency anemia.
symptoms: The primary symptoms of vitamin deficient anemia are very similar to iron-deficiency anemia and other vitamin deficiency diseases. The common symptoms of both conditions include:
Dizziness
Yellowish or pale skin
Breathlessness
General weakness
Unstable movements
Personality changes
Confusion and forgetfulness
Irregular heartbeat
Weight gain
Weight loss
Fatigue
Difficulty breathing

The tricky aspect of vitamin deficiency diseases, including vitamin deficiency anemia is that they develop slowly over time and the symptoms, while mild at first, can be extremely aggressive as vitamin levels drop more.

diseases.name: Vitiligo
diseases.description: Vitiligo is a long-term skin condition characterized by patches of the skin losing their pigment. The patches of skin affected become white and usually have sharp margins. The hair from the skin may also become white. Vitiligo is caused by a loss of melanocytes, which are cells responsible for skin pigmentation. It can affect people of any race or skin tone but is more visible in people with darker skin.
symptoms: Patchy loss of skin color (usually first appears on sun-exposed areas)
Premature whitening or graying of hair, eyebrows, eyelashes
Loss of color in the tissues that line the inside of the mouth and nose (mucous membranes)
Loss of or change in color of the inner layer of the eye (retina)

diseases.name: Vocal Cord Paralysis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vocal cord paralysis is a condition that affects the ability of the vocal cords to function properly, leading to various complications in speech, breathing, and swallowing. This condition can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, making it essential to understand its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options. In this comprehensive article, we will explore vocal cord paralysis in detail, providing valuable insights for patients, caregivers, and anyone interested in learning more about this medical condition.
symptoms: The symptoms of vocal cord paralysis can vary depending on whether one or both vocal cords are affected. Common symptoms include:
Hoarseness: A raspy or strained voice is often the first noticeable symptom.
Breathing Difficulties: Patients may experience shortness of breath or a feeling of tightness in the throat.
Swallowing Problems: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) can occur, leading to choking or aspiration.
Loss of Voice: In severe cases, individuals may lose their ability to speak altogether.

diseases.name: Voice Disorders
diseases.description: People develop voice disorders for many reasons. An ENT (ear, nose, throat) specialist is involved in diagnosing and treating these Voice disorders.
symptoms: If you develop a voice disorder, you may experience one or more of the following:
A strained or choppy voice
A hoarse voice
An unusual change in your pitch
A quivering sound
A breathy, whispery, or weak voice

You may even experience pain in your throat while speaking or feel like your vocal cords are tired. You may even feel pain while touching your throat or the presence of a lump in your throat while swallowing.

diseases.name: Vulvar Cancer - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Vulvar cancer is a rare gynecologic cancer that starts on the outer female genitalia (the vulva), which includes the labia, clitoris, and the opening to the vagina (introitus). Many cases develop slowly from precancerous skin changes, which makes early detection possible and highly effective. When found early and treated by a coordinated, experienced team, outcomes are often excellent, with thoughtful surgical techniques that preserve appearance and function. This article explains what vulvar cancer is, who is affected, symptoms to watch for, how it's diagnosed and staged, modern treatments (including reconstructive options), recovery and follow‑up, and prevention strategies at Apollo Hospitals.
symptoms: Early lesions can be subtle and may be mistaken for benign skin problems. If you notice a persistent sore, patch, or itch that doesn't go away in 2–3 weeks, see a doctor.
Common early signs:
Persistent itching, burning, or soreness
A new lump, thickened patch, or rough/scaly area
Color change (red, white, or dark patch), or a sore that does not heal
Pain with urination or sex
Progressive or advanced symptoms:
Bleeding or ulceration
Increasing pain, swelling, or foul odor from a lesion
A palpable groin lump (enlarged lymph node)
Difficulty sitting or walking due to lesion pain
Any new or changing vulvar spot, especially in the setting of lichen sclerosus or persistent itching, deserves a timely biopsy.

diseases.name: Vulvar Dermatitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vulvar dermatitis is a condition that affects many individuals, yet it often goes unrecognized or misunderstood. This inflammation of the vulvar area can lead to discomfort, pain, and significant distress. Understanding vulvar dermatitis is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers who aim to offer effective treatment and support. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of vulvar dermatitis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of vulvar dermatitis can vary in severity and may include:
Itching: A persistent urge to scratch the vulvar area is one of the most common symptoms.
Redness and Swelling: Inflammation can cause the vulva to appear red and swollen.
Burning Sensation: Many individuals report a burning feeling, especially during urination or sexual activity.
Discharge: Changes in vaginal discharge, such as increased moisture or unusual odor, may occur.
Pain: Discomfort or pain during intercourse or while sitting can be significant.

diseases.name: Vulvar Varicosities - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vulvar varicosities are a condition characterized by the enlargement and swelling of veins in the vulvar region, often resembling varicose veins found in the legs. While they may not be life-threatening, they can cause significant discomfort and distress for those affected. Understanding vulvar varicosities is essential for recognizing symptoms, seeking appropriate treatment, and managing the condition effectively. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of vulvar varicosities, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: The symptoms of vulvar varicosities can vary in severity and may include:
Swelling: Enlarged veins in the vulvar area may cause noticeable swelling.
Pain or Discomfort: Many women experience aching, heaviness, or throbbing sensations in the vulvar region.
Itching or Irritation: The affected area may become itchy or irritated due to increased pressure on the skin.
Visible Veins: Enlarged veins may be visible beneath the skin, often appearing bluish or purplish in color.

diseases.name: Vulvitis - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Vulvitis is a medical condition that affects the vulva, the external part of the female genitalia. It is characterized by inflammation, which can lead to discomfort, pain, and various other symptoms. Understanding vulvitis is crucial not only for those who experience it but also for healthcare providers who aim to offer effective treatment and support. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of vulvitis, providing a comprehensive overview for readers.
symptoms: The symptoms of vulvitis can vary but often include:
Itching: A common and distressing symptom.
Burning Sensation: Particularly during urination or sexual intercourse.
Redness and Swelling: Inflammation can lead to visible changes in the vulvar area.
Discharge: Abnormal vaginal discharge may accompany vulvitis.
Pain: Discomfort or pain in the vulvar region.

diseases.name: Waardenburg Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Waardenburg Syndrome (WS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects pigmentation and hearing. It is characterized by distinctive physical features and can lead to various health challenges. Understanding Waardenburg Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed with it but also for their families and healthcare providers. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Waardenburg Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and long-term outlook.
symptoms: Waardenburg Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can differ based on the type of syndrome. Common symptoms include:
Pigmentation Changes: This includes white patches of hair (often a streak), light blue or different colored eyes (heterochromia), and skin depigmentation.
Hearing Loss: This can range from mild to profound and may affect one or both ears.
Facial Features: Some individuals may have a broad nasal bridge or widely spaced eyes.
Other Symptoms: In some cases, individuals may experience other health issues, such as gastrointestinal problems or neurological symptoms.

diseases.name: Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia - Symptoms and Causes
diseases.description: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is a rare kind of blood cancer. The bone marrow makes too many abnormal white blood cells which crowd out healthy blood cells. These abnormal white blood cells produce a protein which accumulates in the blood, damages circulation and causes complications.
symptoms: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia may not cause noticeable symptoms for years. However, there are some common symptoms of this condition such as,
Unexpected weight loss
Fever
Bruising
Headaches
Feeling of numbness in extremities of your body
Blurred vision
Breathing issues
Reduced levels of red blood cells
Excessive night sweats
Nose or gum bleeding
Confusion
Circulation related problems

diseases.name: Warts - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Warts are benign growths on the skin caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV). They can appear anywhere on the body and are often harmless, but they can be unsightly and sometimes uncomfortable. Understanding warts is essential not only for effective treatment but also for prevention. This article will delve into the various aspects of warts, including their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and prevention strategies.
symptoms: Warts can vary in appearance, but common symptoms include:
Rough Texture: Warts often have a rough, raised surface.
Color Variations: They can be skin-colored, brown, or gray.
Location: Warts can appear on any part of the body, with common warts typically found on the hands and fingers, plantar warts on the soles of the feet, and genital warts in the genital area.
Pain or Discomfort: Plantar warts may cause pain when walking, while other types may be asymptomatic.

diseases.name: Water-Borne Diseases To Watch Out For This Monsoon
diseases.description: With monsoon, certain diseases are on the rise. Most of the illnesses in India are due to water-borne infections. When drinking water comes into contact with faeces of humans or animals, which have various disease producing germs, it causes various illnesses like diarrhoea, gastroenteritis and even polio. Below is a list of common water-borne diseases to watch out during monsoon.
symptoms: Other symptoms like meningitis due to polio, hepatitis due to hepatitis A and E viruses will cause jaundice and other symptoms.

diseases.name: Waterhouse Friderichsen Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Waterhouse Friderichsen Syndrome (WFS) is a rare but serious condition characterized by adrenal gland failure due to bleeding into the adrenal glands. This syndrome is often associated with severe infections, particularly those caused by the bacterium Neisseria meningitidis, which can lead to a life-threatening condition known as meningococcemia. Understanding WFS is crucial for timely diagnosis and treatment, as it can have significant implications for patient health and recovery.
symptoms: The symptoms of Waterhouse Friderichsen Syndrome can vary but often include:
Fever: A high fever is commonly present due to the underlying infection.
Severe headache: Often associated with meningitis.
Nausea and vomiting: These symptoms can occur due to increased intracranial pressure or systemic infection.
Fatigue and weakness: Resulting from adrenal insufficiency.
Hypotension: Low blood pressure due to septic shock.
Skin rash: A petechial rash may develop, particularly in cases of meningococcemia.
Altered mental status: Confusion or decreased consciousness can occur due to severe infection or shock.

diseases.name: Weaver Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Weaver Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects growth and development, leading to a range of physical and cognitive challenges. Understanding Weaver Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and intervention, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Weaver Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions.
symptoms: Weaver Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary in severity from person to person. Common symptoms include:
Overgrowth: Rapid growth during childhood, leading to taller stature compared to peers.
Distinctive Facial Features: Individuals may have a prominent forehead, wide-set eyes, and a broad nose.
Developmental Delays: Delays in reaching developmental milestones, including speech and motor skills.
Intellectual Disability: Varying degrees of cognitive impairment, which may affect learning and daily functioning.
Joint Hyperflexibility: Increased flexibility in joints, which can lead to joint pain or discomfort.
Behavioral Issues: Some individuals may exhibit behavioral challenges, including anxiety or attention difficulties.

diseases.name: Weber Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Weber Syndrome is a rare neurological condition that primarily affects the brain and nervous system. It is characterized by a specific set of symptoms that can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Understanding Weber Syndrome is crucial for early diagnosis and effective management, as it can lead to serious complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Weber Syndrome, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Weber Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can include:
Hemiparesis: Weakness on one side of the body, often affecting the arm and leg.
Ocular Symptoms: Difficulty moving the eye, drooping eyelids (ptosis), and double vision (diplopia).
Speech Difficulties: Slurred speech or difficulty articulating words.
Sensory Loss: Reduced sensation on one side of the body.
Cognitive Impairments: In some cases, individuals may experience memory issues or difficulty concentrating.

diseases.name: Weeping Eczema - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Weeping eczema, also known as weeping dermatitis or exudative eczema, is a common skin condition characterized by inflamed, itchy, and oozing patches of skin. This condition can significantly impact the quality of life for those affected, leading to discomfort, emotional distress, and social withdrawal. Understanding weeping eczema is crucial for effective management and prevention, as it can arise from various causes and may require a multifaceted approach to treatment.
symptoms: Weeping eczema presents with a range of symptoms, including:
Red, inflamed skin: The affected areas appear swollen and may be warm to the touch.
Oozing and crusting: Clear or yellowish fluid may seep from the lesions, leading to crust formation.
Intense itching: The itching can be severe, often leading to scratching and further skin damage.
Dry, scaly patches: As the condition progresses, the skin may become dry and flaky.

diseases.name: Werner Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Werner Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that significantly impacts the aging process, leading to premature aging and a host of associated health complications. Named after the German physician Otto Werner, who first described the condition in the 1900s, this syndrome is characterized by a range of symptoms that resemble those of aging, including graying hair, skin changes, and an increased risk of age-related diseases. Understanding Werner Syndrome is crucial not only for those affected but also for healthcare providers and researchers working to improve the quality of life for individuals with this condition.
symptoms: Individuals with Werner Syndrome may experience a variety of symptoms, including:
Premature Graying and Hair Loss: One of the earliest signs, often noticeable in the late teens.
Skin Changes: Thinning skin, wrinkles, and a loss of elasticity.
Short Stature: Individuals may be shorter than their peers.
Cataracts: Early development of cataracts is common.
Diabetes: Increased risk of type 2 diabetes.
Cardiovascular Issues: Higher likelihood of heart disease and hypertension.
Osteoporosis: Increased risk of bone fractures due to weakened bones.

diseases.name: Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome: Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: Lack of vitamin B1 and alcohol misuse results in Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. Vitamin B1 deficiency may result from malnutrition, alcohol misuse, prolonged vomiting, eating disorders, or side effects of chemotherapy. It is a neurodegenerative condition which damages the brain’s thalamus and hypothalamus. Experts believe that Wernicke’s encephalopathy and Korsakoff syndrome are different stages of the same disease. The condition is incurable, but several treatment options help manage the symptoms.
symptoms: Typically, individuals first develop Wernicke’s encephalopathy, gradually leading to Korsakoff syndrome. The following are the symptoms of Wernicke’s encephalopathy:
Prominent symptoms of WE are:
double vision
a drooping upper eyelid, also known as ptosis
up-and-down or side-to-side eye movements
loss of muscle coordination, or ataxia, which may interfere with walking
a confused mental state, which frequently leads to combativeness or violent behavior
WD can later develop into Korsakoff’s syndrome. People who have WKS have a variety of issues relating to memory. You may experience memory loss or be unable to form new memories.
You may also have the following symptoms if you have WKS:
amnesia for events that happen after the onset of the disorder
difficulty understanding the meaning of information
difficulty putting words into context
hallucinations
exaggerated storytelling, or confabulation
The disorder may also affect the heart and blood vessels resulting in the following:
Drowsiness
Fainting spells
Rapid heartbeat
Decreased blood pressure while standing
Lack of energy
The patients also suffer from various eye issues, such as:
Abnormal eye movement, known as nystagmus
Drooping eyelid
Weakness and paralysis in the eye muscle

If untreated, it may lead to Korsakoff syndrome. Typically, it begins as Wernicke’s encephalopathy, and the patient may recover. However, the unmistakable sign of Korsakoff syndrome is short-term memory issues . Here, patients find it challenging to learn something new or make new memories. For instance, the patient may interact with others. But after a few minutes may not remember the conversation or the person they spoke to. Other symptoms may include the following:
Long-term memory loss
Hallucinations, particularly with those with alcohol withdrawal and disorientation
Difficulty understanding or processing information or amnesia
The desire to unintentionally make up stories to fill in the memory gaps, known as confabulation
Difficulty relating words to any context
Changes in behaviour, such as agitation or anger
Change in gait
Distracted or lack of focus
Sometimes, the symptoms may not improve even after treatment. Also, in severe cases, patients may slip into a coma.

diseases.name: West Nile Virus - Symptoms, Risk Factors, Prevention and Treatment
diseases.description: West Nile Virus (WNV) is a zoonotic disease that affects animals, but can also affect humans. A member of the flavivirus genus, WNV belongs to the Japanese encephalitis antigenic complex of the family Flaviviridae.
symptoms: Eighty percent of people infected do not feel any symptoms.
Out of the rest of the 20%, few of the infected people feel mild symptoms. These symptoms are almost the same as any other viral fever . Mild symptoms of West Nile virus include:
Fever
Nausea
Headache
Skin rash
Fatigue
Body ache
The symptoms of severe disease, which is also named as neuroinvasive disease like meningitis or West Nile poliomyelitis or West Nile encephalitis, include:
High fever
Neck stiffness
Stupor
Disorientation
Coma
Tremors
Convulsions
Muscle weakness
Paralysis

It is projected that about 1 in 150 persons infected with WNV may develop a more severe form of this disease. While severe illness can occur in people of any age, those over the 50 years of age and some immunocompromised individuals (Eg. transplant patients) are at the greater risk for getting severely sick when infected with WNV.

diseases.name: Wet Macular Degeneration - Symptoms, Causes, Prevention, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: The retina is the tissue at the back of your eye that senses light. When the retina’s central portion, called the macula, suffers from degeneration it can affect vision. As it is the leading cause of severe, permanent vision loss in people over age 60, it is also called ‘age-related macular degeneration or Wet Macular Degeneration’ (AMD).
symptoms: You might not notice any symptoms until it affects both of your eyes.
Some common symptoms include things that seem twisted or out of shape. Rare symptoms include your eyes taking a long time to adjust when entering a dark room from sunlight.
Few of the most common symptoms of wet macular degeneration include:
Blurry vision
Dark areas in your central vision
Straight lines seeming bent
Facing problems in recognizing faces
Not able to or facing trouble reading in dim lights
A well-defined blind spot or a blurry spot in your field of vision
Decreased intensity, or brightness of colors

diseases.name: What is Pyloric Stenosis (HPS)? What Are the Symptoms of Pyloric Stenosis?
diseases.description: The human stomach has two sphincters on each end, so that the food eaten , remains in the stomach for the duration of digestion, without any leakage. The sphincter near the heart is known as ‘cardiac sphincter,’ and the one near the intestine is known as the ‘pyloric sphincter.’
symptoms: The following are some of the common signs and symptoms that are usually seen in infants with pyloric stenosis:
Vomiting After Breast or Bottle-Feeding . Usually, the babies start vomiting about half an hour to one hour after food. Initially, the vomiting is not that severe or frequent.

It later progresses to severe and frequent vomiting, with a characteristic ‘projectile vomiting.’ The baby usually throws out the contents of the stomach with force. This happens when there is severe tightening of the pyloric sphincter, and there is no or minimal space left for the food to pass.
Sometimes, there can also be blood in the vomit.
Pain in the Abdomen . The babies usually feel pain in the stomach region in the area of stenosis. This is due to the constricted and tensed muscles.
Feeling Hungry All the Time . Babies with pyloric stenosis usually feel hungry after feeding and throughout the day. These babies usually demand food right after getting fed.
Dehydration . Vomiting after each feed makes the baby dehydrated. It is one of the most important signs, as this has been noted as one of the identifying factors of the conditions by the parents.

Contractions in the Stomach . A wave type of muscular contraction is usually felt in the upper abdomen of the baby. It is felt right after feeding and before vomiting. This occurs because the stomach is trying to force food out of the sphincter and due to the constriction, it has to apply more force. Also, if felt carefully, a sausage shaped solid structure can be felt in the abdomen of the baby. This is the enlarged and tightened sphincter.
Changes in Bowel Habits . As this condition does not allow food to reach the intestine in a normal manner, these babies are usually constipated.
Irritability is caused due to constipation and other metabolic disturbances.
Weight loss is commonly seen in these babies.

diseases.name: What is Schizoaffective Disorder & how is it Different from Schizophrenia?
diseases.description: Schizoaffective disorder is a condition that manifests with the symptoms of schizophrenia and mood disorder. This condition affects men and women. However, young men are more vulnerable to schizoaffective disorder. It is rare and affects only 0.03% of the population. The exact cause of this condition is not known. Its treatment depends on the severity of the condition.
symptoms: The severity and presentation of the symptoms of schizoaffective disorder are unique to every patient. However, the defining features of this condition are:
A major mood episode may be a manic episode or a depressive episode, and
Not less than two weeks of psychotic symptoms during which there should not be a major mood episode.
Hallucination, i.e., seeing or listening to voices that do not exist.
Depression symptoms, such as sadness, worthlessness, and lack of motivation.
Delusion includes false beliefs.
Inability to take care of personal hygiene
Speech and communication problems.
Sudden manic episodes.
Difficulty performing daily tasks at home, school, or office.

diseases.name: What is Spinal Stenosis?
diseases.description: Spinal stenosis is a health condition in which the spaces within your vertebral column (backbone or spine) start narrowing. This ailment can put stress on the nerves that pass through your spine, resulting in pain and other health concerns. This condition mainly affects your neck and the lower back.
symptoms: Not everyone who has spinal stenosis experiences signs or symptoms. However, when symptoms happen to surface, in most cases, they tend to worsen over time. Moreover, the symptoms may vary from person to person, depending on the location of the stenosis and the affected nerves.
The symptoms of cervical stenosis include –
Pain in the neck
Tingling sensation or numbness in the arm, hand, leg, or foot
Weakness in the arm, hand, leg, or foot
Balancing issues
Difficulty walking
Urgency to urinate
Incontinence
The signs of lumbar stenosis include –
Tingling sensation or numbness in the leg or foot
Back pain
Weakness in the leg or foot
Cramping or pain in either one or both legs when standing for a long time or walking
When do you need medical attention?
It is crucial to get in touch with your doctor as soon as you experience the symptoms.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment.

diseases.name: What is Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Skin?
diseases.description: Squamous Cells are a type of cells that form the epidermis, the outermost layer of your skin. When the DNA in these cells develops mutations, it leads to one of the most common types; in fact, the second most common type of skin cancer called squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. It is not usually life-threatening, until left untreated when it spreads to other parts of the body including bones and lymph nodes.

diseases.name: What is Sweet Syndrome? Is Sweet Syndrome Contagious?
diseases.description: Sweet syndrome causes fever with painful skin rash, mostly on the face, neck, and arms. Sweet syndrome is an unknown skin condition called acute febrile neutrophilic dermatitis. However, the exact cause of Sweet syndrome is unknown; but can be triggered due to medication, illness, and infection. Additionally, Sweet syndrome can also occur along with some type of cancer. Sweet syndrome as a disease is not contagious, not a form of skin cancer , and is not hereditary. Sweet syndrome is generally treated with corticosteroids.
symptoms: Sweet syndrome signs and symptoms can vanish after treatment in a few days but can come back again. Some of the common symptoms of Sweet syndrome are as follows:
Fever
Bumps that grow easily in size and spread into painful clusters.
Small painful red bumps on back, neck, face, and arms.
Muscle and joint pain
Skin and mouth lesions
Skin discoloration
The feeling of being unwell.
Thus, if you witness any of the symptoms mentioned above or develop a painful red rash that grows quickly in size, you should immediately get in touch with the doctor to decide on the treatment plan.
Request an appointment at Apollo Hospitals
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

diseases.name: What is Tennis Elbow & It’s Symptoms?
diseases.description: Tennis elbow is a painful inflammation that usually occurs when tendons in your arms are overloaded. In simple words, this condition happens due to overuse of the wrist and arm.
symptoms: Pain related to tennis elbow may radiate from outside of the elbow into your forearm and wrist.
You may develop the following symptoms, related to tennis elbow:
You may feel pain while holding a coffee cup
You experience pain when you lift, move, or use something such as heavy objects and tools.
Shake hands or grip an object
Turn a doorknob

diseases.name: What is The Cause of Buerger's Disease? How Can You Treat It?
diseases.description: Buerger’s disease is a rare disorder characterized by inflamed arteries that eventually get blocked by blood clots. This condition is also known as thromboangiitis obliterans, and is generally observed in the arms and legs.
symptoms: The symptoms of Buerger’s disease are generally observed in the hands and feet are:
Open sores at the toes and fingers
Reddish-blue coloration of the skin
Numbness
Pain
Toes and fingers that turn pale due to cold
Observable vascular inflammation (swelling in the veins)

You must immediately visit the doctor when you observe swelling, redness, and pain in your fingers and toes alongside observable blood clots in your veins. Also, since some people are more likely than others to have Buerger’s disease , you must visit the doctor even if you do not consume tobacco.

Buerger’s disease is first observed in the hands and feet and develops in larger areas with time. Over a while, the blood clots cause infection and may even lead to gangrene . At such stages, the doctors advise the amputation of the affected parts.
Call 1860-500-1066 to book an appointment

No particular tests have been designed to solely confirm Buerger’s disease . Your doctor may nevertheless ask you to perform other tests that would rule out various other conditions. Some of these tests may be:
Blood Tests – Blood tests would help diagnose autoimmune diseases and rule out other illnesses such as diabetes , blood clotting factors, etc.
Allen’s Test – Your doctor would also check the blood flow through the vascular system in your hands. He would perform this test on both the hands by pressing the arteries and releasing it.
Angiogram – Your doctor may even ask you to perform an angiogram to check your arteries’ condition. Computed Tomography (CT) or Magnetic Resonance Imaging ( MRI ) scans can perform the angiogram.
Various risk factors that have been associated with Buerger’s disease are:

Tobacco Consumption – Buerger’s disease is primarily observed in people who consume tobacco in any form. Since the leading form of tobacco consumption is cigarette smoking, you are at a higher risk of acquiring Buerger’s disease if you smoke more than one and a half packs of cigarettes in a day. You are at equally high risk if you smoke hand-rolled tobacco.
Gum Disease – Despite the lack of an explanation, chronic gum disease has also been correlated with Buerger’s disease .
Gender – Males, in general, are far more prone to Buerger’s disease due to higher smoking than females.
Age – The first occurrence of Buerger’s disease is observed in people less than forty-five years of age.

Buerger’s disease is characterized by blood clots in the vascular system of the hands and legs. Owing to the developing blood clots, the hands and legs’ tissues do not receive blood and the accompanied oxygen and nutrients. These tissues eventually die and turn into gangrene. You are most likely to have gangrene tissue if your fingers and toes have lost the feeling of touch and have turned bluish-black. Such affected areas may also develop a foul smell.
Due to its severity, gangrenous tissue is amputated. In severe cases, Buerger’s disease can even lead to a heart attack or stroke .

So far, no treatment exists for Buerger’s disease . The most effective step that a patient can take is to quit all forms of tobacco use and consumption. The absence of tobacco would reduce the vascular system’s swelling and reduce blood clots’ occurrence afterward. Your doctor may prescribe medications that would help you stop smoking, thus preventing inflammation in the blood vessels.
Your doctor would also advise you to avoid nicotine replacement products as these too trigger Buerger’s disease . For such cases, your doctor would encourage you to take non-nicotine based products.
Your doctor may even advise you to join groups or programs that would assist in smoking cessation. These programs would guide you to deal with your cravings and live a tobacco-free life.
Other treatments that your doctor would advise you would be:
Improving the blood flow by dilating the arteries
Intermittent compression to increase the blood flow
Stimulation of the spinal cord
Amputation of tissue that has turned into gangrene
Some other experimental treatments that your doctor may or may not advise you to go through are:
Growing New Blood Vessels – You would be prescribed drugs that would stimulate new blood vessels’ growth.
Nerve Surgery – The nerves to the affected areas are surgically cut. This procedure would increase the blood flow to the region and also control the pain.
Bosentan – This drug, although prescribed for the lungs to treat high blood pressure , has shown to improve blood flow in patients suffering from Buerger’s disease .
Blood Vessel Procedure – This is a procedure wherein a thin catheter is inserted to open the blood vessels and improve blood flow.
Prevention of Buerger’s Disease

Since the primary cause of Buerger’s disease is tobacco, it is necessary to completely stop the use and intake of tobacco in any form. If you are a regular smoker, you may find quitting smoking or its consumption hard. You must talk to your doctor regarding the various strategies and techniques to quit smoking. These techniques would help you lead a healthy life and reduce the chances of an inflamed vascular system, developing clots, and gangrene in your body.
Conclusion

Buerger’s disease is a rare disease associated with excessive smoking that leads to blood clots in the extremities. To avoid and cure this disease, you must quit using all forms of tobacco. You must also visit your doctor, who would prescribe you the right alternatives, treatments, methodologies, and techniques to quit tobacco and introduce healthy habits.
Although no primary treatment has been discovered for this disease, quitting tobacco has been considered the most successful strategy to improve the disease’s status in the body.
FAQs
What are some home remedies that can be employed to treat Buerger’s disease?

Changes in lifestyle and introduction of habits such as exercise, skincare (especially in areas affected by Buerger’s disease ), prevention of infection, taking good care of your gums, and avoiding passive smoking can assist in curing Buerger’s disease .
How are gum care and Buerger’s disease-related?

Although not confirmed, gum infection has been directly correlated to Buerger’s disease . Some studies show that bacteremia is associated with periodontitis , which would directly induce inflammation of the blood vessels.

diseases.name: What Is the Most Appropriate Treatment for Pulmonary Hypertension?
diseases.description: Pulmonary hypertension is a medical term for a condition where high blood pressure affects the right side of your heart and the arteries in your lungs.

diseases.name: What is thrombosis? What are the first signs of thrombosis?
diseases.description: Most of us hurt ourselves in some or the other way and bleed. After a certain period, the blood from the site of the cut stops, and we see a rough mass of blood. That hard mass is known as a blood clot or thrombus. The formation of a blood clot is crucial for the body. This mechanism is necessary for our body, or else we would be blood deficient right now. So when does it become harmful for us? When the blood clot forms inside a blood vessel, it disturbs the normal functioning of your circulatory system. The blood cannot flow expectedly and is known as thrombosis. Thrombosis comes from the word thrombus that means blood clots.
symptoms: The signs of thrombosis can be painful or uncomfortable . They are:
Heaviness in legs , unbearable pain with cramps and soreness
Discomfort and itching throughout your leg
Frequent aches and a warm feeling in the leg
Discoloration, thickening, or ulceration of skin in the leg
Swelling in the leg
Deep vein thrombosis carries the risk of pulmonary embolism.
Shortness of breath
Chest pain and pain while deep breathing
Pain in the chest while coughing
Fatigue and weakness, dizziness, fainting
Pulse rate increases rapidly
Cough with traces of blood

diseases.name: What Is Trichomycosis? - Causes, Symptoms and Treatment
diseases.description: Trichomycosis is a skin and hair bacterial infection . Because it has no evident symptoms and does not cause discomfort, this condition frequently remains untreated.
symptoms: Some people have no symptoms, and doctors may only discover the infection after a thorough examination.
The unmistakable yellow, red, or black nodules that cling to the hair shaft may be noticed by others. Changes in the texture of the underarm hair may also be seen.
Perspiration that smells bad
Excessive sweat in the affected area
Sweat stains on clothes that are dark
Hair loss in the afflicted area
These signs indicate that the patient should consult a doctor or dermatologist for a diagnosis. The infection has no long-term consequences, but early treatment may make it easier to treat.

diseases.name: What Kind of Diet Should You Follow if You Have Nephrotic syndrome?
diseases.description: Nephrotic syndrome is a kind of kidney disorder caused by the damage of blood vessels responsible for filtering out waste and excess water from the body. It is a condition that causes the body to pass excess protein in your urine. It’s a kidney disorder that can affect both adults and children. However, the kidney damage caused by nephrotic syndrome can be treated with proper diet and timely medical attention.
symptoms: Foamy urine.
Swelling of your feet, legs, ankles, and sometimes even hands and face.
High blood pressure or cholesterol.
Fatigue.
Loss of appetite.
Feeling full at all times.

diseases.name: What Levels in Blood is Considered High Cholesterol?
diseases.description: Cholesterol is waxy substance that is found in the cells of our body. It is made by our liver and is also found in several food items like meat and dairy products. While we need some amount of cholesterol for our body to function normally, too much of it in the blood can lead to health issues like coronary artery disease.
symptoms: High cholesterol often does not show any symptoms. You may have high cholesterol levels for years without knowing about it. When your body has high cholesterol , it eventually leads to a build-up on the walls. This build-up is known as plaque which may harden over time and narrow the arteries.

This is where health issues start. Your body needs to transfer a certain amount of blood to every organ. When the arteries get narrowed, the blood flow to the organs from the heart gets hindered and causes serious health problems. The hardened plaque may also break into pieces and lead to the formation of blood clots which completely block the flow of blood. In some cases, the arteries may get completely clogged with plaque accumulation .

A blocked artery to the heart because of either of the reasons can cause a heart attack . Similarly, a blocked artery to the brain may lead to a stroke. The only way to detect high cholesterol is through regular blood tests. Unfortunately, most people discover their high cholesterol levels only after they experience a life-threatening event.

diseases.name: What support would you need to have if you have Myasthenia Gravis?
diseases.description: Myasthenia gravis is a condition that causes the muscles to weaken easily. The cause of this condition is the disruption of the communication that takes place between muscles and the nerves. As of now, there isn’t any cure for myasthenia gravis yet, but treatment can help relieve the signs and symptoms.

diseases.name: What You Should Know About Influenza
diseases.description: Influenza is a contagious viral infection, which causes respiratory illnesses. Commonly referred to as flu, it can attack the throat, lungs, and nose, by spreading through the upper or lower respiratory tract.

diseases.name: What's better for soothing Arthritis Pain? Ice or Heat?
diseases.description: Although common in the elderly, arthritis pain is more than just age-related wear and tear of the joints. Arthritis has several forms and can also occur in children and young adults. Women and overweight people are more likely to develop these joint diseases.
symptoms: Symptoms of arthritis include:
Joint pain
Swelling in the knee and around the joint
Tenderness
Joint stiffness
Restriction of movement
Pain during weight-bearing activities, such as walking, rising, standing, etc
Occasional warmth and redness around the joint
In RA, you may experience tiredness and reduced endurance.

diseases.name: Wheat Allergy: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis And Treatment
diseases.description: People with a wheat allergy have an abnormal immune system reaction to at least one of the proteins present in wheat.
symptoms: Common symptoms include:
Eczema
Urticaria
Hives
Hay fever
Angioedema
Nausea
Vomiting
Abdominal cramps
Rare symptoms are:
Arthritis
Anaphylaxis
Chest pains
Headache
Joint and muscle pains
Bloated stomach
Dizziness
Diarrhoea
Palpitations
Unexplained cough

diseases.name: When should you be Worried about Breast Rash?
diseases.description: Breast rash is a common condition that may be caused due to skin infection. In rare cases, breast rash can turn out to be a potentially dangerous health condition.
symptoms: Symptoms of breast rash include:
Blisters
Redness of skin
Sores
Swelling and itching
Formation of pus
Breast rash formed due to an infection may show symptoms such as fever , chills, pain. However, rashes from infections tend to get better as your body fights off infection.
Persistent itching
Rash that does not go away
Swelling and enlargement of breasts
Tenderness
Pitted orange peel on the skin.
Bruised red or purple skin that does not get better

diseases.name: Whiplash - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Whiplash is a common neck injury that occurs when the head is suddenly jerked forward and then backward, often as a result of a car accident. This rapid movement can strain the muscles and ligaments in the neck, leading to pain and discomfort. Understanding whiplash is crucial not only for those who have experienced it but also for anyone looking to prevent such injuries. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, prognosis, and frequently asked questions about whiplash.
symptoms: The symptoms of whiplash can vary in intensity and may not appear immediately after the injury. Common symptoms include:
Neck Pain: This is the most prevalent symptom, often described as a dull ache or sharp pain.
Stiffness: Difficulty moving the neck, especially when turning the head.
Headaches: Often starting at the base of the skull and radiating towards the forehead.
Fatigue: General tiredness and lack of energy.
Dizziness: A feeling of lightheadedness or imbalance.
Numbness or Tingling: Sensations in the arms or hands, indicating nerve involvement.

diseases.name: Whipple's Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Whipple's Disease is a rare but serious condition that primarily affects the gastrointestinal system, leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact a person's health and quality of life. Named after Dr. George Whipple, who first described the disease in 1907, it is caused by the bacterium Tropheryma whipplei . Understanding Whipple's Disease is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment, as it can lead to severe complications if left untreated. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Whipple's Disease, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Whipple's Disease presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Diarrhea: Often chronic and may be accompanied by weight loss.
Abdominal Pain: Cramping or discomfort in the abdomen.
Fatigue: Persistent tiredness that does not improve with rest.
Weight Loss: Unintentional weight loss due to malabsorption of nutrients.
Joint Pain: Arthritis-like symptoms affecting the joints.
Fever: Low-grade fever may occur in some cases.
Nutritional Deficiencies: Symptoms related to deficiencies in vitamins and minerals, such as anemia or osteoporosis.

diseases.name: White Matter Disease : Symptoms, Causes and Treatment
diseases.description: White matter disease refers to the damage to the brain’s white matter due to decreased blood supply to the area. It may result in memory, balance, and mobility problems. White matter illness is more likely to occur in those at increased risk for cardiovascular disease. The blog explains white matter disease, its symptoms, and treatment options.
symptoms: White matter in the brain aids with focus and problem-solving. Additionally, it significantly impacts walking, balance, and mood. Thus, one may notice the following signs when something is wrong with that part:
Problem remembering or learning new things
Difficulty solving problems
Depression
Difficulty walking
Balance problems and falling more often
Sluggish thinking
Urinary incontinence
Alzheimer’s disease , which affects the brain’s grey matter, is distinct from white matter disease. A doctor will need to perform tests to make a diagnosis if one is experiencing memory problems.
The following are the different ways the white matter disease is treated:
White matter disease may lead to balance and walking issues that may be treated with physical therapy, which often includes fall prevention education and rehabilitation.
The symptoms of depression can be reduced by arranging therapy sessions with a psychologist about issues with low mood and by visiting a psychiatrist for prescriptions of antidepressants.
The doctor can treat urinary incontinence with various methods, including medication, lifestyle modifications, and surgical procedures.

diseases.name: Whiteheads - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Whiteheads, a common skin condition, are a type of acne that can affect individuals of all ages. While often dismissed as a mere cosmetic issue, they can significantly impact self-esteem and overall skin health. Understanding whiteheads is crucial for effective management and prevention. This article will delve into the definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, complications, prevention strategies, and prognosis of whiteheads, providing a comprehensive overview for those seeking to understand this prevalent skin condition.
symptoms: Whiteheads are characterized by:
Small, round, white or flesh-colored bumps on the skin.
A smooth surface that may feel slightly raised.
Occasional tenderness or sensitivity in the affected area.

diseases.name: Who is a Universal Donor? Know all the Other Blood Groups Too
diseases.description: A universal donor is a person who can donate blood to any recipient of any blood group.

diseases.name: Whooping Cough (Pertussis)
diseases.description: Whooping cough is a highly contagious respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis bacteria.
symptoms: Runny nose and mild cough early on
Severe coughing fits
High-pitched whoop after coughing
Vomiting after coughing
Breathing pauses in infants

diseases.name: Why Do Men Go Bald? Is There Anything You Can Really Do About It?
diseases.description: Hair is an integral part of a person’s appearance . Hereditary baldness (baldness that runs in genes) always raises concerns. Let’s learn more about baldness and ways to prevent it.

diseases.name: Why is it important to get whooping cough treated quickly?
diseases.description: Whooping cough, also known as Pertussis, is a respiratory infection in humans that is mainly caused by a bacteria called Bordetella Pertussis. It is a highly communicable disease, and the main source of infection to others is by droplet route (when an infected person sneezes or coughs, the germs spread via air and infect others). Earlier, whooping cough was called a childhood disease, but now it has been found that the disease can affect people of any age from infants to old age.
symptoms: Whooping cough can mimic the symptoms of any other respiratory illnesses, but some differentiating factors make it unique from others. To differentiate the disease, it is important to gather a detailed history of the patient by assessing the signs/symptoms and observing physical findings. In some patients, a Whooping sound may not always be present, but a sound of hacking cough is often present.
Mild Cough (Dry cough)
Runny nose
Fever (<102 degrees Fahrenheit)
Vomiting
Difficulty in breathing
Watery eyes
Ear infections

diseases.name: Why is it so Important to Detect Hydrocephalus Early?
diseases.description: Hydrocephalus is defined as the buildup of excess fluid in the cavities inside the brain. The fluid doesn’t flow or get absorbed anywhere, leading to blockages that can put pressure on your brain. It is common in infants or adults above the age of 60. It is important to get the condition treated early, or it may lead to severe impairment in the brain.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms associated with hydrocephalus vary among individuals. Infants and people above 60 years are at a higher risk of developing hydrocephalus.
Symptoms in infants:
● A rapid increase in the size of the head
● A bulging spot on top of the head
● Unusually large head.
Physical symptoms:
● Seizures .
● Vomiting.
● Irritability.
● Poor growth.
● Poor responsiveness to touch
Symptoms in Kids :
● Poor performance in school.
● Irritability or crankiness.
● Personality changes.
● Problems with walking and talking.
● Vision problems.
● Headache .
● Laziness.
● Seizures.
● Nausea .
● Poor coordination.
● Poor appetite.
● Abnormal growth of a toddler’s head
● Impaired vision.
● Headaches.
● Lethargy
● Memory loss .
● Issues with concentration and other thinking skills
● Frequent urge to urinate or loss of bladder control
Symptoms in older adults:
● Difficulty walking.
● Memory loss.
● Loss of bladder control.

Complications of hydrocephalus vary in individuals and are often hard to predict. If an infant develops hydrocephalus, it may result in physical, intellectual, and developmental disabilities. When treated at the right time, it may pose fewer complications.

Even after the treatment, adults who experience a decline in memory may have poor recoveries. In some cases, the symptoms may appear even after treatment. How severe the complications are going to be after the treatment depends on:
● Timely diagnosis and treatment of hydrocephalus.
● The severity of initial symptoms.
● Medical or developmental problems.
In several cases, the exact cause of hydrocephalus remains unknown.
The risk factors in newborns are:
● A possible complication of premature birth and bleeding within the ventricles of the brain
● Infection in the uterus during pregnancy leading to damage in fetal brain tissues.
● Abnormal development of the nervous system leading to obstruction in the cerebrospinal fluid flow
