Other factors contributing to the development of hydrocephalus in people of other age groups include:
● Brain tumours or lesions
● Spinal cord tumour
● Bleeding in the brain from a head injury
● Central nervous system infections
● Previous traumatic injuries to the brain

If you have mild symptoms of hydrocephalus, you may not need treatment. In severe cases, the doctor will recommend surgery. There are two types of surgical approaches for the treatment of hydrocephalus – shunt and endoscopic third ventriculostomy (a surgical procedure where the excess fluid is drained out of the brain).
● Shunt

The placement of a shunt (a long flexible plastic tube) is the most common treatment for patients with hydrocephalus. The shunt is placed inside the brain to keep the fluid flowing in the right direction.

One end of the shunt is placed in one of the ventricles of the brain. The other end is placed in another part of the body, like the stomach. This will redirect the excess fluid from the brain to the stomach.
● Endoscopic third ventriculostomy

It is a surgical procedure used in some cases. Using this approach, the excess cerebrospinal fluid is drained from the ventricles. The surgeon will use a small video camera to get the visualisation inside your brain. They will make a small hole either at the bottom or in between the ventricles. This will help release the excess cerebrospinal fluid from the brain.
Very few cases of hydrocephalus can be prevented. The precautionary measures include:
● Regular health checkups during pregnancy.
● Use of safety gears such as helmets while riding a motorcycle.
● Wearing seatbelts while driving the car.
What is the survival rate with hydrocephalus?

When caught early, the survival rate with hydrocephalus is high. The survival rate in infants below 3 months is extremely low. For hydrocephalus patients above the age of 6 months, the survival rate is 64%.
Can hydrocephalus be treated without surgery?

Currently, there is no way to cure hydrocephalus without surgery. The excess fluid needs to be drained from the brain. With the right diagnosis, the doctor may recommend either the shunt system or the endoscopic third ventriculostomy. Depending on the severity of the hydrocephalus, some people may need additional treatment as well.
Does hydrocephalus affect memory?

Memory loss is one of the symptoms of hydrocephalus in adults. In some cases, adults who experienced memory loss may have poor recoveries. When diagnosed and treated early, the symptoms may go away. In some cases, some of the symptoms reoccur.

diseases.name: Why Placenta Previa Needs Extra Care
diseases.description: The placenta is an organ which develops during pregnancy. It provides oxygen & nutrition to the baby and removes wastes & toxins. The placenta is attached to the baby via the umbilical cord. At most times, the placenta is attached at the top or side of the uterus, away from the cervix. Placenta previa takes place when the baby’s placenta ends up covering the mother’s cervix partially or totally.
symptoms: It is quite possible that you would not even know that you have placenta previa until and unless your doctor discovers it during a routine ultrasound . The main symptom of this condition is bright red vaginal bleeding without any pain during the second half of the pregnancy. The flow could range from being light or heavy accompanied by contractions. Other symptoms may include:
Cramps or sharp pains
Bleeding which starts, stops and then starts again days later
Bleeding after intercourse

diseases.name: Williams Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Williams Syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 7,500 births. Characterized by a unique combination of physical, cognitive, and behavioral features, this condition has garnered significant attention in the medical community due to its distinctive characteristics and the challenges it presents to affected individuals and their families. Understanding Williams Syndrome is crucial not only for those diagnosed but also for healthcare providers, educators, and the general public, as it fosters awareness and support for those living with this condition.
symptoms: Williams Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary widely among individuals. Common symptoms include:
Distinctive Facial Features: Individuals often have a broad forehead, short nose, full cheeks, and a wide mouth with full lips.
Cardiovascular Issues: Many individuals experience heart problems, particularly supravalvular aortic stenosis, which can lead to serious complications if not monitored.
Developmental Delays: Children with Williams Syndrome may experience delays in speech and motor skills, although they often have strong verbal abilities.
Cognitive Challenges: While individuals may have mild to moderate intellectual disabilities, many exhibit strengths in areas such as music and social skills.
Hypercalcemia: Elevated calcium levels can occur, particularly in infancy, leading to potential health issues.
Sociability: A hallmark of Williams Syndrome is an outgoing and friendly personality, often described as "overly friendly."

diseases.name: Wilms Tumor - Early Signs, Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment Explained
diseases.description: Wilms Tumor in Children: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment Options
symptoms: The symptoms of Wilms tumor can be vague and are often mistaken for other common childhood illnesses. However, if you notice these symptoms, especially if they are persistent, it is important to see a doctor for a proper evaluation.
As the cancer progresses, other symptoms may appear:
High Blood Pressure (Hypertension): The tumor can produce hormones that cause a child's blood pressure to rise.
Nausea and Vomiting
Loss of Appetite
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or a general lack of energy.
Trouble Breathing: If the cancer has spread to the lungs, it can cause a persistent cough or shortness of breath.
If you have a gut feeling that something is wrong with your child, do not hesitate to seek medical attention.

diseases.name: Wilson Disease - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Wilson Disease is a rare genetic disorder that affects the body's ability to metabolize copper, leading to its accumulation in various organs, particularly the liver and brain. This condition is significant not only because of its potential to cause severe health complications but also due to its treatability when diagnosed early. Understanding Wilson Disease is crucial for timely intervention and management, which can significantly improve the quality of life for those affected.
symptoms: Wilson Disease can manifest in various ways, and symptoms may vary depending on the organs affected. Common symptoms include:
Liver Symptoms: Fatigue, jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), abdominal pain, and swelling due to liver dysfunction.
Neurological Symptoms: Tremors, difficulty speaking, changes in behavior, mood swings, and cognitive decline.
Psychiatric Symptoms: Depression, anxiety, and personality changes.
Other Symptoms: Kayser-Fleischer rings (copper deposits in the eyes), arthritis, and kidney problems.

diseases.name: Wilson's Disease - Diagnosis and How You Can Manage it in the Long-Term
diseases.description: Wilson’s disease is a rare genetic disorder that is of autosomal recessive type. This is present equally in males and females. When there is a history of Wilson’s disease in the family, then there are more chances for the next generation to carry the gene in their body. Their offspring will act as either the carrier or will have the mutated ATP7B gene expression in their body. Approximately 1 in 30,000 individuals are prone to this disease.
symptoms: Wilson’s disease does not show symptoms at an early stage. Only when it predominates the liver and brain with copper, some signs and symptoms are visible. Neurological problems, liver damage , and psychiatric problems are associated with Wilson’s disease. The first symptom appears from the age to 6 to 45. The symptoms mentioned here are common for the liver. ● Weakness ● Tiredness ● Weight loss ● Abdominal pain ● Kayser-Fleischer rings or sunflower cataract ● Jaundice ● Vomiting ● Muscle cramps ● Edema (swelling of legs and abdomen) ● Lack of physical coordination ● Spider angiomas (visible blood vessels on the skin) Sometimes psychiatric problems are seen associated at the early stage like mood swings and personality change. The symptoms related to the brain are: ● Vision impairment ● Mood swings ● Depression ● Drooling ● Change in personality ● Irregular walking phase ● Migraine At an advanced stage, problems related to the muscular system like muscle cramps, pain, and seizures may be evident . Other symptoms include: ● Kidney stones – Frequent kidney stones and pain on the lower abdomen ● Osteoporosis – Weakening of the bones ● Arthritis

diseases.name: Winged Scapula - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Winged scapula is a condition characterized by the protrusion of the shoulder blade (scapula) away from the back, resembling a wing. This abnormal positioning can lead to discomfort, limited mobility, and functional impairment of the shoulder. Understanding winged scapula is crucial, as it can significantly affect daily activities and overall quality of life. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of winged scapula, including its definition, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: The symptoms of winged scapula can vary depending on the severity of the condition and the underlying cause. Common symptoms include:
Protrusion of the Scapula: The most noticeable sign is the scapula sticking out from the back, especially when pushing against resistance.
Shoulder Pain: Discomfort or pain in the shoulder region may occur, particularly during movement.
Limited Range of Motion: Individuals may experience difficulty lifting their arms or performing overhead activities.
Muscle Weakness: Weakness in the shoulder and upper back muscles can be present, affecting overall arm function.

diseases.name: Wiskott Aldrich Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Wiskott Aldrich Syndrome (WAS) is a rare, X-linked genetic disorder that primarily affects males. It is characterized by a triad of symptoms: eczema, recurrent infections, and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count). Understanding WAS is crucial not only for those diagnosed with the condition but also for healthcare providers and families, as early diagnosis and management can significantly improve quality of life and outcomes. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Wiskott Aldrich Syndrome, including its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment options, and more.
symptoms: Wiskott Aldrich Syndrome presents with a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity among affected individuals. The three hallmark symptoms include:
Eczema: This skin condition often appears in infancy and can cause itchy, inflamed skin. It may worsen with environmental triggers such as heat, sweat, or allergens.
Recurrent Infections: Individuals with WAS are prone to infections due to their compromised immune system. Common infections include respiratory infections, ear infections, and skin infections.
Thrombocytopenia: Low platelet counts can lead to easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from cuts, and an increased risk of bleeding disorders.

diseases.name: Wolf Hirschhorn Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Wolf Hirschhorn Syndrome (WHS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects various aspects of physical and cognitive development. Characterized by distinctive facial features, growth delays, and intellectual disabilities, WHS is significant not only for its clinical manifestations but also for the insights it provides into genetic disorders. Understanding WHS is crucial for families affected by the syndrome, healthcare providers, and researchers working in genetics and developmental disorders.
symptoms: Wolf Hirschhorn Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms that can vary significantly from one individual to another. Common symptoms include:
Distinctive Facial Features: These may include a prominent forehead, a flat nasal bridge, widely spaced eyes (hypertelorism), and a small chin.
Growth Delays: Children with WHS often experience growth retardation, leading to shorter stature compared to peers.
Intellectual Disabilities: Most individuals with WHS have some degree of intellectual disability, ranging from mild to severe.
Seizures: Many affected individuals experience seizures, which can vary in type and frequency.
Skeletal Abnormalities: Some may have skeletal issues, such as scoliosis or limb malformations.
Heart Defects: Congenital heart defects are common in individuals with WHS.

diseases.name: Wolfram Syndrome - Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
diseases.description: Wolfram Syndrome , also known as DIDMOAD syndrome, is a rare genetic disorder characterized by a combination of diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy, and deafness. This condition is significant not only due to its complex nature but also because it can lead to severe complications if not diagnosed and managed properly. Understanding Wolfram Syndrome is crucial for patients, families, and healthcare providers to ensure timely intervention and support.
symptoms: Wolfram Syndrome presents a variety of symptoms, which can vary in severity among individuals. The most common symptoms include:
Diabetes Mellitus: Often the first symptom to appear, it is characterized by high blood sugar levels due to insufficient insulin production.
Optic Atrophy: This refers to the degeneration of the optic nerve, leading to vision loss or impairment.
Sensorineural Hearing Loss: A progressive loss of hearing that can range from mild to profound.
Diabetes Insipidus: A condition characterized by excessive thirst and urination due to the inability of the kidneys to concentrate urine.
Urinary Tract Abnormalities: Some individuals may experience issues such as urinary incontinence or recurrent urinary tract infections.
Psychiatric Disorders: Depression, anxiety, and other mood disorders may occur in some patients.

diseases.name: Wrist Problems and Injuries
diseases.description: Wrist problems include a range of injuries and conditions affecting the bones, tendons, ligaments, and nerves of the wrist joint. Common problems include sprains, fractures (especially of the distal radius), tendinitis, nerve compression (carpal tunnel syndrome), and arthritis. The wrist is particularly vulnerable in falls and repetitive-use activities.
symptoms: Wrist pain (acute or chronic)
Swelling
Reduced range of motion
Weakness in grip
Numbness or tingling (if nerves involved)
Clicking or popping with movement (ligament injuries)

diseases.name: Xanthelasma
diseases.description: Xanthelasma appears as yellowish cholesterol-rich plaques around the eyelids. It is usually benign but may be associated with lipid abnormalities and cardiovascular risk.
symptoms: Soft yellowish patches around eyelids
Usually painless skin lesions
Slow enlargement over time
Cosmetic concern

diseases.name: Xeroderma Pigmentosum
diseases.description: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a rare inherited disorder in which the skin has extreme sensitivity to ultraviolet (UV) light due to impaired DNA repair mechanisms.
symptoms: Severe sun sensitivity from early life
Freckling and pigmentation changes
Dry skin and premature skin aging
High risk of skin cancers
Eye irritation in sunlight

diseases.name: Xerophthalmia
diseases.description: Xerophthalmia is an eye condition caused by vitamin A deficiency, leading to dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea and potential vision loss if untreated.
symptoms: Dry eyes and irritation
Night blindness
Bitot spots on conjunctiva
Corneal dryness or ulceration
Blurred vision in severe cases

diseases.name: XXX chromosome disorder or Triple X Syndrome: Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
diseases.description: Generally, each person has one pair of sex chromosomes in each cell. The presence of an extra X chromosome in each of a female’s cells is known as trisomy X, commonly known as triple X syndrome, 47, or XXX. Although girls with this disorder are often taller than average, this chromosomal change does not result in any distinctive physical characteristics or genetic disorders. The majority of women with trisomy X have normal sexual development and can conceive.
symptoms: The signs and symptoms of Triple X Syndrome can vary significantly from one individual to another. Some females may have no noticeable symptoms at all, while others may experience mild to moderate developmental, physical, or emotional difficulties. These signs often become more apparent at different stages of life.

diseases.name: XYY Syndrome
diseases.description: XYY syndrome is a chromosomal condition in males caused by an extra Y chromosome (47,XYY). Many individuals are mildly affected, but some have learning and behavioral difficulties.
symptoms: Tall stature
Speech and language delays
Learning difficulties
Motor skill challenges
Behavioral or attention concerns in some children

diseases.name: Yaws
diseases.description: Yaws is a chronic bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum pertenue, primarily affecting skin, bones, and cartilage in children living in tropical regions.
symptoms: Initial painless skin lesion
Secondary skin ulcers or nodules
Bone pain and swelling
Deformities in untreated chronic disease

diseases.name: Yellow Fever
diseases.description: Yellow fever is a viral hemorrhagic disease transmitted by infected mosquitoes in tropical regions of Africa and South America.
symptoms: Fever and chills
Headache and muscle pain
Nausea and vomiting
Jaundice in severe cases
Bleeding and organ failure in critical illness

diseases.name: Yellow Nail Syndrome
diseases.description: Yellow nail syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by yellow thickened nails, lymphedema, and respiratory manifestations such as chronic cough or pleural effusion.
symptoms: Slow-growing yellow thick nails
Nail curvature or detachment
Lymphedema (usually legs)
Chronic sinus or lung symptoms
Pleural effusions in some patients

diseases.name: Zellweger Syndrome
diseases.description: Zellweger syndrome is a severe peroxisome biogenesis disorder present from birth, affecting multiple organs including brain, liver, and kidneys.
symptoms: Hypotonia (poor muscle tone) in newborns
Feeding difficulties and poor growth
Developmental delay and seizures
Vision and hearing impairment
Liver dysfunction

diseases.name: Zellweger Syndrome Disease: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment
diseases.description: Zellweger syndrome (ZS) is a genetic disorder passed down from parents to children. The nerves and the metabolism is severely affected in the newborn. Newborns may have brain, liver, and kidney issues and difficulty feeding or moving.
symptoms: Zellweger syndrome is quite rare. Both males and females can be born with this disorder. It affects several parts of body, including:
Brain and Nervous System: Abnormal brain growth leading to seizures , diminished or absent reflexes, vision and hearing disability, severe mental retardation, and developmental delay
Muscles and bones: Deficient muscle tone (called hypotonia ), bone defects in the legs, hands, and feet
Liver damage: Enlarged liver with impaired function, jaundice
Kidney issues: Renal cysts , hydronephrosis
Facial abnormalities common in ZS include:
Flattened face
High forehead
Broad nose bridge
Wide-set eyes
Epicanthal folds (skin folds at inner corners of eyes)
Underdeveloped eyebrow ridges
Other symptoms include enlarged spleen , hearing and vision issues, bleeding in the digestive tract, seizures, underdeveloped muscles, movement issues, and problems in feeding.

diseases.name: Zenkers Diverticulum
diseases.description: Zenker’s diverticulum is an outpouching of the upper esophagus that can cause swallowing problems and regurgitation, typically in older adults.
symptoms: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia)
Regurgitation of undigested food
Chronic cough or aspiration
Bad breath (halitosis)
Sensation of lump in throat

diseases.name: Zika Virus Infection
diseases.description: Zika virus infection is a mosquito-borne viral illness. Most cases are mild, but infection during pregnancy is associated with serious fetal complications.
symptoms: Mild fever
Rash
Joint pain
Red eyes (conjunctivitis)
Headache or fatigue

diseases.name: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome
diseases.description: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is a condition in which gastrin-secreting tumors (gastrinomas) cause excessive stomach acid production and severe recurrent peptic ulcers.
symptoms: Abdominal pain
Recurrent peptic ulcers
Chronic diarrhea
Acid reflux and heartburn
Nausea or gastrointestinal bleeding in severe cases

diseases.name: Zoonotic Diseases
diseases.description: Zoonotic diseases are infections transmitted from animals to humans through direct contact, vectors, food, water, or environmental exposure.
symptoms: Fever and fatigue
Respiratory or gastrointestinal symptoms
Skin lesions or rashes
Neurological symptoms in severe infections

diseases.name: गंभीर जन्मजात हृदय रोग – जोखिम कारक
diseases.description: जन्मजात हृदय रोग (सीएचडी) सभी मान्यता प्राप्त संरचनात्मक जन्म दोषों में सबसे अधिक प्रचलित और गंभीर हैं। उनका अनुमानित प्रचलन 0.9% है, जिसका अर्थ है कि हर 110 नवजात शिशुओं में से एक इस बीमारी के साथ पैदा होता है। उन्हें मूल रूप से बहु-कारक (अर्थात कई कारकों की भागीदारी) माना जाता है और परिणामस्वरूप, दोष के लिए एक ही कारण का पता लगाना मुश्किल है। चूंकि भ्रूण का हृदय गर्भावस्था के 14 - 60 दिनों के बीच विकसित होता है, इसलिए आनुवंशिक रूप से अतिसंवेदनशील व्यक्ति में संक्रमण या दवाओं के रूप में इस चरण के दौरान उत्पन्न होने वाली कोई भी समस्या गंभीर सीएचडी का कारण बन सकती है। सी.एच.डी. से पीड़ित कई बच्चे अपने जीवन के एक वर्ष में ही मर जाते हैं, और जो बच जाते हैं, उन्हें प्रायः कई शल्यचिकित्साओं, लम्बे समय तक अस्पताल में रहने तथा संबंधित विकलांगताओं के लिए आजीवन उपचार की आवश्यकता होती है।
